items.statement: No major disruption in India business from geopolitical events; Middle East sales cycles slightly longer recently but normalizing.
items.quote: In the Middle East business, which is a small contributor, even there, we have not seen any major impact or disruption in our business -- in our existing business. We have seen small impact in the sales cycles, they become slightly longer in the last few weeks, but we are seeing that also coming back to normal as the overall situation normalizes in the region.

items.statement: FY27 ROA expected towards upper end of medium-term 2-2.2% range, with ~10 bps compression from FY26's 2.3% if no policy rate hike
items.quote: We should be in the medium term range with a bias towards hitting the upper end of the medium term range in the ROA, which is our computation.

items.statement: Full FY27 assessment to be given with Q1 results; Q1 yields sideways, full year margin compression expected
items.quote: This year also we'll give a full assessment for the year in along with the quarter 1 call.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 NIM fell 12 bps sequentially to 3.8% due to 14 bps yield compression from lower acquisition pricing and portfolio attrition, partially offset by 4 bps CoF benefit
items.quote: Net interest margin for the quarter dropped by 12 bps sequentially from 4% in Q3 FY26 to 3.8% in Q4 FY 26, largely due to moderation in net interest income as I explained above.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 spread compression expected as lower-priced new book replaces higher-yielding run-off, partially offset by opex efficiency and lower credit costs
items.quote: Through the year, we will see some contraction in the margin, which will get partially offset by opex efficiency and a partially offset by lower loan losses.

items.statement: Q4 CoF down 4 bps sequentially to 7.3% (down 60 bps YoY); Q1 CoF expected marginally lower by 2-3 bps from maturing high-cost NCDs and NHB refinance reset
items.quote: Year-on-year cost of funds have moderated by 60 bps to 7.3% against 7.9% in Q4 FY25. Sequential cost reduced by 4 bps on account of rate transmission on existing borrowing.

items.statement: Money market borrowing at elevated rates; 3-5 year tenor, CP 5% of book at 3-12 month tenor; OIS used to convert fixed NCDs to floating near repo
items.quote: We generally borrow between 3 years to 5 years, generally borrow 3 to 5 year with some part of 10 year, but last year I think generally it was 3 year and a 5 year.

items.statement: Home loan industry IHL growth ~9.5%; BHFL targets 21-23% AUM growth, driving faster non-home loan growth to maintain PBC via assignment
items.quote: At an industry level as well if you look at basis the data which we got last published on IHL growth in the industry is close to 9.5%.

items.statement: Q4 disbursements grew 23% YoY to INR17,506 cr; sequential growth improved to 6% from 4% in Q3
items.quote: Disbursements on a Y -o-Y basis grew 23% from INR14,250 crores to INR17,506 crores. On a sequential basis, disbursement growth for this quarter was 6% which improved against 4% growth in Q3.

items.statement: Product mix: Home loans 54.1%, LRD 22.4%, LAP 10.8%, DF 11.5%; LRD grew 44%, LAP 24%, HL 18%, DF 13% YoY
items.quote: Portfolio composition remained well -diversified with home loan being dominant product with 54.1% mix, LAP at 10.8%, LRD at 22.4%, and DF at 11.5%.

items.statement: Sambhav (affordable + near prime) monthly disbursements INR410-425 cr in Q4; on track for INR600 cr+ monthly in next 12 months; AUM ~INR9,000 cr (70-30 affordable/near prime)
items.quote: Sambhav loans now are acquiring in the in the range of INR410 crores to INR425 crores of average monthly disbursements during the quarter, the quarter gone by, and business is well on track to achieve INR600 crores plus of a monthly disbursement over next 12 months.

items.statement: GNPA stable at 27 bps QoQ (improved from 29 bps YoY); NNPA 11 bps; Stage 2 improved 1 bp to 36 bps; PCR ~60% (up 1.2% QoQ); annualized credit cost 19 bps (10 bps ex-stage 2 strengthening)
items.quote: Asset quality continued to remain healthy with GNPA in line with Q3 FY'26 at 27 bps and NNPA also stable sequentially at 11 bps. Annualized credit cost for the quarter was 19 bps as compared to 11 bps in Q4 FY25.

items.statement: Stage 2 PCR increased 6% as prudence measure, not due to stress; bounce rates improving across all segments including April
items.quote: Given a overall macro scenario, we just thought that instead of a creating any other overlay then which creates another problems, we just thought that it is better that internal Stage 2 assets because Stage 2 assets in any case we know are in they are not Stage 1, they have moved to a certain kind of a difficulty level.

items.statement: Home loan attrition ~20%, BT-out ~10% (mostly to PSU banks, then HDFC/ICICI); Q4 BT-out did not decline as usual post rate cut due to aggressive bank pricing
items.quote: BT-out rate also remains in the same range of what we had in terms of that is attrition is ~20%, BT-out would be 14% BT-out would be in the range of 10%.

items.statement: PSU banks largest source of BT-out; competitive intensity high in Q4 from both PSU and private banks; BHFL matches bank pricing (SBI, HDFC) in prime housing
items.quote: So this is largely the banks. Public sector banks are the largest component, followed by HDFC or ICICI. So largest is public sector

items.statement: IHL (regulatory home loan) at 50.45% of total assets, above 50% minimum; reported monthly, never breached; co-lending/pool purchase explored but won't move needle
items.quote: As long as you are above 50 and 60, there is no ticker from a regulator which can be there on the number what should be there because it's a regulation.

items.statement: Network expanded to 226 branches, 182 locations; Sambhav operational in 73 locations (72 Tier-4)
items.quote: Geographical network of the company now spans across 226 branches and 182 locations.

items.statement: Borrowing mix: money market 49%, bank 41%, NHB 10%; QoQ bank +140 bps, CP +110 bps, NHB +120 bps, NCD -370 bps; floating rate borrowings 63% (incl. OIS)
items.quote: Borrowing mix remained well -diversified with money market composition at 49%, bank borrowings at 41% and NHB refinance at 10%.

items.statement: FY26 NIM moderated 7 bps vs initial 15-20 bps estimate; Opex/NTI 19.7% vs 20-21% estimate; GNPA 27 bps vs 35-40 bps estimate; ROA/ROE ahead of July '25 guidance
items.quote: Company managed NIM moderation to 7 bps as against our initial assessment of 15 to 20 bps on account of higher fee income and assignment income than planned.

items.statement: On-book yields: HL 8.5-8.6%, LAP +150 bps, LRD 7.9-8%, DF 11.5-11.75%; incremental HL yield ~8.05-8.10%
items.quote: Home loans would be in around 8.5 -8.6 corridor, LAP would be around 150 bps above that, LRD around 7.9-8% corridor, and developer finance would be 11.5-11.75 corridor.

items.statement: Fee income grew to INR297 cr from INR200 cr (insurance + foreclosure); assignment income balances home vs non-home loan growth mix
items.quote: Fee income last year was INR200 crores and this year it was INR297 crores, broadly driven by insurance income and some part of foreclosure income.

items.statement: Money market pricing in ~75 bps rate hike via OIS; if policy rates don't rise, CoF inches up and margins compress; if policy hikes, pass-through ~15-20 bps protects spreads
items.quote: If you look at a n OIS today, it prices in a 75 bps kind of a rate hike scenario, which I'm not fully certain.

items.statement: No micro stress seen; Stage 2 strengthening purely prudential; bounce rates improving QoQ including March and April
items.quote: In our portfolio in all the metrics, whether it's a first bounce or first 12 -month bounce, early bounce, whether it is prime, non -prime, affordable, LRD in any case we don't have, LAP, all the bounce metrics also are showing a downward trend.

items.statement: Dedicated front-end teams for near prime (centralized hub) and affordable (regional hubs) under Sambhav; salaried mix 68%, CIBIL>750 at 65%, ATS INR28 lakh
items.quote: Dedicated front -end teams are deployed for both near prime and affordable businesses with differentiated underwriting model. We have centralized hub-based model for near prime while having regional hubs for affordable.

items.statement: Sequential mix shift: LRD +50 bps, LAP +10 bps, HL -50 bps, DF -10 bps; non-home growing faster to offset HL BT-out and maintain PBC
items.quote: Portfolio mix remains well -diversified across products with sequential increment in LRD by 50 bps and LAP by 10 bps, offsetting reduction in home loans by 50 bps and construction finance by 10 bps.

items.statement: CAR 22.46%, PBC 60.88% (both above regulatory thresholds); net worth INR22,527 cr; ROA 2.3%, ROE 12.1% for FY26
items.quote: The company maintains comfortable capital adequacy position with CAR at 22.46% and PBC at 60.88%, both above regulatory thresholds.

name: Canara Robeco Asset Management Company Ltd

items.statement: Closing AUM was approximately INR1.07 lakh crores as of March 31, 2026, up 3.2% year-on-year.
items.quote: Our closing AUM stands at approximately INR1.07 lakh crores, up by almost 3.2% year-on-year, supported by a base of over 50.8 lakh investor folios across India.

items.statement: Quarterly average AUM grew 14% year-on-year to approximately INR1.17 lakh crores.
items.quote: Our quarterly ave rage AUM also grew by 14% year -on-year to close approximately at INR1.17 lakh crores, a testament to our disciplined investment philosophy and enduring trust of our investors

items.statement: Equity-to-debt mix is approximately 91% to 9%.
items.quote: Our growth has been well -rounded, driven by a healthy equity -to-debt mix of appr oximately 91% to 9

items.statement: Individual investors contribute approximately 86% of assets, institutional investors 14%.
items.quote: Individual investors centric investor base contributing approximately 86% and institutional investors 14% of our assets.

items.statement: Distribution ecosystem expanded to over 56,000 empaneled partners and 29 branches from 23 last year.
items.quote: Progress has also been fueled by a robust and growing distribution ecosystem of over 56,000 empaneled partners, an d we've grown our branch es to 29 branches from 23 of last year

items.statement: SIP AUM contributes roughly one-third of total AUM.
items.quote: SIP is an important constituent for us. It contributes roughly one-third of our AUM.

items.statement: Overall yield for FY26 was about 35 bps; equity yield 37 bps, fixed income 30 bps, liquid 3 bps.
items.quote: In terms of the split, for the financial year FY26, our equity AUM contributed yield was about 37 bps, fixed income was about 30 bps, liquid was about 3 bps, and on an overall basis we were at about 35 bps.

items.statement: Management is comfortable with yields in the 32-40 bps range but focuses more on PAT than yield.
items.quote: For us, we are comfortable with yields being in the range of 32 to 40. That's the range we look at, but we focus more on PAT.

items.statement: Revenue from operations grew 17% year-on-year to INR424.9 crores; total income grew 13% to INR454.6 crores; PAT grew 7% to INR203.8 crores.
items.value: Revenue INR424.9 cr, PAT INR203.8 cr
items.quote: In FY26, our revenue from operations stood at INR424.9 crores as compared to INR364.5 crores in FY25, representing a 17.0% year-on-year growth. In FY26, total income stood at INR454.6 crores, compared to INR403 crores in FY25, representing a growth of 13.0% year-on-year. Profit after tax for FY26 stood at INR203.8 crores, compared to INR190.7 crores in the previous year, marking a robust 7% year-o

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio target range is 40% to 50%.
items.quote: The way we like to look at employee cost or total cost is our cost-to-income ratio. We like it to be between 40% and 50%. That's the range we look at.

items.statement: Employee benefit expense for Q4 FY26 was INR23.7 crores; full-year expense increased 21% to INR107.1 crores.
items.quote: So, there is a one-off of expenses has been seated in the last years, but it is better to look at the yearly cost, which has been increased by 21% from INR88.5 crores to INR107.1 crores.

items.statement: TER replaced by BER with GST separate; impact still being evaluated, at worst neutral, at best may gain a couple of basis points.
items.quote: We are still evaluating impacts of that and are talking to our key distributors to see how best we can share that impact between the two of us. So, it's still an evolving situation with us. At worst, we will be neutral on this, at best we probably may gain a couple of basis points.

items.statement: Technology investments made to support regulatory environment; one-off costs in Q4 related to labour code, employee costs, and technology.
items.quote: Well, one-offs are related to the labour code, some one-offs are related to some employee costs, and there are some, which are related to technology investments that we've made to support the regulatory environment.

items.statement: Currently focused on active mutual fund space; not launching ETFs, index funds, or AIFs in near term as they would impact overall yield.
items.quote: Not in the in the near-term, because that will only -- that will help you grow the AUM, but it will impact the overall yield.

items.statement: Plan to launch another NFO in the next four to five months; board approvals obtained, awaiting regulatory approval.
items.quote: On the NFO, we will be launching another NFO in the next four to five months. We have already got Board approvals for the next one, but they still need to go through a process of getting the regulatory approval before we are able to announce it.

items.statement: Setting up dedicated sales teams across five locations to drive SIP growth; expect directional change in SIP book in next six months.
items.quote: But in terms of going forward, what we are planning to do is actually set up sales teams dedicated to SIPs. So, we are doing that across five locations and we'll expand it further if needed. But we are putting resources behind this initiative and you will see in the next six months, a directional change in the way the SIP book will grow for us.

items.statement: Digital channel contributes 28% of AUM.
items.quote: So, the digital AUM -- 28% of our AUM comes from the digital channel. So that is the number that is there for the digital, the direct channel, and majority of that will be in the digital format.

items.statement: ELSS SIPs facing challenges due to tax changes; not all ELSS AUM is SIP-based, and AUM decline is largely mark-to-market from 15% equity market correction.
items.quote: For example, ELSS as a scheme has SIPs in it, but because of the changes in taxes, that will see some challenges going forward across the industry.

items.statement: B30 AUM decline in Q4 was largely mark-to-market impact, in line with industry.
items.quote: When you look from a B30 perspective, it is largely, Q4 mark-to-market impact, which has happened. Also, I'm sure you'll appreciate that when you look at the overall assets for us, it is predominantly dominated by equity. So, to that extent, from a March perspective, we got impacted, but it is in line when you look from an industry perspective also, there is a similar impact on the B30 in the mark

items.statement: CIO for equities has been with the firm for over 10 years with 18+ years experience; strong in-house research team with full sector coverage.
items.quote: Our CIO for equities has been with us for over 10 years and has over 18 years of work experience. So very, very strong team in there.

items.statement: Launched digital campaign three days ago targeting investors who paused SIPs to reactivate them.
items.quote: We just three days ago launched that on our digital platform. A very nice campaign aimed at investors who for whatever reason have paused their SIPs.

items.statement: Priorities: consistent risk-adjusted returns, deepen retail and SIP-led franchise, expand product offerings, leverage technology, cost discipline, operational efficiency, long-term value creation.
items.quote: Our priorities remain clear. We will aim to deliver consistent risk-adjusted return and performance, deepen retail and SIP-led franchise, expand our product offerings, and leverage technology to enhance investor experience. At the same time, we remain focused on cost discipline, operational efficiency, and long-term value creation for all our stakeholders.

items.statement: Sector may see 3-4% growth in FY27 to ~USD 9.6-10.0 bn; seeds category remains a structural 5-10% CAGR story
items.quote: The sector may see 3-4% growth in FY2 7 to ~USD 9.6 –10.0 bn. Seeds category remains a structural 5–10% CAGR story.

items.statement: Expect high double-digit growth in seeds business in FY27 driven by combination of volume and price growth
items.quote: So I expect a combination of price and volume growth and expecting to deliver high double-digit growth again this year.

items.statement: Revenue growth probably double-digit in FY27 due to price increases of 5-10% as input costs up 15-20%
items.quote: So revenue growth probably will be maybe double digit. I don't know what it could be because our input cost has gone up by 15% to 20%. It is going to lead to price increase for sure. It will be 5%, 8%, 10%.

items.statement: Margins expected stable-to-soft in near term; crop protection standalone margins marginally down in Q4 due to inventory liquidation of Clasto and Benzilla
items.quote: Volumes might shrink due to less acreage, but margins are expected to remain stable -to-soft.

items.statement: B2C crop protection gross margin softened in Q4 due to liquidation of Clasto and Benzilla inventory; consolidated margin supported by CSM, SPH, exports and seeds
items.quote: On crop protection, stand-alone basis it was marginally down because, you know B2C business because of Benzilla and Clasto.

items.statement: Rabi season impacted by unseasonal rains damaging crops across 2.49 lakh hectares; summer sowing down 4.7% yoy as of end Mar'26
items.quote: As of end of Mar‘26, summer sowing is progressing at a slower pace, down 4.7% yoy, primarily driven by decline in Rice (-7.1%), Cereals (-3.8%), and Oilseeds (-6.1%).

items.statement: Farmers will plant crops even in worst monsoon years; acreage historically does not drop below 85-95%; down-trading to lower-cost seeds and crop protection products likely
items.quote: Even then area zone does not go below 85%, 95%, even 90%. So farmers will plant something. They might make different choices. They might also down-trade on the kind of seed they buy.

items.statement: Input costs increased 15-25% across raw materials; company has announced price increases and is passing on cost increases where possible
items.quote: So we have seen 15% to 25% is generally the range.

items.statement: Price increases announced for new supplies; carryover inventory from Jan-Mar at lower prices will exhaust before new prices establish in market
items.quote: All the new supplies, we have been supplying at a higher price.

items.statement: Cost increase reality for Kharif season locked in; even if war ends, 3-4 months to unwind; company calibrated on inventory buying only what can be sold
items.quote: for Kharif t his is the reality we have to live with it. We will have to live with it. We don't have a choice

items.statement: Exports revenue de-grew 33% to ₹77 cr in Q4FY26 from ₹114 cr due to volume and revenue decline in Metribuzin and Pendimethalin; CSM grew 59% to ₹66 cr
items.quote: Exports topline de-grew by 33% to ₹ 77 cr from ₹ 114 cr due to de -growth in volumes and revenue from Metribuzin and Pendimethalin. CSM Q 4FY26 revenue displayed promising growth by lodging 59% growth to ₹ 66 cr from ₹ 41 cr.

items.statement: Three new export molecules in pipeline for commercialization in next 2-3 years; advanced stages of process establishment and registration
items.quote: There are 2, 3 new molecules. So we have narrowed down the list which used to work. Now we ha ve got about 3 molecules, which should get introduced in the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Overall annual capacity utilization improved in FY26 vs FY25; record production levels achieved through manufacturing efficiency and operational excellence
items.quote: Overall Annual capacity utilization has also improved in FY26 in comparison to FY25.

items.statement: Launched ALSTOR (dual action granular insecticide), FIPLAM (broad-spectrum formulation), and obtained registration for Spiro (three-way patented herbicide for Paddy); Seeds launched 2 new products
items.quote: We have currently launched ALSTOR, a dual action granular insecticide and FIPLAM, a broad-spectrum formulation designed to manage both sucking and chewing pests. We have also obtained registration for Spiro, a three-way patented herbicide for Paddy.

items.statement: Broadening customer base and securing additional registrations with global players across technicals portfolio to drive share gains
items.quote: Across the technical’s portfolio, we are continuously broadening our customer base and securing additional registrations with global players to drive share gains.

items.statement: Inventory levels slightly elevated at quarter end vs same quarter last year; collection cycles remain smooth; healthy cash and liquid balance of ₹541 cr as of 31 Mar'26
items.quote: At quarter end our inventory levels remain slightly elevated in comparison to the same quarter of last year; collection cycles remain smooth. We have healthy cash and liquid balance of ₹ 541 cr as of 31st Mar ‘26.

items.statement: Built low-cost raw material inventory in anticipation of war from January; inventory days higher in FY26 due to this strategic build
items.quote: So, we did not want war to happen -- wait for war to happen. We did take some risk to build some inventory.

items.statement: India's FCO 2026 amendment will modernize biostimulant fertilizer standards by standardizing humic acid and seaweed formulations, improving product reliability and regulatory clarity
items.quote: India’s FCO 2026 amendment will significantly modernize bio stimulant fertilizer standards by standardizing humic acid & se aweed formulations, thereby improving product reliability & regulatory clarity.

items.statement: Global crop protection market ~USD 70-75 bn in 2026, projected 5.0-5.5% CAGR; China supply concentration remains key issue; US demand supportive, Brazil weak, China pricing pressure a concern
items.quote: The global crop protection market, estimated at approximately USD 70–75 billion in 2026, and is projected to grow at a CAGR of around 5.0 –5.5%.

items.statement: Acephate exports face structural challenge as raw material suppliers compete in American markets; prioritizing domestic market for acephate while balancing customer retention
items.quote: There is a structural challenge on acephate side because the same people those who supply us raw material, they compete with us in the American markets.

items.statement: Seeds category structural 5-10% CAGR story; sector may grow 3-4% in FY27 to ~USD 9.6-10.0 bn subject to Middle East crisis
items.quote: Seeds category remains a structural 5–10% CAGR story. This is subject to on-going middle eastern crisis.

items.statement: Near-term outlook contingent on Middle East conflict evolution; below-normal monsoon (92% LPA) and reduced acreage pose key risks; El Niño odds rising
items.quote: The near-term outlook remains contingent on the evolution of the Middle East conflict. While healthy reservoir levels of approximately 54% are supportive for the ongoing season, reduced acreage and forecasts of below-normal rainfall could pose key risks.

items.statement: War-led petrochemical disruption affecting solvents and energy costs; raw material prices increasing across the board; supply chain volatility persists
items.quote: War-led petrochemical disruption, supply chain, solvents, energy costs, everybody increasing the prices of raw material, all of that, when you factor in, it is very, very difficult to put a finger and say, look, what will happen?

items.statement: Launched Idea2Impact platform for open innovation ecosystem; Saksham GIS platform for scientific village identification; Sampark Plus for farmer-level demand signals; digital-led field AV Van campaigns and Anubandh Edge retailer platform
items.quote: In Q4, we launched Idea2Impact platform to establish an open innovation ecosystem to source, validate and commercialize agri-innovations. Rallis India Limited April 28th, 2026 We also launched Saksham (GIS platform) which enables scientific identification of high- potential villages for targeted market

items.statement: Aquafeed business at experimental stage; products outsourced similar to early Soil & Plant Health business; 1-2 more cycles before strategic investment decision
items.quote: I would like to see one more year, this year, to say where I am able to take it and then start thinking of this strategy. But yes, it is an important segment.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 expected to be impacted by ongoing MENA disruptions and API suspension; no specific numbers given
items.quote: Factors contributing to Q4 muted performance persist and we expect its impact on Q1 results of the current year also.

items.statement: Water pipe demand remains at macro level but execution deferred; state-funded orders executing now, Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 expected post-monsoon
items.quote: Macro level demand has not died down. Macro level demand remains the same. It is only deferment. Hopefully, this year, the business should pick up and the industry should respond very quickly.

items.statement: Seamless pipe domestic demand ~1.5 mt with opportunities from ONGC deepwater projects
items.quote: Demand in seamless segment domestically, it is more or less 1.5 million approximately and there are multiple players. So as the government or the PSUs have announced certain projects in deepwater exploration, we can see some opportunities -- big opportunities to come when these projects are executed.

items.statement: Margins uncertain; not confirmed as bottomed out due to unpredictable crude, freight, capacity utilisation and API suspension
items.quote: So if you say that this has bottomed out, maybe, may not be.

items.statement: Stainless steel (seamless and welded) margins challenged; improvement targeted H2 FY27 via value-added approvals
items.quote: So impact of that will come, I think in this year, the second half. So -- but otherwise, I must say that complete business of stainless steel will face the margin challenge.

items.statement: Seamless segment margins expected to improve on robust demand
items.quote: So, there will be improvement -- yes, there will be improvement in margins in seamless segment because we envisage that demand should remain robust and that will actually result into the little bit better margins.

items.statement: Abu Dhabi subsidiary order book ~$180m (171k tons) giving ~9 months visibility
items.quote: As of March 31, 2026, the subsidiary holds an order book of approximately $180 million, which is close to 171,000 metric tons, giving a visibility of approximately 9 months of operations.

items.statement: DI pipe overcapacity persists; other segments (LSAW, HSAW, seamless) well placed; no new DI capacity added
items.quote: In ductile iron pipes, there may be some oversupply in terms of capacities. But apart from this, other segments are well placed like longitudinal, helical as well as seamless. So, if in future demand is there, the capacities are available to cater the demand.

items.statement: Abu Dhabi seamless plant and Saudi LSAW/HSAW JV on fast-track; land secured, equipment LCs opened
items.quote: Ordering for equipment with advanced payments and opening of LCs has started. Project company has signed long-term lease agreement with AD ports for land parcel. In Saudi Arabia, company established a joint venture company with its investments of 51% and balance 49% is by Buhur Group in KSA. This JV will set up a LSAW and HSAW facility.

items.statement: Steel booked only after firm pipe order; no inventory speculation; diesel/freight cost escalation risk on delivered contracts
items.quote: We don't accumulate or hold steel in anticipation of getting the order. So it is basically like it's a very narrow -- within a very narrow time line, we book the steel the moment we get the order for the pipe. So eventually, the volatility in the raw material prices is to the account of the manufacturer.

items.statement: DI pipe escalation clauses (pig iron index) cover ~30-33% pass-through domestically; no guarantee on export contracts
items.quote: as you mentioned that 30%, 33% or the strategy was like that in ductile iron pipe to pass on the cost or to protect the company from the volatility in raw material prices, especially for ductile, it was like that we do have the stocks with us als o, coal stocks. We are getting the coal shipped every quarter. So that is something which is already in -built in the pricing mechanism

items.statement: API monogram suspended after audit; NCs closed; re-audit scheduled May 2026; approval timeline speculative
items.quote: Auditors appointed by API authorities are scheduled to revisit our factory in Nashik in May 2026 for verification. Following this, the final approval to use the API monogram on seamless pipe is expected in due course. Given this, providing a specific time line for approval at this stage would be very speculative.

items.statement: MENA conflict since 28 Feb 2026 halted all shipments from India and Abu Dhabi; vessels unavailable; Abu Dhabi sales limited to trucking range
items.quote: Consequently, all shipments from India and Abu Dhabi facilities in Middle East are suspended until further notice and further -- until safety conditions allow for safe passage. Abu Dhabi plant sales are restricted to customers in the countries, which are within the trucking range.

items.statement: INR48 cr forex loss in Q4 from USD revaluation (INR88.88 to INR94.84)
items.quote: Company also reported a INR48 crores foreign exchange cost during this quarter following the revaluation of U.S. dollar-denominated exposures. This was driven by the rupee's sharp decline over the quarter. It fell from INR88.88 per dollar to INR94.84 per dollar.

items.statement: Standalone net debt INR2,453 cr (LT INR529 cr); Consol net debt INR2,528 cr (LT INR692 cr) at 31 Mar 2026; balance sheet can absorb higher debt for MENA projects
items.quote: As on 31st March 2026, company stand -alone net debt reduced to INR2,453 crores as compared to INR3,154 crores on the previous year. And this includes long-term debt of INR529 crores only. Net institutional debt on a consol basis has reduced to INR2,528 crores as compared to INR3,346 crores, which was on 31st December '25. Long-term debt on 31st March was INR692 crores only.

items.statement: Comfortable with net debt/EBITDA ~2-2.5x including working capital if EBITDA returns to INR3,500 cr levels
items.quote: If we go back to that , similar levels in some time, then we would still be in the range of, let's say, 2, 2.5 debt to EBITDA, all including working capital, everything.

items.statement: Unpredictable environment: MENA conflict, shipping/insurance, API suspension, Jal Jeevan execution, diesel/freight inflation, crude volatility
items.quote: We are projecting the business for future is very unpredictable. The management is taking all possible steps to safeguard its interest and see how best we can ramp up the operations and business in domestic market, pending the export market opens up.

items.statement: Jindal Hunting JV revenue INR149 cr, PAT INR43.2 cr in FY26 vs INR177 cr/INR51.5 cr FY25
items.quote: In Jindal Hunting joint ventures, joint venture where Jindal has 51% and Hunting has 49%, we generated a revenue of approximately INR149 crores with INR43.2 crores of PAT. This is a bit lower as compared to previous year where the top line was INR177 crores and INR51.5 crores was the PAT in FY '25

items.statement: Shifting DI pipe capacity to alternative sizes/export/domestic to mitigate underutilisation
