items.quote: CNG volumes grew by 17% year -on-year. During the fourth quarter, starting from January '26 to March '26 and 18% for the financial year '25 -'26, while PNG volumes increased by 5% during the fourth quarter from Jan to March '26 and 6% for the financial year 2025 -'26

items.statement: Added nearly 50,000 new domestic PNG connections in Q4 FY26, highest ever; 137,000 for FY26, total 1.1 million households
items.quote: Customer addition remained strong with nearly 50,000 new domestic PNG connections added in this quarter, which is our highest addition ever. For the entire financial year '25-'26, we added about 137,000 new customers, taking our total household tally to 1.1 million.

items.statement: Added 214 industrial and commercial customers in Q4 FY26, total 9,965 I&C customers
items.quote: In the Industrial and Commercial segment, we added 214 customers during the fourth quarter, starting from January '26 to March '26, bringing the total to 9,965 customers across a diverse range of industries and commercial establishments.

items.statement: EV charging subsidiary ATEL operates 5,100 charge points across 26 states, 226 cities, 54 MW capacity; on track for 10,000 points near term
items.quote: In our e -mobility business, our network continues to scale rapidly. ATEL, our subsidiary company now operates 5,100 EV charge points across 26 states and union territories covering 226 cities, supported by around 54 megawatts of installed capacity.

items.statement: Consolidated CGD network with JV IOAGPL: 1,169 CNG stations, 13.1 lakh PNG homes, 11,529 I&C consumers, 28,000 inch-km steel pipeline, 10,500 km MDPE pipeline across 53 GAs
items.quote: Along with our 50 -50 JV company, IndianOil -Adani Gas Private Limited, IOAGPL, our consolidated nationwide CGD network today stands at 1,169 CNG stations. 13.1 lakh PNG homes, 11,529 commercial and industrial consumers, 28,000 -inch kilometers of steel pipeline and 10,500 kilometers of medium-density polyethylene pipeline, MDPE pipe.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 revenue up 16% to INR 1,696 cr; FY26 revenue up 18% to INR 6,415 cr. Q4 EBITDA up 13% to INR 310 cr; FY26 EBITDA up 5% to INR 1,225 cr
items.value: Revenue INR 1,696 cr, EBITDA INR 310 cr
items.quote: Total revenue for the fourth quarter starting Jan to March '26 rose by 16% to INR1,696 crores, while revenue for fiscal year 2025 -'26 increased by 18% to INR6,415 crores, driven by overall volume growth. Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization, which is we call it EBITDA for the fourth quarter starting Jan to March '26 increased by 13% to INR310 crores, while EBITDA for the f

items.statement: Q4 FY26 PBT up 8% to INR 214 cr; FY26 PBT down 1% to INR 863 cr. Q4 PAT up 4% to INR 156 cr; FY26 PAT INR 637 cr
items.value: PBT INR 214 cr, PAT INR 156 cr
items.quote: Profit before tax, PAT, the fourth quarter starting from January '26 to March '26, increased by 8% to INR214 crores. This is PBT, profit before tax, while PBT for the financial year '25 -'26 was marginally lower by 1% to INR863 crores. Profit after tax earlier was PBT and now it's a PAT for the fourth quarter increased by 4% to INR156 crores, while PAT for financial year '25-'26 was INR637 crores.

items.statement: Expect same revenue growth in FY27 as FY26 (18%); EBITDA target around INR 1,500 cr for FY27
items.quote: We are expecting the same revenue growth, which we are currently having in '25-'26 in the next financial year. And EBITDA growth will in line of growth in volume. So we are expecting around -- we can say INR 1,500 crores of EBITDA.

items.statement: Gas pool price for March 2026 was $12.42 per MMBtu; pool includes APM, non-APM, HPHT, Vedanta, RLNG contracts; imported LNG added in April
items.quote: For the month of March, the gas pool price was $12.42 per MMBtu.

items.statement: Government supplied full 6-month average gas to priority sectors; additional volumes allocated beyond 6-month average to meet incremental CNG/PNG demand
items.quote: Government made an arrangement to supply these additional volumes, which were higher than the 6-month average. So that was available and allocated later.

items.statement: Price increases calibrated; not fully passed through to consumers to protect volume growth; focus on operational excellence and digitalization for cost savings
items.quote: Price has been calibrated. We have not been able to pass through in the interest of a consumer while we maintained our reasonable profitability, which is in front of you all through our announcement of results.

items.statement: PNG constitutes ~50% of volumes; CNG + domestic PNG ~78%; industrial ~20%, commercial ~2.5%
items.quote: plus domestic is around 78% and the balance is industrial plus commercial, 22%. Suresh P. Manglani: And the gas... Ravindra Desai: And if you want further breakup, the industrial volume would be around 20% and the rest is commercial around 2.5

items.statement: CNG sourcing: 85% from APM, HPHT, WG and term contracts; ~15% spot purchases via diversified Brent-linked and asset-linked contracts
items.quote: For CNG (T) so 85% of our volumes are met from the APM allocation plus HPHT and WG volumes and the different contracts for care. So balance around 16%, we are buying from the market on a spot basis. So we have a different portfolio of various indices, including the Brent-linked contracts plus asset-linked contracts.

items.statement: Government prioritized PNG/CNG supply, appointed GAIL as nodal agency, created gas pool mechanism with weighted average pricing during West Asia crisis
items.quote: Government of India also took several policy initiatives to bring uniformity in grants of the permissions within time, which we are very happy to state that have been reciprocated very well by several state governments.

items.statement: Daily execution: 400+ home connections, 2 new business connections, 1 CNG station per week, 3 km pipeline laying per day
items.quote: Every day, we are connecting 400 -plus home connections. Every day, we are connecting 2 new businesses. Every week, we are building 1 CNG station. Every day, we are laying 3-kilometer pipeline in the country.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions in West Asia disrupted global energy markets, causing higher gas prices, supply chain challenges, currency volatility
items.quote: Since late February, geopolitical tensions in West Asia have disrupted global energy markets, resulting in higher natural gas prices, supply chain chal lenges and compounded currency volatility.

items.statement: ESG: CareEdge rating 83/100, NSE Sustainability score improved to 73 from 67; HSE awards for process safety and industrial hygiene
items.quote: I'm pleased to share that ATGL's ESG performance continues to strengthen along with its operational, physical and financial performance with a CareEdge -ESG rating of 83 out of 100, placing us among the top performers in the peer group, alongside an improvement in our NSE Sustainability score to 73 from 67.

items.statement: Management expects similar capex spend in FY27 as in FY26
items.quote: When I look at the coming year, we see a similar number of capex, similar number in terms of the capex spend for FY '27 as well.

items.statement: Merger with Devyani International expected to be completed by end of FY27
items.quote: I would say it looks like by the end of this financial year, we should be in a position to consume the merger. That's the likely scenario by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: KFC SSSG was 4% in Q4 FY26, 6% excluding Navratri shift, highest in 14 quarters
items.quote: KFC SSSG grew at 4%. 6% without the impact of Navratri last year, 2 days were in March and 7 days were in April. This year entire Navratri was in March. So underlying growth is 6%. And the 6% is highest in 14 quarters.

items.statement: April KFC SSSG trending similar to Q4 underlying 6% growth
items.quote: For the quarter, we delivered 4%, ex Navratri, 6%. So that kind of momentum we are seeing in April as well from an SSSG point of view.

items.statement: Sri Lanka delivered 11% SSSG in Q4 FY26, sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth
items.quote: From SSSG perspective, 11% for the quarter, which was from a revenue perspective, 15% in LKR and 16% in INR terms.

items.statement: Sri Lanka April SSSG positive despite high base
items.quote: But yet, we continue to deliver positive SSSG in April as well.

items.statement: KFC restaurant EBITDA margin improved 110 bps to 16.8% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: This, along with the operating leverage, which we generated out of positive SSSG, meant that we improved our restaurant EBITDA by 110 basis points, which came in at 16.8%.

items.statement: Consolidated restaurant EBITDA margin up 100 bps to 13% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our consolidated restaurant EBITDA grew 21% year-on-year and margin was 13%, up 100 basis points.

items.statement: KFC gross margin stable despite value offer rollout due to vendor support; potential 50-70 bps gross margin impact if vendor support ends
items.quote: As a result, we've been able to hold on to the gross margin. That's the reason. Having said that, if I look into the future and if the vendor partner support goes away, we expect the gross margin impact of anywhere or a gross margin investment of anywhere between 50 to 70 basis points.

items.statement: Additional 75-100 bps marketing spend behind KFC brand in Q4 FY26
items.quote: So, while I'm not giving the exact number, anywhere between 75 basis points to a 100 -bps additional marketing spend we have put behind the brand.

items.statement: Pizza Hut India restaurant EBITDA declined 6% in Q4 FY26 due to operating deleverage
items.quote: However, restaurant EBITDA decline came in at 6% on account of operating deleverage.

items.statement: Sri Lanka restaurant EBITDA margin 14.6%, down 20 bps due to minimum wage increases
items.quote: We had a margin which came at 14.6%, down by 20 basis points, and the entire benefit of the operating leverage because of the SSSG did not flow through the bottom line on account of high minimum wages being experienced in a particular country, and there were 2 increases last year.

items.statement: LPG price increase of 25-40% could impact EBITDA by 30-50 bps
items.quote: The bigger challenge right now is the LPG price where the impact could be anywhere between 25% to 40% increase in terms of the cost, which could impact the EBITDA by 30 to 50 basis point.

items.statement: Added 19 KFC, 2 Pizza Hut India, 3 Pizza Hut Sri Lanka stores in Q4 FY26; total 1,052 restaurants
items.quote: In the quarter, we added 19 KFC restaurants, two Pizza Huts in India and three Pizza Huts in Sri Lanka. Our total restaurant count was 1,052 as of 31st March '26.

items.statement: Opened 73 KFC, 7 Pizza Hut India, 9 Pizza Hut Sri Lanka stores in FY26
items.quote: We opened 73 KFC restaurants during the year, 575 total restaurants. Pizza Hut revenue for the year declined by 7%, revenue of INR507 crores with a restaurant EBITDA of minus 3.3%, 570 basis points below last year. We opened 7 restaurants during the year, a total of 341 restaurants. Sri Lanka business grew 16% in LKR terms, with restaurant EBITDA of 14.9%, down 50 basis points. We opened 9 restaur

items.statement: KFC per store capex INR 2.1-2.2 crores; Pizza Hut per store capex INR 1.35-1.4 crores (excl. fees)
items.quote: KFC number looks like anywhere between INR 2.1 crores to INR 2.2 crores per store. So that's pure capex without any initial fee or renewal fee as a part of it. Pizza Hut, we have always called out that per store capex is like INR1.35 crores to INR1.4 crores per store.

items.statement: Sri Lanka store expansion to accelerate to high single-digit or low double-digit annually for next 2-3 years
items.quote: I think from where we are in terms of the margin, the SSSG, the overall business condition, we should be able to accelerate store expansion as well as in Sri Lanka, which would be anywhere between, let's say, a high single digit or low early double digits as well. So that's possible for the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: KFC price hikes of 1.5-2% implemented; Pizza Hut ~2% in April; no further hikes planned unless raw material prices spike
items.quote: So currently for KFC, the price hike has happened in the range of 1-odd percent. And in March, also a small amount of price hike happened. If I add up both the price hikes, it's in the range of 1.5% to 2% price hike for KFC. Similar price hike has been tak ing place for Pizza Hut or has taken place for Pizza Hut as well in the month of April, around about 2%. We don't see any further price hike in

items.statement: KFC dine-in/takeaway mix stable at 57% in Q4 FY26, supported by value campaigns exclusive to those channels
items.quote: The dine-in and takeaway mix for the quarter remained stable at 57% same as las t year. This was on account of improved performance we have seen in those channels, backed by the value campaigns, which Sanjay spoke about, which are exclusively available in dine-in and takeaway channels only

items.statement: KFC digital kiosks implemented in 73% of restaurants, driving higher APC
items.quote: Our digital kiosks now have been implemented in 73% of restaurants. And clearly, there's an APC upside that we get from the kiosks compared to what we would get at the counter.

items.statement: KFC strategy targets aware non-users via INR 99 meal + behavior-changing advertising; BOGO for developed markets
items.quote: I think what is working here is -- I don't know whether you've seen the advertising that we have run along with the INR99 product, that advertising has really addressed directly at aware non-users and it encourages them to come to KFC and see the kind of range because that is the consumer that's a simple consumer insight.

items.statement: Own delivery app SSSG growth continuously exceeding aggregator partners by significant margin for 1.5-2 years
items.quote: Our own delivery channel, our own app performance has continuously exceeded the delivery partners in terms of the SSSG and the growth. And that's by quite a bit of margin in terms of the performance of our own delivery app vis-a-vis aggregators.

items.statement: Exceptional items include INR 6.2 crores Labour Code impact and INR 6.6 crores merger-related ESOP modification costs
items.quote: These exceptional items include the impact of INR6.2 crores on account of Labour Code changes and INR 6.6 crores towards merger -related costs, really the ESOP modification for employee-retention.

items.statement: LPG availability and price volatility in India and Sri Lanka remains evolving risk; Pizza Hut closures <3% in April
items.quote: The April remains the same. So, we haven't seen any KFC closure in April as well. And in fact, in case of Pizza HUT, the closures, which was less than 5% in March, it has come down and now it's less than 3% in case of Pizza Hut, and KFC continues to be zero closer.

name: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Ltd

items.statement: Targets sustainable high-teen growth and mid-teen to high-teen ROE
items.quote: we are more focused on what is our Company's strategy and objectives, which is to have a sustainable high-teen growth, and a sustainable, hopefully mid-teen to high-teen ROEs.

items.statement: Retail Health industry grew 30.2% YoY in H2 FY26 vs 11.2% for non-life
items.quote: At industry level, Retail Health insurance premiums have grown by 30.2% YoY in H2 FY26, significantly outpacing the broader non-life industry growth which came at 11.2% YoY during the same period.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 IND AS underwriting profit Rs 186 crore, up 200% YoY; combined ratio improved 2.7% to 95.7%
items.quote: Our IND AS underwriting profit for the quarter was Rs. 186 crore, an increase of 200% YoY over Rs. 62 crore in Q4 FY25. This was driven by an improvement in combined ratio by 2.7%, which was 98.4% in Q4 FY25 and came to 95.7% in Q4 FY26.

items.statement: FY26 underwriting profit turned positive at Rs 206 crore; combined ratio improved 2.3% to 98.8%
items.quote: As against the full year loss of Rs. 165 crore during FY25, underwriting profit turned positive at Rs. 206 crore for FY26, a positive delta of Rs. 371 crore. This was driven by improvement in combined ratio by 2.3% from 101.1% in FY25 to 98.8% in FY26.

items.statement: Retail loss ratio improved 3% YoY to 64.8% in Q4 FY26; progressive quarterly improvement of 0.8%, 1%, 3% in Q2, Q3, Q4
items.quote: The retail loss ratio improved 3% YoY to 64.8% in this particular quarter for FY26. Our retail loss ratios have improved by 0.8%, 1% and 3% YoY during Q2, Q3 and Q4 of FY26 respectively, underscoring progressive improvement every quarter.

items.statement: Normalized PAT at 8% investment yield grew 45% YoY to Rs 1,222 crore; ROE expanded to 13.1%
items.quote: Under this normalized framework, our profit after tax increased 45% YoY in FY26 to Rs. 1,222 crore and ROE expanded from 10.1% in FY25 to 13.1% in FY26.

items.statement: Fresh retail growth 38% YoY in Q4 FY26 on N basis; policies up 11% YoY
items.quote: Fresh retail growth on N basis for the quarter was 38% YoY. Fresh growth was driven by both value and volume as the number of Retail Health policies expanded by 11% YoY.

items.statement: FY26 fresh retail growth 37% YoY on N basis; GWP crossed Rs 20,000 crore at Rs 20,369 crore
items.quote: Overall, GWP increased 16% YoY on N basis to Rs. 20,369 crore. This is a very important milestone for us to cross Rs. 20,000 crore in GWP as we complete 20 years of establishment of Star Health in this calendar year.

items.statement: Proprietary channels (agency + digital D2C) contribute over 90% of retail business
items.quote: Our proprietary distribution channels, which are the agency channel and the digital D2C, now contribute over 90% of the retail business and positions us to deepen the insurance penetration beyond the urban areas with emphasis on new-to-insurance customers.

items.statement: Annual price increases across all products; repricing ~80% of book from Q4 FY26 to Q1 FY27
items.quote: We are expecting to reprice almost 80% of the book between what we started from Q4 going up to Q1 this year. And that will show up in the earnings going forward.

items.statement: Pricing based on product loss ratios, not GST; GST benefits fully passed to consumers
items.quote: The pricing strategies of the company is base d on the performance of the product in terms of the loss ratios. On that basis only we are taking the price increases. I believe that it should be fair to all the stakeholders. It is based on fully defined actuarial principles

items.statement: Retail claim settlement ratio up 3% to 92%; renewal ratio up 2% to 99%; NPS up 8 points to 62
items.quote: The retail claim settlement ratio increased by 3% to 92% for the full year. Our renewal ratio on full-year basis increased by 2% to 99%. The company-level NPS improved by 8 points to 62 at March 31, 2026.

items.statement: Renewal retention improved 300 bps on GWP and 100 bps on NOP; customers opting higher sum insured and riders
items.quote: If you look at our renewal retention numbers for the current financial year, there is a 300-bps improvement in terms of GWP. That clearly reflects that the customers are now opting for higher sum insured and they are also willing to opt for riders, which are beneficial for them.

items.statement: Target 1 million agents in next two years; adding 1 lakh agents annually; agent productivity up 37% on fresh, 18% overall
items.quote: We are confident of getting to 1 million in the next two years. We maintain this, that we will be adding 1 lakh agents every year for the next many years. If you look at our agent productivity, even for this year it has improved by about 37% on fresh, and overall, 18% on total business.

items.statement: Market share sustained at 31.3% in Retail Health for FY26
items.quote: Notwithstanding all the underwriting discipline above, we have ma intained a category leadership in Retail Health segment with market share at 31.3% in FY26

items.statement: Volume retention 86-87%, best in industry; persistency best on both volume and value
items.quote: Star Health with the kind of scale that we operate, we have the best persistency in the industry, both on volume as well as on value. So, I think on volume basis, we have seen almost close to 86-87% retention in terms of volume.

items.statement: IND AS implementation mandated from April 1, 2026; Star Health ready with audited IND AS financials for multiple quarters
items.quote: We welcome the IRDAI's formal mandate on implementation of IND AS accounting standards from April 1, 2026. At Star Health, we have always believed it to be the most relevant framework and have aligned all our business and investment decisions towards these principles. Our IND AS financials have been reviewed by our joint statutory auditors for multiple quarters now, and we enter the IND AS regime

items.statement: Awaiting IRDAI guidance on EoM; Star Health operating within current guidelines
items.quote: broadly we await IRDAI's guidance on EoM. There has been some data that the regulator has asked which all of us have supplied. But you will appreciate that we have been a very disciplined company in terms of EoM. We are probably the only company in this space operating within the current guidelines.

items.statement: Marked-to-market equity loss Rs 558 crore in Q4 FY26; Rs 127 crore for full FY26
items.quote: The geopolitical tension-induced correction in the equity markets led to a Rs. 558 crore marked-to-market loss during the quarter. As a result, we reported a loss of Rs. 55 crore for Q4 FY26 compared to a profit of Rs. 271 crore during Q4 FY25.

items.statement: Loss ratio improvement driven by frequency reduction (partly cyclical, partly structural via Telemedicine/Home Healthcare)
items.quote: the overall impact, specifically in Quarter 4, has been the improvement in frequency that we have seen over the last year. So that cut across the entire book, it doesn't play out only for one thing. And all of this has been enabled because of the continuous efforts we have been taking on the Telemedicine and Home Healthcare front, along with all other prevention measures.

items.statement: Telemedicine calls >40,000; Home Healthcare calls >90,000 in FY26; Q4 saw 9x jump in consumption
items.quote: We had more than 90,000 calls for the year, for specifically the calls that came for Home Healthcare. But eventually the numbers that utilized Home Healthcare were much lower. But the Telemedicine calls were more than 90,000. Pure Telemedicine calls were in excess of another 40,000.

items.statement: Digital acquisition: 95% fresh premiums collected digitally; app 14M+ downloads, 1.5M+ MAU
items.quote: Acquisition and onboarding are now predominantly digitalized with 95% of all fresh premiums collected digitally. Our mobile application, the customer app, has over 14 million downloads, playing a pivotal role in driving customer engagement, acting as the primary interface across the policy lifecycle. Monthly active users of the app have scaled past the 1.5 million mark with desirable levels of sel

items.statement: Group Health recalibrated: SME now 78% of Group business vs 58% in FY25; focusing on profitable segments
items.quote: We have been focusing on our SME segment which for the current financial year has contributed to 78% of our overall business, which was 58% in FY25. So, we continue to maintain this strategy, and we are absolutely clear that we will go behind businesses which are profitable in nature and SME is one of those businesses.

items.statement: Medi Assist platform transition nearly complete; final products shifting this quarter; seeing efficiency and effectiveness gains
items.quote: So, on the platform shift on the claims processing, that is now nearly complete. We are just entering the final phase of our last set of products that will be shifted on to that platform. By this quarter end, I think we should be fully through. So, we are clearly seeing efficiencies coming across for which we had thought for the platform and that's playing out.

items.statement: Management guides steady-state consolidated EBITDA per ton at INR 3,500-3,600
items.quote: So steady-state range, you can build around INR 3,600 a ton or INR3,500 for a safer side, you take it, I think we should be able to deliver within that range.

items.statement: Food business to remain EBITDA neutral till FY27, then target INR 1,500-2,000 per ton EBITDA from FY28
items.quote: we have always been saying that food will remain an EBITDA neutral till FY '27. And after that, we will try and build INR1,500 per ton to INR2,000 a ton kind of EBITDA in the food from FY '28.

items.statement: Food volume growth target for FY27 is double-digit, mid-teens
items.quote: we would certainly want in FY '27 food volumes to grow in double digit, at least in mid-teens kind of number, which we are looking at.

items.statement: Alternate channel volume share target 30-35% in coming years from 15% currently
items.quote: I'm sure in the years to come, we will have close to 30%, 35% of our volumes coming in from the alternate channel, which is today at 15%.

items.statement: April demand sluggish due to inventory accumulation in March; recovery expected in May-June
items.quote: when we got into April, we did see some of the sluggishness in the demand because a lot of people who had accumulated inventories in the month of March are now consuming it, and therefore, we see not a very encouraging demand scenario as far as April is concerned, but I'm very sure that in the month of May and June, it will recover, and we will have a fairly good quarter Q1 as well.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 consolidated gross margin INR 12,000+ per ton, EBITDA INR 3,400 per ton, up 19% and 23% YoY
items.quote: We have been able to maintain the gross margins per ton plus of INR12,000 and EBITDA closer to INR3,400 a ton for the quarter, which is again a growth of 19% and 23% year-on-year for both the metrics.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated gross margin INR 11,500+ per ton, EBITDA INR 3,500 per ton
items.quote: for the full year, the per ton metrics on a gross profit per ton as well as EBITDA per ton , we have been able to deliver plus of INR11,500 ton for gross profit and EBITDA closer to INR3,500 a ton.

items.statement: Standalone Q4 FY26 gross margin INR 12,000+ per ton, EBITDA INR 3,500+ per ton
items.quote: On stand-alone, again, the per metric ton metrics, the unit metrics rather, I would say, continue to be healthy. Gross profit of plus of INR12,000 and EBITDA plus of INR3,500 for the quarter

items.statement: Standalone FY26 gross margin INR 11,200 per ton, EBITDA INR 3,600 per ton
items.quote: whereas for the full year, we are able to deliver a gross profit of INR 11,200 of gross profit and INR3,600 on the EBITDA.

items.statement: Food segment Q4 FY26 profit INR 35 crore; FY26 segment result INR 200+ crore
items.quote: The segment recorded also -- segment also recorded a profitability of close to INR 35 crores in Q4. And for the full year, we had a segment result of plus of INR 200 crores.

items.statement: Food margins may be prioritized below volume growth in FY27; could be slightly lower than current ~3%
items.quote: Harsh Shah: In that case, whatever that 3%-odd margins, which we have done would be slightly lower? Shrikant Kanhere: Maybe, yes.

items.statement: Edible oil complex prices rose ~10% in March; passed on to consumers by mid/end March
items.quote: the edible oil complex went up in the month of March, close to 10%. And I think that 10% of increased prices and every player has passed it on to the consumer somewhere in mid of March or end of March.

items.statement: Packing material cost up 10-15% but only 2-3% of overall cost; impact ~25-50 bps; price corrections to be taken by end April
items.quote: packing material for us is close to, I would say, 2%, 2.5%, 3% of our overall cost, not more than that. And if it has gone up by 10%, 15%, the overall impact per se would not be more than a quarter basis or 50 basis points. But as we approach to the en d of April, I think we will take the corrections

items.statement: When edible oil prices fall, company times price reductions to retain margins before passing to consumers
items.quote: when the prices goes down, we try and time our -- time it such that we are able to get as far as margins before passing it on to the customer.

items.statement: Direct reach 970,000 outlets; rural reach 63,000 towns with 55,000 outlets serviced every 3 months; total direct+indirect reach 2.6 million outlets per Nielsen
items.quote: Now we reach more than 900,000 outlets directly, 970,000 rather, I would say. On rural reach, we are there, 63,000 towns listed. Of those 63,000, close to 55,000 outlets get built every 3 months. And this is the area where we would continue to focus and gr ow. Overall, direct plus indirect reach as per the Nielsen is now 2.6 million

items.statement: HoReCa channel grew 64% YoY in Q4; branded exports grew 48% YoY
items.quote: HoReCa as a channel on which we are putting focus for the last couple of years grew by 64% year -on-year. And the branded exports, which is again also a focus area for the company, grew by 48% year-on-year when we talk about the Q4 numbers.

items.statement: Edible oil market share improved 60 bps in Q4; e-com/Q-com market share remains above 30%
items.quote: On market share, we have been able to see consolidation in market share of edible oil for the quarter where it improved by 60 basis points. In e-com and Q-com also, our market share of edible oil continue to remain above 30% level.

items.statement: Wheat flour market share flat at 5.3-5.4%; basmati rice market share improved 330 bps to ~9%
items.quote: our wheat flour market share more or less remained flattish at 5.3%, 5.4% kind of number, which we had earlier also. But one significant improvement, which we saw in the basmati rice where our market share improved by 330 basis points, and now we are closer to 9% kind of market

items.statement: New Oleo chemical installation at Krishnapatnam expected by early Q1 / Q4 FY27 to add volume
items.quote: our new installation coming up at Krishnapatnam by end of early Q1 of -- Q4 of '27 should be able to add more volume to this segment.

items.statement: Specialty chemicals now 7-8% of Oleo portfolio; diversification ongoing
items.quote: gradually, we are diversifying into the specialty chemical, which now contributes close to 7% to 8% of the portfolio.

items.statement: GD Foods (acquired last year): Q4 volume +24%, FY volume +15%; Q4 revenue +21%, FY revenue +12%; material margin 55%/54%
items.quote: GD Foods, which was acquired last year, continued to grow. In Q4, the volume grew by 24%, but -- and full year volume grew by 15%, revenue growth of 21% for the quarter and 12% for the full year. We continue to maintain the material margin at level of 55% and 54% for the quarter and full year, respectively.

items.statement: Iran conflict caused vessel availability issues, crude-linked commodity cost spikes (chemical, coal, packing), rupee depreciation; cost impact to hit in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Conflict also resulted into supply chain availability of the vessels because of the inventories tightness was observed throughout the industry. All the crude -linked commodities went up and as a result, chemical, coal, packing material, all costs shot up i n the month of March

items.statement: No plans to enter palm oil plantation business; promoter Wilmar has plantations in Indonesia/Malaysia
items.quote: As we speak today, we don't have any plan because our promoter, Wilmar itself, they are into a big plantation in palm in Indonesia and Malaysia. But as far as AWL is concerned, as we speak today, we don't have any plans to get into this.

items.statement: Food volume target >1.5 MMT (currently 1.2 MMT) to start margin consolidation; expects 1.5-1.6 MMT in FY27
items.quote: I think food anywhere closer to -- or anywhere more than 1.5 million tons of volumes, I think we should be able to start consolidating the margins. This year, we closed at 1.2 million ton s. I am hopeful that next year, we will go beyond 1.5 million ton s, 1.6 million tons as far as th e food is concerned

items.statement: Edible oil demand sensitivity: every INR 10 price increase reduces demand by 1%; inventory and supply chain managed based on price trends and seasonality
items.quote: at every INR 10, we see demand slowing down by 1% and vice versa. As prices comes off, the demand increases. Basis the international price analysis, we also revise our inventory and supply chain and also depending upon the season and the festivals.

items.statement: Quarterly AUM growth guidance unchanged at 5-7%
items.quote: Our overall guidance remains unchanged at 5% to 7% on a quarterly basis.

items.statement: Gold loan share may gradually move closer to 25% of AUM
items.quote: Given the firm outlook on gold prices and addition in branches, this share of gold may gradually move closer to 25%.

items.statement: Co-origination expected to remain at 18-19% of AUM
items.quote: Co-origination disbursements account for 16% of total disbursements and 18% to 19% of AUM for last quarter, and we are expected to remain at similar levels all through FY27.

items.statement: Portfolio mix between MSME and gold expected to remain stable at 75-25%
items.quote: Overall, the portfolio mix between MSME and gold is expected to remain stable between 75% and 25%.

items.statement: Spreads expected to hold at current 9% level
items.quote: In terms of our pricing, spreads for the last quarters have been at 9%. We are expected to hold the spreads at the current level.

items.statement: Opex expected to decline by 20-25 bps through the year
items.quote: Cost, while we will continue to invest in distribution, our opex is expected to decline by 20 to 25 basis points through the year.

items.statement: Credit cost expected to remain range-bound at 1.38% with marginal 5 bps benefit
items.quote: We will continue to be cautiously optimistic and while we have a credit cost at 1.38%, we are expected to remain range-bound all through the year with some marginal benefits of 5 basis points here or there.

items.statement: Added 46 branches in FY26, total network 251; expect to stabilize at 275 branches
items.quote: We added 46 branches in FY26, taking our total network to 251 branches. We expect to stabilize at 275 branches during the year, allowing us to consolidate and evaluate the performance of these investments before scaling further.

items.statement: AUM at INR 11,270 crores, up 29% YoY and 8% QoQ
items.quote: In terms of business, our AUM for the March '26 is INR 11,270 crores with a growth of 29% on a Y-o-Y basis and 8% on a Q-o-Q basis.

items.statement: MSME AUM at INR 8,873 crores (79% of AUM), up 22% YoY and 4% QoQ
items.quote: Our MSME AUM is at INR 8,873 crores, which is 79% of AUM, as Mahesh was talking about, with a growth of 22% on a Y-o-Y basis and 4% on a Q-o-Q basis.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM at INR 2,374 crores (21% of AUM), up 63% YoY and 22% QoQ
items.quote: loan against gold AUM is now INR 2,374 crores, which is 21% of AUM, as Mahesh mentioned, with a growth of 63% on a Y-o-Y basis and 22% on a Q-o-Q basis

items.statement: Opex at 3.93%, down 69 bps YoY, flat QoQ
items.quote: In terms of cost, our opex for the quarter is 3.93%, which is a 69-basis points reduction on a Y-o-Y basis and almost same as on a Q-o-Q basis.

items.statement: GNPA 2.61%, down 10 bps QoQ and 13 bps YoY; PCR 41.64%
items.quote: In terms of asset quality, our GNPA is at 2.61%, which has seen a reduction of 10 basis points on a Q-o-Q basis and almost 13 basis points on a Y-o-Y basis. Our PCR stands at 41.64%.

items.statement: Credit cost for quarter at 1.38%
items.quote: Our credit cost for the quarter is 1.38%.

items.statement: CRAR 32.8%, leverage 1.9x debt/equity, tangible net worth INR 3,465 crores
items.quote: In terms of business return ratios, our capital adequacy is sufficient at 32.8%, as Aseem was mentioning, with a tangible net worth of INR 3,465 crores as of March'26.

items.statement: Present in only one-fourth of districts within operating states; 30% district penetration in states present
items.quote: We are currently present in only one-fourth of the districts within operating states, which provides us with a significant runway for expansion.

items.statement: Gold loan branches at 220 out of 251 total branches
items.quote: It's close to 220-odd branches out of 251.

items.statement: More than 90% of book is variable rate
items.quote: More than 90% of the book is variable.

items.statement: Fully compliant with new regulatory circular effective April 1st
items.quote: We are fully compliant with the new regulatory circular effective April 1st.

items.statement: Management cautious on macro risks: fuel inflation, interest rates, monsoon, household leverage
items.quote: It's very difficult to pencil in what that impact is going to be. So just to be on the side of caution, what we've said is that we will continue to probably maintain the credit cost.

items.statement: ~75% of customers are first-time borrowers against property
items.quote: We have, in terms of our acquisition, almost 3/4 of our customers borrow for the first time. In fact, borrow against their property for the first time.

items.statement: Average ticket size below INR 2.5 lakhs
items.quote: Our average ticket sizes continue to remain below INR 2.5 lakhs.

items.statement: No need for DSA/connector channels for next 2 years; direct model sufficient for 20-24% growth
items.quote: For at least the next two years, we don't seem to have that need to go and chase growth through other channels.

items.statement: Collection staff count stable at ~550
items.quote: The account number is largely the same. I mean, some four or five here or there, but largely the same.

items.statement: Capital sufficient for 2 years growth to INR 18-19k crores AUM at 24-26% CRAR
items.quote: We are at 33% CRAR. If you just extrapolate on INR 11,000 crores, we can easily move 2 full years to around INR 18,000 crores to INR 19,000 crores.

items.statement: No management overlay on provisions; only model refresh adjustments
items.quote: We don't have any additional overlay. It's just the refresh of the model happens in March, and that refresh is reflecting on stage wise provisioning.

items.statement: Overall AUM growth guidance of 20-25% for FY27
items.quote: Yes, Meghna, so we've been giving an overall guidance last year also. And we said we will be a 20%, 25% AUM growth company, and we'll continue with that.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM growth of 20-22% even with flat gold prices
items.quote: But overall level, even if you have a flattish kind of a price play next year, we still should see a 20%, 22% growth on the AUM on the gold side for a flattish price.

items.statement: ROA improvement of 20-30 bps in FY27 over FY26 average
items.quote: So the trajectory will be in that direction. So if you're seeing a 20, 30 bps improvement on ROA, then at a PBT level, if I say 40 bps, that should come from credit cost or opex.

items.statement: Credit cost to remain range-bound in FY27
items.quote: In FY27, the credit cost should remain in a range bound, we should work on the opex.

items.statement: AUM reached INR20,153 crores, 27% YoY growth; ex-BL growth 41%
items.quote: In business, the AUM reached INR20,153 crores, translating to a growth of 27%. Excluding BL, it's about 41% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM INR10,352 crores, 76% YoY growth with 12% tonnage growth
items.quote: Gold reached INR10,352 crores, an AUM growth of 76%, substantiated by a tonnage growth of 12%.

items.statement: Mortgage AUM INR9,362 crores, 16% YoY growth
items.quote: Mortgage AUM reached INR9,362 crores, an AUM growth of 16%

items.statement: Q4 disbursals INR11,664 crores, up 109% YoY
items.quote: disbursals of INR11,664 crores in Q4 FY26, up 109%.

items.statement: Gold disbursals Q4 INR10,744 crores, up 37% QoQ and 135% YoY
items.quote: Gold disbursals for the quarter reached INR10,744 crores compared to INR7,853 crores in Q3 FY '26 and INR4,580 crores in Q4 of the previous year, indicating a growth of 37% and 135%, respectively.

items.statement: Doorstep gold loan AUM INR1,730 crores, 108% YoY growth, 17% of gold AUM
items.quote: Our doorstep gold loan business continues to perform with an AUM increasing by 108% Y-o-Y to INR1,730 crores.

items.statement: Co-lending book INR2,127 crores (21% of AUM) with 4% spread
items.quote: So our overall book under CLM is 21%, which is around INR2,100 crores. And that gives an AUM level spread of around 4%.

items.statement: Opened 148 new gold branches in FY26, total 750+ branches; will continue expansion in FY27
items.quote: As promised, we have opened 34 new gold branches this quarter, bringing our total to 148 new branches this year, and we will continue to expand our branches in FY27, too.

items.statement: Merged 70 ST LAP branches into gold branches (Vyapar model)
items.quote: In our collaborative initiative involving gold and ST LAP business, we have successfully further merged additional 7 branches, taking the total to 70 branches this year.

items.statement: Branch capacity 60-65 crores per branch; mature branches at 20 crores AUM
items.quote: So the capacity of every branch we have is to accommodate at least INR60 crores, INR65 crores of portfolio. And that's the size of the safe room. That depends on the locker, how much lockers we can keep it in the branch

items.statement: NII grew 23.1% QoQ and 14.8% YoY; yields down 12 bps YoY due to gold growth mix
items.quote: Our yields reduced 12 bps year-on-year due to a never before growth in the gold loan book. When you grow so much, obviously, there is going to be some impact on yield.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing down 4 bps QoQ; leverage increased to 4.6x
items.quote: Our weighted average cost of borrowing was marginally lower in the quarter by 4 bps. However, with the leverage increasing to 4.6% in Q4, in the ROA tree, you will see interest expenses optically going up by 10 bps.

items.statement: 30-35% of borrowings fixed (including CPs); gold book reprices on maturity
items.quote: So if you factor commercial paper of a longer duration also, roughly 30%, 35% would be fixed. So there is some insulation there.

items.statement: Credit cost 0.7% in Q4, 0.8% for FY26 (down from 1.7% in FY25)
items.quote: On a full year basis, credit cost as a percentage of average total assets is down from 1.7% in FY25 to 0.8% in FY26.

items.statement: GNPA 1.9% (down 20 bps QoQ), NNPA 1.3% (down 10 bps QoQ), PCR 32.3% flat
items.quote: GNPA has also declined 20 bps quarter-on-quarter to 1.9% from 2.1% and the net NPA has declined 10 bps to 1.3% quarter-on-quarter. We have been able to hold our PCR flat at about 32.3%.

items.statement: Entity 1+ DPD improved to 6% from 7.1%; 30+ and 60+ DPD improved 70bps and 50bps QoQ
items.quote: On asset quality, our Asset quality improved quarter-on-quarter with entity 1+ DPD improving to 6% from 7.1% in December and entity 30+ DPD improving by 70 bps and entity 60 + DPD improving by 50 bps over the last quarter.

items.statement: Write-offs ~INR14-15 crores in Q4; none in Q3
items.quote: This quarter, we would have had about maybe INR14 crores, INR15 crores roughly.

items.statement: CRAR 22.4% (up from 20.5% in Q3); raised INR450 crores subordinated debt in Q4
items.quote: Consequently, in spite of the healthy asset growth, our CRAR at 22.4% as of March is up from 20.5% in Q3.

items.statement: Raised $250 million ECB to date
items.quote: We have raised about $250 million in ECB till date.

items.statement: Tanked up on liquidity in Q4 to counter geopolitical volatility; optically increased finance cost
items.quote: We tanked up on liquidity in the quarter to counter volatility caused by the geopolitical situation in the Gulf. While it has optically increased finance cost and optically reduced the net interest income for the quarter, it gives us a hedge against the uncertainty and interest rate volatility in Q1.

items.statement: New gold loan LTV norms from April 2026: 85% up to 2.5L, 80% up to 5L, 75% above 5L; 90% of book already below 75%
items.quote: Now it has changed to 85% for exposure up to INR2.5 lakhs and 80% for exposure up to INR5 lakhs and anything above INR5 lakhs, it is 75%. So there is room g iven by the regulator for playing on the LTV. While 90% of the book is less than 75% for FEDFINA, we don't see any impact coming out

items.statement: New income assessment requirement for gold loans above 2.5L effective April 2026; systems live with credit bureau integration
items.quote: When the exposure increases INR2.5 lakhs, we need to do a basic assessment on the income and basically the cash flow of the customer to understand the profile a bit more in detail. So, we are prepared and after April 1, we are completely on. We are live with our systems, our integration with the credit bureau to understand the existing obligations not.

items.statement: Collection personnel nearly 2x since start of FY26; moved ST LAP collections in-house
items.quote: Additional personnel have been recruited, call center, legal and recovery teams at the end of '26, we have almost 2x the collection personnel that we started with.

items.statement: BL portfolio INR886 crores fully assigned and derecognized; secured on-book ratio >99.5%
items.quote: we 100% assigned our business loan portfolio of INR886 crores, which was executed and derecognized from our AUM. In addition to improving capital efficiency, it also ring-fenced us from further deterioration in the unsecured lending market.

items.statement: ROA 2.6%, ROE 14% in Q4; PAT INR100.5 crores (first time above 100 crores)
items.quote: PAT was up 14.4% sequentially quarter-on-quarter and 40% year-on-year, boosted by the incremental interest income from the asset growth and lower credit costs. We crossed the psychological milestone of INR 100 crores of PAT.

items.statement: Opex/avg assets 5.5% (down from 5.9% YoY); core PPOP up 22% YoY ex-DA income
items.quote: as a percentage of average total assets reduced to 5.5% from 5.9% a year ago and 5.7% in Q3, giving us some green shoots on economies of scale playing out on an expanding balance

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty in Gulf driving cautious outlook; cost of borrowing hardening post-February
items.quote: On the interest rate outlook, we saw cost of borrowing hardening post February as well as hedge rates on our foreign currency borrowing going up materially. With the current geopolitical situation, we remain cautious in terms of outlook.

items.statement: Competition pressure in gold loans not yet materialized but may play out
items.quote: The competition pressure that you are talking about is yet to play out is the way I would put it. The competition yet to get those branches in the spaces that we are operating and we are yet to see that pressure play out, although it might, but it has not yet played out.

items.statement: Target secured loan book growth of 22%+ for FY27 and advance book over ₹16,000 crores by FY29
items.quote: As we look ahead, we plan to organically grow our secured loan book at the rate of 22% plus for FY '27 and further acceleratin g the growth to achieve an advanced book of over ₹16,000 crores by FY '29.

items.statement: Target 235 branches by end of current year and 300+ by FY29
items.value: 235 branches by end of current year; 300+ by FY29
items.quote: We aim to expand our footprint by deepening presence in contiguous states and intensifying penetration within the existing markets with a target of 235 branches by the end of the current year and making it 300 plus by FY '29.

items.statement: Target ROTA 1.35%-1.4% for FY27 and 1.6%+ by FY29 with ROE 15%+ by FY29
items.quote: To achieve ROTA expansion in the coming year and with a target to make it 1.35% to 1.4% in FY '27 and 1.6% plus by FY '29 with an ROE expansion of 15% p lus by FY

items.statement: Credit cost guidance 0.15%-0.25% for FY27 with negative bias, aiming below 0.3% by FY29
items.quote: And if I talk about the credit cost going forward, we always intend to maintain in the range of 0.15% to 0.25%, and we are quite confident to maintain in this particular range just with a negative bias for the next year.

items.statement: Opex to average assets target 2.9%-3% for FY27 with lower bias
items.quote: As a percentage of the average asset opex over the medium term to take it below 2.85% , in the year 1, that is our current fiscal FY '27, we intend to keep it between 2.9% to 2.95% or 2.9% to 3%.

items.statement: NIM improved to 4.06% in Q4 FY26 from 4.01% in Q3 FY26 due to deposit repricing
items.quote: NIM showing early signs of improvement and improved to 4.06% in Q4 FY '26 versus 4.01% in Q3 FY '26 and the same is attributed to reducing cost of deposit on repricing at maturity.

items.statement: Cost of deposits declined to 5.75% in Q4 FY26 from 5.86% in Q3 FY26 due to initial repricing
items.quote: Cost of deposit has started showing declining trend and stood at 5.75% in Q4 FY '26 against 5.86% in Q3 FY '26, that is a quarter back, backed by initial start of the deposit repricing.

items.statement: Gross advances ₹8,687 crores, up 20.9% YoY and 6.4% QoQ; fresh disbursements ₹919 crores in Q4 and ₹3,508 crores for FY26
items.quote: As of March 31, 2026, our gross advances stood at ₹8,687 crores, reflecting sustained momentum in credit growth. On a year -on-year basis, advances grew by 20.9%, while sequentially growth stood at 6.4%.

items.statement: MSME segment grew 9% QoQ and 46% YoY; LAP grew 5% QoQ and 19% YoY
items.value: MSME 9% QoQ, 46% YoY; LAP 5% QoQ, 19% YoY
items.quote: The growth driver for the quarter is MSME/business segment, which grew by 9% on quarter-on-quarter and 46% on year-on-year basis followed by LAP, which grew by 5% on quarter-on-quarter and 19% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Out-of-Punjab advances 24% of portfolio vs 21% a year ago, growing >2x Punjab rate
items.quote: Out of Punjab advanced portfolio constituting 24% as on March 31, 2026 compared to 21% a year back.

items.statement: GNPA 2.54% (down 14bps QoQ, 4bps YoY); NNPA 1.24% (down from 1.35% QoQ, 1.30% YoY); PCR improved to 51.89%
items.quote: Asset quality improved and remain well managed during the quarter with gross NPA stood at 2.54%, improving 14 basis points sequentially and 4 basis points year -on-year basis. Net NPA stood at 1.24% compared to 1.35% a quarter back and 1.30% in the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: Gross slippage ratio 1.61% for FY26 and 1.27% for Q4 FY26; net slippage 0.08% for Q4; write-offs near nil
items.value: Gross slippage 1.61% FY26, 1.27% Q4; Net slippage 0.08% Q4
items.quote: The gross slippage ratio stood at 1.61% for the year and 1.27% for Q4 FY '26 and net slippage ratio for the quarter being 0.08%, while write -offs remained al most NIL during the quarter.

items.statement: SMA-1 and SMA-2 improved to 4.92% of advances from 6.46% QoQ
items.quote: Early stress indicator also shown improvement with SMA -1 and SMA-2 accounts at 4.92% of the advances against 6.46% a quarter back, supported by proactive collections and early delinquency management.

items.statement: NBFC-MFI net NPA ₹5.49 crores (17.3% of segment); recovered ₹60-70 lakhs in Q4; no fresh lending; fully provided
items.quote: If I talk about the value, the value basis, this particular value, the outstanding net NPA now is ₹5.49 crores. And the same value a quarter back was ₹6.08 crores. So we typically, in the current quarter, we recovered around ₹60 lakh to ₹70 lakh from those NPA accounts.

items.statement: CASA stable at 34.7%; retail deposits >90%; savings deposits ₹3,182 crores (31.76% of total)
items.quote: Bank continued to have stable CASA and the same stood at 34.7% as on 31st March 2026. Bank continued to focus o n granular and retail -centric deposit franchise. Retail deposit share continue to be above 90%.

items.statement: CD ratio 82.3% average, 86.7% at year-end vs 80.4% and 82.2% in Q3
items.quote: The credit-to-deposit ratio remained healthy with average CD ratio of 82.3% and 86.7% being at the end of the year , compared to 80.4% and 82.2%, respectively, in Q3, reflecting efficient fund deployment.

items.statement: Capital adequacy ratio 22.3%; average LCR 211% for Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains well capitalized. The capital adequacy ratio stood at 22.3% and average LCR for the quarter was a strong 211%, providing sufficient headroom to support our future growth.

items.statement: ECL transition evaluated as P&L neutral to positive; current provisions sufficient
items.quote: Initial understanding, yes, we are still working. initial understanding, it will not be P&L negative. So we will be either P&L neutral or P&L positive with this ECL.

items.statement: 98% of loan book secured; 89% of non-corporate portfolio collateralized by immovable property/FDRs; avg ticket size ₹18.3 lakhs
items.quote: The growth in advances continued to be driven predominantly by our secured lending products and around 98% of the loan book continue to be secured with around 89% of our non-corporate portfolio is being collateralized by immovable properties/bank FDRs.

items.statement: Fee income 0.9% of assets for FY26; target 0.85%-0.95% for FY27 with upward bias
items.quote: So typically, as far as the other income is concerned, other incom e, which is presently 0.9% on the asset basis. So we intend to make it between 0.85% to 0.95% also current year.

items.statement: PPOP for mature branches (5+ years) 2.75%-3.25% vs bank-level 2.1%
items.quote: If I talk about the PPOP levels at the above 5 -year branches, which is above 5 years, the same number remain presently is in the range of 2.75% to 3.25%.

items.statement: Branch network expanded to 211 branches across 5 states and 2 UTs; 77.3% SURU branches
items.quote: As of March 2026, our branch network expanded to 211 branches across 5 states and 2 union territory, strengthening our presence in rural and semi-urban market, with 77.3% branches being SURU branches.

items.statement: Management targets 20% volume and EBITDA growth once conditions normalize, with capacity to support it
items.quote: But once conditions stabilize , we still expect us to return on our targeted 20% growth trajectory, supported by our strategic initiatives and already available capacity.

items.statement: Cash flow target of INR 600 crores by 2027, with INR 333 crores generated in FY26 exceeding INR 250 crores target
items.quote: we were able to generate a cash flow of INR 333 crores exceeding our initial target of INR 250 crores and we remain on track for achieving our total target of INR 600 crores by 2027

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR 150-200 crores, focused on cash flow reinvestment to support 20% growth
items.quote: FY27, or in fact, even in the year later, I think our CAPEX strategy is now focused on our cash flows. So, what we are expecting is majority of or maybe 60-70% of our cash flows, we will put back into CAPEX. So, maybe INR 150 crores – INR 200 crores, something like that, to generate enough capacities to grow at 20%.

items.statement: Installed capacity at 6.8 lakh tons; added 1.2 lakh tons at Dadari in FY26; targeting 8-8.5 lakh tons by end FY27 including Sanand
items.quote: Our installed capacity now stands at approximately 6,80,000 metric tons , with the Dadari facility continuing to anchor our growth. During this year, we added about 1,20,000 tons of capacity at Dadari, completing our 1 st Phase of this expansion.

items.statement: IHT Wire Phase-II adding 6,000 tons on existing 9,000 tons; March utilization at 25%, rising 10-15% monthly
items.quote: Phase- II of the expansion is also progressing as planned, adding 6,000 tons of capacity on the existing 9,000 tons .

items.statement: LRPC wire started with 18,000 tons capacity, generating positive EBITDA from end of FY26
items.quote: Next, we started our LRPC wire product with 18,000 tons of capacity, which has also started towards the end of this year generating positive EBITDA.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 volumes at 80-85% of normal; auto segment strong but other segments sluggish due to steel price hikes and geopolitical issues
items.quote: Q1, we started with, of course, lesser volumes. In fact, last month, our volumes were cut to an extent of 35%. However, those are back. We are now expecting about 80 -85% kind of our volumes to be there. But other than volume, there is also an issue in demand as of now.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 7% (INR 80 cr on INR 1,136 cr revenue); FY26 EBITDA INR 325 cr up 17% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was INR 80 crore, with a margin of 7% and net profit came in at INR 40 crore, up 21% year-on-year.

items.statement: Gas price spike of INR 4,000-5,000/ton hit March EBITDA; 30-40 day order book delays pass-through; blended gas cost up ~50% in Q1
items.quote: there was a substantial increase in our gas prices to a tune of INR 4,000 to INR 5,000 a ton on our product level, which is something that we had to absorb because we have a 30- to-40-day order book.

items.statement: 30-40 day order book; fresh orders booked at higher prices reflecting gas cost increases
items.quote: Now this being a very exceptional increase, consumable is not something that we are able to take on previous orders. So, any orders that we booked after are being impacted o n our cost, we have taken our increase.

items.statement: Product mix stable: ~55% low carbon, 25% high carbon, 20% stainless; speciality <3-4% currently
items.quote: Yes, so overall our product mix has remained the same. I think 55 %-ish of low carbon, 25 high carbon and 20 percent stainless steel in general.

items.statement: Payables increased via purchase discounting facilities; vendor paid advance, company gets credit; payable days may rise further to reduce working capital days
items.quote: we have also included a lot of discounting limits from this year, which is where you are seeing the payable going high. So, this is part of the discounting facility that we have done in purchases.

items.statement: Discounting increases interest expense but not disproportionately; interest already paid via regular limits
items.quote: That will definitely lead to increase in our interest expense, but not disproportionately. So, we are already paying that interest even today, but that is done through our regular limits.

items.statement: Balaji Wire and Bansal High Carbon units at negligible utilization; remaining 4-5% shift to Bansal Wire in 6-8 months
items.quote: So, those two units again are operating at almost negligible capacity utilization. All of it has mostly shifted to Bansal Wire . I think maybe the next, the last 4 -5% that would be remaining would shift in another maybe 6-8 months.

items.statement: Sanand 50% land to be sold; backward integration deferred for at least 2 years
items.quote: So, sir, the balanced 50% land, we would be trying to sell it off to get that cash in. We have deferred our backward integration project. And for the next couple of years, it does not fit in our strategic investment scheme.

items.statement: FY26 volume 4.58 lakh tons (+33% YoY), highest ever; Q4 volume 1.17 lakh tons (+20% YoY)
items.quote: For the full year, volumes stood at 4.58 lakh metric ton , compared to 3.44 lakh metric ton in FY25 (erroneously said FY26), translating into 33% year-on-year growth and making the highest annual sales volume achieved by the Company

items.statement: FY26 capacity utilization 67-68%; targeting 70%+ in FY27, 80-85% optimal for returns
items.quote: We had the capacity utilization for FY26 was 67%-68% overall.

items.statement: Steel Cords: only Indian player; 2 lakh ton target; INR 2,000-2,500 cr capex over 5-7 years; EBITDA INR 600-800 cr at maturity
items.quote: Once we get our approval, our definite goal is still 2 lakh tons of steel cotton.

items.statement: Steel Cords barriers: technology, trained people (60), exclusive supplier tie-ups, long approval cycle, low capex/ton via own machinery division
items.quote: Technology is one. To get the right people is another. We already have about 60 trained people in this field. And it is not very easy to get the right set of people. Technology also, we have exclusive collaborations, exclusive tie -ups with our suppliers.

items.statement: Steel Cords first trial order expected from top 4 Indian tire companies; one customer cleared Phase-II, others by year-end
items.quote: So, the order we would be receiving would be from the top four companies in India. Yes, our year started slowing because of the fire incident, but we picked up. It will be our first trial order.

items.statement: B2C segment expanding: 16 new products launched for West and South India; distribution and brand visibility focus
items.quote: This segment has also started picking up and we have launched 16 new product offerings for the Western and Southern part of the country.

items.quote: Because the steel prices have gone up substantially, especially post the start of the year. The prices are already up on the range of almost 10-15%.

items.statement: Project portfolio ARR to exceed INR10,000 by FY29 and surpass INR14,000 by FY31

items.statement: Planned capex of INR3,600 crores with INR400 crores invested by FY26, funded 60% debt and 40% internal accruals
items.value: INR3,600 crores total; INR400 crores invested
items.quote: Our planned capex of approximately INR3,600 crores, of which INR400 crores has already been invested by FY '26, will be funded through a balanced mix of debt and internal accruals. Around 60% will be financed through borrowings with the remainder supported by internal cash generation.

items.statement: No heavy rare earth magnets used currently; government policy released but no material update

items.statement: Quick commerce NOV growth CAGR of 60% over three years
items.quote: We've given overall guidance of 60% CAGR and that would obviously mean some reasonable store expansion, but we're not planning to give out any specific number guidance on that.

items.statement: On track for 3,000 dark stores by March, no guidance beyond that
items.quote: On store addition, we're on track on our guidance for March of 3,000 stores. We remain firmly on track. We're not going to give any guidance beyond that.

items.statement: FY27 growth will not be 100%, no specific short-term guidance given
items.quote: Yes, it will not be 100%, but we are not guiding to a specific number. We need that flexibility in the medium term and short term to respond to how the market dynamics are.

items.statement: Confident in delivering 60% CAGR over three years based on assortment, geography, and demand densification
items.quote: We are fairly comfortable and confident that over a period of three years, we should be able to deliver this CAGR of growth.

items.statement: Quick commerce targeting 5-6% margin at steady state, contribution margin to improve year-on-year
items.quote: As we move to 5-6% margin that we are saying we will get to at some point, contribution margin will go up and on a year-on-year basis, we'll see that trend consistently.

items.statement: NCR quick commerce doing 5-6% margin implying 8-9% contribution margin
items.quote: We are not sharing that data point. I don't think it matters also, but broadly, it'll be somewhere in that range.

items.statement: Food delivery will reinvest incremental margin into growth rather than expand margin percentage
items.quote: If we can find ways of effectively reinvesting any incremental margin that we get in our business, or any business, we would do that because the objective is to optimize for growth of absolute profit and not the profit margin percentage.

items.statement: June quarter acceleration driven by AOV reversal, fewer days in March quarter, and seasonality
items.quote: The only other factor will be seasonality. It's a different season so we see different consumption patterns and summer driving growth in certain categories.

items.statement: Customer retention not significantly impacted despite higher prices in some geographies
items.quote: We haven't seen too much impact on customer retention despite us being sort of more expensive for customers in certain geographies.

items.statement: MTU additions strong due to continued marketing spend for new customer acquisition
items.quote: MTU additions remain strong because we continue to spend on marketing for new customer acquisition. So those spends haven't come down in the last quarter and hence the overall fixed cost remains in line with the previous quarter and the MTU addition also remains strong.

items.statement: Lower orders per customer due to accelerated new customer addition with lower initial frequency
items.quote: Yes, largely the latter, Swapnil. We haven't seen too much impact on customer retention despite us being sort of more expensive for customers in certain geographies. Most of this is on account of the acceleration in new customer addition that we have seen in the last couple of quarters.

items.statement: Low customer acquisition cost due to competitors pulling back on marketing
items.quote: We feel a lot of our competitors in the market have pulled back on this so we're seeing extremely low cost of customer acquisition and we, therefore, continue to see value in keeping marketing spends high at this point.

items.statement: Competitive activity unchanged, maintaining pricing discipline and healthy growth principles
items.quote: Competitive activity hasn't meaningfully changed from the last time we were on this call. Our stance about it is also the same that we will keep an eye out for it but do the right things for the business.

items.statement: No plans to match Swiggy's Toing model, Bistro remains small experiment
items.quote: At this point, we don't have any plans to do what Swiggy is doing with Toing. We're not clear on what problem it solves for consumers or for restaurants. Till the time we don't get the clarity, we'll just stay put on our focus areas, which is Zomato.

items.statement: Competitive intensity high across all tiers, different players aggressive in different markets
items.quote: The competitive intensity is fairly high pretty much wherever everybody is. Akshant Goyal: Different set of players in different markets. Someone is aggressive somewhere at this point. For us, it's competitive everywhere

items.statement: Dark store mix shifting from 80% urban/20% tier 2-3 towards more geographic diversification
items.quote: That's changing, Sachin. We're not giving specific guidance but increasingly, as we also mentioned in the letter, a large part of our growth will come from geographic diversification so we will see that mix change over time.

items.statement: Automation increasing in warehouses based on ROCE framework, no fixed capex guidance
items.quote: But directionally, yes, we are seeing automation increasing in all our warehouses. We will see that happening over the next few years as well. But how much of it is automated is a function of the framework on ROCE.

items.statement: Platform fee increases applied broadly, discounts targeted to price-sensitive cohorts in specific geographies
items.quote: What we mean is that the platform fees is applicable to all customers, but the offers or discounts can be targeted to a certain cohort of customers who are more price sensitive in certain locations and geographies where these subsidies actually deliver growth.

items.statement: Fuel price increases passed to consumers historically without meaningful demand impact
items.quote: In the past, going by the last 12 to 18 months, experiences and examples like the GST hike happened, where we were fairly easily able to pass it on to consumers without too much impact on demand.

items.statement: No plans to add new categories to District, travel not a focus area
items.quote: Garima, we have no plans to add any more category to District than what we already have, and travel is not a focus area for us at this point.

items.statement: Assortment expansion through whichever means possible, store size hyperlocal decision
items.quote: That means we are going to expand our assortment by whichever way we can. Akshant Goyal: For us, it's like square foot space. Size of the store is a function of lot of factors including availability, specific neighborhood and urban infrastructure in that neighborhood

items.statement: Inventory days fairly steady, no meaningful increase from Q3 to Q4 except scale growth
items.quote: But Q3 to Q4, there hasn't been any meaningful increase apart from the increase expected because of the growth in the scale of the business. Akshant Goyal: That doesn't change the inventory days anyway. Inventory days are fairly steady and we're not seeing that increase unlike what you suggested

items.statement: Orders per day per store flat, not a constrained metric for achieving 5-6% margin
items.quote: There could be arguments that can be made for that number to not go up and still the business might deliver 5-6% margin. That's also possible.

items.statement: Ad revenue primarily from brands selling on Blinkit platform, non-paid ads insignificant
items.quote: Non-paid ads, basically ads by brands or platforms which don't sell on the Blinkit platform, that's insignificant for us.

items.statement: Hyperpure included in $1 billion EBITDA guidance, will be meaningful despite being smallest business
items.quote: The statement that we have made includes all the businesses that we are in today, including Hyperpure. It might be the smallest, but it will still be meaningful and relevant.

items.statement: District events cancellations due to artist visa issues will not impact overall business growth outlook
items.quote: I don't think this will impact the overall broad growth path of the business. Events is just a part of the business, and we have multiple categories now. A few concerts getting delayed or postponed or even canceled will not impact the outlook on the business.

items.statement: Targets 10-12% volume growth in FY27
items.quote: we are targeting around 10% to 12% of volume growth from here on

items.quote: Yes, so for like CPVC it will be around 75% and for ECH it will be around 80%

items.quote: Leading to our EBITDA margin has been normalized range of 23 % on account of better sweating of the plants and also normalized level of raw material prices

items.quote: I would defer giving any guidance on the EBITDA margins. But what we have achieved so far, we would be maintaining in that range

items.statement: Exports only 4-5% of revenue, primarily to Europe
items.quote: See, company put together we hardly have around 4% to 5% of exports and that too it's to the Europe

items.quote: So, it was majorly because of one of the loan that where we had we had a mark-to-market impact. So, it's just a mark -to-market impact which has been there in the interest cost put together

items.quote: Historically it has depreciated by around 3% or 2%. But sinc e last one and a half year because of many global reasons, it has depreciated more. So that is the reason because of which we have to take mark-to-market impact

items.quote: So definitely I'm sure that we will be freezing on something and announcing this year so that we can have a consistent growth beyond FY29, FY30 onwards

items.statement: Guided 25% revenue growth for FY27
items.quote: I'm confident of delivering 25% revenue growth in FY '27.

items.statement: Demand momentum strong; new product inquiries healthy; existing product demand robust

items.statement: CDMO: four additional validated products beyond first; regulatory approvals pending; revenue expected in FY27

items.quote: we are embarking on ambitious expansion of our R&D centre, one that will elevate it into world -class internationally renowned facility, purp ose-built to meet the demand of tomorrow's industry. With planned 10x capacity expansion

items.quote: So the margin recovery is more likely to happen from Q2. So from Q2 financials, you'll be able to see a significant increase in our EBITDA margins.

items.statement: No revenue degrowth expected in FY27
items.quote: We will not degrow in FY '27, Devanshu. The idea is to grow.

items.quote: Over FY '27, we plan to add 10 to 12 new refreshing products especially bottom-wear products for our customers, not just line extensions, but genuinely new formats that opens up new purchase occasions and customer cohorts.

items.quote: As far as demand scenario is concerned, I think overall demand is not as weak maybe as how it was maybe 6 months or a year back. Quarter 4, when I speak to my peers, many retail companies, apparel companies have given positive commentary around demand scenario.

items.quote: Demand remains intact, and our execution momentum is strong. We remain confident of delivering sustainable growth while continuing to invest for scale.
