items.value: 42% revenue CAGR, 31% profit CAGR, 152% ROCE, 137% ROE
items.quote: Our continued efforts have resulted in a strong 5-year revenue CAGR of 42% and a healthy 5-year net profit CAGR of 31%. We continue to deliver exceptional return ratios, with ROCE at 152% and ROE at 137% for the financial year '25-'26.

items.statement: AI-first operating model with agents for coding, testing, deployment, workflow automation, communication monitoring and risk flagging; 60-70% customers using AI
items.quote: As per our commentary, we are already using AI for at least 60% to 70% customers, and we have increased their output with the same number of the resources.

items.statement: Repositioned as AI-first organization and 360-degree AI transformation partner; AI embedded in delivery, execution and client engagement
items.quote: We have repositioned ourselves as an Al-first organization, where AI is not an overlay but 1s embedded into delivery, execution and client engagement

items.statement: Acquisition attempts made but no good companies found; dropped idea to focus on organic growth
items.quote: We tried acquisition, but unfortunately, we could not find good companies. So, we dropped that idea. Now I'm focusing completely on the business, because if you go for acquisition, then you will have to spend a lot of time as well.

items.statement: Frappe/ERPNext partnership added to diversify ERP offerings alongside Odoo; both have own markets and costing aspects
items.quote: To initiate our own ERP business, our own ERP dimension, we added ERP or Frappe partnership also. So that if any specific customer is getting onboarded, we can offer two ranges of ERPs instead of specifically focusing on Odoo.

items.statement: Guided FY27 AUM growth of around 20%
items.quote: Now, as we stepped into a new financial year, we are geared up to get back on the track of growth and well -poised to achieve AUM growth of around 20% for the financial year 2027.

items.statement: Guided FY27 credit cost of 1.7% to 1.75% of average AUM
items.quote: At this point of time, we will probably be guiding you for a credit cost of 1.7% to 1.75% for the next financial year; depending on how the buckets trend over the year, this could look better from here, but our guidance will be about 1.7% to 1.75%.

items.statement: Guided steady-state credit cost of 1.5% to 1.6% for FY28-30
items.quote: So, we are probably looking at anywhere between 1.5% to 1.6% of credit cost as a steady -state number. I think we are confident about that.

items.statement: Guided FY27 spread of around 13.5%
items.quote: Our belief is that I think even for the current financial year, which is FY27, and thereafter, we should be able to operate at a spread of around 13.5%, depending on the leverage, the margins will stack up where they are.

items.statement: Guided FY27 opex to average AUM of 7% to 7.25%
items.quote: Our sense is, I think it will largely remain around the 7% to 7.25% levels, and not show any big decline during the year despite the 20% growth that we'll achieve.

items.statement: Guided FY27 disbursements of INR 6,500-7,000 crores
items.quote: And we should be able to get close to about INR6,500 crores to INR7,000 crores of disbursements in the coming year.

items.statement: Guided FY27 branch additions of 60 to 75
items.quote: So even for this financial year, we intend to open 60 to 75 branches.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 unique customer collection efficiency at 98.1%, x-bucket collections at 99.3%
items.quote: For the quarter ended March 31, 2026, we clocked a unique customer collection efficiency of 98.1%, which is one of our best in the history of Five -Star. Our x-bucket collections for the quarter came in at 99.3%, which has helped contain forward flows from x-bucket.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 slippage ratio dropped to 0.7% from 1.9% in Q3; GNPA stable at 3.37%
items.quote: Our slippage ratio has dropped from 1.9% in the last quarter to 0.7% in this quarter . This has helped our NPA remain largely stable between quarters at 3.37%.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 credit cost stable at 1.88% of average AUM vs 1.76% in Q3
items.quote: Credit cost has remained largely stable at 1.88% of the average AUM for Q4 compared with 1.76% in last quarter.

items.statement: Current bucket customers increased to 82.69% in Q4 from 81.77% in Q3
items.quote: After quarters of continued drop, the current proportion of customers who are in current buckets has moved up by close to 1% from 81.77% in Q3 to 82.69% in Q4.

items.statement: Stage-3 provision coverage at 41.4%; overall coverage at 1.84%
items.quote: We continue to have a good provision coverage ratio both on the overall assets and on the Stage- 3 assets. Our overall coverage is at 1.84%, and on Stage-3 we are at 41.4%.

items.statement: 61-90 day bucket improved to 4.8% from 5.1%
items.quote: In fact, our 61 to 90-day bucket has actually come down from about 5.1% to 4.8%, because of which you see a small drop in the Stage -2 provision coverage.

items.statement: April collections trending in line with typical seasonal patterns; no material deterioration expected
items.quote: So far, April is trending quite well. I think we are largely in line with a typical April month, both in collections across various buckets. And our belief is that I think this quarter also should be fairly good from an asset quality perspective.

items.statement: Strong lead indicators for disbursements; business and collections split operational from April 1
items.quote: Disbursements are looking up. In fact, one of the things that we have done, and we had also highlighted this in the commentary in the presentation and in the exchange release, the split between business and collections is fully operational from the 1st of April, and we expect that this will pave the way for a strong disbursement to come in.

items.statement: No major impact from geopolitical scenario on portfolio; sub-1% exposure to potentially affected segments
items.quote: The proportion of that portfolio is firstly extremely small for us, sub-1%. And even on that, we are not seeing any alarm signals at this point of time. The repayments are coming in well, in line with the other portfolio.

items.statement: No pricing change planned for FY27; yields not sensitive to ticket size shift within 3-5 lakh range
items.quote: At this point, there is no issue from a pricing perspective, and it is not like we are -- we have been slow on disbursements because of pricing. The slowdown in disbursements is a conscious call given the challenges that we faced. And we don't really envisage at this point of time for any pricing drop to happen at least in FY27.

items.statement: Cost of funds dropped to 8.95% in Q4 from 9.12% in Q3; FY26 cost of funds 9.21% vs 9.64% in FY25
items.quote: Our cost of funds for the quarter dropped from 9.12% in Q3 to 8.95% in Q4 and for the full year, we saw a drop in our cost of funds from 9.64% in last year to 9.21% this year.

items.statement: Senior management exit during FY26 had no impact on performance; business and collections teams separated from April 1
items.quote: There was a senior management exit during this year, but I want to clearly lay down the fact this has no impact on our performance. As can be seen from our results, this is a testimony to the strength and depth of our team, both at the management and the branches level.

items.statement: FY26 PAT INR 1,099 crores (2% YoY growth); Q4 PAT INR 269 crores (3% QoQ decline due to higher personnel expense)
items.quote: For the quarter, we achieved a PAT of INR 269 crores, while this is 3% lower as compared to the previous quarter on account of higher personal expense, I want to reinforce the fact over PAT, for the full year we grew even in such a challenging year by 2%, and we clocked a full year PAT of INR1,099 crores.

items.statement: FY26 ROA 8.68% and ROE 16%; Q4 ROA 8.37%
items.quote: Our return on average AUM and return on equity for the financial year 2026 remains healthy at 8.68% and 16%, respectively.

items.statement: FY26 write-offs ~INR 160-165 crores
items.quote: So, FY26, our write-off would have been about close to INR160 crores. I can give you the exact number later, but somewhere around INR160 crores to INR165 crores.

items.statement: Digital collections at 84% in Q4 FY26, up from 80% a year ago and 53% two years ago; target ~90%
items.quote: We are about 84% of collections, which came in digital, in Q4 FY26. So, 16% will be in cash, and this has been gradually moving up. If you look at over the last one year, we have moved this up from 80% to 84%. And if you look at the last two years, we have actually moved it from about 53% to 84%.

items.statement: Average ticket size increased from INR 3.5 lakh to INR 4.2 lakh; core focus remains INR 3-5 lakh segment
items.quote: If you see the average ticket size between last year and this year, it has moved from 3.5 lakh per customer to 4.2 lakh per customer. So, we are still operating in the sweet spot of 3 lakhs to 5 lakhs.

items.statement: Board declared same dividend as last financial year
items.quote: I'm happy to share that the Board has declared the same dividend that we got in the last financial year. So that also gives a good positive sign to the retail shareholders.

items.statement: Geopolitical risks monitored but no material impact seen; rating upgrade unlikely until H2 FY27
items.quote: Rating upgrade, at least till the end of the year, or maybe till the second half of the year, is out of question till we start showing some benefit.

items.statement: Revenue target of INR2,000 crores and EBITDA margin of 15-18% targeted between FY29 and FY30
items.quote: So as for our internal guidance, we are sort of aiming for FY29 at least for the top line, maybe around FY30. So, you can say between FY29 to FY30 is when we are planning to achieve this, both for your top line guidance as well as margin guidance.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned between INR100-120 crores for solar, knitting machines and PM MITRA Park
items.quote: So FY27 capex plan will be between INR100 crores, INR120 crores. Primarily, there is one large investment on our on-ground solar. So, the cash outgo and the commissioning will happen this year.

items.statement: Remaining INR300-350 crores of INR1,000 crore investment plan to be deployed over next 3 years in fabric and processing
items.quote: Out of that about INR675 crores is already deployed. The remaining INR300 crores, INR350 crores odd which is pending is to be deployed in next 3 years primarily.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 spread increased to INR148/kg from INR123/kg in Q3; expected to continue in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Just to give you a number, our spread in Q3 was about INR123 per kilo, which has gone up to about INR148 kilo in Q4.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved from 10% to 11.7% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: But what I can tell you that our EBITDA margins went up about 10% to 11.7%.

items.statement: Targeting 15% fabric revenue contribution in FY27 from 12% in FY26
items.quote: This year, of course there will be an increase of this fabric percentage. We are targeting almost 15% of our revenue to come from fabric.

items.statement: Strong demand tailwinds in Q4 FY26 from US tariff resolution, India-EU FTA, China yarn demand and domestic market
items.quote: I think one big factor was the overhang from the US reciprocal tariffs and the penalty tariffs which was on India. I think subsequently India-US trade deal got agreed and both squashed the tariff itself, sort of that unleashed a lot of demand factors.

items.statement: China yarn demand tapering down since March 2026
items.quote: I think we have seen a tapering down on demand since March, at least in our set, of customers and channel partners. We have seen a tapering of demand there.

items.statement: New 25,000 spindle unit stabilized at 98%+ utilization in Q4 FY26
items.quote: In Q4, we achieved 98% plus utilization.

items.quote: 15 machines are already in house and another 25 machines at least from quarter three onwards, we should start receiving.

items.quote: At this year the commissioning will be around July to August. So probably we'll get about 7 to 8 months of benefit. Primarily your summer seasons would have gone, so benefit would be in the range of about INR4.5 crores is what we can expect.

items.quote: On the cotton front, prices moved upwards, rising from approximately INR55,000 per candy in December '25 to around INR62,000 currently.

items.quote: So, a mix of Indian and imported cotton fee, it varies. But on a, at an average level we have almost about 30% of our requirement from export as an imported cotton, 25% to 30% on imported cotton and rest is all domestic.

items.statement: Working capital elevated due to strategic cotton inventory build; targeting 110-120 days sustainable level
items.quote: But it usually has been between 110 to 120 days for us also. And I think that is the level we are planning to maintain.

items.statement: Receivables increased 43% due to revenue growth and extended credit in Q2-Q3; expected to normalize

items.statement: Net debt INR118 crores at 0.1x net debt to equity; no buyback planned, cash flow directed to growth capex
items.quote: Further, our balance sheet remains strong with net debt of INR118 crores, which represents 0.1 x net debt to equity ratio.

items.statement: Dividend payout maintained at 8% of profit; policy of 8-12% payout balanced with growth capex needs
items.quote: So therefore, we are adhering to our policy of 8% to 12% payout. So last year, the payout was 8%. This year also, we have retained our payout of 8%.

items.statement: Received 50-acre land allocation in PM MITRA Park Virudhunagar for fabric and processing integration
items.quote: I am also pleased to share that we have received approval for land allocation in PM MITRA Park Virudhunagar, Tamil Nadu.

items.quote: So, this quarter, it was almost about 14% of our top line came from exports. I want to clarify one part in your question. We do not export directly to U.S.

items.statement: Yarn mix: 65-70% 100% cotton, 30-35% synthetic blended
items.quote: So, see, our mix is almost 65% towards 100% cotton yarn and rest 35% is on synthetic blended

items.quote: Let's say we have a very concentrated portfolio of strategic customers which consume almost 40% to 50% of our volume, and these are all large top brands.

items.statement: Cautious optimism: demand tailwinds from FTAs but risks from West Asia conflict, energy prices, inflation and gas availability
items.quote: We see it as a case of cautious optimism. So, there is a lot of demand tailwinds which is happening because of the FTAs getting signed and even the domestic market doing better. There is definitely a risk on the side of West Asia conflict and impact from that.

items.quote: There was a sale of nonstrategic or noncore land parcel, which we have done. And out of that, about INR8-point-something crores of profit has been realized.

items.statement: Targeting ROCE improvement to double digits through working capital optimization and margin expansion
items.quote: Our ultimate objective, by optimizing the working capital, by optimizing the margins, we have an objective to go to a double digit of the ROCE going forward.

items.quote: having said this, maybe anything around 60% to 70% of revenue growth will be there even coming financial year.

items.quote: On that around 60% to 70% growth will be there as an absolute amount.

items.quote: anytime actually which we are tender's participation is around INR25,000 crores to INR30,000 crores but our win rate is around 20%, 25%.

items.quote: So the Capex would be around INR120 crores to INR130 crores.

items.quote: targeting 1.5 gigawatt of EPC commissioning to scale the execution capabilities because 7.8 gigawatt of portfolio is there which needs to be commissioned next to 2 to 2.5 years.

These 25 gigawatts again further divided into 16 gigawatts of solar and around 9 gigawatts of BESS both go and even EPC, EPC scope.

items.quote: this revenues from this data centres around 7% to 8% of our total revenue will be constituting this financial year around 7% to 8% of revenue from data centre will constitute in this financial year. items.quote: We right now are like ratio between the EPC contracts and the products is about 90% to 10%, which we would like to upgrade towards products with the ratio of 70% to 30%.

items.quote: if you see in the overall revenue of the overall profit of the year it is absolutely, -- it is increased by almost a kind of 30 basis points. Last year we were at 7.2% percent and this year we were at 7.5% close to.

That too if you see on the numbers we are operating cash flow. We are positive by INR125 crores.

items.quote: if you net it off we are still having cash surplus of about INR100 crores. After netting of all the debt still the company is sitting on INR100 crores of cash, cash positive.

items.quote: we are going to supply these systems to the all DPSUs and even Indian defence as well as Indian defence and even export also.

items.quote: EBITDA margins for this year will remain same or maybe we will have a little improved margins of by about 20, 30 basis points yes.

items.quote: It is a confirmed order book for sure. It is INR 9,000 crores of order book is confirmed. It is on hand at this point of time.

items.statement: Expect high single-digit volume growth and more than double-digit EBITDA growth in carbon black for FY27
items.quote: In the carbon black business now with our additional capacity coming in, we expect to see a high single-digit volume growth. We should see more than double-digit growth in EBITDA as well for next year.

items.statement: Aquapharm targets 20-25% top-line growth in FY27
items.quote: Aquapharm should see a very strong growth in top line in FY27. I think in the region of 20-25% is something which we believe should be able to achieve.

items.statement: Cost reduction program on track to unlock INR200-250 crores savings over next 4-6 quarters
items.quote: Cost initiatives across yield improvement, throughput enhancement and feedstock diversification are on track to unlock over INR200-250 crores of savings over the next 4-6 quarters.

items.statement: Expect double-digit EBITDA growth in FY27 fueled by volume momentum, leaner cost structure and better pricing realization
items.quote: As the environment normalizes and volumes recover, we are confident of delivering double-digit EBITDA growth fueled by volume momentum, leaner cost structure and better pricing realization.

items.statement: Long-term INR40 billion EBITDA target by 2030 remains on track
items.quote: From 2030 perspective, we are very confident, we remain on track and with all the initiatives that we are taking, we believe that we should be able to deliver those numbers.

items.statement: 90,000 tons brownfield expansion at Tamil Nadu completed in Q4 FY26; total installed capacity now 880,000 tons per annum
items.quote: With the 90,000 tons Brownfield expansion of rubber carbon black at our Tamil Nadu during this quarter, our total installed capacity is now 880,000 tons per annum.

items.statement: Superconductive specialty black line of 1,000 MTPA at Palej mechanically ready but commissioning delayed due to gas shortage
items.quote: The superconductive specialty black line of 1,000 MTPA at Palej, Gujarat is mechanically ready for commissioning. However, commissioning has been delayed due to gas shortage.

items.statement: Specialty black line of 20,000 tons at Mundra ready, commissioning in next few weeks
items.quote: The specialty black line of 20,000 tons in Mudra is now ready as well and we'll be commissioning it in the next few weeks.

items.statement: Aquapharm expanded capacity from 130,000 tons to 167,000 tons during FY26
items.quote: During the year, we have successfully expanded our capacity from 1,30,000 tons to 1,67,000 tons, enabling us to serve higher volumes going forward.

items.statement: Nanovace pilot plant at Palej fully equipped and ready for commissioning within coming weeks
items.quote: Just a word on Nanovace, which is our platform for battery chemicals and the pilot plant at Palej is fully equipped and ready for commissioning within the coming weeks.

items.statement: Expect commercial volumes from battery chemicals business starting FY28 after qualification period
items.quote: I would expect that FY28 is when we will start seeing commercial volumes going up. We will share more details as we progress in getting more qualifications with our customers.

items.statement: Global tyre majors building strategic inventory buffers, transitioning from just-in-time to just-in-case approach
items.quote: Global tyre majors are increasingly building strategic inventory buffers, transitioning from just-in-time to a more resilient just-in-case approach in order to mitigate supply chain disruptions.

items.statement: Domestic customers increasing inventory cover by at least 3-4 days minimum across specialty and tyre segments
items.quote: our custo mers are increasing their cover for beyond increasing that by at least 3-4 days minimum as we see as of now. And this is true for specialty as well as for tyre customers

items.statement: Indian tyre sector poised for robust high single-digit growth in FY27 supported by vehicle usage, aging fleet, capacity expansion, premiumization and EV adoption
items.quote: The Indian tyre sector in FY27 is poised for robust, high single-digit growth. High vehicle usage and aging commercial vehicle fleet support steady tyre replacement demand in India. The industry is also benefiting from capacity expansion, premiumization and electric vehicle adoption.

items.statement: Oil and gas business at Aquapharm expected to see substantial restocking impact in first two quarters of FY27 with drilling activity rising ~30% at current crude levels
items.quote: based on historical trends, drilling activity should r ise by around 30% at current crude levels. Overall utilization level should also increase with faster commercialization of new products and diversification of our product

items.quote: Given that price contracts carry an inherent quarterly lag effect, the full impact of cost pass - through will reflect in our numbers by Q2 FY27, at which point our margins profile should normalize. items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margins same as previous quarter; real impact of cost initiatives yet to come

items.quote: On power side, the pricing, there are two components of it. One is the bilateral agreements that we have. Now there the price is moving well. items.statement: Brent crude rose from ~$60 to ~$100 per barrel in Q4 FY26, now hovering near $120; raw material prices, packing costs and freight costs escalated sharply
items.quote: Our raw material is directly linked to crude price and this quarter crude rose sharply and witnessed high volatility. Brent started at around $60 per barrel and ended March at around $100 per barrel. As we speak, it's hovering close to $120 per barrel.

items.statement: West Asia conflict caused massive logistics cost increases, vessel rerouting via Cape of Good Hope adding 14 days transit time, tightening container availability
items.quote: Vessels are being rerouted via the Cape of Good Hope, adding at least 14 days to transit time and increasing logistics costs significant ly. items.quote: Lead time and freight rates increased significantly, alongside a 25-30% rise in raw material prices. Yellow phosphorus, acrylic acid, malic acid and other raw materials. Packing material costs also went up materially (up to 1.5 times).

items.statement: Net borrowings reduced by INR454 crores to INR4,536 crores in FY26 while funding INR750 crores capex; working capital cycle tightened further
items.quote: Net borrowings reduced by INR454 crores to INR4,536 crores during FY26, even while we funded INR750 crores of capex. Our working capital cycle has tightened further.

items.quote: Even if crude remains at $90 level, I think considering the volume growth, the revenue growth, we will require another INR100 crores worth of incremental working capital. items.statement: Target net-net reduction in overall leverage in FY27 through cash generation from operations exceeding growth investment needs
items.quote: Yes, we feel that we can generate more cash from operations and what we require to invest in growth. And therefore, there should be net-net reduction in overall leverage.

items.statement: India-EU FTA ratified, providing duty-free access to 1.8 million tons carbon black market; US tariff reduction and duty refund benefits also favorable
items.quote: The India-EU FTA has been ratified, bringing duty-free access to an important market within sight. The recent U.S. tariff reduction and duty refund benefits will also work in our favor.

items.statement: China implementing supply-side reforms including VAT rebate cuts, provincial value-added mandates and stricter capacity guidelines, expected to drive structural price improvement across chemicals
items.quote: With China implementing supply -side reforms, including VAT rebate cuts, provincial value -added mandates an d stricter capacity guidelines, we expect structural price improvement across various chemicals and we expect to benefit from the same in the near future

items.statement: ~40% of total sales volume exported; South Asia primary market unaffected by West Asia conflict; proactively rerouted shipments to alternate geographies
items.quote: Around 40% of our total sales volume is exported, with South Asia being the primary market and remaining unaffected by the ongoing conflict. To navigate the disruptions in West Asia trade routes, we have proactively rerouted shipments to alternate geographies, ensuring continuity and minimizing any impact on international sales.

items.statement: Europe imports ~500,000 tons carbon black annually; India currently supplies ~100,000 tons; EU FTA to eliminate 4.5% duty on Indian tyre exports to Europe (one-third of India's tyre exports)

items.quote: Specifically, if you talk about the green chelates portfolio, where we last quarter also mentioned that we have started receiving trial orders and supplies have started to both P&G and Henkel. items.statement: Deepening presence in Europe and Japan through service-led model with customized solutions for key players
items.quote: We are deepening our presence through a service-led model in Europe and Japan, aiming to drive volume and market-shared growth through customized solutions with key players in these markets.

items.statement: US market underserved; US customers diversifying away from China/Russia toward Indian players; PCBL competitive despite logistics costs
items.quote: Yes. But even with that we are competitive in the US market. It's an underserved market. And the US customers are also trying to diversify away, because the competition is China, Russia as you said, they want to diversify to other Indian players. Therefore, we believe we are still competitive in multiple applications.

items.statement: West Asia conflict created significant disruptions: logistics cost spikes, feedstock cost increases, vessel availability issues, transit time extended by 14 days

items.quote: We believe that maybe in a quarter's time, we'll see crude soften back to that 80-90 level.

items.quote: in our last earn ings call, we did guide for INR 300 crores to INR350 cror es of annualized EBITDA for FY27. We are confident that we should be near that number unless there is more loss of business due to war in our B2B business or in our Middle East operations

items.quote: At the moment, what we have done is we have stopped hiring for the field. This is a move on account of the West Asian crisis, which is creating a shadow in India also.

items.statement: IT transformation investment of INR30 crores planned over next 3 years
items.quote: So, towards that, we have lined up about INR30 crores for the next 3 years to come in into the business.

items.statement: FY26 IT transformation spend of INR10 crores completed
items.quote: We initiated the first phase of our IT transformation with an investment spend of around INR10 crores in the last financial year.

items.statement: Added net 700 employees in FY26, 650 in sales; employee base now 3,768
items.quote: We significantly strengthened our distribution engine with an addition of around 700 employees during the year, of which 650 people in sales.

items.statement: Private Wealth plans to hire 25-30 relationship managers in FY27
items.quote: We intend to hire around 25 to 30 relationship manager in this financial year.

items.statement: AUM INR23,230 crores; total customer assets INR97,000 crores as of 31 March 2026
items.quote: As on 31st March, our AUM stood around INR23,230 crores and total customer assets were INR97,000 crores.

items.statement: Monthly SIP collection reached INR151 crores in March 2026
items.quote: Our SIP book continues to build steadily with the monthly collection reaching INR151 crores in March.

items.statement: NRI assets managed INR12,000-13,000 crores; NRI income INR90 crores in FY26
items.quote: To give you numbers on NRIs as a whole, we have about INR12,000 crores to INR13,000 crores of assets that we manage for NRIs. And altogether, we have made an income of about INR90 crores in the last financial year.

items.statement: Private Wealth AUM approximately INR2,400 crores as of 31 March 2026
items.quote: AUM as on 31st March was approximately INR2,400-odd crores.

items.statement: PMS AUM grew from INR450 crores to INR1,450 crores over 3 years; 8% YoY growth in FY26
items.quote: If you look at the presentation, in FY '23, our AUM was only INR450 crores asset management business. Now it is INR1,450 crores.

items.statement: Distribution income grew 10% in FY26; mutual fund net inflow market share improved from 0.33% to 0.40%
items.quote: Distribution income grew 10% during the year. Our net inflow market share in equities for mutual fund improved from 0.33 to 0.40 reflecting an improving competitiveness and deeper client engagement.

items.statement: Health insurance premium INR22 crores in FY26, first year of offering
items.quote: You have seen in the last year, the penetration of insurance and especially health insurance, which we started actually doing last year, we did close t o INR22 crores of premium in health insurance

items.statement: FY26 profitability impacted by INR54 crores transformation expenses (INR29 cr sales hires, INR15 cr marketing, INR9 cr labor code provision)
items.quote: What you saw last year, though the mutual fund insurance income, that is the distribution income has gone up, a substantial portion, which comes from brokerage went down. So that is why you have seen an effect on ROE being reduced.

items.statement: Plan to borrow for future MTF and loan against shares funding instead of using own cash
items.quote: We intend to borrow and finance the future requirements with regards to the MTF book and the loan against share book and the NBFC.

items.statement: Open to buyback after SEBI regulations finalized; no capital raise planned
items.quote: With regard to buyback, we will wait for the SEBI regulations to come out. There is a discussion paper out it seems. So, after that, we will take a view. We will be open to the idea at the appropriate time.

items.statement: Launching new AIF via GIFT City route; 1-2 new PMS schemes planned for FY27
items.quote: On the schemes of new AIF, we are launching one, which will take -- it is in application stage and AIF through the GIFT City route. That is what is there in the pipeline. We have built the PMS team. And my feeling is maybe for this financial year, maybe 1 or 2 more schemes in PMS also.

items.statement: DIFC entity licensed, operations started February 2026; client onboarding to begin end of April 2026
items.quote: we have received all the licenses, and we had started operations in the month of February. This is largely a private banking business. We are external asset m anagers to private banks. So the onboarding with the private banks are in progress. Client onboarding hasn't yet started, which will take -- by the end of this month is when we'll start client onboarding

items.statement: DIFC hiring relationship managers; minimum ticket size $1 million
items.quote: The relationship manager or the salespeople are in the process of recruitment. The minimum ticket size that generally private banks require in DIFC is about $1 million.

items.statement: West Asia conflict causing client hesitation; no panic redemptions but delayed financial decisions
items.quote: The West Asia conflict has had a little bit of apprehensions because clients have -- while we are not seeing across the NRI client base that we have, we are not seeing panic redemptions, but clients are choosing not to make any financial decision at this time until they are clear about -- or they have some certainty about the future.

items.statement: 58-60% of income from clients with 7+ year vintage; mutual fund AUM per client rose from INR3.5L to INR5L
items.quote: Most of our income, actually, 58% of our income comes from the clients who have been with us for more than 7 years. So we have been -- like I said in my beginning, we handhold our clients and participate with them throughout their wealth creation journey, and that is what we see.

items.statement: Added 1.5 lakh clients in FY26; higher revenue per client vs industry due to dual broking and mutual fund revenue
items.quote: In terms of client recruitment, yes, 1.5 lakhs client. And unlike -- so in our case, since we hire clients for broking as well as for mutual funds, the idea is to handhold the client and let the client re main with us for a longer time

items.statement: New sales hires expected to break even in 12-18 months depending on product mix
items.quote: We expect the new salespeople to break-in within 12 to 18 months. It all depends on the product mix. When the market -- the stock market especially is not well, it will be done through insurance. Otherwise, stock market itself can take it.

items.statement: Mutual fund AUM per client increased from INR3.5 lakhs (FY22) to INR5 lakhs (FY26)
items.quote: In FY '22, it was close to INR3.5 lakhs, mutual fund AUM per client has gone to INR5 lakh per client.

items.statement: INR9 crores provision for new Labor Code implementation in FY26
items.quote: Just to note, FY '26 also includes a provision of around INR9 crores towards the implementation of the new Labor Code, which is in line with our regulatory requirements.

items.statement: Private Wealth has 55 RMs, 90 total staff across 8 cities; no new city expansion planned, focus on deepening existing hubs
items.quote: We have approximately 5 branches in Kerala, Chennai, Hyderabad, Bangalore, Bombay, Pune, we have just recently started, Delhi and Calcutta. We don't intend to expand more cities as of now, but we want to go deeper as far as these cities are only concerned.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM growth guided at 20-25% for FY27 if gold prices remain at current levels
items.quote: So, I think if they remain here, we should see AUM growth of around 20% to 25%.

items.statement: Consolidated credit cost guided at 1.5-1.7% for FY27 versus 2.7-3% in FY26
items.quote: Next year, our credit cost on the whole will be around 1.5% to 1.7%.

items.statement: ROA expected to reach 3-3.5% in FY27 driven by 120-130 bps credit cost decline
items.quote: So that 2.4% ROA should grow by -- I think it should end at 3%, 3.5%, but one can work out the numbers based on assumptions of growth or the way -- and the credit cost.

items.statement: IIFL Home Finance AUM growth guided at 18-20% and disbursement growth at 25-27% for FY27
items.quote: We are expecting a book growth of about 18%, 20% in FY '27 and disbursement growth would be about 25% to 27%.

items.statement: Off-book AUM (DA + co-lending) target raised to 40-45% from current 34-36%
items.quote: The total off-book proportion, which is DA and co-lending put together will be 34%, 36% in that range. Our endeavor will be to take it to 40%, 45%.

items.statement: Co-lending share of AUM targeted to grow to ~20% from current ~13-14%
items.quote: And within that, co -lending also has been growing relatively, and we think that co -lending should grow e ven further because co - lending has become a very formalized and a very well laid out process

items.statement: Quarterly average cost of borrowing fell 25 bps QoQ to 9.16% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our quarterly average cost of borrowing decreased 8 basis points Y-o-Y and 25 basis points on a quarter-on-quarter basis to stand at 9.16%.

items.statement: Standalone credit rating upgrade to AA+ could reduce cost of funds by 100-120 bps
items.quote: I believe that our cost of funding can go down easily by 100 to 120 basis points once the rating improves.

items.statement: Consolidated loan AUM grew 38% YoY and 10% QoQ to INR 1,08,180 crores in Q4 FY26
items.quote: For the quarter, the consolidated loan AUM grew by 38% on a Y-o-Y basis, and up 10% on a quarter-on-quarter basis to close at INR1,08,180 crores.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM grew 150% YoY and 11% QoQ to INR 52,581 crores with 62 tons in Q4 FY26
items.quote: driven by gold, which closed at INR52,581, up by 150% on a Y-o-Y and 11% quarter-on-quarter basis with a healthy tonnage at 62 tons.

items.statement: Core products (home, gold, MSME, microfinance) AUM grew 45% YoY and 11% QoQ to INR 1,04,198 crores (96% of total)
items.quote: our core products, loan AUM comprising home, gold, MSME and microfinance are up 45% on a Y-o-Y and 11% on a quarter-over-quarter basis to INR1,04,198 crores and this segment aggregates around 96% of our overall AUM.

items.statement: Assigned loan book grew 85% YoY and 11% QoQ to INR 23,704 crores in Q4 FY26
items.quote: The assigned loan book, which is coming through our partnership with the bank, has grown out s martly to INR23,704 crores, up 85% on a Y-o-Y, 11% quarter-on-quarter basis

items.statement: Co-lending asset book grew 36% YoY and 9% QoQ to INR 14,384 crores in Q4 FY26
items.quote: our co-lending asset book stands around INR14,384 crores, which is up 36% Y-o-Y and more importantly, 9% quarter-on-quarter because the new regulation came up 1st of January.

items.statement: Gross NPA at 1.5% and net NPA at 0.7%, down 77 bps and 32 bps YoY respectively
items.quote: Healthy gross NPA number reasonably below to our stated number of around 2%. Our gross NPA stood at around 1.5 and net NPA of 0.7, which is down 77 basis points and 32 basis points, respectively, if you compare to the same period last year.

items.statement: Ind AS provision coverage on NPAs at 93% with ECL implementation
items.quote: With the implementation of ECL, our Ind AS provision coverage on NPAs stands healthy at 93%, with a larger share of secured assets that we have in the portfolio.

items.statement: Microfinance seeing robust recovery with improving collection efficiency and stabilizing asset quality
items.quote: Microfinance is seeing a robust recovery with improving collection efficiency and stabilizing asset quality.

items.statement: IIFL Home Finance plans to open ~100 affordable housing branches in FY27 in phased manner
items.quote: We plan to open about 100 branches this year in a phased manner.

items.statement: Gold loan branch expansion planned in FY27 after no expansion in FY26 to penetrate underserved segments
items.quote: Two, we'll also be expanding our branch footprint a little. I mean, last year, we did not, but now we may. This year, we will.

items.statement: IIFL Home Finance exited micro LAP and prime segments; focusing on affordable (12%+ yield) and emerging with higher LAP mix
items.quote: we have exited that business, and we don't i ntend to do that business going forward. So that is one big reason as to why the growth was muted. So now we have reworked on our strategy

items.statement: IIFL Home Finance LAP mix at 18% of AUM; targeting higher yield affordable LAP (INR 13-15 lakh tickets)
items.quote: Today, if you look at the overall AUM, our LAP mix is about 18%, 80% is HL, 18% is LAP and the rest is construction finance.

items.statement: PMAY 2.0 interest subsidy with 5-year lock-in expected to reduce balance transfers and improve customer retention in affordable housing
items.quote: this scheme would ensure that customer on book would be there for a longer time because there is incentive if customer stays with the company for 5 years.

items.statement: Fully compliant with new RBI gold loan guidelines effective 1 April; credit assessment implemented for loans above INR 2.5 lakh
items.quote: We are fully complied with the new guidelines from 1st April. And basically, loans above INR2.5 lakh, they want the credit assessment to be done and the loans to be monitored.

items.statement: New co-lending regulations formalized from 1 Jan 2026; co-lending book grew 9% QoQ post implementation
items.quote: More importantly, interestingly, with the implementation of the new co-lending regulation, the company is able to scale this process well with leading banks and our co-lending asset book stands around INR14,384 crores, which is up 36% Y-o-Y and more importantly, 9% quarter-on-quarter because the new regulation came up 1st of January.

items.statement: Raised INR 28,165 crores in Q4 FY26 via term loans, bonds, CPs and INR 7,046 crores via direct assignment
items.quote: we raised close to INR28,165 crore s with a mix of term loan, bonds, commercial papers and INR7,046 crores was raised through direct assignments of loans

items.statement: Cash and committed credit lines at INR 6,638 crores; positive ALM with net gearing at 3.8x
items.quote: Our cash and cash equivalent, including committed credit lines from banks stood healthy at around INR6,638 crores and are adequate to meet not just our near-term liabilities, but also to fund our continuous growth momentum.

items.statement: Comfortable with net gearing up to 4.5x; equity raise planned when timing is right
items.quote: 4.5x is okay. I don't think up to 4.5x is any challenge. Typically, you can go up to 6.7x based on the capital adequacy.

items.statement: Consolidated ROE annualized at 17.89% and ROA at 2.97% for Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our healthy trajectory with our annualized ROE for quarter 4 standing at around 17.89%, similar to what we have reported in the previous years and particularly prior to fiscal '24.

items.statement: Capital adequacy: NBFC 17.8%, HFC 42.1%, Samasta 26.5% - all well above 15% minimum
items.quote: Capital adequacy has stood well with -- standing at around 17.8% for the NBFC. HFC at 42.1% and Samasta Microfinance at 26.5%, each of which are well below the minimum threshold of 15% reflecting a successful movement with the off-book model that we hold.

items.statement: Income tax assessment orders expected within days; any demand will be appealed; no material adverse outcome expected
items.quote: The group companies have already started getting the assessment orders. So the process is going at a full -- good speed. And our IIFL Finance also which we're getting our assessment order in a few days' time.

items.statement: Expects brokerage revenue to catch up in coming periods as regulatory impact is behind and volumes are up
items.quote: Now with a higher base in the current financial year over last financial year, we expect the brokerage line item to catch up for coming periods, given that the regulatory impact is behind and our volumes are up.

items.statement: Expects strong growth in MTF book in coming periods due to strong balance sheet and largest broker position
items.quote: We definitely have a very strong balance sheet to grow this book. Over the last few years, there has been a very strong growth of our MTF assets. We expect a similar strong growth in the coming periods because we are the largest broker in terms of Industry cash brokerage revenue pie.

items.statement: Expects meaningful variable returns from alternate funds in coming financial periods as multiple funds have reached last cohort with IRRs well above hurdles
items.quote: As far as the variable additional return is concerned, so we don't give out guidance. However, as explained in our last con call, we have multiple number of funds, which has reached in the last cohort of their life, where our IRRs are well above the hurdles, and we expect meaningful variable returns to accrue in the coming financial periods.

items.statement: AMC AUM crossed ₹1.5 lakh crores with 34% YoY growth to ₹3.7 lakh crores total AUM
items.quote: Our Asset Management and Private Wealth business continued momentum during the year with robust net flows of ₹70,000 crores and an AUM of ₹3.7 lakh crores, which is up by 34% year -on-year.

items.statement: AMC AUM grew 15% from FY26 average of ₹1.57 lakh crores to latest ₹1.8 lakh crores
items.quote: Our latest AUM at ₹1.8 lakh cr is already 15% higher than the FY26 avg. of ₹1.57 lakh Crs.

items.statement: SIP AUM book of ~₹30,000 crores as of Mar'26 with SIP run rate of ₹1,500 crores per month
items.quote: FY26 SIP flows crossed ₹ 16,000 Cr. mark, up 78% on YoY basis with a market share of 4.7% resulting in a SIP AUM book of ~₹ 30,000 cr as on Mar'26.

items.statement: Alternates fee-accruing AUM grew 40% from average ₹15k crores to closing ₹21k crores
items.quote: We raised our largest growth capital fund IBEF V raising close to a billion dollars. This leads to 40% growth in fee accruing AUM from average AUM of ₹15k Crs to closing AUM of ₹21K Crs.

items.statement: Private Wealth ARR AUM at ₹46,000 crores with 440+ RMs, 32% having 3+ years vintage
items.quote: Focus is now on growing ARR AUM which is currently at ₹46,000 Crs through various initiatives including advisory solutions, strengthening leverage solutions as a value add for UHNI clients, exclusive co-investments leveraging group synergy, etc.

items.statement: Housing Finance adjusted disbursement grew 28% to ₹2,291 crores and AUM grew 25% to ₹6,100 crores
items.quote: Disbursement (adjusted) grew 28% YoY to ₹2,291 Crores. Consequently, AUM (adjusted) grew by 25% to ₹6,100 Crs.

items.statement: Investment Banking completed 52 deals with cumulative raise of ₹83,600 crores and fees income grew 39% to ₹309 crores
items.quote: Our IB business still has successfully completed 52 deals in FY26 with cumulative raise of ₹ 83,600 cr and our fees income delivered a strong 39% revenue growth YoY basis to ₹ 309 Cr.

items.statement: Operating PAT grew 16% YoY to ₹2,360 crores in FY26, Q4 grew 25% to ₹661 crores run rate
items.quote: Our operating profit after tax in the year FY26 grew by 16% YoY to ₹2,360 crores, led by a 33% growth in the profits of Asset and Private Wealth businesses.

items.statement: Asset Management now contributes 33% to Group Operating PAT in FY26 vs 26% in FY25
items.quote: Asset Management now contributes 33% to Group's Operating PAT in FY26 vs 26% in FY25.

items.statement: Annuity revenues now over 60% of total revenues, Asset and Private Wealth contribute ~50% of operating profit
items.quote: Annuity businesses contributing over 60% of the group's revenues have risen in the last 5 and 10 years, and will continue to rise going forward, resulting in improved quality as well as predictability of our cash flows.

items.statement: SIP run rate of ₹1,400+ crores per month, slight decline in passive MF due to international funds and microcap fund restrictions
items.quote: We are having a SIP run rate of ₹1,400+ crores a month. There is a slight decline in passive MF side due to 1) Our international funds are no longer able to take new mon ey and 2) the microcap fund is also locked

items.statement: Net flow market share higher than AUM market share in Q4FY26 and April 2026
items.quote: For Q4FY26, our net flow market share was higher than the AUM market share

items.statement: TER changes did not impact fees, slightly improved for cohort of AUM; yield compression due to mix effect from faster-growing passives with lower retention
items.quote: Our fees as a consequence of the TER changes continued to remain unimpacted. In fact, they have slightly improved for our cohort of AUM as that category did not get impacted. On the alternate side, our retention rates have been maintained. If you see a compression in yields for us, it is on account of mix effect.

items.statement: FY26 was year of investments in people, brand and technology; other expenses up 10% YoY with ~5.5% of net revenues spent on marketing and technology
items.quote: FY26 was a year of investments on all fronts in the group, be it people, brand or technology. We've not left any stone unturned to maintain our leadership position in our businesses.

items.statement: Q4FY26 other expenses up 20% sequentially due to higher marketing, brand promotion and CSR expenses
items.quote: Q4FY26 includes a predominant impact of higher marketing , brand promotion and CSR expenses. Bulk of which have actually been incurred in th is quarter resulting in a delta slightly higher on a sequential basis

items.statement: Investment team now over 50 members strong across alternate and mutual fund including passive
items.quote: Over the last period, we have increased the team size on both the alternate and mutual fund in terms of managers and research. Overall, the investment team, inclusive of passive is now over 50 members strong.

items.statement: AMC launched 5 new MF Active Products in FY26, now covering 82% of Industry AUM; 8 funds to cross 3-year vintage by Mar'27, 16 by Mar'28
items.quote: We launched 5 new MF Active Products in FY26 increasing our presence to 82% of Industry AUM. Importantly, only 6 of our funds have a vintage of over 3 years vs 42/29/26 funds with similar vintage in the case of top 3 peers. We expect 8 funds to cross 3 years vintage by Mar'27 and 16 funds by Mar '28.

items.statement: Alternates launching Private Credit fund of ₹3,000 crores, first Commercial RE Fund and Series VII of Residential RE Fund
items.quote: This AUM growth will be further supported by a strong launch pipeline with our maiden Private Credit fund of ₹3 ,000 Crs, first Commercial RE Fund and launch of Series VII of our Residential RE Fund.

items.statement: Private Wealth works with 9,000 families, ~50% have UHNI potential; AUM per RM rising despite RM base increase
items.quote: On our quality of clients, we work with 9,000 families, of which almost 50% have UHNI potential. The scale and quality of clients is steadily improving.

items.statement: Wealth Management focused on research and advisory model to maintain cash market revenue share; targeting high-value traders to protect market share
items.quote: Our Wealth Management business, that we are building on, have always been focus ed on the research and advisory model. If you look at our model, whether it is the franchisee segment, the direct side and the branch model, we are very well aligned with our research and advisory-led model, along with technology in the overall business

items.statement: Alternates gained market share with distinct products turning into brands; differentiated basket mixing listed/unlisted and quant-based investing
items.quote: On the alternate side, we have gained market share. We are amongst the top few in the industry with very distinct products with strong storylines. A lot of our products are turning into brands & are being asked by the investors for investing.

items.statement: F&O regulatory changes and higher margin requirements impacted market breadth in FY26
items.quote: The strong operating performance has been delivered in the backdrop of head winded external environment, be it weak markets impacting mark -to-market in our AUM in multiple businesses coupled with multiple regulatory changes, like the F&O changes, r equirement of higher margins, etc., impacted market breadth

items.statement: Housing Finance raised $100mn from Asian Development Bank; strong capital adequacy and low leverage provide growth levers without external equity
items.quote: MOHFL raised $100mn from Asian Development Bank (ADB), validating the strong franchise. We expect Housing Finance business having formed a strong base and a very strong leadership team to witness strong growth over 2-3 years.

items.statement: Operating PAT 10-year CAGR 33%, EPS CAGR 28%, ROE 23%; investment book 10-year CAGR 40% with 18% IRR
items.quote: Our operating businesses have delivered a 10-year compounded operating profit after tax growth of 33% per annum, EPS growth of 28% per annum, return on equity of 23%. This strong growth is supported by our investment book, which grew by 40% compounded since inception, led by a combination of strong IRRs as well as reinvestment of the operating profits post distributions.

items.statement: Quarterly volatility in investment book due to market drawdowns; long-term IRR range 15.5%-19% with 18% compounding
items.quote: One will see a lot of quarterly volatility in this book depending on the market volatility, unrealized gains / losses. That's why we separately report our operating profit after tax number for each business, causing no confusion about this line item with the operating businesses.

items.statement: Management declined to provide FY27 margin guidance due to high input cost volatility
items.quote: At this stage, we will be constrained to give any guidance on margin front. Maybe once the external environment settles down a little bit, hopefully, it should in a couple of quarters' time, then we'll be able to guide the street on our margin target for FY27.

items.statement: Took ~4% portfolio-level price increase in March; full impact visible Q2 FY27
items.quote: we have taken pricing action to the tune of around 4% in the month of March. The result of which should be visible in quarter 1 to a large extent and full impact should be visible quarter 2 onwards.

items.statement: Crude-linked raw materials up sharply: LABSA +60-65%, HDPE/PP +50-55% in March-April
items.quote: If you look at January, and if you look at prices today, they are up by 60%, 65%. If you look at HDPE, PP, packing material item, which is roughly 15% to 20% of our purchases that has gone up by about 50%, 55%, and that has happened in March and April.

items.statement: High competitive intensity in Dishwash: rivals cutting MRPs, increasing grammage; Exo Liquid launched with bio-enzymes to compete with market leader
items.quote: Competitive intensity remains high with several players reducing MRPs and offering more quantity at the same price. During the quarter, we strengthened the Exo portfolio with the launch of the bio-enzyme-based dishwash across formats.

items.statement: Remain debt-free with INR1,000 cr cash balance; net working capital improved to 15 days (-4 days)
items.quote: Net working capital improved to 15 days, a reduction of 4 days. We remain debt free with a strong cash balance of INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR3.5 per share for FY26
items.quote: The Board has recommended a final dividend of INR3.5 per share for FY26.

items.statement: Actively scouting for acquisitions with INR1,000 cr cash; in active dialogues with a couple of targets; robust screening process
items.quote: Yes, you are right, and we have been scouting for right assets. And very aggressively, we are looking for right asset. But as we have mentioned earlier, we are going to pick up the asset, which actually adds to the overall shareholders' value. And we are in active dialogues with a couple of them.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected in similar range as FY26
items.quote: Similar. It will be in similar range only.

items.statement: FY27 effective tax rate expected at 25-26% under Section 115BAA
items.quote: It will be, we will be going for 115BAA. So, rate should be around 25% to 26%. It should be hovering between 25% to 26%.

items.statement: Higher crude prices could keep inflation elevated, affect consumer spending and rural farm income; weaker rupee adds to cost pressure
items.quote: Higher crude prices could keep inflation elevated and may affect consumer spending. This is also a risk to rural demand if farm income gets impacted in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Insurance subsidiaries plan to seek forbearance and transition to Ind AS from 1st April 2027
items.quote: Accordingly, both our insurance companies plan to seek forbearance for a year and would transition to Ind AS from 1st of April 2027.

items.statement: Completed buyback of balance 3% Allianz stake in March, making insurance businesses 100% Bajaj-owned
items.quote: I am happy to confirm that in March, our insurance subsidiaries, that is Bajaj General and Bajaj Life, have completed the buyback of the balance 3% Allianz stake, making our insurance businesses now 100% Bajaj- Made in India, Made for India, and Made by India.

items.statement: Bajaj General combined ratio elevated at 113.6% in Q4 due to retro treaty timing; full-year combined ratio healthy at 101.9%
items.quote: The combined ratio for the quarter was elevated at about 113.6% for the quarter as against 104.8% for the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Bajaj General ROE excluding surplus capital stands close to 18.5%
items.quote: The ROE excluding surplus capital, which is at about 200% solvency, stands close to 18.5% for the period.

items.statement: Bajaj Life VNB grew 29% to INR 709 crores; NBM expanded to 24.5% from 22.1%
items.quote: Our VNB for the quarter grew at a very healthy 29% up from INR 549 crores to about INR 709 crores for the quarter. The NBM is for the quarter up to 24.5% as against 22.1% reported for the same period last year, an expansion of about absolute 2.4%.

items.statement: Bajaj Life targets stable product mix: PAR ~25%, non-par plus annuity 25-30%, term 10%+, ULIP ~40%
items.quote: we have always maintained that we would want to have, you know, a PAR at about 25% plus-minus, annuity plus non-par savings again in the 25% to 30% range, term we would aspire to be 10% plus, and ULIP will be about 40%.

items.statement: Bajaj Life expects higher growth than H2 FY26; agency channel growth trajectory positive
items.quote: You should see a better growth than what you saw in our second half. That much I can say. And all our businesses are in now a growth trajectory.

items.statement: Bajaj Housing Finance GNPA 0.27%, NNPA 0.11%
items.quote: Healthy asset quality continued to be maintained with GNPA and NNPA at a very small 0.27% and 0.11% respectively.

items.statement: Bajaj Finance investing in AI implementation and accelerated gold loan branch expansion
items.quote: have also been investing in AI implementation and that also impacts the ratios to some level. However, we are seeing acceleration in both growth and improvement in operating efficiencies due to the AI investments we've been making.

items.statement: Bajaj Housing Finance AUM grew 22.7% with growth across home loans (18%), LAP (24%), LRD (44%), developer finance (13%)
items.quote: A stable quarter with AUM growth of 22.7% driven by good momentum in disbursements amidst higher portfolio attrition. Growth was very well distributed across all the business segments. Home loans for the company grew at about 18%, loan against property grew 24%, lease rental discounting grew 44%, and developer finance grew 13%.

items.statement: Global consumption-driven economy supportive; no lead indicators of slowdown, only temporary inventory correction

Unlike the disruption during COVID where there was a dip in the consumption, this disruption has not caused a dip, rather a boost in consumption.

items.statement: Transitioning to value-added: premium PP yarns, special fabrics, non-woven technical textiles (automotive, geo-textiles, artificial leather)

items.statement: FIBC remains core (food/agri 52%, industrial 23%, construction 12%, automotive 7%, mining 6%) with growing value-added share
items.quote: From an end-user perspective, our revenues are well-diversified across sectors such as food and agriculture 52%, industrial packaging 23%, construction 12%, automotive 7% and mining and building materials 6%.

items.statement: Deep long-term relationships: significant revenue from repeat clients >20 years; diversified across geographies and industries
items.quote: A key strength of our business is the depth of our customer relationships, while a significant portion of our revenues coming from our repeat clients, many of whom have been associated with us for over 20 years.

items.statement: Export diversification: Europe 56.5%, South America 21.8%, North America 16.9% of exports in FY26

items.statement: Geopolitical risks managed through diversified supplier/customer base and long-term partnerships; agility demonstrated across multiple crises

items.statement: Evaluating M&A proposals in India and abroad; no near- to mid-term deals visible; focus remains on capex and dividend payout
items.quote: Of course, we keep evaluating certain M&A proposals and opportunities inside India and outside of India. So if something really aligns with our strategy, definitely, we will like to invest in that. But so far, there is nothing that we can see in the near to mid term.

items.statement: Hedging mechanism for both copper (100% imported) and aluminium; backward integration for XLPE/compounds (purchase raw resins, compound in-house); comfortable inventory for Q1 FY27; diversified vendor base for resins/compounds; no raw mater
items.quote: thanks to the backward integration that we have, we typically purchase only the raw resins, and we do compounding in-house. So thanks to our heavy inventory, we are comfortable for possibly in the first quarter of coming year as well.

items.statement: Transmission line execution expected to rise to 21,000-22,000 circuit km/year (vs 15,000 km avg 2015-2025); every INR 100 spent on T&D translates to 15-20% cable demand; power sector ~40-45% of cable consumption, manufacturing/private indus
items.quote: Today, going forward, the anticipation is that it should go to 21,000 - 22,000 circuit kilometers per year. Now so much of renewable capacity is getting added. All of this has also to connect with the transmission and distribution space.

items.statement: Middle East escalation impacted exports (16% of FY26 export revenue) and domestic trade sentiment in March; crude at ~$100/bbl, INR at record low 94.83/USD to pressure inflation; RBI likely extended pause; high-frequency indicators (air tra
items.quote: The sharp rise in crude oil prices and depreciation of the Indian rupee, which hit a record low of INR 94.83 per USD will exert upward pressure on inflation in the quarters ahead. CPI is also expected to edge higher, and the RBI is likely to remain on an extended pause.

items.statement: BEE norm changes caused temporary channel inventory adjustments in fans; government capex on track (86% of revised budget spent by Feb 2026); RDSS and rooftop solar schemes driving demand; Union Budget INR 12.2 lakh cr capex for FY27
items.quote: the Union Budget, which was announced in February, a very strong INR 12.2 lakh crores budget announced, which, again, if you add private capex to that, we see today around INR 36 lakh crores, INR 37 lakh crores to be invested in FY27.

items.statement: Non-MF revenue growth target of 20%+ for FY27
items.quote: We feel that this is kind of keeping in line with our projections that you will see the non-mutual fund business grow more than 20 percentage.

items.statement: KRA revenue expected to be flat in FY27 after price cut and NSE KRA addition
items.quote: So we will keep about flat revenue. I would not read a lot more into this. I'm expecting that the KRA machinery continues to kind of grow with the industry and enable the industry a lot more.

items.statement: Aim to retain Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin level of ~46.5% in FY27
items.quote: our aim is to at least re tain what we are in Q4, right, in terms of the EBITDA margins for next year

items.statement: Non-MF EBITDA margin target of 20% by end of FY27
items.quote: On a sustainable basis, we have said that we will get to a 20% margin by the end of next year. I think we are on target for that, too.

items.statement: Expect revenue growth on falling headcount in FY27
items.quote: And our belief is that in FY '27, we will see all the revenue growth on falling headcount, some bit of fall, which means we may choose not to do some backfill.

items.statement: Opex growth target sub-9% for FY27 with employee cost growth sub-5%
items.quote: We will look at a sub-5% and overall, definitely sub 9% kind of a growth in expenses.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin at 46.5%, up from 45% YoY
items.quote: Percentage EBITDA climbed back to just in excess of 46%, about 46.5%.

items.statement: Non-MF EBITDA margin at 16.5% in Q4 FY26, up from 12-13% range
items.quote: This quarter, they are upwards of 16 percentage. So I think on a sustainable basis, we have said that we will get to a 20% margin by the end of next year.

items.statement: Cost increase contained at 9% YoY including depreciation, 7.8% excluding depreciation
items.quote: if you see the actual numbers on a year -on-year basis, including the depreciation increase because of the additional investments, my cost increase has bee n 9 percentage. And if you actually remove the depreciation, the cost increase has actually been only 7.8

items.quote: New SIP registrations went up to about 1.26 crores. Our typical baseline number is about 1 crores to 1.1 crores in a quarter. This was a significantly higher number than 4Q last year, grew about 46%. Industry grew 27%.

items.quote: SIP collections crossed the INR20,000 crores milestone in the month of March, grew 25% year-on-year and almost touched INR59,000 crores for the quarter. And this is about 17% up year-on-year, while compared with 4% for the industry.

items.statement: MF AUM at INR 55.1 lakh crore, up 21% YoY with 68% market share
items.quote: From a mutual fund business perspective, AUM at INR55.1 lakh crores is obviously significantly lower than the INR58.5 lakh crores that we achieved at some time in 4Q, but because of the impact of what's happening in the Middle East, it came down. However, this represents a 21% year-on-year growth and holding 68% overall share.

items.quote: KRA now decisively be the number 2 player, leapfrog from being number 3 about 1.5 years back to number 2.

We certainly want to scale it even faster, but at 15.3% it's kind of underscoring all the diversification that we have tried to do in a very focused manner in the last 4 years.

Obviously, there was a reaction from the industry, not for a day or 2, but for a long time that in order to broaden the franchise and bring in lower-value consumers.

items.statement: MF yield compression <1% QoQ in Q4 FY26, entirely due to passive mix shift; individual asset class yields stable
items.quote: And if you actually see our yield, the compression on a quarter-on-quarter basis has been less than 1%. And if you drill down further, I think you can very clearly see that this is entirely -- I'm not saying 50%, 25%, but this is entirely because of the impact of the mix, which is that you have seen the passives grow over the last quarter more than what the active funds have grown.

items.statement: No material yield renegotiation expected with AMCs; passive yields already at very low levels
items.quote: I don't think there's any room for us to kind of have any renegotiation on that given that it's actually at really low levels now. So as the passive increase, there will be some impact on the mix and there will be some impact on the yield, but it will be very muted.

items.statement: Final dividend of INR 4/share declared; FY26 total dividend payout INR 305 crore
items.quote: And the Board has declared, subject to confirmation by shareholders, a final dividend of INR 4 which means for the year, we'll be disbursing a revenue of INR305 crores.

items.statement: Retail participation, SIP flows, and investor base continue to expand structurally
items.quote: Despite these headwinds, retail participation, SIP flow, and the broader investor base in India continue to expand structurally, reinforcing the long-term opportunity in our markets.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded 250 bps YoY to 17.4% in Q4 FY26

items.quote: We want to be transparent with our investors that FY26 our margin compressed at the consolidated level on a full -year basis. items.statement: Upgraded insurance broking category from direct broker to composite broker, enabling reinsurance segment entry
items.quote: A key strategic development during the year was the upgrade of our category from di rect broker to composite broker, which now allowed us to expand into the reinsurance segment as well.

items.statement: Finance costs rose to INR 221.3 crore in FY26, driving margin compression
items.quote: The two principal drivers of this margin compression were higher consolidated finance costs of INR 221.3 crores and the calibrated approach in our financing, segment and reduction in net gain on fair value changes.

items.quote: Our broking client base, including Stoxkart grew to 13.39 lakh accounts as of FY26

items.statement: Expects commodity broking share to keep increasing due to regulator support, new products, and retail participation
items.quote: It should gradually because worldwide commodity business is much larger even as compared to equity business and even our regulator is very proactively wants that co mmodity segment should grow

items.statement: SEBI issued circulars easing compliance for stockbrokers; RBI direction on bank exposure to capital market intermediaries reshaping funding landscape

items.statement: RBI circular on NBFC leverage for proprietary trading expected to have minimal impact as surplus funds deployed in arbitrage are sufficiently capitalized
items.quote: we have checked and we are sure that whatever funds are required for our current level of arbitrage, those funds are available with us as we are sufficiently capitalized. So, there would be minimal impact or rather very negligible impact or maybe no impact on our operations.

items.statement: NBFC borrowing mix: bank borrowings 85% in FY26 (up from 79%); raised INR 25 crore fresh NCDs; broking entity raised INR 150 crore NCDs
items.quote: On the borrowing side, our NBFC continues to maintain a well -diversified borrowing mix with bank borrowings forming 85% of the mix in FY26 up from 79% in FY25. Our borrowing program is supported by ICRA A- stable rating on the long-term bank loan and CARE A- stable and IVR A-stable rating on our NCD program.

items.statement: Consolidated debt-to-equity at 1.53x; consolidated net worth INR 1,304 crore

items.quote: there are certain large secured accounts, which are classified as GNPA and we have sufficient security available with us for the recovery. However, the legal process or the settlement process is taking some time.

items.statement: NBFC NIM moderated to 7.3% from 8.2% in FY25 due to elevated funding costs

items.statement: Financing business deliberately calibrated disbursements in unsecured and microfinance segments due to industry-wide stress; normalization emerging in Q4 FY26

As a result, most participants, ourselves included, deliberately calibrated disbursements and prioritized secured lending segments.

items.quote: So I mean, just to give you a rough idea in terms of the top line, what we are expecting is somewhere close to around 20% to 22% growth in FY '27 because like I said, the U.S. market has been sort of been slow because of the geopolitical issues.

items.quote: So if I talk of the CapEx first, then we are, I think, left with around -- from the IPO proceeds, somewhere around INR35 crores, INR36 crores of CapEx, which we intend to utilize in this financial year.

items.statement: No traditional order book; business driven by customer planning and ODM design wins; visibility of ~6 months

items.quote: So our working capital cycle is, if I have to give a generic statement is as per in line with our other businesses. So in terms of numbers, I can say that it is around 60 to 75 days.

items.statement: Raw material prices rising (aluminum, copper); ODM flexibility allows design changes to mitigate supply chain disruptions
items.quote: Prices are definitely going up because as -- if you are following the industry, so metals have gone up like aluminum, copper, everything is -- the prices are rising.

For the full-year, EBITDA stood at INR789.1 crores, up 61.8% year-on-year

items.quote: FMEG there are some impact what we have planned to achieve breakeven in March 2026 could not be achieved. There were two major reasons. items.statement: Raw material prices (copper, aluminium, PVC) volatile; currency and freight added pressure; timely pricing actions and disciplined procurement critical

items.statement: Wire volume growth expected ~11-12%; cable volume growth expected ~25% over next two years driven by B2B, infrastructure, data centers, renewables, export
items.quote: If you see at a smaller level than in cable, we see higher growth when I compare to wire side for next two years. If I can figure out like in wire our growth may remain around 11%-12%, while in cable we, since our base is small, we are expecting growth of 25% in terms of volumes.

items.statement: New entrants acknowledged but confident in quality, brand, distribution, export and B2B focus to maintain above-industry growth

items.statement: Balance sheet and working capital position remained healthy; tight control on inventory and receivables
items.quote: Our balance sheet and working capital position remained healthy during the year, supported by tight control on inventory and receivables.

items.statement: Target 70% secured assets by March 2027
items.quote: We remain on track to achieve our stated target of 70% secured assets by March 2027.

items.statement: Steady-state credit cost of 2% expected from FY28

items.statement: Target ROA of 2% by FY28

items.statement: Steady-state loan growth of 20-25%

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio guidance of 55% plus or minus 2%

items.statement: Steady-state NIM of 7% plus or minus 0.5%

items.statement: ESAF 2.0 StratoNeXt digital transformation to complete before Q3 FY27
items.quote: We are making steady progress on the same and expect the implementation to be completed well before end of this calendar year i.e. before Q3 FY 27.

items.statement: Full-year disbursements of INR 42,530 crore, up 103% YoY

items.statement: 82% of total disbursements towards secured assets

items.statement: Q4 FY26 NIM improved to 7.3% from 6.6% previous quarter

items.statement: Pre-provisioning operating profit up 166% YoY to INR 241 crore
items.quote: Pre-provisioning operating profit stood at INR 241 crore, up 166% year-on-year, driven by business growth and higher fee income.

items.statement: GNPA declined to 5.4% from 6.9% YoY
items.quote: GNPA declined to 5.4% from 6.9%, and NNPA declined to 1.8% from 3.0% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Slippages reduced to INR 106 crore from INR 427 crore YoY
items.quote: Slippages reduced significantly to INR 106 crore, compared to INR 427 crore in Q4 last year.

items.statement: Slippage ratio improved from 10.5% in FY25 to 6.5% in FY26
items.quote: Our slippage ratio on a gross basis reduced from 10.5% for FY 25 to 6.5% for FY 26.

items.statement: Credit cost improved from 6.7% in FY25 to 4.7% in FY26
items.quote: Credit cost came down from 6.7% in FY 25 to 4.7% in FY 26.

items.statement: No ARC sales or technical write-offs in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Notably, there were no ARC sales or technical write-offs during the quarter, reflecting underlying portfolio stability.

items.statement: Secured loan mix improved to 61% from 53% YoY

items.statement: MARG advances grew 47% YoY with Gold and Mortgage loans each over 50%
items.quote: Overall, MARG advances grew by 47% year-on-year, with Gold loans and Mortgage loans each delivering growth of over 50%.

items.statement: Microfinance book stable at INR 8,746 crore, share reduced to 39% from 47%
items.quote: On the advances side, our microfinance book remained stable at INR 8,746 crore as of March 2026. The secured loan mix improved to 61%, compared to 53% last year, driven by the continued scaling of the MARG portfolio.

items.statement: Crossed 10 million customers with strong women borrower representation
items.quote: During the year, we c rossed a milestone of 10 million customers with a strong representation of women borrowers

items.statement: Retail deposits at 92% of total deposits, 88% of bulk deposits have non-prepayment clause
items.quote: On the liability side, retail deposits remained strong at 92% of total deposits, compared to 93% last year. Further, 88% of bulk deposits carry a non-prepayment clause, providing stability to our funding base.

items.statement: LCR at 143.35% as of March 2026
items.quote: Our Liquidity Coverage Ratio stood at 143.35% as of 31st March 2026, indicating a comfortable liquidity position.

items.statement: CASA ratio at 23.9%, up 7% YoY to INR 6,181 crore
items.quote: CASA balances grew to INR 6,181 crore, up 7% year-on-year, with a CASA ratio of 23.9%.
