items.quote: As of March 31, 2026, total deposits stood at INR 25,850 crore, registering a year-on-year growth of 11% over INR 23,276 crore, with a credit-deposit ratio of 83.5%.

items.statement: Geopolitical developments remain a watchpoint for microfinance sector
items.quote: While external factors, including geopolitical developments, remain a watchpoint, we believe the sector is now on a more stable trajectory.

items.statement: Guided for double-digit organic revenue growth in FY27 in constant currency, excluding inorganic contribution from ES-Tec.
items.quote: We continue to expect double-digit organic top-line growth, excluding any inorganic contribution from ES-Tec, and we expect to exit FY27 with an operating margin run rate that exceeds 18%.

items.statement: Closed two Full Vehicle Programs in Q3 and Q4; expects at least two more to close in next 8-12 weeks, each multi-year, multi-domain, tens of millions of dollars.
items.period: Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26, next 8-12 weeks
items.quote: Today, we have visibility into multiple Full Vehicle Programs across our pipeline. Two of these were closed during Q3 and Q4, and we expect at least another 2 to close over the next 8 to 12 weeks.

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margin at 16%, up ~200 bps sequentially from Q3, reflecting operating leverage and disciplined cost management.
items.quote: From a profitability standpoint, our EBITDA margin for the quarter came in at 16%, representing a roughly 200 basis points improvement from Q3.

items.statement: Broad-based Q4 growth across Automotive (13.6% QoQ USD), Aerospace & IHM (4.6% QoQ), Technology Solutions (12% QoQ); Education up 36% QoQ.
items.quote: Growth was broad-based across services, supported by deal ramp-ups, normalization at a few large customer engagements, and improving decision velocity across OEMs, particularly in Automotive, which grew 13.6% over Q3 in U.S. dollar terms.

items.statement: Won 4 large deals in Q4 and 2 in April, including Full Vehicle Program with Japanese OEM, PLM transformation with European luxury OEM, and strategic engagements with North American and European OEMs.
items.quote: Deal activity remained strong during the quarter with the closure of 4 large deals in Q4, followed by 2 milestone wins subsequent to the quarter end in April.

items.statement: Top 20 customers now account for ~88% of business; seeing C-suite influence and real influence across manufacturing customers' requirements.
items.quote: Our top 20 customers now make up almost 88% of our business. And what we're seeing through the investments that we've made and with the type of business that we are securing is real influence at the C-suite level.

items.statement: Deliberately protected delivery capacity and invested through downturn; headcount up 66 QoQ to 12,646; will remain selective in hiring aligned to growth priorities.
items.quote: At the end of the quarter, our total headcount stood at 12,646 associates, representing a net addition of 66 employees sequentially. This reflects our deliberate decision earlier in the cycle to protect and strengthen our delivery engine.

items.statement: Net cash position improved to INR 1,188 crore from INR 524 crore QoQ; total DSO improved to 95 days from 111 days; billed DSO 59 days, unbilled 36 days.
items.quote: At the end of the quarter, the net cash position stood at INR 1,188 crores compared to INR 524 crores at the end of Q3. Our collection efficiency improved during the quarter with total DSO, both billed and unbilled, coming in at 95 days at the end of March.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR 8.35/share and special dividend of INR 3.35/share, total INR 11.70/share for FY26, subject to shareholder approval.
items.quote: Our Board has recommended a final dividend of INR 8.35 per share for FY26, representing a payout of 62%. In addition, the Board has proposed a special dividend of INR 3.35 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR 11.70 per share.

items.statement: ES-Tec integration on track; cross-sell into VW and extension of services to existing customer base showing tangible progress and proof points.
items.quote: The post-merger integration plans with ES-Tec are very much on track. Both Uttam and I were in Wolfsburg a couple of weeks ago to assess not only the cross-sell opportunity that we're looking to drive at VW, but also to assess the synergies that we've got within the Tata Technologies customer base.

items.statement: Aerospace revenue at over $40 million annual run rate, grown 8x in 4 years; propelled by Airbus EMES3 program, propulsion manufacturers in North America, and Air India MRO in India.
items.quote: In the last 4 years, our Aerospace revenues have grown 8x and is now at over $40 million in terms of annual run rate. We expect the strong growth momentum to continue.

items.statement: Embedded Software revenue growing at 60% CAGR over last 3 years; portfolio mix improving with Mechanical, Digital, and Embedded capabilities.
items.quote: Revenue from our Embedded Software segment has grown at a solid 60% CAGR in the last 3 years.

items.quote: We are deploying AI across all of our delivery LOBs and across the enabling functions and have fairly aggressive targets in terms of the unit-cost of delivery in each of those areas.

items.statement: Middle East crisis may tighten discretionary customer spend via commodity supply chain impacts (aluminium, plastics), but not expected to impact capex or new product commitments; factored into guidance.
items.quote: I fully expect discretionary spend amongst our customers to tighten if the Middle East crisis continues to extend. Now having said that, I don't expect that to impact capex or indeed the commitments that are being made to new products.

items.statement: FY27 double-digit organic growth guidance based on order book and probability-adjusted pipeline, not factoring in demand environment improvement; expects consistency across quarters with faster H2 growth.
items.quote: Now the guidance that we've provided is very much driven by the order book that we have and the probability-adjusted pipeline that includes deals that we are very much in the process of trying to close. So, it's not factoring in any improvement to the demand environment.

items.statement: Reversed INR 56 crore of INR 140 crore exceptional provision for employee benefits under new India Labor Law after greater clarity on implementation.
items.quote: Upon further assessment and greater clarity on implementation, we determined that the actual impact would be lower than initially estimated. Accordingly, we reversed provisions amounting to INR 56 crores in Q4, resulting in a one-time exceptional gain for the quarter.

items.statement: Free cash flow generation of INR 742 crore in FY26 with 87% EBITDA-to-FCF conversion; strong balance sheet with solid cash position and robust liquidity.

items.statement: Targets $1 billion revenue North Star within next 2-3 years via sustained double-digit organic growth complemented by 1-2 inorganic transactions.
items.quote: If we can do that and we can sustain that next year, we can complement that with 1 or 2 inorganic transactions. I think within the next 2 to 3 years, we have the opportunity to get to where we need to get to.

items.quote: We have secured the electrolyser PLI for INR444 crores and hydrogen PLI for approx. INR510 crores.

items.statement: Domestic demand deferred due to ALMM II uncertainty; overseas orders delayed by Middle East disruption

items.statement: EBITDA guidance INR7,000-7,700 crores for FY27; 19-20% margin long-term; cell production 80-85% utilization on 15.4 GW in FY28

items.statement: Commodity price impact partially passing through; new orders factoring higher prices; export pricing 25-26 cents/Wp FOB vs domestic utility 16-17 cents/Wp

items.statement: Overseas revenue >90% from US; Europe, Africa, Middle East identified as next growth markets; 15-20% revenue from non-US/non-India in 3 years

First is the effect of inventory, higher inventory, which I also explained in my earlier reply that in the March ending quarters, the overall inventory has gone through the roof because of lower shipments for the overseas market.

items.statement: ROC remains top quartile despite working capital increase; capital allocation driven by 20-25% ROC/ROE hurdle
items.quote: Abhishek, just to add to while you're right on asking about the working capital, but we shouldn't take our eyes off the main true north is ROC and we see despite the rise in working capital, our ROC remains truly top quartile.

items.statement: Enabling resolution for fundraise over next couple of months; amount and objects to be clarified soon
items.quote: However, right now, we are taking the enabling resolution to do this fundraise over the next couple of months. We'll be soon coming out with the clarification on the amount, etc.

items.statement: IRA benefit $0.07/Wp; FY25 IRA benefit ~$40M at 87-88% conversion; multifold increase expected with new 2.6 GW US facility
items.quote: We have been getting IRA for $0.07 per watt peak against per watt peak of panels sold. There are some costs to incur when you convert that into cash. So, we factor around 87%-88% percent only of the eligible IRA. So last financial year, roughly around $40 million was our cumulative benefit from IRA.

items.statement: BESS economics: 18-20% margins without policy support; 20 GWh capacity; market price $110-120/MWh; India needs 60-80 GWh annually, 300 GWh cumulative over 5-7 years
items.quote: To explain it further, you expect the business to generate around 18 % to 20% margins without any support from the policy perspective or any MOAT of regulatory inculcated.

items.statement: C&I and utility buyers prioritize warranty servicing over 25-30 years; banks funding projects with visible OEM track record; survival-mode pricing not sustainable
items.quote: So, you may expect some cases wherein the players who are in the race or mode of survival may even get down to any point of price that can't be ignored. But fact here is the buyers, the C&I , be the utilities, anyone, are looking for suppliers who are able to demonstrate warranty servicing over the next 30 years.

items.statement: No supply-demand imbalance foreseen for 5-10 years; ALMM regulations align capacity with demand; oversupply only in lower-efficiency modules where Waaree doesn't play
items.quote: So, we really don't foresee any scenario anytime next 5, 10 years of time will be the supply is going to be much higher than demand. Yes, we foresee a balance between supply and demand.

items.statement: Jignesh Rathod appointed CEO; transition from Waaree 1.0 to 2.0; export team built for Italy (3 people, 2 more joining)
items.quote: We have built an export team dedicated to Italy with three people and two more are joining.

items.statement: APSL (T&D) acquisition integrated; EPC business combined with T&D arm to capture market share in India and overseas
items.quote: In fact, on top of it, EPC company with an acquisition of transmission and distribution arm, APSL, will be also available to capture a good amount of share in the market of EPC in India and overseas as well.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions delaying Middle East orders; ALMM II timeline uncertainty; commodity price volatility; working capital pressure from inventory build
items.quote: Last quarter, largely because of the disruption in the Middle East. The new order from the overseas market have deferred from maybe a quarter to a quarter's time.

items.statement: EL platform commercialization expected before end of calendar year 2025 (festive season)
items.quote: We believe by this festive would be a good timeline for the products to come out.

items.statement: Factory 3.0 Phase 1 trial production by end of calendar year 2025, full 42,000 units/month operational by end of FY27
items.quote: We are expecting commencement of trial productions by before end of this calendar year, likely around festive or just around that timeline. And the full 42,000 should be operationalized before end of this FY for sure.

items.statement: AGM improved 5pp YoY to 24% with subsidy, 9pp to 21% without subsidy in FY26; COGS reduced ~9pp
items.quote: Unit economics, we've entered the FY -- we've ended FY '26 at a great place, improving our AGM by about 5 percentage points. This is with subsidy, up from 19% to 24%. Without subsidy, margin improvement has been even sharper, from 12 percentage AGM to 21 percentage AGM and this has been driven by a consistent reduction in COGS, which reduced by about 9 percentage through the course of FY '26.

items.statement: EBITDA loss narrowed ~1500-1600bps YoY in FY26; Q4 EBITDA loss improved 2000bps to -2%
items.quote: We saw more than a 1500-1600 bps improvement in EBITDA losses from FY '25 to FY '26, with Q4 being an incredible 2,000 bps improvement in EBITDA losses, with EBITDA losses coming down from 23% to about negative 2%.

items.statement: Lithium carbonate prices rose from $8/kg to ~$24/kg (2-2.5x); NMC commodity basket up 30-50%; cell cost up 30-50% depending on procurement timing
items.quote: Lithium particularly was a pretty crazy commodity, has been a pretty crazy commodity, going up from I think a base of $8 per kilogram to about $24 per kilogram in a very short span of time. It's cooled down a little since then, but Yes, it's still up more than 2x to 2.5x.

items.statement: Volumes up 66% YoY in FY26; Q4 volume 83,000 units; Rizta ~75% of sales
items.quote: Overall volumes are up almost 66%, with Q4 itself delivering 83,000 units, which is almost 80% of the volume that we did just a couple of years ago. And a large part of this, in fact, I would say almost all of this growth is ascribed down to the new product Rizta, which has grown remarkably well and today is almost three-quarters of our sales.

items.statement: Pro-Pack attach rate reached 93% in Q4 FY26 (highest ever); South ~98-99%, Middle India ~85-90%, Rest of India 81%; new stores ramp to 80%+ within 2-4 quarters
items.quote: Pro-Pack attach rates not only have held steady, they've actually gone up, with Q4 FY '26 being the highest ever Pro-Pack attach rate at 93%.

items.statement: Strategic sourcing, pre-buying, inventory planning and LFP chemistry adoption mitigated commodity spikes in FY26; multi-chemistry (LFP, NMC, NCA) and multi-vendor approach for de-risking
items.quote: What we did was a lot of work in strategic sourcing, pre-buying, and inventory planning, which is what allowed us to sidestep or at least push out a lot of these hits in FY '26. Engineering for alternate technologies, for example, like LFP, which allowed us to mellow down or even again buy our way out of the spike in lithium-ion battery prices overall.

items.statement: Charging network: 6,000+ LECCS fast charging points; charging sessions growing faster than charger count; positive unit economics with line of sight to standalone EBITDA positivity
items.quote: We now have more than 6,000 fast charging points on the LECCS standard across the country. And in the recent years, the number of charging sessions on public fast chargers has compounded faster than the total number of chargers, which is a really positive thing for the underlying unit economics of these fast chargers, one that already obviously has had positive unit economics and we believe will h

items.statement: LECCS charging standard adopted by 20+ OEMs, CPOs, suppliers via LEAF consortium; targeting national and international standardization
items.quote: There are more than 20 plus stakeholders of OEMs, CPOs, and suppliers and providers who've joined the newly created consortium called LEAF, which is now pushing this as not just a national but also soon an international charging standard.

items.statement: Factory 3.0 at AURIC (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar) with higher vertical integration (battery pack, transmission, painting, electronics, CED coating in-house); logistics advantage for Middle/North India markets
items.quote: This plant, apart from it driving the bulk of EL's growth in the coming quarters, it also will help unit economics because it has higher vertical integration than what Ather does today, with battery pack assembly, transmission assembly, painting, electronics assembly, and CED coating coming in-house.

items.statement: R&D filing 283 patents in FY26 (643 total); AtherStack 7 launched with Infinite Cruise, Vernacular Dashboards, pothole detection
items.quote: R&D firing on full gear, 643 patents filed till date with 283 patents filed just in FY '26 alone. We also launched AtherStack 7 in FY '26, which had a lot of new features like Infinite Cruise, Vernacular Dashboards, pothole detection, so on and so forth.

items.statement: Other financial assets increased due to IPO proceeds in fixed deposits and nominal Maharashtra state subsidy receivables; FAME/PM E-DRIVE subsidies coming regularly
items.quote: So, that is largely the fixed deposits or the term deposits as we call it, which is the IPO money sitting there. Pooja Seth: And is there anything because of the EV subsidy receivables that we used to get? Sohil Parekh: Yes, that also sits there, but that's a very nominal sum because all the FAME-related incentives or the PM E -DRIVE is coming in regularly. Only the Maharashtra state subsidy, whic

items.statement: FY27 guidance: around 50% top-line growth and 50% plus bottom-line growth
items.quote: In coming financial year '27, we hope to continue to maintain the growth trajectory, and we see around 50% top-line growth and 50% plus bottom-line growth.

items.statement: Nuts EBITDA target 15%+ and PAT 10%+ for next two years
items.quote: So the way we look at going forward is that in the short term, in the coming next two years, we will try to maintain this 15% plus EBITDA and 10% plus PAT.

items.statement: Ice cream EBITDA target 14-15% at full capacity utilization by Q1 FY29
items.quote: Our expectation is the ideally 3 years down the line when the full capacity utilization happens, then EBITDA should be 14% to 15% minimum.

items.statement: Ice cream PAT margin minimum 3% in FY27
items.quote: And the PAT in FY26, PAT was almost 1.7% or 1.8%. So PAT will also enhance beyond 3% minimum, I'm saying this conservatively, minimum on that.

items.statement: 2 lakh sq ft factory under construction at Halkarni MIDC; 35,000 sq ft operational adding 10 MT/day nuts capacity
items.quote: And our plan is that in the coming next two financial years further. So slowly this capacity we will keep adding, like 10 to -- we have gone 20 this year, next year we'll go 30, and again next year we'll reach 40.

items.statement: Nuts capacity: 10 MT/day (FY26) -> 20 MT/day (now) -> 30 MT/day (FY27) -> 40 MT/day (FY28)
items.quote: Our earlier capacity as of March 31, FY26 was 10 metric tons per day finished nuts production. This capacity has been enhanced as on today to 20 metric tons per day finished nuts production.

items.statement: Ice cream capacity 1 lakh litres/day; target full utilization by Q1 FY29
items.quote: We'll keep enhancing capacity utilization; our existing capacity is 1 lakh litres per day in ice cream, so we'll continue to enhance the capacity utilization with a target of full capacity utilization by Q1 FY '29.

items.statement: Nuts utilization: FY26 70% on 10 MT/day; FY27 90% on old + 25% on new 10 MT/day
items.quote: In FY26, our existing capacity, as I have spoken in the earlier call also, 70% was the utilization of the existing capacity. And this financial year, the existing capacity 10 metric ton will be utilized almost fully -- so fully means we can have a 90% utilization with some balance space available. And the new capacity of 10 metric ton will be utilized 25%.

items.statement: Ice cream utilization FY26 ~25%; Q1/Q4 seasonally higher
items.quote: Around in ice cream side, the utilization in FY26 is 25% -- almost you can say 25%.

items.statement: Melt N Mellow retail outlets 34,200 with 15,490 deep freezers; nuts 11,000 touchpoints; footprint 300+ towns in India and 300+ in Singapore
items.quote: Melt N Mellow now reaches 34,200 retail outlets, supported by a cold chain network of 15,490 deep freezers, enabling deeper market penetration and stronger last-mile availability.

items.statement: Deep freezer network to expand further in FY27; 25 FOCO parlours (Mellow & Co.) to open in Pune and Mumbai starting July-August
items.quote: The deep freezer network we have already expanded from 3,000+ to 15,000+ during FY '26. This continuous investment in deep freezers will further continue and expand in the current financial year, that is FY '27.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated: revenue INR304.41 cr (+48% YoY), EBITDA INR41.95 cr (+66%, 13.78% margin), PAT INR22.2 cr (+64%, 7.59% margin, +89 bps)
items.quote: Coming to our financial performance for the full year, total revenue stood at INR304.41 crores., reflecting a growth of 48% year-on-year. EBITDA increased by 66% to INR41.95 crores with a margin of 13.78%, while the profit after tax, PAT increased to INR22.2 crores with a growth of 64% year -on-year and a PAT margin of 7.59%, which is up 89 basis points year -on-year.

items.statement: Nuts FY26: 15% EBITDA margin, 10% PAT margin
items.quote: So we, if you can see our financials in FY26, we have achieved 15% EBITDA margin -- 15%. And 10% is the PAT margin.

items.statement: Ice cream FY26: 7% EBITDA margin on INR95 cr revenue; 1.7-1.8% PAT margin
items.quote: This year, 7% EBITDA on a top line of INR 95 crores has been achieved, which is ahead of our planned profitability which was planned in FY '27.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin 12.21% adjusted for INR2.88 cr ESOP cost (vs 12.03% Q4 FY25)
items.quote: So if you take our EBITDA in Q4 FY26, which is including this adjusted to this ESOP expenses, then our EBITDA margin is 12.21% in Q4 FY26. And the EBITDA margin in Q4 25 was 12.03%.

items.statement: Nuts pricing power from Tier 2/3/4 distribution and in-house processing drives consistent margins
items.quote: And there we give -- and that gives pricing power. In Nuts segment, the pricing power which Krishival has is one of the strength which Krishival is having. And that has translated into this consistent margin in the nuts segment.

items.statement: Ice cream raw material cost spike in Q4 due to seasonally high ice cream sales mix (INR43 cr in Q4 vs INR47 cr in 9M)
items.quote: So Q4 has -- this year's Q4 has a peculiarity of enhanced ice cream operations. So almost the first 9 months' ice cream sale is INR47 crores, and last three months' ice cream sale is almost INR43 crores.

items.statement: Ice cream SKUs 189 (3rd highest in India); nuts SKUs 67; premium ice cream SKUs launched in May to reduce seasonality
items.quote: We also continue to expand our product portfolio with over 189 SKUs in ice cream, which is almost the third highest among the ice cream brands in India, and over 67 SKUs in nuts and dry fruits, reflecting our focus on innovation and evolving consumer preferences.

items.statement: Ice cream demand >50% from Maharashtra; rest from Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Goa; metros: Mumbai, Pune, Hyderabad, Bengaluru
items.quote: So, the deep freezer expansion is going across these five states: Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and Goa. If you want to see a major metro -wise how it is proportioned, so Mumbai, Pune, Hyderabad, and Bengaluru t-- these are the four metros which are being targeted or focused upon.

items.statement: Nuts: integrated sourcing/processing is barrier; large FMCG entrants cannot easily replicate quality assurance at scale
items.quote: In the nuts, the most important thing is that from the January to December, customer should get a assured quality of nut, which is possible only if there is strength in sourcing. So what I feel is that in India, unless there is a back end of sourcing, proc essing in-house, you cannot give a quality nut on table to the customer

items.statement: Nuts and ice cream working capital cycles complementary (nuts peak offsets ice cream slack)
items.quote: there is a working capital cycle of nuts and dry fruits is very complementary. When there is a peak of nuts, then there is some slack period in ice cream, right? And that gives a very good complementary positioning for working capital

items.statement: Expansion funded by internal accruals, existing equity, and debt; rights issue INR100 cr (INR35 cr received Jan, INR25 cr for nuts plant, INR10 cr nuts WC)
items.quote: Our expansion will continue to be funded through a mix of internal accruals, existing equity, and debt.

items.statement: Rights issue INR100 cr: first call INR35 cr received (INR25 cr nuts plant, INR10 cr nuts WC); INR65 cr in two further calls this calendar year
items.quote: Now the rights issue which we have raised in INR100 crores recently, out of that INR35 crores first tranche we received in the month of January. And this INR35 cr ores, INR25 crores is for these new facility in the first question which I said , the 2 lakh square foot factory unit is being constructed along with for the nuts division over there

items.statement: ESOP cost INR2.88 cr in Q4 FY26; FY27 ESOP cost will be less than FY26
items.quote: FY27, certain ESOP costs will be there that we have not yet worked out. But obviously, it will not be more than this.

items.statement: Ice cream volume FY26: Magic Cones 4.74 cr units, Chocobar 3.5 cr units, Cups/Sundaes 1.78 cr units
items.quote: We have sold Magic Cones around 4.74 crore units we have sold in financial year '26. Around 3.5 crores units of Chocobar we have sold in FY '26, around 1.78 crores units of cups and sundaes we have sold in FY '26.

items.statement: Near-term input cost and supply chain volatility for globally sourced commodities; diversified sourcing model mitigates structural impact
items.quote: There is some near -term volatility in input costs and supply chains, particularly for globally sourced commodities; however, our diversified sourcing model positions us well to manage these risks, and we do not see any structural impact on our growth trajectory.

items.statement: Core lead-acid business expected to grow high single-digit to early double-digit in FY27
items.quote: I would still believe that the core business at this situation has a potential to do at least a high single-digit to early-double digit growth.

items.statement: Medium-term CAGR for core business expected around 11% over next five years
items.quote: If you see, the five-year CAGR was 11%. And I don't see any reason for the next five-year CAGR to be different from that, (+/-1%) maybe.

items.statement: Board approved Rs. 1,400 crore investment in Exide Energy Solutions for FY27 covering capex and opex working capital
items.quote: we have already got a Board approval and this has been announced in the past of investing Rs. 1400 crore in the Fiscal Year '27, which is a mix of both CAPEX as well as the OPEX working capital requirement which we have to fund.

items.statement: Total equity investment in Exide Energy Solutions stands at Rs. 4,802 crore till date
items.quote: With this, the total equity investment made in Exide Energy, our subsidiary till date, stands at Rs. 4,802 crores.

items.statement: Cylindrical lines expected to start customer sample delivery around this month; prismatic line to initiate product trials shortly thereafter
items.quote: Our cylindrical lines are expected to start customer sample delivery by around this month onwards, while the prismatic line will be initiating product trials shortly thereafter.

items.statement: Phase-I lithium-ion cell manufacturing capacity is 6 GWh split equally between 3 GWh cylindrical (NMC) and 3 GWh prismatic (LFP)
items.quote: So, our capacity is divided cylindrical in 3 and prismatic in 3 gigawatts.

items.statement: Domestic demand favorable in H2 FY26 driven by low inflation, low interest rates, GST 2.0 reforms and rural revival
items.quote: Low inflation rates, low interest rates and the consequence of GST 2.0 Reforms increased end-consumers' affordability, especially in the second half of FY26. Rural India experienced strong broad-based revival as well, driven by rising income, upbeat sentiment and infrastructure development.

items.statement: Auto OEM business grew 25% YoY for second consecutive quarter in Q4 FY26, hitting highest-ever quarterly revenue
items.quote: The GST 2.0-led demand surge continued in Q4, as auto OEM business recorded its second consecutive quarter of (+25%) year-on-year growth, also hitting its highest-ever quarterly revenue, breaking the mark set in Q3.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin maintained sequentially at 11.7% despite 90 bps gross margin decline due to commodity inflation
items.quote: The Company was also able to maintain, on a sequential quarter basis, the EBITDA margin of 11.7%, buoyed by strong volume growth, improved product mix, and better realization, which was also helped a lot by various manufacturing excellence projects.

items.statement: Gross margin declined 90 bps QoQ from 31.6% in Q3 to 30.1% in Q4 due to Rs. 150 crore net negative material cost impact
items.quote: the gross margin, if you see, has come down by about 90 basis points. Though we have been able to improve our EBITDA but even if you see quarter-on-quarter movement, the gross margin has come down from, let's say, it was in Q3, it was 31.6 and in Q4, in the last quarter, it was 30.1.

items.statement: Price increases of 5-6% taken in aftermarket across three tranches in Jan, Mar, Apr 2026 to pass through commodity inflation
items.quote: from January onwards, we could not sustain the cost inflation of material. Therefore, we started taking price increases stage-by-stage. So, 1st January, 1st March, 20th March, I think in three tranches, we have taken increases which maybe amounts to about, let's say, about 5% to 6%- this varies on different businesses.

items.statement: Sulfur prices surged from Rs. 15/kg to Rs. 75/kg over trailing four quarters; April exit at Rs. 74/kg vs March exit at Rs. 58/kg
items.quote: Sulfur is a byproduct of the petrochemical refinery plants, right? And since the petrochemical refiners' plants are operating at a lower capacity utilization, because of crude shortage, even the generation of sulfur has also come down. And therefore, just to run the business, sulfuric acid costs have gone to Rs. 75 April exit, compared to Rs. 15 in the beginning of the year.

items.statement: Lead prices in India sold on import parity; 10% rupee depreciation offset LME softness, no net benefit on lead costs
items.quote: Lead as an index has been softer year-on-year. But, in India, lead is sold, even recycled leads and pure leads are sold on import parity prices. So, because the currency has softened by about 10%, the reduction in LME has been over offsetted by the Rupee depreciation.

items.statement: Polypropylene container costs hit in Q4 due to crude shortage; Q1-Q3 were stable
items.quote: Regarding plastics, because we use polypropylene containers, this was directly hit in Q4. Q1 to Q3 was pretty stable. But Q4, we got a hit because of shortage of crude, which is coming to India.

items.statement: Order inflow and execution healthy across railways, motive power and industrial UPS in industrial infrastructure segment
items.quote: Order in flow and execution remained healthy across sectors like railways, motive power, and industrial UPS.

items.statement: Exports declined to 5% of revenue from 8% few years ago; geopolitical tensions expected to impact exports for at least H1 FY27
items.quote: Geopolitical tensions continue to impact Exports business. We expect these uncertainties to remain for at least in the first half of this current year.

items.statement: Exports recovery expected in FY27 as baseline low; targeting Western Europe and US markets to regain 8% revenue share
items.quote: Exports was already 8% of our revenue a couple of years back. So, we came down to 5%. So, I think there's a good chance to increase our share of Exports and therefore the incremental revenue.

items.statement: Auto and non-auto revenue split roughly 53:47; auto replacement to non-auto ratio 70:30
items.quote: Auto and non-auto is almost half-half, roughly, or maybe 53:47, kind of. Auto is OEM and aftermarket put together is about 50%. And the ratio between auto replacement and non-auto, as you know, it's standard is 70:30, (+/-1%).

items.statement: Solar vertical crossed Rs. 1,000 crore full-year revenue for first time in FY26
items.quote: I am happy to inform you that we have incubated and nurtured this solar vertical for the last few years and this year they have crossed the Rs. 1000 crore mark for the full year.

items.statement: Home UPS revenue around Rs. 2,300 crore in FY26; Telecom now 2-3% of revenue
items.quote: The UPS revenue would be, just a minute, it would be more than INR 2000 crores, around INR 2300 crores.

items.statement: OEM price negotiations ongoing for commodity pass-through; some OEMs agreed, others in negotiation; typical lag one quarter
items.quote: we have again approached them, and everybody knows this, it's not a surprise that the way the commodities ’ prices are growing, particularly the commodities which are esse ntial for batteries, acids, plastics, LPGs, and of course, currency is also hitting the lead prices. I think we are constantly in touch with the major OEMs, some of them agreed, and with some of them the negotiations are

items.statement: Government support needed for Make in India cell manufacturing; expects policy intervention once 20-25 GWh domestic capacity established
items.quote: I would like to believe unless there is about 20 -25 gigawatt of capacity in India, or let's say 20 gigawatt s, that is a minimum base where we will get a lot of support from the government

items.statement: West Asia conflict and crude shortage driving commodity inflation (sulfur, plastics, LPG) and rupee depreciation pressuring input costs
items.quote: Globally, the West-Asia conflict continues to be an ongoing threat. With regard to availability and pricing of commodities such as LPG, sulfuric acid and plastics, the situation is quite alarming. Rapidly increasing commodity rates, coupled with rupee depreciation, continue to pressurize our input costs.

items.statement: Lithium prices volatile; doubledigit increase in last 2-3 months due to supply-demand constraints and China policy changes
items.quote: Today, lithium has again gone up by double digit in the last couple of months due to various supply-demand constraints. So, it's not proper for me to do a math based on assumptions on commodity prices because all those things will depend on that.

items.statement: Lithium-ion cell manufacturing target: 85% plant utilization and 90% yield for cost competitiveness
items.quote: what we are targeting is that with maximum utilization of the plant more than 85%, yield is 90%, and with some amount of localization, which you already know that a lot of local suppliers are coming, we will also be able to meet the targeted price, what is the landed price today.

items.statement: Acquired 61% stake in Dalco-GFT at 7.75x CY2025 EBITDA, transaction valued at $136 million
items.quote: We have acquired 61% stake in the company at a valuation of 7.75x of calendar year 2025 reported EBITDA. The transaction is valued at $136 million.

items.statement: Planned annual capex of approximately $5 million per year for new production lines
items.quote: There is already a plan to put in approximately $5 million of capex every year. And the company is generating very good cash flows.

items.statement: Current utilization at 85% with 6 lines; space for 3 more lines in existing facilities
items.quote: Utilization is around 85% of the capacity.

items.statement: Targeting mid-teens revenue growth (15%+) versus historical 10% CAGR
items.quote: We should be able to grow in the mid-teens rather than 10%. That is our ambition going forward.

items.statement: Current EBITDA margin 17%; focus on maintaining margins while growing faster
items.quote: For a needlepunch nonwoven company, the term metrics are excellent. 17% margin in an automotive or automotive dominated company is very creditable.

items.statement: Acquisition funded via $60M debt at AAML (~6%) and $35M additional debt at US entity (5.5% SOFR-based); aim to pay down in 2-3 years
items.quote: So a U.S. company now, the total debt is $50 million. Earlier, it was $15 million. So additionally, $35 million is loaded there, and we have raised $60 million in India.

items.statement: No significant seasonality; automotive platforms provide stable production with 5-6 year contractual life
items.quote: There is no obvious seasonality in the business. And because automotive is a large part of the business, and because you are specked in to the platforms, the production throughput remains fairly constant.

items.statement: 85%+ sole-sourced on automotive platforms; supply 6 largest Tier 1s serving US, Japanese, Korean OEMs
items.quote: Almost 85% or maybe slightly higher than that even as sole sourced by the customer from only the company. So it's a deep relationship.

items.statement: Raw materials are polymers (polyester/polypropylene staple fiber); 65-70% sourced locally in US, rest from Korea and Vietnam
items.quote: It's mostly polymers. It is basically staple fiber that goes into the line and that staple fiber is generally some form of polyester or polypropylene or a combination thereof. And about 65% to 70% of the polymers are sourced locally in the U.S.

items.statement: Return on capital of 40% pre-acquisition; TAM of $2.5B across segments
items.quote: It has capacity of 75 million pounds and it has achieved a growth rate of 10% with a margin of 17% and before acquisition return on capital of 40%.

items.statement: Entire existing top management retained with 39% equity stake; founder holds 16-17% for 4-year period
items.quote: We are retaining the entire management team who still own 39% of the equity stake at the company.

items.statement: Manufacturing to remain in US near consumption centers; products ship high air content making transport costly beyond 500-700 miles
items.quote: Because needle punch nonwovens are high loft materials, basically, you're taking fiber and making a fabric by punching those fibers together. So there's a huge amount of air gaps within the product by design. And so essentially, you are shipping air.

items.statement: Integration risk mitigated by low-touch model, same technology platform, no manufacturing relocation, lean team of <150 employees
items.quote: We are hardly making any change. We are making no change to the operating team. So basically, we are the wind which beneath their wings, we are not the guys who are going to go there and shake things up.

items.statement: Needle-punch nonwoven platform used for automotive (noise/vibration), geotextiles, roofing, flooring; high fungibility across segments
items.quote: Needle-punch nonwoven as a platform itself is very fungible. You can do many things with the same equipment. Of course, you have to do add-on, bolt-ons plus to make it sort of tailor made for the end application.

items.statement: Working capital at 60 days, in line with Arvind Limited
items.quote: The working capital number, just to tell you, the first number is about 60 days, which is exactly in line with what we have in Arvind Limited.

items.statement: Top quartile in delivery, price, innovation in automotive; geotextiles opportunity to take share from larger players
items.quote: Within the automotive space, for our product category, we are one of the most respected companies out there. Our performance will be top quartile in terms of delivery, price and innovation, all 3.

items.statement: US infrastructure bill driving geotextiles demand; automotive market protected from China competition
items.quote: The large opportunities in the geotextiles side with the infrastructure bill being signed, there's a lot of infrastructure that's currently built out in the U.S. and the opportunity to grow disproportionately fast exists in this segment.

items.statement: $110M total debt raised ($60M India, $50M US) to fund $84-85M equity outlay for 70% economic interest
items.quote: The EV of the acquisition is about $136 million. There is about $16 million-$17 million of net debt in the company, and we are purchasing 70% economic interest. So we are putting about $84 million, $85 million of outlay to purchase that.

items.statement: FY26 Agri Machinery EBIT margin 12.6% (+190 bps YoY) led by easing material costs, operating leverage, cost control

items.statement: FY26 Construction Equipment Q4 EBITDA margin 12.7% (+386 bps YoY) from operating leverage, cost discipline, favorable mix
items.quote: EBITDA margin came at 12.7%, up by 386 basis points Y-o-Y, led by leveraging -- operating leverage, improved cost discipline and more favorable product mix.

items.statement: Key risks: geopolitical uncertainty (West Asia), supply chain disruption, commodity inflation, El Nino (65-70% probability), below-normal reservoir levels, potential government capex slowdown
items.quote: Additionally, evolving geopolitical developments are reinforcing the importance of the domestic infrastructure creation and supply chain resilience, which should structurally benefit the sector over time. At the same time, we remain mindful that the geopolitical uncertainty may lead to a temporary supply chain disruption, volatility in the input cost and potential pressure on the pace of the gover

items.statement: Emission norms for <25 HP tractors deferred to Oct 2026 with 9-month transition; minimal impact in FY27
items.quote: Luckily, for this year, emission norms have been deferred. So that was one negative impact which was at play, which will not happen. It will only come into play for horsepower tractor, which is less than 25 horsepower from 1st of October. But there also the industry has about 9 months' time to continue to sell the old inventory.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of minimum INR2,500 crores with EBITDA margin of 25% plus/minus 2%
items.quote: So we expect minimum INR2,500 crores revenue for FY '27, right? And we will maintain 25% plus/minus 2% of the guidance.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 26.2%, up from prior year

items.statement: Full year FY26 EBITDA margin maintained at 23.6% despite headwinds
items.quote: EBITDA for the year was INR500 crores, with margins maintained at INR23.6 crores -- 23.6%, sorry, reflecting our ability to sustain profitability across cycles.

items.statement: INR191 crore investment in new sun control film line adding 1,200 lakh sq ft capacity with advanced robotics, commercial production by June 2027
items.quote: We announced an additional INR191 crore s investment in a new sun control film line, adding around 1,200 lakh square feet capacity, supported by advanced robotics and automation.

items.statement: TPU backward integration line expected to be commissioned by October 2026
items.quote: Looking ahead, the upcoming TPU line expected to be commissioned by October 2026 will further strengthen our innovation capabilities.

items.statement: Sun control lines running at 75-80% utilization, expected to reach full utilization by next year; PPF lines at 85-89% utilization
items.quote: Our sun control lines are running around 75% to 80%. So with current expected CAGR of around 15%, 20% growth there, which we are expecting for this year. By next year, we will be fully utilized.

items.statement: New sun control line commercial production starting June 2027 (Q1 FY28) at existing location with advanced automation
items.quote: So this new sun control film expansion, commercial production will start by June 2027. So that is Q1 FY '28.

items.statement: US inventory at roughly 16 million sq ft in transit plus warehousing; strong demand cycle for Q1-Q2 season
items.quote: We still have a good, I can say, roughl y, if we talk of the U.S. territory, it's around 16 million is already there in transit plus warehousing.

items.statement: FY26 revenue mix: 50% sun control films, 25% PPF, 25% IPDs; architectural is 25-30% of sun control sales and growing
items.quote: So our revenues for last year, I mean, were almost 50% from sun control films and both 25% from PPF and 25% from IPDs.

items.statement: Garware Home Solutions targeting INR200 crores revenue by FY28 including PDLC and new products
items.quote: So we expect like by next financial year-end, we should cross around INR200 crores from Garware Home Solutions plus other new products together because this all mostly would be part of Garware Home Solutions.

items.statement: Onboarded 4 large automotive OEMs in India with direct agreements; 2 more under discussion with samples approved
items.quote: We have 4 big partnerships with OEMs. That means direct agreement with the OEMs. So they take our material to their showrooms. We have 4 such strong partnerships and 2 are already in discussion and samples are already approved.

items.statement: Expanded global footprint with 11 new global application studios including UAE and US; India application studio network grown to over 250 locations, targeting 300+
items.quote: Globally, we expanded our footprint with 11 new global application studios, including in the UAE and the U.S. In India, our Garware application studio network has grown over 250 locati ons, and we are on track to cross 300 shortly.

items.statement: Garware Home Solutions: 6 studios operational, targeting 50 by end of FY27
items.quote: We are confident of scaling this to 50 studios by the end of FY '27.

items.statement: US revenue share 45% in FY26 (down from 48% in FY25 due to tariffs); Middle East sales ~$15M targeting $20-22M in FY27 at 25-30% CAGR
items.quote: Last year, it was 45%. It was -- I mean, if you talk of FY '25, it was 48%. Last year, because of tariff and all situation, it was 45%.

items.statement: Currency advantage partially hedged: 45-50% of raw materials imported or import parity, balance benefits from dollar appreciation
items.quote: I can say 45% to 50% impact is definitely nullified with that, right? So for the balance, definitely, we get an advantage of that.

items.statement: Able to pass on maximum raw material cost increases; industrial products pass-through quick, consumer products with inventory buffer, sun control films ~10-15% correlation to polyester cost
items.quote: I can tell you that we have been able to pass maximum of it because industrial product business is normally -- the consumer are directly affected, so we do that. So that is already passed on.

items.statement: D2C margins 25-30% higher than distributor margins in PPF; 30-40% higher in architectural/home solutions
items.quote: In D2C, it is usually, I can say, 30%, 40% higher than the distributor margin. It depends case-to-case basis, how do we negotiate. But D2C is always better because then there are no distributors or dealers in between.

items.statement: No demand impact seen from inflation/interest rates currently as peak summer season drives strong demand in India and globally; Middle East construction activity robust
items.quote: We are not seeing that kind of impact. This might be more can be visible during weak season of Q3. But fortunately, for us, all those things is happening into the peak season. So we are not seeing the impact as of now. The demand is pretty high in this season.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty hearings and government visits completed on cheap imports from China/Korea; positive decision expected within this month or next month
items.quote: All hearing, submissions and everything happened, all visits what government officials do, that has also been done. So we expect a positive news pretty soon as fast as maybe this month or next month.

items.statement: Debt-free balance sheet maintained with cash and liquid investments of INR774 crores at year-end FY26
items.quote: We continued to maintain a healthy debt-free balance sheet with cash and liquid investments of INR774 crores at year-end.

items.statement: D2C revenue share currently 10-15% of overall revenue (40% in India); targeting 25% then 35% from Global/Garware Application Studios
items.quote: As of now, I can estimate the D2C business is only 10% of overall our revenue. In India, it is like -- I can say it's like 40% as high as. But together with world market, I can say it is only 10% to 15% right now, right?

items.statement: Middle East subsidiary completed; exploring value-addition/manufacturing for supply chain resilience
items.quote: The subsidiary has already been completed. The work has been completed. Now there is some -- already some work has gone into this some kind of, I would say, manufacturing or some kind of value addition. That work is going on.

items.statement: Tariff refund from US government uncertain timing and accounting treatment; company being conservative on recognition
items.quote: But this is like I'm not sure like I cannot guarantee because this is a government matter. And the time it c omes, definitely, I mean, then only I can confirm about that because it's something which is accounting-related matter.

items.statement: Large PPF customer setting up in-house manufacturing; management sees no volume impact as they are not sole supplier and Garware/Global brands growing strongly
items.quote: I don't see any impact on our business because our growth has been phenomenal. Our -- I mean, Global and Garware brand, we have doubled what we were doing last year, and we expect that to grow in a steep skyrocketing in the coming years.

items.statement: Onboarding established distributors from competition in US and UK reflecting superior quality and distribution network
items.quote: We witn essed strong traction in the U.S. and U.K. with the onboarding of several established distributors from competition, reflecting superior quality of our products and unmatched distribution network.

items.statement: Built dedicated Middle East team from top competition; separate architectural-focused team in India; new R&D team for TPU products
items.quote: Like we said, we have a separate team, which is -- which comes from the top competition and the entire team is built in the Middle East, and they are growing pretty fast.

items.statement: Brand building momentum: ~18 lakh annual website visits, 8 crore+ annual impressions on Meta platforms; digital marketing driving D2C strategy
items.quote: Alongside our brand-building efforts are gaining momentum with around 18 lakh annual website visits and over 8 crore s impression annually across Meta platform, stre ngthening our customer connect.

items.statement: Management expects domestic market to stabilize by end of Q1 FY27 and West Asia supply channels to be fully operational by mid-May 2025
items.quote: we are quite confident that by the end of the quarter, the market would quite likely stabilize on the domestic front. And like we said, on the West Asia front, we have anyway taken measures to ensure that the supply channels that we have now are not dependent on the Hormuz Strait.

items.statement: Domestic business grew at 9-9.5% in Q4 FY26 excluding West Asia impact; dual pricing in wholesale/rural channels caused transaction slowdown
items.quote: the domestic business was growing at more or less close to 9%, 9.5%, which we have said. And the small pressure that we had in the month of March was only because of West Asia.

items.statement: Retail/B2C channel (75% of business) growing at healthy clip; wholesale/B2B channel (25%) impacted by GST transition and dual pricing
items.quote: 75% of our business is basically retailing or B2C and 25% is B2B or wholesale. Now our retailing business, which is basically urban as well as e-commerce, modern trade, out-of-home has done fairly well.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 operating margin 16.4%, PBT margin 16.8%, PAT margin 14.5%; full year FY26 operating margin 17%, PBT margin 17.4%, PAT margin 13.4%
items.quote: you will see that we were at 16.4% in the current quarter, 18.3% before that, 18.3% before that and 14.9% in Q1. If you take a look at PBT, we see that our PBT margin has more or less remained at a good constant line.

items.statement: Management confident of managing margins within a band despite fuel and laminate inflation, while investing in brands and innovation
items.quote: the team is confident that within a certain band, we'll be able to manage it.

items.statement: Calibrated price increases starting Q1 FY27 including grammage adjustments and price hikes on packs above INR 10 due to fuel and laminate inflation
items.quote: there will be calibrated price increases starting from this quarter. We are also optimizing our sourcing between India and international manufacturing facilities for key geographies to mitigate supply-related challenges, expected to be fully operational by mid-May.

items.statement: Wheat prices dipped in Q4 but rising due to unseasonal rains; palm oil up but covered for 5 months; sugar stable; cocoa down; laminate up due to Middle East conflict; milk prices rising
items.quote: flour has been on a bit of a receding trend. So, we know that the wheat output has been good. So Q4 saw a dip. In the last 1 month, we see an upswing in the flour prices because of unseasonal rains, high heat and some quality issues in the arrivals.

items.statement: E-commerce salience doubled to 6% of domestic sales in FY26 from 4% in FY25; 70% of e-commerce from quick commerce; adjacency categories growing 2.7x on e-commerce
items.quote: the salience of e-commerce has moved to 6% of overall sales in 25-26 from 4% of overall sales in 24-25.

items.statement: Signature brands (Treat, Little Hearts, Jim Jam) outpacing company growth by 3x; Cheeze Dipped became second largest in sandwich cracker segment in 3 months; wafers, cake & rusk, dairy growing double digits
items.quote: our signature brands, Treat, Little Hearts and Jim Jam. They're actually outpacing the overall company growth by about 3x as we see, and we continue to see growth in the coming quarter also.

items.statement: Competitors gradually moving to full INR 5/10 price points; number 2 player reported double-digit volume growth possibly due to higher wholesale exposure (40% vs Britannia's 25%)
items.quote: Our understanding is that the 25% for us is as close as 40% for them. So they would have got the advantage, yes.

items.statement: GST rate cut benefit more visible in higher-priced packs; INR 5/10 packs less perceptible; compliance improvement expected from 5% GST rate
items.quote: the benefit of GST rate cut will be more visible in packs which are of a higher pricing configuration because the consumer sees that, okay, something was INR 50 is now INR 44.

items.statement: International business impacted by West Asia conflict: vessel unavailability, Strait of Hormuz closure, higher fuel and freight costs; manufacturing shifted from Oman to Mundra for North America exports
items.quote: Our international business revenue and profitability was impacted during the last quarter, owing to vessel unavailability and slow down in demand in those markets. We were unable to dispatch vessels, as you know, because the Strait of Hormuz was locked.

items.statement: Evaluating alternate energy sources as long-term solutions to mitigate fuel supply disruptions and increase self-sufficiency in India
items.quote: we are also evaluating alternate energy sources as long-term solutions to mitigate fuel supply-led disruptions so that, as in India, we become much more self-sufficient to be able to manage if any shocks like these come in the future.

items.statement: Volume growth of 5.5% in Q4 FY26; revenue growth 7.1% YoY; PAT growth 21.1% YoY (boosted by tax case closures)
items.quote: So we had a volume growth of close to 5.5% upwards.

items.statement: Full year FY26 revenue INR 18,858 crores (7.5% YoY); operating profit INR 3,208 crores (11.6% YoY); PAT INR 2,533 crores (16.3% YoY)
items.quote: of INR 18,858 crores, which was a growth of 7.5% over last year; operating profit of INR 3,208 crores, which was 11.6% growth over last year; PBT of INR 3,289 crores, which was a 12.4% growth; and PAT of INR 2,533 crores, which was a 16.3% growth over last

items.quote: we have made regional teams supported by marketing, supported by innovation, supported by research and development to really tackle these markets at a much more local level, and we should be able to see the output of that as we continue during the course of the year.

items.statement: Active scanning for inorganic acquisitions with serious intent; targets must address unmet consumer needs or bring new skills/technology/capabilities; health platform also active consideration
items.quote: there is active scanning and there is a very serious intent. But like we said, what we want to acquire has to tick a few boxes for us. Number one, it has to help us do something new.

items.statement: West Asia conflict caused vessel unavailability, Strait of Hormuz closure, fuel cost inflation, ocean freight rate increases; managed Indian production without material disruption
items.quote: We were unable to dispatch vessels, as you know, because the Strait of Hormuz was locked. Also at the same time, you know that there is significant increase in fuel costs and ocean freight rates.

items.statement: Cost efficiency programs (CEP) increased discipline 10x vs 2013-14 and doubled vs 2021; focus on alternate fuels, buying efficiencies, renewable energy, wastage reduction, logistics optimization, packaging reengineering
items.quote: as compared to 2013-14, in about 12 years, we have increased the discipline of CEP, 10x. As compared to 2021, it has actually doubled.

items.statement: Guided for 60+ restaurant openings annually in FY27, up from 48 in FY26
items.quote: Going forward, we plan to further accelerate our expansion by opening 60 plus restaurants annually with all new stores fully equipped with digital modern design and McCafes, reflecting our confidence in the strength of our industry and the opportunity that lies ahead.

items.statement: Gross margin guidance for FY27 at 67%+ given current inflationary pressures
items.quote: Yes, it is in line with the inflation which we are seeing currently in the market. items.statement: Annual price increase guidance maintained at 2-4% year-on-year

items.statement: Targeting INR 3,000 crores revenue milestone as part of Vision 2027
items.quote: In terms of Vision 2027, the journey is for us to balance com p sales as well as new store additions over the next year and first cross say INR3,000 odd crores in sales. items.statement: Q4 FY26 same-store sales growth at 1.5% with mid-single-digit guest count growth across all three months
items.quote: For the quarter, same-store sales growth stood at 1.5% while overall top line grew 9% year-on-year. What is particularly reassuring is the underlying improvement in footfall trend with positive growth across footfalls across all three months of the quarter.

items.statement: April FY27 showing similar positive footfall momentum continuing from Q4
items.quote: Similar momentum is continuing into April as well, setting the base for a good start to the new fiscal year. That said, these are still early days, and we would refrain from calling this a sustained revival until we see a few more quarters and months of consistent momentum.

items.statement: South India same-store sales nearly flat with marginally positive guest count, meaningful improvement vs prior quarters
items.quote: While the West continued to outperform, I'm especially encouraged by the progress in the South where same-store sales growth also ended the quarter nearly flattish and a meaningful improvement versus previous quarters, and that too on the back of GC momentum which was marginally positive.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 gross margin at 68.1%, up ~60 bps sequentially; full-year gross margin 67.7%, up ~140 bps YoY
items.quote: Gross margin for the quarter remained near historic high levels of 68.1%, improving by around 60 basis points sequentially. Restaurant operating margins improved by approximately 70 basis points year-on-year. Our operating EBITDA remains broadly stable year-on-year despite higher advertising and promotion spend and continued growth investments.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 restaurant operating margin at 20.3%, up ~100 bps YoY; operating EBITDA stable at 13.2%
items.quote: FY26 witnessed continued inflationary pressures across key commodities, notably cocoa and coffee. However, the impact was mitigated through supply chain efficiencies and our full-year like-for-like gross margins stood at 67.7%, improving by around 140 bps year-on-year. Restaurant operating margin grew approximately 100 basis points year-on-year to 20.3% while operating EBITDA remained stable at 13

items.statement: Opened record 48 restaurants in FY26, total footprint 478 restaurants across 78 cities
items.quote: We opened a record 48 restaurants this year, taking our footprint meaningfully higher across both existing and newer markets. Going forward, we plan to further accelerate our expansion by opening 60 plus restaurants annually with all new stores fully equipped with digital modern design and McCafes, reflecting our confidence in the strength of our industry and the opportunity that lies ahead.

items.statement: Opened 21 new restaurants in Q4 FY26 alone
items.quote: On the network expansion, we continue to follow disciplined and a prudent approach. We opened 21 new restaurants in quarter 4, taking our total tally to 478 restaurants across 78 cities. New store performance remains encouraging supported by improved site selection and a stronger execution rigor.

items.statement: Everyday value platform (99 meal) driving strong dine-in footfall growth across all regions
items.quote: Our 99 everyday value meal continues to witness strong traction and has driven encouraging dine-in footfall growth across all our regions.

items.statement: Launched monthly coffee subscription program to drive repeat visits and McCafé loyalty
items.quote: Building on this proposition, we are leveraging McCafé to drive a daily habit of coffee consumption in India. Our coffee is already loved by millions of people and to further amplify this, last quarter we launched a monthly coffee subscription program to drive repeat visits and strengthen McCafé loyalty.

items.statement: Rolled out merchandise-led campaigns (sipper, tote bag) for Gen Z engagement via digital media
items.quote: During the quarter, we rolled out two merchandise-led campaigns featuring a sipper and a tote bag aimed at driving Gen Z engagement and sustaining brand buzz within the cohort. These engagements were driven primarily through leveraging digital media and we are encouraged by the strong response and brand affinity that they generated.

items.statement: Digital sales contribution at 76%, up >100 bps YoY; app downloads crossed 52M with 3.5M MAUs growing double-digit YoY
items.quote: Our digital sales contribution stood at 76%, increasing over 100 basis points year-on-year, primarily driven by higher engagement across McDonald's app, McDelivery platform, and self-ordering kiosks. These continue to enhance frequency, personalization, and operation throughput at scale. Cumulative app downloads have now crossed 52 million with approximately 3.5 million monthly active users, growi

items.statement: FY26 inflationary pressures on cocoa and coffee mitigated via supply chain efficiencies
items.quote: FY26 witnessed continued inflationary pressures across key commodities, notably cocoa and coffee. However, the impact was mitigated through supply chain efficiencies and our full-year like-for-like gross margins stood at 67.7%, improving by around 140 bps year-on-year.

items.statement: LPG supply disruptions impacted ~10% of stores from March 10; all restaurants operational with limited menu in affected stores
items.quote: On the operations front, we continue to closely monitor LPG situation and have taken proactive measures to mitigate operational risk as much as possible. Prior investment in store modernization and capability upgrades have translated into greater resilience in this current environment. All our restaurants are operational with less than 10% of the restaurants operating on limited menu.

items.statement: McDelivery platform showing strong growth across dayparts, early evidence of sustainable growth engine
items.quote: Importantly, the McDelivery platform continued to gain scale and salience, witnessing strong growth across dayparts and demonstrating early evidence of a robust and sustainable growth engine.

items.statement: Own channel (app) showing highest growth rate though smaller base; transacting users growing double-digit
items.quote: That's correct. That's correct. For our own channel, we see the highest amount of growth coming on our own channel. Obviously, the base of our own channel is smaller, relatively speaking. So, it does not really come into the result directly as of now, but we believe it should start reflecting over a period of time.

items.statement: McCafé strategy focused on democratizing daily coffee habit; confident despite new entrants including large QSR
items.quote: I think the more the merrier as far as coffee is concerned. Coffee is a category which I think is underplaying right now in India and it's got a huge potential to grow. The more people who can work on creating daily habits, the better for us and better for coffee business. I think our job we've cut out if you look at it our proposition is differentiated. Probably we do the best coffee in the count

items.statement: Happy Meal toys delayed due to BIS certification; expect 9-12 months to restore; books currently used as alternative
items.quote: We foresee that by next year, it will still take almost nine months to one year is in our judgment to be able to bring toys back. But books are already there. We have been -- since the time toys were banned, we've been using books as a Happy Meal giveaway in our restaurants. So, that's what an update on that is.

items.statement: Store closures (6-7 annually) part of portfolio management; not skewed to South; driven by mall closures, highway changes, tenure
items.quote: So, like Akshay said and you also know that we don't like to close too many stores. We would like to do it for portfolio management. But if you look at it from a portfolio standpoint, we would have closed two, three stores, two, three malls shut down. Some of the places there is a new highway which comes up and all of a sudden accessibility is blocked. So, it's not that we are keen on closing more

items.statement: Ranked 6th globally in S&P Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment (restaurants & leisure); included in 2026 Sustainability Yearbook
items.quote: I'm also delighted to share that last quarter we achieved a major milestone in our sustainability journey. items.statement: Highway expansion partnerships with HPCL, BPCL, Jio-bp to drive footprint growth on access-controlled highways
items.quote: Actually, we've got partnerships with HPCL, BPCL, and now Jio-bp. So, that is those partnerships are meant to expand our footprint on the highways. We've done a good job as far as Mumbai-Pune highway is concerned and we see a lot of access control highway coming in and we want to make sure that we've strong partnership so that we can put the network in.

name: Cholamandalam Investment and Finance Company Ltd

items.statement: FY27 AUM growth guided at 20-23%

items.statement: FY27 net credit cost guided at ~1.5% pre-overlay

items.statement: FY27 pre-tax ROA expected to move closer to 3.5%

items.statement: FY27 Vehicle Finance disbursement growth 15-20%, AUM growth ~18%

items.statement: FY27 Home Loan disbursement growth 12-15%, AUM growth 25%+

items.statement: FY27 LAP AUM growth 25-30%

items.statement: FY27 NIM expected to hold at ~8%

items.statement: Q4 FY26 NIM improved 40 bps YoY due to lower cost of funds

items.statement: Q4 FY26 credit cost before overlay declined 20 bps YoY; INR200 cr management overlay added

items.statement: April 2026 early defaults and non-starters significantly lower vs April 2025

items.statement: April 2026 first-cut net credit loss lower than April 2025
items.quote: Second, even at the first-cut level, our net credit loss numbers are lower than those recorded in April last year.

items.statement: Stage 2 assets improved steadily from Q2 FY26; Stage 3 improved in Q4

items.statement: No change to PD-LGD assumptions; overlay based on past stress periods

items.statement: Q4 FY26 aggregate disbursements INR32,913 cr, up 25% YoY; AUM INR2,42,630 cr, up 21% YoY

items.statement: Q4 FY26 Vehicle Finance disbursements up 26% YoY; Auto AUM INR1,19,558 cr, up 18% YoY

items.statement: Q4 FY26 MSME disbursements up 11% YoY; LAP AUM INR52,295 cr (+26%), SME AUM INR9,338 cr (+41%), SBPL AUM INR3,537 cr (+46%)
