MSME segment AUM grew 29% year-on-year. LAP AUM at INR52,295 crores which is a 26% growth year-on-year. SME AUM is at INR9,338 crores, which is a 41% growth and SBPL AUM is at INR3,537 crores, which is a 46% growth year-on-year.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 Consumer segment disbursements up 45% YoY; Gold Loan disbursed INR1,130 cr in Q4
items.value: 45% disbursement growth, INR1,130 cr Gold Loan
items.quote: The Consumer segment delivered 45% year-on-year disbursement growth, driven by sustained momentum across product segments with the newly launched Gold Loan business disbursing INR1,130 crores in Q4 FY'26.

items.statement: Liquidity strong: INR21,186 cr total liquid assets including undrawn lines; ALM comfortable with no negative cumulative mismatches
items.quote: We hold a strong liquidity position with a total liquid asset of INR21,186 crores, which includes undrawn sanction lines. The ALM is comfortable with no negative cumulative mismatches across all-time buckets.

items.statement: Capital adequacy 19.21%, Tier 1 14.73%; INR1,370 cr of INR2,000 cr CCDs converted in FY26, balance INR630 cr to convert in H1 FY27
items.quote: Our Capital Adequacy position stood at 19.21% in March '26, with Tier 1 capital at 14.73%. Out of the total issuance of INR 2,000 crores CCDs, CCD amounting to INR1,370 crores were converted in FY '26. The balance INR 630 crores of CCD is expected to be converted in the first half of FY '27.

items.statement: Equity raise considered if Tier 1 approaches 13%; internal accruals sufficient for <23-25% growth at 3.5% pre-tax ROTA
items.quote: If our Tier 1 ratio were to approach 13%, we would certainly begin evaluating equity-raising options. However, in a scenario where we are delivering a pre-tax ROTA of around 3.5% and growing at a pace of less than 23% to 25%, we believe we should be largely self-sufficient in meeting our capital requirements through internal accruals.

items.statement: Final dividend INR0.70/share (35%) recommended; interim dividend INR1.30/share (65%) already paid for FY26
items.quote: The Board of Directors of the company has recommended a final dividend of INR0.70 per share, which is 35% on the equity shares of the company, subject to the approval of the members of the company at the ensuing Annual General Meeting. This is in addition to the interim dividend of INR1.30 per share (65%) for the financial year FY25-26 declared by the company on 31st January 2026.

items.statement: Management overlay addresses crude/fuel volatility, LPG supply risk, global shipping/commodity flow pressures
items.quote: The overlay addresses potential second-order stresses arising from volatility in crude and refined fuel prices, risk of LPG supply shortfalls and supply-side pressures on sectors dependent on global shipping and commodity flows, while core asset quality indicators remain resilient.

items.statement: No further overlay needed currently; existing INR200 cr deemed sufficient
items.quote: As of now, however, there is no need for any additional overlay.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 ROA 4.1% pre-overlay (3.6% YoY); ROE 23%
items.quote: Return on assets for Q4 FY '26 stood at 4.1% (before overlay) compared to 3.6% in Q4 FY '25 while return on equity for the quarter was 23%, underscoring improved profitability.

items.statement: FY27 iron ore production 26 million tons, dispatches 27 million tons, pellet 7.75-8 million tons, DRI 825,000 tons, wire rod ~150,000 tons
items.value: 26 million tons iron ore production; 27 million tons dispatches; 7.75-8 million tons pellet; 825,000 tons DRI; ~150,000 tons wire rod
items.quote: Our FY '27 guidance reflects the next change in our scale, iron ore production at 26 million tons, dispatches of 27 million tons, pellet of 7.75 million to 8 million tons, DRI at 825,000 tons and a formal entry into steelmaking with wire rod mill production at around 150,000 tons.

items.statement: Consolidated FY27 capex ~INR15,000 crores including standalone INR10,000-11,000 crores, Thriveni ~INR1,000 crores, copper ~INR2,000 crores
items.quote: Console number 15000 crores for capex in this 26-27.

items.statement: Standalone capex INR13,500 crores spent FY24-FY26; FY26 standalone capex ~INR8,100 crores
items.quote: The company has incurred capex of approximately INR13,500 crores during FY24 to FY26. FY26 stand-alone capex alone was close to INR8, 100, reflecting the significant investment phase we are currently in.

items.statement: Copper project requires additional $200-260 million capex; plant 85-90% complete, $800M+ already spent of $1.1B total
items.quote: Based on our current evaluation, including the initial working capital and the mine development, which will be treating these plants, it would require near about $200 million to $260 million.

items.statement: Pellet capacity doubled to 8 million tons with second plant commissioned May 2026; first plant reached 100% utilization in 4 months
items.quote: I'm also pleased to share that the second pellet plant was commissioned in May 2026. This takes our total pellet capacity to 8 million tons per annum and positions us strongly for FY27 volume growth.

items.statement: BHQ beneficiation first phase (30 million tons input, ~12 million tons output) targeted by December 2027; engineering ~90% ordered
items.value: 30 million tons input, ~12 million tons output
items.quote: So our -- in my opening remarks, I mentioned that by December 2027, BHQ first phase of 30 million tons input and around 12 million tons output would be commissioned.

items.statement: Steel plant (blast furnace, arc furnace, coke oven, rolling mill) 1.2 million tons wire rod targeted for commissioning last quarter FY27
items.quote: The steel plant that is a blast furnace, arc furnace, coke oven and rolling mill of 1.2 million tonne wire rod is well underway for commissioning for last quarter this year.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin ~34% last 2 quarters, FY26 33.77% (+418 bps YoY); structural from value-added mix, slurry pipeline, utilization
items.quote: The EBITDA margin has held steady at approximately 34% across both the last 2 quarters, demonstrating structural cost efficiency and not one-off gains.

items.statement: Thriveni FY26 EBITDA margin ~25% (vs ~16% FY25); Q4 FY26 36% margin
items.quote: The total income for the full year stood at approximately INR8,000 crores, to be precise INR7,997 crores with an EBITDA of INR1,990 crores and EBITDA margin of approximately 25%.

items.statement: Pellet plant 1 produced 3 million tons in 9 months; FY27 pellet target 7.5-8 million tons from both plants
items.quote: The first plant -- the first 9 months of operation has achieved 3 million tons, which is within the capacity. We hope to repeat that in the second plant as well. And therefore, we hope to achieve 7.5 million to 8 million tons in this complete year.

items.statement: Strong domestic steel/iron ore demand; pellet realizations supported by strong product quality and domestic demand
items.quote: Realization per ton for quarter 4 FY26 stood at INR9,590, supported by strong product quality and strategic geographic positioning.

items.statement: Second slurry pipeline (195 km Hedri to Ghugus via Chandrapur) to save >INR500/ton logistics on 16 million tons; total annual savings >INR2,000 crores from FY28
items.quote: We expect annual cost savings to surpass INR2,000 crores per annum as all logistics and sustainability initiatives are maturing by March '28.

items.statement: BHQ beneficiation to increase EBITDA/ton: royalty reduction saves INR200-300/ton, internal usage upside INR700-800/ton
items.quote: We think it's on a higher scale because BHQ beneficiated ore will be 66%, 67%. The cost upside is around INR200, INR300, I think we explained in the last con-call and particularly with the revised notification of the government on reduced royalties.

items.statement: Standalone net debt INR3,901 crores (Mar 2026); target net debt/EBITDA 1-1.5x; Thriveni RPS INR2,100 crores reducing over 3 years (INR700 crores paid April 2026)
items.quote: Stand-alone net debt as on 31st March 2026 stands at INR3,901 crores, a manageable level given our EBITDA generation.

items.statement: CHEMAF debt ~$800M; negotiated reduction of $475M; remaining ~$330M non-recourse; additional $200M non-recourse borrowing for completion
items.quote: So actually, the total debt which is there on the books of Chemaf is around USD800 million. Large creditors, mostly we have negotiated. And effectively, once we pay out those creditors, this debt will be reduced by 475 million.

items.statement: Debt raise planned to maintain 1-1.5x net debt/EBITDA; no equity raise planned near term; Thriveni IPO possible later
items.quote: Yes, debt we would be raising. As we have mentioned, we should have a proper mix of debt. The debt should be around 1, 1.5x of the EBITDA, not more than that.

items.statement: Value-added products 32% of FY26 standalone revenue (vs 20% FY25); 30% of EBIT contribution (vs 11% FY25)
items.quote: Value-added products now account for 32% of FY26 stand-alone revenues, up from 20% in FY25. In terms of EBIT contribution, the share is 30%, up from 11% Lloyds Metals and in

items.statement: No exclusivity with Tata Steel on slurry pipeline; open to other steel players
items.quote: No, there is no exclusivity.

items.statement: Government reduced royalty on <45% Fe ore to 50% and <35% to 75%; lowers BHQ input cost
items.quote: So the royalty is paid on material going out of the mine and the lower grade of less than 45 or less than 35 would be going out of the mine and paying a royalty at the rate of 50% or 75%, respectively.

items.statement: Pellet exports increased as new markets sought; iron ore pricing in line with market
items.quote: As volumes have gone up in pellet, we have had to search new markets, and that is why the pellet realizations are a little lower because the newer markets are at a distance.

items.statement: Iron ore realization INR5,806/ton FY26, EBITDA/ton INR1,930; pellet realization INR9,590/ton Q4, EBITDA/ton INR4,040; DRI realization INR27,306/ton Q4, EBITDA/ton INR7,999
items.quote: Realization per ton stood at INR5,848 in quarter 4 and INR5,806 for the full year. EBITDA per ton was INR1,894 in quarter 4 and INR1,930 for FY26, reflecting strong unit economics.

items.statement: Thriveni Odisha iron ore volume target 34-35 million tons FY27 (+39% YoY); Surjagarh mine capacity 55 million tons environmental clearance
items.quote: Overall, the Odisha operation volumes are expected to increase by 39% year-to-year to 34 million tons to 35 million tons in FY27.

items.statement: Copper: Surya plant producing ~40-45 tons/day; FY27 target 9,000-10,000 tons copper; CHEMAF commercial production from July 2027 targeting ~90,000 tons/year
items.quote: So with that, I think we are looking at producing a total of around 9,000 to 10,000 tons of copper for the financial year ending this year. Chemaf will not produce anything this year. It is expected to start production meaningfully by July of 2027 when the plants are expected to be commissioned

items.statement: Congo operations derisked by US-DRC critical minerals agreement (Dec 2025); US strategic support for supply chain security
items.quote: But that risk is mitigated by the fact that we are partnering with the U.S. and U.S. has a strategic and critical minerals deal, which was signed in 2025. So in fact, we have very strong support from U.S.

items.statement: Thriveni ranked #1 among 383 open cast mines by Ministry of Coal; 5-star rating for PB West mine
items.quote: Thriveni ranked number 1 among 383 open cast mines in India by the Ministry of Coal, a reflection of operational excellence across the group.

items.statement: Thriveni receivables 15-30 days (iron ore), 15 days (coal); Lloyds similar; consolidated receivables jump due to Thriveni 9-month consolidation
items.quote: In Thriveni, the receivables are 15 to 30 days. Riyaz Shaikh: Private miner owners, but in coal it is 15 days

items.statement: April 2026 iron ore run rate ~2 million tons/month, strong start to FY27
items.quote: Our monthly run rate in April 2026 is already at approximately 2 million tons, underpinning a strong start for -- to FY27.

items.statement: Targets INR 500 crore+ revenue over next 2-3 years with 15-20% volume growth
items.quote: we are con fident that the momentum built in Q4 will continue as we progress on our journey towards becoming an INR500 crore plus revenue company over the next two, three years

items.statement: Aims for 15-20% volume growth in FY27, will provide exact figure in Q2
items.quote: we are expecting that we should aim for the 15% - 20%. But I think it is better that this quarter is very much not the suitable time that we can disclose. I think because of the situation getting the normal, Q 2 is the things where we can go for the 9 months growth, for the exact figure

items.statement: Brownfield expansion 80% complete, will raise capacity to 3,500 tons/month enabling INR 600-650 crore revenue potential
items.quote: Right now, we are operating about 65% of our capacity. So, basically, it is a 2,000-ton capacity per month and we have done almost 80% of brownfield expansions. And now within one or two quarters, it will be finished. Then the capacity will go es to the 3,500 tons per month.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin guidance 23-25%, Q1 may be impacted by VAM price spike
items.quote: So, 23% - 25% EBITDA margin, we have always guided for the longer term. So, we are aiming to sustain that. And yes, of course, we are aiming for the gross margin 65% for that. But in this situation, this quarter may be affecting our gross margin because of the sudden price increase into the VAM.

items.statement: VAM prices doubled from INR 75-80 to INR 160-180; 60-70% of raw material cost increase passed through via price hikes effective 1st May
items.quote: Almost 60% - 70% (of) price rise (of raw material) we have taken. But from the 1st May, so not April month from the 1st May.

items.statement: Peers have taken 4-5% price hikes in April and ~10% from 1st May
items.quote: So, in April, they have started and 4% to 5% price rise started to taken and from the 1st May, it is almost 10% has taken.

items.statement: Q4 revenue grew 18% YoY led by ~16% volume growth, highest ever quarterly revenue
items.quote: Despite a challenging operating environment during the quarter, we delivered a strong performance with revenues growing by 18% y- o-y, led by a nearly 16% volume growth during Q4.

items.statement: FY26 volume growth 8%, FY25 volume growth 11%, ~19% cumulative over two years
items.quote: if we go about the last 8 quarters, so almost from 8 quarters, 5 quarters, we have delivered almost 2 figures of growth. And if we talk about the FY25, we grew by 11%; FY26, we grew by 8%. So, we have grown approximately 19% in two years.

items.statement: Expanding into Odisha and Chhattisgarh in May 2026; deepening OEM segment in West/Central India, planning metro expansion
items.quote: we are commencing operations and strengthening our footprint in new markets of O disha and Chhattisgarh during May '26, itself. At the same time, we continue to consciously strengthen our presence in the OEM segment. Our initial efforts across West and Central India have delivered promising results, giving us confidence to further scale this business.

items.statement: OEM currently 6% of revenue, targets 15% in 2-3 years with retail at 85%
items.quote: So, we are assuming that after two, three years our revenue will be 85% into the retail and 15% around into the OEMs.

items.statement: New states take 2-3 years to stabilise receivables cycle; bad debts historically below 1%
items.quote: So, actually, it is a two to three years of cycle in newer states, as we are into B2C business model. So, it takes 2 to 3 years to at least get all the engagement to the carpenters, influencers, the very much visibility of the product, the confidence of the product to make the relationship with the dealers, carpenters.

items.statement: Full product range covers waterproof, fast-drying, high-coverage, high-grab, OEM (4 SKUs), cheaper glue, PVC glue; no R&D spend currently
items.quote: we talk about, we have the different elements of the waterproof, we have the fast drying, we have the high coverage, high grab adhesives, we have the OEMs, four product range into the OEMs also. We have the cheaper glue also. So, everything is covered. We have the PVC glue, which are covered the acrylic and PVC sheets to the MDF and plywood. So entire range are covered right now

items.statement: Aware of new competitor capacity in Gujarat but confident due to 30-35% market share, strong dealer/carpenter relationships
items.quote: we are very much aware about this. And as we are into 30% - 35% presence and though we are very much old brand since 20 years, Gujarat is very much strong base of ours. So, we have the very good relationship with the dealers, with the carpenters, very good strong network and competition was earlier. It is not that today now there is a competition.

items.statement: Dividend payout maintained at 15% of PAT for last 6 years; no buyback or special dividend planned as cash needed for growth
items.quote: if you see last 6 years, we have given 15% of our PAT to the stakeholders as per the dividend, and that is very much maintained. One thing is that this FD is about the -- also the liability, INR 90 crores, INR 95 crores liability is there. So, it is there, but so the internal accruals, this fund, we will need it from the growth.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA may be impacted by VAM price spike; expects normalisation within 2-3 months if geopolitical situation stabilises
items.quote: It is too early to say for the entire year. But yes, of course, it will effect on the Q1 . And I believe that all the chemical industries, pharma industries will get th is effect into the Q1 regarding the EBITDA , because as only I think B2C industry, of course, the price rise not pass from the second day, but B2B industry maybe will less bleed but B2C model will bleed.

items.statement: NSE listing process underway, expected soon
items.quote: It is in process. We are into the process and very near, maybe it will be listed on the NSE. So, we are into that process.

items.statement: Transformation journey across HR, technology, sales, marketing, distribution, operations initiated in H2 FY26; early tangible outcomes from Q4
items.quote: Beginning in the second half of FY2 6, we initiated a comprehensive transformation journey across the organization spanning HR, technology, sales, marketing, distribution and operational processes. While these initiatives are still in the early stages, we are encouraged to see the first sign of tangible outcomes emerging from Q4 onwards.

items.statement: Reiterated guidance for sustained double-digit revenue and EBITDA growth in FY27
items.quote: we remain comfortable reiterating our guidance for sustained double -digit revenue and EBITDA growth.

items.statement: Committed to double-digit revenue and EBITDA growth, aiming to under-promise and over-deliver
items.quote: What we have shared is double-digit revenue growth and double-digit EBITDA growth. We will keep focusing on that and improving that.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin reached record 13.2%, up from 11% assumption at start of year
items.quote: At the start of the financial year, we had assumed we would be at around 11% EBITDA margins for the year. We had a couple of good quarters. We expected Q3 to be a slowdown because of the furloughs and the global slowdown. But Q3 turned out to be a record quarter for us , because a lot of positive things happened. Overall, we balance things out , and it became a 13% -plus year for us.

items.statement: Expects margin expansion to continue as all three verticals scale to full potential
items.quote: The day all the three verticals start delivering to their full potential, margins will continue to expand and will expand even faster from where we are today.

items.statement: Believes FY26 margin levels are sustainable and can improve further with operating leverage
items.quote: And we do believe that these numbers are sustainable , and not only sustainable -I think we can do much better job as well. There's lot of operating leverage that we have with revenue growth coming in.

items.statement: Demand outlook for digital and engineering services, especially AI projects, remains very positive
items.quote: While the external environment remains dynamic, the demand outlook for digital and engineering services, especially new initiatives in AI projects, continues to be very positive.

items.statement: Sees strong visibility for double-digit revenue opportunity across all three verticals over next two years
items.quote: We definitely see double-digit revenue opportunity across all the three verticals, and we also see margin expansion with more offshore delivery, better utilization , and strong bench discipline- and like any other offshore company , focusing on a pyramid organization and optimization so that we can continue to deliver value to our clients.

items.statement: 95-98% of FY27 revenue expected from existing 75 active clients per their budgets
items.quote: I would say 95% to 98% will come from existing clients , as per the budget from the 75 active clients that we have.

items.statement: Top 25 clients now contribute 88% of revenue, up from 80% at INR 250 crore revenue
items.quote: If you see our revenue when were at INR 250 crores, our Top 25 clients contributed 80% of our revenue. Today, we are at INR 500+ crores, INR 550 crores; our top 25 clients contribute 88% of our revenue.

items.statement: 100% revenue from U.S. and Europe (70% North America, 30% Europe), zero India clients
items.quote: So, we at Onward Technologies are 100% focused only on the U.S. and Europe. If you look at our revenues, about 70% comes from North America and 30% comes from Europe. That percentage can change every quarter - I'm giving you on an annual -basis perspective. We have zero clients in India, and that applies across all the verticals.

items.statement: Revenue split 50% mechanical engineering, 50% software; transitioning toward digital and AI
items.quote: In quick summary, Onward is an engineering services company where 50% of our revenue comes from mechanical engineering, 50% from the software side. We are trying to transition the company , while mechanical engineering business will continue to grow and remain core to our success, we are investing heavily on the software side and digital side.

items.statement: Embedded engineering expected to contribute 18-30% of revenue in next couple of years
items.quote: While we keep investing in embedded it will contribute about between 18% to 30% of our revenues in the next couple of years.

items.statement: Plans INR 25 crore capex over next two years for labs for existing clients
items.quote: So, on the capex side, we would be doing, in the next two years, close to about INR 25 crores, just for existing clients, and this is more for just setting up the labs.

items.statement: Setting up digital AI lab in Chennai in next couple of months
items.quote: We also are gearing up for setting up our digital AI lab in Chennai in the next couple of months.

items.statement: Plans to grow onshore headcount from 125 to 200-300 in U.S. and Europe over next few years
items.quote: We have almost 125 employees outside India. We'll take that up to 200 to 300 in the next few years.

items.statement: Attrition reduced to record low 14.85% in FY26, below 15% target
items.quote: We were at 14.85% for the last financial year.

items.statement: Revenue per employee grew from INR 8-9 lakhs to nearly INR 22 lakhs over four years, targeting INR 30-40 lakhs
items.quote: If you look at revenue per person, it is now almost close to INR 22 lakhs for us, compared to INR8 lakhs- INR 9 lakhs four years ago. So, it's been a great journey in terms of what our HR team, engineering team, and our delivery organizations have done. Now we have to go to INR 30 lakhs, INR 40 lakhs revenue per person, and that's what we will keep investing in.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend increase to INR 8 per share, 11th consecutive year, highest ever
items.quote: we the Board, have looked at a capital allocation budget as well and recommended an increase in the dividend to INR 8 per share. This will be our 11th consecutive year of dividend, and this INR 8 per share will be the highest that the Board has recommended, which shows the commitment that we have to return value to the shareholders.

items.statement: Board actively considering share buyback given attractive valuation and cash reserves
items.quote: Thank you for the suggestion and recommendation. It's something the Board has been actively considering, and definitely, the price is very attractive , both for the company and for all the investors.

items.statement: Operating cash flows and net cash increased to record INR 127.3 crores
items.quote: This has also translated to strong cash flows, with Operating cash flows and net cash now increasing to INR 127.3 crores, the highest in our history.

items.statement: Revenue CAGR 15.3% and EBITDA CAGR 35.4% over last four years with stable ~2,500 headcount
items.quote: Over the last four years since the pandemic, and especially since the new strategy has evolved focusing on the U.S. and Europe markets, we have delivered a revenue CAGR of 15.3% and an CAGR of 35.4% in this period , while keeping headcount largely stable at around 2,500 employees

items.statement: No current impact from AI tools like Anthropic Claude on engineering services; monitors disruption risk
items.quote: No, it does not affect us. It does not affect engineering companies as of now. But if it does in the next few quarters, we'll definitely share more information with you. The impact today, with what has come out, is more for BPO and IT companies. Again, just to reiterate, Onward Tech is an engineering services company, not an IT company.

items.statement: Customers have already removed AI-automatable work from outsourcing budgets; Onward focuses on domain-based tasks
items.quote: Wherever AI can be used today, or the benefits of AI can be leveraged, customers have already removed that portion from their outsourcing budget when they created the budget this year . They'll continue to reduce the number of hours on those projects and either move that work in-house or do it directly with Microsoft, Anthropic, or platforms like ChatGPT. Onward is focused on the other side of the

items.statement: Peers include L&T Technology Services, KPIT, Cyient, Tata Technologies; niche clients with no direct competition
items.quote: Coming back to Onward Technologies and other companies in our space that have done a fabulous job- Obviously, you know L&T Technologies Services, you know KPIT, and you know Cyient. These are all multi -billion-dollar engineering services companies that have done outstanding work for their clients. The best part about us and all of them is we don't compete for the same clients. We all have our nic

items.statement: 88-90% revenue from time-and-materials (hours-based), 10-12% fixed-price outcome-based
items.quote: It's based on number of hours that we put in. That accounts for about 88% to 90% of our revenues. The balance is based on fixed-price contracts, which is outcome-based.

items.statement: FY27 volume growth guidance of 15% and EBITDA growth of around 15%
items.quote: So the guidance is very similar. Probably we are giving a guidance of both volume at around 15% and even EBITDA at around 15%.

items.statement: Branded domestic business targeting 25% volume growth going forward
items.quote: But we are still committed to driving 25% kind of volume growth, which means that the value growth also will be in the same lines.

items.statement: EBITDA per kg improved on annual basis despite sequential dip in Q4
items.quote: But on an annual basis, in fact, the EBITDA per kilo has improved from previous year. So that's an improvement.

items.statement: No margin contraction; EBITDA percentage decline is optical due to cost-plus model with higher coffee prices
items.quote: The second question, there actually is no margin contraction. So the margin contraction that you see is basically because we are seeing EBITDA as a percentage to top line, and therefore, it is only optical in nature.

items.statement: Green coffee prices stable currently; Brazilian crop may soften prices further in coming months
items.quote: As far as green coffee prices are concerned, they remain to be stable as of now, which is a good sign. The Brazilian crop is around the corner. And with the positive news of good supplies, we have a belief that the prices could further soften in the coming months.

items.statement: No major capex planned for next 2 years; only maintenance capex of INR25-35 crores annually
items.quote: So, there is no capex for '27. We didn't say there would be any capex. As we have been maintaining next 2 years, there will be some maintenance capex of maybe INR25 crores to INR30 crores, INR35 crores, but these are very small capex.

items.statement: Consolidated capacity utilization at ~65% annually; freeze-dried utilization higher; sufficient for 2 years growth
items.quote: So first and foremost our annual utilization would be around 65% or so, a couple of percentage here or there. Last quarter was a little maybe 70%. So that's why I said we are good for another 2 years.

items.statement: Utilization expected to reach 72-73% in FY27 and 80-85% by FY28 with 15% volume growth
items.quote: 65% will go to around 72%, 73%, If I were to be very specific.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR1,073 crores as of March 31, 2026, down over INR750 crores YoY; debt/equity 0.5, net debt/EBITDA 1.45
items.quote: The net debt as of 31st March is around INR1,073 crores, a reduction of more than INR750 crores from last year. Debt to equity is at 0.5 compared to 0.92 a year ago. Net debt to EBITDA is at 1.45 right now compare to 3.1 a year ago.

items.statement: Further debt reduction expected; long-term debt will be paid down; net debt may reach INR1,100-1,200 crores next year with 15% growth
items.quote: Maybe CFO saying that, probably with a 15% growth, probably INR1,100 crores, INR1,200 crores is the level that we probably could be seeing in the next year.

items.statement: Inventory days tightened due to lower coffee prices and operational efficiencies; no guidance for further reduction
items.quote: Of course, yes, you're right, lowering of coffee prices and the better visibility has helped us tighten the inventory cycles. And it's just not the inventory cycle, there are other efficiencies that we have been able to bring in, in most of our operations.

items.statement: ~70% of exports on FOB basis; CIF contracts absorb logistics cost increases; Middle East crisis caused some supply disruptions and energy cost increases
items.quote: Most of it, almost if I take exports, 70% of our sales would be FOB based, right?

items.statement: Shift toward long-term contracts, especially in freeze-dried, providing revenue visibility
items.quote: In fact, some of our freeze-dried capacity is quite long-term now. So that has given a very long-term picture. So there is a movement towards long-term contract.

items.statement: Freeze-dried proportion increased this year but may not rise further next year; small packs ~20% of business, up from ~15% last year
items.quote: So largely, it is around 20% or so. It used to be -- and I'm talking about broad this thing because on a very small quarterly basis becomes difficult to assess. But largely, it is in that zone.

items.statement: Volume growth 18-20% in FY26; EBITDA growth 32% YoY; domestic branded sales INR440 crores; Continental brand #3 nationally, #2 in some regions
items.quote: Our volume growth has been -- and I'm speaking on a little larger four quarter perspective has been in the range of 18%, 20% this year, and the quarter was also very similar.

items.statement: D2C channel contributes 20-25% of domestic sales; double-digit market share on key platforms; #2 player on some platforms
items.quote: we are doing extremely good approximately 20% to 25% of our sales come form the online channel, which is very good -- very good marker for the business that we're doing

items.statement: Evaluating acquisition opportunities to deploy cash flows; no commitments yet
items.quote: And we are thinking, yes, if there's an opportunity in the areas of CCL Products ( any good acquisition that comes our way, we would definitely love to evaluate those

items.statement: Consolidated effective tax rate expected around 17% due to mix of entities at different tax rates
items.quote: Having said that, the average tax rate should be somewhere closer to 17%.

items.statement: Middle East crisis poses supply disruption and energy cost challenges but managed well; no major shipping route disruptions observed
items.quote: The Middle East crisis does pose a challenge with a bit of supply disruptions and energy price increase, but we have managed the situation well and do not see much of disruption going forward.

items.statement: Percol brand in UK at INR25-30 crores; targeting INR100 crores in 2-3 years; evaluating US and Vietnam for B2C expansion
items.quote: U.K., let's say, it's already a INR30 crores, INR25 crores, INR30 crores kind of revenue, we probably are looking to kind of get to INR100 crores within 2 years or 3 years or so.

items.statement: Malgudi snack brand pilot in 100-150 stores showing good response; broader launch expected in couple of months
items.quote: We have done as I told very small 100, 150 stores kind of a pilot. There is a lot of response on various aspects. People have liked the product.

items.statement: Guided AUM growth of 35-40% for FY27 with commensurate disbursements
items.quote: We've given a guidance of AUM of 35 -40%. We could be probably a notch better, but it depends. We'll watch closely how this environment plans out. But directionally, I think we would like to look at a 35 -40% and commensurate disbursements along with it.

items.statement: Expect Opex-to-AUM to structurally decline by end of FY27 despite quarterly fluctuations of 10-25 bps
items.quote: While we've set ourselves an internal benchmark to close the next financial year at a lower opex to AUM ratio than our current levels, you may see fluctuations quarter -on-quarter for 10 to 25 basis points based on our investment trajectory and clustering of our branch opening.

items.statement: NIM expanded 43 bps sequentially to 9.05% in Q4 FY26, achieving 9% target in 3 quarters
items.quote: Our NIM has expanded sequentially by 43 basis points from an 8.62% in Q3FY26 to 9.05% in Q4FY26. In our Q1FY26 call, we had guided that we will restore 9% NIM levels in three to four quarters. Happy to report back that we have achieved the same in 3 quarters.

items.statement: Disbursement yield increased 40 bps sequentially, indicating pricing power
items.quote: A significant contributor to the NIM going forward is our disbursement yield, in my opinion, which has already gone up by 40 basis points. It is a milestone that underscores the successful integration of our new product verticals and digital businesses.

items.statement: GNPA improved to 1.44% in Q4 FY26 from 1.51% in Q3 FY26; NNPA at 0.74%
items.quote: Our GNPA for Q4 stands at 1.44% versus 1.51% in Q3FY26. Credit cost declining trend is in line with the structural strength of our calibration and collections.

items.statement: Credit cost declined to 2.51% in Q4 FY26 from 2.62% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: There has been a quarter -on-quarter decline in credit cost from 2.62% to 2.51%. This improvement is further validated by our 6-month outcome, i.e. 6MoB30+, which continues to further trend positively.

items.statement: 6MoB30+ improved to 1.05% in Q4 FY26 from 1.3% in Q3 FY26; 12MOB90+ for post-Sep'24 cohorts improved over 50%
items.quote: 6 MoB30+ as of Q4 FY 26 is 1.05% versus Q3 FY 26 at 1.3%. The 12MOB90+ for cohorts originated post September 2024 has seen an improvement of over 50% compared to the cohorts originated 12 months prior to September 2024.

items.statement: Stage 1 assets improved to 97.5% in Q4 FY26 from 96.3% in Q4 FY25; Stage 2 at 1.1% vs 1.85%; Stage 3 at 1.44% vs 1.84%
items.quote: Our Stage 1 compo sition in quarter 4 FY26 is at 97.5% versus 96.3% in Q4 FY25. Stage 2 composition in Q4 FY26 is at 1.1% versus 1.85% in Q4 FY25. On Stage 3 composition in Q4 FY26 is at 1.44% versus 1.84% in Q4 FY25

items.statement: AUM grew 69.4% YoY to ₹60,348 crores; new businesses contributed 24% of Q4 disbursements vs 20% in Q3
items.quote: at an AUM of around ₹60,348 crores. This reflects a year-on-year robust growth of 69.4%. • The contribution to AUM from the customer businesses has substantially increased. • The 6 new businesses we’ve launched are responsible for this, contributing close to 24% disbursement in this quarter versus 20% last quarter

items.statement: Consumer durable business onboarded 12,500+ retail outlets across 240 locations; disbursed 54,000+ cases in a month; aim to double customer count in FY27
items.quote: Based on these beliefs, we aim to at least double the consumer durable customer count over FY27, basically strengthening our overall customer acquisition for the company.

items.statement: Commercial vehicle monthly disbursals ~₹125 crores in Q4, up 18% QoQ; FY26 disbursements ₹1,000 crores; used CV 70%+ of mix
items.quote: Average monthly disbursals are approximately now ₹125 crores in Q4, grown by around 18% quarter -on-quarter. Our disbursement yield has also grown by 40 bps in portfolio compared to Q3. We have concluded FY26 with ₹1,000 crores of disbursements.

items.statement: Education loans crossed ₹900 crores disbursements in first year; 500+ consultants/partners; 20% instant sanctions
items.quote: As of March 2026, our education loan has crossed approximately ₹900 crores in disbursals, driven by a distribution network now of around 500 + consultants and strategic partners, firmly aligned with our original vision. We are also seeing a healthy traction in the instant sanction process, which now contributes to nearly 20% of total sanctions.

items.statement: Investing in gold branches, consumer durable network, AI/tech, collections infrastructure; dual-engine strategy of operational fortification and market expansion
items.quote: The first engine is focused on operational fortification, strengthening collections, upgrading technology and improving core execution capability. The second engine is geared towards market expansion, franchise deepening, including investments in new gold branches and consumer durable segments.

items.statement: Long-term borrowings share increased to 86.5% from 83.42% QoQ (was 61% in Q4 FY25); cost of borrowing 7.63% vs 7.65% QoQ
items.quote: On the liability side, as part of our debt strategy and in line with our projected AUM growth, we continue to diversify our liability book, focusing on long -term borrowings. Hence, the share of borrowings from long -term sources has gone up by approximately 3% from 83.42% to 86.50% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Raised ₹2,500 crores via QIP in April 2026; proforma debt-equity 3.78x vs 4.67x pre-raise; simulated CAR 20.74% vs 16.83%
items.quote: Our debt equity ratio stood at 4.67x. This is before the capital raise of ₹2,500 crores, which we did in April of 2026 through the QIP route. Post capital raise and basis March 2026 balance sheet, the proforma debt equity would stand at 3.78x.

items.statement: Liquidity coverage ratio 181%; surplus liquidity ₹7,590 crores as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: Our liquidity coverage ratio at 181% is comfortable. On the liquidity front, our surplus liquidity of ₹7,590 crores stood at the end of March 31, 2026.

items.statement: AI governance under seven-sutra framework aligned with regulator principles; multi-model architecture avoids vendor concentration; DPDP Act compliance with data localization
items.quote: All our AI projects operate inside the seven -sutra governance framework and of course, we are further strengthening our AI governance processes, which we have adopted earlier in alignment with the principle laid out by the regulator.

items.statement: Management sees no material risk from geopolitical tensions due to portfolio skew toward secured/low-risk assets (LAP >₹50L, gold loans, salaried PL, education loans); cautious optimism maintained
items.quote: I don't see any risk. And if you look at your GNPA quarter -on-quarter has improved, the slippage ratios have improved. My 6MoB has significantly improved, even my 90 -plus 12 MoB, if you see, there has been a significant improvement of 50% over. So, if you look at overall from a portfolio point of view, I don't see any risk here.

items.statement: AI hiring platform scaled capacity 168% with 81% cost reduction; no compromise on candidate quality; enables branch/network expansion hiring
items.quote: Our AI-led hiring platform has compressed offer release to now an average of under 1 minute and scaled monthly hiring capacity now dependent on compute alone. We have already pushed the system and has without increasing further compute, improved 168% increase in capacity with 8 1% reduction in hiring related operational costs.

items.statement: PPoP grew 31.6% QoQ to ₹695 crores in Q4 FY26; FY26 PPoP ₹1,934 crores, up 36% YoY
items.quote: The Pre-provisioning Operating Profit (PPoP) during the quarter was at ₹695 crores, a 31.6% increase quarter -on-quarter. For the full year of FY 26, the PP oP is ₹1,934 crores, which is a growth of 36% from ₹1,417 crores a year earlier.

items.statement: NII including fees grew 18.2% QoQ to ₹1,276 crores in Q4 FY26; FY26 NII ₹4,029 crores, up 49% YoY
items.quote: Our Net Interest Income, including the fees and other income continue to grow healthy, standing at ₹1,276 crores for Q4 of FY26, which is up 18.2% quarter-on-quarter and 78.5% year-on-year.

items.statement: Opex-to-AUM declined to 4.13% in Q4 FY26 from 4.76% in Q4 FY25 (28 bps QoQ improvement); structural shift expected to sustain
items.quote: Opex-to-AUM has declined from 4.76% in Q4 last year to 4.13% this quarter on the back of productivity gains in our new businesses. We believe that this is a structural shift in the opex levels that will sustain and further reduce over time.

items.statement: No specific dividend or buyback guidance provided; focus on ROA as North Star metric for sustainable profit creation
items.quote: ROA fundamentally for any company, valuation professionally has to be given the due respect of being a North Star. I mea n I just used it to say that in our heads, a lot of our decisions will be basis on ROA because as a company also, we'll do robust profits plus

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR 700-800 crore, down from FY26 spend of INR 1,125 crore
items.quote: Our capex for FY27 is expected to be in the range of INR 700 crore to INR800 crore as we continue our journey to optimize capex and maximize the returns.

items.statement: FY26 capex was INR 1,125 crore, in line with guidance
items.quote: In line with the guidance given, the capex for the year was at about INR 1,125 crore.

items.statement: FY27 capex breakup: significant portion for Zone IV completion, part for new long-term contract (INR 200-250 crore total), and ~INR 150 crore for maintenance
items.quote: INR750 crore to INR800 crore, a significant part of it will still go in completion of Zone IV and part of it will also go to the new long-term contract, which we signed, right, where we announced total capex of INR200 crore to INR250 crore.

items.statement: Zone IV projects (multipurpose plant, PEDA, calcium chloride, 5 chemistry blocks) to commission in phased manner during FY27; calcium chloride already in commercial runs, multipurpose and PEDA under commissioning trials
items.quote: On Zone IV projects, they are expected to be commissioned in a phased manner during the current financial year. Multipurpose plant and PEDA plants are actually under commissioning trials and should come on stream soon, while others will commission gradually in the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Energy application expansion to 360 KTPA on track, expected to commission soon
items.quote: Our expansion to 360 KTPA is on track and is expected to be commissioned soon in line with the market requirements.

items.statement: Signed backward integration contract with leading global chemical company involving INR 200-250 crore capex over residual 15-year period
items.quote: First one being a backward integration initiative with a leading global chemical company, transitioning the relationship into a more integrated end-to-end manufacturing model with a capex of about INR 200-250 crore to cater to the requirement over the residual 15 -year contract period.

items.statement: Signed $150 million multiyear supply agreement with global agrochemical innovator for critical intermediate through March 31, 2030, with no incremental capex
items.quote: And the second one is a $150 million multiyear supply agreement with a global agrochemical innovator for a critical agrochemical intermediate used in crop protection formulations, extending through March 31, 2030.

items.statement: Overall demand environment for product basket remained largely stable; Middle East shipment disruptions redirected to other geographies
items.quote: The overall demand environment for our basket of products remained largely stable. While we ex perienced disruptions in the shipments to the Middle East, we were able to proactively redirect volumes to the other geographies, ensuring continuity in operations and minimizing the impact on overall volumes

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA grew 29% YoY to INR 342 crore; FY26 EBITDA grew over 15% to INR 1,172 crore despite margin pressure over significant part of portfolio
items.quote: For the full year FY26, revenue stood at INR9,018 crore, up 12% on a Y-o-Y basis. EBITDA grew by over 15% to close at INR1,172 crore, while PAT recorded a growth of about 27% to close the year at INR419 crore.

items.statement: Key raw material prices (benzene, sulfur, aniline, toluene, methanol) up over 60%; elevated freight rates increasing cost of global trade
items.quote: In particular, the prices of key raw materials such as benzene, sulfur, aniline, toluene, methanol went up by over 60%. E levated freight rates are also resulting in an i ncrease in cost of global trade

items.statement: Freight cost significantly increased in Q4 due to higher export shipments and fuel rates, accounting for bulk of increase in other expenses
items.quote: The freight cost has significantly increased in the current quarter, driven by increase in export shipments and also due to increase in the fuel rates accounting for the bulk of the increase in the other expenses.

items.statement: Working capital expanded due to significant elevation in raw material prices, causing uptick in net debt and interest expenses; normalization may take time but net debt expected to decline in current year given lower capex intensity
items.quote: Working capital requirements expanded during the quarter, driven primarily by significant elevation in raw material prices, causing an uptick in net debt as well as interest expenses. While we are working with our customers and suppliers to optimize the working capital cycle, the normalization of this might take some time. However, given the capex intensity is lower, we still anticipate the net de

items.statement: Debt expected to taper off in FY27 as capex intensity decreases, EBITDA and cash flow improve
items.quote: But yes, going forward, as the capex intensity is going down, the capex is coming down, the EBITDA and cash flow is improving, the debt for this year will start tapering off.

items.statement: Raw material cost increases (aniline, methanol up significantly, some more than doubled) impacting MMA economics; naphtha-gasoline spread also a factor
items.quote: It also has an impact in terms of our raw material cost goes up, right, both aniline and methanol at a significantly elevated level. So, in that context, our ability to offer certain pricing to customers, that also gets impacted by ultimately raw material cost prices having to be passed on.

items.statement: Deepening customer relationships via long-term contracts; backward integration with leading global chemical company; multiyear supply agreement with global agrochemical innovator
items.quote: These developments mark a strategic shift towards a deeper integration, enhanced earnings visibility and improved capital efficiency.

items.statement: Increasing regulatory scrutiny in China on nitration chemistry assets, pushing for continuous operations and safety; may lead to consolidation of smaller inefficient players over time
items.quote: I think there is a sort of increasing scrutiny, especially on sort of nitration chemistry -related assets. And we see more and more regulatory constraints rightfully being put on these chemistries to avoid sort of hazardous operations, which are kind of non-safe, right? So, move more towards continuous operation, put additional sales in place.

items.statement: Capacity utilization at healthy levels (80-85%+), deliberately pushed sometimes at expense of slight margin compromise; further upside possible in DCB and ethylation chains
items.quote: I think improving utilization levels of all of our existing assets has been a deliberate strategy. And I think we have pushed volumes sometimes even at the expense of a slight compromise on the margins. And that is reflected in the utilization levels that you see.

items.statement: Zone IV capex delayed 3-4 months due to 35% reduction in contract labour availability (LPG issues, election migration); initial revenue from Zone IV assets expected from Q2 FY27
items.quote: There is a 35% reduction in the contract labour availability in the region where we are executing capex. And right now, the project is in the kind of last mile connectivity like where a lot of pipeline work needs to happen, which is usually significantly labour intensiv

items.statement: Zone IV capex delayed by 3-4 months due to 35% reduction in contract labour availability and election-related migration
items.quote: This is the phenomenon of this quarter. There is a 35% reduction in the contract labour availability in the region where we are executing capex . And right now, the project is in the kind of last mile connectivity like where a lot of pipeline work needs to happen, which is usually significantly labour intensive.

items.statement: Zone IV capex delay may impact EBITDA realization timeline but EBITDA potential unchanged at INR 300-450 crore
items.quote: No, I think at this point in time, we are not changing the EBITDA potential from all of these initiatives. I think the only thing we are highlighting is on the capex -led growth, I think we have seen a slight delay in the project execution, and that might have an impact on realization of that EBITDA potential in the given time frame.

items.statement: Target net working capital days of 55-60 days; Zone IV not expected to materially change trajectory
items.quote: Ideally, we would like to remain within 55 to 60 days kind of average levels. But as I mentioned, it does vary depending on the market situation. But from an objective standpoint, I think we like to target 55 to 60 days kind of levels.

items.statement: Tax rate expected in 9-15% range for FY27 onwards due to IT depreciation benefits from Zone IV
items.quote: We should be in the range of maybe around 10% to 15%. This year, there are a lot of earlier tax litigations, which came in our favor, and that is why you have seen a lot of prior adjustments and the deferred tax adjustments and everything.

items.statement: Net debt/EBITDA at 3.6x (INR 4,300 crore net debt, INR 1,172 crore EBITDA); target to reduce net debt in current FY despite capex
items.quote: We are roughly at a 3.6 x level, just to get that perspective right. Going forward, of course, the anticipation is that the EBITDA will increase and the net debt will go down.

items.statement: Working capital dynamic due to export destination mix; US exports have 2-3 month voyage time vs 7-10 days for Middle East
items.quote: For example, in last quarter, a significant part of export was done to U.S., which typically on an average has 2 to 3 months of voyage time. So, your working capital requirements are much larger versus Middle East where voyage times are as low as 7 to 10 days, your working capital exposure is significantly lower.

items.statement: $87 million unhedged FX loan; INR 5 depreciation caused INR 39 crore revaluation loss; natural hedge from export portfolio
items.quote: So, we have roughly around $87 million of an FX loan, which is unhedged and is open. Rupee depreciated by close to INR 5 from a level, I guess 31st December was at INR 89.8 or something and 31st March was at INR 94.8.

items.statement: MMA demand complex with regional volatility; gasoline-naphtha cracks volatile (-ve to $20/bbl); Middle East situation key
items.quote: I think the gasoline naphtha cracks have been very volatile. And yes, there are days in which it has gone negative. There are days in which it has also gone up $20 per barrel, right, given the sort of extremely volatile Middle situation that we have seen over the last 6 weeks.

items.statement: 4 key contracts: advanced polymer intermediate secure; MMA contract met annual target volumes; nitric acid contract on track; agrochemical intermediate volumes being made but margin pressure
items.quote: Out of 3 contracts, one was for sort of advanced polymer intermediate that continues to operate as per the contractual terms. There is no volatility there. It is relatively secure and predictable earnings coming from that particular contract.

items.statement: Methanol and sulfur physical availability well covered; methanol coverage couple of months, sulfur few weeks via domestic contracts
items.quote: No. In terms of physical availability, we are well covered so far as far as both of these commodities that you mentioned. It does come at an increasingly higher cost to ensure that sort of all of our plants are fed 100% of the requirement.

items.statement: Augene JV (Superform) to commission June-July, ramp to full utilization in current FY; recycling JV to commission this calendar year but not meaningful contribution yet
items.quote: From a JV point of view, we expect Augene to commission within hopefully, June, July kind of time frame, which is the JV with Superform. And that should actually ramp up to a full utilization level within the current financial year.

items.statement: Gross block expected INR 9,500-10,000 crore by end FY27 after Zone IV commissioning
items.quote: End of FY2 7, we should be in the range of around INR 9,500 crore to INR10,000 crore. We do not have the exact number, but around that range.

items.statement: Partnership/JV momentum increasing despite West Asia war; repeat long-term contract from global major validates value proposition
items.quote: In fact, we see momentum increasing because people are increasingly looking at more robust supply chains, more secure supply chain for their global requirements going forward. And we expect many such conversations to proceed and conclude in the coming financial year as well.

items.statement: West Asia war a serious challenge today: 60%+ raw material price increase in 2 weeks, 10% revenue market shut; managing via agility
items.quote: I do not know how do you; so for us, it is a challenge today, right? I think it is not easy to handle more than 60% increase in raw material pricing in a 2 weeks' time frame. It is not easy when 10% of your revenue, which is going to a market suddenly shuts, right?

items.statement: Cost initiatives and operating leverage on track; most cost initiatives implemented will accrue fully in current year
items.quote: Most of the initiatives on the costs that are implemented, they will start accruing fully in the current year. Operating leverage, all initiatives are on track. There is no delay in any of these.

items.statement: China nitration incidents positive for industry long-term; higher safety standards may remove inefficient operators; AIL uses safer continuous nitration
items.quote: I think it is good that the regulatory standards, the standards on safety will go up, and that will help in general, overall chemical industry, and that is good for the society

items.statement: Bayer contract asset 50% used for Dicamba intermediate; steady volumes expected to improve utilization in coming FY
items.quote: I think as I mentioned in the last call, I think sort of 50% of that asset is used to manufacture one particular intermediate that goes into Dicamba. And there, we are seeing steady volumes right now.

items.statement: Backward integration capex for one contract adds fixed margin for remaining 15 years; second contract revenue potential over 4 years (FY27-30)
items.quote: It is an additional fixed margin that we will get for the remaining period of 15 years.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target INR800-850 crores, conservatively INR800 crores
items.quote: Our target for the entire year is INR800 crores and that we are very confident to achieve.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 29-31% for FY27
items.quote: Yes, we'll do our best to maintain the same margin or even increase the margin.

items.statement: Gavasad expansion 3 adding 6,500 MVA, total capacity 14,000 MVA, commissioning April 2027, capex INR120 crores funded internally
items.quote: Our Gavasad expansion number three, which will add 6,500 MVA and take our total installed capacity to 14,000 MVA, remains on track for commissioning in April '27.

items.statement: Existing 7,500 MVA capacity to run at near full utilization in FY27; new facility to drive growth from FY27-28
items.quote: For financial year '27, we expect to run our existing 7,500 MVA capacity at almost full utilization and the new facility will drive the next leg of growth from financial year '27 -'28 onwards.

items.statement: Order book INR452 crores as of call date, 30-32% export
items.quote: As of now, we have an order book of almost INR452 crores.

items.statement: Strong domestic demand driven by record 55 GW renewable capacity addition in FY26; US demand recovering after tariff reduction to 10%
items.quote: India commissioned 55 gigawatts of renewable energy capacity in year '26, a record high and this sustained momentum continues to underpin strong order inflows in our domestic renewable transformer business.

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margin 21% vs 29% full year due to lower export mix and oil price doubling in March
items.quote: In Q4, our total export was around INR52 crores and the domestic is around INR100 crores. And export we could not ship in the tune of almost like INR35 crores to INR40 crores in the month of March.

items.statement: Transformer oil prices doubled (100% increase) from February; other commodities up 10-25%; price hike discussions ongoing with customers, some agreed
items.quote: So oil prices have become almost double than what we used to buy in month of February. So February till today, it has increased to almost 100%. And all other commodity has increased in range of 10% to 25%.

items.statement: Price revision discussions with all customers; some domestic customers already agreed and supply resumed
items.quote: We have already received couple of price revision, and we have already resumed supply to them.

items.statement: Transformer oil 8-12% of total transformer cost; copper and aluminium hedged at order booking
items.quote: I think it depends on the transformer because, you know, it varies from different rating of transformers to different application of transformers, but it is somewhere between 8% to 12%.

items.statement: US exports 18-19% of revenue; Middle East 30% of revenue in FY25-26; US tariff reduced from 50% to 10%
items.quote: So we have done around 18% to 19%. I mean, 18% to 19% of our revenue has come from the US exports.

items.statement: Year-end inventory INR100 crores; production higher than dispatches due to March shipping disruptions
items.quote: No, so, I mean, as of year-end March 31, we have a total inventory of close to INR100 crores.

items.statement: Debt-free with cash and equivalents INR246 crores; operating cash flow INR192 crores
items.quote: Shilchar remains debt free with cash and cash equivalents of INR246 crores at the end of financial year '26.

items.statement: New facility to enable 160 MVA 220 kV class transformers; PGCIL approvals to follow commissioning
items.quote: Yes, so the new facility what we are making will have a capacity to make transformers up to 160 MVA 220 kV class.

items.statement: FY26 dispatches ~6,000 MVA (79% utilization on dispatch basis); production utilization higher
items.quote: I think so almost 6,000 MVA.

items.statement: Middle East shipping crisis deferred INR35-40 crores March dispatches; US tariff uncertainty moderated Q3 order intake
items.quote: a significant volume of shipments scheduled for delivery to Middle East customers in Mar ch '26 could not be dispatched due to the crisis in West Asia and the resulting logistics

items.statement: Industry expanding capacity but demand strong enough to absorb; confident of securing orders for new capacity
items.quote: So like I said, it's not, I mean, everyone is expanding right now. But at the same time, if you look at the numbers and if you look at the, you know, demand being generated, I think there is enough, you know, orders in the market.

items.statement: PV clause orders protected from commodity inflation; fixed-price orders subject to force majeure price revision
items.quote: We do have some orders right now which are based on the PV clause where we are not worried about anything because whatever the EMA PV says at the time of dispatch, we will charge accordingly to the customer.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; focus on capacity expansion execution
items.quote: Once the facility is ready, we'll be going for all the different approvals.

items.statement: Targeting INR400 crore+ revenue in Q1 FY27
items.quote: So we are targeting INR400 crores plus revenue for the quarter 1 FY27.

items.statement: 5-year plan: 35% revenue CAGR to hit INR5,000 crore by FY31
items.quote: As we move forward, we have drawn a 5-year growth plan to achieve 35% revenue CAGR and hit INR5,000 crores revenue by FY31.

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance near INR100 crore for Kisan capacity and brownfield expansions
items.quote: So for FY27, the total capex requirement would be near about INR100 crore.

items.statement: South India plant expected by FY28 end after land acquisition and 18-month execution
items.quote: So you can expect that South India plant will come somewhere in like FY28 end, towards FY28.

items.statement: Three existing plants can each deliver INR1,000 crore revenue; Varanasi now fully operational
items.quote: We are ready with 3 plants, which can give revenue of INR1,000 crores each.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 revenue ~INR350 crore; targeting INR400 crore in Q1 FY27 implying double-digit volume growth
items.quote: So if you look at like the revenue for the quarter 4 was around INR350 crores, and we are targeting INR400 crores.

items.statement: Apollo standalone EBITDA target INR8,000-10,000/ton; Kisan target INR5,000-6,000/ton sustainable, then INR10,000/ton
items.quote: So Apollo, we are like targeting 10% margin, like around INR9,000 to INR10,000 per ton at EBITDA level.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA/ton journey from INR6,000-8,000 to INR10,000-12,000 over 2-3 years
items.quote: So on a consol basis, you can assume that INR6,000, INR7,000, INR8,000 per ton then the journey towards INR10,000, INR11,000, INR12,000 per ton in next 2, 3 years.

items.statement: Aggressive pricing maintained despite rising PVC to keep dealer confidence; limited inventory gains
items.quote: So despite the NSR going up, despite PVC prices going up, we continued with our aggressive pricing strategy because that's what we had like, promise with our dealers, okay?

items.statement: PVC resin price expected stable within +/-5% range near term
items.quote: So we are not seeing too much of ups and downs in the PVC prices in the near future. It should remain stable in the within range of plus/minus 5% only.

items.statement: Demand encouraging; low base gives headroom; rural outperforming urban; agri demand good; construction projects spilling over
items.quote: Demand is like April was good. It could have been better, but it was expected because of heavy March. May, June, it's a seasonal quarter for the industry. Demand from agri is good.

items.statement: Plumbing/construction ~60-65% of sales; agri & govt infra ~35%; CPVC growing 10-12%, water tanks 20-30%, window profiles ramping to 4-5% of construction plumbing

items.quote: Walter Pack, we are operating somewhere 75% kind of a capacity.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 30.3%, up 424 bps YoY driven by richer product mix, higher exports, operational efficiencies
items.quote: EBITDA grew 53% to INR807.6 million, with margin expanding 424 bps to 30.3% - a result of three deliberate levers: a richer product mix, higher export contribution and operational efficiencies across our manufacturing footprint.

items.quote: ROE for FY26 stood at 19.5%, an improvement of 226 basis points Y-o-Y and ROCE expanded sharply to 35.5% from 25.3%, a jump of close to 1,014 basis points.

items.statement: FY26 exports INR911.4 million, up 60.5% YoY; Q4 exports INR255.5 million, up 74.6% YoY
items.quote: On export, FY 26 was a record year at INR 911.4 million, witnessing 60.5% Y -o-Y growth.

items.statement: Strengthening presence across ASEAN, Europe, North America; enhancing on-ground sales in Turkey, Brazil, Argentina, Colombia, South Korea, Germany
items.quote: We are strengthening our presence across 3 regions, including ASEAN, Europe, North America, while also enhancing our on -ground sales capabilities in Turkey, Brazil, Argentina, Colombia, South Korea and more recently added Germany.

items.statement: New generation products contribute ~24% of consolidated revenue in FY26
items.quote: A quick word on the revenue mix. New generation products now contribute around 24% of consolidated revenue, validating our premiumization strategies.

items.quote: For FY 26 segment -wise, 2 -wheeler contributed 38.3%, passenger vehicle 41.7% and consumer and others around 20%, a well-balanced diversified mix.

items.quote: Furthermore, during the year FY26, we added Hero MotoCorp, Autoliv USA, FCA USA, Orafol USA (for Nissan), Yazaki, River and many other customers.

items.quote: But as you may be aware, at SJS, these are aesthetic decorative products. They get refreshed every year and the new prices get priced in automatica lly. items.statement: FY26 free cash flow INR1,426.6 million; cash flow from operations 77.7% of EBITDA
items.quote: We generated free cash flow of INR 1,426.6 million during FY26, with cash flow from operations at 77.7% of EBITDA.

items.statement: Net cash position INR2,437.1 million vs INR77 million total debt; ICRA upgraded long-term rating to AA- (Positive)
items.quote: We closed the year with a net cash position of INR 2,437.1 million against just INR 77 million of total debt.

items.statement: Final dividend declared at 35% of face value (INR3.5 per share)
items.quote: Reflecting this, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR 3.5 per share or 35% of face value.

items.statement: Board appointed Mr. Randhir Singh Kalsi as Independent Director
items.quote: Furthermore, I would like to announce that our Board of Directors have appointed Mr. Randhir Singh Kalsi as an Independent Director of the Company.

items.statement: Actively pursuing inorganic acquisitions; ~INR243 crores available for deployment; targets in North America, Southeast Asia, India; bite-size, margin-accretive
items.quote: We've done 2 acquisitions in the last 4 years. And as I've said in my earlier calls, we are generating a lot of cash. So, we have close to about INR243 crores in our books now available for deployment, for expansion projects and for new acquisitions, and we'll generate free cash in this year as well. So, we are looking at targets. We already have a few in mind, which we are in discussions with.

items.statement: Global geopolitical uncertainties (wars) may cause short-term hiccups but business continues
items.quote: On a global view, we still have challenges of multiple wars going on. We don't know, which way they will go. But overall, what all these wars have taught us, if we look back, is that business continues. There are some short -term hiccups that do come. But I think finally, sense prevails and business comes back to normal.

items.statement: Full year FY27 EBITDA margin target around 23%, aiming for 25% over next couple of years
items.quote: I think this year, the full year target is to have an EBITDA margin of around 23% in terms of EBITDA. So -- and our aim is that ultimately, over the next couple of years, the EBITDA margin should reach to about 25% annually.

items.statement: Skid assemblies capacity expanding from 6,000 to 15,000 units per annum by next two quarters; peak utilization 75-80%
items.quote: Currently, we have scaled our skid assemblies capacity from 2,000 units per annum to 6,000 units per annum, and we are on track to further expand the same by the next two quarter to 15,000 skids per annum.

items.statement: Two robotic welding lines commissioned; new annealing furnace targeted for commissioning by end of this year
items.quote: have commissioned 2 robotic welding lines to enhance automation, precision and operational efficiency. In addition, we are also investing in advanced manufacturing capabilities, including a new annealing furnace facility targeted for commissioning by the end of this year

items.statement: Exclusive long-term contract with one supplier for skid assemblies; annual pipeline shared, broken into quarterly POs; order book not disclosed due to agreements
items.quote: we work on a long-term contract with our, with the suppliers with whom we have an exclusive contract. And they have given a pipeline for the entire year and then they break it down into quarterly POs.

items.statement: Skid assemblies sold 617 units (~INR21.2 cr) in last 4 months of FY26; targeting 60-70% utilization of 15,000 capacity by March FY27 (INR325-330 cr revenue at 75% utilization)
items.quote: In the last financial year, we achieved a strong traction in our skid assemblies business with the sales of 617 skid assemblies, which resulted in an overall sales of approximately INR21.2 crores, and this has been done over the last 4 months itself.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 23.86% (+326 bps YoY); FY26 EBITDA margin 22.6%; skid assembly margins in line with company average
items.quote: We have achieved an EBITDA margin of 23.86% in Q4, which also reflects our strong operating leverage and also is a result of the continued improvement in our product mix.

items.statement: Value-added products (assemblies, fittings, bellows) 52% of FY26 sales; domestic share rose to 31% from 26% driven by skid assemblies and Hyd-Air
items.quote: Our value -added product segment, which includes assemblies and fittings and bellows contributed 52% of the total sales. The domestic sales contribution has also increased to 31% from 26%.

items.quote: In the current year, on an annual basis, we did about INR 8 crores of business from the metal bellows section. And the majority of the business came in, in Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Design finalization and stringent end-customer quality audits are current bottlenecks for skid assembly ramp-up; expect to streamline over next couple of months
items.quote: the main bottleneck is from the design aspect, where the design which was initially to be provided by the principal is actually now being done by our entire team. So designing of the skid assemblies is the critical aspect here.

items.statement: Income tax demand ~INR40 cr (FY18 assessment year reopened); management confident of reversal on appeal due to prior disclosures and time-bar issues
items.quote: We have already -- we had done the necessary disclosures in both our financials and our income tax return. So we are confident that this is something, which will be -- which would come in our favor in the appeal that we are going to file.

items.statement: US tariff on products reduced to 10-15% range from mid-February; no current tariff issues
items.quote: I think it's around 15%, but I will have to just double check. I think in the range of between 10% to 15%.

items.statement: International skid assembly supply targeted in FY27; open to partnerships beyond exclusive domestic partner
items.quote: our aim is to have or to start at least some supply of skid assemblies in the international market in the current financial year.

items.statement: New data center hose assemblies under development and customer approval; annealing furnace to support; sales expected from next quarter
items.quote: We have already started developing those products. It is under approval at the customers end. Also, our annealing plant that we are coming to commission would also contribute to this.

items.statement: Skid assembly ASP range INR3-3.25 lakh per unit; wide range due to varying data center specifications
items.quote: I would say to consider an average, I think INR3 lakhs to INR3.25 lakhs would be an average that we can consider in terms of the average selling price for skid assembly.

items.statement: Guided 20% AUM growth, 20% profit growth, and 17-18% disbursement growth for short to medium term
items.quote: As we go ahead, we would continue with similar guidance of 20% AUM, 20% profit and 17% to 18% disbursement growth.

items.statement: Targeting INR50,000 crore AUM in 3 years from current INR30,571 crore
items.quote: If I look at the trajectory of numbers that I've guided 20% growth, if I look at 3 years from now, the next milestone, obviously in 3 years should be INR50,000.

items.statement: Guided cost-to-income ratio reduction of ~50 bps in FY27 after 55 bps improvement in FY26
items.quote: We're looking at another 50 bps probably in the next financial year.

items.statement: Guided 8-10 bps year-on-year spread contraction assuming current LAP mix of 25-26%
items.quote: We have always guided that our spreads year-on-year will probably see some contraction to the extent of about 8 bps to 10 bps.

items.statement: Guided 10-15% growth in direct assignment volume for FY27
items.quote: Probably next year, we would be trying to grow that in the range of anywhere between 10% to 15% in terms of overall DA.

items.statement: Demand remains stable and end-user driven with first-time homebuyers in emerging markets
items.quote: We believe demand in our segment will continue to remain stable and end user driven, supported by first-time homebuyers and increased penetration in underserved markets.

items.statement: Strong PMAY and state-level affordable housing projects driving demand across multiple states
items.quote: Every state government is sitting on almost ready structured houses, BLC advances being given already. So there is too much that is happening at the ground level, and I don't foresee any reason why demand should be under question.

items.quote: Our book yield is, if I'm not mistaken, about 13.52% -- and if you look at our incremental yield, the incremental yield will be in the range of about 13%.

items.quote: Disbursements for FY '26 stood at crores, a 17% Y-o-Y increase, reflecting steady lending momentum across our core markets and a PAT of INR1,096 crores, a 20% Y-o-Y growth.

items.quote: Asset quality remains pristine with gross NPA standing at 1.08%, a sequential improvement of 30 bps versus quarter 3 FY26. Collection efficiency continues to remain strong, above 99.8%.

items.quote: Competitive intensity remains elevated in certain segments, particularly in the urban segment, where banks continue to be active. However, in the low-income segment where we operate, demand trends remain very steady with well-supported structural drivers.

items.quote: Number of employees as at 31st March '26, on-roll was 5,400 and off-roll was 3,900 as compared to 4,600 on-roll last year and off-roll was 4,300 in March '25.

items.quote: FY '26 ROA and ROE, again, without the impact of the new Labour Law code is 4.4% and ROE is 15.9%. For quarter 4, the ROA and ROE is 4.8% and 17.1%.

items.statement: AI and analytics leveraged across sourcing, underwriting, collections; early productivity benefits seen
items.quote: During the year, we are increasingly leveraging AI and analytics across sourcing, underwriting, collections, which is helping us improve turnaround time, strengthening risk assessment and enhance collection efficiencies.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth projected at low to mid-teens with EBITDA margin expansion of 75-100 bps

items.quote: In FY27, we project low to mid -teen revenue growth and as I have been explaining in the last meet and a few calls that I have had the privilege of addressing to you guys that EBITDA margin expansion will happen as committed between 75 to 100 basis points going forward, assuming stable regulations and macroeconomic conditions.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY27 is INR400-425 crores
items.quote: Yes. So I think we guide around that INR400 crores rough number. I think we'll broadly be in that range of INR400 - 425-ish crores.

items.statement: Domestic business grew 10% in FY26 to INR4,027 crores; Q4 softer at 5.2% due to Zuventus restructuring
items.quote: Domestic business grew by 10% in FY26 to INR4,027 crores, led by women's health, cardiac, CNS and oncology. As far as Q4 is concerned, it was softer, mainly due to Zuventus portfolio and team reorganization causing higher attrition.

items.quote: As far as international markets are concerned, I'm very happy to inform that revenue grew by 22% to INR5,177 crores in FY26. This was driven by strong base business growth and successful launches with Manx integration.

items.statement: ARV order book remains robust in emerging markets; non-ARV registrations supporting diversification
items.quote: Rest of the world delivered healthy growth across non -ARV and ARV with non -ARV supporting revenue diversificat ion and ARV maintaining a strong order book.

items.quote: The initial uptake has been promising, especially after the price cut in April 2026 and I must say the pricing which has been done is very competitive and we obviously have a clear story and strategy.

items.quote: Again, the supplies, in a limited sense, what is really happening, the solvents, where the prices have shot up, the solvents that we require for active pharmaceutical ingredients are not available and that is an industry -wide problem that we are facing. items.quote: In-licensing makes up for the domestic about 15% of our sales.

items.quote: For Bevacizumab, the ophthalmic Biosimilar for wet AMD, we received endorsement from CDSCO's Subject Expert Committee, and we plan to launch in H1 FY27, pending approval.

items.quote: So the biosimilar ADC, the only reason I'm not giving out a very specific time line is because the regulatory landscape in India itself is evolving.
