items.statement: Zuventus restructuring caused high attrition (above normal 20-30%) and portfolio/team reorganization in Q4; April back on track
items.quote: I think with the management change and that restructuring, that is what led to a higher attrition in the field force. As you know, acute is largely a short-term treatment, right? So, if you have a gap in the field force, it does lead to a much higher sales drop than what you will see in the normal chronic business.

items.statement: Semaglutide (Poviztra) differentiated as rDNA biologic vs synthetic generics; backed by 40 Novo Nordisk clinical trials
items.quote: A, it's an innovative brand; B, it's an rDNA biologic versus the synthetic generics that have entered the market. Now with this price reduction, I think we have a real sweet spot in terms of the pricing vis -a-vis the generics.

items.statement: Completed Zuventus minority stake buyout for full consolidation; acquired Manx portfolio in UK and Cutimed in Canada
items.quote: As far as Zuventus is concerned, we completed minority stake buyout for full consolidation and expect operational synergies to play out over time. items.statement: Employee expense growth expected ~10% in FY27 vs ~7% in FY26
items.quote: Yes, we expect it to be around 10% next year.

items.statement: Domestic industry growth expected 8-9% in FY27; Emcure targets low double-digit growth (above industry)
items.quote: I think we continue to expect industry growth to be around 8% to 9% , and for us, the target, is to grow faster than the industry – probably at low double-digits.

items.quote: If the war continues for a few months, I think the entire industry or entire industry, not necessarily pharma, all of us are going to be impacted.

items.quote: I think the AI initiative; is in very early days. And obviously, AI landscape keeps changing by the day. But what we are trying to do is really champion it across the compa ny. items.quote: we feel very co nfident about the cash flow generations of this company to be able to pay dividend broadly in the range of close to 15% to 25% of net profit. items.quote: Network expansion will continue. 40-50 stores per year for the next few years should be par for course, unless we do more than that. That, I think, will continue.

items.quote: consumption trends remained broadly stable during the initial months, although wedding -led demand was somehow uneven owing to a softer wedding calendar compared to last year. items.quote: Overall Emerging Business portfolio comprising of Reebok, V an Heusen Innerwear and American Eagle now spans over 390 stores. items.quote: There is a correlation in prices, so our sourcing teams are constantly looking at ways to mitigate impacts of any cost increases. We will continue to do that. items.statement: Targets 25% year-on-year growth and stable EBITDA margins for FY27
items.quote: Yes. So, you've seen us historically grow at a certain pace, and we're going to keep that growth rate constant. So, I feel that there's a positive signal, and we will move in that -- on that basis.

items.statement: Plans INR930 crores capex over 5 years: INR500 crores for Aerospace, INR430 crores for Precision Technology
items.quote: Raymond is embarking on a transformative INR930 crores capital expenditure program over the next 5 years to meet surging international demand. This includes INR500 crores dedicated to Aerospace, projected to scale current capacity significantly and INR430 crores for Precision Technology & Auto Components.

items.statement: Expects ~INR100 crores per year per business (INR200 crores total) for FY27 and FY28
items.quote: Yes. So basically, in each of the businesses, we will approximately be spending about INR100 crores each to build capacities, which will be consistent, yes.

items.statement: New Andhra Pradesh greenfield facility commercial production expected late FY28 (second half/last quarter)
items.quote: Yes. It will be in the second half -- it will be like second half or towards the last quarter FY '28, you're right, because it's calendar year '27, yes.

items.statement: Current facility has capacity to support 25% growth until Andhra plant ramps; modular machine ordering continues quarterly
items.quote: So, we have planned it in such a way that we will not run out of space till we grow. So, we will continue to keep our trend of 25% growth till we reach the new greenfield facility.

items.statement: Aerospace order book INR2,350 crores; over 75% engine-related across global OEMs; 25+ customers with derisked concentration
items.quote: Well, I can't -- I don't think it's okay for me to give you a direct breakup, but let me tell you that over 75% of the products that we make are for the engine segment across the OEMs globally, which should be a good direction for you to know.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 14.5% in FY26 vs 15.9% in FY25; pressure from reduced non-operating income after INR600 crores cash transfer to Raymond Realty
items.quote: While operational performance remains strong, EBITDA margins faced pressure due to a reduction in non-operating income. INR600 crores of cash was transferred to Raymond Realty post the demerger, hence, the difference.

items.statement: Precision Auto EBITDA margin 13.4% in FY26 vs 11% in FY25; includes INR13 crores one-time land sale gain; sustainable margins driven by synergies and cost reduction
items.quote: The EBITDA margin improvement was also on account of higher sales volumes, favorable product mix but also included a onetime gain of INR13 crores from the sale of land in Q2 of FY '26.

items.statement: Aerospace EBITDA margin stable at 22.3% in FY26 vs 22.4% in FY25; Q4 FY26 margin 25.5%
items.quote: The EBITDA margin stood at 22.3% in FY '26 versus 22.4% in FY '25.

items.statement: Hybrid vehicle demand stronger than EV in Europe; EV timelines pushed out 4-5 years; hybrid volumes increasing and offsetting other market issues
items.quote: So, I would say that the demand for hybrids has been much higher than just the demand for EVs, where we have been spending a lot of time as well. And that demand looks very strong for us.

items.statement: Targeting 250-350 new components/year; ~20-25% subassemblies, rest complex components; moving toward co-design and build-to-spec
items.quote: Yes. So I talked about one component a day that we will start to do. And this year, we should manage that, but I don't count your -- all the days in the year. So, I would say 250 is possible to be made this year, and we should be on track for it.

items.statement: Aerospace raw materials (Inconel, stainless steel, titanium, aluminum) 100% imported; localization development started, progress expected in 6-8 months
items.quote: So typically, as of today, you import 100%, right? We have just started development of a few of the materials, which are hopefully, over the next 6 to 8 months, we'll see some progress.

items.statement: Consolidated net cash surplus INR68 crores as of March 2026; engineering business self-funds capex from internal accruals; parent has INR1,000 crores liquidity
items.quote: We continue to remain a debt-free business with net cash surplus of INR68 crores in March 2026.

items.statement: No equity infusion needed from parent; engineering business funds organic growth from cash flows; parent liquidity as safety net
items.quote: So, I guess I think the critical thing is that the balance sheet of the Engineering business itself with the kind of earnings growth trajectory that we are estimating, itself has strength to take care of the growth plans.

items.statement: 25+ aerospace customers across global OEMs and Tier 1s; derisked across platforms (LEAP, GTF, others) and geographies (Europe, US)
items.quote: So, you have to appreciate that we have over 25 customers, and one of our strategies has been to derisk our customers. Even when you talk about the OEM you mentioned, they have more than seven different legal entities.

items.statement: Aerospace component ecosystem has high entry barriers; certification moat protects from low-cost competition; China Plus One strategy driving India sourcing
items.quote: The aerospace component ecosystem remains highly resilient due to extreme barriers to entry. Suppliers who have cleared rigorous certification hurdles are protected by a compliance moat that insulates them from low-cost competition.

items.statement: US tariffs creating logistical complexities and temporary rescheduling in auto; aerospace unaffected by tariffs; auto tariffs now down to 18%
items.quote: However, global trade pressures stemming from U.S. tariffs have introduced logistical complexities, resulting in some temporary rescheduling and delays across the industry.

items.statement: Aerospace RFQ pipeline at record high; steady rise in RFQ activity supporting capacity scaling and multi-year contract conversion
items.quote: Forward-looking indicators remain robust, characterized by a steady rise in the RFQ activity, which is a request for quotation, and the pursuit of new global strategic ventures.

items.statement: Global aerospace OEMs tripled India sourcing to $1.5B annually since 2019; 17,000 aircraft backlog (decade+ visibility) but engine shortages hamper conversion
items.quote: Looking at the aviation sector, it has maintained significant momentum in FY '26 with global OEMs like -- global OEMs tripling India sourcing compared to 2019 levels to reach $1.5 billion annually.

items.statement: Near-term outlook influenced by macro factors: Gulf logistic blockades affecting titanium/aluminum supply, US tariff complexities, EV demand uncertainty in Europe
items.quote: While internal growth indicators remain strong, the near-term outlook is currently influenced by external macroeconomic factors.

items.statement: R&D expensed at 3-5% of cost annually; written off same year as operational cost; some development costs built into pricing
items.quote: Most of the R&D costs are written off as operational costs. It's between 3% to 5% of your cost, but we write it off in the same year because we are considering it as part of our business model to grow aggressively.

items.statement: Depreciation high due to INR800 crores intangibles from merger; non-cash charge provides tax advantage and helps cash flow
items.quote: See, we also have significant intangibles in our books to the tune of around INR800 crores. On that, we have a significant part of depreciation coming, which though in terms of calculation appearing into depreciation, but that's more of -- it's not really, really impacting our cash basically.

items.statement: Corporate/holding company P&L broadly neutral (even-steven) with marginal quarterly fluctuations; focus on Aerospace and Auto segments
items.quote: But broadly, the way you have to look at this business is that Raymond Corporate will be more or less even-steven. Okay, there could be some marginal loss in some quarter or some year and there could be positive some year, etcetera.

items.statement: Evaluating vertical integration (heat treatment, surface treatment) for Andhra plant; strategic discussions with customers on 5-year requirements
items.quote: We're willing to be vertically integrated where it's needed. So, we are moving to a much more strategic level with the customers where they can depend fully on us as a one-stop shop.

items.statement: Aerospace exports to global OEMs in Europe and US; Precision Auto exports hybrid/EV components globally; China Plus One driving diversification
items.quote: We are observing business momentum across domestic and international markets, supported by the China Plus One strategy, integration synergies and focused operational efficiencies across all segments.

items.statement: No specific working capital metrics disclosed; focus on cash flow generation to fund capex
items.quote: See, for doing INR200 crores of capex, I really don't need INR200 crores, right? It's always a mix of accrual and debt. So, our cash flows are supporting us.

items.statement: Management targets 50-75 bps EBITDA margin expansion for full year FY27
items.quote: No/ So 50 to 75, 80 bps is a given. I mean it's not an option. We will deliver it, number one.

items.statement: Management expects double-digit top-line growth and EBITDA growth ahead of top line in FY27
items.quote: But right now, we remain confident of delivering top line numbers and EBITDA ahead of top line, right? And top line, we will grow at double digits.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded 100 bps to 14.6% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA grew 27%, top line 18%, EBITDA 27% and therefore, margin expanded 100 bps to 14.6%.

items.statement: Full year FY26 EBITDA margin was 13.9% due to softness in first two quarters
items.quote: For the full year, because of the softness in the first 2 quarters, EBITDA margin for the full year was 13.9%.

items.statement: India tea margins are now at target levels and management aims to maintain them in FY27
items.quote: So Percy, the tea margins for Q4 are roughly where we want to be. We were not there in the beginning of the year. They started expanding as we went through the year, and we had taken pricing and costs went down. Roughly right now we are where we should be, and we'll aim to be in this ballpark.

items.statement: Sampann margins are heading towards mid-teens after promotion expenses
items.quote: Number three, from a margin perspective, we've always said there's no reason Sampann can't hit a mid -teens plus number. And we're starting to get close to that.

items.statement: India business delivered 16% UVG in Q4 FY26 and 13% UVG for full year FY26
items.quote: So in summary, our consolidated revenue for the quarter grew 18% with the India business delivering 16% UVG. For the full year, we've crossed INR20,000 crores. Revenue grew 15% with India business UVG of 13%.

items.statement: Growth businesses grew 33% in Q4 FY26 and 24% for full year, contributing 31% of India business
items.quote: I talked about growth businesses, contributed 31% of our business -- India business in FY '26. For the quarter, grew 33%, contributing 33%.

items.statement: Sampann grew 69% in Q4 FY26 and 46% for full year FY26
items.quote: Sampann grew 69% in Q4 and 46% full year.

items.statement: RTD grew 28% volume and 23% revenue in Q4 FY26
items.quote: RTD continued its strong performance 28% volume, 23% revenue in Q4 and overall was 10% for the year.

items.statement: E-com plus Quick-com grew 62% contributing 19% of India business in FY26
items.quote: E -com plus Quick -com was up 62% contributing to 19%.

items.statement: Starbucks India delivered 5% same-store sales growth and 7% total growth in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Starbucks, a good part is now -- this is the third successive quarter of positive same -store sales growth. Same-store sales growth of 5% and total Starbucks growth of 7%.

items.statement: Tea prices are benign, trending ~5% above same period last year; coffee prices declining with Arabica at $2.99
items.quote: In terms of the macros, tea prices largely benign, right now trending about 5% ahead of where they were in the same period last year. But barring any unforeseen climate change, we should have largely benign tea cost. Coffee prices coming down. items.statement: Management has pricing power to mitigate cost inflation and protect margins
items.quote: But with the current set of variables, we don't see a high pressure per se. And I think we've got enough in our equity for all the categories for us to take increases to make sure we will mitigate margin.

items.statement: Board approved capacity expansion for tea extracts and Vietnam soluble coffee capacity expansion expected online early 2027
items.quote: Today, our Board has also officially approved capacity expansion on tea extracts, which again, we're running out of capacity and we will start on that projec t as well. So the whole solubles unbranded business will continue to go from strength to strength

items.statement: Vietnam soluble coffee capacity expansion project underway, expected online early 2027
items.quote: And we had already started a project to expand capacity out in Vietnam, which should be online by, I think very early in 2027. That will give it the real next leg of growth going forward.

items.statement: Food Services exited at ARR of INR170 crores in 60 cities; Vending at INR100 crores with 8,000+ machines; Pharmacy at INR30 crores covering 42,000 outlets
items.quote: Food Services exited at ARR of INR170 crores, present in roughly 60 cities. Vending exited at an ARR of INR1,000 -- sorry, INR100 crores, and we have now about 8,000 -plus machines. Pharmacy exited at an ARR of INR30 crores, and we cover about 42,000 outlets nationally now.

items.statement: Sampann full year revenue reached INR1,600 crores, up from 35-37% growth in Q1 to 60% in Q4
items.quote: So Sampann overall for the full year ended at close to INR1,400 crores. But remember, starting from a 35%, 37% growth, if I'm not mistaken in Q1. We are now at 60%. I don't -- yes, this is a INR1,600 crores is the actual number for Sampann for the full year, Percy.

items.statement: Working capital improved to 21 days from 26 days last year; India working capital at minus 2 days vs minus 1 last year
items.quote: Working capital was down now to 21 from 26 days last year, and India was minus 2 versus minus 1 last year.

items.statement: Company holds roughly INR3,000 crores of net cash
items.quote: And we're now sitting with roughly INR3,000 crores of net cash.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR10 per share, a substantial increase from last year
items.quote: The Board recommended a dividend of INR10 per share, which is a substantial increase on where it was last year.

items.statement: Modern trade grew 20% contributing 15% of India business; E-com plus Quick-com grew 62% contributing 19%
items.quote: Modern trade was up 20%, contributing to 15% of India business. E -com plus Quick -com was up 62% contributing to 19%.

items.statement: Management will stop reporting Nielsen market share data for tea as it doesn't capture quick-com, e-com (21% of portfolio) and modern trade gaps
items.quote: Going forward, we will probably stop reporting this because we use them now only for execution and not for actual benchmarking.

items.statement: Middle East shipping disruptions in March impacted international business exports; supply chain continuity restored by April
items.quote: Capital Foods and Organic India grew 8%, while the domestic business grew 15%, but because of the Middle Eastern issues, shipping got disrupted for the month of March, including for the U.S., et cetera, where we transship via Dubai. And therefore, we had a hit on the international business.

items.statement: Geopolitical risks in Middle East could impact fuel prices and broad-based inflation; LPG supply secured via alternate suppliers and dual-use burners
items.quote: The third piece is where if there is a fuel price increase and there is broad-based inflation, that is what should worry us. As of now, I mean, I'm not sure where this is headed. I don't see a reason why it should only impact us. It will be an industry-wide phenomenon if it happens.

items.statement: Free cash flow to EBITDA at 107% for FY26; adjusted EPS INR17.3 vs reported EPS INR15.6
items.quote: Free cash flow to EBITDA was 107%, and we've consistently improved our dividends. In terms of the macros, tea prices largely benign, right now trending about 5% ahead of where they were in the same period last year.

items.statement: Open to acquisitions but currently 'what we like is not for sale, what is for sale, we don't like'; protein segment under evaluation
items.quote: On the acquisitions front, we remain open. But right now, let me say, what we like is not for sale, what is for sale, we don't like, right? So from that perspective, if and when something comes along, which we think will be attractive, we will look at it.

items.statement: Expects Q1 FY27 and subsequent quarters to be better than last year if current yarn prices, dollar-rupee, and cotton prices sustain

items.statement: Expects next year to be better for most textile companies including Vardhman due to competitive raw material, better demand, and less capacity
items.quote: I hope the next year should be better year for most of the textile companies including Vardhman and in the meantime, most of the industry very, very opti, has a optimism based upon all the FTAs which the government has done which is which could be a major growth engine for our garmenters and the home textile.

items.statement: Yarn demand is very good; US brand retail sales up 4-10% in Q1; China buying 30m kg/month vs 7-8m kg historically
items.quote: The demand of yarn is very good. If you look at most of the US, brands, the first quarter numbers there's increase of the retail size increased from 4% to 10% of the various brands.

items.statement: China yarn imports from India surged to 30m kg/month from 7-8m kg; Indian yarn exports now 120m kg/month vs 100m kg average
items.quote: But if we look at the last four, five months' data, China is consistently buying about 30 million kg. So practically another 20 million kg demand came to India and Indian export started reaching or touching almost about 120 million kg plus.

items.statement: Yarn spreads improved 40-50% from $0.60-0.65 to $0.90-0.95 per lb due to cotton alignment and demand
items.quote: with the price of 3.30 today, with this kind of a rupee, I mean $0.90, $0.95 spread is available, which four months back was only about $0.60, $0.65 US cents.

items.statement: Industry average yarn spread for FY26 was ~$0.65; $1 spread considered good historically
items.quote: I can’t say what was Vardhman spread, but the industry spread for th e year average will not be more than $0.65

items.quote: we provided a loss of about INR57 crores, INR58 crores in this quarter on that.

items.quote: If we look at today's price of CCI selling, it is INR67,000 a candy. And they increased this price almost by INR5,000 in last one week only.

items.statement: Synthetic fiber prices rose sharply: acrylic +INR 80-85/kg, polyester +INR 25-30/kg, cellulosics also up
items.quote: If you look at acrylic fiber, the prices increased almost by about 80, 85 rupees a kg in this period, polyester fiber prices increased by INR 25, INR 30 a kg and all other cellulosic also started increasing.

items.statement: Spinning modernization ~90% complete; remainder to finish in next 6-8 months
items.quote: I'm happy to share almost 90% of the modernization got completed in this period and whatever is left, I think this current financial year next 6, 8 months we'll complete

items.quote: All those projects are likely to be commissioned in next 1 to 2 mo nths and after that I think June or July onwards, we should start getting advantage of that also both in terms of green power, as well as from cost reduction

items.quote: one, we have taken up one open-end project which was hold on, so we are likely to restart that. Also, we have taken a new piece of land in PM MITRA Park in Madh ya Pradesh. That land is likely to be given to us as per the government promise as of now by December or January this year

items.quote: practically the working capacity today in India will not be more than 41, 42 million spindles as per the industry estimate.

items.quote: So earlier we were not very sure we really want to expand the garment capacity or not. But definitely the business, whatever small capacity we have doing, we have, they are doing good. items.statement: Direct exports steady at 44-45% of revenue (+/-1-2%)

items.statement: Rupee depreciation from 90 to 94-95 improved export competitiveness and reduced cotton cost in US cents
items.quote: Same way, the another advantage which came to India that with t he rupee moving from 90 to about 94, 95, the our cotton cost in terms of US cents came down and also the conversion was better available to the Indian textile producers

items.quote: Today things are good, it's really, really difficult for me to say w hether New York Future will remain at these prices or what will happen to the China or the war, so it's very difficult

items.quote: As of now, there are no firmed-up thoughts on what we will do with this money, but it's good to always have cash on hand, especially in these uncertain times. So, for now, I have no specific information to share.

items.quote: Impact of war is there on us. The cost of some input materials, consumables has gone up slightly. There is a slightly longer lead time for us in the supply chain. So there is some impact directly on us as a result of this war.

items.statement: AUM at end of FY26 stood at Rs. 234.5 billion, Y-o-Y growth of 15%
items.quote: Our AUM at the end of FY26 stood at Rs. 234.5 billion, registering a Y-o-Y growth of 15%.

items.statement: Disbursements for FY26 grew 11% at Rs. 67.8 billion
items.quote: disbursements for the year grew 11% at Rs. 67.8 billion.

items.statement: Q4 disbursements of Rs. 23.5 billion, 16% higher Y-o-Y and 36% Q-o-Q
items.quote: We disbursed Rs. 23.5 billion, 16% higher than same time last year and 36% growth Q-o-Q.

items.statement: Added 31 branches in Q4, total network 435 branches across 15 states
items.quote: During the last quarter, we added 31 branches, bringing our total network to 435 branches across 15 states.

items.statement: Branch expansion concentrated in Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat to deepen presence
items.quote: This expansion was largely concentrated in focused growth markets such as Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, aimed at deepening our presence.

items.statement: 1+ DPD improved 63 bps sequentially to 3.17% as of Mar-26, GNPA improved 14 bps Q-o-Q to 1.05%
items.quote: Our asset quality remains pristine with 1+ DPD well below 4%, improving by 63 bps sequentially to 3.17% as of Mar -26, while GNPA improved by 14 bps Q-o-Q to 1.05%.

items.statement: Gross Stage 3 and Net Stage 3 improved to 1.05% and 0.68% respectively in FY26
items.quote: Gross Stage 3 and Net Stage 3 improved to 1.05% and 0.68%, respectively.

items.statement: Credit costs improved to 13 bps driven by lower 1+ flow
items.quote: Credit costs improved to 13 bps, driven by lower 1+ flow, and improved across buckets.

items.statement: Total ECL provisioning including COVID-19 and Resolution Framework 2.0 stood at Rs. 1.3 billion as of 31 March 2026
items.quote: Our total ECL provisioning, including that for COVID -19 impact, as well as Resolution Framework 2.0, stood at Rs. 1.3 billion as of 31st of March 2026.

items.statement: Risk-adjusted pricing optimization already started in current financial year to improve yields without increasing risk
items.quote: As we speak, there is no better way to start a good deed than today. So, it has already started in the financial year.

items.statement: Increase in yield does not suggest increase in risk; placement pricing based on individual case has scope of improvement
items.quote: Increase in yield by no manner suggests increase of risk. I will repeat that, increase of yield by no standards equals mathematically to increase of risk.

items.statement: Focus on rebuilding direct sourcing muscle through CSC, digital avenues, website, app with referral program
items.quote: We just want to continue building our own strengths, which is direct sourcing through channels like CSC, develop our digital avenues, which is the website, our own app, which has a referral program.

items.statement: Balance transfer out rate controlled at 5.5% for full year, below 6% guidance
items.quote: This year, also, we have closed at 5.5% on a full year basis. No doubt, customers sometimes get extra money, and they pay back.

items.statement: Ample liquidity maintained with cash and cash equivalents and unavailed cash credit limits of Rs. 19 billion, documented unavailed sanctions of Rs. 9.75 billion
items.quote: As of 31st March 2026, we maintained ample liquidity, including cash and cash equivalents and unavailed cash credit limits of Rs. 19 billion, documented unavailed sanctions of Rs. 9.75 billion.

items.statement: Outstanding borrowing stood at Rs. 204 billion as on 31 March 2026
items.quote: As on 31st March 2026, the outstanding borrowing stood at Rs. 204 billion.

items.statement: Secured commitment of ~Rs. 975 crores (USD 108 million) from marquee multinational financial institution at competitive cost
items.quote: During FY26, we also successfully secured commitment of ~Rs. 975 crores, USD 108 million, from a marquee multinational financial institution at a very competitive cost.

items.statement: 40% borrowing linked to external benchmarks (repo, T-Bill, MIBOR) and 33% linked to up to 3-month MCLR, enabling faster repricing of nearly 73% of borrowing
items.quote: We have an optimum mix of various benchmarks of interest rates such as 40% borrowing linked to external benchmarks such as repo, T-Bill, MIBOR and 33% linked to up to 3-month MCLR, enabling faster repricing of nearly 73% of our borrowing in line with the i nterest rate movements

items.statement: ROA improved 13 bps to 3.5% and ROE improved 38 bps Q-o-Q to 14.67% in Q4
items.quote: Our ROA improved by 13 bps to 3.5% and ROE improved by 38 bps quarter-on-quarter to 14.67% in Q4.

items.statement: No impact seen on bouncing or collections from Middle East war as of April; monitoring 5-6 profiles like travel, tours, hotels, restaurants, energy-related
items.quote: We are also keeping very close watch on what is happening on the quality or maybe market trends based on this Middle East war. But thankfully, as of now, we are not seeing any kind of trend either in bouncing or in our collections.

items.statement: Target AUM of INR 6,500 crores by March 2027 (FY27)
items.quote: I spoke of, March '27, we are likely to exit at INR6,500 crores of AUM.

items.statement: Aim to maintain monthly disbursements at INR 500 crores for 3-4 months then increase to INR 550-600 crores
items.quote: we want to retain at that level for at least next three -four months and then aim for about INR550 crores to about INR600 crores as we progress

items.statement: Target to add 7 lakh new borrowers in FY27 reaching 1.6 million total borrowers
items.quote: I think by the next financial year end, our goal is to add another 7 lakh new borrowers during the financial year, which should take us after the, let's say, dropouts or whatever to closer to1.6 million borrowers from the present 1.1 million that we have.

items.statement: Cost of borrowings expected below 12.5% blended for FY27
items.quote: overall for the year, we believe it should be, below 12.5%.

items.statement: Yield expected to inch up closer to ideal yield during FY27
items.quote: But as we progress, I believe we should inch up closer towards the ideal yield during FY27.

items.statement: Target X-bucket collection efficiency of 99.5% irrespective of book size
items.quote: Any level of growth, I can't compromise on collection efficiency, especially in the X -bucket. It has to be 99.5%

items.statement: Medium-term opex target of 7-8% of AUM
items.quote: See, in the medium term, it should come down to about 7% to 8% opex to AUM

items.statement: Added 1.2 lakh new borrowers in Q4 FY26 vs 63,000 in Q3 FY26
items.quote: If you would have noticed, we h ave added about 1.2 lakh new borrowers during the quarter against 63,000 odd in the last quarter.

items.statement: NIM contracted to 9.9% in Q4 from 11.1% in Q3 due to previous quarter cost of borrowings
items.quote: NIM contracted to 9.9% compared to 11.1% largely on the impact of cost of borrowings which we have seen in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Yield improved to 22.8% in Q4 from 22.4% in Q3 due to better portfolio mix
items.quote: Yield for the quarter got positive impact because of this movement into better portfolio mix. So, it is at 22.8% compared to 22.4% in Q3.

items.statement: Marginal cost of borrowings reduced by 120 bps to 12% in Q4
items.quote: We have seen marginal cost of borrowings redu ce during the quarter by 120 basis p oints, it is stacking at 12%.

items.statement: Disbursement yield at 25.25% with loan pricing between 23-26%
items.quote: My disbursement yield, if I have to give you that number, that is around 25.25%. H owever, it is presently at 22.8 % largely because there is GNPA and there is a book which has flowed into GNPA, so it gets impacted.

items.statement: AUM grew 12% QoQ to INR 4,420 crores with 80% under new guardrails
items.quote: AUM closing was INR4,420 crores, which is higher compared to last quarter AUM of INR3,948 crores. This is after eight quarters we have seen an increase in the AUM and the AUM increase was 12% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Monthly disbursements increased to INR 500 crores in Q4 from INR 400 crores in Q3 and INR 300 crores in Q2
items.quote: We managed to disburse around INR 500 crores a month during the last quarte r, which was up against the INR400 crores per month that we used to disburse in Q3, w hich again was against the INR 300 crore s in Q2 per month.

items.statement: New customer share at 45% in Q4 (10% new-to-credit, 35% new-to-Spandana)
items.quote: the share of new customers last quarter was about 45%, which comprised both new-to-credit as also new-to-Spandana.

items.statement: Total borrowings since rights issue at INR 3,116 crores; borrowed INR 1,272 crores in Q4
items.quote: we have borrowed INR1,272 crores during the quarter. The total borrowings since the rights issue we have done is at INR3,116 crore s.

items.statement: X-bucket collection efficiency improved to 99.7% in March 2026 from 99.3% in December 2025
items.quote: X-bucket collection efficiency has been seeing improvement for us month after month. For March 2026, it was at 99.7% against 99.3% for December 2025.

items.statement: GNPA improved to 3.8% from 4.2%; NNPA improved to 0.73% from 0.92% QoQ
items.quote: The GNPA stood at 3.8% versus 4.2% in December. The NNPA is now down to 0.73% against the 0.92% compared to the December quarter.

items.statement: Criss Financial GNPA improved to 6.5% from 11.45% QoQ; micro-LAP GNPA at 1.2%
items.quote: Last quarter it was about 11.45% GNPA, this quarter it is at 6.50%. Yes, we've done one ARC transaction in the entity and also the collection efficiencies have started improving. So, leading to both these things, you know, the current GNPA is at 6.5%.

items.statement: LOS migration to Perfios platform underway; individual loan product launch before end of Q1 or early Q2 FY27; JLG migration by Oct-Nov 2025
items.quote: It has started moving and hopefully we should have our first product, which is the individual loan product, either before the end of this quarter or early next quarter and the JLG migration might happen sometime in October-November types.

items.statement: 1,250 branches adequate for up to INR 12,500 crores AUM; only frontline headcount may increase for growth
items.quote: head office is adequately capacitized, I don't need to open branches because I've got 1,250 branches in a steady state, and even if I take a INR10 crores assumption, you know, I'm well equipped for INR12,500 crores of AUM.

items.statement: Opex reduced to INR 161 crores in Q4 from INR 195 crores in Q3; first PAT of INR 5 crores after six quarters of losses
items.quote: Our opex came down to about INR161 crores last quarter as compared to INR195 crores and we had for the first time after six quarters had a PAT of INR5 crores against a loss of INR95 crores in the previous quarter.

items.statement: PPOP strengthened to INR 39 crores in Q4 from INR 8 crores in Q3; PBT of INR 8 crores vs loss of INR 125 crores
items.quote: Our PPOP h as strengthened, we were at INR39 crores for Q4 compared to INR8 crores reported for Q3 FY26. Like you have noticed and Venky explained, this quarter w e have reported INR 8 crores of PBT compared to the loss of INR125 crores in the last quarter.

items.statement: Industry following SRO guardrails effective April 1, 2025 including 3-lender norm and INR 2 lakh indebtedness cap; SRO conducting third-party evaluations
items.quote: the guardrails issued by the SROs are being followed in total, effective 1st of April, which is also reflecting in how the industry book is behaving. Whether it is our three-lender norm or the INR2 lakh indebtedness FOIR, and more importantly, one of the SRO is also doing a third -party evaluation of various lenders to ensure that they are well within the guardrails

items.statement: Spandana follows stricter 30-day DPD cutoff vs industry 60-day norm for new disbursements
items.quote: today nobody is lending beyond 60 days, however Spandana follows 30 days. So, that's where we are right now.

items.statement: Micro-LAP portfolio at INR 322 crores in subsidiary Criss Financial; new individual loan product launching June-July with ticket size INR 1-4 lakhs, 24-month avg tenure, unsecured
items.quote: Micro-LAP as I said is about INR 322 crores , this will be about INR 260 crores odd. But we are launching a different individual loan in the month of June or July, which is going to be a better underwritten product wherein there will be a personal visit by a credit officer, questions being asked, PAN being collected, 100.00% e-NACH repayments, so on and so forth.

items.statement: Digital repayment share at 22%; targeting 50% industry-wide to reduce meeting center dependence
items.quote: Today, for instance, at Spandana, my average is about 22% . Now, if customers are paying me online and if I expect them to attend meeting center just for the sake of attending, it's not going to happen. So, there is always going to be a conflict between meeting center and digital repayment.

items.statement: Customer satisfaction score improved from 22% in Q3 to 71% in Q4; targeting 95% by end of Q1 or early Q2 FY27
items.quote: We started focusing heavily on customer satisfaction and our score, which was about 22% in Q3 has gone up to 71%. We are still not very happy, we are aiming for a 95% score either before the end of this quarter or early next quarter

items.statement: Rejection rates remain 60-65%; 98% of disbursements to customers with clean repayment history (no 30+ DPD)
items.quote: Rejections continue to be in the range of 60% to 65%, and it may remain so for a while. Now, what will happen is some of these customers who for whatever reasons could not pay, defaulted, with no adverse intent, you know, it was just their capacity, may come back into the mainstream in about two-three years

items.statement: El Nino and fertilizer issues anticipated as seasonal risks; focusing on collection efficiency in X-bucket and 1+ bucket to prepare
items.quote: We've been hearing about the El Nino and fertilizer issue, so a lot of queries people keep asking how is it going to impact the portfolio. Well, it's something which is seasonal, which is expected, anticipated, but we are trying to be cautious in terms of how we source new customers and especially focus more on ensuring that our collection efficiency both in the X-bucket as also in the one plus bu

items.statement: CFL merger process begun; expected to complete in 5-6 months
items.quote: On the merger front, the process has begun, might take another 5 -6 months, we are working on it. So the CFL merger is definitely in due course, it's going to happen.

items.statement: Capital adequacy at 35.9% with net worth of INR 2,130 crores as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: Accordingly, the capital adequacy is also very strong. CAR stood at 35.9% with a net worth of INR2,130 crores as of 31st of March.

name: Home First Finance Company India Ltd

items.statement: Guided ~25% YoY AUM growth for FY27
items.quote: Based on where w e are today, we are positioned to deliver around 25% year -on-year AUM growth

items.statement: Spread guidance maintained at 5% to 5.25%
items.quote: Our aim remains to deliver a spread at a portfolio level in our guided range of 5% to 5.25%.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance 30-40 bps for FY27
items.quote: Guidance on the credit cost is the same. 30bps to 40bps.

items.statement: Operating cost to assets expected at 2.6%-2.7%
items.quote: As we continue to invest for growth, we expect this ratio to remain broadly range-bound within 2.6% to 2.7%.

items.statement: AUM at INR 15,878 cr, up 24.9% YoY
items.quote: Our assets under management stood at INR1 5,878 crores as of March '26, up 24.9% year-on-year and 6.4% sequentially.

items.statement: Q4 disbursement highest ever at INR 1,572 cr
items.quote: Disbursement in Q4 was the highest ever at INR1,572 crores, up 23.5% year-on-year and 19.3% q-o-q.

items.statement: FY26 disbursement INR 5,424 cr, up 12.9% YoY
items.quote: For FY'26, the disbursement stood at INR5,424 crores, a growth of 12.9% over FY25.

items.statement: Co-lending book grew to INR 593 cr, 3.7% of AUM
items.quote: The co-lending book grew to INR593 crores and now represents 3.7% of AUM.

items.statement: Spread ex co-lending at 5.3% in Q4
items.quote: As a result, our spread, excluding co-lending, remained healthy at 5.3%.

items.statement: NIM 5.9% in Q4, 5.7% for FY26
items.quote: Net interest margin for Q4 stood at 5.9%, while there was a modest sequential compression of 10bps, NIM remains robust and continues to reflect the strength of our business model. For FY26, NIM stood around 5.7%.

items.statement: Incremental borrowing cost ~7.6% in Q4
items.quote: Incremental borrowing costs during the quarter remained favourable at around 7.6%, which gives us confidence in the resilience of our spread profile.

items.statement: 1+ DPD 4.7%, down 60bps QoQ; 30+ DPD 3.2%, down 50bps QoQ
items.quote: Our 1+ DPD is at 4.7%, down 60bps sequentially. 30+ DPD improved to 3.2%, down by 50 bps sequentially.

items.statement: Stage 2 at 1.4% (-30bps QoQ), Gross Stage 3 at 1.8% (-20bps QoQ)
items.quote: Stage 2 reduced by 30bps to 1.4%. Gross Stage 3 improved to 1.8%, down by 20bps q-o-q.

items.statement: April collections better than Apr'25 and Apr'24; fresh slippages lower
items.quote: Early indicators from April demonstrate good collection outcomes compared to the same month in previous years. Fresh slippage % is lower than what was seen in April 2025 as well as April 2024.

items.statement: Added 6 branches, 5 touch points in Q4; network 171 branches, 373 touch points
items.quote: During the quarter, we added 6 new branches and 5 touch points, increasing the network to 171 branches and 373 touch points.

items.statement: Plan to add 30-40 branches per year
items.quote: Our branch strategy is to add about 30 to 40 branches every year. So that is what we are planning.

items.statement: Net 221 employees added in FY26; total headcount 1,855
items.quote: During 2026, we also added net 221 employees in largely customer-facing goals, taking our total headcount to 1,855.

items.statement: All senior leadership positions filled across states
items.quote: All senior leadership positions in the branch network have been filled across all states and are now fully focused on delivering strong results in this financial year.

items.statement: PLR cut 10bps in Jan; no further cut planned near term
items.quote: We have already done with the 10 basis points in January. So we will want to stay put for now.

items.statement: Origination yield 13% in Q4; portfolio yield ex co-lending 13.2%
items.quote: Portfolio yields, excluding co-lending, stood at 13.2%, while disbursal yields for the quarter stood at 13%, reflecting continued pricing discipline and healthy customer acquisition quality.

items.statement: Mumbai-Pune developer-led sourcing scaled over 18-24 months
items.quote: Mumbai-Pune, you can say transition has been taking place over the last almost 18 to 24 months. It's just that it's become much larger now

items.statement: No new competitors in South; existing players vary by season
items.quote: No new names as such. Set of existing players, so depending on the season, depending on the year, there are some players who are more active. So nothing significant to report in terms of new competition.

items.statement: QIP of INR 1,250 cr completed in Apr'25
items.quote: Following the INR1,250 crores QIP completed earlier in Apr'25, our balance sheet remains very well capitalized.

items.statement: Cost-to-income 32% in Q4, 32.5% for FY26 (improved 330bps YoY)
items.quote: Cost-to-income for Q4 was 32%, improving 10bps sequentially. For FY26, the cost-to-income stood at 32.5%, an improvement of 330 bps y-o-y.

items.statement: Management guides for ~30% growth and historically beats it
items.quote: We always guide about 30%, we always beat that guidance.

items.statement: Health insurance growth accelerated post-GST with higher sum insured and unlimited products
items.quote: However, what has happened post-GST is that in health insurance, for instance, people are buying higher sum insured than they were buying earlier.

items.statement: Term insurance riders attachment increased post-GST price reduction
items.quote: On the term side, the change has been, again, because the customer is seeing a 18% reductio n, because, prices have not changed on both health and term

items.statement: Paisabazaar EBITDA positive in Q4, expected significantly positive next year
items.quote: Paisabazaar, on an operating basis, is positive on EBITDA this quarter, and honestly, internally at least, we expect it to be significantly positive next year.

items.statement: Paisabazaar contribution margin healthy, EBITDA minuscule but positive in Q4
items.quote: Right now, Q4, the contribution margin is healthy, and at an EBITDA level, it is still minuscule, I'd say, very small but it's positive.

items.statement: Paisabazaar fixed costs stabilized, operating leverage expected this year
items.quote: The fixed cost option will be better, and as we scale, the PAT margins will emerge. That's what we're expecting in this financial year.

items.statement: Core insurance book claims ratio under 80%, 20% delta vs industry
items.quote: If Policybazaar was an insurance company, our total costs and the claims paid out on our book, and when I'm looking at a fully loaded, delayed book, are less than 80%.

items.statement: Phygital channel ~25% of savings/term/health, high contribution margin
items.quote: It's about 25% right now of our savings, term, and health business. If you've just looked at together.

items.statement: No new growth opportunities explored at board or management level in last 3 months
items.quote: So, on both of them, today, we are not exploring, either as a board, or I can tell you as a Management, any other growth opportunity.

items.statement: POSP agent mix shifted: 83% premium from small agents vs ~50% year ago
items.quote: In terms of premium, 83% of the premium comes from the small agents now. If you look at the same number a year ago, that would have been close to 50-50 in terms of premium.

items.statement: Paisabazaar applying for stock broking license as prerequisite for bond license
items.quote: The stock broking license that you were talking about is a prerequisite for acquiring a bond license. So that is why you see that license being applied.

items.statement: Paisabazaar targeting daily SIP format for mutual funds to build engagement
items.quote: instead of moving to a monthly SIP format, bringing in a daily SIP fo rmat. And that can build a lot of engagement

items.statement: Paisabazaar has 5.8 Cr consumers, ~50% of active credit Indians
items.quote: Paisabazaar has about 5.8 Cr consumers that it has acquired till date and that almost represents 50% of the active credit Indians in India.

items.statement: PB Connect wholesale business stopped, was losing ~₹0.5 Cr/month
items.quote: We have decided to stop the wholesale business, and it's a decision that we've taken, because we don't see any strategic value of that business.

items.statement: No regulatory communication on commission caps, only media speculation
items.quote: I haven't seen anything, neither have any of the insurance companies seen anything. I don't think most of the people in the regulatory have also seen anything. Only the media has seen it.

items.statement: Management welcomes deferred revenue structure in life and lower EOM in health
items.quote: One conversation that's been on in the life insurance industry is about some form of deferred revenues. We don't want to participate in that debate. We are very positive about it.

items.statement: Renewal ARR grew 63% YoY to ₹1,126 Cr in Q4
items.quote: And for the quarter, this is at an ARR of ₹1,126 Cr, up from ₹689 Cr, so that's a growth of 63% year-on-year.

items.statement: New protection premium grew 57% YoY for FY26, 67% in Q4
items.quote: The new protection business in Q4FY26 was up for the year 57%, health at 68%, so even in this, 67% year-on-year protection story, health continues to be slightly ahead of the pack.

items.statement: Core online insurance premium up 39% YoY for FY26, 44% in Q4
items.quote: The core online insurance premium is up 39% for the year. And the new protection premium is up 57% for the year. However, when you look at the same numbers on the quarter, they are 44% and 67% each.

items.statement: Insurance CSAT consistently above 90%, Paisabazaar CSAT reached ~90%
items.quote: We're continuing to improve our customer onboarding and claim support and the insurance CSAT is now consistently above 90%. Even our Paisabazaar CSAT, which used to be at about 72%, has finally reached about 90%.

items.statement: PB Partners covers 99% PIN codes with 450,000 advisors
items.quote: PB Partners has 450,000 advisors. And it is the most diversified business. 99% of the PIN codes in the country are covered.

items.statement: UAE business grew 54% YoY on cross-border health/life and claims assurance
items.quote: Our UAE business grew 54% year-on-year. They have built their strength on the basis of cross-border health insurance and life insurance products, as well as the claims assurance program.

items.statement: Phygital quality management critical: verification calls, cultural focus on claim settlement, persistency, renewal rates
items.quote: The biggest challenge that we have been working on from day one is the quality of the business, because suddenly we have a situation where you're not on a recorded line, etc, etc.

items.statement: AI focus on productivity and customer experience, not near-term margin optimization
items.quote: I think right now, we are in a stage where we want to make sure that we are leveraging AI in the best possible way. And we've tried to give you a flavour for that, which is to say that we are focused right now on increasing the productivity of our sales team.

items.statement: Paisabazaar aims to list in 4-5 years, not board-approved yet
items.quote: Our idea is that Paisabazaar goes on to list itself, maybe in 4-5 years, whenever, but that's the whole idea to which the team is driving towards.

items.statement: PB Health raising capital, PB Fintech has pro-rata right at 26-28% stake
items.quote: PB Health is going to be raising capital. They will be close to that. They have not come to PB Fintech to raise capital yet.

items.statement: Health insurance premium growth has been 60%+ for 13 consecutive quarters
items.quote: In health, for the last 13 quarters, we have grown at 60%+; 60% growth over 4 years.

items.statement: Protection business grew 67% with health ahead of term
items.quote: Can you split that 67% protection growth into how much is term and how much is health?

items.statement: Conversion rates have increased as customers are more aware of insurance value
items.quote: our conversion rate has gone up. So, for the people who are coming, more of them are buying, because I guess they are a little bit more aware about the value of insurance.

items.statement: Agent mix shifted to 83% premium from small agents vs 50-50 a year ago
items.quote: 83% of the premium comes from the small agents now. If you look at the same number a year ago, that would have been close to 50-50 in terms of premium.

items.statement: PB Health acquired one operating hospital in Noida (₹150 Cr revenue, ₹20-30 Cr profit) and launching second in Gurugram within weeks
items.quote: We've acquired one hospital, which is an operating hospital, makes about ₹20 -30 Cr of profit in a year, does about ₹150 Cr of revenue. So that's operational and running in Noida. Our next hospital is to go live in the next few weeks.

items.statement: Management discussed buybacks and dividends informally but no board-level discussion or formal plan exists
items.quote: at least once we've had a conversation about buybacks and divid ends. That's it. I can just say that. That's a conversation. It's not even gone to the board

items.statement: Paisabazaar employee productivity and incentive penetration now at Policybazaar levels
items.quote: incentives is a much higher percentage of their comp. They're almost unbelievable, because it has almost come to Policybazaar levels in that respect.

items.statement: Term insurance commission less than 5% on NPV basis over 30-40 year product life
items.quote: when you do that, then you'll actually find that, especially in term insurance, the commission is not as high as people think it is. Commission is less than 5%.

items.statement: ULIP take rates are lowest in business; giving everything to customer with waiver of premium and tax advantages
items.quote: our take rate s on the ULIP side are probably the lowest take rates, probably, of the entire business that we do

items.statement: Contribution margin dip in new initiatives due to mix changes; focus on 12-month rolling basis not quarterly
items.quote: There is some small mix changes, sometimes there is quarterly, annual shifts. Please, in our numbers, just look at them on a 12 -month r olling basis

items.statement: POSP competitors merging/trying other things; PB now much larger than competition with opportunity to deepen penetration in smaller cities
items.quote: some of the competitors, we are now much larger than the competition than we've ever been. And the number two thing is that there are some changes going on; somebody is merging with somebody.

items.statement: PB Corporate team mostly internally built with strong culture; barely hiring from outside
items.quote: We are barely hiring f rom outside, it's mostly internally built and internally driven, and we are building our own culture which is, as most of you appreciate, is quite strong

items.statement: Industry cost structure unsustainable without participation from regular claimers; doing this out of necessity not joy
items.quote: without this participation, please appreciate the cost is going to become unsustainable for the industry; we're not doing this out of joy, we're doing this out of necessity.

items.statement: Expects revenue growth acceleration in FY27 across payments, financial services, and marketing services recovery
items.quote: We are seeing strong tailwinds in payments, both in offline merchants as well as online merchants, which obviously has a full license now. And is adding new customers and so on. And we are also seeing very good growth in financial services.

items.statement: Targets 15-20% EBITDA margin in 2.5 to 3 years from now
items.quote: EBITDA, we will maintain about two and a half to three years from now, that we should be able to get to those sorts of EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Postpaid relaunch ramp-up significantly faster than previous iteration
items.quote: Yeah, Manish, better than last time. Classic internet dissemination or diffusion of services style. It took X number of time. This is taking X by a significantly large number of time.
