items.quote: So yes, in HAM only we have one project which is MPRDC, rest all projects, HAM projects are from NHAI.

items.statement: Higher net worth requirements and technical eligibility norms favor established players like Ceigall
items.quote: The tightening of the technical and the financial eligibility norms in the bidding process, higher net worth requirement, additional performance securities, and the greater emphasis on the PPP projects continue to favour established players with the proven execution capabilities and credentials.

items.statement: International bid pipeline includes INR13,000 crores highway project in Romania (17 km) and AED250 million project in Dubai
items.quote: And international only one tender was there that was Sobha in Dubai and one tender in EU. Sobha was about AED250 million and in EU it was close to INR13,000 crores, which is again under evaluation, which is in Romania.

items.statement: LOA received for Sahebganj–Areraj–Bettiah corridor, the single biggest project at INR2,160 crores total project cost
items.quote: One of the key highlights for the year was the LOA of Sahebganj–Areraj–Bettiah corridor, which remains the biggest project, single biggest project Ceigall has received till date. The total project cost is INR2,160 crores.

items.statement: Delhi-Amritsar-Katra Expressway project achieved COD during FY26
items.quote: Additionally, the Delhi-Amritsar-Katra Expressway project has successfully achieved COD during the year, marking it an important milestone in our project lifecycle.

items.statement: Entered binding document for Malout Abohar Sadhuwali HAM asset monetization with NEO Asset Management; non-binding offers signed for Bathinda-Dabwali and Jalbehra Shahbad
items.quote: On the HAM monetization front, I am pleased to share that Financial Year '26 has been a defining year for our capital recycling strategy. We have entered into a binding document for Malout Abohar Sadhuwali asset with NEO Asset Management. This is the first transaction of its kind for Ceigall. It validates our execute-monetize-recycle framework. For Bathinda-Dabwali and Jalbehra Shahbad, we have si

items.statement: Unencumbered cash of INR166 crores and unencumbered FDR of INR75 crores as on March 31, 2026 (corrected from earlier stated INR266 crores and INR146 crores)
items.value: INR166 crores cash, INR75 crores FDR
items.quote: We have an unencumbered cash lying in our bank on 31st March, which is close to INR266 crores, and unencumbered FDR close to INR146 crores (It was erroneously mentioned that the unencumbered cash and unencumbered FDR stood at INR 266 crores and INR 146 crores, respectively. The actual figures should be read as INR 166 crores for unencumbered cash and INR 75 crores for unencumbered FDR. ).

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20-30-40% with order book expected to rise from Rs 199 cr to Rs 275-300 cr in 15-20 days
items.quote: I will only tell you why we are conservative and giving you the estimates of 20 to 30 to 40 percent. We are entering the new year with 199 and in 15 days time you will see the numbers going to upwards of 275 to 300 crores.

items.statement: Order book of Rs 199 cr with pipeline of Rs 480 cr; expected to jump to nearly Rs 300 cr in next 15-20 days
items.quote: Our order book of approximately 199 crores, it has gone up already by now, along with a pipeline of 480 crores.

items.statement: Order book expected to reach Rs 275-300 cr in 15-20 days with execution targeted by September-October
items.quote: We are entering the new year with 199 and in 15 days time you will see the numbers going to upwards of 275 to 300 crores. And these all have to be done in the next. And this, the year is just beginning, and this has to be executed by September, October.

items.statement: Consciously accepted tighter margins in data centre, solar, semiconductor projects to build credentials and pipeline; 68 cr solar project was a benchmark
items.quote: From a strategic standpoint, we made a conscious decision to accept relatively tighter margins in data centre orders, solar orders, and semiconductor projects to establish credentials and build a strong pipeline of orders.

items.statement: Expect margin improvement after reference projects commission; Altair merger plugged Rs 1 cr annual drain
items.quote: After a reference commissioning, I don't think so. We will need to then take business decisions on the on the on the new projects that has largely been taken care of.

items.statement: Hyderabad facility on 2 acres with 50,000 sq ft built-up area, capacity of 2,000 sq m/day, one PUF and one rock wool panel line
items.quote: Our Hyderabad facility spans approximately 2 acres of land with a built -up area of around 50,000 square feet and a production capacity of about 2,000 square metres per day, supported by 1 manufacturing line for puff and one for the ro ck wool panels

items.statement: Factory automation and innovations improved margins from feared 5-6% to 7.99%; large solar player approved facility after audit
items.quote: Our factory did various innovations which really got the bottom line to 7.99%. At one stage of time, we were, we thought we would be around 5 to 6%, but there are some very beautiful innovations, engineering, supply chain amendments that we did.

items.statement: Entered data centres, solar technology, semiconductor segments with multi-year investment visibility; 23 active solar leads, Waaree/Satvik/Gupin references established
items.quote: During the year, we expanded our presence into data centers, into the solar technology sector, semiconductor segments, areas that are expected to see sustained multi-year investments.

items.statement: Waaree 68 cr solar project commissioning by July; 23 active solar leads; CG Electronics semicon reference; large solar player approved factory
items.quote: A key milestone here was the 68 crore body solar project, reinforcing our focus on long-term growth over short-term margins. We have already seen the results of that, that with that order there was substantial amount of orders which flowed in based on that benchmark creation by us.

items.statement: Another 1-2 large solar orders of Rs 60-80 cr each expected soon; customers waiting for finalization
items.quote: Between 60 to 80 crores, you will find very soon one more, two more, two more.

items.statement: One of two remaining Indian cleanroom players after Japanese acquisitions; targeting vacuum in solar/data centre before semiconductor where Japanese are established
items.quote: We are building India's largest clean room company. One of the two companies that remained in game, the rest of our competition is now acquired by the Japanese.

items.statement: Aart revenue doubled from Rs 14 cr to Rs 34 cr driven by non-pharma and microelectronics references; Kelvin at 60.53% stake strengthening HVAC
items.quote: Aart has more than doubled. Aart is where FTCL, your company, holds 28% stake. They have increased the top line from 14 crores to 34 crores, driven by reference wi ns in non-pharma and

items.statement: Altair merged into Advantek, stake increased to 34.99%; plugged Rs 1 cr annual loss; planning to raise Kelvin stake to 70-72%, Aart stake increase later
items.quote: Advantek we have now, we have 80% in Altair, Advantek by twenty-six percent, we amalgamated, and now... Resultant, we are holding 30, 34.99 %.

items.statement: Plan to increase Kelvin stake to 70-72% soon; Aart stake increase when compliance readiness and numbers hit
items.quote: Kelvin, we have gone to 60 and we are going to, we're going to, we're going to enhance the stake very soon there to 70 to 72%.

items.statement: Working capital and debt to rise near-term due to large order execution; retention collections from H2 FY27 to improve cycle
items.quote: You will see for the moment the debt rising, the working capital rising, because we have borrowed to meet the... Fantastic demand which is emerged.

items.statement: Approaching clients for price revision under force majeure due to war-driven commodity inflation, aluminium/power/gas shortages
items.quote: So when this particular thing hit us, there are our team is approaching all the clients due to force majeure. We are approaching all the clients for a price revision.

items.statement: T-grade modular ceiling system developed for semiconductor/solar; load capacity 1500-1600 kg; lighter 70mm version for solar, 130mm/210mm versions for semi
items.quote: And that is what we have today, a very strong system which can take loads of around 1500, 1600 kilos, which can be modified very quickly.

items.statement: Employee costs increased to build capacity for future growth; top-class talent acquisition underway for Vision 2030
items.quote: We also continue to invest in people and infrastructure with employee costs increasing as we build capacities for future growth and execution at scale.

items.statement: Supply chain disruptions, steel price spikes, raw material shortages, geopolitical factors caused March delays; force majeure clauses invoked
items.quote: We also experienced some delays during March due to the global geopolitical factors and raw material shortages, which impacted some of the projects timeline.

items.statement: Advantek pursuing Euro certification to open export markets; engaging administration for PLI coverage on import substitution
items.quote: You will see, you will see that happening. So, when European certification happens, our markets are open, so advantek will grow faster.

items.statement: Rs 84 lakh sundry debtor write-off per NCLT order; Rs 1 cr one-time legacy impact from Altair-Advantek merger
items.quote: From a financial standpoint, there was a write-off approximately of 84 lakhs in sundry debtors as per an NCLT order, which had an impact on profitability of the year.

items.statement: Consolidated FY26 revenue Rs 221.72 cr (+46.93% YoY), EBITDA Rs 23.16 cr (+28.31%), PAT Rs 15.82 cr (+18.95%)
items.quote: From a financial standpoint, in FY26, we reported a consolidated total income of 221.72 crores up 46.93% year on year from 150.90 crores last year, with a EBITDA at 23.16 crores, growing 28.31% year on year from 18.5 18.05 crores.

items.statement: Standalone FY26 revenue Rs 143.39 cr (+2.38%), EBITDA Rs 12.96 cr (-21.5%), PAT Rs 9.06 cr (-24.75%) due to future-readiness investments
items.quote: On A standalone basis, the company reported a total income of 143.39 crores, up 2.38% year on year from 140.05 crores last year. EBITDA stood at 12.96 as compared to 16.51 crore, down 21.5% year on year and PAT at 9.06 versus 12.04 in the previous year, down 24.75% year on year.

items.statement: H1 FY27 execution of Rs 200 cr order book possible; H2 historically stronger than H1 across last 4-5 years
items.quote: Otherwise, this 200 for sure will be definitely within six months.

items.statement: Projected revenue growth of 35% to 40% for FY27 with EBITDA margin target of 10% to 10.5%
items.quote: We grew about 40% last year in terms of revenue, and we have historically mentioned that we will be looking for 40% growth for the next two years. So, yes, the projected revenue growth is about 35% to 40%.

items.statement: Targeting Contract Manufacturing revenue share of 55% to 60% and Services share of 9% to 10% in FY27
items.quote: We will be looking to target about 55% to 60% contribution from Contract Manufacturing and Services I think somewhere around 9% to 10% that we have really maintained historically as well.

items.statement: EBITDA margin sweet spot maintained at 10% to 10.5% excluding one-time provisions
items.quote: No, so we would maintain an EBITDA of around 10 % to 10.5%. That is our sweet spot, and we will keep our consistent growth and numbers in the area.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin at 8.8% after INR 5 crore expected credit loss provision
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter grew to 202% year -on-year to about INR 31 crores, with EBITDA margins improving by 431 basis points year -on-year to 8.8%.

items.statement: DAAS execution pipeline of 12+ active projects with INR 1,800+ crores GDV under execution
items.quote: Our DAAS execution pipeline remains strong with currently about 12 plus active projects and about INR 1800 plus crores of GDV under execution, providing strong future revenue visibility.

items.statement: Contract Manufacturing capacity of 9 million metric tons annual offtake giving INR 900-1,000 crores annual revenue potential
items.quote: With respect to the numbers with the current asset base, we have about 9 million metric tons of offtake annually. That's about INR 900 crores to INR 1,000 crores of material capacity on an annual basis.

items.statement: Revenue predictability of INR 6,000+ crores over next five years from current asset base and Capacite contract
items.quote: So, the current asset base actually gives us a revenue predictability of more than INR 6,000 crores for the next five years.

items.statement: Planning INR 25-50 crores investment in Contract Manufacturing capacity deposits in FY27
items.quote: We will look to invest more in this financial year, maybe about INR 25 crores to 50 crores, depending on the opportunities that we get.

items.statement: Contract Manufacturing utilization improved to 50% in Q4 FY26 from 39% YoY, targeting 75-80% peak utilization in FY27
items.quote: We will be looking to reach a peak utilization of more than 75% to 80% in this financial year itself.

items.statement: Annualized utilization rate well above 65-70% based on Q4 FY26 performance
items.quote: If you look at our utilization and that to just the 4th Quarter, at an annualized rate, we are well above 65% to 70%.

items.statement: Asphalt revenues grew 88% sequentially to INR 30 crores in Q4 FY26 with active customers nearly doubling to 28
items.quote: Another important highlight during the quarter was the strong traction in asphalt, which is our newly launched product category. Revenues from asphalt increased to INR 30 crores in Q4 2026, growing 88% sequentially.

items.statement: DAAS revenues grew 264% YoY and 61% QoQ to INR 36 crores in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our DAAS, Developer-as-a Service, business also continued to scale well during the quarter. DAAS revenues stood at INR 36 crores in the quarter, registering a growth of 264% year -on-year and 61% sequentially.

items.statement: Net working capital days reduced to 66 days in FY26 from 110 days YoY, targeting to sustain or improve
items.quote: The net working capital days further reduced to 66 days in FY26 from 110 days a year ago, while the net debt -to-equity improved significantly to (-0.09x).

items.statement: Stuck receivables reduced to INR 40-42 crores with significant recovery expected in FY27
items.quote: The 180 -plus number, the stuck receivables, now are in the range of about INR 40 crores, INR 42 crores, and we expect a significant amount of recovery in this financial year.

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity improved to -0.09x in FY26; working capital facilities of INR 100-150 crores being secured
items.quote: We got a INR 30 crores sanction from one of the banks, and this is what we have mentioned before also that we will be going for about INR 100 crores to INR 150 crores of working capital facilities.

items.statement: Raw material cost inflation fully passed through; steel price changes do not impact profitability
items.quote: For us, it is a clear pass -through. Our business model is such, if steel is sold at 90,000 and if the market is at 95 ,000, so for us, it is a complete pass -through.

items.statement: Contract Manufacturing grew 169% YoY in Q4 FY26 with volumes up 91% to 11.29 lakh metric tons
items.quote: Our Contract Manufacturing business scaled strongly during the quarter, with revenues growing 169% year-on-year. Volumes delivered increased 91% year -on-year to 11.29 lakh metric tons in Q4 Financial Year 2 026.

items.statement: Wallet share ranges from 25-50% for top customers to 5-10% for very large companies, aiming to increase across all
items.quote: It is a mixed bag, right from the top most customers where we actually contribute to maybe somewhere around 25% to 50% of their demand to then going to maybe about just 5% to 10% in terms of companies which are very, very big.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 targeting 85-90% revenue predictability for the full year through order tie-ups
items.quote: Our aim is in Q1, we should be able to predict around 85% to 90% of our top line and similarly of the bottom line as well.

items.statement: Operating cash flow turned strongly positive at INR 142 crores in FY26
items.quote: Operating cash flow also turned strongly positive during the year, reaching INR 142 crores, reflecting disciplined working capital management, stronger cash generation and a structurally improved business model.

items.statement: OCF-to-PAT ratio currently ~1:2, targeting ~1:1.5 in FY27
items.quote: Ratio. I mean, currently we are at about 1 :2, somewhere around that, and I think the next year we will be looking to be somewhere around 1 :1.5 maybe.

items.statement: Took INR 5 crore additional expected credit loss provision in Q4 FY26 as conservative approach on receivable risk
items.quote: We have taken an additional expected credit loss of about INR 5 crores. This is in line with taking a more conservative approach in terms of the receivable risk that we generally take in our balance sheet.

items.statement: Business model moat built on execution capability, technology platform handling 800 daily deliveries and 6.5 lakh documents digitized annually
items.quote: Today, we are handling about 800 deliveries per day. We are handling thousands of documents. Last year itself, we digitized about 6.5 lakh documents, and we have reached a point where we are creating automated entries using AI just by clicking a picture of a delivery chalan.

items.statement: Technology platform minimizes dependency on human workforce enabling operating leverage
items.quote: The model that we operate on we keep our costs significantly under control because the entire business is managed to the tech platform that we have developed, and that keeps the dependency on human workforce to a minimum.

items.statement: Technology platform to be opened to customers/vendors via subscription or transaction fee model in future
items.quote: There will be an option to kind of open it up to customers and vendors, but we don't look at this as a pure SaaS model where we will be selling the program that we have built.

items.statement: Revenue expected to cross INR 1,000–1,050 crores in FY27 with SessionM acquisition closed
items.quote: With the acquisition having closed, we are comfortable that revenues will cross INR 1,000–1,050 crores in FY27.

items.statement: Run rate ARR at INR 765 crores end of FY26, excluding SessionM acquisition closed May 1st
items.quote: We ended the year at a run rate of INR765 crores.

items.statement: New ACV of INR 121 crores in FY26, similar to prior year, from new logos and expansion
items.quote: in terms of new business, we continue to see strong ne w business. We have new ACV of INR121 crores, similar to that of last year

items.statement: Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin 19%, full year FY26 14.7%, up from prior year
items.quote: We closed Q4 at a 19% adjusted EBITDA margin. A good improvement from last year. For the full year again, we had a pretty good 14.7% margin.

items.statement: Steady-state EBITDA margin target 25–30% driven by 70% gross margin, 15–16% tech, similar sales & marketing, 5–7% G&A
items.quote: I think this is a very high gross margin business. So, we at steady state we'll be at like a 70% gross margin. We spend about 15% to 16% on tech, we spend a similar amount on sales and marketing, we spend about 5% to 7% on G&A. So, net-net, this should be a 25% to 30% steady-state, probably more, EBITDA margin business.

items.statement: Organic platform NRR 114% delivers 85–90% gross margin on expansion revenue, lifting overall gross margin ~1% in FY26
items.quote: Looking at FY26 over FY25, our overall gross m argins increased by about a percent thanks to this overall NRR of 110%, right

items.statement: Inorganic NRR 94% in FY26 due to migration discounts and churn during platform upgrades from Brierley and Persuade
items.quote: On the inorganic side, our net retention rate for the year is 94%. As we had mentioned in the DRHP and spoken about last time as well, typically on inorganic, you acquire the business, you get a bunch of customers, then you upgrade them onto the Capillary platform from the older platform that they were on. During this upgrade, you tend to give them a discount, not everyone migrates, right?

items.statement: AI-led migration platform developed to accelerate customer upgrades from acquired stacks to Capillary in 12–18 months vs 24–36 months previously
items.quote: we've now developed an AI-led platform to upgrade customers from our acquired stacks to Capillary. We think this will significantly improve the pace of, you know, upgrades, one. Second, I think it also improves the experience for the customer. So, instead of a big migration and a lot of work, it's typically a two-to-four-week UAT which then the customer needs to do. We are very hopeful that this w

items.statement: Operating cash flow INR 150 crores vs adjusted EBITDA INR 107 crores in FY26; free cash flow to PAT 200%; upfront billing and collection
items.quote: The business inherently generates cash, and this can be seen from the fact that we had adjusted EBITDA of INR107 crores and operating cash flows of INR150 crores. Now, this happens because we bill and collect money upfront in a healthy growing business. So, a good KPI to look at over here is free cash flow to PAT. That's also at a very healthy number of 200%.

items.statement: Cash return on invested capital 22%; return on capital employed 3% in FY26
items.quote: And in terms of return on capital employed, we have seen a constant improvement and today stand at about 3%. And a more relevant term for a cash-generating business like ours is a cash return on invested capital, and this stands at 22%.

items.statement: Finance cost ~INR 1 crore in Q4; accumulated tax losses keep tax expense negative; depreciation & amortization ~INR 19 crores in Q4
items.quote: Then about depreciation and amortization exp ense of about INR19 crores for Q4. Again, this trend would continue given the acquisitive nature of the business. And finance cost of about a crore

items.statement: Exceptional income INR 25 crores in Q4 from churn indemnity under Kognitiv acquisition; one-time, excluded from normalized PAT
items.quote: In Q4 we had a one-time exceptional income of INR25 crores. Now, this exceptional income represents compensation received under a churn indemnity clause in the Kognitiv acquisition, which was triggered because seller failed to meet certain agreed commitments.

items.statement: SessionM integration may dilute percentage margin expansion in FY27 despite absolute EBITDA growth; migration discounts and churn on inorganic base
items.quote: Now, in terms of the percentage numbers, you might see a dip given we have just announced acquisition of SessionM. But on absolute dollar or rupee value number, you would continue to see healthy growth.

items.statement: Contribution margin improved 170 bps sequentially in Q4 FY26, driven by ~110 bps logistics cost reduction and ad revenue growth.
items.quote: A lot of that is that logistics down about 110 basis points. This is coming as you scale back, your in-sourcing push, right?

items.statement: Q4 FY26 exit contribution margin at 4% baseline after recovering from Q2/Q3 FY26 logistics disruptions.
items.quote: So that one-time logistics disruption is kind of behind us. And hence, going forward, the baseline from contribution margin perspective is the 4% Q4 exit rate that we have.

items.statement: Fulfillment margin has scope to improve over next two quarters alongside ad revenue growth.
items.quote: I think there is still in addition to ad revenues improving there is still some scope to increase our inaudible 50:05 margins which might happen over the next two quarters.

items.statement: Meesho Mall contribution margin currently lower than core marketplace as business is in investment phase for next few years.
items.quote: So the contribution margin would be lower than the core marketplace, primarily because right now in the investment phase our goal is to on-board a lot more brands.

items.statement: Annual transacting users grew 33% YoY; India online transactor penetration ~30% vs 80%+ in other emerging markets.
items.quote: India is closer to 30%. And that's why even at a large base we are able to grow our annual transacting user base at 33% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: First-year user frequency has doubled over last three years due to pricing, assortment, and AI improvements.
items.quote: Almost a doubling of frequency has happened from a baseline perspective in the last three years.

items.statement: Mature cohorts (FY24 and before) reach 15+ orders per year; comparable Chinese value e-commerce at ~100x frequency.
items.quote: As users kind of mature on the platform, their frequency in almost a three-year time period starts going up to 15 times or more.

items.statement: Prepaid share increasing; prepaid orders have lower revenue but also lower cost, net neutral on contribution margin.
items.quote: And typically prepaid orders will have lower revenue but also lower cost. So from a contribution margin perspective, they will be net neutral.

items.statement: Cash-on-delivery share declining due to prepaid discounts and lower prepaid order costs; BNPL still early.
items.quote: The cost of prepaid orders kind of coming down and we passing consequentially some of them back to our consumers with better prepaid discounts, etc etera. have been the driving force so far in terms of cash on delivery share coming down.

items.statement: Logistics cost reduction driven by prepaid mix shift, volume density gains, and Valmo innovations.
items.quote: One I think which we briefly touched upon, the movement from cash on delivery to prepaid transactions has been improving the cost structure that we have.

items.statement: Valmo sort centre automation planned over next few years; may use partner investments or own capex based on payback math.
items.quote: our goal is in the next few years to basically bring state -of-the-art automation within all our sort

items.statement: No specific capex model pinned down for mid-mile automation; will decide based on payback period.
items.quote: We haven't pinned down a specific model. We continue to kind of see pretty good encouraging results from some of our partners who would want to kind of invest and set up some of these facilities on our behalf.

items.statement: Ad revenue as % of NMV increased QoQ in Q4 FY26; ad product catalogs live grew >40% YoY and QoQ.
items.quote: The number of catalogs or products which are now live on kind of ads has improved significantly on a Y-o-Y basis, more than kind of 40%, but even on a Q-o-Q basis continues to see improvement.

items.statement: Over two-thirds of sellers by GMV active on ads; focus on activating more sellers and products before pricing.
items.quote: More than two thirds of our sellers when weighted by GMV are active on ads.

items.statement: Meesho Mall targets mass India with affordable brands, not just premium customers; national and regional brands scaling selection.
items.quote: Meesho Mall is not just focused on the premium customer. I think it's going to be focused on anyone who cares about value. So, it's going to be mass India.

items.statement: Seller concentration decreasing as more sellers become active and larger; Pareto seller base expanding rapidly.
items.quote: The concentration on sellers continues to kind of reduce as we have more and more sellers who kind of become active as well as larger on the platform.

items.statement: Quarterly cash flow volatile due to NMV timing in last 15-20 days; LTM FCF better trajectory measure.
items.quote: So, let's say in a quarter where there is more, I would say sale or NMV which is coming in the last sort of 15 to 20 days of the quarter, versus let's say a subsequent quarter, then we see this kind of volatility.

items.statement: Tax payments adjusted from net cash balance; expected to be returned based on profit trajectory.
items.quote: Some of the taxes that have been kind of paid out in terms of cash payouts, those we expect to be returned back to the company based on the trajectory of our sort of overall profit and PPT.

items.statement: No specific EBITDA break-even guidance; FCF improving quarterly but Q2/Q3 FY26 logistics headwinds impact carries over.
items.quote: There will -- we'll have impact over a 12-month period, so if anything, which we had which stems in Q2 and Q3 of FY '26 will continue to last for some time and hence there will be consequential impact of that being carried over for the next few quarters as well.

items.statement: People cost growth lower than NMV growth; operating leverage expected over next few years.
items.quote: Our NMV will increase and our people cost and NMV growth there would be lower than our NMV growth rate.

items.statement: NMV/GMV ratio ~58.8% in FY26, stable at 58-60% for last three years.
items.quote: I think roughly the NMV to GMV ratio has been between 58% to 60% for the last three years. I think for FY2026 as well the number is about 58.8% to be specific.

items.statement: Average SKUs per order close to 1; platform built for frictionless single-SKU orders from different sellers.
items.quote: Hence the number of SKUs per order are at pretty close to one or sort of slightly higher than one.

items.statement: High inflation generally a tailwind for value-focused players as consumers trade down; absolute spend may be headwind.
items.quote: Value-focused sort of companies actually tend to gain share during times when inflation goes higher because of course budgets are tighter for people across.

items.statement: Marketing spend governed by ROI hurdle rate, not % of NMV; will invest aggressively while returns attractive.
items.quote: We look at what is the return that this spend is generating and as long as that spend is generating above our sort of hurdle rate returns. Then we kind of continue to invest in terms of growing our market.

items.statement: Technology infrastructure costs have 2-3 year cloud contract cycles; renegotiation yields discounts as scale increases.
items.quote: A large proportion of this cost is in relation to cloud providers. And there we have a certain contract life cycle of two to three years where we kind of renegotiate some of those contracts.

items.statement: Valmo share not target-driven; volumes allocated to most cost-efficient partner per lane (currently ~50-55%).
items.quote: We do not take a specific goal of how much Valmo share should be. We will continue to give volumes to the player who is the most cost-efficient for every lane.

items.statement: Third-party logistics partners profitable on Meesho volumes; no incentive to reduce capacity; win-win relationship.
items.quote: We believe that all our third-party logistics partners make money when they serve our volumes. So I don't think there's any incentive for anyone to not work with us.

items.statement: FY27 credit growth guided at 1-2% above industry growth
items.quote: We expect our credit growth to be 1% or 2% over the industry growth.

items.statement: FY27 NIM guided at 3.75-3.80% for full year
items.quote: With respect to margins, we expect that NIMs to be in the range of 3.75% to 3.8% for the full year, though we are at 4% plus at the exit quarter of this year.

items.statement: FY27 ROA guided at 1.7-1.8% for full year
items.quote: Given the current macroeconomic environment and the anticipated effects on the net interest margins discussed earlier, we expect the ROA for the full year to be between 1.7% to 1.8%.

items.statement: FY27 credit cost expected below 1%
items.quote: Credit cost, I can think around less than 1% we can think of.

items.statement: FY27 GNPA expected below 1.5%, net NPA below 1%
items.quote: GNPA is expected to be less than 1.5% and net NPA to be less than 1% for the full year.

items.statement: FY27 slippages expected below 1% of asset book
items.quote: Slippages would be expected to be below 1% of the asset book.

items.statement: FY27 LCR to be maintained at 115-120%
items.quote: LCR would be maintained around 115% to 120%.

items.statement: FY27 cost-to-income ratio guided below 50%
items.quote: Our cost-to-income ratio would be below 50% as we have been continuously planning, and we'll endeavor to retain that way.

items.statement: FY27 investment portfolio yield enhancement of 15-20 bps via HTM rebalancing
items.quote: We expect 15 to 20 basis points investment portfolio yield, yield enhancement through strategic rebalancing of the HTM portfolio during '26-'27.

So, our exposure to US market is not direct. It is indirect and we are impacted indirectly and also recovering indirectly

items.statement: Geopolitical risks: Gulf war disrupting gas supply and freight; US tariffs impacting export cycles; gas cost volatility; delayed cost pass-through in denim/knit; FTA benefits not yet realised
items.quote: the recent impact of the Gulf War is also very significant. We have headed into global uncertainties, and these things have also disrupted the trade flows. The impact has been visible in terms of volatility in the key raw material costs and has also significantly increased the other cost components, like dyes and chemical costs, freight costs, impacting the overall cost structure of all textile pr

items.statement: Chhata spinning operations curtailed (~₹250 crore revenue impact in FY26); focus on profitable revenue over volumes; no further spindle/loom closures planned currently
items.quote: we closed Chhata operations. So, for the year, we had approximately ₹250 crore of revenue from Chhata spinning. So, which has impacted this revenue degrowth. And second has been a tough marketing environment, particularly because of the U.S. tariff, which we have witnessed in Quarter 3 that impacted our major exports.

items.statement: Core business mid-term organic growth target 16-18% YoY
items.quote: As you know, during the last couple of quarters, as part of GREAVES.NEXT strategy, I have said that our growth ambition in the midterm is between 16% to 18%. So, we continue to hold that.

items.statement: Core business EBITDA margin target 13-15% as business scales
items.quote: Once again, we have said that we will maintain 13% to 15% EBITDA margins as we scale the business.

items.statement: Capex plan INR 500-700 crore over next 5 years focused on product development, capability enhancement, international expansion
items.quote: So, after the revamp of the strategy and launch of GREAVES.NEXT, we earmarked INR 500 crores to INR 700 crores of CAPEX. This CAPEX will be focused in three major areas.

items.statement: Invested in dual conveyor setup for single-cylinder engines, robotic AI inspection system at Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar plant, conveyorized cable assembly line at Excel facilities
items.quote: We invested in a dual conveyor setup for our single-cylinder engines, which will lead to capacity increase to meet the growing demand. We also deployed a robotic vision-based AI inspection system to enhance quality control, traceability, and efficiency at our plant in Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar. We commissioned a conveyorized cable assembly line in Excel facilities.

items.statement: Secured single largest institutional order worth INR 35 crore for gensets covering supply, installation, commissioning and long-term maintenance
items.quote: We also secured our single largest institutional order worth INR 35 crores. This covers end-to-end delivery, including supply, installation, commissioning and long-term maintenance.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA grew 49% YoY in Q4; standalone EBITDA margin expanded 40 bps in FY26 supported by strong demand and cost optimization
items.quote: For FY '26, our standalone revenue stood at INR 2,365 crores, with an EBITDA of INR 320 crores, with PBT before exception al items at INR 312 crores, reflecting a 23% year-on-year growth, with EBITDA supported by 40 basis point margin expansion, supported by strong demand and cost optimization initiatives.

items.statement: Input cost pressures from aluminum, copper, platinum; passthrough mechanism activated in Q1 to recover margins
items.quote: However, there is a passthrough mechanism, which we have already activated in Q1. So, therefore, we do see some recovery on account of price.

items.statement: International revenues increased from ~9% in FY25 to 13% of total in FY26; deepened Euro V+ engine exports via Ligier partnership across Europe, Middle East
items.quote: As a result of all of these activities, international revenues increased from approximately 9% in FY '25 to 13% of the total in FY '26.

items.statement: Non-3-wheeler diesel engines now 63% of mobility solutions; launched 650 kVA genset with in-house developed engine; Magnus G Max and Magnus 6th Gen scooters launched
items.quote: Within that diesel segment, we have a 63% market share. And that actually has increased during this year. So, that was on the domestic side. On the export side, this is a new business which we started during the year, which is supplying the Euro V+ compliant engines to a micro car application.

items.statement: Onboarded ~350 retailers in aftermarket with roadmap to scale to 3,000 by FY27; exited non-core low-return segments (2-wheeler parts, construction equipment, select battery/digital)
items.quote: We accelerated the retailer engagement, onboarding approximately 350 retailers with a clear roadmap to scale this to 3,000 by FY '27. At the same time, we exited non-core and low-return segments such as two-wheeler parts, construction equipment, and some select battery and digital platform businesses.

items.statement: Remaining 20% stake in Excel Controlinkage to be acquired in Q2 FY27, after which Greaves will own 100%
items.quote: Yes, you're right. We have a predetermined path. The last 20% of the ownership of Excel is planned to be done during Q2, after which we w ill own 100% of the

items.statement: Greaves Electric Mobility FY26 volume growth 51% YoY per Vahan; market share expanded from 3.6% to 4.4%; ~12% share in 4 competitive states (TN, Odisha, Bihar, WB); 8% share in East region
items.quote: As per Vahan, we have delivered a volume growth of 51% year-on-year in Full Year '26. Our market share has expanded from 3.6% in Full Year '25 to 4.4% in Year '26.

items.statement: DRHP for Greaves Electric Mobility IPO extended by SEBI to Sep 30, 2026 due to volatile geopolitical situation; IPO timing to be decided by investment committee
items.quote: The DRHP has been, all DRHPs which were expiring till 30 th of September have been given an extension by SEBI till 30 th of September. So, our DRHP which was expiring on 6th or 7th of May therefore gets extended till 30th of September

items.statement: New Group CFO Manish Poddar joined with 25+ years experience; leadership team strengthened in H2 FY26 with focus on operations capability development
items.quote: I would like to welcome our new Group Chief Financial Officer – Manish Poddar. He is joining our leadership team, and he brings over 25 years of experience across financial leadership, strategy and corporate governance.

items.statement: Watching evolving macroeconomic environment and commodity cycle; will act with agility to mitigate potential headwinds
items.quote: At the same time, as Manish mentioned, we are watching the evolving macroeconomic environment and will act with agility to mitigate any potential headwinds.

items.statement: Focus on maintaining working capital discipline and prudent capital allocation
items.quote: We remain committed to driving operational efficiency, maintaining working capital discipline and ensuring prudent capital allocation.

items.statement: Balance sheet remains strong with healthy cash balance; planned investments aligned with strategic priorities
items.quote: Our balance sheet continues to remain strong with a healthy cash balance. Our planned investments are completely aligned with our strategic priorities, focusing on R&D and technological upgrades, capacity expansion and digital tools.

items.statement: GST 2.0 and stable monetary conditions supported 9% auto industry growth in FY26
items.quote: Here too, the auto industry had a good FY '26. It registered a 9% annual growth. This growth was supported by structural tailwinds such as GST 2.0, along with a stable monetary condition.

items.statement: Multi-fuel technologies to coexist with EVs for extended period; Greaves focused on fuel-agnostic portfolio and OEM partnerships
items.quote: While EV adoption is accelerating, we still see multi-fuel-based technologies will coexist for an extended period. Against this backdrop, our automotive business delivered a 48% year-on-year growth in Quarter 4.

items.statement: Greaves Finance AUM stood at INR 521 crore as of March 2026
items.quote: The Greaves Finance Limited, the total asset under management for the financing business stood at INR 521 crores as on March '26.

items.statement: Impairment provision of ~INR 16 crore taken in Q4 for e-technology investment that did not scale up as expected
items.quote: During this quarter, the management made an impairment for the value of certain tangible and intangible assets under development. This relates to our investment in an e technology, which has not scaaled up or realized our expectations due to the underlying changes in the project execution and customer demand. Resultantly, we have on a conservative basis made a provision of almost INR 16 crores dur

items.statement: FY26 volume and value flat, plus/minus 1% vs prior year
items.quote: However, as you can see from the results, both the top line and the bottom line have more or less remained flat, plus/minus 1% of what it was last year.

items.statement: Expect normal year with 5-10% volume growth next year but high uncertainty
items.quote: We expect that the next year will be like a normal year, which is about 5% to 10% growth rate, but there is too much uncertainty in the future.

items.statement: Margins temporarily improved in March due to inventory lag; expect better margins going forward but not dramatic
items.quote: But we are optimistic that I think we have seen the bottom. So probably the margins going forward will be a little better than what we have experienced in the last year.

items.statement: Ammonia cost doubled from ~INR50/kg to over INR100/kg; finished good prices raised to protect margins
items.value: INR50 to over INR100 per kg
items.quote: Going forward, yes, like ammonia, as you said, we were in the region of about INR50 a kg and now we are over INR100 a kg. So obviously, the cost of production has risen, and we have had to pass it on to customers.

items.statement: Ammonia supply disruption in March resolved; plants running at 60-85% utilisation; expect supply chain to stabilise in 3-6 months
items.quote: Yes. So our plants are running. We have a little bit of headroom. On an average, we must be having between 60% and 85% capacity utilization, and that we continue to get enough raw material to keep there.

items.statement: Ammonia contracts now short-term due to high prices; nobody willing to commit long-term
items.quote: Yes. At the moment, the ammonia contracts are all short term because prices are high and nobody is willing to commit well, it's not day-to-day, but it's fairly short compared to what we used to do earlier because nobody is willing to commit longer term.

items.statement: Kurkumbh project delayed; mechanical completion end of June, commissioning early next quarter
items.quote: Yes. So that project was to be commissioned in this quarter, April to June. We are slightly delayed. It will probably be the beginning of the next quarter that the project will get commissioned. Mechanical completion is going on. Mechanical completion is going to be completed somewhere at the end of June.

items.statement: FY27 capex ~INR80-90 crore for completion of Dahej project and maintenance; no major new projects
items.quote: So around -- it will be around INR80 crores to INR90 crores.

items.statement: Chinese acetonitrile imports reduced after antidumping duty; market share improving
items.quote: In the last quarter, I think there has been some improvement from us. I mean, in the sense that they have reduced their imports because they have raised their prices. So more and more, our market share has been increasing.

items.statement: New methylamine entrant Aarti adds overcapacity; absorption will take time
items.quote: Methylamines, there is an overhang of capacity because a new player has come in. So there's RCF, Balaji, Aarti and us now. So there is a bit of overcapacity of methylamines, and that will take some time to fill up until the market – it is at a level where all of us have underutilization of capacity there.

items.statement: Pharma 50-60% of sales, agro 15-20%, total ~70-75%
items.quote: Maybe between 50% and 60% of our sales are to pharma and another maybe 15%, 20% to agro. Total, it's about 70%, 75%.

items.statement: Overall production volume up ~1% YoY in FY26
items.quote: Yes, I think we have produced overall, I think, about 2% more, 1%? Kanchan Shinde: 1%. Kirat Patel: 1% more than last

items.statement: War-related supply chain uncertainty persists; hope Hormuz Strait reopens; green ammonia 3-5 years away
items.quote: It will take some time for the industry to sort the supply chain out, maybe another 3 months, maybe 6 months for it to stabilize. Hopefully, by that time, all this Hormuz Strait will be opened out, and we will be able to manage a reasonable amount of material coming through.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance 5-10% for next year; top line boosted by 30-40% price increase from February levels
items.quote: Well, between 5% and 10% volume growth. As I said, the prices just now have gone 30%, 40% higher than what they were in February. So in terms of top line, obviously, there will be a lot of increase. But in volume growth, it will be between 5% and 10%.

items.statement: Expect healthy volume growth in FY27 over low base of FY26, targeting positive growth above industry average
items.quote: Yes, we certainly look forward to a positive growth. And it should be in access to the industry average because we had a bad year last year. So, for us, it is a low base on which we have to grow this year. So, we expect healthy growth over last year.

items.statement: Capex on hold; will evaluate after first two quarters of FY27 before deciding on further plans
items.quote: No, we are putting CAPEX on hold because we have already invested for all the developments and we will observe first two quarters as I told you last time before we decide for the further CAPEX plans.

items.statement: Second manufacturing plant timeline undecided; will wait for first two quarters of FY27 to decide when, how, where
items.quote: No. As I said earlier in the question, we will wait for first two quarters to make up our mind when and how, where.

items.statement: Building products margin 14-18%; agriculture margin 8-10% depending on season
items.quote: You see, building products offer a better margin than agriculture. Normally, agriculture would have about 8% to 9% margin, or 10%, it depends on time of the year, while building product offers from 14% to 18%.

items.statement: Agriculture and building product demand back to almost average normal after initial war-related price shock
items.quote: Demand for agriculture and building products were impacted immediately after the war broke out because of the sudden very high increase in the raw material and finished goods prices. But now they have settled. So, demand is again back to almost average normal.

items.statement: PVC resin sourced via combination of local purchase and imports
items.quote: We import and we buy locally as well. So, it is a combination of local as well as import.

items.statement: Market share: MP majority/leading, Rajasthan significant, Maharashtra sub-10% and developing
items.quote: Maharashtra, MP and Rajasthan, if you ask me, MP would have a fairly large market share. We are the leading brand and the majority market share. Rajasthan also, we have a significant market share. But Maharashtra, we are still developing. We are under a development stage. So, we will have much lower market share, maybe sub-10% at the moment

items.statement: Trade receivables declined to INR 28 cr from INR 48 cr due to reduced institutional sales in Q4
items.quote: You see, our outstanding are mostly towards institution. And you must have seen in the Q4, we have reduced our institutional sales as per our projections given to you. So, this is why the outstandings have declined.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 inventory build-up (INR 72 cr) is strategic seasonal stocking for April-June agriculture peak season
items.quote: See, normally you will see every year in March, all the manufacturers build up inventory because the main season starts from April. And you are always ready for the coming season at the end of March because April, May, June is a major quarter for agriculture sales.

items.statement: Targeting substantial revenue increase in FY27 and aim to reach INR 1000 cr revenue guidance previously stated
items.quote: We are working to improve our figures because last year was a very difficult year for us because there was heavy rains, as we have been telling you, in our areas of operation, which has impacted our markets very badly. So, we are revitalizing the whole thing. Fortunately, going forward, if rain gods are right and everything is right, we should be able to aim substantial increase over last year. An

items.statement: FY27 growth dependent on normal monsoon; heavy rains in FY26 badly impacted markets
items.quote: We are working to improve our figures because last year was a very difficult year for us because there was heavy rains, as we have been telling you, in our areas of operation, which has impacted our markets very badly.

items.statement: Loan growth target for FY27 is 15-16% or matching industry growth
items.quote: we are still aiming to get between 15% and 16%. But if the industry were to do higher than that, we will match industry.

items.statement: CEO term ends September 30, 2026; succession process underway with RBI approval timeline
items.quote: my term ends on the 30th of September. And I expect that all of this will happen in such a fashion that the new incumbent can be in position before or immediately after the end of my term.

items.statement: NIM drivers: asset mix shift to Retail/MSME, rate hike benefit, repricing of 60-65% deposits, revenue-focused goal setting
items.quote: The NIM drivers for us are largely change in asset mix, is the biggest driver. So, if we can get more larger proportion of our book to be Retail and MSME, automatically NIMs open up

items.statement: NIM improved 15 bps over last two quarters (6 bps in Q3, 9 bps in Q4) and expected to continue widening
items.quote: over the last two quarters our NIMs have improved by about 15 basis points, I mean six basis points in Q3 and nine basis points in

items.statement: Gold loan book grew 46% YoY to INR24,729 crores with 57.18% average LTV and INR2.71 lakh average ticket size
items.quote: During the last financial year, our gold loan business grew by 46% and now stands at INR24,729 crores with an average LTV of 57.18%.

items.statement: MSME loans grew ~15% YoY; mortgage and auto loans also saw significant growth
items.quote: our focus on MSME loans has ensured that our book has grown by approximately 15% for the year.

items.statement: Portfolio buyouts across products ~INR2,000 crores; shifting preference to PTCs over buyouts
items.quote: Our total portfolio buyout across products is roughly in the order of magnitude of about INR2,000 crores at the end of the last quarter.

items.statement: GNPA 1.43%, NNPA 0.29%, PCR 79.87% (ex write-off), slippage ratio 72 bps FY26, 15 bps Q4, credit cost 3 bps Q4
items.quote: Overall gross NPA reduced by 177 basis points from 3.2% to 1.43%. Net NPA reduced b y 63 basis points from 0.92% to 0.29

items.statement: Gold loan risk managed via VaR framework with caps; 30-day moving average with 25-50% standard deviation applied
items.quote: we are using the Value at Risk framework, and we've built a mechanism by which we actually measure this risk. And using Value at Risk, we can see periods of volatility.

items.statement: Technical write-off INR1,163 crores FY26 (INR1,048 crores in Q4); no P&L impact, only PCR impact
items.quote: these all these accounts have already been 100% provided. Provisions have already been created. So, we are doing the technical write- off

items.statement: ECL transition: no floating provisions held; no material one-time or steady-state impact expected given low SMA (0.6%) and high PCR (80%)
items.quote: we don’t estimate any material impact over there, mainly because of few factors that if you see our numbers, SMA numbers, is on a declining trend and is close to 0.6% of our total book

items.statement: Credit cost at trough (3 bps Q4); expected to trend up due to geopolitical stresses, not improve
items.quote: My own view is that we've seen the trough when it comes to credit cost. Credit cost for this quarter was three basis points. I don't think a credit cost can be lower than this

items.statement: Operating costs to rise from current efficiency frontier; investing in distribution, technology; aim to maintain positive operating leverage
items.quote: we've reached a point where expenses cannot be kept at this level indefinitely and we will have to start doing a little bit of investment both in distribution, a little bit more investment in technology

items.statement: Branch count stable at 948 (down from 955); planned expansion in Tamil Nadu, Andhra, Telangana, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Delhi
items.quote: If you see our numbers for the last seven -eight quarters actually branches have not grown, they've only shrunk. So we came dow n from 955 to 948

items.statement: Launched SIB RED digital bank end-March; building digital assets (Fincredibles blog) for customer acquisition
items.quote: we launched a new digital offering called SIB RED, which is a full-fledged digital bank in and of itself towards the end of March.

items.statement: CASA grew 17.5% YoY to INR39,621 crores; retail deposits (ex-bulk) grew 15% to INR1,20,116 crores
items.quote: CASA amount increased by 17.5% year-on-year to INR39,621 crores.

items.statement: Deposit cost up 2-3 bps Q4 due to selective repricing for growth; 60-65% deposits to reprice lower in FY27
items.quote: we have slightly moved the deposit rate considering the deposit growth. So if you see our deposit prices compared with the market rates, we were little lower than the other competitors.

items.statement: FX revenue streams increased substantially; launching TF Online platform for corporate/MSME export/import engagement
items.quote: There's been very substantial increase in our FX revenue streams. And in order to make that even more buoyant, we are working on a new solution called TF Online

items.statement: Board actively searching for CEO successor; process to conclude before September 30 term end
items.quote: The Board is actively engaged in the search process. I can confirm that the search process is on.

items.statement: Employee expense one-off write-back of ~INR80 crores from actuarial valuation in Q4
items.quote: That is mainly with regard to the write-back what we obtained based on the actuarial valuation. So that amounts to around say close to INR80 crores.
The bank declared a return on asset of 1.03% and a return on equity of 12.76% for the financial year.

items.statement: Geopolitical stresses (Middle East) may deteriorate slippages and credit cost; no material customer behaviour change yet
items.quote: I think if anything, both slippages and credit cost should trend upwards, especially given the geopolitical stresses that we see emanating from the Middle East and elsewhere.

items.statement: ECLGS guarantee claims: first 75% easy, second 25% challenging due to settlement restrictions; new scheme details not fully reviewed
items.quote: getting the first 75%, I think generally has been easy. The second 25% have been a bit of a challenge because there are a few guidelines that are there on the ECLGS which says, see, suppose you were to go for a settlement with a borrower. That is not an allowed method of settlement under the ECLGS scheme.

items.statement: Highest ever net profit INR1,455 crores FY26 (+12% YoY); total business INR2,23,620 crores (+15%)
items.quote: The bank declared its highest ever net profit for the year at INR1,455 crores for the financial year 2025-2026, which implies a growth of 12% compared to INR1,303 crores in the prior year.

items.statement: Soft demand environment due to macroeconomic headwinds and client-specific issues led to revenue erosion
items.quote: our performance during the quarter and year under review reflects a ve ry soft demand environment due to sustained macroeconomic headwinds, leading to some client -specific issues and as a result, erosion of

items.statement: Onboarded Vikram Puranik as COO replacing Selva who stepped down for personal reasons
items.quote: We recently onboarded Vikram Puranik as our Chief Operating Officer. Vikram joins us with a strong background in engineering services, delivery operations and capability building, havin g served as a senior leader at leading engineering services organizations. He comes in place of Selva, who's decided to step down on account of personal

items.statement: Hired new leaders for Data & AI, ERP, Global Partnerships, Life Sciences verticals and Americas business from Tier 1 companies
items.quote: We brought in a leader for our data and AI practice. We brought in a leader for our overall ERP practice. We've brought a leader for our global partnerships and alliances based in San Francisco. And we also now have a new leader for our Lifesciences vertical. As you know, we had inducted Komal Jain as a leader for our Americas business back in

items.statement: Sales team strength to increase 30-40% YoY by middle of FY27
items.quote: By the middle of FY '27, I reckon that our sales team strength would have gone up by 30% to 40% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: No revenue guidance given for FY27 due to market volatility
items.quote: Now going forward, as you know, Girish, we do not give ou t guidance. But if you look at the investments that we have made, we've gotten a large number of leaders who have come in at the leadership level

items.statement: Q4 FY26 TCV deal signings of $208 million, 3% higher than Q3, second consecutive quarter above $200 million
items.quote: We've signed deals worth $208 million TCV during Q4, which is 3% higher than what we signed in Q3 of FY '26.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 18.5%, up 30 bps QoQ; FY26 EBITDA margin 16.3%, up 333 bps YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margin for Q4 increased to 18.5%, which is an expansion of 30 basis points quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Steady-state EBITDA margin expected at 15%+ as investments in sales, leadership, AI orchestration and productivity benefits will erode margins from current levels
items.quote: our steady state margins that we should expect is going to be upward of 15% and there will be an erosion from where we are today, obviously, because of these investments.

items.statement: AI deals require upfront productivity commitments causing revenue deflation in immediate and medium term
items.quote: Now what happens in an AI deal is we have to commit to the savings and underwrite some of the savings right up front, which is why you see revenue deflation in the immediate and the medium term.

items.statement: DSO increased sequentially to 62 days due to unanticipated collection spillover into early April; adjusted DSO would be 55 days
items.quote: While our DSO for the period under review increased sequentially to 62 days, the increase was caused by an unanticipated spillover of some collections in the first couple of days of April. If we would adjust for the collections realized by 3rd of April 2026, our DSO would have been 55 days.

items.statement: Board proposed final dividend of INR 4 per share; total FY26 dividend INR 6.50 per share including interim
items.quote: the Board of Directors has proposed a final dividend of INR 4 per share, subject to shareholders' approval. This, combined with the interim dividend paid out after our Q2 Board meeting, takes our overall dividend for the full financial year to INR 6.50 per share.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 revenue $145.3 million, down 3.7% QoQ in constant currency; FY26 revenue $597.5 million, down 6% YoY in dollar terms
items.quote: revenue for the quarter declining 3.7% quarter-on-quarter in constant currency and in dollar terms, to $145.3 million.

items.statement: FY26 adjusted PAT INR 6,595 million, up 27.6% YoY; adjusted basic EPS INR 22.14 per share
items.quote: Adjusted for this incremental provision for U.S. federal tax and the onetime provision made on account of changes in Labor Code, normalized PAT for the year would have been $74.2 million, up 21.5% year-on-year or INR 659.5 crore, up 27.6% year-on-year. This would translate into an adjusted basic EPS of INR 22.14 per share.

items.statement: Investing in AI platforms, sales team augmentation, leadership hiring, and AI orchestration layer capabilities
items.quote: We continue to make investments in our business, including in the areas that Angan alluded to, i.e., augmentation of our sales team, focus on our AI orchestration layers and enhancement in our domain and service line capabilities.

items.statement: Life Sciences MedTech sector faced client-specific operational issue causing biggest degrowth; issue believed to be behind
items.quote: It is Life Sciences. And within Life Sciences, it is the MedTech sector, medical devices sector. So it is more manufacturing-orientated. So that's where we face the issue, which is why it is reflected in our Life Sciences business.

items.statement: Top 5 clients flatlined due to seasonal issue, not client-specific; growth expected to resume
items.quote: I don't think we have a client-specific issue in our top 5 clients. I think the top 5 clients are pretty strong. It is a seasonal issue. I don't see that to be a problem. The growth will be back on the top 5.

items.statement: Larger players competing for mid-sized deals due to AI leveling playing field; opportunity for smaller companies if AI story executed well
items.quote: Yes. So that is absolutely happening, Girish, because what happens is in an AI world, it becomes a level playing field for all partners to try and bid for all kind of work because it is more outcome-based or nonlinear kind of revenue streams.

items.statement: BFSI spending stable but shifting from traditional services to AI-oriented work; no increase in overall pool size
items.quote: The spending remains to be strong. Only the shift of the spending pool is moving from the more traditional side of the businesses to more AI-oriented work, and we are participating in that and winning our share of the business.

items.statement: Market uncertainty and volatility from trade, tariffs, geopolitics making demand environment challenging; no visibility on Q1 growth resumption
items.quote: The only reason I am holding back on committing anything is because the market is very uncertain and it's volatile. And every quarter, I come and say something and there is a market event that happens that disrupts the equation.

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margin benefited ~340 bps from one-offs: 170 bps forex tailwind, 170 bps from lower provisions (performance-based comp, leave encashment, equity comp from exits)
items.quote: I would say the forex tailwind gave us a 170-basis point benefit. And the other items that I talked about gave us another 170 points benefit. So it's about a 340-point benefit that we got in the fourth quarter.

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents INR 2,637.3 crore, up 19% YoY; strong balance sheet enabling continued investments
items.quote: We ended the year with cash and cash equivalents of INR 2,637.3 crore, up 19% year-on-year.

items.statement: Elevated ETR from incremental U.S. federal tax and Labor Code changes limited to FY26; ETR expected to normalize to historical levels from FY27
items.quote: The elevated ETR due to incremental U.S. tax, as I had called out on our earlier calls, was limited and will be limited to FY '26, and we expect ETR to settle closer to our historical ETR level starting FY '27.

items.statement: Net new TCV soft in Q4 due to client decision delays from uncertainty; deals pushed to Q1, not lost
items.quote: Q4 specifically, our net new is obviously very soft. But I don't think there is anything more to read towards it. It is only because so many of our clients are delaying decision-making because of the uncertainty. It's not that we have lost any deals. It's just getting pushed to Q1.

items.statement: Walked away from low-margin, non-strategic deals costing ~200 bps of growth in FY26
items.quote: at least 200 basis points of growth roughly went away because we walked away from low-margin, non-strategic deals.

items.statement: E&U vertical grew 1.8% QoQ in Q4; other verticals declined due to soft demand and client issues
items.quote: Among our verticals, E&U registered a sequential growth and was up 1.8% during the quarter. The other verticals witnessed a degrowth on account of the reasons I just mentioned.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA $97.5 million, up 18.2% YoY; PAT $58.3 million lower due to Labor Code and U.S. tax impacts
