items.quote: It is truly double digit, most probably, in the mid-teens, I would say. That is what is the expectation for the growth.

items.statement: Stationary engine order book of $100 million finalized, targeting revenue by FY29-30
items.quote: The stationary engine side is the order book is for the first $100 million is finalized and is with us. So as slated earlier -- as stated earlier, I would say, we will be able to reach that $100 million sort of revenue in '29, '30.

items.statement: FY27 capex decision by September; FY28 depends on FY27 performance; monitoring net debt to EBITDA
items.quote: On FY 2027 itself, we are not very clear about the capex as today because we have taken some interim requirements. But September we have to decide on the capex even for FY 2027. FY 2028 depends on the performance of FY 2027.

items.statement: Net debt to EBITDA at 2.43, targeting below 2 in current year and 1.5 subsequently
items.quote: we are already at 2.43 net debt to EBITDA. We are looking at, going forward, it'll be less than 2, I would say, in the coming, the current year itself, totally. And then it'll go down furt her to 1.5

items.statement: Alloy wheel exit rate ~3 million annualized in March; capacity 5.5 million; targeting ~4 million next year (70-80% utilization)
items.quote: our exit rate is around close to 3 million (nos) on the annualized basis as of March, and our capacity is around 5.5 million (nos). I think we should t ouch around close to 4 million (nos) in the next year

items.statement: Powertrain utilization at 65-70% with 85% upper limit; new large engine business at ~10% utilization
items.quote: Powertrain, we are still at around 65%, 70% because there are some pockets and segments where the customers are not doing well. But I think 85% will be the upper limit.

items.statement: Aluminum price pass-through enforced; declining supply where pass-through absent; legacy prices being reset across aluminum plants
items.quote: And also, on the aluminum price reset or the aluminum price pass-through, we have been very clear with the customers. Where aluminum price pass-through is not there, then we are declining to supply.

items.statement: Powertrain margin improvement driven by R&M reduction, manpower efficiency, new products at new prices averaging legacy prices; scale benefits not yet realized
items.quote: I would say that the repair and maintenance which went on for almost 4, 5 quarters, which was depressing the EBIT margins, was the main -- EBITDA margins were the main reason for that change.

items.statement: Input costs rising: power, cutting oil, carbide tools from China, labor (<$1/hr contract labor expected to double/triple); capex cost inflation high due to currency depreciation
items.quote: The new orders are coming at new prices. There are legacy issues which we need to address on all the consumables, like power, the cutting oil, which is petroleum-based, the tools which are carbide based, which is imported from China, which has increased multiple-fold in the last time.

items.statement: Negative working capital impact INR400 cr (FY25) and INR600 cr (FY26) due to aluminum ramp-up; payment cycles now set; similar level expected forward
items.quote: I think the plants which are suppose the aluminum business was ramping up in the last few years. Earlier it was mainly powert rain driven, so that means suddenly there was a spike in the working capital requirement and now rationalization has happened

items.statement: DR Axion greenfield plant at Sriperumbudur: land acquired via Suprash/Srikara for ~INR150 cr; civil construction ongoing; commissioning by December
items.quote: The greenfield project is already on. The civil construction is on, and the plant will be commissioned by December. So next year it will be in operation.

items.statement: Aluminum entities (Craftsman, DR Axion, Sunbeam) consolidation for synergy; targeting ~INR6,500 cr aluminum revenue by FY27; shared campus planned in Chennai
items.quote: We'll be around INR6,500 crore in the aluminum business in the FY 2027 or so. Just an approximation. I don't want to give any guidance. Please, negate that if it is taken as a guidance.

items.statement: Sunbeam capacity utilization ~70% to drop to 45-50% due to exit of unviable legacy products; capacity to be reallocated to new customers/products
items.quote: Capacity utilization, which is around 70%, will come down to around 45%, 50% in the near for the Sunbeam because some of them are legacy products unviable to continue manufacturing.

items.statement: DR Axion utilization at 80-85%; expanding capacity due to strong incremental orders from existing and new Indian OEMs
items.quote: On DR Axion, I think, we are operating at a reasonable capacity, which is beyond this capacity we cannot really extend ourselves because we are a very critical component supplier

items.statement: Alloy wheel revenue ~INR280 cr in FY26; Bhiwadi plant margins high single to double digit; Hosur plant single digit due to ramp-up
items.quote: Around INR280 crores is the revenue in the last financial year for the alloy wheel.

items.statement: Aluminum EBIT margin ~10.3% flat YoY; near-term margin expansion unlikely due to ongoing capex depressing margins; improvement expected after $1B scale and capex slowdown
items.quote: If you're going at this rate, no. Because the future capex in this year will again spoil the margins. Whatever gains we are making on the installed capacity.

items.statement: Aluminum business targeting $1 billion revenue in 2-3 years at current aluminum prices
items.quote: I think it will be 2 to 3 years' time. It is also a little sensitive towards aluminum prices, but I would say that at the current aluminum prices, I think 2 to 3 years we should be there.

items.statement: Manpower cost inflation major concern (20% YoY vs 5-10% historically); automation/semi-automation to offset incremental cost; labor code and minimum wage resets adding pressure
items.quote: What is worrying us more is not the debt, as I mentioned. What is worrying us the inflationary manpower cost, which is very difficult to pass on to customer.

items.statement: Export inquiries increasing from Europe and North America for 4-wheeler aluminum; selective in choosing viable, sustainable business
items.quote: We are getting inquiries for 4- wheelers for export market. Both Europe and North America, we are increasing, and there is more increasing inquiry trend, at least.

items.statement: Alloy wheel expansion Phase 2 deferred; waiting on commodity pass-through stability and import competition post-BIS norms
items.quote: We'll take a decision after this financial year. I don't think we'll take a decision in this financial year to further stretch the alloy wheel capacity.

items.statement: Sunbeam land sale elusive; buyers seeking discount to current market price; prices up 15% YoY due to road widening; not willing to sell at lower price
items.quote: We have seen that the property prices are shooting up. But still, I think the sale is little elusive because whoever is looking for buying it is asking a discount from the current market price.

items.statement: Capex cost inflation high: land prices up, equipment costs up 10-20% in dollar terms over 20 years, but dollar doubled; early capex investment provides competitive advantage
items.quote: The capex cost for anybody entering this business is very, very, very large, totally. Here we are using a mixture of our own equipment manufacturing for the special purpose machines, and very, very prudently we are adjusting the requirements to still be competitive and get more orders.

items.statement: Focus on value-added aluminum (casting + machining); exiting pure casting; 95% of Craftsman aluminum is machined; DR Axion critical casting with basic machining; Sunbeam domestic lacks machining
items.quote: Frankly speaking, we are focusing on value-added products like casting and machining. We are not interested really to do only the casting portion.

items.statement: Domestic farm sector doing better; truck segment muted; export of truck engine blocks continuing contrary to earlier discontinuation plan
items.quote: The domestic business farm sector has been doing better. Truck segment is somewhat muted, I would say, in general. So, the other business about the export of some truck engine blocks to outside India, which we said will be discontinued, but that is going to continue

items.statement: Labor Code and minimum wage resets increasing bottom-of-pyramid labor costs; protests in NCR region; government actions driving wage inflation
items.quote: Now the new labor code also is coming to picture, and this minimum wages will be getting reset. This is on the bottom of the pyramid.

items.statement: No explicit fund raise mentioned; debt reduction via EBITDA growth; land sale of Gurgaon would reduce consolidated debt from INR3,100 cr to ~INR2,700 cr
items.quote: The land sale of Gurgaon, if you take away the land sale of Gurgaon, then look at the debt, we should look at the debt at, say, INR2,700 on the consolidated basis, not at INR3,100.

items.statement: Targets FY27 ROA of 1.2% in Q1 rising to 1.6% by Q4
items.quote: We are guiding for 1.2% ROA for this June quarter and then gradually increasing to 1.6% by Q4 of this year.

items.statement: Targets FY27 cost-to-income ratio of 67-68%
items.quote: On a full year basis in the coming year, we will be targeting somewhere around 67% to 68%.

items.statement: Targets FY27 credit cost of 70-80 bps
items.quote: I think for the next coming year, our credit cost will be somewhere in the region of 70 to 80 bps.

items.statement: Targets FY27 PAT of over Rs 300 crore (2x FY26)
items.quote: So with the credit cycle in the MFI industry behind our back, I think that's the kind of number that we are targeting as a bank.

items.statement: Targets quarterly slippages of Rs 75-90 crore for FY27
items.quote: We would be targeting somewhere -- anywhere between ₹75 crores to ₹90 crores as a whole for the bank on a quarter -on-quarter basis

items.statement: Targets retail asset slippages of 1.25% in H2 FY27
items.quote: I would look at anywhere between 1.25% for the portfolio overall put together.

items.statement: Expects NIM to remain range-bound at 8-9% in FY27
items.quote: I think our NIMs will be range bound between 8% to 9%.

items.statement: Targets asset growth of 20-30% in FY27
items.quote: We're targeting to grow at around closer to 20% to 30% of the asset size.

items.statement: CGFMU claim of Rs 450-550 crore expected in FY27 across 3 cohorts
items.quote: At this particular point in time, we are looking at the first cohort that is to be claimed somewhere in Q1, all things going well. And overall, I think we will be claiming somewhere in the region of ₹450 crores to ₹550 crores

items.statement: CGFMU coverage mitigated Rs 650 crore P&L impact during stress cycle
items.quote: The CGFMU initiative has played a significant role during the stress cycle and has provided mitigation of approximately ₹650 crores in terms of P&L impact

items.statement: Inclusive finance disbursements back to Rs 500 crore per month in Q4
items.quote: On the inclusive finance side, disbursements have largely returned to earlier run rates of ₹500 crores per month of disbursements

items.statement: Digital deposits contribute ~50% of incremental deposit flows
items.quote: If you look at things as they stand today, about 50% of our net incremental flows are coming from the digital channel, and that will continue for this year as well.

items.statement: Collection efficiency for inclusive finance portfolio inching towards 99.7%
items.quote: Collection efficiency also continued to improve with the current book for inclusive finance portfolio inching towards 99.7%.

items.statement: Branch expansion rationalized with focus on realistic costing; corporate headcount and costs muted
items.quote: branch expansions are also extremely rationalized and economical. We focus on having branches of realistic costing and not very fashionable costing, and that ensures that we are able to operate and go live with our branches at the earliest and get working

items.statement: Cost of funds hardened; elevated deposit rates not coming down; using refinancing lines to manage mix
items.quote: Cost of funds have definitely hardened. It's becoming increasingly difficult to raise money. We have noticed that the elevated rates of Q4 haven't quite come down the way they typically come down in the earlier previous years.

items.statement: No significant impact from farm loan waivers seen so far; industry matured to handle cycles
items.quote: Not in the industry. I can talk about broadly even the industry figure is available and hence, obviously not on us as well when I say across the industry. So we haven't seen any impact and hopefully will not

items.statement: Monitoring impact of war and crude prices; CV segment sensitive to diesel price hikes >10-15%
items.quote: The only segment which can get impacted, which will be the commercial vehicle, if there's an increase in diesel prices substantially beyond 10% or 15%, likely that there could be an impact.

items.statement: NPA interest collections increased to Rs 15 crore in Q4 from Rs 5-6 crore; expected to sustain at Rs 12 crore/quarter
items.quote: And also the fact is that there has been an uptick in terms of the NPA collections. It has now moved to around what was around ₹5 crores, ₹6 crores has moved to around ₹15 crores during the last quarter. It will broadly sustain at around ₹12 crores

items.statement: Digital ecosystem building with credit on UPI, secured cards, digital MSME loans, digital deposits; prequalified base for cross-sell
items.quote: Along with the secured credit cards, digital MSME loans and digital deposits, these offerings are helping us build a fully integrated digital banking ecosystem. We now have a prequalified base of customers across these digital products, creating a very st rong opportunity for future cross-sell and deeper customer engagement

items.statement: CGFMU claim process: 3 cohorts eligible in FY27; claims filed after 1+ base year + 6 months NPA; trust turnaround ~60 days
items.quote: It's a credit guarantee trust. So we are not claiming parity from the government. It's a fully funded trust, the credit guarantee trust. So our experience fairly has been good. They will have obviously their own internal turnaround times for making the claim, which I presume will be around 60 days.

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance of INR 140-150 crore for 4-5 hubs, 10-12 spokes, and automated lab
items.quote: For FY'27, the capital outlay for the new centers, including the lab, the new automated lab, is estimated to be INR 140 crores to INR 150 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 40%+ for FY27 despite new center additions and tech/talent investments
items.quote: we feel that we'll be able to comfortably deliver more than 40%. And like Dhiren said, while the guidance would be 40%, we'll try to deliver a better number than that.

items.statement: Price hike of 1-1.5% expected in Q1 or Q2 FY27 on select tests
items.quote: this year also we'll be taking roughly about 1% to 1.5% of price hike. Maybe in Q1 or Q2, we may take depending on the -- not every year we do the price hike across tests.

items.statement: FY26 capex outlay was INR 169 crore including replacement capex
items.quote: Coming to the update on capital investment in the current period , the overall capex outlay has been INR 169 crores, inclusive of replacement capex.

items.statement: FY27 new center capex of INR 120-130 crore for 4-5 hubs and 10-12 spokes plus automated lab
items.quote: for the new centers, which have been outlined in the investor presentation, which are roughly about 4 to 5 hubs and 10 to 12 spokes, the Capex would be between INR 120 crores to INR 130 crores.

items.statement: Maintenance capex for FY27 estimated at INR 10-15 crore or 2-2.5% of revenue
items.quote: It'll be around INR 10 crores to INR 15 crores. Dhiren Gala: So, typically, the maintenance capex is roughly about 2% to 2.5% of our topline

items.statement: FY27 expansion plan: 4-5 hubs, 10-12 spokes, automated lab in Panjagutta, and genomic testing launch
items.quote: Coming to our expansion plan for FY'27, we would be commissioning 4 to 5 hubs and 10 to 12 spokes across the network. We're also coming up with a state -of-the-art, totally automated lab in Panjagutta, Hyderabad with an automated track system

items.statement: Ambegaon center in Pune achieved breakeven in 1 year; Khammam and Nandyal hubs breakeven in 2 quarters vs 3-quarter guidance
items.quote: Our Ambegaon center has achieved breakeven in 1 year, in line with our guidance. Further, the 2 hubs launched in Q3 FY'26 in our core markets, Khammam and Nandyal, achieved breakeven within just 2 quarters, outperforming our guided timeline of 3 quarters

items.statement: Kolkata: 2 centers opened in Q1 FY26 breakeven in <9 months; 7 hubs total with 3 recently opened
items.quote: out of which 2 centers, which were added in Q1 of FY'26, they did breakeven in less than 9 months. The rest of the centers like Phoolbagan, Diamond Harbour, they just opened a couple of quarters back.

items.statement: Bangalore: Yelahanka hub breakeven, HSR near breakeven; flagship center in Bannerghatta with PET-CT/MRI coming in months; Rajajinagar hub finalized
items.quote: Yelahanka did break-even and HSR is almost close to break-even. So that's one of the reason why we've already finalized one flagship facility there and we also finalized one more location in Rajajinagar

items.statement: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 26.6% YoY driven by 18.5% volume growth and 8.1% mix change; wellness segment growing ~30% consistently
items.quote: The consolidated revenue for the current quarter stood at INR 219 crores, reflecting a strong revenue growth rate of 26.6% Y -o-Y. And this strong revenue growth, just like the previous quarter was driven by test volume growth of 18.5% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Pune (PH Diagnostics) grew 16% YoY in Q4 with 15% footfall growth; expect double-digit growth for next 1-2 years
items.quote: Turning to PH , we delivered a year -on-year growth of 16%, primarily driven by network expansion and favorable seasonality during the quarter.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 43.5% (+379 bps YoY) driven by operating leverage and faster new hub breakeven; FY26 full-year margin 41.4%
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood healthy at 43.5% in the current quarter with an improvement of 379 basis points Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin ~35% for FY26
items.quote: Yes. So while we don't maintain books as per Indian GAAP, but it should be close to about 35%.

items.statement: Revenue per test INR 488 and per footfall INR 1,808 in Q4; 4.3% increase due to new hub ramp-up (radiology-heavy mix)
items.quote: The revenue per test and revenue per Footfall stood at INR 488 and INR 1,808, respectively, during the current quarter.

items.statement: Wellness packages are ~50-50 pathology-radiology mix; retail wellness realization ~INR 2,500, corporate ~INR 1,800-2,000
items.quote: It's in the range of INR 1,800 to INR 2,000 Anshul. So, for Q4, generally, at a full year level, it was more or less closer to INR 2,000.

items.statement: Genomics launched as long-term play; no significant revenue expected in next few years; centralized in Hyderabad lab serving 6 states
items.quote: Genomics is a long-term play. I don't think we'll see any significant revenue coming in the next years.

items.statement: B2C revenue 92%; radiology 37% of revenue; corporate wellness sees churn due to aggregators and price sensitivity but large corporates retained 2-3 years
items.quote: The B2C revenue stood healthy at 92%. Our radiology business stood at 37%.

items.statement: Hospital labs focus on in-patients; Vijaya differentiated by integrated pathology+radiology, large format centers, 20-25% cheaper than hospitals, dense spoke network
items.quote: Hospitals are basically probably designed to take care of the needs of their in-patients. So, if you look at their labs, which are more or less like back in kitchens, they have to cater to their in -patients.

items.statement: Online players/aggregators have no direct lab impact; they outsource diagnostics to players like Vijaya for corporate wellness
items.quote: So, there is no much impact from online players because for the past five years post-COVID, we've seen different multiple online players. You know, the names have changed.

items.statement: AI solutions require CE/FDA validation and licensing before retail release; only 6-7 solutions expected to be approved for customer use
items.quote: Especially in radiology, these patches that come for any kind of a specific organ, they're basically patches which have to be layered on to our radiology information software. So they need certain licensing, just like we would need a CE or an FDA some background to bringing in any kind of AI

items.statement: Workforce grew from ~2,000 to 3,500+ over 5 years; developing second-line talent in new geographies; digital marketing spend INR 6-7 crore FY26, doubling in FY27/FY28
items.quote: Our workforce has grown from nearly 2,000 employees to over 3,500 employees over these 5 years, welcoming close to 1,500 new members into the Vijaya Family.

items.statement: No franchise model planned; all centers company-owned and operated; North India expansion not planned for 3-5 years
items.quote: At the moment, I would not be able to comment on the future, but all of these centers that we operate today are company-owned and company-operated. And we do not have any kind of, probably an idea on wanting to start franchising right now.

items.statement: Cash balance INR 280-300 crore; no immediate inorganic plans but evaluating 8-15 assets yearly if valuation reasonable and B2C-aligned
items.quote: anything that comes to us in terms of an inorganic or a merger and acquisition, JV, whatever it might be, if it is in the same value system and it is B2C-driven, even if it's pure pathology or radiology and ethos matches, we're more than happy to look at that asset.

items.statement: 5-year track record since listing: centers doubled 81 to 162, footprint 2 to 6 states, revenue CAGR 17% vs 15% guidance, EBITDA margin undiluted, revenue crossed INR 800 crore
items.quote: Over the last 5 years since listing, we have delivered a revenue CAGR of 17%, exceeding our guidance of 15%. Most importantly, this growth has been achieved without any dilution in the EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Volumes remain subdued due to West Asia conflict with no clarity on recovery timing
items.quote: The trend is continuing right now. So, volumes remain a bit subdued, and there's no clarity also on when things will pick up exactly.

items.statement: Import cargo from US, Europe, Middle East impacted; export of food, beverage, rice, frozen foods affected
items.quote: Basically, if we look at on the import side, all the cargo, which is coming from U.S., Europe and Middle East is impacted. And after this West Asia crisis, the outbound commodity on the export side, which is food and beverage, rice and basically frozen foods, so they are getting impacted.

items.statement: Jaipur ICD next hearing in July for final arguments; hopeful for positive order
items.quote: So Jaipur, we have our next hearing in July, which is listed for final argument. So, we're hopeful for a positive order within that hearing or very short thereafter if it gets adjourned to another hearing.

items.statement: Actively looking for owned and third-party sidings for new ICDs regardless of short-term demand
items.quote: We're still on the lookout. We're looking both owned as well as accessing some third-party sidings. And regardless of the short-term demand, we're trying to create assets for long term.

items.statement: Employee cost rose 12-13% due to headcount increase for domestic operations scaling, Ankleshwar preparation, retention bonuses
items.quote: Yes. So, it's a mix of everything. So, the headcount is also going up as we're scaling up in domestic operations, that's also a team is being set up. Ankleshwar is coming. So, it's a bit in advance this headcount is coming, but we're preparing for the future. And other than that, also there's some retention scheme bonuses and etcetera that we've added.

items.statement: Targeting 15% growth for rail segment, 5% for CFS, 15% for Snowman long-term assuming fewer disruptions
items.quote: It's tough to give a guidance. But as and when we add new terminals, depending on how many we add, we would be trying to target a 15% growth for the rail segment. CFS is probably around 5%. Snowman also, we're targeting about a 15% growth.

items.statement: Container business capex INR90 cr; Snowman INR30 cr; Indore project INR150 cr (INR50 cr land spent, INR100 cr over 2 years); Jaipur INR70 cr over 1-1.5 years; additional INR125 cr for electric reach stackers, EVs, 3 rakes, new warehouse

items.quote: Yes. So, ICD, wherever -- I mean, how we've historically done it is that when we hit about 70%, 80% capacity utilization, we extend the yard. items.statement: Double stacking at 40% for FY26 (Q4 42%), range 39-42% through year
items.quote: Double stacking, we're at 40% for the year. Q4 was at 42%. But so, throughout the year, it was kind of between 39% to 42% kind of thing, and it's given an average of 40%.

items.statement: Snowman INR1,000 cr revenue target deferred to FY29 from FY28; targeting 15% EBITDA margin (INR150 cr EBITDA) at that scale
items.quote: INR1,000 crores is still our plan. Maybe it gets deferred by a year or so. On the margin front, as more 5PL increases, the percentage of EBITDA would go down, but the overall EBITDA would go up. Our target would be that something like at INR1,000 crores. It's a 15% EBITDA margin on a blended basis, and we have a INR150 crores EBITDA.

items.quote: If you look at our capacity, we're at about 160,000 pallets. The next competition is at 80,000 pallets. items.quote: yes. So, we have repayments of around INR30 crores in next financial year. Kunal Tokas: Including lease and debt, principal and interest. items.quote: Typically, in the warehousing, we have had a few R&Ms and there were certain start-up warehouses wherein the power cost was high initially, that has resulted into a little depleted margin. items.statement: Not actively looking for buyer for CFS business
items.quote: For the last few quarters, we've confirmed that we're not looking actively for a buyer on it.

items.quote: Yes, it's reported in our press release. So, for the quarter, say we've done 188,000. 96,000 is Rail and 91,000 is CFS roughly.

items.quote: So further one more point. You are seeing the 10% growth, that is the overall growth in revenue. So only the trading part, which is trading and distribution. So, there is a growth of 23% and all COGS is related to trading only. Other segments are not attributing to that.

So, we'll be investing in solar as well across our locations more. Electric reach stackers are th

items.statement: MAT rate reduced 1%; ATI tax benefit gone for FY27; sufficient MAT credits to avoid cash tax for 3-4 years
items.quote: So, tax rate, yes, there's been a change basically. So, MAT reduced by 1%, but there was a question of old regime, new regime because the ATI tax benefit has gone away for us. So, we're missing out 1 year of ATI tax benefit, which would have been FY '27 for some of our facilities. But we're going to have enough MAT credit, that we're not going to pay cash tax for the next, say, 3 years, at least,

items.statement: Rail throughput grew 10% YoY in FY26 vs flat market; targeting 15% growth via domestic volumes, Ankleshwar (this year), Indore (2 years), Jaipur (2 years), new locations
items.quote: So, from last year, we've had about 10% growth and the overall market didn't grow by 10%. So, we added market share as well as some domestic volumes. And we're going to continue to expand on our domestic volumes and new locations. So, when Ankleshwar will come in, say, within this year; Indore say, two years from now, Jaipur will also probably come in 2 years from now. So all this will continue ad

items.statement: Snowman FY27 capex guideline INR50 cr: more BTS, one owned warehouse, land purchase, vehicles
items.quote: Yes. So, we're looking at more BTSs this year, but we do have some plans to buy land and probably one owned warehouse we'll target, plus some vehicles. Maybe around INR50 crores capex is the guideline for FY '27.

items.statement: Launched AI-led platforms Prudent Edge for MFD partners and FundzEdge for retail customers with voice support in regional languages.
items.quote: We are now taking the next step in that journey with the launch of very powerful AI-led platform called Prudent Edge for our mutual fund distribution partners and FundzEdge for our retail customers on the

items.statement: AUM reached INR 1.33 trillion as of 5th May 2026, up 9.7% from FY26 average AUM of INR 1.21 trillion.
items.quote: Our AUM as of 5th May has already climbed to 1.33 trillion. This is 9.7% higher than the average AUM of full FY '26.

items.statement: Average AUM for Q4 FY26 was INR 1,28,000 crore, up 0.3% sequentially despite 14.5% market fall.
items.quote: Our average AUM for Q4 FY '26 was INR 1,28,000 crore, which grew by modestly 0.3% sequentially. This is particularly noteworthy because market fell by 14.5% during the same period.

items.statement: Equity AUM grew 15.4% YoY in FY26 from INR 1,00,100 crore to INR 1,15,480 crore driven by net new money and Indus acquisition.
items.quote: Our equity AUM grew by 15.4% during FY '26. It moved from approximately INR 1,00,100 crore in 2025 to INR 1,15,480 crore in March 2026.

items.statement: Equity AUM declined 8.2% QoQ in Q4 FY26 due to mark-to-market losses of INR 14,550 crore, partially offset by record net sales of INR 4,300 crore.
items.quote: Equity AUM declined by 8.2% during the quarter. This was primarily due to mark-to-market losses of INR 14,550 crore, reflecting sharp market correction during the period.

items.statement: Monthly SIP book stood at INR 1,188 crore as of March 2026, up INR 209 crore over 12 months; market share improved 20 bps to 3.65%.
items.quote: As of March 2026, our monthly SIP book stood at ₹1188 crore. We have added about ₹209 crore to the SIP book over the last twelve months.

items.statement: FY26 mutual fund revenue grew 21% in line with 21.7% average AUM growth; yield stable at 91 bps for third consecutive year.
items.quote: our mutual fund revenue growth at 21% is in line with our quarterly average AUM growth of about 21.7%. Despite impact of back book repricing, our yield has remained more or less stable at 91 basis point, not only for the year, but for last three years in a row.

items.statement: Insurance revenue grew 18% in FY26 on 35% health and 28% life fresh premium growth; commission rationalization from Oct 2025 softened revenue growth.
items.quote: our insurance revenue grew by 18%. This was on the back of a very strong growth in fresh premium with health insurance growing by 35% and life insurance by 28%.

items.statement: FY26 total revenue grew 19.4%, commission expenses grew 19.8%, employee costs ex-ESOP up 21.2% due to Indus acquisition and labor code provision.
items.quote: total revenue from operation grew by 19.4% and our commission and fee expenses, has also grew in the same line and the same pace at 19.8% on a full-year basis. Excluding ESOPs, employee expenses during the entire year went up by 21.2%.

items.statement: Expect existing employee salary bill to increase ~14% in FY27; March 2026 salary bill INR 8.93 crore revised to INR 10.2 crore in April 2026.
items.quote: we expect that the employee cost for the existing base will increase by approximately 14% in FY '27. If I give the indication that our salary bill has moved from INR 8.93 crore in March 2026 to INR 10.2 crore in April 2026.

items.statement: FY26 operating profit grew 18.2% with stable operating margin at 23.6%; PAT grew 13.5% dragged by negative other income of INR 4.7 crore in Q4.
items.quote: Led by a healthy operational performance, operating profit grew by 18.2% and operating margin were stable at 23.6%. Profit after tax was lower at 13.5% compared to operating profit growth, mainly led by a dent in other income due to market correction in the month of March.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 5.1% QoQ led by 69% insurance growth; operating profit up 19.5% QoQ; PAT up only 2.6% due to negative other income.
items.quote: On a quarter-on-quarter basis, our revenue grew by 5.1% sequentially, led by a 69% growth in insurance revenue. Operating profit grew by 19.5% sequentially, aided by lower employee costs.

items.statement: SEBI TER changes: revised TER inclusive of GST is revenue neutral for GST-registered distributors but removes anomaly favoring unregistered ones; exit load 5 bps benefit removed, industry negotiating clarity by end of month.
items.quote: revised expense ratio which will now be inclusive of all statutory levies including GST. It is a revenue neutral for those who are registered under GST, but the big advantage is that it removes the earlier anomaly where a GST registered distributor earned less than an unregistered one.

items.statement: Expect 2-3 bps impact on back-book yield from exit load removal; new business yield expected neutral; will share impact with distributors at existing ratio.
items.quote: On the book, we are expecting about two, three basis point impact as far as exit load related pass on is TER rationalization is concerned. But still, a couple of AMCs are yet to communicate clearly.

items.statement: GST rationalization gives Prudent ~15% competitive advantage vs non-GST registered distributors whose AMC yield falls by 15%.
items.quote: their yield from AMC will come down by 15%. So, automatically, we are competitive by almost 15% compared to the rate of AMC.

items.statement: Life insurance growth driven by TULIP (term+ULIP) category, now biggest selling category; ULIP sales up 5-6% YoY but yield maintained on other categories.
items.quote: tulip category, the term plus ulip category, I think we have been pushing this category very, very actively. So, whatever we lost in terms of life insurance business from the guaranteed plans, what we tried to recover through this particular product category

items.statement: Life insurance persistency maintained at 94-95%, no persistency challenges despite renewal growth slowdown.
items.quote: Persistency is still the highest. I think still we are maintaining more than 94%-95% of persistency. So, there is no challenges on a persistency side.

items.statement: SIF flows INR 90 crore in Q4 FY26; current run rate INR 25-30 crore/month; 1,000+ of 6,000 industry SIF-certified distributors on Prudent platform.
items.quote: we did around INR 90 crores kind of business in SIF in last quarter. So, currently, I think month-on-month, we believe that we have attained a run rate of around INR 25-30 crores now

items.statement: SIF margins in line with mutual fund margins; treat SIF as part of mutual fund sales and margin.
items.quote: the SIF margins are in line with mutual funds. So, there is not much difference between SIF margin and the mutual fund margin. So, you can consider SIF as part of the mutual fund sales or mutual fund margin only going forward.

items.statement: Indus acquisition AUM grew from INR 2,085 crore at acquisition to INR 2,250 crore currently; 100% manpower retention; exploring further acquisitions but nothing concrete.
items.quote: the AUM is INR 2,250 crore. It has grown in line with my overall AUM growth and the gross sales, net sales, SIP book, everything has been reasonably great. I think the retention of manpower is absolute. Everybody is there. Not a single person is left.

items.statement: Employee count 1,540 as of March 31, 2026; new annual salary bill INR 10.2 crore; ESOP cost ~INR 7 crore annualized at Rs 2,600 share price, may rise 15-20% next year.
items.quote: As of 31st March is concerned, the precise number is 1,540 people. And their new salary bill would be, I said about INR 10.2 crore. So, that is about the entire number of employees.

items.statement: B2B2C channel contributes 90% of AUM and 93-94% of new flows; direct+Indus channel 10% of AUM and 6-7% of new flows.
items.quote: Right now, it is 90-10. So, 90% contribution comes from the AUM, while 90% of the contribution is from our B2B2C channel, and around 10% contribution is from the direct plus Indus channel.

items.statement: Top 5 AMCs contribute ~50% of AUM; flow share similar with 1-2% shift to newer AMCs.
items.quote: top 5 AMCs, as you said, contribute around 50% of the AUM. And between direct and the regular channel, I think the ratio what we maintained earlier also, that still continues as it is.

items.statement: Highest ever equity gross sales, net sales, and new SIP registrations in FY26 despite competition; health insurance and life insurance at record highs.
items.quote: my equity gross sales was the highest ever, equity net sales was the highest ever, equity gross new SIP registration was highest ever, my health insurance business was highest ever, my life insurance business was second highest ever.

items.statement: Competition from B2C platforms increases MFD awareness of platform benefits; GST changes expand platform market opportunity; not worried about brokerage wars.
items.quote: the other side of this coin, I would say that because of so many B2C platforms, I think more and more MFDs are becoming aware about the advantages of platform. So, we also get this indirect advantage of platforms being more popularized.

items.statement: Other financial products revenue INR 33 crore in FY26 (PMS INR 22 cr, FD INR 6 cr, rest smallcase/LAS); ex-Liquiloans, growth ~35% YoY.
items.quote: INR 22 crore has come from PMS, INR 6 crore from FD, and rest is probably small case and LAS and everything. So, I think small, small product, but majority of the income is coming from mobilization through PMS AIF.

items.statement: Expect healthy other income by June 30 if markets hold; mutual fund portfolio gains reversed to INR 11.5 crore from Q4 loss of INR 4.7 crore.
items.quote: all the losses on mutual fund portfolio have since reversed. Current gain on the mutual fund portfolio stand at approximately INR 11.5 crore and if market remained at current level, I think by 30th June we expect a very healthy income from other income side.

items.statement: SIP momentum may slow if poor market returns persist; cancellations increased in FY26 but investor confidence remains higher than historically.
items.quote: If the kind of returns continue for a longer time, definitely there could be some impact on the new SIP and the cancellation both. Having said that experience of investors, the confidence level of investors is much, much different compared to what it used to be earlier.

items.statement: Own brands revenue grew 7% YoY in Q4 FY26 driven by elite and premium portfolio double-digit growth
items.quote: After a challenging few quarters we delivered a marked improvement in Q4, returning to growth with revenue up 7% year -on-year. This was driven by improved traction in own brands and another solid performance in our Wine Tourism business.

items.statement: Elite and premium share reached 79% of own brands in Q4 FY26 up from 75% previous quarter
items.quote: In terms of elite and premium, the share of elite and premium has again grown in this quarter, even though I had said some time back that's probably as good as it could get, but it has gone up to 79% in Q4 as opposed to 75% in the previous quarter

items.statement: The Source range sales grew over 35% in Q4 FY26 and over 20% for full year FY26
items.quote: I would like to briefly highlight the performance of The Source range, which continues to go from strength to strength. The Source sales grew by over 35% in Q4 and over 20% for the full year FY '26

items.statement: Wine Tourism revenue grew 17% YoY in Q4 FY26 driven by 11% footfall increase and room revenue ramp-up
items.quote: We delivered a robust 17% Y -o-Y revenue growth in Wine Tourism in Q4, driven by 11% increase in footfalls and a strong ramp-up in room revenues following the launch of our third resort, The Haven by Sula in Q3.

items.statement: Room capacity expanded 50% to 154 keys with The Haven by Sula launch in Q3 FY26
items.quote: And with the addition of The Haven by Sula, our room capacity has now expanded by 50% to 154 keys. So that's quite a significant achievement during the year and just shows that we are very focused, focused like a laser on continuing to grow this key segment for us.

items.statement: Capex for FY26 was approximately INR 25 crore; FY27 regular capex expected lower than FY26 excluding Chandon acquisition
items.quote: At the same time, capex for FY '26 stood at approximately INR 25 crores. We expect regular capex in FY '2 7 to remain lower than the FY '26 levels as well, excluding the proposed asset purchase agreement with Chandon

items.statement: Signed binding agreement to acquire Chandon's 19-acre estate in Dindori, Nashik for Wine Tourism expansion; regulatory approvals pending
items.quote: We have signed a binding agreement to acquire Chandon's 19 -acre estate in Dindori, Nashik, to expand our Wine Tourism footprint even further with this beautiful, I would say, spectacular property. We have very exciting plans for this property. However, the transaction is currently underway with regulatory approvals pending, and we still need to sign the conveyance deed.

items.statement: Operating costs reduced 3% YoY in Q4 FY26; Q4 EBITDA margins improved ~200 bps sequentially vs Q3 and 9M average
items.quote: That said, we took decisive measures to optimize operating costs. These actions resulted in a 3% Y-o-Y reduction in operating costs, enabling us to maintain EBITDA at similar absolute levels despite the lower gross profit. Importantly, if we look at sequentially, Q4 EBITDA margins improved by approximately 200 basis points versus the quarter 3 and 9 months FY '26 average.

items.statement: Planning 2-3% annual price hikes in free pricing states including Maharashtra; holding prices on wines above INR 1,200 due to upcoming EU duty reduction
items.quote: In general, we would take something like 2% to 3% a year in the free pricing states. Now I have said this once before that we would probably hold our hand on wines that cost more than INR 1,200 a bottle because we are very mindful of the fact that pretty soon, there is going to be duty reduction on those EU wines.

items.statement: Net cash from operations increased 70% YoY to INR 99 crore in FY26; WIPS receivables at INR 86 crore as of March 2026
items.quote: Net cash generated from operations increased 70% Y -o-Y to INR 99 crores as compared to INR 58 crores in FY '25, primarily driven by favorable working capital movement. Our WIPS outstanding receivables stood at INR 86 crores as of March 2026 compared to INR 72 crores last year.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR 2 per share for FY26
items.quote: The Board has recommended a final dividend of INR 2 per share, supported by improved operating cash flows and a strong retained earnings position.

items.statement: UP new policy enables significant retail license expansion; Sula is category leader in non-fortified wine in UP with 50%+ growth in FY26
items.quote: The good news in UP is that the new policy will enable a significant expansion in retail licenses that augurs well for us as Sula is by far the category leader in non-fortified wine in UP. And so, we are expecting to see another bumper year in UP in FY '27.

items.statement: Industry discounting levels unsustainably high; potential casualties among domestic wine producers
items.quote: Having said that, still the level of discounting is, I would say, unsustainably high for the industry. At this kind of level of discounts, I would not be surprised if there were some, I would say, casualties among the industry, I'll be very frank, and that will not be us, but you can say that some of the producers unfortunately continue to run unsustainable discounts.

items.statement: Packing material cost increases expected in FY27 due to West Asia conflict
items.quote: We are very mindful of the fact that now in FY '27, we are going to face some pressure from packing material cost increases because of the West Asia conflict primarily.

items.statement: Not pursuing spirits/tequila acquisitions; no compelling opportunities found despite evaluating craft brands
items.quote: Well, I had mentioned maybe a year ago that we would be open to it and we have continued to look at it. It would not have been that we would be looking to launch our own tequila, but there have been a lot of interesting small craft brands coming up in India in spirits, and we have looked, but we've not found anything compelling enough.

items.statement: Targets INR30,000 crore AUM by 2030 with 5%+ ROA, 20%+ ROE, and 10 million lives touched
items.quote: Vision 3030, which would be elaborated by the CEO, Mr. Sadaf. Going forward, our focus remains very clear to grow responsibly, to maintain strong asset quality, to continue the diversification, to leverage technology and do res ponsible lending, and most importantly, to remain committed to serving the low -income households and women entrepreneurs with trust, dignity, and responsibility

items.statement: Aims to reach INR30,000 crore AUM by 2030 with 5%+ ROA and 20%+ ROE
items.quote: So basically, the Vision 3030 means that Muthoot Microfin is aiming to reach INR30,000 crores AUM by 2030. And we are going to explain how this journey is going to take about.

items.statement: Targets 53% JLG and 47% non-JLG portfolio mix by 2030 with average ticket size of INR1.5 lakh
items.quote: What our vision is, that by end of 2030, we will have 53% portfolio in JLG loans and around 47% portfolio would be in non-JLG products, which would be MSME, Muthoot Small Enterprise Loans, which is the individual loans, around 33%.

items.statement: Plans 75% digital collections by 2030 from current 40% incremental run-rate
items.quote: Today, we stand at around incrementally 40% of our collection is digital. By 2030, 75% would be entirely digital.

items.statement: AUM grew 13% YoY to INR14,005 crore as of FY26 end
items.quote: we are closing the financial year with around INR14, 005 crores of portfolio under management, whic h is a 13% growth year -on-year

items.statement: Q4 FY26 disbursements grew 46% YoY and 15% QoQ to INR2,876 crore
items.quote: if you look at Q4, we have disbursed around INR2,876 crores, which is almost 46% growth year-on-year and 15% growth quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Non-JLG portfolio reached 17% of AUM (INR2,387 crore individual loans) with near-zero delinquency
items.quote: Our small and micro-enterprise individual loan portfolio grew t o around INR2,387 crores with near-zero delinquency

items.statement: GNPA improved to 3.89% and NNPA to 1.14% in FY26
items.quote: It has come down to 3.89% from 4.85% in in the previous year, as well as the net NPA stands at 1.14%.

items.statement: Overall collection efficiency improved to 96.43% in Q4 FY26, up 340 bps YoY
items.quote: Currently, we are at 96.43%. That is a growth of almos t 160 basis points from quarter -on-quarter and almost 340 basis points improvement from year on year

items.statement: X-bucket collection efficiency at 99.8% for last two quarters, back to pre-FY25 levels
items.quote: The X-bucket collection efficiency last two quarters consistently at around 99.8%. And if you look at that to the pre-2025 period, we were at similar range.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 standalone NIM at 12%, improving from yield changes in H2 FY26
items.quote: The NIM is started improving. We are at 12% NIM standalone Q4 of the current financial year.

items.statement: Cost of funds declined to 10.27% in FY26 from 11.02% in FY25; incremental borrowing cost at 9.9%
items.quote: We had a cost of fund of 11.02%. That cost of fund has come down to 10.27%, and it is further likely to come.

items.statement: Incremental cost of borrowing over last 12 months at effective rate of 9.9%
items.quote: if you look at the incremental cost of borrowing whatever we have borrowed in the last 12-month period, the effective cost is around 9.9%.

items.statement: Credit cost fell to 2.8% in Q4 FY26 and 3.5% for full FY26 vs 9.4% in FY25
items.quote: with respect to credit cost, we are at 2.8% in Q4 and for the full year we are at 3.5%. But if you look at in the previous year, we were at almost 9.4% full year credit cost.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 standalone ROA 2.1% and ROE 10%; full year profit INR170 crore
items.quote: And we have reported a 2.1% ROA standalone Q4 and 10% ROE for the quarter. And when we look at for the full year, the overall profit for the full year is INR170 crores.

items.statement: Opex ratio improved to 6.4% in Q4 FY26 from peak of 7% in H1 FY26
items.quote: we have currently 6.4% opex in Q4 of the current financial year. But it has peaked to almost 7% level where the portfolio was not growing, but we have doing all these investments.

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio at 3.34x with net worth of INR2,854 crore; sufficient capital for 12-15 months growth
items.quote: if you look at the debt-equity ratio, we are at 3.34 times. So we have enough room in our equity to do the growth that we are planning.

items.statement: Individual loan product (Muthoot Small Enterprise Loan) disbursed INR2,536 crore in FY26; portfolio INR2,383 crore at 23-25% ROI
items.quote: one of the major ones is the Muthoot Small Enterprise Loan, which is the individual loan product. So in this we have done INR2,536 crores of disbursement, and portfolio stands at around INR2,383 crores.

items.statement: LAP product disbursed INR26.5 crore in FY26 with 100% collection; ticket size INR4 lakh at 18-22% ROI
items.quote: We disbursed around INR26.5 crores last financial year, and the AUM stands at around 47%. This is also a product which is having 100% collection as of now.

items.statement: Gold loan referrals at INR7 crore/month via Muthoot Fincorp; exploring co-lending
items.quote: We are also doing a gold referral with our group company, which is Muthoot FinCorp, and we are doing around INR7 crores of referrals month on month.

items.statement: Staff productivity rose from INR7.6 lakh to INR12 lakh monthly disbursements; targets INR18-19 lakh by 2030
items.quote: The staff which used to do loans of around INR7.6 lakhs is now doing a loan of around almost INR12 lakhs per month. And average ticket size whi ch was around INR60,000, it has gone to around INR1 lakh

items.statement: Separate 1,800-member credit underwriting team using generative AI for loan appraisal
items.quote: We are the only microfinance company who has from the day one believed in a separate underwriting team. So we have 1,800-member separate team. At every branch has a credit officer who is now assisted with this generative AI technology through which he can underwrite these loans.

items.statement: Launched NatCat insurance product to insulate portfolio from climate risks like floods and cyclones
items.quote: We have developed a product which are natural calamity product, insurance product, NatCat, through which we ensure that even if there are floods or cyclone, our portfolio is insulated from there.

items.statement: RBI's supportive regulatory direction creating transparent, disciplined gold loan ecosystem
items.quote: Never before has the Reserve Bank of India taken such a supportive and structured approach towards lending against gold. The recent regulatory direction is helping create a more transparent, disciplined, well-governed, and professionally managed gold loan ecosystem.

items.statement: Targets INR1,000 crore profit by FY30 with 5% ROA and 20%+ ROE
items.quote: The INR1,000 crores profit, is that the number for FY30? Sadaf Sayeed: Yes, your interpretation is correct. Yes

items.statement: Long-run sustainable credit cost target of 2.5% with diversification into gold loan, LAP, individual loans
items.quote: We believe that on a long-run basis, we would be having a credit cost of around 2.5%, and that is what we feel that we can sustain.

items.statement: GNPA, NNPA, SMA book consistently coming down; on-time portfolio improving; collection efficiency improving quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: The GNPA, NNPA is consistently coming down. The SMA book is coming down. On-time portfolio is improving in the overall portfolio.

items.statement: Cost of funds reduced from 11% to 10.27%; incremental borrowing cost at 9.9%; 75 bps reduction YoY
items.quote: We were at 11% in the previous year. Currently, we are at 10.27%. And if you look at the incremental cost of borrowing whatever we have borrowed in the last 12-month period, the effective cost is around 9.9%.

items.statement: Q4 standalone ROA 2.1%, ROE 10%; full year profit INR170 crores
items.quote: We have reported a 2.1% ROA standalone Q4 and 10% ROE for the quarter. And when we look at for the full year, the overall profit for the full year is INR170 crores.

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio at 3.34x; net worth INR2,854 crores; sufficient capital for 12-15 months growth without equity raise
items.quote: If you look at the debt -equity ratio, we are at 3.34 times. So we have enough room in our equity to do the growth that we are planning. So at some point we will have to look at equity, but immediately in the next 12 to 15 months, we have enough capital to grow the business.

items.statement: Free funds INR700-800 crores carried across year; adequate HQLA; contingency funding plan for INR2,000-3,000 crores in short time
items.quote: We have almost INR700-INR800 crores of free funds carried across the financial year, plus we have adequate investments in HQLA. We have contingency funding plans in place where we can raise almost INR2,000 to INR3,000 crores fund in very short time.

items.statement: Added 80,000 new clients in Q4; strategy focuses on existing client cross-sell and new client acquisition
items.quote: In Q4, we have brought in another 80,000 clients into the Muthoot Microfin ecosystem.

items.statement: Diversification from 85:15 to 83:17 (microfinance:other); targeting deeper household engagement with gold loan, LAP, individual loans
items.quote: In terms of our diversification strategy that we were talking 85% to 15%, we are at 83% to 17%.

items.statement: 12% of field roles are female ROs; female attrition 50% lower than male counterparts; hired 200 women on Women's Day
items.quote: Now we are al most 12% to our total field role are female ROs, and we have seen these are the these population the attrition is low and their productivity in terms of the collection efficiency, in terms of the customer grievance is comparatively less. And more, more things to highlight is their attrition. Their attrition is 50% lesser than the, their counterpart

items.statement: 15,735 employees, 90% in field roles; senior management average vintage 10 years; trust index improved from 85% to 88%, targeting 90%
items.quote: Currently, we have 15,735 strong employees across pan-India. Out of that, 90% people are on the field role who are meeting customer and satisfying their needs, customer service.

items.statement: CRISIL rating upgraded to A+ positive outlook from stable; M1C1 grading maintained for 10 consecutive years; first MFI to complete global rating; ECB listed on INX Gift City
items.quote: We have rating done by CRISIL A+, and there is an upgrade in the outlook as well. So currently we are A+ positive outlook, which was upgraded from stable. We have consistently got M1C1 grading, again done by CRISIL.

items.statement: ESG rating upgraded to highest ESG 1+ by Care Edge-ESG
items.quote: During the last financial year, the company has upgraded got an upgradation of the ESG rating from Care Edge-ESG, and we have been upgraded to the highest ESG rating, that is ESG 1+.

items.statement: PCR ratio strong at 71.5%
items.quote: And the PCR ratio is very strong at 71.5%.

items.statement: 100% NACH achievement in enterprise loan portfolio; using account aggregator for banking and savings habit evaluation
items.quote: We have seen recently 100% NACH achievement in enterprise loan portfolio. And we are using accounts aggregator not only to evaluate their banking habit, to evaluate their savings habit also.

items.statement: Internal audit: 460+ team, 5,758 branch audits last year; Teis 360 in-house software; enhancing product-level audit oversight for diversified portfolio
items.quote: Last year, we conducted 5,758 branch audit reports. In the way forward, we are going continuously focus on the optimization of audit software, that is Teis 360, in-built in -house audit software, and enhance product-level audit oversight as we are going into the mix, we are diversifying our portfolio.

items.statement: Targets 5% ROA and 20%+ ROE by 2030 driven by NIM expansion to 13.5-14%, operating cost below 5%, and credit cost around 2.5%
items.quote: I think 2030 onwards, I think that is what the profitability we are guiding towards around 5% ROA. This will translate with three-four things. One, our NIM expansion, both on the yield side, the portfolio yield will improve because we will have lesser NP A affecting the portfolio yield, and at the same time, the weighted average yield across various products will improve. Currently, it is 18.8%, i

items.statement: Guides 20% AUM CAGR focusing on qualitative, sustainable growth rather than maximum pace
items.quote: Yes, I think the idea is to have a qualitative growth and a sustainable growth. So we are looking at a 20% growth and also, we have grown in terms of our balance sheet.

items.statement: Expects NIM to expand from current 12% to 13.5-14% by FY30 via yield improvement to 22-23% and cost of funds reduction
items.quote: We are already at 12% NIM, we are looking at 13.5% to 14% NIM expanding. And operating cost will go down because we are leveraging from the existing customer base, existing branches.

items.statement: Portfolio yield currently 18.8%, expected to rise above 22-23% by FY30 due to product mix shift and lower NPA drag
