items.quote: I think we've maintained, Shaleen, consistently that on a sustained basis, high single digits, let's say, anywhere starting from 7-ish going up 8%, 9% depending on the hotel and the region and the quarter you pick.

items.statement: Expect 60-plus hotel openings across brands and geographies in FY27
items.quote: In FY '27, we expect 60 -plus hotel openings across brands and geographies.

items.statement: Recent acquisitions expected to contribute over INR250 crores incremental revenue in FY27
items.quote: Our recent acquisitions are expected to contribute over INR250 crores in incremental revenue.

items.statement: Ginger brand portfolio target of 250 hotels under development or in operation by end of FY27
items.quote: We expect the Ginger brand itself to have a total portfolio of 250 hotels either under development or in operation at the end of FY '27.

items.statement: FY26 capex over INR1,000 crores with INR650 crores for renovations, maintenance and digital, rest for greenfield projects
items.quote: IHCL in FY '25 -'26 spent over INR1,000 crores towards capex, out of which around INR650 crores was used for renovations, routine maintenance and digital initiatives, while the rest half was used towards greenfield projects.

items.statement: Annual capex guidance of INR1,000-1,200 crores going forward
items.quote: Even going forward, we will continue to invest INR1,000 crores to INR1,200 crores annually to strengthen our existing competitive advantages and at the same time, build new ones.

items.statement: Pipeline remains strong at 31,000-plus keys, largely capital-light
items.quote: Our pipeline remains strong at 31,000-plus keys and continues to be largely capital light.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin of 35% in FY26 reflecting operating discipline
items.quote: Even as we invested meaningfully for future growth, we delivered EBITDA margin of 35%, reflecting operating discipline and structural efficiency.

items.statement: Stand-alone EBITDA margin expanded 120 bps to 45.1% in FY26
items.quote: Stand -alone basis, revenue grew 10% year -on-year to INR5,640 crores, EBITDA grew 13% year-on-year to INR2,543 crores, yielding EBITDA margin of 45.1%, an expansion of 120 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: Domestic demand resilient with Goa showing 25%+ growth in April, Kerala and Chennai could improve
items.quote: Goa, we have seen almost in the month of April north of 25% growth in all our hotels. Some have gone to 30% and beyond. So, averaging at 25%. Goa is definitely back since the last few months, March and April, and the trend is not changing. Kerala could improve and Chennai could also improve.

items.statement: International hotels subdued due to West Asia conflict, INR40-50 crores revenue impact on consolidated basis
items.quote: We did see some loss of revenues in some of our hotels internationally, including London. And that's what we tried to summarize also on the slide on impact of the West Asia conflict, about INR40 crores to INR50 crores of revenue on the consol basis.

items.statement: Rates are rupee-denominated on portal, benefit from rupee depreciation via international translation and domestic tourism boost
items.quote: So, they are rupee -denominated. I think that's a decision we took a few years back. So that remains the way it is. We do get the benefit of rupee depreciation in two ways. One is, of course, our international hotels translation happens at the average exchange rate for the period.

items.statement: New businesses vertical grew 25% in FY26 to INR753 crores revenue, 31% CAGR over 4 years
items.quote: Our new businesses vertical comprising Ginger, Qmin, Ama, Stays & Trails and Tree of Life delivered 25% growth in FY '26. This resulted in a consolidated revenue of INR753 crores. Over the past 4 years, the new businesses vertical has delivered a CAGR of 31% growth.

items.statement: Ginger Mumbai Airport crossed INR100 crores revenue with 56% EBITDA margin, Qmin at 100+ outlets and INR200 crores GMV
items.quote: The flagship Ginger Hotel at Mumbai Airport crossed the milestone of INR100-plus crores in revenue for the first time, while delivering an industry -leading EBITDA margin of 56%. Qmin expanded its footprint to 100 -plus outlets, while Ama crossed the milestone of 375 bungalows in its portfolio with 85 villas signed during the year. Qmin also on a GMV has crossed almost INR200 crores last year.

items.statement: Foreign tourist arrivals at ~30% for stand-alone, business travel increasing with India's economic prominence
items.quote: As we had mentioned earlier, it's close to 30% for stand-alone is what we call foreign tourists or people who are having forei gn passports. And that is slightly lower for the enterprise because, I guess, the stand-alone has hotel in the bigger cities

items.statement: Foreign business arrivals growing with summits and delegations, tourist arrivals below pre-COVID levels
items.quote: We should not look at foreign arrivals as tourist only. I think we have to coin a new term called foreign business arrivals. Whether they come for AI Summit or they come for now the Africa Summit, which is going to happen or in September, October, we'll have again a B20 or a G20 kind of event happening.

items.statement: Gross liquidity over INR4,300 crores providing flexibility for organic and inorganic growth
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains exceptionally strong with gross liquidity of over INR4,300 crores, giving us significant flexibility to pursue both organic and suitable inorganic growth opportunities.

items.statement: Board proposed dividend of INR3.25 per share (25% of consolidated PAT), up 44% from FY25, 48% CAGR over 4 years
items.quote: the Board has p roposed a dividend equivalent to 25% of consolidated PAT amounting to INR3.25 per equity share, subject to shareholders' approval. This includes a one -time special dividend of INR0.50 per share to commemorate IHCL's landmark 125th AGM as well as the exceptional gains realized during the year

items.statement: Deployed over INR500 crores across four strategic acquisitions in FY26, ANK & Pride integration progressing well
items.quote: Alongside this, we deployed over INR500 crores across four strategic acquisitions, expanding our presence into high-growth adjacencies and strengthening future revenue streams.

items.statement: Portfolio at 630+ hotels, 64,000+ keys, 375+ Ama Villas, total 1,000+ units combined
items.quote: With over 630 hotels, 64,000-plus keys in the portfolio, we continue to scale with discipline through a strong mix of managed, leased and owned assets, creating long-term visibility with capital efficiency. Along with our 375-plus Ama Villas, Ama, which is our homestay brand, our portfolio has now crossed the milestone of 1,000 units when combined with 630-plus hotels portfolio.

items.statement: Capital-light model at 68% of operating portfolio and 93% of pipeline
items.quote: Our capital-light strategy continues to be a defining competitive advantage with 68% of our operating portfolio and 93% of our pipeline under managed or asset-light formats.

items.statement: Stand-alone RevPAR grew 12% in Q4 FY26, industry-leading
items.quote: Our stand-alone performance in Q4 was also the best ever with industry-leading 12% growth in RevPAR.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 expected above 12% growth with domestic outperforming international
items.quote: We think we should be above 12% for the quarter.

items.statement: West Asia conflict causing international demand headwinds, monitoring duration and impact
items.quote: The headwind is, of course, the West Asia conflict, which we have talked about. I think the good tailwind is that we have a good base to sort of work on. And that's particularly true for second half of May and end of -- till end of June.

items.statement: Potential work-from-home resurgence could impact corporate travel, but institutional memory from COVID exists
items.quote: But I think the good thing is that the institutional memory has been bu ilt. COVID is only 4, 5 years back. So, everybody knows what to do if such a situation arises. And we will obviously figure out a way of handling that if it does come to that level

items.statement: Next Capital Market Day to be announced in coming weeks with updated long-term ROCE and capital-light targets
items.quote: So, because you remind us it's time to announce our next Capital Market Day, which we will do so in the next few weeks. We were just waiting for the right moment.

items.statement: Management stopped giving volume guidance due to geopolitical uncertainties but expects growth
items.quote: So we stopped giving guidance due to the geopolitical scenarios and uncertainties. But we are, of course, expecting growth, but we don't give guidance on that.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY27 is INR1,500-1,800 crores
items.quote: In this financial year, between INR1,500 crores to INR1,800 crores.

items.statement: Board approved additional INR2,000 crores capex for capacity expansion, AI automation and sustainability
items.quote: The Board of Directors has approved an additional capex of INR2,000 crores, which will support capacity expansion and infrastructure development across both OHT and on-highway tyre categories, AI enabled automation across on-highway tyre category, and also the company's sustainability initiatives.

items.statement: Maintenance capex is about INR200 crores per year extra
items.quote: This is only project. And maintenance is about INR200-odd crores every year, which will be extra, which is also in the past has been always mentioned extra.

items.statement: PCR tyre launch by end of calendar year 2026 with 6,700 tyres/day initial capacity
items.quote: So we will start around the end of the year, calendar year, as Rajiv mentioned. And in the first phase, we should be getting to 6,700 tyres.

items.statement: 2-wheeler tyre capacity currently 100,000 tyres/month, scalable with market response
items.quote: Presently, we are having a capacity of about 100,000 tyres a month. And again, it will go up as per the market response.

items.statement: OHT volumes grew 5% YoY in Q4 to 85,820 MT; FY26 annual volumes hit record 317,356 MT
items.quote: For the quarter, our OHT sales volume stood at 85,820 metric tons, a growth of 5% year-on-year. For the financial year '26, our volumes stood at 317,356 metric tons.

items.statement: Europe H2 recovery driven by easing channel inventories; Americas improving traction; India sustained momentum
items.quote: From an end market perspective, in Europe, H2 showed good recovery over H1, driven by easing in channel inventories. Similarly, in the Americas market, we are witnessing improving traction supported by higher channel activity.

items.statement: Q4 standalone EBITDA margin 22.9%, FY26 margin 22.7%; near-term margin pressure expected from RM cost increases
items.quote: So at this moment, we are seeing the pressure to come. We are evaluating the situation and see how much we can pass on. But at this moment, we may have some price pressures, margin pressures.

items.statement: Price hikes of 3-5% taken across geographies, targeting additional 2% in current month; may take further hikes
items.quote: So price hike, we have taken between 3% to 5% already across various geographies, and we are targeting around 2% in this very month, towards the end of this month. And we'll continue to watch this, and maybe we may have to take further price hikes.

items.statement: Freight cost at 4.5-5% of revenue in Q4, expected to rise marginally
items.quote: It was about 4.5% to 5%, and we expect it to go up marginally, the way things are, subject to no further disruption.

items.statement: Product mix shifting toward high-end radialized and specialized IF/VF technology products
items.quote: So we are moving more towards the high-end radialized products, the specialized products like IF/VF technology products. So we are working on those as a product mix.

items.statement: On-highway distribution: ~90 primary distributors complete, dealerships to expand with sales ramp
items.quote: The distribution, like I said, the primary distributors are all complete. We are about 90 in all for these categories. And the dealerships will be expanded as per the sales ramp.

items.statement: Gross debt INR4,049 crores, cash INR3,154 crores, net debt INR895 crores as of March 31
items.quote: As on 31st March, the gross debt and cash and cash equivalents were INR4,049 crores and INR3,154 crores, respectively. Accordingly, we have a net debt of INR895 crores.

items.statement: Peak debt level not assumed; funding mix for INR3,800 crores remaining capex under evaluation
items.quote: We can't assume anything. It's a volatile world. It's a moving world. Projects are being announced. So we can't assume anything. We'll keep on making announcements as and when we make changes to it.

items.statement: Final dividend of INR4/share recommended, total FY26 dividend INR16/share
items.quote: The Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of INR4 per equity share, subject to shareholder approval at the upcoming AGM. This is in addition to the INR12 that we have paid per share for the previous 3 quarters.

items.statement: Deloitte Haskins & Sells appointed as joint statutory auditor subject to AGM approval
items.quote: the Board has approved the appointment of Deloitte Haskins & Sells Chartered Accountants LLP as joint statutory auditor on the recommendation of the Audit Committee and subject to approval shareholders at the ensuing AGM.

items.statement: On-highway revenue vision INR5,000 crores by 2030 maintained
items.quote: So our stated vision is INR5,000 crores revenue by 2030. We are holding on to that position.

items.statement: Carbon black captive consumption 30%, external sales 70%; margins at industry average
items.quote: 30% we are consuming locally from the current capacity, around 70% is sold in the market, and margins are as per industry average.

items.statement: Management aims to push median EBITDA margin from ~8% towards high single digits (~9%) over time.
items.quote: Our objective is to take the median towards a high single digit, which is about 9%. So, that in a bad year like this, our EBITDA will be around 6.5%-7%, and in a good year, we will even cross 10% or 11%.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY27 is around INR 200 crores, similar to normal run-rate.
items.quote: No, I think it will be around that amount is what we should look at.

items.statement: Ice cream facility utilisation expected at 35-40% in first year; full utilisation targeted in 6-7 years assuming 20-25% YoY growth.
items.quote: in the first year, we are expecting the utilization to be around 35% to 40%. And we had mentioned that it will take us about six to seven years to utilize this facility completely.

items.statement: Milk selling prices raised ~4% in Q4; VAP prices raised across categories (paneer +5%, ice cream +13%); further selective hikes taken in April and continuing in May.
items.quote: we increased our milk prices by about 3.96% or 4% you could say for the quarter. And across value-added products, we had increased prices everywhere, like curd prices increased. There is again a mixed change also is there because different regions might have had different impact. Even paneer, we took up prices by 5%. Ice cream prices went up by about 13%, etc., so as we speak now, we have again in

items.statement: Increased competition as national brands enter Heritage's core markets and Heritage expands North/West; market fragmenting but Heritage holds franchise and grows volumes.
items.quote: Heritage is now available in North India and West India and all of that in Mumbai, Delhi, and all the same way, some of the national brands are also coming to our markets, right? So, there is increased competition in all markets. And that is also another reason why the market is getting more and more fragmented. But see, as far as we are concerned, there are two things that are most important for

items.statement: Acquired majority stake in Peanut Butter & Jelly (Get-A-Way ice cream) in Jan; total ~71% stake after additional 20% tranche; INR 9 crores paid, purchase price allocation created goodwill/intangibles.
items.quote: In the month of actually January, we have invested in PBJL Company. So, in that regard, actually, there is a purchase price allocation, whatever the price that we have paid, actually INR 9 crores. Then there is an agreement between these two parties to acquire actually additional 20%. So, that is a potential acquisition. Both together in the first or second quarter, it is going to be around 71% of

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin improved to 13.76% driven by higher volumes, better realizations and operational efficiency
items.quote: Operating EBITDA stood at INR 55 crores , up 42% year -on-year with EBITDA margins which have improved to 13.76, which is driven by higher volumes, better realizations and enhanced operational efficiency.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 12.31% supported by strong volume growth, improved margins and higher capacity utilization
items.quote: Operating EBITDA reached a new peak at INR 177 crores, up 42% year-on-year. EBITDA margins expanded to 12.31% for the year supported by strong volume growth, improved margins and higher capacity utilization.

items.statement: Management expects FY27 margins to be better than FY26 average but does not provide quarterly guidance due to volatility
items.quote: I would say strategically, as we are at a higher capacity utilization levels, we expect margins to be better than the average of last year, at least for this coming year.

items.statement: Nitrile latex running at almost full 100% capacity utilization; NBR at 100% utilization for next 4 quarters until new capacity in Q1 FY28
items.quote: We are running at almost full 100% capacity utilization now for Nitrile latex. And at least going forward, we expect to run at full 100% capacity utilization.

items.statement: No major capacity expansion in FY27; new NBR and synthetic latex capacity expected in Q1 FY28; de-bottlenecking projects underway
items.quote: FY '27, no. Most of this capacity will come on stream in FY '28. So, in FY '27, we will have growth for the whole year. And, yes, there are some de-bottlenecking projects which will help a little bit.

items.statement: New R&D center approved with planned spend of INR 20-25 crores on infrastructure
items.quote: We are building a new R&D center this year for which we have got approval from the board and we are going to spend somewhere between INR 20 crores to INR 25 crores, building a new R&D center.

items.statement: FY26 record high sales volumes up 14% YoY; highest ever export volumes also grew 14% YoY
items.quote: For FY '26, the company delivered a strong performance, achieving record high sales volumes, up 14% year-on-year and highest ever export volumes also grew, growing at 14% year-on-year.

items.statement: Demand stable across key core markets; Nitrile latex demand improving gradually over three years
items.quote: Demand is stable across key core markets and the proactive risk mitigation measures help us along with a strong balance sheet position help us navigate this volatility.

items.statement: Raw material prices increased ~70% in Q4 tracking crude; company covered supplies till end of June but faces week-to-week uncertainty
items.quote: We have seen the crude prices have gone up by about 70% in a couple of months. So that is about, round about the increase we are also looking at in raw material prices.

items.statement: Short-term margin improvement in Nitrile latex due to war situation and competitor supply issues; structural oversupply remains
items.quote: The war situation, we were actually better placed than some of our competitors in March, in the month of March. So, that helped for sure in Nitrile latex gains, as far as Nitrile latex margins, but as far as long-term is concerned, it still remains an oversupply.

items.statement: Middle East exports contribute ~12% of top line; facing freight cost increases and Chinese competition in Turkey/Egypt
items.quote: Vivek Thakur: 12%. Abhiraj Choksey: 12%, there we go. Okay. So, 12%. So, it is definitely a significant number. We are trying to make that up from other geographies and including India

items.statement: FY26 operating cash flow INR 200+ crores with INR 50 crores from working capital; expect structural profit improvement but working capital needs may rise with higher raw material prices
items.quote: Nothing is one time or very little is one time because it is, I mean, the whole year, in fact, was a challenging year in some sense. Only in March, you can argue there were some perhaps short-term benefits. But the remaining 11 months were sort of regular 11 months with challenges. So, we expect it to only improve cash generation, on an annual basis.

items.statement: Net cash positive ~INR 70 crores as of March 31 (cash/investments INR 160 crores vs total debt INR 92 crores); net debt-to-equity 0.08
items.quote: As of March 31st, we have a total debt of about INR 90 crores. And our investments and cash bank balances are INR 160-odd crores.

items.statement: Final dividend of Rs. 5.50 per share declared; total FY26 dividend Rs. 8 per share including interim
items.quote: The Board has announced a final dividend of Rs. 5.50 per equity share, which is subject to shareholders' approval. This takes the total dividend for FY '26 to Rs. 8 per equity share, including the interim dividend which was declared earlier.

items.statement: Proactively secured key raw materials in early March to ensure uninterrupted supplies; covered till end of June; multiple energy streams (gas/coal) prevented production loss
items.quote: We covered, Vivek mentioned in his opening remarks that we took a risk, covered a lot of the materials so that we could keep the plants running in March and April as soon as the materials stopped from the Middle East.

items.statement: Chinese latex entering Turkey/Egypt markets due to Middle East supply disruption; temporary competitive disadvantage from higher costs
items.quote: For the first time, we are seeing in Turkey and Egypt, for example, Chinese latex coming in there. So, that is something we are sort of watching closely.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty recommended by DGTR not notified by Finance Ministry; not built into FY27 plans; High Court provisional orders pending
items.quote: The Finance Ministry did not notify the anti-dumping duties that were recommended by the DGTR, which is part of the Commerce Ministry. There are some other legal cases on the same issue, not Apcotex, but they are ongoing.

items.statement: Sharp drop in crude prices would hurt margins due to high-cost inventory; demand destruction concern from sustained high petrochemical prices
items.quote: I think, look, a fall will definitely hurt us because we are covering for material. The call we have taken is that we are going to cover raw materials and ensure plants are running and we are not going to take a call on where crude prices and petrochemical prices go.

items.statement: New long-term incentive plan for senior management (5-year vesting, first payout 2030); new ApcoBuild leader appointed last year; R&D talent acquisition and grooming underway
items.quote: For one was a new policy on long-term incentives for certain senior management employees that we have just introduced in the last quarter. It is to be paid out over a period of five years, so that provision has been made. That will be paid out in the 5th year in 2030.

items.statement: One-time provisions in Q4: INR 14 crores employee benefits (LTIP, litigation, gratuity policy), INR 4 crores turbine impairment, INR 2 crores depreciation from useful life change (40 to 15 years)
items.quote: Employee benefit expenses include certain provisions of approximately INR 14 crores which relate to long-term incentive plan, pending litigations based on external legal advice and higher gratuity and leave encashment obligations arising from policy changes. Additionally, an impairment assessment of turbine and related accessories at our Valia facility, it resulted in recognition of impairment los

items.statement: Rajpat Logistics subsidiary expected to add 25% revenue on top of current ~INR400 cr base over next 2-3 years
items.quote: currently we are in the 400 cr bucket, correct? So, I can definitely say that Rajpat will add another 25% from that.

items.statement: Targeting ROCE above 15% from Rajpat Logistics subsidiary business
items.quote: we are expecting a upward of 15% in return on capital employed from that business, ROCE.

items.statement: Air cargo rates hardening 15% internationally since March; volume growth expected but rate growth to exceed volume growth
items.quote: As I'm talking to you from March, 15%, international rates have increased. So, rates are hardening.

items.statement: Government target to increase airports from 140 to 220 and passenger aircraft fleet from 700 to 1,800 creates structural growth opportunity
items.quote: government has a target of increasing the number of airports from 140 to 220. For companies like us, has immense opportunity due to this.

items.statement: FY26 profit before tax crossed INR10 cr milestone, up 34% YoY; PAT up 26% to INR9.58 cr
items.quote: profit also before tax rose -- crossed the milestone of INR10 crores. We have achieved the profit -- in fact our profit grew by over 34% year-on-year to INR10.30 crores.

items.statement: Air freight segment profit increased to INR11.26 cr in FY26 from INR8.53 cr in FY25
items.quote: segment air freight division profit increased to INR11.26 crores in FY 2025-26 compared to INR8.53 crores in the previous year.

items.statement: Finance cost reduced substantially to INR35 lakhs from INR1.18 cr in previous year
items.quote: our finance cost reduced substantially through INR35 lakhs only, from INR1.18 crores in the previous year.

items.statement: Company is practically debt-free with over INR20 cr cash and cash equivalents
items.quote: We are practically debt free company, although we have small amount of debt just for operational flexibility. As can we know in our company balance sheet we had more than INR20 crores cash and cash equivalent in hand.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR0.40 per equity share (30% of PAT) for FY26
items.quote: the Board has also recommended a final dividend of INR0.40 per equity share for 2025-2026. It is basically 30% of our profit after tax

items.statement: No immediate plans to enter warehousing asset business; current operations yield higher ROCE than warehouse operations
items.quote: our current operations are giving us more ROCE than if we venture into the warehouse operation. So that is the process going on but never say never.

items.statement: Actively pursuing redevelopment of non-core property with adjacent properties; meeting scheduled next week
items.quote: we have one property is there, which is we are actively pursuing for the redevelopment. At the same time, that adjacent to our property, there are two more properties are also there.

items.statement: Rajpat Logistics subsidiary formed in Dec 2025 to add asset-light trucking vertical with minimal receivables
items.quote: we've formed one subsdiary company in the last December quarter, Rajpat Logistics Limited. As we are talking, we are continuing to getting code for doing logistic business in top corporate of India.

items.statement: Implemented automated system to stop transactions when customer outstanding exceeds comfort threshold without manual intervention
items.quote: For the trade receivable control , I think probably we are the only one of the company in our industry who have put the system so that if the outstanding increase more than certain days for a customer which we are not comfortable, then the system only stop it and there is no manual intervention.

items.statement: Leveraging AI and automation to improve productivity without job losses; using institutional knowledge alongside system-driven controls
items.quote: we are trying to do the more automation now so that more and more automation can happen and the existing manpower can be used more productively. We are a sensitive company and we don't want anybody to lose the job.

items.statement: Geopolitical situation creating supply issues but benefiting organized players with rate hardening
items.quote: this is actually, I can tell you, unfortunately, it's a favourable position for us because we are organized players. But at the same time, rates are hardening.

items.statement: Management believes company is undervalued relative to performance and committed to valuation rerating
items.quote: Patel Integrated Logistics Limited is undervalued relative to its performance with double-digit revenue growth, liberal dividend payments and unmatched operational leverage, we are expecting very soon the company will have a valuation rerating

items.statement: Expects 10-14% growth in international business for FY27, possibly up to 15%
items.quote: Yes, we expect 10 to 14% growth in our international business this year, as per our current business plan. Last year there was 4% growth, this year we expect 10 to 14%. Maybe even 15%.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected around INR 120 crores including land acquisition
items.quote: No, it'll be closer INR 120 crores and the reason for that is we're also looking at land.

items.statement: Total announced capex of INR 240 crores over next 18 months including INR 40 crores for land
items.quote: So I mean, you know, you need to factor all that in that it's a total announcement of 240 crores. To be honest, it's not 120, 120 is just for this year.

items.statement: Capex split 90% for machines and 10% for infrastructure and building
items.quote: Fundamentally it is 90% for machines and 10% for infrastructure and building and plant.

items.statement: Maintenance capex at 10% of turnover covering maintenance, quality, new product development and small improvements
items.quote: We spend 10% of our turnover on a combination of maintenance, quality, new produc t development, and small -small capex improvements, which could be for balancing the lines

items.statement: Effective utilization near full at several plants; brownfield capex initiated with machinery orders placed and arriving
items.quote: While reported utilization is roughly 85%, in reality effective utilization at several of our plants is much closer to full, when you take into account the demand variations, once you adjust also for m aintenance, shift patterns, changeovers, and generally the demand pattern from different segments

items.statement: Major enhancement projects commissioning from June-July through FY27 to Q1 2028; partial benefits from current quarter
items.quote: We expect commissioning of major enhancement projects starting from June -July and continuing through this financial year and beyond up to the first quarter of 2028. You will start seeing partial benefits initially from the current quarter and more during the rest of the year.

items.statement: Mahant Toolroom order book doubled to INR 50 crores from INR 25 crores at acquisition announcement
items.quote: They have an order book close to INR50 crores now, and we expect full operational control between mid-April and May.

items.statement: Mahant Toolroom order book executable pace depends on defence rollout speed; not predictable over 12-18 months
items.quote: No, it doesn't work like that in aerospace. It means the significance of that is when we announced the acquisition, they had an order book of INR25 crores. The pace depends on how much they scale, that means enhanced pace will depend on whether a particular landing gear on one aircraft for example is rolled out right across, okay, and how fast.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 19.5% from 18.3% driven by structural initiatives
items.quote: For the full year, revenue from operations grew 11% to INR1,335 crores. EBITDA increased by 19% year-on-year to INR267 crores and margins expanded to 19.5% from 18.3% in this financial year.

items.statement: Margin improvement from solar energy, automation, yield improvement, and renegotiated vendor costing
items.quote: These include higher use of solar energy leading to lower power and fuel costs, higher automation reducing dependence on labour, continuous improvement in yields, and renegotiated vendor costing across material components, logistics, insurance across all elements of material related costs.

items.statement: Industrial business targeted at 18-20% EBITDA margin requirement; aspirational goal 18-21% consistently
items.quote: The kind of industrial bearings we are focusing on are as profitable as what NRB currently makes which is at the end of the day a 18 % to 20% EBITDA margin is a requirement for us to focus in any area. At some if some of it is 30%. Yes. And some of it might be 14%. Will it average out to what we have over the next five years? Will it pan out and be in line with our aspirational goal of maintaining

items.statement: Domestic business resilient despite global challenges; export demand impacted but international business grew 4%
items.quote: While export demand was impacted, NRB and its subsidiaries remain more resilient than many of those around us. Our international business did grow over the previous year to a little over 4%.

items.statement: Replacement market grew 4% but challenging last quarter; focus shifted more to OEMs
items.quote: I think the last quarter has been extremely challenging for most companies in the replacement and distribution space and we to be honest, revised our plan and decided that we would focus more on OEMs.

items.statement: Automotive applications in transmission, driveline, chassis, steering; not in engine or wheel applications
items.quote: We are in transmission, driveline, chassis and in steering. We're not much in wheel applications and therein lies a huge opportunity for us.

items.quote: For the last year the number was 1,204 crores digital transaction. Prior to that that was 940 crores. So good impressive growth has been seen. Our mobile app is ranked number one in Google Play store.

items.statement: Management expects FY27 performance to improve progressively, with new product scale-up meaningful in H2 FY27
items.quote: As we look ahead to FY '27, we expect to increasingly benefit from the foundations that have been laid with performance improving progressively as the year unfolds, especially as our new products scale up meaningfully in the second half.

items.statement: Major investment phase substantially complete; no large greenfield capex needed for FY27-28 growth plan
items.quote: Over the past few years, we have invested materially to build global scale capabilities and capacity, particularly in biosimilars, insulins, peptides and complex generics. As we stand today, this major investment phase is substantially complete.

items.statement: Malaysia drug product Line 2 qualifying soon; drug substance doubling by end FY27; minor debottlenecking in Bangalore
items.quote: The DP has happened. The Line 2 has is getting qualified as we are speaking and will get operational soon. DS, the drug substance doubling will happen towards the end of this financial year.

items.quote: Biosimilars revenue for Q4 FY '26 stood at ₹2,756 crores, representing a 12% year-on-year increase, driven primarily by advanced markets.

items.quote: EBITDA was at INR1,073 crores with a margin of 23%. Adjusted for generic lenalidomide in the base, this was up 29% year -on-year.

items.statement: Biosimilars Q4 EBITDA INR 720 cr at 26% margin, up 33% YoY; FY26 biosimilars EBITDA up 40% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at ₹720 crores, representing growth of 33% on a year-on-year basis. This translates into an EBITDA margin of 26%.

items.quote: EBITDA margins were at 8% , improved nearly 300 basis points over Q3 of this fiscal, driven by higher volumes and operating leverage.

items.quote: If you remember in March '25, including structured instruments, we had, in fact, more than $1.5 billion of net debt. That's down to $1.1 billion now. So, it will hover between $1.1 billion to $1.2 billion subject to working capital.

items.quote: We've seen tremendous success with our biosimilar ustekinumab, which continues to gain market share. And in fact, if you've seen the IQVIA numbers as of February and the overall market is close to a fifth already.

items.statement: CRDMO FY26 revenue INR 3,739 cr, up 3% YoY; EBITDA margin 25% in line with revised guidance; 85 client/regulatory audits completed
items.quote: FY '26 revenue from operations were at ₹3,739 crores, up 3% year-on-year. Operating EBITDA margin at 25% for the year was in line with Syngene's revised full year guidance.

items.statement: Average cost of borrowing 5.6%; blended with working capital <7% gives ~6.5% blended cost.
items.quote: Average cost of borrowing for us is about 5.6% -- average is 5.6% at this point of time. And the working capital, which is less than 7%. So that is the blended. If you blend it out, it should be in the range of 6.5.

items.statement: Industry pursuing permanent cotton import duty removal; government dialogue ongoing; expects action within 6 months.

items.quote: Moreover, during FY26, the Company reported strong cash conversion ratio of approx. 98%, which has been computed based upon operating cash flow to PAT, excluding finance income.

items.statement: Investing heavily in AI across functions; agentic AI deployed for marketing keyword optimization (20,000 line items), training all team members.
items.quote: We've already taken major steps and initiatives already showing us very good results. If I give you a small example, let's say, when you do a Google campaign, there are about 20,000-line items on which you are spending on Google Search.

items.statement: Open to acquisitions but nothing in pipeline; Mebaz turnaround cited as proof of capability; targets too small for scale.
items.quote: While there is nothing in the pipeline that we have, or nothing that we are actively exploring, the way I would put it is, overall, we do have the cash in our books to ex plore acquisitions

items.statement: Historical 50% profit dividend payout; capital allocation policy under review, concrete answer expected by next earnings call.
items.quote: Up until now, what we've been doing in the history of the Company after IPO is that we've been doing about 50% profits as dividends.

items.statement: Consumer sentiment turned neutral after war onset in late Feb/early March; May impacted by Adhik Maas, June/July weddings expected to offset.
items.quote: But given that the war started in the later parts of end of Feb, early March, that's when I feel that consumer sentiments, not to a large extent, but then again became sort of neutral.

items.statement: Twamev EBOs mostly build-to-suit with 18-20 month lag; targeting 5-6 signings in FY27, openings staggered into FY28/29.
items.quote: Let's say, if we sign a property today, the store actually opens 18 months from now to 20 months from now.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 footfalls up low single digits after many quarters of decline; conversion stable at high levels; average basket size up ~1.5%.
items.quote: If I speak about just the last quarter, we saw footfalls improving by low single digits. Although that low single digit looks like a low number, it's -- after many quarters, we saw that increase happening.

items.statement: Other expenses down 7% YoY in Q4 due to inventory efficiency (lower job work) and lower Q4 marketing spend vs prior year.
items.quote: One was, if you see our inventory, we are bringing efficiency in the inventory thing. So as a result, our job expenses have gone down. Our marketing costs overall were higher than last year. But if you look at only Q4, it was a bit lower.

items.statement: GST rate revision in Sep'25 increased blended GST from ~10%, permanently widening retail-to-net sales gap; growth rates to align from FY27.
items.quote: Now the average, pre -GST change, was -- approximately 10% was our blended GST, which has now increased sli ghtly. And hence, this difference is here to stay now between the 2 numbers at a decent

items.statement: March 2026 was a tremendous month driving Q4 growth; April decent; May impacted by Adhik Maas, July weddings to boost June.
items.quote: Majority of the quarter growth actually came from March itself, which actually was a tremendous month for us. And overall, we saw that footfalls had improved pretty decently.

items.statement: Overseas destination weddings not target audience; domestic weddings with foreign guests are strong opportunity for quick turnaround.
items.quote: To be very honest with you, my honest answer here would be anyone doing an overseas wedding, that wedding family is typically not our target audience at all.

items.statement: FY27 volume target of 250+ MMSCM, double-digit growth over FY26's 223.67 MMSCM
items.quote: Next year we are planning double-digit and it will be fairly, you can say 30% plus sort of expectation we are making over what we have done YoY. So, this year like you know, 223 MMSCM we had. So, we will be definitely crossing 250 or maybe more, maybe much more.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA per SCM target of INR 5.3-5.5, up 10-15% from current INR 5+
items.quote: And on the EBITDA front also, we will be plus INR 5.2 rupees and in the range of INR 5.3 rupees to INR 5.5 rupees per SCM.

items.statement: FY27 Namakkal-Trichy capex planned at INR 150-180 crore, adding to INR 257 crore already invested
items.quote: And this year, FY'27, we have planned exceeding INR 150 crore more in that particular GA. And maybe, if things all permit well, we may be exceeding INR 150 crore also, maybe INR 170 crore, INR 180 crore we are targeting internally.

items.statement: FY27 total CNG station additions planned at 36 stations
items.quote: And this time we are expecting another 36 to be added. We will not be able to really grow. See, we had done 111, we did in several years, and this year alone we did 39. So another 36 we have kept moderately to be said to my stakeholders.

items.statement: Gross margins 25-26% in FY26, up from prior year; target to maintain in FY27 despite geopolitical volatility
items.quote: So the gross margins that we see, they are in the range of 25% to 26%. They have increased from previous year. Now, as the situation is unfolding in the Gulf, so keeping that in mind, we expect the margins in the same range.

items.statement: CNG cost increases from APM ceiling price rise to $7/MMBTU and NWG formula increases passed on to consumers in April, protecting margins
items.quote: So there was a cost increase primarily due to two factors. One was increase in the ceiling price of APM gas, which was $6.75 per MMBTU for previous financial year. Now it is $7 per MMBTU for current financial year. And a significant amount of increase in gas prices under NWG formula. So, due to these two increases, our cost for CNG had increased and we were able to successfully pass on the resulta

items.statement: Over 75-80% of CNG volume fed through domestic sources; long-term contracts with Shell and GSPC insulate from Qatar supply disruptions
items.quote: You see, our portfolio for CNG sector, which is the most profitable volume-wise also and net margin-wise also, is broadly, you see, more than 75% to 80%, you can call it to be more precise, is fed through domestic sources. As regards RLNG and Qatar, which you mentioned, we have got long-term contracts with Shell and GSPC.

items.statement: CNG station network reached 150 stations as of March 31, 2026, up 26% YoY from 111; PNG pipeline network 6,695 inch-km
items.quote: Additionally, IRM Energy expanded the CNG station network, for which we are really proud of a network of 150 stations landmark we have crossed this time as of 31st March 2026. Last year the same comparable figure was 111 stations up to FY'25. This represents a massive 26% YoY growth in the CNG segment.

items.statement: Total debt INR 72 crore (incl. lease liability) at FY26 end, down from INR 140 crore; net cash INR 170 crore; peak debt FY27 seen at INR 70-80 crore
items.quote: right now, at the end of March, we are around INR 49 crores of term loans. So, looking at the CapEx this year and we have a INR 45 crores term loan sanctioned. So, peak debt will be in this range only , INR 70 crores to INR 80 crores for this financial year

items.statement: Namakkal-Trichy FY27 capex funded from INR 194 crore IPO proceeds; other GAs funded from internal accruals and INR 40-45 crore term loan
items.quote: So, Namakkal and Trichy, we have, you know, IPO funds available with us. So, as of the close of March, we have about INR 194 crores of funds available. So, through that we will do the CapEx in Namakkal and Trichy. For the other three GFs, largely we rely on internal accruals, plus we have a line from term loan from the bank of about INR 40 crores -INR 45 crores is available in that.

items.statement: Dealer collections targeted daily by 1 PM; proceeds parked in overnight/liquid funds earning ~INR 2 crore other income in Q4 FY26
items.quote: We expect the dealers to deposit the proceeds, you know, the following day. Like, you know, 6:00 to 6:00 a.m. -- 6:00 a.m. to 6:00 a.m. we are doing the metering. And then we want our all dealers to deposit their proceeds, net of their commission back to us by 1 o'clock every day.

items.statement: NGT order for Fatehgarh Sahib implementation delayed due to gas supply constraints; will pursue stricter enforcement when supply improves
items.quote: The moment, because, see, demand destruction is happening already, and at that point of time, if we force them more, then these companies will be in a more agitated mood and then difficulty will come on our credibility also. So we are taking a very cautious approach in that. The moment the supply situation is balanced or it is slightly favored strategically, we would like to compel the government

items.statement: Namakkal-Trichy mix expected to evolve to 70% CNG, 20% domestic/commercial PNG over 1-2 years, similar to Banaskantha and Diu-Gir Somnath
items.quote: So going forward, as and when we lay the infrastructure, this mix over a period of one or two years will be between 70 and 20, just like what we have seen it in other GAs like Banaskantha and Diu & Gir-Somnath.

items.statement: Signed MOU with TNSTC for 71 PNG buses running, 50 more expected May 2026; 120 taxis converted to CNG in Trichy; LNG dispensing facility commissioned at Rasipuram
items.quote: From the institutional partnership standpoint, we have signed an MOU with Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation in Namakkal for deploying PNG buses, with 71 buses currently continuing, 50 additional buses are expected in May '26 this time, and the total current consumption stands approximately 6,000 kilo per day, attributing to 17% of the total CNG volume in the Namakkal and Trichy GA.

items.statement: Farm Gas (33% stake) now very profitable due to CBG demand; Venuka Polymers (50% JV) near break-even, revenue expected to double or 2.5x next year from irrigation and power conduit diversification
items.quote: Farm Gas had been doing some business. Initially they faced certain challenges due to farmer agitation and all that last year , so there was slight -- but they are cash positive. But in the current six months or rather you can say four, five months, they are very, very profitable currently. You understand the kind of gas shortage which has happened. So government is also encouraging CBG. Venuka Po

items.statement: EBITDA per SCM >INR 5 in FY26, targeting 10-15% improvement in FY27
items.quote: EBITDA per SCM, currently you can say that company-wise if you see -- segment-wise I would not like to mention, but company-wise you see it is more than INR 5 EBITDA per SCM. And we, going forward, will improve it by another 10% to 15% going forward in the next financial year.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 PAT impacted by one-time INR 1.34 crore JV receivable provision and INR 2.86 crore erroneous bank charges, both expected to reverse in Q1 FY27
items.quote: So the difference between that of the both quarters is INR 2 crores, so largely that is the reason. And one bank charges have been levied of around INR 2.8 crores, which we have spoken with our bank, and we are pretty sure from the bank side that it will be taken care in the next coming months. So that was the one-time effect.

items.statement: Management expects 20% plus revenue growth in FY27 and EBITDA growth to outperform revenue growth
items.quote: Looking ahead, with multiple growth levers in place, capacity ramp -up and expanding product portfolio, deeper market penetration and a strong R&D engine, we are confident in our ability to deliver 20% plus revenue growth and create long-term value for our stakeholders.

items.statement: PAT growth expected to outpace EBITDA growth due to fixed depreciation and finance costs from Jammu facility
items.quote: With improving scale and operating leverage, we expect EBITDA growth to outperform revenue growth, as the Jammu plant utilization ramp up further. PAT growth should outpace EBITDA growth added by the fact that the depreciation and financial costs related t o the Jammu facility are largely fixed and already reflected in the base.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to improve in FY27 over FY26
items.quote: So this is, again, a complex area to comment on the margin expansion. But what we can say that it should be better than the current year. Next year, the margin should be better than the current year.

items.statement: New Baddi general block capex estimated at INR150-170 crores across FY27 and FY28 with revenue potential of INR450-500 crores
items.quote: But on an overall level, the way we are seeing it right now, the overall capital outlay should be in the range of INR150 crores, INR170 crores. And the overall potential of this block at an optimum level should be in the range of INR450 crores to INR500-odd crores revenue.

items.statement: Jammu facility completed first full year of operation with steady ramp-up; Baddi facility at higher utilization prompting new land acquisition for general block expansion
items.quote: A key highlight during the year was the successful completion of the first full year of operation at our Kathua facility in Jammu. The ramp -up has progressed steadily, and I would like to appreciate the effort of our team across all functions for ensuring smooth execution while maintaining high standard of quality and compliance.

items.statement: Jammu facility exit run rate INR90+ crores quarterly in Q4 FY26; nearing EBITDA breakeven, expected to turn EBITDA positive in coming quarters
items.quote: So this quarter, so basically, if you talk about full year, Jammu is achieved around INR300 crores. And this quarter, we are nearing EBITDA. And in coming quarter, as we said that the Jammu ramp-up is going on. We are very much positive that in coming quarter, we should be able to achieve EBITDA positive as well as start covering the fixed cost on Jammu part.

items.statement: CDMO customer base expanded to over 350 clients including leading Indian pharmaceutical companies
items.quote: Starting with the CDMO business, we continue to deepen our presence in the domestic pharmaceutical market by expanding our customer base to over 350 clients, including several leading pharmaceutical companies in India.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin 15.4%; Q4 EBITDA margin 14.9% due to product mix change; ex-Jammu EBITDA margin estimated ~18%
items.quote: EBITDA for the full year came in at INR250.3 crores as against INR198.2 crores last year. Operating margins for FY '26 came in at 15.4%.

items.statement: API price increases due to Middle East conflict largely passed through to CDMO customers on cost-plus basis
items.quote: So yes, so due to this going on conflict, there is certain uptick in prices of our raw materials and major ingredients. You rightly said, our cost -- our pricing with CDMO's customers on cost-plus basis. So largely, those increase has been passed to our customers.

items.statement: Cephalosporin API prices reduced in Q2-Q3 FY26, stabilized in H1 Q4, increased in April 2025
items.quote: So yes, if you remember, our cephalosporin prices have reduced during the quarter 2 and quarter 3 of this financial year and started stabilizing in first half of quarter 4 before this conflict plays out.

items.statement: Raw material availability not a concern; price increases due to supply-side disruptions from Middle East conflict
items.quote: Sudarshan Ji, as far as the availability is concerned, there is no such problem, what should I say, so prices are going up. That is the one thing, but availability is not at all a concern. So nothing is in shortage.

items.statement: Cephalosporin facility in Baddi received UK-MHRA approval; Jammu blocks received PIC/S certification via SMDC Ukraine
items.quote: Our cephalosporin facility in Baddi received UK-MHRA approval, while our Jammu blocks received PIC/S certification through SMDC Ukraine. These certifications will support our entry into regulated international market and strengthen our positioning as a quality -focused pharmaceutical manufacturing partner.

items.statement: All facilities compliant with Schedule M and international regulations (MHRA, EU-GMP, PIC/S)
items.quote: So, schedule M is now effective across the country. And it is better that we comment on our capability. Our all facilities are well compliant with the local regulation as well as the international regulation. We have the approvals like if you see in the last year also, we have received MHRA certification.

items.statement: Exports contributed 31% of FY26 revenue and 28% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Exports for the full year contributed 31% to the overall revenue.

items.statement: CDMO business well diversified across major Indian and global pharma companies with no over-reliance on any single customer or product
items.quote: So Vansh, as far as our CDMO business is concerned, our business is well diversified amongst major pharmaceutical companies of India as well as globally. And it is well diversified, not having over-reliant of any customer or any product.

items.statement: Branded Generics domestic split ~70% domestic, 30-35% exports; trade generics model with hybrid distribution strategy
items.quote: Normally, we do not track our geography -based business at a business area level. But roughly, it is in the range of 70% domestic and 30%, 35% exports.

items.statement: Semaglutide R&D progressing with positive exhibit batch results; targeting wave 2 launch after initial market entry by competitors
items.quote: Yes. So for semaglutide, we are closely monitoring the market and we are working in our R&D and our initial R&D have worked on the product, and we are getting a positive figure from there. So there are 2 things that one is the market side and the other is our execution of our exhibit batches and filing to the local FDA.

items.statement: Sharon Bio revenue ~INR240 crores in FY26 with better margin profile than group average EBITDA margin
items.quote: Sharon has been performing well. It has integrated good enough over the last 2 years of our acquisition. This year, their revenue is around INR240-odd crores. As we said, it has mainly presence in export regulatory markets. So their margin profile is better as far as our average EBITDA margin is concerned.

items.statement: Depreciation and interest costs for Jammu facility already reflected in FY26 base; new capex interest to be capitalized for 1.5 years until commercial production
items.quote: Yes. So the cost of depreciation and interest is already taken care last -- in the FY '26, right? So if there is an improvement in EBITDA, so PAT will outperform the EBITDA.

items.statement: CDMO growth driven by increased product portfolio, new customers, and deeper wallet share with existing customers; Branded Generics growth driven by geographical expansion and deeper penetration
items.quote: Our CDMO business revenue came in at INR314.8 crores, up by 41% year-on-year, mainly led by increased product portfolio, adding new customers and deepening our wallet share with existing customers. The Branded Generics business revenue stood at INR133 crores, growth of 46% on a year-on-year basis, showcasing a pure testament to our distribution strategies.

items.statement: Schedule M compliance creates advantage for compliant players like Innova Captab
items.quote: And definitely, those who are complying will be in an advantage phase that I can say.

items.statement: Margin expansion depends on product basket, geographical presence, and overall revenue growth; unable to quantify exact delta
items.quote: So this is, again, a complex area to comment on the margin expansion. But what we can say that it should be better than the current year. Next year, the margin should be better than the current year. Because how it is a complex that will depend on the product basket, geographical presence, everything.

items.statement: FY27 target: double-digit top-line growth and double-digit bottom-line growth; bottom-line to grow faster than top-line
items.quote: our idea is even in the year of consolidation to keep a double-digit top-line growth and a double-digit bottom-line growth

items.statement: FY27 store plan: gross addition of >100 EBOs, net addition of 30-40 stores
items.quote: We plan to add a gross of about 100 EBO stores in FY '27; however, we will continue to exit underperforming stores during the year and we think the net increase would be 30 to 40 this year

items.statement: FY27 capex similar to FY26 (~INR180 cr); FY26 breakup: INR50 cr SAP, INR60 cr Hyderabad garmenting factory, balance stores & plant maintenance
items.quote: the capex for the next year also would remain almost on the similar lines. So, of the INR180 crores, INR50 crores is on account of our SAP implementation that we did. About INR60 crores on account of our new garmenting factory in Hyderabad, and the balance are all new stores and plant maintenance capex

items.statement: Factory utilizations now above 90% (some 95%+), up from traditional 80-85%, driving opex reduction
items.quote: Our factory utilizations, which tradit ionally used to be between 80% -85%, have all gone above 90%. There are factories which we have operated at 95% plus also

items.statement: Garmenting Q1 FY27 order books completely full; booking latter half of Q2 now
items.quote: my first quarter order books are completely full. I am doing the latter half of second quarter order booking right now

items.statement: Branded Apparel core four brands EBITDA margin 7.8% (excl. emerging businesses); target double-digits in 2 years
items.quote: The core four brands' revenue was INR1,667 crores with an EBITDA margin of 7.8%, which is without these new businesses. So, the core brands are actually quite okay at 7.8% and we will endeavour to take it to double-digits over the next two years' time

items.statement: Emerging businesses FY26: INR140 cr revenue, INR30 cr loss; will be reported separately from next quarter
items.quote: For the year, it is about INR140 crores, but on this INR140 crores, because we invest in these businesses, we incur losses. So, when you start looking at the four core brands, if you take out roughly INR140 crores of turnover and if you add back t he losses to the profit, then you'll start seeing that the four apparel brands actually deliver between 7.5%-8% profit already

items.statement: Sleepwear segment annual EBITDA drag ~INR20 cr; provisions taken in FY26
items.quote: It's about INR20 crores was the annual drag. So, that we should get back, but this year to do that we have had to take some provisions

items.statement: Premiumization (wool, linen) to lift gross margin, but rising Merino wool and flax prices may offset gains
items.quote: the gross margin should go up because , two things here. Number one is as you sell more premium products, directionally your gross margin should go up. However, currently there is a challenge that the wool prices are going through the roof, Merino wool prices. Also, flax prices are going up

items.statement: Net working capital days improved from 87 to 77 in FY26; target <70 days in FY27
items.quote: We will also be working on the inventory and we are actually targeting less than 70 days of working capital, sorry, yes, less than 70 days of working capital in the next financial year

items.statement: Debt-free with net cash surplus of INR179 cr as of FY26 end
items.quote: We remain debt-free with a net cash surplus of INR17 9 crores

items.statement: Strategy: premiumization (wool suiting, linen shirting, premium garments) and casualization (smart casuals, polos, chinos, denim) led by ColorPlus
items.quote: For FY '27, our strategic growth pieces include premiumization across all segments , i.e., shift towards wool in suiting; linen in shirting, and more premium category of garments in branded apparel. The second lever that we are going to push is casualization

items.statement: UK FTA announced, EU FTA announced (not yet implemented); garmenting expects incremental EU/UK orders improving mix and margins
items.quote: The advantage that we got was the UK FTA was announced and now the EU FTA is also announced, though they are not implemented but will get implemented. So, we started getting a lot of interest from these places

items.statement: New leadership: CEO Satyaki Ghosh (88 days), CFO E.C. Prasad (3 months), CMO Kalpana Singh (joined March from HUL), seeking CIO
items.quote: With the recent appointment of Rak esh Tiwary as Group CFO, Prasad as Lifestyle CFO, and myself as the CEO, and I just introduced Kalpana as the new CMO, Raymond Lifestyle Limited is poised to accelerate its growth agenda

items.statement: Branded Apparel like-for-like retail growth double-digit in Q4 FY26
items.quote: We witnessed double-digit like-for-like growth in retail channels of Branded Apparel segment

items.statement: Branded Textile Q4 FY26 revenue INR831 cr (+14% YoY), EBITDA INR115 cr (+126% YoY) driven by volume, premiumization, ASP growth, scale
items.quote: In our Branded Textile segment, revenue grew 14% to INR831 crores in Q4, driven by robust volume growth and premiumization. EBITDA for the segment grew by 126% to INR115 crores on account of improved product mix, strong volume, ASP growth, and scale leverage

items.statement: Garmenting Q4 FY26 revenue INR342 cr (+38% YoY), EBITDA INR14 cr (vs -INR7 cr), margin 4.1%; highest-ever monthly revenue in March
items.quote: The segment reported a revenue of INR342 crores in Q4 FY26 as compared to INR248 crores in the same quarter previous year, reflecting a growth of 38% Y-o-Y. The segment reported an EBITDA of INR14 crores in Q4 FY26 compared to negative INR7 crores in Q4 FY25, and the EBITDA margin for the quarter was at 4.1%

items.statement: High-value cotton shirting (B2B) Q4 FY26 revenue INR197 cr (+6% YoY), EBITDA INR20 cr (vs INR61 cr with INR53 cr one-time subsidy)
items.quote: In our high value cotton shirting, the B2B segment, revenue grew at 6% to INR197 crores in Q4 and EBITDA for the segment was INR20 crores as compared to INR61 crores in Q4 last year, but last year Q4 EBITDA of INR61 crores had a INR53 crores one-time subsidy from the government for our Amravati plant

items.statement: Key risks: West Asia conflict (Brent >$100), below-average monsoon (92%), potential US tariff escalation, raw material price inflation (wool, flax)
items.quote: We are closely monitoring from Raymond the US -Iran conflict, which has kept brent crude prices hovering over $100 . And leading to increased energy, raw material prices, and freight costs. Domestically, we face the dual challenge of extreme heat waves affecting multiple states and below-average monsoon forecast at 92%

items.statement: ESG targets: renewable energy 5-6% increase from FY25 baseline in FY26, 25% by 2030; Scope 1&2 emissions down 4-5% from FY25, target 15% reduction by 2030; 40% female representation by 2030
items.quote: On renewable energy, we are on track to increase our renewable percentage between 5% to 6% this year from our baseline of FY25, and we remain on track to increase this to 25% of our total energy requirement by 2030. On Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions, we have reduced between 4% and 5% this year from our baseline year of FY '25, and we are on track to reduce these by 15% by 2030

items.statement: FY27 AUM growth guidance of 22-25% (3x GDP) and ROA target of 3%+ with mid-to-late teens ROE over 8-10 quarters
items.quote: Our sense is we should be able to grow business at about three times of GDP, so look at anywhere between 22% to 25%, and that's our commitment to the Street on a forward-looking basis unless we see something massive.

items.statement: FY27 credit cost guidance of 2.7-2.8% after FLDG benefit and management overlay
items.quote: And going forward also, we would expect the credit cost to be in the range of 2.7% to 2.8%, that is what is the plan projection.

items.statement: NIM improved 25bps YoY to 9.4% in FY26; cost of funds fell 48bps to 8.5%; incremental CoF at 8.6% in Q4FY26
items.quote: For FY26, NII grew by 20% Y-o-Y to INR1,377 crores and NIMs improved by 25 basis points year-on-year to 9.4%. The cost of fund for FY26 decreased by 48 basis points year-on-year to 8.5%.

items.statement: Management expects to hold CoF at 8.5-8.6% in FY27 with NIM expansion from D2C mix shift to 65%
items.quote: I think we will definitely not see a reduction in the cost of fund, but we will be able to hold on to the numbers that we have demonstrated this year. So, maybe we will not see any further reduction, but I think 8.5% to 8.6% is something we'll be able to hold and with the expansion in the D2C mix should see improvement in yields

items.statement: AUM grew 22% YoY and 10% QoQ to INR 16,594 Cr; D2C AUM grew 39% YoY to INR 9,800 Cr (59% of total)
items.quote: Our AUM has grown by about 22% on a year-on-year basis and about 10% over the previous quarter to reach INR 16,594 Cr, outpacing the industry, reflecting the sustained momentum and growth driven by direct-to-customer business which now accounts for 59% of our total assets under management.

items.statement: Consumer finance AUM reached INR 5,000+ Cr; MSME AUM grew 43% YoY to INR 3,691 Cr; Rural AUM grew 8% QoQ to INR 1,009 Cr
items.quote: The AUM has grown to now about INR5,000 crores plus. During the quarter, we've added few more partners, further strengthening our distribution capabilities.

items.statement: GNPA 1.2%, NNPA 0.6% in Q4FY26; Stage-2 assets fell from 2.6% (Sep) to 1.5% (Mar); X-bucket collection efficiency 99.4% (MSME) and 99.6% (Rural)
items.quote: GNPA and NNPA improved quarter-on-quarter to 1.2% and 0.6% respectively. Credit cost improved from 3.2% in FY25 to 2.8% in FY26, which is in line with the guidance given in the previous calls.

items.statement: Rural finance GNPA ~4bps; 84% of MFI book covered under CGFMU; 100% loans underwritten via proprietary Nu Score
items.quote: The GNPA remains negligible at about four basis point as of March '26. Additionally, I must reiterate that 84% of our MFI book is covered under CGFMU, providing strong risk protection.

items.statement: RBI Feb 2026 guideline allows FLDG cash collateral benefit in ECL computation; management created INR 66 Cr overlay for macro uncertainty
items.quote: During the quarter, RBI issued the guidelines on treatment of default loss guarantee in computation of ECL, permitting NBFC to factor in the cash collateral as FLDG, thereby alignin g the regulatory approach with IndAS requirement

items.statement: Added 66 branches (net 64) in Q4FY26; 17 new MSME branches and 64 rural branches added in FY26; rural network now 342 branches
items.quote: We have added 66 branches and merged two branches during the quarter.

items.statement: Total borrowings INR 12,258 Cr; 60% variable rate; 25% offshore/DFI funding; debt-equity improved from 3.9x to 3.1x; capital adequacy 22.6%
items.quote: Total borrowings at the end of the quarter stood at INR12,258 crores, with around 60% linked to variable interest rate, positioning us well to benefit from the ong oing decline in interest rates

items.statement: D2C mix at 59% (target 65%); Consumer 30%, MSME 22%, MFI 6% of AUM; fee income from placement INR 31 Cr and credit funds INR 38 Cr
items.quote: Within the AUM mix, the direct-to-customer business contributed 59% with MSME finance at 22%, consumer finance at about 30%, and MFI at 6%.

items.statement: Consumer finance: 70% repeat customers; 25-26k loans/day underwritten via scorecards; MSME avg ticket INR 11-15L with 100% registered mortgage
items.quote: 70% of our customers are repeat customers, which demonstrate powerful proof of underwriting quality and customer stickiness on our

items.statement: Exclusively diamond jewellery (18K gold studded); rings 28%, studded mangalsutra/pendants 25-27%, earrings 15-17%, necklaces 10%, bangles/bracelets 5-6% each
