items.statement: Working capital efficiency funded FY26 capex, significant improvement in inventory management
items.quote: We try to make an improvement in working capital management, and that also is reflected in the non-operating other income. So these were some N O C IL initiatives which we undertook, which is already reflected in FY '26 results

items.statement: No project debt borrowed yet, has bank lines above Rs.100 crores at repo-linked rates
items.quote: So as of today, we have not borrowed any debt. We are having some lines above Rs.100 crores from the bank, but we will utilize it when needed. It depends on that. And it is repo-linked interest rates.

items.statement: Customer stickiness significantly improved over 3-5 years due to deeper penetration, supply reliability, approvals
items.quote: And with all the approvals and the increased volumes that we have got with also the ability to prove our supply reliability and with the trust that we have gained, it's significantly -- the stickiness needle has significantly moved over the last 3 to 5 years.

items.statement: Price critical but not everything; customers value supply reliability, quality, performance during difficult times
items.quote: Absolutely. While price is critical, but it is not everything. That's why we need to prove our capability, our ability to supply reliably in quality and also during difficult times.

items.statement: Increased competitive intensity from Chinese players in latex market
items.quote: There is increased competitive intensity from Chinese players in that market.

items.statement: Volume mix 70% domestic, 30% export; value mix 67% domestic, 33% export
items.quote: In terms of volume, 70% is domestic, 30% is exports. In terms of value, , it could be 67-33.

items.statement: US volumes recovering positively after duty reduction, should gain traction in coming year
items.quote: Yes. So that is moving up, like we had mentioned also. So that's a positive development. And we are seeing that -- so I think it normally takes some time before supply chains can kind of N O C IL adjust to any change of this sort. But we are seeing it in the positive direction, and we should see it gain traction in this coming year

items.statement: Geopolitical developments in Middle East creating uncertainty in crude-linked raw materials, freight, shipping
items.quote: As we speak today, the geopolitical developments in the Middle East continue to create uncertainty across global energy, feedstock and logistics markets.

items.statement: Volume index reached 150 (base 100 = Q1 FY20), second time in history after 4 years
items.quote: Volumes for Q4 FY '26 stood at 150, considering a base of 100, which was Q1 FY '20. The 150, I think this is the second time in history we have achieved this is after 4 years, after 10 or 12 quarters.

items.statement: Performance-linked ESOP metrics behind target due to external environment, creating roadmap to get back on track
items.quote: Clearly, our metrics were along the lines of profitability and volume growth. So we are a bit behind as far as what we have set out to do. There are significant measures internally, which we had taken. So a combination of external environment has also played a role, but we are kind of really creating a road map to see how we can get back on track on that front.

items.statement: Management targets 15%+ ROE over medium to long term; no specific combined ratio guidance given
items.quote: But as I think the team has mentioned that the intent would be from a medium- to long-term perspective, maintain the 15% plus ROE guidance.

items.statement: Crop insurance business lost INR590 crores in FY26 due to re-tender; company will participate in next tender cycle to regain and grow crop business
items.quote: Chola MS suffered the loss of crop insurance business consequent to the re-tender, which impacted the quarter 4 GDPI by INR124 crores and over INR590 crores for the year.

items.statement: Conscious reduction in 2-wheeler book by over INR225 crores in FY26; share dropped from 19.6% to 10.6%; further moderation expected but not at same level
items.quote: And the quantum of 2-wheeler volume reduction was at least over INR225 crores last year. Look, while that part of the 2-wheeler portion may moderate to an extent further, but you are not going to see the similar level of drop.

items.statement: Combined ratio for FY26 at 115.2% (112.2% without 1/n effect); includes motor TP reserving augmentation impact
items.quote: Consequently, the combined ratio for the year was at 115.2% and 112.2% without the 1/n effect. The combined ratio of 112% includes the impact of the motor third-party reserving augmentation.

items.statement: Motor OD claims ratio rose ~10% for Chola MS vs 5-7% industry; 7-8% pricing improvement seen in last 2-3 months; expect OD loss ratio reduction over next 6 months
items.quote: Over a period of last 2 to 3 months, we have seen about 7% to 8% improvement in the price realization for us, which gives us the confidence that over the next 6 months, we should start seeing the reduction in the motor OD loss ratio.

items.statement: Motor TP reserving increased 10% above peers due to rising court award severity and no TP premium hike in 4 years; claims ratio higher by 2.71% YoY
items.quote: Recognizing the rising severity in court awards and third-party claims and the continued absence of increase in motor third-party premium, Chola stepped up its motor third-party reserving in the year. This has rendered the overall company claims ratio higher than the previous year by about 2.71%.

items.statement: FY26 ROE at 10.4% on average net worth; 3-year average ROE peaked at 14.4%; target 15%+ ROE medium to long term
items.quote: The return on equity for the year on average net worth was at 10.4% and the 3-year average ROE peaked at about 14.4%.

items.statement: Solvency ratio at 1.96x, down from 2.18x due to higher claims growth; expected to improve with claims ratio improvement and profit retention (no dividend)
items.quote: The solvency computation is a function of the premium growth as well as the claims growth. So this year, you would have seen that the claims growth is higher, some in terms of a claims ratio. Therefore, it has pulled in more capital. We're bringing the solvency level down from 2.18x to 1.96x as we discussed earlier.

items.statement: Board decided to seek forbearance for Ind AS transition from April 1, 2027; significant combined ratio drop expected in adoption year but will level out
items.quote: The Board of the company, after a careful evaluation, has decided that the company will seek forbearance for transitioning statutory accounting to Ind AS from April 1, 2027. This is to ensure a calibrated transition. It is fairly clear that there would be a significant drop in combined ratio in the year of adoption, but would level out over the years.

items.statement: Motor TP pricing unchanged for 4-5 years despite inflation; industry and company representations made to regulator and ministry for two-way correction
items.quote: And while the industry has been clamoring for a two-way correction in the motor third-party pricing. One, rationalization reduction where required and increase where required. We've not been getting it, though I think multiple representations at company level, at industry level has happened both to the regulator as well as the ministry.

items.statement: Motor mix: 49%+ cars, 40%+ CVs, 10.5% 2-wheelers; 24% motor premium from new vehicles (higher in cars, moderate in CVs, lowest in 2-wheelers)
items.quote: Within motor, the company for the year had a composition of 49% plus in cars, 40% plus in CVs and about 10.5% in 2-wheelers. The company for the year secured about 24% of its total motor premium from new vehicles, which proportion was hig her in cars, moderate in CVs and the lowest in 2 - wheelers

items.statement: Motor OD market share grew to 5.89%; TP market share lost ~0.5%; overall motor share stable at 5.25% despite 2-wheeler reduction
items.quote: Our market share in the OD has been growing up and TP has been moderated. In fact, we lost about 0.5% market share in TP and grew the motor OD market share to about 5.89%.

items.statement: Long-term non-motor premium received in advance grew to INR570 crores (from INR250 crores); company retains long-term business (no reinsurance cession)
items.quote: So I think as at March, we have something like about INR570 crores or so is what we are carrying, which has moved up from INR250 crores as at the previous March '25. So there, we continue to stay focused, notwithstanding the fact that we absorbe d the costs upfront. And we do not cede the long term on reinsurance

items.statement: Launching Chola Xceed operating app for sales personnel and channel partners to improve partner engagement, performance management, and renewal ratios
items.quote: We are also -- as a key strategic initiative, very soon, we should be launching Chola Xceed an operating app for our sales personnel and channel partners. This app will help us build a very structured partner engagement and also do good performance management of not just our staff, but also the productivity levels across agents, and simplifying the transaction.

items.statement: Rajive Kumaraswami (industry veteran) taking over as MD from V. Suryanarayanan effective June 1
items.quote: As was mentioned by Mr. Sridharan, I'm happy to welcome Rajive, an industry veteran, who will be taking over from me effective June 1 in steering the company forward.

items.statement: IFRS transition (April 2027) will bring discounting benefit on motor TP reserves to P&L; day-one impact goes to net worth; subsequent benefits to P&L
items.quote: So you will find that as a motor d ominant business, the provisioning that we have on the motor TP side is fairly large. And motor TP will have a discounting element as you move into IFRS. That will bring in a significant amount of benefit back into the P

items.statement: High retail retention (~78% weighted) means IFRS DAC accounting on reinsurance commissions will be net beneficial
items.quote: Even the overall, including the blended commercial and retail is at about 72. So it is at about 78 plus. And even when IFRS comes with DAC coming in on both the commission and the reinsurance commission side, my belief is that it will only benefit. The net position will only be a benefit.

items.statement: Investment corpus INR19,050 crores (ex-fair value); MTM equity gains INR137 crores, debt deficit INR112 crores at year-end; equity MTM recovered to ~INR302 crores recently
items.quote: The investment corpus as at end of the year was about INR19,050 crores without the fair value change. The company had a mark-to-market gains of INR137 crores in equity and a deficit of INR112 crores in the debt portfolio as at the end of the year.

items.statement: PBT INR454 crores after labor code gratuity provisioning and small equity MTM impairment provisioning
items.quote: The PBT for the year was INR454 crores after absorbing labor code-related gratuity provisioning and a small mark -to-market impairment prov isioning on equity investments

items.statement: Management declined to provide EBITDA per ton margin guidance for FY27 due to fluid raw material and subsidy situation
items.quote: Very difficult to predict at this point of time. Let us see how it goes because it is a function of what government is going to compensate and how much we are going to look at price corrections. It is very fluid. I do not want to put any number now.

items.statement: Management expects NACL EBITDA margin to stabilize at 9-10% next year with new product introductions
items.quote: Margin of NACL has improved to 6% to 7%, and that is what we indicated in the beginning, and going forward next year with the change in product portfolio, that should stabilize around 9% to 10%.

items.statement: Management expects Coromandel standalone crop protection revenue growth of 20-25% plus capacity-driven growth in active ingredients
items.quote: Overall, we can see a revenue growth of 20%-25% besides the capacity-driven growth in active ingredients which were mainly for the export market.

items.statement: Granulation capacity expansion project on track for commissioning by December FY27
items.quote: Our project to expand our granulation capacity is gaining momentum. We are on our way to commission this plant by December of this financial year.

items.statement: Senegal rock phosphate mine output to increase 30-40% in current year after reaching 3.5 lakh tons last year
items.quote: Our rock phosphate project at Senegal has stabilized very well and we have reached the output of more than 3.5 lakh tons last year, and we are planning to increase the volume further by 30%-40% in the current year.

items.statement: Additional 20,000 tons Mancozeb capacity at Sarigam underway, expected by mid-FY27 with payback under two years
items.quote: In fact, we are expanding another 20,000 tons at Sarigam. That project is underway, and should come through by middle of this year. Hopefully, there also I think margins are pretty good and we should have a payback in a shorter timeframe of less than two years.

items.statement: New 2,000 TPD Sulphuric acid and 650 TPD Phosphoric acid plants at Kakinada commissioned in March, currently in trial runs
items.quote: In March month, compan y successfully commissioned the 2,000 tons per day Sulphuric acid plant and 650 tons per day Phosphoric acid plant at Kakinada, strengthening its backward integration capabilities. This plant is capable of producing annually 200,000 tons of phosphoric acid

items.statement: Dahej Mancozeb capacity expanded by 10,000 tons with payback under one year
items.quote: We expanded our capacity by 10,000 tons of Mancozeb. I will get back to you on the revenue on Dahej. But the payback will be much faster, less than one year.

items.statement: Record fertilizer sales of 4.3 million tons DAP/NPK in FY26, up 7%, with 17.5% market share in phosphatics
items.quote: On the marketing front, we delivered record sales of 4.3 million tons of DAP and NPK, a growth of 7% over last year. Our consumption has reached the peak of 4.1 million tons, making us the largest player with the highest market share of 17.5% in the phosph atic sector in the country

items.statement: Nano DAP volumes expanded 60% to 42 lakh bottles in FY26 with ~50% market share
items.quote: Overall volumes expanded by 60%. Company marketed close to 42 lakh Nano Bottles by demonstrating product efficacy through extensive field trials, scientific studies and farmer outreach programs.

items.statement: Retail business grew over 30% in FY26 with 300+ new stores added in South India and entry into Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu
items.quote: Company's retail business reported strong performance, growing over 30% in 2025-26. Business expanded its footprint with the addition of over 300 new stores in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka, while also entering new markets such as Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu.

items.statement: Fertilizer manufacturing EBITDA per ton compressed to under INR 3,500 in Q4 FY26 from INR 5,000+ in FY25
items.quote: Last year, it was around INR 5,000 plus that we have mentioned and fourth quarter was compressed; it was less than INR 3,500 for fourth quarter.

items.statement: Standalone crop protection EBITDA margin reached ~19% in FY26 with revenue of INR 3,054 crores
items.quote: On a standalone basis , crop protection business has reached the record turnover and record profitability. As you ca n see, it is close to 19 % EBITDA margin and a revenue of INR 3,000 crores

items.statement: Phosphoric acid contract price fixed at USD 1,360 vs USD 1,290 previously; Ammonia deals at $840-850, Sulphur at ~$800
items.quote: Phosphoric Acid price was fixed at USD 1,360 as against the previous of USD 1,290. The spread of Ammonia has gone up significantly. There are deals which are happening around $840, $850 range. That is where last we heard. And Sulphur is also around the same level, $800 price.

items.statement: NBS rates for Kharif 2026 increased 10% for N, P, S but do not reflect sharp raw material price increases and rupee depreciation post Middle East crisis
items.quote: As you are aware, government has announced the NBS rates for Kharif 2026, increasing nutrient rates by 10% for N, P and S. These rates do not reflect the sharp increase in raw material prices and rupee depreciation post the Middle East crisis.

items.statement: Diversified raw material sourcing beyond Middle East to Southeast Asia, Africa, Canada, Russia, China; Q1 covered, Q2 visibility depends on Strait of Hormuz shipping
items.quote: We have been diversifying our raw material sources through long-term contracts with various countries beyond Saudi and Qatar, like Southeast Asian countries, African countries and Canada and sometime from Russia and China as well. So, fairly we are reasonably covered in terms of the raw material for the first quarter. We do hope that there can be an early resolution to the West Asian crisis and we

items.statement: Sulphur sourcing diversified to Canada, South Asia, Japan; spot transactions currently; visibility up to June; shipping through Strait of Hormuz is key bottleneck
items.quote: used to source predominantly from Middle East. Now we have diversified our sources, wherever Sulphur is available we are buying, and we have been getting some shipments from Canada as well. We are trying some domestic sources also. So, we are getting something from South Asian countries, Coromandel International Limited May 08, 2026 Japan. So, we are looking at all the opportunities. It is quite f

items.statement: Subsidy outstanding INR 2,168 crores at March-end FY26 vs INR 1,654 crores prior year; down sequentially from INR 3,785 crores at September-end
items.quote: Subsidy outstanding at the end of March stands at INR 2,168 crores compared with INR 1,654 crores in the previous year. We have received subsidy claims till the third week of March 2026. While the subsidy outstanding at the end of the year is higher as compared to t he previous year, it has come down sequentially quarter -on-quarter from INR 3,785 crores at the end of September to INR 2,199 crores

items.statement: Inventory elevated due to high raw material prices and strategic stocking for new Kakinada plants and West Asia crisis
items.quote: Inventory has remained at slightly elevated levels, driven primarily by elevated raw material prices and certain incremental inventory that we have kept for our newly inaugurated Phosphoric acid and Sulphuric acid plant in Kakinada. We are also holding some level of strategic inventory considering the ongoing crisis in West Asia.

items.statement: NACL rights issue of INR 250 crores reduced high-cost debt, borrowing cost came down significantly
items.quote: We have completed the acquisition of 53% stake in NACL and also followed on with the rights issue of INR 250 crores to reduce the high-cost debt. So, the borrowing cost has come down significantly from NACL and we have brought in the best practice of Coromandel.

items.statement: NPK share in phosphatics consumption at 60% despite higher prices vs DAP; unique grades at 35% of fertilizer sales
items.quote: Consumption for the year was close to 24 million tons, more or less the same as the previous year, and the mix is favoring NPK, despite relatively higher prices compared to DAP. The share of NPKs in the overall Phosphatics is currently at 60%.

items.statement: Expanded North/Central India fertilizer footprint with >24% growth via channel engagement and farmer connect
items.quote: We continue to expand our footprint across North and Central India markets by active channel engagement and farmer-connect initiatives and registered a growth of more than 24% in these markets.

items.statement: Crop protection domestic: added 1000+ new dealers, new territories, new formulations
items.quote: In domestic market, we expanded our presence by introducing new territories, onboarding over 1000 new dealers and also introduced new formulations.

items.statement: Industry signed off-take for 7 lakh tons green ammonia; Coromandel committed to 20% of its ammonia requirement
items.quote: During the year, industry players signed an off-take agreement of close to 7 lakh tons of green Ammonia. These efforts are expected to play a crucial role in reducing the carbon footprint of fertilizer production, while aligning with India's long-term climate commitments. Happy to share, Coromandel has also taken a lead in this government initiative and agreed for the coverage of upto 20% of its t

items.statement: Empowered committee of government and industry coordinating fertilizer production, planning and raw material sourcing amid Middle East crisis
items.quote: An empowered committee comprising of government and industry officials have been working in close coordination for fertilizer production, planning and raw material sourcing.

items.statement: Phos-acid production up 3% to 4.5 lakh tons in FY26
items.quote: Phos-acid production for the year was up by 3% to 4.5 lakh tons.

items.statement: Middle East crisis causing raw material price spikes and shipping disruptions; subsidy rates inadequate; Q2 raw material security uncertain
items.quote: Last year has been tough year for the sector, as the supply disruption from Middle East has resulted in elevated prices, especially in the fag end of the year. We have seen sudden spurt in key raw materials like Ammonia and Sulphur, and availability of finished fertilizers became a challenge.

items.statement: Dhaksha drone business impairment taken due to long lead time on order execution; recovery expected over next two years
items.quote: During the quarter, we took an impairment on the investments and goodwill in the standalone and consolidated financial results of the company relating to the drones business. This is primarily due to long lead time in execution of certain orders. Managemen t believes the value of the investments to improve and has provided for impairment on a prudent basis

items.statement: Expect 20% revenue growth and 25% EBITDA margins in FY27 on standalone basis
items.quote: We are confident of showing a growth of 20% in the coming year. And we are hopeful we'll also be able to maintain similar EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Target INR5,000 crore revenue and INR1,000 crore+ EBITDA over next 3-4 years
items.value: INR5,000 crore revenue, INR1,000 crore EBITDA
items.quote: we have established a clear road map and are on track to achieve the vision, the foundation of which was laid by our visionary Chairman, Mr. Mahesh Babani, of the INR5,000 crore of revenue and INR1,000 crore plus in the EBITDA numbers over the next 3 to 4 years

items.statement: Phase 1 capex expansion to complete by 30 June 2026, raising capacity to 54,000 MTPA
items.quote: On capex front, we are on track to complete the first phase of our capex expansion by 30 June, 2026. Total installed capacity will increase to 54,000 metric tons per annum after this phase of expansion.

items.statement: Phase 2 multi-speciality aroma chemicals project progressing as planned
items.quote: In parallel, Phase 2 of our multi -speciality aroma chemicals project is progressing as planned.

items.statement: PRIGIV JV implementing additional INR50 crore capex via 51:49 equity infusion
items.quote: additional capex of INR50 crore is being implemented based on the equity infusion by Privi and Givaudan in the ratio of 51% and 49%.

items.statement: Ethyl maltol, maltol, cyclopentanone projects targeting mechanical completion by June 2026
items.quote: we are targeting to do by the end of first quarter of next financial year. So by June of next financial year, we are targeting to complete these projects, mechanical completion as we call it

items.statement: Furfural backward integration expected post 2 years, around FY28-29
items.quote: it will be post, I would say, 2 years. So it's only after 2 years that we will get into that particular act.

items.statement: Biotech demonstration plant capex INR70-75 crore, basic engineering underway
items.value: INR70 crore to INR75 odd crore
items.quote: demonstration plant is being put up with a capex of around INR70 crore to INR75 odd crore

items.statement: Total capacity after 3 phases of capex to reach ~72,000 MTPA by mid-2028
items.quote: After all the first 3 phases of capex expansion, as also mentioned in our investor presentation, Privi will have on its own about 72,000 metric tons of capacities.

items.statement: Sustained 25%+ EBITDA margins across all quarters in FY26, expect 20%+ going forward
items.quote: We have delivered 25% plus margins consistently across all quarters and for the FY 26 on the EBITDA numbers. And we expect to sustain a 20% plus EBITDA margins going forward

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 25.41%, expect similar margins going forward
items.quote: EBITDA margins achieved was 25.41% for the quarter, and we expect the company to maintain such similar margins going forward.

items.statement: Gross margin expected to remain at similar levels, focus on internal efficiencies
items.quote: No. I think you should consider you always stay safe. So we will assume that the gross margin remains at similar level.

items.statement: Industry tailwinds intact, demand for fragrance and flavor ingredients growing
items.quote: The industry tailwinds remain firmly intact. Demand for fragrance and flavor ingredients continue to grow, driven by rising consumption for premium products and increasing focus on wellness and personal care.

items.statement: FY26 growth driven by 6.5% volume, ~8% price increase, balance from product mix
items.quote: it is about 6.5% on account of volume growth and the balance is on account of the product mix and about 8% odd increase in the prices, in fact.

items.statement: Increasing contribution from downstream and value-added products progressing well
items.quote: our efforts towards increasing contribution from downstream and value-added products are progressing well, and this is gradually reflected in the overall mix.

items.statement: Strong transparent relationships with MNC customers, confident on price pass-through
items.quote: we have a very healthy relationship and very transparent relationship with our customers. And they are also able to see that the changes which are happening. I mean these are changes which are once in a lifetime kind of impact that is there. So because of our transparency and trust, we are able to pass on and it is accepted from our customers.

items.statement: 75 products currently, 15 in pipeline, 10 under development, 100 products from one doorstep
items.quote: We have 75 products, 15 more in the pipeline, 10 more under development, 100 products from one doorstep is a great strength to have.

items.statement: Net debt INR876 crore, net debt/EBITDA 1.33x, net debt/equity 0.62x as of March 2026
items.quote: Our net debt as of March '26 stood at INR876 crore. This is, of course, net of cash and surplus money deployed in mutual funds with a net debt to an EBITDA ratio of 1.33 x, reflecting our focus on maintaining financial flexibility while supporting growth investments. Our net debt to equity ratio was a very healthy 0.62x

items.statement: Merger of Privi Fine Sciences and Privi Biotechnologies with parent approved by BSE/NSE, NCLT filing next, expect approval in FY27
items.quote: We are also pleased to share that the company has recently received an observation letter with no objection from both the stock exchanges, namely BSE and NSE, marking an important milestone in the merger process. We shall now go ahead filing with the NCLT, the scheme, and we expect the approval final coming from NCLT during the FY27.

items.statement: Board recommended INR10 per share dividend for FY26 (100% face value)
items.quote: the Board has recommended a dividend of INR10 per share for FY 26 with a dividend payout of 100% of the face value of the share

items.statement: ROE 22.05% and ROCE 22.42% in FY26, target >20% going forward
items.quote: we achieved a number of 22.05% and 22.42%, respectively, thereby reaffirming our visionary Chairman's vision that going forward the company's ROE and ROCE is poised t o be in excess of 20

items.statement: Renewable raw materials on annual contracts with 1.5-2 months inventory + 1 month in transit; non-pinene on 6-month contracts
items.quote: One is the renewable raw material for which we have annual contracts. And based on those annual contracts, typically, we hold about 1, 1.5 to 2 months of inventory. And then there is always inventory in transit because most of these are shipped from Europe or from U.S. So, you have another 1 month of inventory there.

items.statement: Gum turpentine (GTO) not sourced from China, derisked from Chinese supply dominance
items.quote: we were born out of China Plus One. It is now fashionable to say China Plus One, but the necessity of having an alternate supplier for aroma chemicals arose many decades back, and that's how Privi came into being

items.statement: 70% revenue from exports, dollar-denominated; FY26 forex gain ~INR14 crore in other income
items.quote: Definitely, because we are a net exporter per se. So, there is some amount of forex gain that has happened in FY 26. I think we have reported is close to about INR14 crore or so, which falls under other income.

items.statement: Biotech demonstration plant to validate economics; capex intensity key risk for bio-waste routes
items.quote: one of the reasons why these plants do turn out to be economically unviable is the capex cost. So while on an operating basis, most of the bio -waste is available at prices, but it is what you do with it in terms of, one, adding value to it, which is what we are doing. But on the other hand, the capex that is required is significant.

items.statement: Management will not provide specific FY27 revenue guidance; will update quarterly
items.quote: We are not guiding on any number at the moment. We are saying that we will continue to grow. This is just the beginning of the next financial year, we will keep updating you on the situation every quarter.

items.statement: Margin improvement expected after Q1FY27 as geopolitical situation eases and raw material prices normalize
items.quote: Once the geopolitical situation settles, then we will communicate. We will update you in Q1FY27.

items.statement: Order book stands at approximately INR 1,500 crores as of May 7, 2026, sufficient for next two quarters
items.quote: Our order book stands at approximately INR 1,500 crores as of May 7, 2026, providing strong revenue visibility for the coming periods.

items.statement: Order book of INR 1,500 crores expected to be executed in next two quarters
items.quote: Yes, it will be executed in the next two quarters.

items.statement: Strong demand visibility supported by KUSUM 2.0 rollout, Magel Tyala scheme, and state-level solar initiatives
items.quote: We remain constructive on demand prospects, supported by anticipated policy momentum under KUSUM 2.0, continued opportunities under the Magel Tyala scheme and sustained demand across other state-level solar initiatives.

items.statement: KUSUM 2.0 expected to roll out by end of Q1FY27 with orders starting Q2FY27 onwards
items.quote: As per the announcement by the Hon'ble PM, we feel that it should roll out by the end of Q1FY27 and we should start getting orders by Q2FY27 onwards.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin sustained at approximately 16% despite headwinds
items.quote: Despite these challenges, we sustained EBITDA margin at approximately 16% for FY26, reinforcing the robustness of our operating model and our ability to protect profitability while maintaining execution momentum.

items.statement: Raw material price inflation impacted margins by 6-7% in Q4FY26
items.quote: The raw material price has an impact of around 6% to 7% in this quarter.

items.statement: Magel Tyala scheme lower realizations impacted margins by 3-4%
items.quote: There has been a 3% to 4% impact because of Magel Tyala. Like we said in our previous call, the recent tenders we have received have had an impact of 3% to 4%.

items.statement: Operating leverage provided 2-3% margin benefit in FY26
items.quote: Sir, we have got 2% to 3% operating leverage advantage.

items.statement: Export margins approximately 10% higher than domestic margins
items.quote: Export margin is around 10% more as compared to domestic market.

items.statement: Solar rooftop business targeting 15% EBITDA margins
items.quote: And margin wise, we have already given guidelines that we are seeing 15% margins at the EBITDA level for this business.

items.statement: Expanded pump capacity and 0.5 GW module plant expected from Q2FY27; 2.2 GW solar cell capacity targeted by March 2028
items.quote: We are expecting that we will have the expanded capacity in pumps from Q2FY27 onwards. Apart from this, we will also get the capacity of 0.5 GW from Q2FY27 onwards and the 2.2 GW solar cell capacity, we are looking at March'28.

items.statement: 0.5 GW module plant commissioning by end of Q1FY27, contributing to margin improvement
items.quote: We feel that the facility will be commissioned by the end of Q1FY27 and will start contributing to margin improvement.

items.statement: FY26 solar pump installations increased 20% YoY to 86,086 units; Q4FY26 installations up 51% YoY to 28,345 units
items.quote: installation Shakti Pumps (India) Limited May 11, 2026 increasing 20% year-on-year to 86,086 units in FY26 and a robust 51% year-on-year growth in Q4FY26 to 28,345 installations

items.statement: Receivables reduced by over INR 420 crores in Q4FY26 from INR 1,697 crores to INR 1,276 crores, representing 77-day improvement in receivable days
items.quote: Receivables were reduced by over INR 420 crores during the fourth quarter, reduced from INR 1,697 crores as of December 31st, 2025, to INR 1,276 crores as of March 31st, 2026, representing a 77-day improvement in receivable days.

items.statement: Generated INR 124 crores cash flow from operations in FY26
items.quote: As a result, the company generated healthy cash flows from operations of INR 124 crores in FY26, significantly strengthening balance sheet quality and liquidity.

items.statement: Of INR 1,276 crores receivables, INR 916 crores not yet due per tender terms requiring RMS data
items.quote: out of INR 1,276 crores, INR 916 crores is not due. So, now after RMS starts reporting data, that money will get due Shakti Pumps (India) Limited May 11, 2026 and we will receive it because there is enough availability of the funds in all the states

items.statement: Historical receivable days range of 120-150 days; payment terms require 7 days RMS data for 90% payment and 90 days for remaining 10%
items.quote: This has always been our historical trend also. Our receivables have historically also been in the range of 120 to 150 days.

items.statement: Raw material prices for copper, stainless steel, and silicone sheets sharply increased due to geopolitical disruptions
items.quote: There has been a lot of variation in raw material prices including copper, stainless steel and silicone sheets. Also, there has also been an increase in the US dollar.

items.statement: Management expects inflated metal prices to normalize as geopolitical situation is temporary
items.quote: The current raw material prices which are so high, are only this high because of the geopolitical tension. So, we do not think that this will sustain for long. It will have reductions going ahead and after reduction our margins will improve.

items.statement: Competition increased affecting tender prices, but Shakti brand demand remains strong with Maharashtra portal for 25,000 pumps fully subscribed in 25 minutes
items.quote: What I would like to say is that yes, our competition has increased and because of that the price also gets affected a bit. But the important thing that I would like to highlight is that there is a strong demand for the Shakti brand in the market. Like in Maharashtra, the portal for Shakti opened for 25,000 pumps and it was fully subscribed in 25 minutes.

items.statement: Solar rooftop business gaining traction with inverters showing 10% better generation; channel partners established across country
items.quote: We have got very good feedback that our inverters are getting 10% extra generation. With this, we hope that as the word-of-mouth increases, and customers will be attracted more towards Shakti Energy Solutions.

items.statement: EV motor and controller business in vehicle-level trials with automobile companies; results expected in 6-12 months
items.quote: We have also tied up with some other automobile companies, who are testing the motors and we have reached the vehicle level trials. So going forward, you will see that Shakti EV will be a good company.

items.statement: Q4FY26 exports temporarily affected by Middle East geopolitical tensions; dealer/distributor network showing improving traction
items.quote: During Q4, exports were temporarily affected due to delays in order placement amid geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Encouragingly, we have witnessed improving traction through our dealer and distributor network, which we expect to remain a steady contributor going forward.

items.statement: Export platform ready with 100+ country presence; Europe and Vietnam agreements expected to boost exports
items.quote: Further, we have already proved ourselves by exporting to 100+ countries in the world. So, the platform is ready. Now slowly, as you can see, our distributors are growing. Exports is a tough business generally, but yes, our country has also made some agreements, like the recently signed agreement in Vietnam. There have been many more agreements in Europe.

items.statement: PM KUSUM execution timeline extended by government; order execution timelines of 90-120 days extended further
items.quote: In KUSUM's order, we have been given a little more time for execution by the government. So, both these timelines will not match. So I would suggest, you should use the order book and the numbers that we are giving, for your analysis.

items.statement: Maharashtra payment issues resolved; received ~INR 1,200 crores enabling execution ramp-up
items.quote: Yes sir, that problem has been solved. That is why we have increased our execution in Maharashtra. The problem was in December, which is why we reduced our execution at that time. But now, we have got around INR 1,200 crores and our balance sheet strength is retained.

items.statement: Company walked away from INR 200 crores Maharashtra orders in Q3 due to payment uncertainty; resumed after clarity
items.quote: And in the last quarter, to strengthen the Balance Sheet, we left orders of INR 200 crores in Maharashtra, since we were not getting any clarity on payments. And now that we have received clarity, we have increased execution there and did a quarterly revenue of Shakti Pumps (India) Limited May 11, 2026 INR 858 crores

items.statement: Global advances growth guidance 15-16% for FY27
items.quote: In alignment with prevailing global economic conditions, the guidance for global advances growth will be around 15-16%, and global deposit growth around 13-14% for FY27.

items.statement: ROA guidance 1% for March 2027
items.quote: As far as the guidance on the ROA is concerned for the whole year FY 27, we are giving a guidance that we'll be touching a number of 1 % for March 27.

items.statement: Global NIM guidance 2.70-2.75% for March 2027
items.quote: Yes, So we are saying that yes, we will have our NIM of somewhere around from present 2.52 % to somewhere around 2.70 to 2.75 % that we are guiding for March 27.

items.statement: Domestic NIM target close to 3%
items.quote: Domestic NIM we are definitely targeting to get as close to 3 % as possible.

items.statement: CASA absolute target Rs 3.30 lakh crore for FY27
items.quote: we have set targets for ourselves that we should be closing our CASA at somewhere around 3.30 lakh crores, which is a increase of around 10 % in FY 27.

items.statement: RAM book target 62% of advances by March 2029
items.quote: we are targeting a number of say around 62 %, the RAM book and 38 % the Corporate book. So that is for the strategy for the next three years for March 29.

items.statement: Advances target Rs 11 lakh crore by March 2029
items.quote: our advances will also be increasing and we are targeting advance of somewhere around 11 lacs crores as on March' 29.

items.statement: Fresh slippages target Rs 4,000 crore for FY27
items.quote: We have already reduced them to 5,500 crores if you see our presentation in the entire year and we want to further reduce it to 4,000 crores in this financial year.

items.statement: ECL transition impact 0.50% per annum aggregating 2.50% over five years
items.quote: As per our calculation that we have done, the impact will be only 0.50 % p.a aggregating to total 2.50 % over the next five years.

items.statement: ECL credit cost impact not more than 10 bps annualized
items.quote: So as far as the credit costs is concerned and the impact of the ECL guidelines on the credit costs, yes, there will be some impact on the credit cost side because of the ECL guidelines, but we feel that it should not be more than ten basis point on an annualized basis.

items.statement: Corporate pipeline Rs 50,000 crore, RAM pipeline Rs 15,000 crore
items.quote: we have a lot of good pipeline which is approximately 65,000 to 70,000 crores in total pipeline, out of that around 15000 crores is in the RAM book and remaining the pipeline is with the corporate book, which is around 50,000 crores.

items.statement: Global NIM 2.52% in FY26 vs 2.82% in FY25
items.quote: Global NIM stood at 2.52% in FY26 against 2.82% in FY25.

items.statement: Domestic NIM 2.78% in March 2026
items.quote: But our domestic NIM as on March'26, it is at a very healthy 2.78 %

items.statement: Q4 FY26 global NIM 2.58%
items.quote: As far as the NIM is concerned, again, as I said in my opening speech that our global NIM is at 2.58 %, which has come down by nearly 30 basis point from 2.82 % in March 25.

items.statement: Gross NPA ratio 1.98% in FY26, down 129 bps YoY
items.quote: Gross NPA ratio improved by 129 bps YOY to 1.98% for FY26.

items.statement: Net NPA ratio 0.56% in FY26, down 26 bps YoY
items.quote: Net NPA ratio improved by 26 bps YoY to 0.56% for FY26.

items.statement: Slippage ratio 0.83% in FY26 vs 1.36% in FY25
items.quote: Slippage ratio stood at 0.83% in FY26 against 1.36% in FY25.

items.statement: Credit cost 0.48% in FY26 vs 0.76% in FY25
items.quote: Credit Cost improved to 0.48% in FY26 against 0.76% in FY25.

items.statement: PCR 93.57% in March 2026 vs 92.39% in March 2025
items.quote: Provision Coverage Ratio (PCR) improved to 93.57% in Mar26 against 92.39% in Mar25.

items.statement: SMA book Rs 4,700 crore, 0.62% of assets, down from 0.92%
items.quote: Yeah, so it is now at 4,700 crore the overall SMA is there and it is only 0.62 % of our total asset book, which was earlier in March 25 at 0.92 %

items.statement: CRAR 18.01% in March 2026 vs 17.77% in March 2025
items.quote: As on 31.03.2026, Bank's CRAR has improved to 18.01% from 17.77% as on 31.03.2025.

items.statement: CASA ratio 37.64% in March 2026
items.quote: CASA increased YoY from Rs.2.80 lakh crore in Mar'25 to Rs.3.01 lakh crore with incremental growth of Rs. 20,449 crore in Mar'26 and CASA ratio stood at 37.64%.

items.statement: RAM advances 58.74% of total advances in March 2026
items.quote: RAM advances increased by 19.11% YoY from Rs.3.23 lakh crore to Rs.3.84 lakh crore in Mar'26 constituting 58.74% of Advances in Mar'26.

items.statement: 200 branches opened in FY26, 200+ planned for FY27
items.quote: we have already opened 200 new branches in FY 25, 200 branches were opened in this financial Year FY26 and another 200 plus branches will be opening in FY 27.

items.statement: ECLGS 5.0 funding expectation Rs 10,000-12,000 crore
items.quote: we expect to fund around 10-12 thousand crores under the ECLGS scheme.

items.statement: Written-off recovery run rate Rs 2,500-3,000 crore for FY27
items.quote: in the financial year FY 26 & FY 27 also we will be trying to achieve the similar run rate of around 2,500 to 3,000 crores of recovery from these written off accounts.

items.statement: Management declined to give a specific FY27 revenue growth number due to Middle East uncertainty but expects to grow ahead of industry rates.
items.quote: I would say there are uncertain events, which it makes it unfair for us to throw a number so we will not throw. What I will say is, we will continue to grow ahead of the industry growth rate, we will continue to beat that by a meaningful number.

items.statement: Long-term demand drivers across Banking, Transit, and Data Center remain intact and are accelerating despite near-term geopolitical shocks.
items.quote: Each of the segments that we bet on is only accelerating, I mean, leave small transitionary events, supply chain disruptions, Middle East war aside.

items.statement: Order book exceeds INR 1,800 crores entering FY27 with 68-72% executable in the next 12 months.
items.quote: We enter FY27 with an order book exceeding 1800 crores and a healthy pipeline across all segments.

items.statement: 68-72% of the INR 1,800 crore order book is executable in FY27, subject to supply chain and Middle East disruptions.
items.quote: I would say something in the range of 70%-odd, maybe slightly less, let's say between 68 % and 72 % or something like that.

items.statement: No significant margin dip planned despite higher upfront investments; Q4 EBITDA margin was 19% vs guided 20-21% range.
items.quote: We are not planning on any significant margin dip because the scale of the orders increases.

items.statement: Capex increased significantly in H2 FY26 for TIG (Transit & Data Center), Banking software stack rebuild, AI research (Tabular Foundation models), and cybersecurity (Mythos 5.5).
items.quote: We have been now picking material transactions on the TIG side, both in transit and data center. We are also investing heavily behind building the Banking software stack. We are investing heavily behind building the AI stack as well.

items.statement: R&D investment estimated at INR 150-200 crores over next four quarters, with productivity gains from AI dev stack expected to reduce spend.
items.quote: my best guess is we are talking of a number somewhere between 150 and 200 crores, the reason I say it's a guess and it's not a planned number is we are working thro ugh some very specific productivity improvement

items.statement: Stepping up expensed and capitalized investments urgently to capture generational AI and Data Center opportunities; window to act is narrow.
items.quote: we have significantly stepped up both expensed and capitalized investments to meet what we feel are generational opportunities opening up in AI and data centers because the window for us to act is very narrow.

items.statement: Rebuilding entire Banking stack with Aurion AI on agentic architecture; launched AI-native trade finance platform; series of AI-native apps to follow across stack within next couple of quarters.
items.quote: We are rebuilding the Banking stack with Aurion AI , starting with a fully AI-native trade finance platform on agentic architecture that we announced a few weeks back, agents handling workflows, foundation models reasoning over bank data , and decisions in real time.

items.statement: Middle East deal closures and project completions fell short in Q4 due to war; activity restarting but not full steam; diversifying into Europe, Southeast Asia, US.
items.quote: on Q4 and likely Q1 of this year as well was the war in MEA. The Middle East has become an increasingly important growth engine over the last couple of years, as you would have noted, particularly for Banking and we fell really short the re on both committed Q4 deal closures as well as planned project completions

items.statement: Transit business secured large strategic wins in India; pipeline extremely strong; becoming meaningfully more global.
items.quote: In transit, we secured large strategic wins across India and the pipeline is extremely strong. The business is becoming meaningfully more global and that will accelerate in the new year.

items.statement: Data Center secured one of India's largest AI-focused mandates from a leading hyperscaler (INR 350 crore deal); becoming partner of choice for hyperscalers.
items.quote: We secured one of India's largest AI-focused data center mandates from a leading hyperscaler alongside several other wins and are fast becoming a partner of choice for hyperscalers in the AI era.

items.statement: Higher upfront investment and larger projects in FY27 will bring transient working capital pressure; estimated INR 200-250 crore increase.
items.quote: As we get into FY27, I think for some time we will see higher upfront investment than a typical year for us, with larger projects bringing higher working capital needs as they scale.

items.statement: Working capital requirement estimated around INR 200-250 crores; focusing on tighter contracting and payment terms to minimize impact.
items.quote: I feel like the INR 200 crores – INR 250 crore sort of number is the right number. But we have some very specific plans around trying to make the business more efficient.

items.statement: No net debt increase expected; comfortable with overall cash position; transient balance sheet pressure is working capital related, not debt.
items.quote: I don't anticipate debt side. Debt to the extent that we need to maintain some things in some banks because of some businesses here and there, I t hink that's different. But on the net, I don't expect, we are more or less comfortable in terms of the overall cash position

items.statement: Owning full stack (software, systems, hardware) in Transit and Data Center improves contribution margins; margins to improve further as business matures.
items.quote: The reason we get into that owning every point on the value chain is because we do see that the economics of the business fundamentally changes when you own every point on the value chain versus be a point provider in large contracts.

items.statement: Revenue grew 20.2% to INR 1,411 crores in FY26; EBITDA margin 20.02%, PAT margin 15.02% (within guided 20-21% and 15-16% ranges but at lower end).
items.quote: In reality, the revenue actually grew 20.2% to INR 1 ,411 crores. EBITDA margin was 20.02% and PAT margin was 15.02%, we ll within the guided ranges of 20% to 21% and 15% to 16% but towards the lower end of our planned ranges.

items.statement: Geopolitical instability in Middle East could delay deal closures and project execution; management building resilience via geographic diversification and conservative investment planning.
items.quote: We will remain watchful on the macro, we will remain watchful on geopolitical environment which could continue to delay, you know, some deal closures in MEA especial ly, as we saw in Q4

items.statement: Front-ending investments without assured revenue conversion caused P&L pressure in Q4; lesson learned to be more conservative in upfront cost planning.
items.quote: walking into Q4, we were very confident of where the revenue is going to be. And obviously, you fell more than INR 100 crores short of it. So, that investment in your expenses beforehand and then missing the revenue, that is what causes the problem.

items.statement: AI-native transformation led personally by CEO; best talent organized around AI-native way of working; high-quality AI research teams in India and Europe.
items.quote: we are stepping up investments now with urgency, at scale, with our best talent organized around an AI-native way of working that I am leading personally.

items.statement: Acquired InfraRisk, OmniFin, Fintra, Arya to expand Banking product surface area for cross-sell/upsell; may still meaningfully acquire.
items.quote: We acquired InfraRisk, we acquired OmniFin, we acquired Fintra, we acquired Arya, so we have gone in and added net new products into the mix.

items.statement: NBFC platform now has north of 30 clients in India; winning competitive deals; may announce bunch of wins together per disclosure policy.
items.quote: I think, look, NBFC space in India, I think we now have north of 30 clients, some fairly large size NBFCs. We are very competitive in the space.

items.statement: Data Center revenue recognition: fairly large chunk of hyperscaler deals to be recognized within FY27 despite Q4 delays.
items.quote: So, we faced some delays in terms of project execution, like I said, but I would say a fairly large chunk of it within the year.

items.statement: Pharma revenue target INR50-55 crore for FY27, up from INR34.4 crore in FY26
items.quote: INR55 crores is our target for the next financial year '26-'27. We hit almost INR34.4 crores for the current financial year. So we have taken a 50% growth to reach somewhere around close to between INR50 crores and INR55 crores for the Pharma.

items.statement: Overall revenue value growth target 13-15% for FY27, volume growth 10-13%
items.quote: In terms of just volume, it might look like 10% to 15%, anywhere between 10% to 15% of growth is possible. But in terms of value, I'm sure we'll be clocking between 13% to 15% value growth, like what we did this year, 13.3%.

items.statement: EBITDA target INR210 crore for FY27, up from INR173 crore in FY26
items.quote: We are aiming at, at least INR210 crores EBITDA for next financial year, up from INR173, that's 20% price.

items.statement: EBITDA per kg target 42.5-43 for FY27, 43-44 for FY28
items.quote: FY '27, as I expected, we are aiming at, at least 42 to 43, 42.5 could be a good estimate for the full year. And then how it frames in Pharma in '28, probably we can aim at around 43 to 44 range.

items.statement: Capex budget INR80-85 crore for FY27, down from INR120 crore in FY26, focused on brownfield expansions
items.quote: We have a sharp lesser budget of capital investment in this current financial year, which was INR140 crores 2 years ago for 2 consecutive years and [120 years 0:11:33] in this financial year '25-'26. And we hope to control this capex to INR80 crores, INR85 crores in the next year, that is '26-'27 as we will be going only for brownfield expansions now onwards.

items.statement: Total capacity 63,000 MTPA currently, targeting 67,000-70,000 MTPA by end FY27
items.quote: Yes, I think we should be close to 68, 67 because capacity -wise in Pharma, the number of tons won't be too many, at maybe 1,000, 1,200 tons. And brownfield expansions are only envisaged at Mysore and Satara. Satara basically, that is Mahad plant supply. So these are the 2 areas. And the rest of the plants, we see -- and of course, North plant, Panipat, where we are adding thin wall capacities, 4

items.statement: Pharma capacity 1,500 tons currently, targeting 2,500 tons in FY27
items.quote: Currently, Pharma is hardly about 1,500 tons, and we have to still make new investments in that segment to take it up to 2,500 tons in this year.

items.statement: Grasim capacity 12,000 tons across Panipat, Cheyyar, Mahad running at 65% utilization
items.quote: Grasim already, we have capacities created more than 12,000 tons, 5,000 at Panipat, 4,400 at Cheyyar and about 2,500 at Mahad, that is through Satara. So total 12,000 tons of capacity has been created, which is running around 65% capacity as of now, utilization as of now, which was better than last year, which was in 50s.

items.statement: Panipat thin wall capacity 1,000 tons currently, expanding to 2,000-2,500 tons with 4 new machines in July
items.quote: Currently, I think it is about 1,200 tons or 900 to -- sorry, 1,000 tons. It will become 2,000 tons Food and FMCG there. And Qpack also we're adding a little bit. So about 2,000 -- it will become 2,000 to 2,500 tons per annum, including Qpack.

items.statement: Pharma grew 37% YoY in Q4, 200%+ for full FY26, targeting 50% growth in FY27
items.quote: And especially the consolidation of 5 units in Hyderabad into 2 units, that is Unit 1 and 10, has improved the overall performance and efficiencies and resulted in better EBITDA margins. And going forward -- and again, one more notable thing in this quarter is the Pharma packaging. It's grown by 37% over the Q4 of last year and overall growth of the full year is more than 200%, giving us the abili

items.statement: Paint segment grew 13.5% in value, 14.4% in Q4; Asian Paints grew 17% YoY in Q4, Grasim (ABG) grew 60%+ YoY
items.quote: 26% volume growth, I didn't say, it is 14.4% in value terms and 13.5% is the growth in Paint segment. That 60%, what I said is ABG numbers for the quarter, this particular quarter, ABG compared to the previous year Q4, the ABG numbers have shot up by 60%.

items.statement: Food & FMCG grew 15.4% in thin wall, 18% including bulk packs; targeting 20%+ growth in FY27
items.quote: If you combine the thick wall also, food is around 18%. But this 15.4%, I'm sure it will be looking at least 20% growth in the food and FMCG, including the North numbers for the next financial year.

items.statement: Lubes segment declined due to loss of BPCL client (INR14-15 crore revenue), expecting stabilization at current levels
items.quote: Yes. We lost a client BPCL towards the end of last financial year, who used to -- I mean, which used to contribute about a significant amount of sale. But due to tendering system and public sector, they go only by L1 basis. We couldn't match their pricing and we let it go. So one of the reasons why last 4 quarters, we still have loss in sale. Last year itself it was more than INR14 crores, INR15 c

items.statement: Gross margins maintained at 46-47% despite raw material price volatility; full pass-through achieved
items.quote: Certainly, we have passed on the entire price rise to the clients across the segments. And they also appreciated that the reality -- ground realities and even some of them have reduced the period of raw material fluctuation. That means earlier, they used to be quarterly. Now they have come down to a monthly or even sometimes 15, fortnightly correction.

items.statement: EBITDA per kg improved from 37.6 to 40.7 in FY26; consolidation of 5 Hyderabad units into 2 driving efficiency gains
items.quote: That itself should add a rupee or so to the already 40.7 what we have achieved this year compared to 37.6 in the previous year. So there's a jump of 8% -- 8.4% increase in the EBITDA margin, which is a substantial jump, which we lost during the last couple of years, we recovered.

items.statement: Raw material polypropylene price surged from INR105 to INR160, now at INR145-150; clients accepted monthly/fortnightly price adjustments
items.quote: From INR105 in the beginning, it went up to INR160, and now currently hovering around INR145, INR150. So we are, in this kind of a scenario, found our clients very much with us, and I think we can still continue to maintain our profit margins.

items.statement: Berger and Nerolac increasing orders due to supply chain concerns; clients returning in herds
items.quote: On the contrary to your expectation, in fact, we are finding our clients coming back in herds because they are worried about the connectivity, material procurement abilities, and ability to quickly react to the international scenario. So we noticed the jump in call -ups from even old clients like Berger and Nerolac who used to give us only a few grades have now increased their call -ups in the fea

items.statement: Asian Paints IML adoption driving volume recovery; metallic IML technically complex providing competitive edge
items.quote: You said the reason, the IML adoption by Asian Paints in more and more brands is one of the reasons of us getting back their higher volume of business. And that will, I hope, will continue because their artworks are very critical. If you notice their paints in the market, they have metallic IML, which is a top-class IML to handle both technically and visually. So visually it gives an excellent out

items.statement: Recycled plastic (RCP) mandate 30% currently, increasing to 40% from April 2027; applies to Paint and Lube segments only
items.quote: Some of the reasons could be we have taken up a severe preventive maintenance and change of screws and some other parts in the machines to suit to the RCP addition because now recycled plastic has become a mandatory. 30% is mandatory now, and it's g oing to be 40% from next April. So the machines which are equipped with ordinary screws are not able to process such mix, and we have gone for better

items.statement: Working capital stretched due to Pharma 90-110 day payment terms and 3-month inventory requirements; high RM prices also inflated inventory values
items.quote: See, working capital stretch is basically you are looking at a higher valuation also because the last 3 weeks, we have been purchasing material at high price, and that has indirectly might have impacted the value to look higher. And inventory days also be come a little longer because in Pharma, one has to keep 3 months material ready because sudden requirements generally come up in batch quantitie

items.statement: Vibe collaboration: 2 of 3 products in pilot stage, commercial revenue expected end of FY27
items.quote: Yes. I already mentioned during my previous con call that this is a long-term opportunity where we are working with Vibe and development of new set of products, especially closures for high- end chemicals and lubricants. And now the 2 -- out of 3 products they have given us the designs, 2 products pilot molds are ready. But these molds to become commercial and add revenues, it will certainly take

items.statement: IML share 75.5% in Q4, 75.13% for FY26 (76.8% in value terms)
items.quote: Yes, it was for the 4Q, it was around 7 5.5%. And overall year, it is 75.13%. So in value terms, it is 76.8%. So almost 77%, you can say percent is in IML.

items.statement: Pharma sales grew from INR10.7 crore to INR34.3 crore (219% YoY) in FY26
items.quote: Sandeep you should be very happy to note that in the year 1 itself, or I would say, year 1 of full operations, we've grown by 210% compared to the last year, from INR11 crores, INR11.5 crores to almost INR34 crores, INR10.7 crores to INR34.3 crores. So that is a 219% increase in Pharma sales.

items.statement: Solar 17.6 MW expected to generate INR 14.5 cr revenue and INR 12.8 cr EBITDA on full-year basis; wind 9.9 MW expected INR 14 cr revenue and INR 10 cr EBITDA in normal wind year
items.value: 14.5 cr revenue, 12.8 cr EBITDA (solar); 14 cr revenue, 10 cr EBITDA (wind)
items.quote: the solar project, the 17.6 megawatts will give us a total revenue on a full year basis of about INR 14.5 crores and an EBITDA of about INR 12.8 crores. That is, assuming it is operating for 12 months in the year. Since it is only going t o be partially part of the year, we will have a proportionately lower generation. In terms of the 9. 9 megawatts of the wind, in a good, in a normal wind year, w

items.statement: Commissioned 9.9 MW wind in FY26 (6.6 MW March 2026, 3.3 MW April 2026); constructing 17.6 MW solar for Q1 commissioning, full production by Q2
items.quote: We have successfully added 9.9 megawatts of wind capacity in this fiscal. 6.6 was added in end of March '26 and 3.3 in April '26. We are also in the process of constructing 17.6 megawatts of solar capacity, which will be commissioned in Q1 and probably will enter full production during the course of Q2.

items.statement: Started repowering 7.8 MW older wind turbines under new Tamil Nadu policy; evaluating more repowering opportunities
items.quote: In order to improve operating efficiencies, we have started the process of repowering 7.8 megawatts of our older wind turbines under the New Re powering Policy of Government of Tamil Nadu. This was pending for quite some years bec ause the policy was not conducive to repowering. But with the new policy in force, we are proactively looking at all our other older wind assets to see which will benefi

items.statement: Interest cost reduced 21% due to debt decline and 45 bps rate reduction on largest loan
items.quote: Other than the better wind and the refund of excess interes t, we also had a significant reduction in interest costs by about 21% due to both decline in overall debt and 45 basis points reduction in the interest rate in our largest loan

items.statement: Q4 wind availability lower than normal; variation inherent in renewable business; all wind companies faced same issue
items.quote: Basically, there was lower wind in Q4. See, Q4 is typically a very low wind quarter because the main wind for us is in Q1 to Q3, there is not much w ind happening in Q4. But this year, the wind was even lower than normal. So, there is nothi ng we could do about it. It is a matter of God. But this variation will be there. In the renew able energy business, this kind of variation quarter-on-quarter,

items.statement: Tariffs fixed throughout year; significant capacity under C&I and long-term PPAs; no material evacuation issues
items.quote: No. The tariffs were fixed throughout the year because a significant percentage of our capacity is C&I. The rest of it is at long-term PPAs. items.statement: Long-term ambition to double bed capacity from 5,460 (FY28) to 10,000+ by FY33
items.quote: between FY '28 to FY'33, we are hoping that we'll probably be able to double this strength of 5,460 to nearly 10,000 plus.

items.statement: Greenfield capex ~INR35 lakh/bed (Panchkula INR125 crore for 350 beds); Brownfield break-even 4-6 months, Greenfield 12-15 months; acquired asset revenue payback ~11 months
items.quote: The total capex that we have done is INR125 crores to have 350 beds. Which is more or less aligned with our thought process to have a capex within INR35 lakhs per bed.

items.statement: Operating cash flow FY26 INR329 crore (pre-tax INR428 crore); capex/acquisition spend INR430 crore in FY26
items.value: INR329 crore OCF, INR430 crore capex
items.quote: Operating cash flow for FY ’26 was INR329 crores. And if I talk about pre -tax, it was INR428 crores as compared to INR215 crores last year, and the pre -tax was INR299 crores in FY ’25. Amount spent on capex and the acquisition during the year was INR430 crores

items.statement: Vendor management: pays vendor dues by 10th-15th of next month, securing discounts; in-house construction unit speeds Brownfield/Greenfield execution
items.quote: We have a construction unit which is largely dedicated to us. So any renovations or any constructions in the Brownfield or the Greenfield respectively is done at a very fast pace.

items.statement: Ambala 200-bed oncology extension planned; radiation oncology currently in 3 hospitals, to expand as needed; medical/surgical oncology in all 16 hospitals
items.quote: Ambala we have 200 beds which will be coming up for an extension where it will be dedicated to the oncology unit largely.

items.statement: Chemotherapy is day-care; ALOS not applicable; radiation similar; surgical oncology 1-2 procedures based on cancer spread
items.quote: chemotherapy is basically a day -care procedure. And patient come out there and take chemotherapy. So is with the radiation also. It is only the treatment planning and if there is a surgical aspect of the oncology, which takes

items.statement: Disallowance rate maintained at 9% in Q4 FY26; rigorous process to minimize
items.quote: we are remain at 9% disallowance, even in Q4.

items.statement: Rohtak 250-bed Greenfield targeting January 2028; Mohali 150-bed expansion; Tri-City (Panchkula+Mohali) 850 beds to become largest private provider
items.quote: Rohtak will be coming in January 2028, 250 beds. Panchkula we have already commissioned on 10th of April 2026. So that will be definitely delivering and it is already one of the, you could say, top-notch hospitals in that area.

items.statement: Bathinda (from July 2025) at 65-70% occupancy, adding to top and bottom line; Agra (from Feb 2026) adding ~INR5 crore/month revenue, ~INR90 crore FY27, EBITDA positive
items.quote: Bathinda, as I said, because we added in July 2025, that is already adding into our numbers. So we are doing extremely well in Bathinda. So rather we have started operating on an occupancy of 65% to 70%.

items.statement: No export/FX exposure mentioned; business domestic North India focused
items.quote: We r emain a highly capital - efficient, financially strong, doctor -led organization with an unwavering focus on high -quality clinical outcomes and patient care

items.statement: Expects FY27 to be better than FY26 on revenue, margins, cash flow and balance sheet with large debt repayment
items.quote: So all in all, despite some of these headwinds, we think company should do better in FY '27 compared to '26 on all parameters. By and large, the revenue, the margins, the cash flow, all 3 parameters and balance sheet should definitely become far better than what it is today with a large chunk of repayment.

items.statement: Targets retail business growth above 15% in FY27
items.quote: Our target is that the retail business should grow more than 15%, right? And that was in the current quarter also in the whole year, but we ended up at 13% because of lack of sales in March because of the shock.

items.statement: Plans to be PAT positive in FY27
items.quote: For FY '27, right, our plan right now is to be PAT positive.

items.statement: Invested INR140 crores in beverage bottling lines over last two quarters; discussing 3 more lines for FY27
items.quote: So the bottling beverage business, we have invested approximately INR140 crores over the last couple of quarters, December and March quarter. And the first project is already online. It's working.

items.statement: Tomato processing plant with Japanese partner expected to start in January next tomato season
items.quote: The other business which we are working on a collaboration with the Japanese company, it's about tomato processing. That plant would start sometimes, I think, January. That is the next mango season -- sorry, tomato season when that comes through.

items.statement: Two beverage lines (juice and CSD) started in Q4 FY26; 3 more lines planned for FY27
items.quote: And so I'm happy to report that in the quarter, the 2 beverage lines started, one for juice and one for CSD. And there is a discussion ongoing to also put additional 3 more lines during FY '27.

items.statement: PVC pipe demand recovering after price shock; expects stronger water management demand due to below-normal monsoon
items.quote: Since these prices have come down, we have seen demand for PVC pipe already come back. And things -- while March and April, we lost some business due to uncertainty in the market, customers decided to postpone their demand or their orders, especially the farmers.

items.statement: Solar agri pump business grew nicely in FY26; expects further growth in FY27 with government initiatives
items.quote: Another factor, the business which grew last year was also as a part of the Hi-Tech division has been the solar agri pump. That business grew nicely. we expect with also additional government initiative, solar agri business should grow also in '27.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 13.2% in Q4 FY26 from 12.8% YoY; Hi-Tech margin 19.8% vs 17.5%
items.quote: We have been able to improve the margin. Overall margin came at 13.2% as against 12.8% across all the divisions. Within individual businesses, Hi-Tech came out at 19.8% as against last year same period, 17.5%.

items.statement: Polymer prices spiked 50-60% in March (PVC up 50%, LLDPE up 60%); PVC now down to ~10% above Feb levels, LLDPE still ~40% up
items.quote: And we saw that between 20th February to sometimes in 25th of March, prices had gone up substantially, resulting into almost -- at one point, there were more than 50% increase in the raw material prices within a space of about 20 days. And on polyethylene side, it was, in fact, 60% increase.

items.statement: Government project receivables reduced by INR80 crores in Q4 FY26 and INR30 crores in April; expects substantial collection in FY27
items.quote: and project receivables. So there was some movement in this particular quarter where some INR80 crores were reduced in January to March from the government project receivables. And again, in April, we also received INR30 crores

items.statement: Working capital cycle reduced by ~15 days across businesses in FY26 despite volatility
items.quote: And we also focused on working capital cycle and that working capital cycle has been reduced by almost about -- by 15 days in total across different businesses despite all the volatility and the changes which have been there in marketplace.

items.statement: Repaid INR1,300 crores to banks over last 4 years; FY27 debt obligations due in September and March; expects to repay via internal accruals (target INR750-800 crores ops cash flow) and INR150 crores government benefits
items.quote: And I would like to state that, look, between '23 and '26 since we signed restructuring, or since '22 in last 4 years, we also repaid INR1,300 crores total to the banks, and that is possible. And it became possible.

items.statement: Asset sale in Tamil Nadu (MoU signed) expected to close in next couple of weeks per ICRA report
items.quote: Yes. So I think the sale of the assets, as I said, it is happening in Tamil Nadu. We already signed the necessary MoU or whatever else. So it should happen over next couple of weeks.

items.statement: Exploring backup options including refinancing and equity raise if government receivables delayed; more clarity expected by July
items.quote: In terms of backup option, I think we are exploring everything, including refinancing if required. And this scenario of what has happened in March and April necessitates some of the additional backup one must do because things are uncertain. And we are exploring those. And I think sometimes in July, when we speak, we should have more clarity on it.

items.statement: Food business: Onion processing since January going well; mango season starting; zero duty on onions under India-USDA notified rules to boost European exports
items.quote: As we also speak right now, we are currently processing onion since January, and that season has gone reasonably okay for us. So that augurs well for the next year in terms of improving sales of onion, etc., dried onion. And the mango season is just starting as we speak. And this year onwards, '27, '28 onwards, we also expect that once all the rules are notified under India USDA, earlier, we used

items.quote: No, we don't want to confirm or deny. In a sense that Kagome is a global international player, and we are working with them. They have been our customers for Tomato Puree earlier, and we are working with them to increase what you call partnership more. Also, we are definitely working with Reliance Consumer. They are also our customers, and we are doing more things with them.

items.quote: So Maharashtra, just to give you a flavor of the numbers, right, Maharashtra, we sold INR700 crores. South 4 states put together, we sold INR400-odd crores. And North East part, we sold about INR100 crores. So we
