items.quote: Overall, as things stabilize, I think revenues will come back and kick in again. And in terms of the food business, as I said, there are 2, 3 things which are happening, which are positive for the food for the next year. One of the other things which happened during this period that the lower demand was not just linked to the higher raw material prices, which was one of the important factors. But

items.statement: UK and US food businesses had cost challenges in FY26; expects these to not remain in FY27
items.quote: While we had some challenges in our European and U.S. business, those are being addressed. And I think we expect current fiscal year, that is FY '27, they will not remain. So next year looks then quite good for the food business in totality.

items.statement: Employing AI within business and data to improve efficiency, training, dealer outreach, and crop solutions for farmers
items.quote: And where necessary, we are employing within our business and within our data, artificial intelligence to improve the efficiency of business, improve training of people, how do we reach out to the dealers, how do we give more crop solutions to the farmer.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue ~INR1,800 crores (+4.3% YoY); Hi-Tech +8%, Agro Processing +6%, Plastic slight degrowth; full-year revenue +11% (Hi-Tech +20%, Food +9%, Plastic +2.4%)
items.quote: So as we circulated, we had a Board meeting earlier today, and we have circulated the results, you might have seen that overall, when you look at it, we were able to manage approximately a revenue of about INR1,800 crores this quarter as the entire company as against same period last year at about INR1,750. So registering about a nominal growth of about 4.3%.

items.statement: FY26 operating cash flow post working capital ~INR600 crores (76% of EBITDA); targets 4-figure cash flow in FY27 via government receivable recovery
items.quote: If you look at for the whole FY '26, whatever EBITDA we generated, almost about 76% was operating cash flow post working capital change was created in that to -- in north of about INR600 crores, and the idea in the current fiscal FY '27 is to take this amount to 4 figures by recovering the old government receivables and project receivables.

items.statement: Reported PAT negative INR40 crores in FY26 due to one-time tax regime change (25% vs 34%), labour code adjustment, and NCD unwinding; adjusted PAT INR133 crores per investor presentation
items.quote: But when you look at the PAT, for example, for the entire -- the PAT is at minus INR40 crores. But within that INR40 crores, these were onetime issues plus the unwinding of these NCDs, which is a noncash item and not linked to the current year performance. If you adjust that adjusted PAT and which we have given in the investor presentation also on Slide 9 is about INR133 crores, which was INR97 cr

items.statement: Beverage lines generated INR27-28 crores revenue in Q4 FY26 during trial phase; expects meaningful revenue in FY27
items.quote: So I think the 2 lines which we set up have already started working part of February and March. But of course, there is the initial period trials and all of that, those have happened. And we already had, I think, about INR27 crores, INR28 crores revenue clocked before end of March.

items.statement: Food business IPO not imminent; merchant bankers advise market difficulties for smaller issues; may reconsider in H2 FY27
items.quote: Generally, we are some distance away because of also merchant bankers tell us that the market right now has difficulties and smaller issues, especially larger difficulties. If you have a very big issue, then it's a different story. So that is something I think we need to continue to look at market. And based on the advice from merchant bankers, investment bankers, who will look at it. But I don't

items.statement: Sterling expects to cross 95 resorts and 4,500 rooms in 2027 with more than 20 sign-ups in pipeline
items.quote: We expect to cross 95 resorts and 4,500 rooms in 2027, with more than 20 sign-ups in our pipeline actively coming on board.

items.statement: Demerger of Sterling Holiday Resorts expected to complete by Q1 FY28
items.quote: We expect this process to get completed by Q1 of FY '28, which was the original timeline that we had intimated.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR 0.50 per INR 1 face value share for FY26
items.quote: I'm also happy to mention this point here that our Board of Directors have recommended a dividend of INR 0.50 to INR 1 face value share, subject to approval of the shareholders.

items.statement: Sterling investing in asset protection for monsoon readiness by mid-June
items.quote: So we are undertaking spends to ensure that in the event of a terrible monsoon, our assets are protected first. That's number one because in case there is any issues pertaining to that, it would cost us a loss more, which will impact us in Q3 to get this repaired. So that is step number one that we are taking care of and we should be able to take care of that by mid of June.

items.statement: Group plans capital expenditure primarily in technology and software
items.quote: We have some plans of that for capital expenditure, which is into software basically - technology. Because as you know, travel and not only travel, even other parts of our business, notably financial services and DEI depends a lot on technology. And therefore, there will be increasing investment in technology.

items.statement: Sterling added nearly 1.5 resorts per month in FY26, 33 resorts over 24 months at 29% CAGR
items.quote: We added nearly 1.5 resorts or launched 1.5 re sorts per month last year and almost 33 resorts over the last 24 months, a 29% CAGR growth in resorts over the last 2 years

items.statement: Sterling now operates 78 resorts with 3,800 rooms across 65 destinations
items.quote: We now have 78 resorts, hotels and retreats, approximately 3,800 rooms across 65 destinations in India.

items.statement: Short-haul outbound travel growing double-digit in Q1 FY27; long-haul westbound subdued due to geopolitical tensions
items.quote: Yes, we are witnessing double-digit growth as far as the short-haul business is concerned. And that's obvious reasons because people are looking at destinations which are closer by because time taken to make that decision and the availabili ty of visa and such things are far more easier for the short-haul destinations

items.statement: Corporate travel volumes continue at 7-8% growth trend, no reduction seen
items.quote: So currently, on the Corporate Travel side, we aren't seeing any reduction in volumes. They continue to trend at similar trend lines that we have seen in the previous year, which is a 7%, 8% growth that we have seen.

items.statement: MICE pipeline strong but corporates taking wait-and-watch approach, demand expected to shift to H2 FY27
items.quote: There is a bit of wait-and-watch approach that corporates are taking at this point in time and hence, we believe that some of this demand will come back and translate in the latter half of the year.

items.statement: Sterling EBITDA margin 31% and PBT margin 21% for FY26, debt-free with cash reserves near INR 3,400 million
items.quote: For the full year FY '26, Sterling delivered a total revenue of INR 5,487 million. EBITDA stood at INR 1,701 million, and the margins are healthy at 31%. Our profit before tax is at INR 1,142 million with PBT margins of 21%.

items.statement: Travel segment EBIT margin 3.3% for FY26, down 11% YoY due to geopolitical impact on overseas subsidiaries
items.quote: We reported a total travel revenue of INR 67,025 million for the year, which is an increase of 4% and our EBIT was down 11% to INR 2,218 million, with an EBIT margin of 3.3%, and this largely reflects the geopolitical impact in our overseas subsidiaries.

items.statement: Financial Services EBIT margin 48% in Q4 FY26 and 46% for full year, retail forex margins stable at 2-2.2%
items.quote: For the quarter in question, the forex revenue increased by 3% to INR 813 million and EBIT improved by 17% to INR 392 million with an EBIT margin of 48%. For the full year, our reported revenue and EBIT remained flat at INR 3,261 million and INR 1,493 million with an EBIT margin of 46%.

items.statement: Sterling forward bookings strong for Q1 FY27 with occupancy and ARR increasing in April-May
items.quote: Q4 revenues, if you have noticed, you would have seen an increase in occupancy, you would have seen an increase in the ARRs. These 2 factors on a constant 3,810 rooms will definitely help us get the revenues up in the current financial year. And we are already seeing that happening in the month of April, and to some extent in May also.

items.statement: DEI expects 50-60% recovery in Middle East business by end of year
items.quote: I think what we forecast going forward would b e approximately a 50% to 60% recovery towards the end of the

items.quote: We are seeing airfares surge by 30% to 50% on most westbound routes.

items.statement: Prepaid forex card expanded to 28 global currencies from 12 in December 2025
items.quote: A noteworthy development on our prepaid forex card is that it has expanded today to 28 global currencies, from 12 that we were operating in December of 2025, creating India's one of the largest widest currency portfolios on the prepaid forex card segment.

items.statement: Sterling room revenue grew nearly 40% in Q4 FY26, occupancy 64%, ARR up 12% to INR 6,347, RevPAR up 16%
items.quote: Room revenue for the quarter grew nearly 40% at INR 672 million. Occupancy improved to 64%. ARR increased by 12% to INR 6,347 and the RevPAR increased 16% despite a 20% increase in overall room inventory.

items.statement: Corporate travel acquired 8 new accounts in Q4 FY26 across financial services, automobile, telecom, energy; 4 large accounts in pipeline
items.quote: We acquired 8 new accounts in Q4 FY 2026 across financial services, automobile, telecom and energy sector, and 4 new large corporate accounts are in the pipeline.

items.statement: DEI signed 15 new potential partners in Indonesia, Singapore, China, Macau, Hong Kong for next 6 months
items.quote: In fact, just as we speak, we've signed up about 15 new potential partners in the coming 6 months that we'll be opening in between Indonesia, Singapore, China, Macau and Hong Kong.

items.statement: RBI's new forex norms positive - allows AD2 licensees capital account transactions up to INR 25 lakh, no new FFMC licenses to be issued
items.quote: Yes, it's a big positive for us. One is because our license, which is an AD2, largely is a current account- based transaction license. What it has allowed or what the circular talks about is that we can now undertake capital account transactions, by definit ion, trade transaction up to INR 25 lakh per transaction

items.statement: RBI redefining forex landscape with AD1, AD2, AD3 categories; existing 1,500-1,700 FFMC licenses to remain only ones
items.quote: The second advantage or the positive that I see is that RBI is now not going to issue fresh F FMC licenses. So, what's going to happen is the current universe of 1,500 or 1,700 licenses that are there in the market are the only ones who are going to

items.statement: DEI business 50% dependent on Middle East (UAE), March 2026 revenue severely impacted by geopolitical conflict during Eid peak season
items.quote: DEI overall business was 50% depending and is contributed from the Middle East region. Whilst the Q4, Jan and Feb were trending in the right direction, we were posting about 9% better performance than the same Jan, Feb of the previous year. March turned to be a train smash.

items.statement: Forex float stable at INR 16 billion on prepaid card load volumes of USD 764 million, indicating customers not spending due to weak sentiment
items.quote: Our float as we speak, stands at about INR 16 billion on a total prepaid card loa d volumes of USD 764

items.statement: Group net cash position ~INR 800 crores; plans to repay long-term loans over next couple of years
items.quote: We also would like to sort of pay off our debt, which will be possible over the next couple of years because there are some long-term loans, which has fixed payment periods.

items.statement: No fund raise mentioned; group has net cash of INR 800 crores and Sterling debt-free with INR 3,400 million cash reserves
items.quote: Our cash reserve stands close to INR 3,400 million, while continuing to maintain a completely debt-free balance sheet.

items.statement: Board granted in-principle approval for demerger of resort business into Sterling Holiday Resorts in March 2026
items.quote: Before we move on to the segmental analysis, I will discuss the strategic divestment announcement that was made in March 2026, where the Board has granted in-principle approval for the demerger of our resort business into Sterling Holiday Resorts.

items.statement: Sterling occupancy 64% in Q4 FY26, targeting 65-70% optimal occupancy for full year
items.quote: From a leisure business, again, I've been maintaining that a good occupancy for the entire year, it will be approximately 65, closer towards 70. That's a good optimum occupancy to maintain and hold.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions materially impacting long-haul forward bookings, especially Europe, UAE, CIS markets with complete volume drop
items.quote: Geopolitical tensions have materially impacted travel demand with long -haul forward bookings witnessing weakness, especially in the European destinations and some part of our eastbound destinations, including a complete drop in volumes in UAE and CIS

items.statement: FY27 capex of INR 35 billion with 80% for growth and capacity expansion
items.quote: For FY'27, we have outlined a CapEx of INR 35 billion, with nearly 80% towards growth and capacity expansion projects.

items.statement: India capex ~INR 3,000 crore for truck and car tyre capacity; Europe capex for Hungary passenger car tyre expansion
items.quote: Close to INR 3,000 crores out of the INR 3,500 crores would be in India, where we are expanding capacity both in truck and car tyres. In Europe, in the Hungary plant, there is only a passenger car tyre expansion, which is also already well underway.

items.statement: Capacity utilisation at 90% across India and Europe; full utilisation expected
items.quote: The capacity utili sation was at a high of 90% across both our India and Europe Operations

items.statement: Strong demand in India with high teens volume growth in OE and replacement; April shows equally strong growth
items.quote: As indicated earlier, this quarter had significantly higher spends, with the activation spends relating to sponsorship of Cricket Jersey, and yet we reported the margins that we mentioned at 14.6%.

items.statement: India Q4 EBITDA margin 14.6% vs 11.2% YoY despite higher A&P spends; Europe margin 14.6% vs 14.3% YoY
items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 7.6 billion, a margin of 14.6% compared to 11.2% in the same period last year.

items.statement: Raw material costs to rise mid-to-high teens sequentially in Q1; price hikes of 6-8% announced in India, 2% in Europe; more hikes needed
items.quote: Raw material costs are expected to rise in high teens on a sequential basis. And we have already announced price increases of 6 % to 8% for this current quarter. More price increases would further be needed.

items.statement: India volume growth high teens in OE and replacement; TBR replacement 20%+, PCR replacement 20%+, OEM TBR 20%+, PCR single digit
items.quote: TBR replacement, PCR replacement, for this quarter, we had 20% plus growth. OEM, TBR 20% plus PCR single digit.

items.statement: Transitioned to concessional tax regime effective FY27; tax rate reduces from 34% to 25%; deferred tax benefit ~INR 570 crore recognised in P&L
items.quote: Following the enactment of the Finance Act 2026, we decided to transition to the concessional tax regime effective FY '27. With this transition, our applicable tax rate reduces from 34% to 25%, and consequently, our deferred tax liabilities have provided a positive net impact of almost INR 570 plus crores.

items.statement: Enschede plant closure on track; last day June 30; EUR 43 million non-cash write-off taken; EUR 55 million+ cash provision for social plan and legal costs in FY27
items.quote: The closure of the Enschede plant production remains on track. And as mentioned earlier, we have assessed now the fixed assets at the plant as we enter into the last month, and a non-cash write-off of EUR 43 million has been taken on the fixed assets this quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated ROCE 13.4% for FY26, up 240 bps YoY
items.quote: Helped by healthy margin performance, our consolidated ROCE for FY'26 stood at 13.4%, an improvement of around 240 basis points compared to FY'25.

items.statement: Export volumes mid-single-digit growth; Europe and US key markets; US demand weak; rupee depreciation benefits group not standalone
items.quote: Exports were impacted by events through the year. So the overseas markets were muted. We had mid-single-digit growth in the export volumes and a high teens in both OE and replacement.

items.statement: No marked difference in dealer inventory levels in India
items.quote: In India, there's no marked difference in terms of inventory levels at the dealers.

items.statement: All competitors announced price increases; Apollo and CEAT slightly ahead; no aggressive discounting expected due to cost push and strong demand
items.quote: everybody has announced price increases. Apollo T yres and CEAT are slightly ahead of some of the other peers. So price increases have been announced by everybody

items.statement: Geopolitical developments in West Asia creating volatility in raw material, energy, logistics costs; demand outlook for H2 FY27 uncertain
items.quote: Growth in certain international markets was impacted by the geopolitical developments in West Asia, which continue to create significant uncertainty and add volatility to raw materials, to energy and to logistics costs.

items.statement: Recognised as Top Employer 2026; India Operations first time, European entities continued track record
items.quote: Apollo Tyres has been recognised as the Top Employer in 2026, with India Operations receiving the recognition for the first time, while our European entities continued their strong track record.

items.statement: New OEM approvals: BMW, MINI, Genesis, KIA, Mahindra; upgraded premium products launched in replacement across India and Europe
items.quote: In passenger vehicle tyres, we secured fresh approval from leading OEMs, including BMW, MINI, Genesis, KIA and Mahindra. In replacement as well, we introduced upgraded premium products across India and Europe Operations.

items.statement: OEM pricing formula with 3-month lag; some negotiated increases; small increases received but not enough to offset cost push
items.quote: With a large number of our OEM customers, we follow a pricing formula which kicks in with a lag of three months. So the pain would be there for three months and then the entire raw material basket cost push goes up.

items.statement: A&P spends normalised at ~2.5% of sales going forward vs 4% in Q4 due to cricket sponsorship activation
items.quote: Going forward, we would expect, as growth kicks in, etc., for it to be around a 2.5% plus of sales. We would move up in a longer term trend, but not to the extent what is being seen is in this quarter.

items.statement: Reifencom Q4 revenue EUR 40 million, EBITDA just under 2%
items.quote: So the Reifencom number for this quarter was EUR 40 billion and EBITDA just under 2%.

items.statement: EBITDA improved 25% YoY in Q1 CY26 driven by sales mix and operational efficiency
items.quote: EBITDA improved by 25%, 24.8% like year-on-year, first quarter last year versus this year quarter 1.

items.statement: EBIT margin excluding prior-period depreciation charge reached 27.8% in Q1 CY26
items.quote: If I exclude the exceptional item of depreciation, it has actually gone up to 27.8%, which is consistent with the growth that we have seen in the EBITDA.

items.statement: Sequential EBIT margin at 8% of sales in Q1 CY26 after removing prior-period item
items.quote: Then we are at 8% EBIT for the quarter, which is in line with the EBIT that we have demonstrated in the quarter 4 last year and almost 1.7% or 170 basis points higher versus the quarter 1 of last year.

items.statement: Low to medium double-digit raw material cost impact overall; most costs passed through to customers
items.quote: I think overall, we have probably low to medium double-digit raw material impact on our products overall. The good news there is, firstly, there's no issue with availability.

items.statement: Price pass-through implemented swiftly; future orders locked at new pricing by end of March
items.quote: In fact, by end of March, we had almost all our future orders locked in with the new pricing.

items.statement: Demand growing at usual industry rates of 5-7% annually; large MNC customers growing 2-5%, regional customers faster
items.quote: usually 6%, 5% to 7% is the increase every year. Some customers increase more. Some customers do less. For example, the large customers that we play in, usually, they are less, maybe 2% to 3% to 5%.

items.statement: No raw material availability issues due to global procurement power; occasional shipment delays from overseas
items.quote: So being a large multinational company, we have resources. We have the procurement power, I guess, to source these materials from different parts of the world. So availability is not an issue.

items.statement: Solar captive electricity project at Khopoli plant signed and under execution; expected to go live in next few months
items.quote: I'm also happy to report that we actually engaged in a formal agreement for developing a solar captive electricity project in our Khopoli plant. So that's been signed. It's being executed now, and we expect to go live in the next few months.

items.statement: Capital spent on solvent cooling equipment across plants to reduce solvent consumption
items.quote: We've installed a lot of equipment. We spent some capital in solvent cooling, for example.

items.statement: Capacity not a constraint; significant room to grow
items.quote: I think we have a lot of room to grow, if I can say that, yes. So capacity is not a constraint at the moment.

items.statement: ECB loan from parent of INR 100 crores repayment extended to June 2027 per RBI guidelines; service cost benchmarked to FD returns
items.quote: this is an ECB loan from the parent, which is covered by the RBI guidelines on the tenure for the repayment part. So we have paid a part of it. A part of it still remains, which has to be paid over a period of time as prescribed, by June '27.

items.statement: Other income driven by INR 6.5 crores interest on income tax refund, higher FD interest, and FX gains from exports
items.quote: So it's about INR 6.5 crores that we have received.

items.statement: No inorganic opportunities currently on radar; focus on organic growth aligned to value proposition
items.quote: I think the short answer is not at the moment. But if something comes up, we would definitely look at that. But right now, it's not in our radar at the moment. So organically, there's a lot of room to grow.

items.statement: Total recordable safety incidents improved 67% YoY; behavioral safety improvements noted across plants and offices
items.quote: Actually, our total recordable incidents year-on-year improved by 67% which is a great achievement.

items.statement: Khopoli, Rudrapur, Silvassa plants developing zero liquid discharge status; adopting post-consumer recycled content ahead of anticipated India regulations
items.quote: Khopoli, Rudrapur, Silvassa, they continue to develop a zero liquid discharge status, and we are looking at eliminating waste and liquid waste in other plants as well.

items.statement: Focus on higher-value business aligned with innovation, premiumization, sustainability; selective participation in customer portfolio
items.quote: We are going after higher-value business, which is also consistent with our strategy and our strength in terms of the innovation leader in the industry.

items.statement: Pragmatic average-cost pricing approach used for raw material pass-through considering inventory mix of old and new purchases
items.quote: we looked at our inventory, current inventory, old inventory, new inventory, what we need to order, etcetera. And we take a pragmatic like an average -- almost like an average cost view on what we have, and we went with the price increase accordingly to our customers

items.statement: Net export position positive; FX fluctuations work both ways with rupee depreciation helping exports but increasing import costs
items.quote: we have a good representation of the exports in our overall business. So the rupee fluctuations actually works both ways. And when you look at month-to-month and quarter-to-quarter, while from a last year standpoint, the rupee is devaluating. But from a quarter-on-quarter basis, there are a lot of swings happening.

items.statement: Amit Gupta joined as CFO last month; previously CFO at Procter & Gamble Health Limited and regional finance lead for Asia, Middle East, Africa
items.quote: I actually joined as the CFO of the company last month, so almost like completing a month in this particular role. I had joined the company relocating back from Singapore to India. My last assignment was with Procter & Gamble Health Limited in their health care vertical as the regional finance lead for Asia, Middle East and Africa.

items.statement: War-related raw material price volatility ongoing; situation changing daily with prices moving both up and down
items.quote: the situation is changing every day, as you can imagine, due to the political situation there. What we have seen in last -- I think it started like end of March, we see prices going up significantly. And then we see kind of a bit of, let's say, tapering, and we are even seeing sometimes the prices are changing again negatively and positively.

items.statement: Daman property put up for sale after curtailing operations there
items.quote: So we have a property in Daman, which we have actually put up on sale. So we have curtailed our operations there and it's related to that.

items.statement: Management targets Apollo Cash disbursements of ~50 crore and AUM of 10-15 crore in Year 1, reaching 15-20% of total loan book.
items.quote: our internal goal at this poi nt in time from a disbursement standpoint, is probably, you know, a total disbursements. To the tune of, I think the first one year would be , you know, close to about 50-odd crores of total disbursement. I think the AUM will end up becoming, you know, maybe, probably, like, 10 to 15 odd crores

items.statement: Retail book proportion rose from 24% to 51% of AUM in Q4 FY26; management expects it to keep rising toward 100%.
items.quote: previously, 24% of our AUM was our retail b ook, but in this quarter, 50%, 51% of our book has been our retail book. And we expect this number to only go upwards

items.statement: Apollo Cash monthly disbursements grew 300% MoM: Feb ~30 lakh, Mar ~1.2 crore, Apr ~3 crore.
items.value: Feb 30 lakh; Mar 1.2 crore; Apr 3 crore
items.quote: just in Fe bruary, we did, you know, just 30 lakhs or so of lending, right? And in March, that, you know, went 300% up to, obviously, 1.2 crores, and in April, it's already up to 3 crores

items.statement: Retention strategy: lower pricing (ROI and processing fee), higher loan amounts, and faster 3-click repeat journey for returning customers.
items.quote: once they basically come onto our platform, show that, you know, they're a good customer making repayments on time, we basically, you know, try and essentially, next time when they come to our platform, you know, reduce the pricing for them

items.statement: Debt-to-equity is super low; no external fundraise planned currently.
items.quote: This is not something which is, you know, we are focusing on at this point in time, because I think, you know, our debt to equi ty is super low. So we aren't, you know, really expecting any kind of external

items.statement: Target segment is 'Bharat' — blue-collar, gig workers, rickshaw drivers, domestic help; not prime borrowers; algorithm rejects profiles that don't match historical high-performing customer patterns.
items.quote: our goal is to actually lend to people who are truly Bharat, righ t? Like, a good example would be, like, a rickshah driver, or a, yo u know, a help, as an example, or blue-collar workers, gig workers, things like that, right? That is the TG

items.statement: Management aims to sustain poultry segment performance and recover Animal Healthcare from Q1 FY27
items.quote: this is a base, and we want to sustain this

items.statement: Poultry Healthcare grew 41% in Q4 and 21% for FY26 driven by deeper market penetration and sustained vaccine demand
items.quote: The P oultry Healthcare division delivered a strong performance during the year, growing by 41% in Q4 and 21% for the entire financial year

items.statement: Animal Healthcare faced tender delays but Q4 PPR execution improved with 6.3 crore doses supplied
items.quote: execution under Hester Biosciences Limited 15 May 2026 the National PPR immunization program did improve, and we have supplied 6.3 crore doses in Q4 for PPR

items.statement: Standalone PAT up 174% in Q4 and 64% for FY26; consolidated PAT up almost 100% for full year
items.quote: While standalone revenue remained flat for the entire financial year, the profitability improved significantly with the PAT up by 64%

items.statement: Profitability supported by stronger execution in Poultry Healthcare, favorable product mix and operational discipline
items.quote: the overall improvement was supported by stronger execution in the Poultry Healthcare business, favorable product mix and continued operational discipline

items.statement: Fill-Finish and BSL-3 facilities capitalized; BSL-3 optimization underway to improve utilization efficiency and operating cost
items.quote: we are also undertaking optimization initiatives aligned with our current operational and scale -up requirements with focus on improving utilization efficiency and operating cost ov er the long-term

items.statement: Africa strategy evolving with expanded registrations and strengthened on-ground presence; PPR eradication program remains long-term initiative
items.quote: We expanded registrations across the key African markets during the year and strengthened our on-ground presence through our country-level teams

items.statement: Africa sales invoiced in USD for cross-border and local currency for domestic; Tanzania vaccination drive discussed as opportunity
items.quote: Invoicing to the other countries in U.S. dollars and for the local, it is a local currency

items.statement: Regulatory requirements evolving globally requiring ongoing compliance investment; no specific capex quantified
items.quote: Regulatory processes are time and again evolved from the drug department and one has to comply

items.statement: Receivables at INR 92 crores; management working to reduce debtor days after Q4 sales jump of 33%
items.quote: we are working on that to reduce the receivables overall, the number of days

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR 70 crores from INR 102 crores; debt-to-equity at 0.19x considered comfortable
items.quote: Currently, sir, the debt is around INR70 crores, right? It's reduced from INR102 crores, okay? So I think this is - the debt to equity is currently 0.19 times

items.statement: Partial divestment of stake in Texas Lifesciences completed; exceptional item related to this transaction
items.quote: During the year, we also undertook a partial divestment of our stake in Texas Lifesciences as a part of our -- of a broader capital allocation and strategic focus exercise

items.statement: Poultry Healthcare revenue mix 70% vs Animal Healthcare 30% in FY26; target steady-state 50-50 mix
items.quote: There has been a time, I think, 2 years ago where both were almost 50%, 50%, and that is what we are aiming at

items.statement: External risks include tender timing volatility and raw material cost pressures from geopolitical and supply chain disruptions
items.quote: we remain mindful of external risks, including the volatility in tender business timing and increasing raw material costs linked to the global geopolitical developments and supply chain disr uptions happening

items.statement: Petcare segment scaling gradually; no commercialized pet vaccines yet; Africa has 3-4 private vaccine producers plus state-owned units
items.quote: At the moment, none because we don't really have any commercialized vaccines in the Pet division at the moment

items.statement: Significant capacity installed; focus on optimizing utilization; future capex depends on evolving regulatory and technology needs
items.quote: we have installed quite a bit of capex, and we aim to optimize the utilization

items.statement: FY27 revenue target of INR 250 crores and EBITDA margin target of at least 15%
items.quote: This quarter itself we have done INR 59 crores. So, multiplying by 4, you will see INR 240 crores is easily feasible. So, given some growth here and there, hitting INR 250 crores I think is certainly possible.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin projected to move from 11% to at least 15%
items.quote: I think EBITDA margin should move from 11% to at least 15% is our projection.

items.statement: CES order book grew from $2.84 million to nearly $5 million, a 60-70% increase
items.quote: CES orders have shot up from actually, it was $2.5 million when we started the year. In June 24 last year, the work on hand was $2.84 million. Today, the work on hand is close to $5 million.

items.statement: MES order book declined from $0.5 million to $0.25 million
items.quote: Coming to mechanical side, that is not a great jump. It is rather a decline. In Q1, it was around $0.5 million, and it is currently at $0.25 million.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA improved to INR 552 lakhs from INR -42 lakhs YoY; PBT improved to INR 379 lakhs from INR -2 crores
items.quote: EBITDA has gone up from INR (-42) lakhs INR 552 lakhs, and PBT INR (-2) crores last year quarter Q4 to INR 379 lakhs in this Q4.

items.statement: Beryl Q4 revenue INR 11 crores with a loss of INR 70 lakhs
items.quote: The Quarter 4 turnover was INR 11 crores. As I said, it's the beginning of the year. Generally, the workflow is less for them. So, we had a loss of about INR 70 lakhs, INR 70,000.

items.statement: Standalone core business EBITDA margin expected to reach 15-16% in FY27 after MES downsizing
items.quote: our engineering services from India, now that we have curtailed the excess staff in MES, both the MES and civil from India, that's our core business, standalone business, will certainly go up by at least 15%-20% and EBITDA in the region of 15%-16%.

items.statement: Nashik office construction expected to complete by end of FY27, saving INR 2-2.5 crores annually from FY28
items.quote: Hopefully, in June, we will be raking the ground. And by the end of the financial year, the building should be up and ready. So, probably the cost savings of around INR 2 crores - INR 2.5 crores per annum can accrue in the next financial year, 2027-2028.

items.statement: MES BIW auto team downsized from 160 to 60 people by end of March 2026
items.quote: in the month of Jan, we have taken a call to downsize the team from 160 to 60 people gradually, and by end of March, the team has been downsized from 160 to 60.

items.statement: MES poles and towers team grew from 45-50 to 80 people
items.quote: poles and towers and electrical substation work is ramping up rapidly in the United States, and the team from 45 to 50 people last year are currently around 80 people and growing.

items.statement: Beryl integration adding 15-20 engineers in India to support design services over next couple of quarters
items.quote: once the training is over, those engineers, including the American engineers, will come here and train a team of 15-20 people, which would take at least a couple of quarters.

items.statement: Beryl's 4-member US sales team to cross-sell Mold-Tek detailing and design services
items.quote: The main strategic alliance with Beryl, one of our ideas was to use their sales team to work for our bread and butter detailing and designing. So, they have a 4-member pretty strong sales team having 10 to 15 years of experience in US structural designing and drafting and inspection services.

items.statement: Ovation half Mold-Tek's size despite 8-9 years; grew via acquisition and smaller base
items.quote: Ovation numbers are half our size even today though they are almost 8-9 years old. So, the team has also gone through the route of acquisition. They acquired a company nearby Atlanta that is a detailing company with about 8-10 members and then they started building up their Indian team.

items.statement: Hedging policy changed: forwards limited to 25-50% of turnover from 100% previously
items.quote: That is why we have also decided to stop the forwards and limit the forwards only to 25%-50% of company's turnover. Earlier it used to be 100%.

items.statement: MTM loss of INR 4.9 crores in Q4 FY26 due to rupee depreciation from 83-84 to 95
items.quote: There are INR 5 per dollar. It amounts to almost INR 4.9 crores for the quarter forwards which were done in the past. Because at 85-level, 89-level, 92-level, various levels we have done the forwards in the past.

items.statement: Zero debt on books; INR 25-30 crores in deposits
items.quote: The company is sitting on a pile of INR 25 crores to INR 30 crores of deposits. It has zero debt on the books. There is not even a working capital debt on the company's books.

items.statement: Preferential allotment of 2.9 lakh shares at INR 164 cancelled as investor did not fund
items.quote: the investor has taken a call not to invest in that $0.5 million which he committed. So, we cannot judge his decision because we can't influence anybody to make a forcible investment. So, that is why the preferential issue was cancelled.

items.statement: Beryl acquired November 2025 for residential design/inspection; 30% of consideration locked in for 3-year retention
items.quote: we have put that moneys in the lock-in as a standby guarantee. So that about 30% of the acquisition monies were kept aside for a minimum working time of 3 years continued service with the company.

items.statement: Beryl 40-person team fully retained after 5 months; 6 Indian engineers deployed to Tampa
items.quote: Not even a single person resigned from the 40-member team. So, that is the proof that our HR practices and the way we give freedom to the engineers and marketing team over there is really acclimatized to our culture.

items.statement: Poles and towers revenue expected to grow from $0.8-1M to $1.5-2M in FY27
items.quote: Poles and towers revenue for last year must have been anywhere around $800K to $1 million. That's less than a million, around $800K. But this year, it should cross $1.5 million to $2 million.

items.statement: MES BIW auto loss of INR 7-8 crores annually eliminated by downsizing
items.quote: tightening of the BIW team, which has been bleeding the company for the last two years to the tune of about INR 7-8 crores every year. And now it has been tightened to almost 60 people from 160 people.

items.statement: Interarch partnership stalled due to US-India trade uncertainty and duty concerns
items.quote: right from the days when we started, unfortunately, the trade talks between U.S. and India are in a kind of limbo. And buildings which are supposed to be made by Interarch and provided other services by Mold-Tek are all come under uncertainty.

items.statement: Receivables doubled YoY due to 81% Q4 revenue jump; Beryl added 2 months in December
items.quote: if you see the Q4-to-Q4, the jump in turnover is 81% from INR 32.6 crores last Q4 to in absolute rupees it is INR 59 crores, 81%. Obviously, debtors will increase.

items.statement: E-commerce on ground remains the key growth driver; e-commerce on air has been steady with limited growth.
items.quote: E-commerce, especially e-commerce on ground continues to be our growth driver, including the surface on ground as such. While the e-commerce on air has been steady, not very much too much growth over there.

items.statement: General Price Increase (GPI) implemented from 1 January 2026; pass-through better than last year and expected to exceed 4% on blended basis.
items.quote: Yes. So we did GPI from 1st of January, and it has been a little better than what we had last year as such. So it has provided a positive impact, helping us to mitigate the impact of the year-on-year inflation levels as such.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin varies quarter-on-quarter (13.5%-17.5% range); focus on yearly margin optimization rather than quarterly guidance.
items.quote: So far as depreciation is a major part of having a big setup of air as well as on the ground that we have. Yes, the quarter-on-quarter comes with variations with peak season kicking in typically in second half of the year. So we...our focus is normally to ensure a year-on-year yearly margin.

items.statement: Consolidated capex FY26 INR 360 cr (INR 200 cr aircraft maintenance, INR 120 cr standalone); FY27 similar recurring aircraft capex INR 100-150 cr, ground capex mainly lease/ROU assets, automation and IT spend.
items.quote: So if you look at the consol numbers, our capex for the year is almost INR 360 crores, whereas standalone, it is INR 120 crores. In consol, out of INR 360 crores, INR 200 crores is mainly coming from aircraft, which is in the nature of engine or aircraft maintenance.

items.statement: ATF price increases from March 2026; fuel surcharge mechanism neutralizes Brent/currency volatility; profitability impact largely neutralized from April.
items.quote: As you know, we have a fuel surcharge mechanism where any increase or drop in Brent is largely compensated or neutralized with the...between ATF and fuel surcharge. So far as ATF is moving in tandem with Brent and of course, with the currency fluctuation also, we have surcharge for both fuel as well as currency in our commercial. So to an extent, those..that volatility is neutralized largely.

items.statement: B2C volumes largely from D2C brands and aggregators; large platform share very small; no single customer has significant share.
items.quote: Very small percentage from large platform. Largely, our customer base is consisting of either D2C or sometimes aggregators. Again, at an individual level, customers ....single customer would not have a significant share of business.

items.statement: Air cargo: ~two-thirds on own freighters, ~one-third on commercial airline belly space/road across 25+ additional airports.
items.quote: Almost one third of the air load would go on commercial. Again, it's a mix of both the lanes where we operate our own aircraft. But at the same time, there are 25-odd additional airports where we don't fly, but we carry on the commercial airlines. So overall, about two third of the volumes are managed by on our own airlines, aircraft and one third is with the commercial airlines.

items.statement: Customers can shift between air and ground based on priority; ground transit time difference narrowing to 24-48 hours on many lanes.
items.quote: And again, as the ground becomes more and more efficient, the difference between air and ground can be not more than, say, 24 or at almost 48 hours depending on the lane. So as the customers become better enabled to plan for to manage their flow of the shi pments across the country, they will....they are also able to flex to choose between good at ground or good at air for that matter

items.statement: West Asia crisis not creating significant new charter opportunities; passenger airline capacity moving internationally; domestic charters continue but no big indication of new opportunities.
items.quote: So, we may not see that ...as of now, at least we don't have that big indication of new opportunities coming for charters because the passenger airlines also are ...I mean, it's moving internationally. So, while it was a good, I would say, enabler or help in the COVID period, as of now, we don't see any indication while, of course, we keep on exploring those pieces.

items.statement: Wage code implementation and labor/security framework changes during FY26; focus on compliance, employee welfare, productivity and network efficiency.
items.quote: The year also saw a dynamic cost and regulatory environment, including the implementation of the wage code and related changes across labor and security frameworks. Blue Dart remained focused on compliance, employees' welfare, productivity enhancement and network efficiency.

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR375-400 crore
items.quote: So next year, I mean, financial year '27, we expect around INR375 crores to INR400 crores of overall capex, which will be spent across new projects as well as renovation of some of our high-value cinemas.

items.statement: FY27 screen additions expected around 120 screens with 55-60% capital-light
items.quote: about 120 -odd screens visibility we have to open, we have that we'll be opening next yea r. And the percentage of screens opening in FOCO and asset -light model will -- was 55% this year. It will continue to be between 55% to 60

items.statement: Gross debt target of INR500 crore in near term
items.quote: Our gross debt as of 31st March is ar ound INR760 crores, and we intend to bring it down to about INR500 crores levels

items.statement: FY27 capex split: INR225-250 crore new projects, INR80-100 crore renovations, balance maintenance and IT
items.quote: Roughly around about INR225 crores to INR250 crores we will spend on new projects, which will be across payments which are due for projects which are under fit-out as well as new handovers that will take within the year. And about INR80 crores to INR100 crores will be spent on renovation and the balance we will spend on maintenance and IT related capex.

items.statement: Smart screen capex 30-40% lower than mainstream cinema
items.quote: So we expect that our per screen capex for a smart screen will be at least 30% to 40% lower than mainstream cinema in that same location.

items.statement: 138 screens signed under capital-light model (52 FOCO, 86 asset-light) to be executed over 18 months
items.quote: Overall, I think going forward, we have about 138 screens, which are signed under capital-light, of which 52 are under FOCO model and about 86 are unde r asset-light. So that's one. Second, in terms of going forward, our rental cost, of course, in capital-light model and franchisee model is going to be lower as compared to cinemas where we invest our entire capex and that appears in our P&L

items.statement: Smart screen pilots: 2 screens opening by mid-July, targeting 28-30 screens in FY27
items.quote: Yes. I think by July 15, a couple of pilots will open. I think we're calling them pilots. We're very confident because the se are in good cities. Good deals have been signed by the developers. Demographic studies have been done. So by July 15 or mid -July, at least 2 of them are open, and we're hoping to open close to 28 to 30 screens under this model

items.statement: FY26 added 93 screens (55% capital-light), 18 screen exits vs 72 in FY25
items.quote: Of the 93 new screens added in FY26, 55% came under capital -light formats with around 44% of additions in underpenetrated South India. Screen exits dropped sharply to 18 from 72 last year as the post -merger portfolio rationalization is largely behind us.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 14.4% from 8.4% in FY25
items.quote: On an IND AS 116 adjusted basis, FY26 revenues was a record of INR6,742 crores, up 16% year-on-year. EBITDA before exceptional items doubled to INR968 crores with margins expanding from 8.4% to 14.4%, reflecting both strong revenue growth and the cost discipline we have sustained for several years.

items.statement: FOCO management fee run rate INR13-14 crore per annum, growing 40-50%
items.quote: And our management income has seen a sharp increase, even though at an absolute level, it is about close to INR10 crores for financial year '26. But on a run rate level, it is at about INR13 crores to INR14 crores per annum, and it's growing.

items.statement: FY27 content pipeline broad across Hindi, English, regional; confident on occupancy improvement
items.quote: Looking ahead, FY27 content pipeline is broad and diverse across Hindi, English and regional cinema, giving us strong confidence in the trajectory. On the Hindi front, anticipated titles include Cocktail 2, Dhamaal 4, Welcome to the Jungle, Awarapan 2, Ramayana: Part 1, King, Love & War and with several other films also lined up.

items.statement: No impact from IPL on cinema attendance; zero correlation observed
items.quote: No, I thin k IPL is completely -- has no impact on cinema going at all. We have seen no correlation. So many movies have got released in the last few weeks ever since IPL has started, whether in the city where it is being played or in any case, the city in which it i s being played, there's only so much capacity that city can take in a stadium and all these cities are pretty populated

items.statement: FY26 ATP INR280 (+8% YoY), SPH INR147 (+10% YoY); Q4 ATP INR315, SPH INR165
items.quote: ATP for the year stood at INR280, which is up by 8% compared to previous year and SPH at INR147 compared -- up by 10% , both record highs. In Q4, ATP touched INR315 and SPH INR165.

items.statement: Net debt reduced 90% since merger to INR161 crore as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: Our net debt now is nearly down 90% since the merger to a negligible level of INR161 crores as of 31 March 2026.

items.statement: FY26 free cash flow all-time high at INR790 crore
items.quote: Robust operating performance, sustained cost discipline and reduced capital intensi ty have driven consistent free cash flow generation over the past 3 years, with FY26 free cash flow reaching an all-time high of INR790 crores

items.statement: Board to evaluate capital allocation (dividend/buyback) once net cash positive; nothing off the table
items.quote: And definitely, we want to get into a situation where we are cash positive. And of course, then the Board will meet and decide what should be done with the accruals. We haven't given it much thought at the moment.

items.statement: Too early for regulatory positives from new Tamil Nadu CM; not on immediate agenda
items.quote: It is too early. It's just -- I think only today he's become the CM. There is no -- I don't think that is probably number 1 on his agenda just now. So we don't know of any regulatory positive or what kind of news is going to come out of Tamil Nadu.

items.statement: Macro headwinds from West Asia crisis acknowledged but cinema historically resilient due to low ticket size
items.quote: But having said that, we -- history has shown that cinema being still a very small ticket size, if you look at PVR, ATP is INR280. And overall, if you look at India, India is -- maybe the average ticket price is somewhere between INR100 and INR150 maybe if you look at all the single screens, multiplexes, which are there. It's still a very -- and our average transaction size is 2 to 2.5 when people

items.statement: India box office grew 11% to INR13,519 crore in FY26; 10-year CAGR 7-8%
items.quote: Against this backdrop, FY26 was the strongest year in the industry's history with collections rising 11% to INR13,519 crores. The standout was a resurgence of original Hindi cinema with Bollywood collections growing 55% year-on-year, delivering its best year ever.

items.statement: Advertising growth subdued due to blockbuster delays; H2 FY27 expected stronger with mega titles
items.quote: On advertising, just to -- while these numbers are a bi t subdued, most of our growth this year also came in from a lot of sleeper hits, which became really, really big at the box office, which was great news. And there were about 2 or 3 big blockbuster films like Jana Nayagan and Toxic, which technically moved. If those 2 films would have got released because they were a Pongal release and then e

items.statement: Preferred partner for top mall developers (Phoenix, Prestige, DLF, Oberoi, Nexus)
items.quote: And big developers like Phoenix, Prestige, DLF, Oberoi Realty, Nexus Malls, they continue to expand into various regions and various cities. So we are very much their preferred partner with most of the -- in fact, all of the top developers in the country today.

items.statement: Theatrical-first model dominant: 470 films theatrical vs 30 OTT-direct in CY2024 per EY report
items.quote: If you look at OTT ver sus exhibition, there was an EY report, which basically just got released, wherein calendar year 2022, 217 movies first came to the theaters and 105 came to OTT. This year, 470 have come to theatrical and only 30 have gone to OTT. So a theater -first model is a very clear model for all the producers

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; Gautam Dutta (CEO) and Gaurav Sharma (CFO) active on call
items.quote: And as far as advertising is concerned, I will let Gautam Dutta, our CEO, answer you -- address that question for you about the impact of any challenging times on advertising revenues. Gautam, would you like to answer this?

items.statement: Targeting INR14,000 crores revenue in FY27 while maintaining current EBITDA margins
items.quote: Backed up by a strong order book of INR21,300 crores and robust opportunities across all verticals, we are targeting to achieve a revenue of INR14,000 crores in FY '27, while maintaining current margins.

items.statement: Expect defense revenue to cross INR4,500 crores in FY27
items.quote: The robust sales pipeline, coupled with strong execution capabilities position us well to sustain this momentum, and we should cross defense revenue of INR4,500 crores in FY '27.

items.statement: Planned annual capex of INR2,050 crores for FY27
items.quote: To support these growth plans, the company has invested INR2,700 crores over the last 2 years, and entering into FY '27 with a planned annual capex of INR2,050 crores.

items.statement: Proposed dividend of INR11 per share for FY26-27, up from INR10 per share
items.quote: The company has proposed a dividend of INR11 per sh are for FY '26-'27, up from INR10 per share in the previous year, reflecting confidence i n its financial health and commitment to the
