items.statement: Incremental costs in FY27 for Asset Management from new strategies (MF license, SIF, private credit, CRE fund)
items.quote: maybe in FY '27, we will have some incremental costs coming in our asset management business. As Ashish also alluded to the fact that we are launching the new strategies and obviously for our mutual fund license as we are moving towards the SI F business, there will be an incremental

items.statement: Nuvama Private RM count grew from 90 to 150 over 4 years; selective onboarding continues
items.quote: over the last 4 years, amidst this entire competition noise, multiple players coming in we've been able to add about 60% of our capacity. We moved from 90 to about 150 now.

items.statement: Distributed mutual funds at INR9,000-10,000 crores across firm
items.quote: Distributed MF. Yes, a border line INR9,000 to INR10,000, correct.

items.statement: MF license final inspection done; expect license in 2 months, then SIF launch with long-short strategy migration
items.quote: Our final inspection has happened, and hopefully, if we get the license in another 2 months, maybe plus a couple of months from there, we should launch our SIF in which over a period of time, we will migrate our long-short strategy

items.statement: RBI bank guarantee norms impact estimated at INR10-15 crores/year net of deposit costs
items.quote: we did the math that has an impact net of deposit costs of maybe some INR10 crores, INR15 crores a year. So not much should get covered in.

items.statement: Firm ROE at 28% for FY26
items.quote: Our ROE has been healthy at 28% for FY '26.

items.statement: Dividend of INR14 for H2 FY26 declared, taking total payout to ~50% of profit
items.quote: we have again declared a dividend of INR14 for H2 FY '26 that takes it to roughly 50% of our profit being paid as dividend which is consistent with our dividend distribution policy.

items.statement: New entrant RM hiring with lofty valuation promises but no visible monetization; career damage risk highlighted
items.quote: we've witnessed over the last 12-15 months, a large number of new players are making lofty promises to RMs of future valuations, which seem extremely stratospheric to us and no visible monetization signs.

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 40-50% YoY minimum till 2030
items.quote: Our Honorable CMD sir has already given 40% to 50% growth year-on-year till 2030.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance range of 16-20% for FY27
items.quote: We'll try to maintain in the range of 16 to 20%.

items.statement: Order book of INR 1,831 crores as of 31st March 2026
items.quote: Order books remain strong at approximately INR1,831 crores as on 31st March 2026, providing healthy revenue visibility going forward.

items.statement: Order book expected to be fully executed in FY27
items.quote: This entire FY26-27. This year will be executing the entire order book.

items.statement: Bidding pipeline of INR 3,000+ crores with 60-70% success ratio
items.quote: The bidding pipeline might go above INR3000 crores also. Now it is only depending upon the success ratio that we might see or the pricing at which the bidding closes because we don't want to compromise on our margins also.

items.statement: Next phase of capex focused on backward integration like rolling mills, operational in FY27
items.quote: Most of the capex will be a backward integration to further improve our margins and availability of materials will help us for that. So if you see maybe rolling mills or something which will be our prompt kind of a thing, that's major capex that we will be going.

items.statement: Manufacturing capacity reached 4,00,500 MTPA with 30-34% utilization in FY26
items.quote: Our current manufacturing capacity has now reached 4,00,500 metric ton per annum.

items.statement: Capacity utilization expected to reach 40-60% in FY27
items.quote: If I look at this order book, we might go to 40%, 55%, 60% this year with the growth.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded from 16% to 20% in FY26
items.quote: EBITDA margin also expanded from 16% last year to 20% during the current year.

items.statement: Raw material escalation >5% passed through to customers; inventory hedging used for other contracts
items.quote: In bigger contracts and everything, clear cut raw material condition is that if there is any escalation more than 5%, it is passed on to the customer. In other contracts where we don't have, we already have piled up the inventories or we have taken inventory on our books so that we don't have hit on the margins.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions impacting fuel costs; using green hydrogen blended with LPG for galvanizing plant
items.quote: As per the regulations, we can blend 20 to 25% green hydrogen into the LPG. So, we are following that rules and what happens is that it reduces the cost to a small extent only, but it is a uniqueness that, you know, that gives us, you know, that utilization of green hydrogen.

items.statement: Diversifying into rolling mills, container manufacturing, aluminium extrusions, tubular towers, fasteners, cables and conductors
items.quote: We are getting into container manufacturing, we are getting into aluminium extrusions, onshore tubular towers, fasteners, then offshore tubular towers and cables and conductors.

items.statement: Group company orders at 20-25% of order book; BSNL telecom order INR 819+ crores is largest single order
items.quote: This year, out of INR1800 crores, 20 to 25% is only group companies. Rest all is outside.

items.statement: Inventory days increased to 195 days due to strategic stockpiling for geopolitical hedging
items.quote: We need to have this in hand because of the geopolitical conditions, we need to stock up, pile up the inventory so that we don't have impact on the margins, we don't have impact on the availability of the raw materials.

items.statement: Short-term debt increased for inventory stockpiling; long-term debt-to-equity low; average borrowing cost 8.5-9%
items.quote: My average cost of borrowing will be somewhere into 8.5 % to 9%. So, I don't take any high-cost debt. I don't take from any venture capitalists.

items.statement: No equity dilution planned; Main Board migration when SEBI criteria met (likely 3-year requirement)
items.quote: Regarding the current conditions for the Main Board -- once our specific requirements are fulfilled, we will proceed to list the company on the Main Board.

items.statement: 5-year revenue CAGR 100%, PAT CAGR 136%
items.quote: Over the past five years, the company has scaled its business and continued its growth momentum. During this period, our compounded annual growth has been remarkable with 100% CAGR in the revenue and 136% CAGR in net profit.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions creating fuel cost uncertainty and potential supply disruptions
items.quote: Next year also we are trying to see that, you know, if there is a major disruption in the geopolitical condition, then we might, but also to highlight over here that we are powering our galvanizing plant along with LPG, we are powering with green hydrogen.

items.statement: Asia's largest hot-dip galvanizing plant commissioned at Matar with 90,000 MTPA capacity and 15 MT single dip
items.quote: One of the bigg est milestones for the company has been operationalizing Asia's largest galvanizing plant with a capacity of 90,000 metric tons per annum and with a single dip capacity of 15 metric tons

items.statement: Approved by global tracker leaders Nextracker and GameChange Solar for solar structures
items.quote: In the solar structure vertical, we are proudly associated with almost all major renewable energy executing organizations in India and are also approved by global tracker leaders, Nextracker and GameChange Solar.

items.statement: Management targets 20-25% overall revenue growth and 25-30% growth in wind energy fasteners and springs in the short term.
items.quote: And as a company, we are looking to grow 20% to 25% sector in overall revenue term and in wind also we are looking to grow around 25% to 30% in short term for our fasteners and spring category.

items.statement: Chennai Phase 1 reached ~5 crore/month run rate (60 crore annual); Phase 2 adds another 5 crore/month by June/July, targeting 120 crore annual capacity by year-end.
items.quote: And now we are seeing the similar runway as of now we will going to have in April, May, June. And parallelly we started the Phase 2 capex, which should be completing by June end, July. And that again will add another 5 crores per month capacity or annual capacity of additional 60 crores.

items.statement: FY27 capex of ~50 crore planned for new Wada land acquisition and development, funded from internal accruals and bank borrowing.
items.quote: For the current year, we are seeing approximately INR50 crores something we may be able to deploy plus minus depend when we finalize the land or able to start the construction of the building.

items.statement: New Wada facility construction timeline estimated at 12-15 months after land acquisition, with land deal expected to close by June/July.
items.quote: So, you can fairly estimate one year to one, 15 month something you can fairly estimate and parallelly we are ordering for the plant and other machinery, erection of something happening and taking the final approval.

items.statement: Offshore wind partnership expected to contribute ~10% of fastener sales in 2-3 years; bolt supplies to global wind OEM in India commenced in Q4 FY26.
items.quote: And in short term in two to three years, we see offshore wind partnership contribute about 10% of our fastener sales.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin 16.51% down from 17.1% due to ~1% forex loss (INR 3.23 crore); margins expected to stabilize at 17-19% in FY27 absent further volatility.
items.quote: But going ahead considering there is no further volatility, we expect the margins to stabilize between 17% to 19%.

items.statement: Raw material costs 100% pass-through; process cost increases (gas, etc.) being passed through with lag, price revision discussions started April 2026.
items.quote: See, so basically raw material is 100% pass through. So, and of course, currently because of gas and some other issues, this process costs have also increased. So, with the lag effect, we are confident to get this price increase from our customer and for which we already started discussion since beginning of April itself.

items.statement: Inventory days at 103 days, target to reduce by ~10 days; Chennai ramp-up may temporarily increase inventory but overall level not expected above 103 days.
items.quote: Otherwise, overall inventory level are at 103 days and we see it should not go above 103 days and we were trying that we can reduce this inventory days by some 10 days or so.

items.statement: Export share to remain 35-40% of sales; hedging policy reduced to 40% of estimated export collections (12-month forward covers) from previous 70%.
items.quote: Yes. So, I think export will continue to be between 35% to 40% of our sales. And depending on the new product addition, new customer addition, this may vary on year-on-year basis, but broadly this will remain between 35% to 40% of our total sales.

items.statement: EU-India FTA expected Jan 2027 to zero out 3.7% import duty, but CBAM costs may offset benefit; positive sentiment for Indian suppliers in medium term.
items.quote: And I think that FTA will be implemented in early FY27 or sorry, in Jan 27. And by this implementation, the import duty will be zero on our products in Europe. But on other side, there is an impact possible of CBAM on which European countries are working on.

items.statement: SFS (fasteners) crossed INR 108 crore (64% YoY), now largest growth driver; DSS 49%, CSS 17% of FY26 revenue; fastener addressable market expanded from $1B to $2.5B with bolt/nut addition.
items.quote: During the year, SFS revenue crossed INR100 crores milestone, reaching INR108 crores, and registered a strong growth of 64% year-on-year.

items.statement: ~10-15% annual growth from new customers, 10-12% from new parts with existing customers, 5-7% organic growth; targeting 25-35% wallet share with key accounts.
items.quote: So, I think 10% of new customer addition, about 10% to 12% of new parts from existing customer like bolts or Gallock or even retractor spring, and organic growth of 5% to 7% happening in the organic business with the existing part has resulted is this 30% growth last year.

items.statement: CSS competitors: NHK Spring (Japan, plants in Aurangabad/Gurgaon) and Stumpp Schuele & Somappa (India, Bangalore); European imports still present.
items.quote: In CSS, we have mainly two competitors. There is a Japanese company NHK Spring, which is having manufacturing plant in Aurangabad and Gurgaon. And there is a Indian company Stumpp, Schuele and Somappa, which is having manufacturing plant at multiple locations with major head office in Bangalore.

items.statement: Patent case on wedge lock washers ongoing; next hearing in June 2026, only submissions so far, no arguments yet.
items.quote: The next hearing itself is dated in June only. So, not much more movement has taken place, only submissions have been going on, but no arguments have taken place at all.

items.statement: Wada disc spring utilization ~80%, coil spring has spare capacity; fastener division at Wada near optimum; productivity improvements and line balancing to optimize utilization for FY27 targets.
items.quote: And in disc spring, we are more or less optimum utilized, which is almost 80% approximately. And same for the fastener division at Wada, number one.

items.statement: Chennai land exhausted after Phase 2; backup plan to lease facility for stud manufacturing and expand bolt capacity in-house; new Wada land acquisition critical for growth beyond FY28.
items.quote: we don’t have any land after we complete the Phase 2 expansion, that means the INR120 crores per annum. Number two, as a backup plan, we have so this in ’26, ’27, we are targeting approximately INR80 crores something from the Chennai

items.statement: Fastener sales crossed INR 100 crore milestone in FY26 (INR 108 crore), addressing $2.5B global market vs $1B previously with studs only.
items.quote: And now with bolts and nuts, we are addressing US$2.5 billion of the global market and our fastener sales is approximately INR100 crores we crossed in FY26.

items.statement: Management targets at least 25-30% annual revenue growth and 30% absolute profit growth for the next 5-6 years.
items.quote: So revenue growth for us, our internal thing is that we want to grow by at least in a year by 25%, 30% for sure. And the profit also, we want to, in absolute terms for the next 5, 6 years, growth by 30% for sure.

items.statement: FY26 brand business guidance was INR359-360 crores; actual achieved INR370 crores.
items.value: Guidance: INR359-360 cr; Actual: INR370 cr
items.quote: Yes. Our guidance was INR359 crores, INR360 crores. We did INR370 crores.

items.statement: Brand business EBITDA margin currently ~13%; expected to reach 18-19% EBIT margin at INR1,000 cr scale.
items.quote: So for example, if we are operating at, say, 12% to 13% EBIT now, once we cross the INR1,000 crores mark, we should operate at is 18%, 19% EBIT.

items.statement: Brand business revenue FY26: INR369.61 crores (India INR231.98 cr, Overseas INR137.6 cr), 14.1% of total revenue.
items.quote: Brand business in India was INR231.98 crores and outside India was INR137.6 crores. Total Brand business we achieved INR369.61 crores.

items.statement: No major capex planned except working capital for brand launches; INR10-12 cr marketing spend for new brand in first 12-14 months.
items.quote: Yes, we'll require at least INR10 crores to INR12 crores in marketing initially, but I think the balance sheet can easily support that in the next 12 to 14 months.

items.statement: Actively looking to acquire a brand in surveillance, drone, AI space with legacy and good team to gain operational efficiencies.
items.quote: We are in active lookout of looking at any brand which we can look in the surveillance drone AI space. So the brand which has some legacy, which has a good team, so we can then just get operational efficiencies built in and use our balance sheet to grow.

items.statement: Launched own brand 'Vertual' in air purifier category; pre-launch in 2-3 days, market availability from May 22-23 in India and US via Amazon.
items.quote: this month you will hear that we launched our own brand also in this space. This brand c ategory, we have launched -- we are planning to launch it in U.S. and in India. Same categories of products what we do in Honeywell, but different models and slightly similar specification

items.statement: Make-in-India surveillance/AI vendors are smaller, yielding higher margins but requiring extended credit, increasing receivables.
items.quote: And this Make in India companies are mainly into surveillance and AI. And the end customer at some point is either a PSU or government or somebody. And in this case, because the suppliers or the vendors whom we are dealing with, their size is much smaller and that's why you get a higher percentage margin.

items.statement: Receivables rose from INR237.76 cr to INR565.11 cr (13.4% to 21% of turnover) due to 100% Q4 revenue growth and extended credit in new AI/data center/surveillance businesses; expected to normalize.
items.quote: So the receivables has gone up from INR237.7 crores to INR565. So if you understand from the turnover point of view, so that was 13.41% of turnover in the last year. And now currently, that is coming around 20%.

items.statement: Short-term debt includes INR171 cr supply chain financing for MSME payments via TReDS platform at 8-9% interest; core debt rose only INR14 cr (INR69.53 cr to INR83.72 cr) vs 50% revenue growth.
items.quote: Rest of the thing, INR171 crores is the supply chain vendor financing for the MSME payment. So that is getting reflected in the balance sheet under the short-term debt liabilities.

items.statement: Middle East freight costs surged from $1,500-1,700 to $7,500-8,000 per container due to Red Sea routing; 45-60 days inventory buffers in place.
items.quote: And now you can only move the material through the Red Sea, where the initial, say, the freight cost was between $1,500 to $1,700, which has now gone to $7,500 to $8,000.

items.statement: Inventory levels increased to manage material shortages and hedge future price escalations.
items.quote: So when the material is in shortage, you keep buying whatever material is available and also you pass it with you for, say, a period of 30 to 40 days so that your commitment with various customers can be met what you have done that. So yes, the inventory level also goes higher because then you don't have the availability.

items.statement: Demerger of brand business planned in 2-3 years (15 months no plan, then 12-15 month process); target 3-4 brands near-term, 6-7 long-term, each INR1,000 cr+ scale.
items.quote: So for the next 15 months, there is no plan. But then probably after that, we could initiate this because that's also another, I think, 12 to 15 months process to demerge that.

items.statement: Actively seeking acquisition in surveillance/drone/AI brand space with SI capabilities and sales track record.
items.quote: we are looking at in the surveillance space and in the surveillance AI space, if we can acquire a company which is a brand which has a certain amount of SI and cert ain amount of sales that business. So we are actively looking at that space

items.statement: Working capital for next 15 months manageable via debt and internal accruals; fundraise only if large acquisition (>30% of size) materializes.
items.quote: So currently, we think through debt and internal accruals, we will be able to look at the working capital for the n ext 15 months for sure. If there's a large opportunity which comes to acquisition or at least 30% of our size. And if we look at that kind of acquisition, then only we'll require money

items.statement: Added talent in servers, surveillance, AI to support new categories; operating leverage to reduce manpower cost from 6-7% to 4-5% at scale.
items.quote: And now with the operating leverage what we have and the scale we have all the met prices also will start falling into play. So like your manpower cost will not be about 2%, 2.5%. Your logistics cost will be around 1%, 1.1%.

items.statement: Key risks: Middle East supply chain disruption (freight, containers, port congestion), raw material cost inflation (30-40%), consumer demand sensitivity to price hikes, receivables normalization timeline.
items.quote: The biggest threat for us is right now supply chain disruption and the cost of raw material because the cost used to go up in IT used to go down. But right now, the cost has gone up by 30%, 40%, especially memory and storage and CPUs. That's where the cost is.

items.statement: Intangible assets rose to INR406 cr due to new ERP (Microsoft Business Central), CRM, supply chain software, server licenses, new offices, and Noida distribution center.
items.quote: So intangible has gone up to 406. So that is a large expansion in terms of the network office and everything. We have all the systems and all the software licenses and everything what we have purchased. So this is the reason you are seeing this growth in the intangible asset.

items.statement: FY27 capacity utilization expected at 50-60% of expanded 36,000 MT capacity; full utilization targeted in FY28
items.quote: So we may get a less percentage of optimum capacity utilization of ALCU Industries, but we do expect that total capacity is 50% to 60% we should be able to utilize in this year. And, of course, '27-'28 would be a full year where we will be completely operating at 36,000-ton capacity.

items.statement: ALCU plant started Feb 7, 2026; 6,000 MT capacity added; remaining 8,000-9,000 MT by Sep-Oct 2026 (before Diwali) to reach 35,000-36,000 MT total
items.quote: So currently, I mean we are already we have added some 6,000 metric tons of capacity and the remaining 8, 000 to 9,000 tons or so will be added over a period of around September or October or before Diwali we are expecting to operate at 100% capacity planned in ALCU.

items.statement: FY26 volume 18,024 MT, up 6.5% YoY; ALCU contributed ~800 MT in Feb-Mar 2026
items.quote: No, volume will be around 18,024 metric tons.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 4.66% in FY26, up 35 bps YoY; EBITDA/MT improving with new value-added products
items.quote: EBITDA reached 857.8 million with a margin of 4.66, an increase of 35 basis points year-over-year improvement.

items.statement: Back-to-back hedging on LME for copper/aluminium insulates margins from commodity price swings
items.quote: To protect our margins, we have continued our strict back-to-back hedging policy for copper and aluminium procurement.

items.statement: Industry research indicates India power demand growth rebounding to 5-5.5% driven by data centers, industrial consumption, energy transition
items.quote: Industry research indicates a rebound in India's power demand g rowth to 5 % to 5.5% range, driven by data centers, industrial consumption and the ongoing energy transition

items.statement: New specialized products launched: aluminium paper-covered conductors, aluminium enamelled wires/strips, PV round ribbon, multi-paper covered copper conductors, copper bus bars; CTC (3,000 MT) and copper foils coming
items.quote: we have successfully introduced several new s pecialized product categories, which includes aluminium paper-covered conductors, aluminium enamelled wires and strips, PV round ribbon, multi-paper covered copper conductors and copper bus bars

items.statement: Customer qualification ongoing for new products; trial orders received; leverage existing relationships with large institutional/global clients
items.quote: So, sir, the qualification progress is already going on. So many customers have already visited and they have small trial lots orders have also been started coming.

items.statement: Key peers: Precision Wires, Ram Ratna Wires, KSH International; 50-60% product overlap; target market share 11.3% post-expansion from 5.7%
items.quote: Yes, so not in 100% of our products we have direct competition with our peers, but few of the peers namely are Precision Wires, Ram Ratna Wires, KSH International, and there are many more, but they don't compete in each and every product of Vidya Wires.

items.statement: Working capital cycle at 60 days; target 50-52 days by increasing creditor days and reducing debtor days from 41 to ~35 days; inventory 21-24 days
items.quote: And we are taking measures to bring this down to say the levels of 50 to 52. Currently it is at 60 days of working cycle. So we are planning to increase our credit period days and reduce our debtor days basically.

items.statement: INR 100 crore of IPO proceeds used to repay working capital borrowings, reducing interest burden and strengthening credit profile
items.quote: In line with our commitment to a lean balance sheet, we have utilized INR100 crores to repay our working capital borrowings, successfully reducing our interest burden and strengthening our credit profile.

items.statement: Exports at 12% of volume; target 25% export / 75% domestic mix; export margins better than domestic
items.quote: So Ayush, currently we are at 12% of exports of the total business volume. Yes, we are definitely targeting the international market and our target is that we should have a balance of 75% domestic and 25% export.

items.statement: Gujarat Category 3 location qualifies for GST subsidy of 45-50% of investment over 10 years in annual tranches
items.quote: So, we all we are basically our new unit is in the category three, so urban area basically. But still we will have having we will be having a GST subsidy for the next 10 years. So this will be able to, you know, 45 to 50% of our investment what we have done would come as a subsidy over a period of 10 years in tranche of 10 years basically.

items.statement: EBITDA per metric ton improved in FY26; expected to improve further with new product mix; peers at ~INR 66,000/MT
items.quote: Already in the last year also our EBITDA per metric ton has improved and we are expecting that this will be better considering new product addition and of course our selection of the new product has also been on the same motive that the EBITDA per metric ton needs to be improved.

items.statement: Major expansion from ~19,000 MT to 36,000 MT capacity underway; no further capex announced beyond current plan
items.quote: So sir, currently we are already b een doing the major expansion, you can understand that from around 19,000 ton metric ton capacity we are planning to make it 36,000 metric ton capacity. So a good volume growth we are already planning. So I think we are sticking to this and make it more operational and efficient performance with the added capacity

items.statement: Raw material imports 40-50% of needs (copper rods/cathodes); diversified supplier base (5-6 domestic + international); Middle East crisis raised freight/packing costs marginally
items.quote: So, import part will be always like this much percentage, means maybe around 40 to 50%. So we believe in, you know, managing like we can we don't want to put all eggs in one basket. So we have imports also and we have domestic supply also.

items.statement: Middle East crisis increased ocean freight and packing material costs; supply chain challenges for both import and export
items.quote: Yes, definitely. Nobody will be left aside. So we are also part of this because the ocean freights have gone up, we are not getting many time vessels. So this problem is there for export also and this problem is also still continues for import as well.

items.statement: Other expenses jumped sequentially from INR 28M to 83M in Q4 due to one-time items; normalized run rate expected going forward
items.quote: So basically, there were some expenses which we had not considered. They have been expensed out in this quarter. So rest going forward, the expenses will be in line with the revenue percentages only and we will not see any major increase in each quarter basically.

items.statement: FY27 guidance: 15%+ organic revenue growth, 25% revenue growth on acquired portfolio, 20%+ PAT growth
items.value: 15%+ organic revenue growth, 25% acquired portfolio growth, 20%+ PAT growth
items.quote: We expect to sustain 15% plus revenue growth organically and 25% revenue growth in acquired brand with 20% plus PAT growth in FY27 too.

items.statement: Medium-term philosophy: 15% revenue and 20% PAT growth YoY for next 3-5 years
items.quote: Our philosophy is to grow 15% on a revenue and 20% on a PAT basis on a year-on-year basis for coming 3 to 5 years down the

items.statement: IPM grew double-digit over past 5 months; Corona outperformed at nearly 2x industry rate
items.quote: IPM, the industry has recorded double-digit growth over the past five months, which is an extremely positive development for IPM and for all of us.

items.statement: FY27 IPM growth expected at 10-10.5% with 1.5-2% volume growth
items.quote: am anticipating about 10% to 10.3% overall growth as far as this year is concerned, with the volume growth of about 1.5% to 2

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin improved 80bps to 20.9%; Q4 margin 17.6% down 90bps due to new division costs
items.quote: EBITDA margin has seen a healthy improvement of around 80bps. EBITDA margin for FY26 stood at 20.9%.

items.statement: Gross margin sustained at 81.4% in FY26; target to maintain 80%+ range
items.quote: as far as gross margins are concerned, it is 81.4% for FY '26 full year. We have altways said in our commentary that we would be maintaining the gross margins at the range of 80% in the coming years down the line

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margin decline due to INR 14 cr employee cost for two new divisions and INR 1.6 cr R&D spend
items.quote: in the Q4, INR 9 crores was additionally spent in the form of the forming of two new divisions and deployment of MRs and the MR expense of almostINR 5 crores which is being standing in other expenses inthe form of MR expenses in the form of allowances which we give to them

items.statement: Two brands crossed INR 100 cr revenue; 8 brands in INR 50-100 cr club
items.quote: We are proud to announce that, as per PharmaTrac's MAT March 2026 data, two of our brands have surpassed the INR 100 crore revenue milestone and continue to demonstrate consistent growth.

items.statement: Chronic and semi-chronic segments contribute 72% of revenue per PharmaTrac MAT March 2026
items.quote: With these businesses, now we are contributing 72% to our overall revenue, as per PharmaTrac's MAT March 2026 data.

items.statement: Adding new 600-kg line expansion and commissioning dedicated hormone plant operational in Q1/Q2 FY27
items.quote: We are undertaking the expansion of our manufacturing capabilitics through the addition of a new 600-kg line cxpansion, alongside the commissioning of our dedicated hormone mamufacturing plant, which is expected to become operational in Q1 or Q2 of FY27

items.statement: Received EAEU GMP certification enabling access to Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Armenia, Kyrgyzstan
items.quote: The receipt of EAEU GMP certification marks an important milestone in our international growth journey. This certification enables us to assess and expand our presence across key Eurasian markets, including Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Armenia, and Kyrgyzstan.

items.statement: Launched 3 biosimilar products in FY26: Fostine R, Tricium DnaB, Wyntide and Tyvenza
items.quote: We also have marked our enfry into the biosimilars and biologics market with the launch of three biosimilar products in FY26, that is Fostine R, Tricium DnaB, Wyntide and

items.statement: Completed two strategic acquisitions in FY26: Wokadine (ranked #2 in Povidone Iodine) and Bayer Zydus portfolio relaunch in Q4FY26
items.quote: We have successfilly completed two strategic acquisitions in FY26, the recent acquisition of Wokadine and the carlier acquisition of the Bayers Portfolio, whose relaunch was initiated in Q4FY26

items.statement: Wokadine acquisition targets 25% revenue growth for 3-4 years and 400bps gross margin improvement in year 1
items.quote: we arc anticipating about 25% revenue growth for at least 3 to 4 years in the Wokadine. And what I understand as far as 14 different SKUs of Wokadine, few are out of NELM and majority of arc in NELM. items.quote: On the input cost, and rupee depreciation is a factor there. Yes, it is playing out. It is impacting us because a big part of our raw material cost base is imported and to that extent, there is exposure.

items.statement: Good demand momentum in Roofing over last 2-3 months driven by rural economy resilience and pricing headroom vs steel roofing
items.quote: What we are witnessing, and I can say that on the evidence of the last 2 to 3 months is there is good momentum on the demand front, certainly better than what it was last year and last couple of years, honestly.

items.statement: Pipes demand fundamentals intact; green shoots of recovery in government spending on water and pipeline from Q4
items.quote: the fundamental macro demand scenario sti ll remains intact. The amount of construction and hence, the consequence of that on the demand for pipes still remains where it was

items.statement: Construction Chemicals including Clean Coats grew 58% YoY in Q4 and 45% for full year; crossed Rs. 100 crores revenue milestone
items.quote: I am pleased to highlight that we crossed our first milestone of Rs. 100 crores revenue in this segment during the year.

items.statement: Walls segment revenue grew 14% in Q4 and 13% for full year led by Panels and Boards at 20-25% growth
items.quote: This performance was primarily driven by Panels and Boards segment which delivered growth in the range of 20% to 25% during the year.

items.statement: Walls sales mix roughly 60% AAC Blocks, 25% Panels, 15% Boards
items.quote: So roughly, it will be 60%, 25% and 15%.

items.statement: Parador India positioned at premium end as Made in Germany product; building pipeline in commercial and retail focused on metros
items.quote: It is still positioned at the premium end of the segment. It is a Made in Germany product and that is the proposition that we are building.

items.statement: Pipes range comparable to largest player with over 3,000 SKUs across CPVC, uPVC, OPVC, HDPE and manufacturing footprint across 4 regions
items.quote: We carry over 3,000 SKUs and from CPVC, uPVC, OPVC to HDPE, the entire range is available with us, point number one.

items.statement: Government removed anti-dumping duty on PVC resin in early April as proactive action given market volatility
items.quote: If I remember correctly, that came in, in April, not in March. That was almost 3, 4 weeks after all of this had happened is when it came. So sometime in April, first 10 days of April, if I remember correctly.

items.statement: Debt reduced from Rs. 929 crores in December to Rs. 851 crores at year-end through working capital management; comfortable with additional Rs. 200-250 crores
items.quote: I am pleased to note that through focused working capital management and tighter operational controls during the second half, we were able to reduce borrowings, and it stands at Rs. 851 crores at the end of the financial year.

items.statement: Clean Coats acquisition completed for 4.5 months contributing Rs. 20 crores; integration progressing well
items.quote: Clean Coats number for the 4.5 months is Rs. 20 crores.

items.statement: Provision of Rs. 74 crores for diminution in equity investment in BirlaNu International GmbH (Parador) reported under exceptional items
items.quote: I would also like to draw your attention on provision created for diminution in the equity investment in BirlaNu International GmBH amounting to Rs. 74 crores, which has been reported under exceptional items in the standalone financial statements for the quarter.

items.statement: Pipes volume growth in Q4 in zone of 2-3%; Walls blended volume growth about 20% plus in Q4
items.quote: Pipes volume growth is in the zone of about 2% to 3% . And the second one was? Sanjay Kumar: Walls? Akshat Seth: Walls overall volume growth in Q4 will be a blended of about 20

items.statement: Parador residual equity value Rs. 200 crores vs original investment Rs. 273.5 crores; impairment based on DCF and CCA valuation models
items.quote: So, it is around Rs. 200 crores as on 31st March, our original investment was Rs. 273.5 crores.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of INR950 crores based on ~50% utilization of expanded ethanol capacity
items.quote: the top line guidance of an average of INR950 crores is also very conservative in nature. And we have factored in only about 50% capacity utilization of the expansion.

items.statement: Ethanol division sustainable EBITDA margin guided at 12-15% long-term
items.quote: on previous calls, I have maintained that we will achieve between 12% to 15% EBITDA in this division on a sustainable basis.

items.statement: Full capacity utilization could push consolidated revenue above INR1,100 crores
items.quote: I think with full capacity utilization, our consolidated revenue will cross INR1,100 crores.

items.statement: Consumer division targeting INR500 crores revenue in medium term (INR300-350 crores from oils, INR150 crores from food)
items.quote: I don't see any reason why this segment for us should not get to INR500 crores in the medium term. This will be propelled by growth within the oil basket as well as food products.

items.statement: Up to INR20 crores capex planned for FY27 for byproduct value addition in ethanol division
items.quote: We're looking at investing up to INR20 crores in a value addition project in our byproduct stream in the ethanol division. But other than that, we have no large capex plans.

items.statement: Ethanol capacity expanded from 130 KLPD to 282 KLPD; Phase 2 commissioned in FY26
items.quote: successfully commissioned Phase 2 of our ethanol expansion, increasing capacity from 130 KL to 282 kiloliters per day.

items.statement: Current ethanol order book of 47.9K KL (INR400 crores) for PSU OMC cycle one tender till 31 Oct 2026
items.quote: the orders that we received is for the ongoing ESY in the cycle one tender of PSU OMCs alone. And this is till 31st October of this year.

items.statement: Expect additional orders from private and PSU OMCs in current ESY; next cycle bidding in Sep-Oct 2026
items.quote: in this ESY alone, we expect to get more orders from private as well as PSU OMCs. And of course, from 1st November, we will be rebidding for the next cycle.

items.statement: Ethanol division EBITDA margin 17.3% in FY26 vs 13% in FY25; sustainable range 12-15%
items.quote: this year's particular in nature because I think grain prices softened a little bit and we did do some value addition in our byproducts. And in the last quarter, we had an exceptional item which actually increased our EBITDA margin to 18.8%.

items.statement: Consumer division EBITDA margin at 8.3% for FY26
items.quote: at the consumer division level, it's about 8.3% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Consumer division demand improving driven by expanded distribution, innovation and new product launches
items.quote: Overall, the demand is improving, driven by expanded distribution, innovation, and new product launches in our food basket.

items.statement: Consumer division revenue split: ~90% oils, ~10% food products; food portfolio profitable from year 1-2
items.quote: our food products contribute roughly 10% and 90% comes from our oil portfolio.

items.statement: New product launches in FY26: hing; pasta performing well on quick commerce; more launches planned for FY27
items.quote: We also expanded our packaged foods portfolio with the launch of newer categories such as hing, which received a strong market response.

items.statement: Consumer channel mix: ~50% modern trade, ~40% general trade, ~8-10% army CSD/CPC; direct coverage of ~50,000 outlets
items.quote: We have about 50% modern trade, 40% general trade, and about 8%-10% comes from our army channel.

items.statement: Present on all quick commerce apps pan-India; exports to Bhutan (scaling) and Nepal (recent start)
items.quote: we are very proud to say that we are present in Q-com across all the apps as well as across geographies. So we are present across the country. And we are also present in neighbouring markets like Bhutan and Nepal.

items.statement: Passed on packaging cost increases; rice bran oil prices up but olive oil prices down, managing edible oil input costs
items.quote: we have passed it on to some extent. For example, there's a huge increase in packaging material costs. So that we have passed on. Raw material wise, in the food category, we don't see as much inflation. On the edible oil side, while rice bran prices have gone up, olive oil prices have come down.

items.statement: Working capital days improved to 62 days (Mar 2026) from 66 days (Mar 2025); operating cash flow INR61.1 crores vs INR48.8 crores
items.quote: Working capital days further improved to 62 days as of 31st March 2026, as compared to 66 days from last year, demonstrating tighter operational control and more efficient utilization of resources.

items.statement: Strong cash generation provides financial flexibility for growth while maintaining balance sheet discipline
items.quote: Healthy cash generation remained another key highlight during the year, with cash flow from operations increasing to INR61.1 crores in FY26 compared to INR48.8 crores in FY25. This strong cash generation provides greater financial flexibility to support future growth initiatives while maintaining balance sheet discipline.

items.statement: Government discussing higher ethanol blending beyond E20; potential ethanol exports to Nepal under consideration
items.quote: there's a lot of action happening at the geopolitical level, which will affect the ethanol policy, whether it's to do with domestic consumption or permitting exports. That we will see over the next few weeks.

items.statement: Evaluated food sector acquisition opportunities but nothing finalized; will inform market when concrete
items.quote: We've evaluated a few opportunities in the food sector, but nothing that we have firmed up yet. And we will let the community know as and when.

items.statement: Auditor change was planned succession; new auditors already audited Modi Biotech for 2-3 years
items.quote: this was always planned. I think this is more of a succession which we started this journey started, I think, two to three years back. So the auditors who have been appointed were already auditing our Modi Biotech results for the last two, three years.

items.statement: Ethanol division FY26 revenue INR337.4 crores, EBITDA INR58.2 crores; Q4 FY26 revenue INR92.2 crores, EBITDA INR18.5 crores
items.quote: Ethanol division: In Q4 FY26, our revenue stood at INR92.2 crores, and for FY26 stood at INR337.4 crores. EBITDA for Q4 stood at INR18.5 crores, and for FY26 stood at INR58.2 crores.

items.statement: Consumer division FY26 revenue INR183.5 crores, EBITDA INR15.2 crores; Q4 FY26 revenue INR50.9 crores (highest ever quarterly)
items.quote: Consumer division: Revenue for Q4 FY26 stood at INR50.9 crores compared to INR48.5 crores in Q4 FY25, and FY26 stood at INR183.5 crores compared to INR179.4 crores in FY25.

items.statement: Bulk division FY26 revenue INR198.3 crores, EBITDA INR2.6 crores; leaner inventory model improved working capital
items.quote: Bulk division: In Q4 FY26, our revenue stood at INR100 crores as compared to INR56.1 crores in Q4 FY25, and FY26 stood at INR198.3 crores as compared to INR158.6 crores in FY25.

items.statement: Advertising spend INR12 crores (6.5% of consumer revenue); 60% external, 40% quick commerce
items.quote: our total ad spend for this year is INR12 crores. Akshay Modi: It's about 6.5%. This is what I think we had projected anyway. So yes. This is purely only advertising. We are not talking about other below the line advertising. This is purely above the line advertising

items.statement: Brand ambassador Karisma Kapoor engagement ongoing; digital marketing focused on female target audience on Jio Cinema, Hotstar
items.quote: Celebrity engagement. Yes, our brand ambassador is Karisma Kapoor and that is ongoing. It hasn't ended.

items.statement: Expect full utilization of Dahej and Roha facilities in FY27
items.quote: As far as '26, '27 is concerned, then we expect full utilization of both our Dahej and Roha facilities in this financial year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin on manufactured sales is close to 24-25%
items.quote: So if you see the actual EBITDA margin on manufactured sales, it would be close to 24%, 25%, which was what the target of the company was as far as synthetic food colors and certain other value-added products.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to rise further as value-added products increase
items.quote: And as these value -added products and certain specia lized products used in certain industries continue to increase in quantity, the EBITDA margins of the company are expected to rise even further from the same manufacturing facilities

items.statement: Capex for CoatIcon pharma product line expected between INR5-12 crore
items.quote: On the pharma, on the Coat Icon range, on the scale-up of the manufacturing of that particular product line, our outflow is expected to be between INR5 crores to INR12 crores.

items.statement: Capex for other new products expected between INR75-85 crore in first phase
items.quote: And with regards to our other new products, which we wish to introduce, the capex outflow is expected to be between INR75 crores to INR85 crores in the first phase.

items.statement: Most capex to be spent in FY27
items.quote: Most of it yes, most of which will be spent in FY27.

items.statement: High-margin value-added products currently 5% of portfolio, expected to reach 10-12% in FY27
items.quote: Currently, the contribution of the high-margin, high-value products in our total product portfolio mix is around 5% and increasing gradually. In the coming year 2026, '27, we expect it to go to around in the range of 10% to 12% or it may be higher also.

items.statement: Value-added products contribution expected to double in FY27 from FY26 levels
items.quote: And 2026, '27, we expect the contribution to double from what it was in '25, '26.

items.statement: Demand remains highly robust for FY27
items.quote: Now with regards to the outlook, which you have asked for '26, '27, the demand of the company remains highly robust.

items.statement: Customer inventory levels were 50% reduced during tariff period
items.quote: Yes. Of course, the inventory levels at the customer end was almost 50% reduced because of the tariffs.

items.statement: Expect demand improvement from geopolitically impacted markets as situation eases
items.quote: Once the geopolitical situation starts improving, you will see the demand for color also improving from these markets. And as such, we see good times, we are very confident of better performance going ahead as soon as the geopolitical scenario starts improving.

items.statement: US sales sustained at INR150-200 crore range despite tariff volatility
items.quote: The fact that we were able to sustain our sales in the U.S. market in such a volatile event is a matter of great satisfaction for us.

items.statement: Exports to US are 19% including Canada, not 44%
items.quote: And with regards to the percentage share of our exports into the U.S., the percentage is not 44%. Our exports to the U.S. are pegged at 19%. And that includes Canada also.

items.statement: US market has stabilized, more growth expected from other emerging markets
items.quote: More than U.S. U.S. has now stabilized . But more growth will come from the ot her markets which are right now severely impacted, which is doing worse at this time, only then you can be more hopeful of improvement

items.statement: US dependency will reduce over next 3-5 years, more sales from EM
items.quote: Certainly, yes. Certainly yes. We see more sales coming from EM. EM market is always something where there is sales growth in percentage points.

items.statement: Debtors turnover improved from 2.91% to 2.66%, inventory turnover improved from 4.99% to 4.70%
items.quote: Like I explained while I was going through the ratio analysis, the debtors turnover period has slightly reduced from 2.91% to 2.66% and the inventory turnover ratio has also reduced from 4.99% to 4.70%.

items.statement: Interest cost increased due to withdrawal of export finance subvention scheme from December 2025
items.quote: Just you might have seen the difference on the interest cost of the company, which is due to the subvention on export finance, which has been withdrawn by the Indian government as of December 2025.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity ratio very low at 0.28%
items.quote: Our debt-to-equity ratio remained very low at 0.28%, highlighting prudent fiscal management and disciplined capital allocation.

items.statement: Invested INR4.5-5 crore in analytical equipment for R&D facilities
items.quote: We have invested in excess of INR4.5 crores to INR5 crores only on the analytical equipment in these R&D facilities.

items.statement: R&D facilities have 60+ dedicated chemists including PhDs
items.quote: These have in excess of 60 dedicated chemists only working on R&D projects, right from developing in-house process, protocols to pilot plant production and then passing it to the plant for commercialization of these products.

items.statement: Revenue INR380 crore vs INR382.30 crore previous year
items.quote: During the year in question, the company reported a revenue of INR380 cr ores as against INR382.30 crores during the financial year '24 -'25

items.statement: EBITDA INR78 crore vs INR68 crore previous year, margin improved from 17.91% to 20.52%
items.quote: The EBITDA for year 2025-'26 stood at INR78 crores compared to INR68 crores in the previous financial year. Accordingly, the EBITDA margins improved from 17.91% to 20.52%.

items.statement: Net profit INR49.15 crore, up 10.80% YoY
items.quote: Profit before tax increased to INR65.97 crores as against INR60.16 crores in financial year '24-'25, while the net profit stood at INR49.15 crores, reflecting a year-on-year growth of 10.80%.

items.statement: ROCE improved to 20.90% from 20.17%, ROE increased to 14.94% from 14.92%
items.quote: Return on capital employed improved to 20.90% from 20.17% in the previous year, while return on equity increased to 14.94% as against 14.92% in the previous year.

items.statement: New product line at Dahej expected to generate INR125-150 crore sales at capex in first phase
items.quote: And in the first phase, we will hope to get about anywhere between INR125 crores to INR150 crores of sales at capex.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions impacting Iran, Bangladesh, Philippines markets
items.quote: Countries like Bangladesh have also been, for decades, a good market, which has again been disturbed since last 2 years. They don't have any money to buy food or rice or diesel, what they will buy color. So there are several such markets, wherein the economies are teetering right now.

items.statement: Order book at INR 1,628 crores as of March 31, 2026, providing visibility for close to 2 years of execution from continuing operations
items.quote: As of March 31, 2026, our order book stood at INR1,628 crores, which remains healthy and provides the visibility for close to 2 years of execution from continuing operations.

items.statement: Core orders intake grew 32% year-over-year in FY26, with revenue up 12% and 15% above budget for core services
items.quote: Core orders, the backbone have risen by 32% from FY24-25, with the revenue for the same period witnessed 12% upside and for this year 15% above the budget for the core services.

items.statement: Order backlog for core services alone increased around 40% year-over-year as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: I can tell you that order in hand for core services alone has increased by around 40% year-over-year.

items.statement: Expect 85% to 90% of March 31, 2026 order book to be executed in FY27
items.quote: So typically these are short cycle orders which gets complete within 12 months. So the order in hand that you see as on, say, 31st March 2026, expect around 85% to 90% of that to be executed in FY'26-'27.

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA margin at entity level was 11% for full year FY26 and 18% for Q4 FY26, excluding one-off items
items.quote: However, I'm happy to share that excluding the one-offs, your company delivered 11% EBITDA at the entity level in the current financial year, reflected solely by the operational performance.

items.statement: Underlying EBITDA margin base set at 11% for FY26, expected to be at par or better in future years
items.quote: So, I can safely say that the base is set and, you know, the efforts it should be, you know, at par if not more at least but at least at par for the for the future years.

items.statement: Full year FY26 revenue at INR 1,269 crores, up 21% year-over-year driven by core services (14% growth) and upgrades (24% growth)
items.quote: Revenue for the full financial year stood at INR 1,269 crores, which is up from INR 1,047 crores. This marks an impressive 21% increase driven by strong performance across Core Services and Upgrades, which grew by 14% and 24% respectively YoY.

items.statement: Received INR 343 crores from BHEL settlement in FY26, fully closing all obligations and claims between parties
items.quote: pursuant to the settlement agreement signed with BHEL earlier this year, the company has successfully received INR 343 crores in the financial year 25-26. With receipt of the above-stated amount, all the obligation from your company in respect to the projects covered under the settlement agreement stand closed, and both parties have fully released and discharged each other against any and all futu

items.statement: Surplus cash of INR 450 crores lent to group cash pool account at 5.5-6.35% yield, benchmarked to HSBC rates
items.quote: INR 450 crores loan that you see is a loan or lending to our cash pool account. Any surplus cash which we have, we either have two options, either to lent to cash pool or invest in FDs for the working capital surplus with the commercial bank.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR 7 per equity share (70% of face value) for FY26, highest in at least 10 years
items.quote: We are pleased to also announce that the board has recommended dividend payout of 70% of the face value, which is subject to the approval of the shareholders of the company at the ensuing Annual General Meeting.

items.statement: Durgapur manufacturing facility demerger to JSW Energy on track, targeting closure within calendar year 2026, definitely within 12 months from March 31, 2026
items.quote: The realistic timelines, well within 12 months is definitely there. The target is to close within this calendar year, that's the target, but I can say that within 12 months from, say, 31st March of 2026 is definitely the expectation.

items.statement: Five-year long-term service agreement signed with JSW Energy to secure manufacturing capacity for core services, with option to extend
items.quote: We have signed as part of the deal, we have signed a five-year contract with them, which can be extended as mutually convenient to both the parties.

items.statement: Target addressable market for core services estimated at INR 3,500-4,000 crores, with current market share around 18%
items.quote: Market size, it will be about INR3,500 crores to INR4,000 crores as a target market.

items.statement: Core services order intake grew 32% YoY in FY26, with 25% CAGR over four years since strategy launch in July 2024
items.quote: As a result of that, at least for this year growth Puneet mentioned 32% in core orders in particular, but also over four years, the CAGR is 25%.

items.statement: FGD mandate recalibrated: Category C (>50% of installed base, >200 GW) removed, Category B optional with no tariff pass-through, only Category A (~8 GW) mandatory
items.quote: However, post this notification, what has happened, category C, which is more than 50% of the install base that is more than 200 gigawatt, which was supposed to be like FGD ready by certain date. has been taken out.

items.statement: Strategy shift to asset-light, service-led model reducing fixed cost exposure; Durgapur demerger supports this transition
items.quote: This transition marks a significant shift towards an asset-light, service-led structure, reducing fixed cost exposure while ensuring continued access to manufacturing and the service capabilities through appropriate commercial arrangements.

items.statement: Expanded international presence across Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Australia, UAE, Malaysia, Indonesia, and Morocco during FY26
items.quote: During the year, we have expanded our presence across multiple international markets, including Saudi, Turkey, Australia, UAE, Malaysia, Indonesia and Morocco.

items.statement: Delivered 18 new first-of-kind products in services during FY26; automation and control business secured orders across domestic and international markets
items.quote: This year, we have had a pleasure of receiving orders for 18 new first-of-its-kind products, which is remarkable.

items.statement: Renewable energy growth poses potential threat to thermal services, but management notes thermal remains essential for grid stability and embedded energy needs
items.quote: On the threat side as the renewable is coming in, there could be a little bit of a slowness. But at the same time, let me give you a back-of-the-envelope calculation, Sunny. To even get a 100 gigawatt of renewable, you still require a 300 gigawatt of the embedded energy.

items.statement: Management committed to service-led strategy, focusing on disciplined execution, cash conversion, and profitability; CFO Aashish Ghai noted personal thanks to investors for support during turnaround
items.quote: I, on personal note, would also like to thank all our investors for their continued support and trust that you have shown in us during the last 2 years. Your trust motivates the management to drive the results and turnaround like the one we are witnessing in the company.

items.statement: Expects industry to grow at strong single-digit in FY27; TVS aims to grow ahead of industry
items.quote: See, we are expecting a good single-digit growth on the industry this year. And we are seeing good growth momentum.

items.statement: Demand strong across domestic and international for all models; confident of Q1 growth better than industry
items.quote: What is most important is our demand both in domestic and international for all our models are extremely good.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin at 13.1%, highest ever; aims to continue EBITDA margin improvement journey
items.quote: During the quarter, company's operating EBITDA was at INR 1,679 crores as against last year INR1,172 crores. Company registered a PBT of INR1,358 crores during this quarter as against INR851 crores in Q4 last year.

items.statement: TVS Credit book size grew 15% to INR 30,631 crores; disbursed loans to over 53 lakh new customers in FY26
items.quote: The book size is now INR 30,631 crores. Q4 TVS credit reported sustained growth in disbursements supported by improved consumption sentiment and traction across all retail financing segments.

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at around INR 3,500 crores including INR 1,000 crores+ for 1.5 million capacity addition and R&D expansion
items.quote: So all put together, the capex for next year for TVS Motor will be likely to be around INR3,500 crores.

items.statement: Adding 1.5 million units capacity to reach ~8.3 million in next 12 months; work started in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Immediately, we are looking at increasing the capacity by another 1.5 million, to go to somewhere around 8.3 million because the demand is good and first time we have to add significant capacity in the next 12 months.

items.statement: Commodity inflation 3-5% of revenue in Q1; passed on 35% of price increases; using mix, cost reduction and pricing to offset
items.quote: See the commodity, I think this is unprecedented. I think it is around 3% to 5% because as we speak, there are challenges, but we were able to increase prices 35% of the price increases we were able to offset by increasing prices.

items.statement: Scooter share at 38% including EV, targeting over 40%; strong premium/super-premium growth; economy segment challenged
items.quote: Fortunately for TVS we have, for example, currently SSP, including EV, the scooter category share is almost 38%. And according to me, that is likely to go over 40%, which means scooters are likely to grow faster.

items.statement: TVS Credit customer base near 2.4 crore; disbursed to 53 lakh new customers in FY26
items.quote: Overall, the customer base is almost 2.4 crores now. TVS Credit continues to focus on leveraging technology, innovation through digital transformation, deeper customer relationships and while maintaining strong risk management practices with external credit rating of AA+.

items.statement: Q4 international revenue INR 2,999 crores; FY26 exports 15.8 lakh units, up 33%; LatAm focus for next 2-3 years
items.quote: Q4, we're at almost INR3,000 crores -- INR2,999 crores. And spare parts, total spare parts is -- overall spare parts is about INR1,122 crores.

items.statement: EV 2-wheeler penetration rose to 7.8% in Q4 from 7.1% YoY; FY26 penetration 6.6% vs 6.2%
items.quote: Just to give you some data, the overall -- the penetration in Q4 was almost 7.8% vis-a-vis 7.1%. If you look at year as a whole, the penetration has moved from 6.2% to 6.6%.

items.statement: EV 2-wheeler monthly run rate moved from 30-32k to ~40k, targeting 50k/month soon
items.quote: Currently, we are doing about -- last year, if you look at our average was about 32,000. Around 30,000 to 32,000. We have now moved maybe around 40,000 and we will soon move to 50,000 per month.

items.statement: Joint development agreement with Hyundai Motor for electric 3-wheeler; Hyundai leads design, TVS co-develops using EV platform and 3W expertise
items.quote: TVS Motor has recently signed a joint development agreement with Hyundai Motor Company to commercialize an electric 3-wheeler. This is going to be redefining the mobility and as you know Hyundai Motor will lead the design and co-develop the EV 3-wheeler by leveraging its research and development expertise, advanced mobility technologies and human-centric design approach.

items.statement: Invested INR 2,400 crores in FY26 (mainly Norton, TVS Credit, Dubai infra); FY27 investments lower by INR 500-600 crores
items.quote: Next year, the investments will be much lower. It will be maybe another INR500 crores, INR600 crores lower than this INR 2,400 because we are very confident that many of the investments whatever we have made is going to start yielding better revenues and start getting results for us.

items.statement: Channel inventory improving after April supply issues; target 21-30 days stock; May production better than April

items.statement: Cautious on Q1-Q2 due to raw material availability, supply chain tier-2 disruptions, geopolitical logistics delays (15% lead time increase)
items.quote: The uncertainty is on raw material availability, timely availability, okay? The costs are high, but a couple of days delay here and there is one worry. Another worry which we are getting over completely is the supply chain tier 2 disruption, but that we are coming out of it fully.

items.statement: Tier-2 supplier labor challenges across India; supporting suppliers; situation improving in May
items.quote: Second, across India, we are seeing some challenges with respect to labor. It is not only unique to South, but many, many areas, especially the Tier 2 suppliers.

items.statement: TVS Credit portfolio quality improved with reduction in total credit cost and GNPA; external rating AA+
items.quote: Overall, the portfolio quality has improved through reduction in total credit cost and GNPA. Financial year 2026, the TVS Credit disbursed loans to over 53 lakh new customers.
