items.statement: Focus on Gujarat as white space for organised retail; no pan-India chain has penetrated Gujarat deeply; targeting 4 key cities (Ahmedabad, Surat, Rajkot, Baroda) first
items.quote: Just take out the data from any stats and maybe all the pan-India you can take it out. Apart from one player, there is no other player who has penetrated the Gujarat market or been successful.

items.statement: Trade receivables spiked to INR56 cr in March due to IIJS Tritiya exhibition and early Akshay Tritiya; now back to normal; wholesale debtor days ~30 days
items.quote: 24th of March, there was an exhibition in Bangalore, IIJS Tritiya. And, of course, because of exhibitions, there was a spike in sales. That's it. Akshay Tritiya this year came in a little early if you understand, from 30th of April 2025 to 19th April 2026. Hence, that last 10 days of March were a little bit of -- there was a little bit spike in sales, and the debtors. Now it has come down again to

items.statement: Target debt-to-equity 1:1 to 1.5:1; peak debt for 4 new stores seen at ~1.2x equity this fiscal; no equity dilution planned
items.quote: We want to stay -- we want to keep the debt levels at 1:1 ratio ideally or 1:1 point, maybe leverage to 1.4, 1.5. But generally, right now, I think for these 4 showrooms, it will be around 1:1.2 at peak debt, at least for this fiscal year that I am understanding.

items.statement: Recent customs duty hike and advance authorisation changes on gold imports; impact uncertain, will monitor consumer reaction for 1-2 months; not seen as discouraging yet
items.quote: So see, these are very immediate events or it has just been a few days that these all things are happening. And generally, we would take some time, let's say, a week or 2, in fact, a little bit more to understand what -- how the market and the consumers are reacting.

items.statement: PM's appeal to avoid gold purchases for a year may dampen daily wear demand but occasion/bridal demand expected to hold; exchange share may rise to 50-60%
items.quote: I don't think so things are going to really -- let's -- see, again, what you're telling me about -- what you're asking me is about strategy and what we are seeing is that there is a huge market, there is a new market that we are exploring. And -- we are in this game for a very long term. And hence, these kind of things will come.

items.statement: Inventory gain from gold price rise estimated at INR10-12 cr for FY26 (not finalised); interest cost would have been ~INR8 cr higher if GML used
items.quote: But I think assuming that around INR10 crores to INR12 crores or INR10 crores to INR11 crores or INR12 crores should be an inventory gain number. That is what we are anticipating on the -- I mean, if gold prices were not to increase, I think somewhere around INR40 crores, INR45 crores should be the

items.statement: No material competition from Shringar in antique bridal segment; unorganised sector price gap exists but brand trust protects organised players
items.quote: Not really. I mean, seeing there -- I think they are coming into a plain gold segment of wedding jewellery. We are into an antique segment of wedding jewellery. So as such, there is no competition.

items.statement: 280+ professionals and 200 skilled artisans; no management changes mentioned
items.quote: We have a state -of-the-art manufacturing facility equipped with advanced casting laser, 3D printing technologies supported by 280 -plus professionals and 200 skilled artisans.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY28 guidance of US$400 million organic revenue with around 40% EBITDA margins
items.quote: we're also using the opportunity today to reaffirm our long-term guidance of FY '28, which is a US$400 million of organic revenue with around 40% of EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Reiterated FY28 guidance of US$400 million revenue and 40% EBITDA margin
items.quote: we are confident of a strong FY '27 and also reiterate our FY '28 guidance of US$ 400 million revenue and 40% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Q4 revenues at almost US$48 million, up almost 47% from previous quarter
items.quote: the Q4 has really marked a strong recovery in line with what we had anticipated, in line with what we had mentioned, with the revenues at almost US$48 million, up almost 47% from the previous quarter.

items.statement: Customer base holds almost two-thirds of Indian market share by value of generic Semaglutide market as of end of April
items.quote: our customer base total as on end of April holds almost two-thirds of the Indian market share by value of the generic market, as it is further improving.

items.statement: First and only CDMO partner for first three generic Semaglutide approvals in highly regulated markets US and Canada
items.quote: We are the first and the only CDMO partner for the first three generic Semaglutide approvals in all the highly regulated markets, US and Canada.

items.statement: Strong visibility on commercial ramp-up throughout FY27 with multiple customers due for approvals across emerging markets
items.quote: with multiple other customers who are due to get approval across various emerging markets, we see a really strong visibility on the commercial ramp-up throughout FY '27.

items.statement: Second DDC line installed and undergoing qualification, expected to be available for commercialization in next quarter (Q1 FY27)
items.quote: the new line which has been installed already a couple of months back is currently undergoing qualification and will be due for availability for commercialization in the next quarter.

items.statement: Third DDC line to be added by end of FY27, bringing total to three lines
items.quote: by end of the year, we will have three lines installed.

items.statement: Biologics funnel expanded almost 4x versus previous year; added European biosimilar partner, US biosimilar major, second project from top three global animal health company
items.quote: In fact, in this year, we have expanded the funnel almost 4x versus previous year. And during the year, we saw a European biosimilar partner getting added, a US biosimilar major coming on board, and we also secured the second project from one of the top three global animal health companies.

items.statement: Biologics commercial manufacturing expected FY29 onwards; meaningful contribution expected in FY28
items.quote: the real kicker is once the commercial manufacturing starts for biologics, which is I would say still beyond the current time horizon which we are looking at FY28. We see the commercial manufacturing happening '29 onwards. However, the contribution from biologics will already be meaningful in FY28.

items.statement: Signed 10 new licenses, licensing and CDMO deals; launched 15-plus products in injectables and soft gelatin base business
items.quote: whether in terms of the 10 new licenses we signed, licensing and CDMO deals, we launched 15-plus products, really added customers which together with our expanding capabilities in our SPD site, we will really be deepening meaningfully our specialty injectable offering.

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA INR919 million, more than 5x sequentially with margin expanding 1,550 basis points quarter-over-quarter
items.quote: the Q4 EBITDA reported was INR919 million, which is more than 5x sequentially and the margin expanding by 1,550 basis points quarter-over-quarter, reflecting a strong operating leverage on our higher CSA revenues.

items.statement: Full year FY26 EBITDA declined about 35% due to delayed Semaglutide approvals
items.quote: For the full year, the EBITDA declined about 35% due to delayed Semaglutide approvals which weighed in on our second half of the results.

items.statement: Elevated inventory levels (INR440 crores vs INR158 crores) fully funded by customers and fungible; no risk carried
items.quote: these inventories are part of our entire production process. So these purchases are fully funded by our customers and fungible. So precisely that is the inventory that we are carrying. There is really no risk that we carry on our inventories that we are carrying.

items.statement: Customer advances at similar levels to previous quarter (INR250 crores)
items.quote: the number would likely be at almost the similar levels. There's not significant change on that number.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing trending below 9%, 210 bps lower than prior year after four notch upgrades since listing
items.quote: we've had four notch upgrades during the course of this year ever since we got listed last year. And these four notch upgrades are helping us repeatedly take our overall cost of borrowing down. We are trending below 9% today, which is 210 bps lower than what it was in the prior year.

items.statement: US$100 million capex for capacity expansion fully funded through incremental borrowings from domestic and international banking relationships
items.quote: All our capacity expansions that Arun and Neeraj talked about are fully funded through incremental borrowings, both from domestic and international banking relationships that we have.

items.statement: Successfully completed 49 regulatory and customer audits including surprise FDA inspections at two sites (EIRs received); renewed EU GMP certification at flagship and sterile injectable sites; received ANVISA approval
items.quote: We saw the year successfully completing 49 regulatory and customer audits, and these include who's who. In fact, we had surprise FDA inspection during the year at two of our sites, and we completed both successfully getting the EIRs. We have renewed our EU GMP certification both at our flagship site as well as our sterile injectable site. We had ANVISA approval coming through the year.

items.statement: Added almost 400 people at flagship site; expanded front-end US operations and quality teams
items.quote: We have our flagship site where thanks to all the expansion project, we have added almost 400 people, which is where the bulk of our growth is going to be coming. We have also expanded and deepened the strength of our other organization, whether it is in front-end in the US or whether it is in operations and in quality.

items.statement: Expect 50%+ ROCE in medium term
items.quote: We expect to scale meaningfully, building towards the 50% plus ROCE expectation that we have for ourselves during the medium term.

items.statement: Demand-supply gap for Semaglutide expected to persist for next 2 years with robust demand and supply constraints
items.quote: the demand-supply gap will continue to be there at least for next 2 years. So -- while I cannot forecast the future, but I can tell you certainly over a next 2 year period, there will be a challenge more -- I mean, demand will be robust and the gap will be more from supply than the demand.

items.statement: CDMO terms are ex-works; any tariff impact (e.g., Brazil 28% duty) borne by customers
items.quote: as a CDMO, all our terms with our customers are ex-works. So really, any impact of whether it's a tariff or otherwise will actually be to the customers to really be taking over.

items.statement: Customers securing capacity via reservation with upfront fees and take-or-pay contracts
items.quote: customers have done capacity reservation with us. And that capacity reservation includes blocking capacity and submitting to pick up that capacity both by paying upfront fee as well as take-or-pay kind of contract.

items.statement: Brazil is largest Semaglutide market outside North America per IQVIA; significant opportunity in Turkey, Saudi Arabia, Southeast Asia, LatAm
items.quote: Brazil today, if you look at IQVIA, Brazil is the largest market outside of North America for Semaglutide, right? So it's a very -- it's a large country, significant population, and a country which is very focused on weight reduction. So it is going to be a very significant market.

items.statement: Oral Semaglutide expected to capture 25-33% of total market; injectables to remain overwhelming majority
items.quote: we don't expect the orals to be taking about anywhere between 25% to maybe a third of the total market. So the market will overwhelmingly stay as injectable.

items.statement: Management will not slow down store expansion despite macro challenges
items.quote: We will continue. We will not slow down our expansion at all because we are very excited about the long-term consumption story in this country and it is our hope and belief that these issues are not permanent in nature and they will go away.

items.statement: Opened 105 stores in FY26, added 77 new cities, total 795 stores in 535 cities
items.quote: We opened 25 stores during quarter 4 and 105 stores during the full year. In full year '26, we added 77 new cities to our network, in line with our agenda of deeper penetration into India. This takes the total store count to 795 as of March '26, and we are now present in 535 cities across the country.

items.statement: Will maintain at least 40% discount vs leader brands on private labels; price increases selective, not on opening price points
items.quote: Our discount vis-a-vis the market leaders on private brands will at least remain the same. That will be our endeavour. So currently, if there is a price discount of 40% vis-a-vis the leader brand, even if we have to tinker with pricing, we will ensure that the discount will at least be 40%, and if possible, obviously, it will be our endeavour to make it more.

items.statement: Fabric prices rising 10-11% currently; petroleum derivative inputs seeing inflation
items.quote: I can give you a general range of what we are experiencing as of today. So, the fabric prices are goin g up at about 10% to 11%. And yes, that is what we are experiencing every day now, at this moment

items.statement: Private brands 74.1% of revenue (+100bps YoY); 2 brands >INR 1,000 cr, 6 brands >INR 500 cr
items.quote: Our private brands contribute 74.1% to our revenue in full year '26, which is a 100-bps improvement year-on-year. Two of our private brands are now INR 1,000 crores plus in revenue, and another 6 private brands are INR 500 crores plus in revenue.

items.statement: FY26 SSSG 11%: 7% from new customers, 2% from existing buying more, 2% from premiumization
items.quote: So of that 11%, 7% has come because of new customers and new transactions in our store. 2% has come because our existing customers have bought more number of things. And the balance 2% has come because our customers have bought a higher price point.

items.statement: Quick commerce expanded to 745 stores across 505 cities; 1.3 crore registered users
items.quote: Our quick commerce operation expanded to 745 stores across 505 cities in the country, and our registered users on quick commerce grew to 1.3 crores people.

items.statement: Healthy balance sheet with significant cash; deploying cash for growth initiatives
items.quote: We have a very healthy balance sheet with a significant amount of cash, which, as you can see, we are deploying for all growth initiatives.

items.statement: Dividend policy decision rests with Board; management cannot express independent view
items.quote: So Percy, your observation is absolutely valid. We have a very healthy balance sheet with a significant amount of cash, which, as you can see, we are deploying for all growth initiatives. But to comment on this, I will have to rely on my Board, because I cannot express any view independent of the Board, on this matter.

items.statement: New marketing campaign viewed 1.6 billion times on Instagram; 300 million+ unique viewers
items.quote: Our new campaign has now been seen 1.6 billion times on Instagram, which makes it among top 10 campaigns on Instagram ever. And there are 300 m illion-plus unique viewers of our total population, which is on Instagram, which would be less than 1 billion, I suppose

items.statement: Small format stores deliver same store EBITDA, revenue per sq ft, and ROCE as large format
items.quote: Specifically, I can confirm to you that the small format stores, which are going deeper, they are delivering the same level of store EBITDA. And their revenue per square foot, not the absolute, per square foot is also similar to our stores in larger towns. And finally, our return on capital employed is also similar.

items.statement: Targets 40-42% revenue CAGR for next 4-5 years
items.quote: I feel that this growth momentum should continue next five, six years, and we should be able to grow at around 40%, 42% for next four or five years minimum.

items.statement: Expects to maintain 24-25% EBITDA margin in FY27 with expansion from FY28
items.quote: We this year also we should be able to maintain around 24%, 25% EBITDA. This year we will be increasing some expenses on the new factory also. But from next year onwards, we will see gradual increase in the profitability.

items.statement: Targets INR360-400 crore revenue for FY27
items.quote: Between INR360 crores to INR400 crores is our target to invoice this year.

items.statement: Targets INR500+ crore order booking in FY27
items.quote: We have a target to book at least INR500 plus crores order this year also.

items.statement: Targets 20%+ export revenue share in 2-3 years
items.quote: Our target would be that eventually in next two to three years, we at least do 20% plus from exports.

items.statement: Sukrut Electric targets INR150-160 crore revenue in 4-5 years
items.quote: Sukrut, we assume that in next four to five years, we should be able to cross at least INR150 to INR160 crores of revenue.

items.statement: Greenfield capex INR153 crore, INR80 crore spent, balance in 2-3 months
items.quote: Close to INR80 crores is already done and balance is now getting done in next two or three months.

items.statement: Fundraise of INR100-110 crore planned for 550kV capacity, testing infra, brownfield expansion, working capital
items.quote: Around INR100 to INR110 is what we are eyeing. And that will be mainly for the capex for the increased production range up till 550 kV and the testing infrastructure.

items.statement: Current capacity 9,000-10,000 bushings, 75-80% utilized in FY26
items.quote: Our present capacity of 9,000 to 10,000 bushing, we have been able to produce 7,000 plus bushing this year. That's the reason I mentioned around 75% we have been able to utilize.

items.statement: Greenfield adds 5,000-7,000 RIP/RIS units annually, total capacity ~15,000 bushings
items.quote: The new facility is expected to add approximately 5,000 to 7,000 units of annual capacity, focused on high-value RIP, RIS products with gradual ramp-up over the next few years.

items.statement: Greenfield trial production by end Q2 FY27, commercial production by H2 FY27
items.quote: Trial production remains on track, with commercial production targeted in H2 of this ongoing year.

items.statement: Order book INR400+ crore as of March 31, 2026, visibility 1-2 years
items.quote: Our order book as on 31st March '26 stood at INR400 plus crores, reflecting our very strong customer confidence and robust demand visibility.

items.statement: Order book mix: 15-18% OIP/high current, balance RIP
items.quote: Sir, the order booking is of the almost same proportion as of what we have been invoicing. Okay. So, close to 15% to 18% is combination of OIP and high current and balance is of RIP.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin 25.7%, up 260bps YoY from scale, price recovery, hedging, export/retrofit mix
items.quote: EBITDA margins stood at 25.7% compared to 23.1% in FY25, a growth of almost 260 basis points. This reflects our continuous focus on maintaining margin discipline even during a phase of accelerated growth and expansion.

items.statement: RIP localization and exports to drive margin expansion from FY28
items.quote: From next year onwards, we will see gradual increase in the profitability and reduce our import dependency, our margin expansion should begin.

items.statement: Pass-through arrangements with customers for commodity, currency, supplier price changes
items.quote: There is an arrangement with the customer that we would also be transferring that price rise to them. And they are able to give it to us.

items.statement: FY26 volume ~7,200 bushings, roughly half RIP, half OIP/HCP
items.quote: It is, it is almost half-half. Around 3,500, 3,600 for both.

items.statement: Greenfield will produce dry RIP bushings up to 550kV, distinct from existing OIP facility
items.quote: So, this will be dry bushings which will be made in this factory. And in the present factory, we have oil-impregnated bushing. This will be resin-impregnated bushing.

items.statement: Transformer OEMs giving 24-36 month blanket orders with scheduled deliveries
items.quote: Today the situation is the transformer companies are giving us blanket orders for the next 24 to 36 months and they want us to prepare our side for those all delivery execution.

items.statement: Retrofit revenue ~6-7% of total, high margin, growing with international reach
items.quote: So, I understand it should be close to 6% or 7% of our overall revenue. And we see that gradually it will keep on increasing the way we are expanding our reach.

items.statement: Four Indian players (incl. CG Power, Hitachi, MIM) investing in localized RIP capacity
items.quote: No, there are three or four players in India who are putting up facility for localized RIP. Apart from us, CG Power, Hitachi India, and MIM, in Bhiwadi, Massa Izolyator Mehru, the Russian subsidiary in India.

items.statement: Chinese bushings not restricted in India; Indian pricing, availability, service preferred
items.quote: Chinese bushings are never restricted in India since last 6 years, 7 years. There is always an option available with an Indian buyer to buy bushings from China and they have not been doing.

items.statement: Currency hedging executed well, limited FX impact on margins
items.quote: And we also did our currency hedging very correctly, so then we were not too much impacted by the fluctuations.

items.statement: Working capital requirement INR28-30 crore, may be funded from raise
items.quote: And also we have a working capital around the INR28 crores or INR30 crores, which we might remain open with an option to close it from the raised funds.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity 0.17x, near debt-free, prefers equity over debt
items.quote: Our debt-to-equity ratio stands at a comfortable 0.17 times, a testament to our disciplined capital management and the inherent financial strength of the business.

items.statement: Sukrut acquisition closed, revenue INR25-26 crore in FY26, targeting 5-6x growth
items.quote: The Sukrut acquisition closed during the year. Our focus is now on operational stabilization, professionalization, and value creation.

items.statement: Supply chain and talent retention are key scaling constraints
items.quote: Supply chain and people.

items.statement: Cyber incident under investigation, loss already expensed in P&L
items.quote: We have filed a police complaint and there is an investigation which is happening. And it will only be revealed after the investigation is over whether we are able to recover or not.

items.statement: Bushing cost ~5% of transformer revenue; 7 bushings per transformer (3 LV, 3 HV, 1 neutral)
items.quote: Approximately 5% of the transformer revenue is a bushing cost. And every transformer will need three bushings on the LV side, three bushings on the high voltage side, and a neutral bushing.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guided at 30-40% and PAT growth at 50-60%
items.quote: For FY27, our initial outlook indicates revenue growth of approximately 30% to 40% and PAT growth of about 50% to 60%.

items.statement: FY27 blended EBITDA margin guided at 29-31%
items.quote: I feel blended where we have guided 29% to 31% of the EBITDA margin, which will probably will see in in coming quarters as Apnar will start giving us about the revenue that we anticipate

items.statement: 51 approved ANDAs covering 150+ strengths as of March 2026, up from 22 in March 2025
items.quote: As of March 2026, we had a portfolio of 51 approved ANDAs collectively covering more than 150 product strengths. Over the past year, our approved ANDA portfolio has more than doubled, increasing from 22 ANDAs in March '25 to 51 in March '26.

items.statement: 30 approved ANDAs covering 100+ strengths to be launched over next few quarters
items.quote: Out of the approved product portfolio, 20 ANDAs have already been commercially launched, while an additional 30 approved ANDAs covering over 100 strengths will be launched over the next few quarters.

items.statement: 27 molecules with 60+ strengths under development for next 24 months visibility
items.quote: Beyond our approved product portfolio, we currently have about 27 molecules involving more than 60 strengths under various stages of development. This broad and differentiated product pipeline provides strong visibility for growth over the next 24 months.

items.statement: Acquired 75% stake in Apnar Pharma with USFDA-approved facility; remaining 25% by end of 2026
items.quote: We acquired 75% stake in Apnar Pharma in Q4FY26, with the remaining 25% is expected by end of this year. The plant acquisition with its USFDA-approved manufacturing facility provides significant strategic advantages.

items.statement: Apnar facility targeted INR180-200 crores revenue in 2-3 years
items.quote: In two to three-year timeframe, we feel we should be able to do about INR180 crores to INR200 crores revenue from the Apnar facility.

items.statement: Emerging markets EBITDA margin 18-19% in Q4FY26; expected to sustain at 20-21% in FY27
items.quote: As I stated in my opening remarks, last quarter our EBITDA margin stood at about 18% to 19% on emerging market. As we add another INR10 crores, INR20 crore, INR30 crores, INR40 crores of revenue as we move forward, I think the margin will sustain at 18%, 19%, maybe add another 100 basis points to 200 basis points. So may can settle at about 20%, 21% on EBITDA.

items.statement: Emerging markets per unit realization improved from INR1.20 to INR1.90 (60-70% jump)
items.quote: Just to give you a little more perspective, when we started, I mean, probably about one year, 1.5 back, our per unit realization on emerging market capacity was about INR1.20 paisa, which we are already about INR1.90 paisa. So, you can see there is a significant jump of about 60%, 70% jump realization with the same capacity that we have now on the emerging market unit matrix.

items.statement: Amerisyn JV budgeted INR50-100 crores revenue in FY27 with ~40% EBITDA margin
items.quote: We feel this year, probably we'll do about INR80 crores to INR100 crores of revenue from that JV, maybe a little conservatively, maybe INR50 crores to INR70 crores. That's what has been budgeted between say INR70 crores, INR80-odd crores on an average basis. We feel we'll be able to achieve that with decent profitability. Profitability, which will be almost an average of what our US EBITDA busines

items.statement: Net working capital 187 days in FY26 vs 114 days FY25; ex-Apnar ~104 days; Apnar sales to normalize from FY27
items.quote: We have had the Apnar thing coming in the last quarter. So, the working capital has shown that jump, while sales have not come in from Apnar. So, that has inflated our working capital. If we take out Apnar, it is around 104 days, the net working capital cycle.

items.statement: INR100 crores unutilized IPO funds for sterile manufacturing; deployment starting FY27
items.quote: So that INR100-odd crores of IPO fund is for a specific purpose that is already been given in our DRHP. So, we plan to start the operations for that particular purpose within this year. So, I think part of it will be utilized this year, subsequently going forward for the next couple of years in terms of the development of our sterile manufacturing.

items.statement: CDMO-CMO ~47-48% of regulated revenue; own products ~50-53%; mix expected to continue
items.quote: I think CDMO and own product are almost the same, which we continue continue to do around 50% to 53% of our own product, and 47%, 48% of CDMO-CMO taken together. And we expect it to continue on the same line, 2% or 3% here and there.

items.statement: US business target INR2,500-3,000 crores in 3-4 years; total accessible market ~$1B for approved products
items.quote: As a company, we are building at least INR2,500 crores to INR3,000 crores of revenue just coming out of the US in the next three to four years' timeframe. So, everything that we aspire to be become about INR3,000 crores to INR4,000 crores revenue from the US as we speak.

items.statement: Effective tax rate ~23% long-term (up from 17% in FY25 due to US profits and Apnar)
items.quote: Drastic jump is because of US taxation and Indian taxation are at 26%. The US is at 20%, 21%. So, since we have started earning in Apnar trade, there's a tax provision on Apnar trade, which is being affected. So, overall, 21% to 23% rate is going to be a long-term thing

items.statement: Guidance conservative due to geopolitical/macro uncertainties (shipping, US inflation); may revise after 1-2 quarters
items.quote: As we speak, there are a lot of moving parts in terms of external environment, which is not very conducive, shipping lines, everything, overall atmosphere, even in US in terms of inflationary pressures, etcetera. So we have decided to be a little conservative. Let us wait for one or two quarters. Let us see how things settle in the world.

items.statement: PIC/S approval for emerging markets facility expected by June-July 2026 for mid-tier markets (South Africa, Vietnam)
items.quote: We are also in the process of obtaining PIC/S approval for our emerging market facility by June, July of this year. This approval will enable us to make our footprint in key mid-tier markets, some of them in countries like South Africa, Vietnam, and so on and so forth.

items.statement: Expects compound AUM growth of 30-35% annually over medium term
items.quote: we expect a compound growth of AUM at around 30% to 35% annually over the medium terms.

items.statement: Expects PAT growth of 40-45% in current year
items.quote: we believe profitability growth can remain stronger with PAT expected growth at around 40% to 45% in current year.

items.statement: AUM reached INR 1,626 crores as of March 2026, up 27% YoY
items.quote: Our asset under management increased to INR1,626 crores as of March '26, reflecting a strong year -on-year growth of over 27%.

items.statement: On-book AUM stood at approximately INR 1,519 crores
items.quote: Our on -book AUM stood to approximately INR1,519 crores, demonstrating healthy organic growth across our core operating markets.

items.statement: Disbursements during FY26 were INR 821 crores
items.quote: Disbursement during the year stood at INR821 crores, while our customer base expanded to more than 42,800 customers.

items.statement: Branch network increased to 176 branches across six states
items.quote: At the same time, our branch network increased to 176 branches across six states, reflecting our continued investment towards strengthening distribution reach.

items.statement: Net interest income increased 39% YoY to INR 161 crores
items.quote: Our net interest income for financial year '26 increased by nearly 39% year -on-year to INR161 crores.

items.statement: PAT increased over 38% to INR 49.7 crores
items.quote: Profit after tax for financial year '26 increased by over 38% to INR49.7 crores despite continued investment towards branch expansion.

items.statement: ROA at 3.08% and ROE at approximately 13.7%
items.quote: Our profitability metrics also remained healthy during the year with return on assets at 3.08% and return on net worth at approximately 13.7%.

items.statement: Average cost of borrowing reduced to 10.8% from 11.48%
items.quote: Our average cost of borro wing reduced to 10.8% from 11.48% in financial '25.

items.statement: NIM expanded to 11.26%
items.quote: At the same time, NIM expanded to 11.26%, reflecting improving lender confidence, better pricing discipline, and gradual improvement in our funding profile.

items.statement: Incremental borrowing cost at 10.25-10.30%
items.quote: the incremental cost stood to around 10.25% to 10.30%.

items.statement: Expects further 20-25 bps reduction in borrowing cost
items.quote: I believe that we will be able to convert and translate into the rate of interest going forward by another I can say 20 to 25 bps on a minimum side.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded from Acuite A-/Positive to Acuite A/Stable
items.quote: Another important milestone during financial '26 was the upgrade in our external credit rating by Acuite Ratings from Acuite A-/Positive outlook to Acuite A/Stable outlook.

items.statement: Maintains relationships with over 40 lenders across banks, SFBs, NBFCs, and FIs
items.quote: Today, we maintain relationship with more than 40 lenders across public sector banks, private banks, small finance banks, NBFCs, and financial institutions.

items.statement: Net worth increased sharply to approximately INR 465 crores post-IPO

items.statement: IPO proceeds: ~25% of rental allocation deployed by FY26, remainder by H2 FY27; ~11% of manufacturing/rental expansion proceeds deployed, remainder in FY27.
items.quote: As a part of the rental business expansion strategy, we have already utilized approximately 25% of the IPO proceeds allocated towards building rental assets by FY26, while the remaining amount is expected to be utilized by the second half of FY27.

items.statement: High attrition at factory labor level (all on payroll, no contractors); admin/sales attrition much lower; 11 employees honored for 5-year tenure.
items.quote: The reason the calculated attrition is high is because we don't use contractors for labor; all factory laborers are on our own payroll. At the factory level, attrition is high, but at the administrative and sales levels, it is much lower.

items.statement: Rental yields: MS scaffolding 32-38% per annum, aluminum scaffolding 60-66% per annum; aluminum rental duration 4-5 months, steel ~1 year.
items.quote: In MS scaffolding, the yield varies from 32% to 38% per annum, and in aluminum rental, the yield is 60% to 66% per annum.

items.statement: Industrial safety gear (footwear) trading division deferred 3-4 months to focus on core priorities; will leverage 2,500 customer network.
items.quote: We have deferred that for about 3 or 4 months because we have many other things to handle currently. We plan to open a trading division for industrial safety products because we work with nearly 2,500 customers.

items.statement: TAN plant expected to reach 75-80% capacity utilization in FY27
items.quote: definitely that Mr. Narinder Goyal has promised me that by all means he will reach 75 %- 80%. That is his commitment to me. So, it is his commitment to me and I am sure that he will meet that

items.statement: TAN production estimated at 160,000-170,000 tons in FY27 assuming nine months operation
items.quote: So, let's assume that we have got about nine months production to be very conservative. So, we are saying that we have roughly about 1,60,000 - 1,70,000 tons of production would be possible.

items.statement: TAN budgeted price around Rs 37,000-38,000 per ton for revenue estimation
items.quote: A budgeted number normally for this is about Rs. 37,000, Rs. 38,000 a ton. That is the normal number that you might think about.

items.statement: Urea sales volume expected to exceed FY26 level of 3.4 million tons in FY27
items.quote: We are confident that we will do better than last year, but whether we will touch 35, is a touch and go here and there, but we will definitely exceed what we did this year.

items.statement: New urea plant (1.3 mtpa brownfield) estimated at Rs 9,500-10,000 crore, funding not a challenge
items.quote: The price is INR 9,500 crores to INR 10,000 crores. That is the upper bound as far as brownfield projects are concerned. Aman Kothari: For 1.4 million tons? Abhay Baijal: For 1.3 million tons, roughly the same. Now that you know the balance sheet of Chambal, I don't think there is much of a challenge in funding

items.statement: TAN project (240,000 mtpa) in commissioning phase; WNA dry run started, downstream commissioning underway
items.quote: Our technical ammonium nitrate project achieved significant progress during FY '26 and has now entered the commissioning phase. Dry run for the weak nitric acid plant has commenced and subsequent commissioning activities for downstream TAN, including AN Melt and HDAN products, are also underway.

items.statement: IMACID JV P2O5 capacity expansion from 5 to 7 lakh mt expected by December 2026; sulphuric acid expansion a year ahead in FY27
items.quote: The increase in P2O5 production capacity from 5 lakh metric tons to 7 lakh metric tons is expected to be implemented in December 26. Further, Sulphuric acid capacity is also being increased, which is expected to be implemented a year ahead in FY '27.

items.statement: Gadepan-1 urea plant undergoing longer shutdown till mid-June 2026
items.quote: We had to have two shutdowns. This was in the end of the year and then in the beginning of this year we are currently undergoing one shutdown for Gad epan-1, which is a slightly longer shutdown which will tend to be happening till about mid-June

items.statement: Complex fertilizer stocks covered till July-August 2026 due to strategic early purchases
items.quote: Secondly, as far as Chambal is concerned, we did make some strategic purchases, very big, early in the beginning of the year, and we are covered at least till July-August in terms of our stocks.

items.statement: TAN market buoyant with 6-7% underlying growth in explosives segment translating to ~70,000 tons annual demand increase
items.quote: I can say that there is an underlying growth of about 6% to 7% in the explosive segment. And, therefore, that translates back into Ammonium nitrate increase. It is about 6% to 7%. And it is a healthy growth, I would say, given that we are already at 1.2 million tons or so of demand.

items.statement: Urea business operates on cost-plus basis; higher gas costs passed through via increased subsidy, no margin impact
items.quote: So, if you understand this business, it is basically a cost-plus kind of business. So, government recognizes the cost and therefore, in terms of higher prices of gas, except for that impact on working capital, we are able to pass on the cost to the government in the form of subsidy, increased subsidy. So, it would not be a problem for us.

items.statement: Ammonia prices surged to $850-900/ton, sulphur to $900-950/ton in Q4 FY26; elevated LNG prices pressured import economics
items.quote: For instance, ammonia prices increased sharply to around $850 to $900 per ton while Sulphur prices also increased from $900 to $950 per ton. Elevated LNG prices further pressured import economics for the industry.

items.statement: Current gas cost around $18.5/mmBtu for Q1 FY27, similar to previous quarter
items.quote: Currently, what I understand, it is USD 18 plus, USD 18.5 plus. It may be around the same number.

items.statement: No buyback proposal on table currently
items.quote: There is no such proposal on the table as of now.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of Rs 6/share, total Rs 11/share for FY26
items.quote: Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of Rs. INR 6 per share, totaling to Rs. 11 per equity share for FY '26.

items.statement: Crop protection, chemicals & specialty nutrients revenue grew 27% YoY in FY26; launched 17 new products; 14 new crop protection + 1 specialty nutrient planned for FY27
items.quote: business delivered another year of strong growth during FY '26, driven by higher market penetration, expanding product portfolio and improved contribution from value- added offerings. Business continued to witness strong growth in both revenues and margins, with contribution increasing by around 27% Y-o-Y. During FY '26, we launched 17 new products, spanning herbicides, fungicides and insecticides

items.statement: Phosphatic fertilizer availability constrained by logistics (28-29 ships stuck at Hormuz); normalization expected in 3 months if route opens
items.quote: We have many ships, about 28 or 29 ships, which are stuck up in the Hormuz. They are carrying material. They are loaded up there and so on. So, it is more a question of logistics than production. That is firstly one thing to understand. That means, if we have an opening up of th is Hormuz in the next one month or so, even if we take a delayed adjustment, because the shipping takes some time to adj

items.statement: Urea energy consumption (GCal/ton) well below government norms across G-1, G-2, G-3 plants, generating energy gains
items.quote: Definitely below the government norms by a percentage, a good percentage. So, normally we do not reveal these numbers publicly, but we are well below the established norms. Therefore, a certain amount of energy gain does accrue to us.

items.statement: Urea sales volumes: G-1 2.67 lakh tons, G-2 1.52 lakh tons, G-3 2.53 lakh tons in Q4 FY26
items.value: 2.67 lakhs ton, 1.52 lakh ton, 2.53 lakhs ton
items.quote: Sales volume for the quarter, in the quarter, G-1 was 2.67 lakhs ton, G-2 is 1.52 lakh ton and G-3 is 2.53 lakhs ton.

items.statement: Urea inventory at 118,000 MT as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: It is about 1,18,000 MT around.

items.statement: Ammonia self-produced with 3-5% surplus; no raw material constraint for TAN
items.quote: This is basically ammonia. And ammonia is self-produced in our case because we have got three plants producing ammonia. And we have about 3 to 5% surplus on account of technical reasons. So, we don't see any shortfall coming from that side as far as TAN is concerned.

items.statement: Evaluating automotive-grade urea production (technical grade) with preliminary government discussions; requires policy approval for gas allocation
items.quote: No, it is definitely possible with our plants, at least one stream or two streams we can take out to do that. And we are, in fact, having some very preliminary discussions on this issue and we are telling the government also that you should allow us to do this technical-grade Urea for automotive purpose. But it is very nascent. I would not give a timeline on this. That depends on government policy

items.statement: Sales volume target for FY27 is 22 million tons, up from ~20 million tons in FY26
items.quote: Actually, sales volume last year, as I said, was around 20 million tons. So this year, we're expecting 22 million tons. That is the kind of target, 10% on Steel Authority of the higher side, we're keeping

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY27 is INR15,000 crores, rising to over INR20,000 crores in FY28
items.quote: Guidance for '26-'27 is INR15,000 crores. And since our expansion projects are ongoing in different, different plants. So in '27-'28, the capex figures will be in excess of INR20,000 crores.

items.statement: Expansion projects cleared for IISCO, Bokaro, and Bhilai steel plants with major packages tendered for IISCO
items.quote: So far as expansions are concerned, actually, we've cleared for 3 plants. One is IISCO Steel Plant, wherein major packages have already been tendered out and farmed up. So another one is Bokaro, and third one is Bhilai, which we're just clearing this now.

items.statement: Medium-term capex outlook: INR15,000 crores in FY27, INR18,000-19,000 crores in FY28, then INR20,000-25,000 crores annually as expansions ramp up
items.quote: In '26-'27, we'll spend around INR15,000 crores. In '27-'28, it can be around INR18,000 crores, INR19,000 crores. And after that, this will go towards every year almost INR20,000 crores to INR25,000 crores.

items.statement: IISCO expansion capex ~INR35,000 crores for 4.5 mt capacity; Bhilai ~INR30,000 crores for 3.5 mt; Bokaro ~INR18,000 crores for 3 mt
items.quote: capex of IISCO is around INR36,000 crores -- maybe INR35,000 crores. And Bhilai, which is yet to be announced is around INR30,000 crores, and Bokaro is somewhere around INR18,000 crores, something like that.

items.statement: Current crude steel capacity 21 million tons; targeting 22.5 million tons production in FY27 through debottlenecking and efficiency gains
items.quote: Our capacity is 21 million tons, and we are targeting to produce 22 million tons. I think it is 22.5 million tons so far as our target is concerned for '26-'27

items.statement: New capacity from expansions at IISCO, Bokaro, Bhilai to come online after 3 years, i.e., from FY31
items.quote: New capacity will start coming after 3 years from now, means from '30-'31.

items.statement: Domestic demand steady on demand and price fronts; Q1 typically muted with destocking, pickup from Q3 onwards
items.quote: Generally, demand remains muted in quarter 1 and quarter 2, as all of us have seen, on the back of more sales in quarter 4. So there are events of destocking in quarter 1, which is taking place and this time also it is there.

items.statement: Margins expected to improve further in FY27 supported by firm steel prices, rupee depreciation, and cost reduction actions
items.quote: With the coal price remaining in range bound -- coal prices remaining on the higher side range bound actually, we hope that the margins will continue to improve further.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 NSR: longs INR53,400/t, flats INR51,000/t; April NSR: longs INR57,600/t, flats INR56,700/t; May NSR similar to April
items.quote: In quarter 4, NSR of -- average NSR of long products was INR53,400 and flat was INR51,000. When we compare this with April, NSR of long products is INR57,600 and NSR of flat is INR56,700.

items.statement: Blended NSR Q4 FY26 INR52,000/t; April-May ~INR57,000/t
items.quote: Blended NSR for the quarter 4 is INR52,000 per ton. And in April, it is around INR57,000 per ton, April and May.

items.statement: Coking coal procurement cost: Q4 avg INR18,200/t; April INR21,000/t; May INR21,800/t; consumption impact blended with 30-day stock
items.quote: Coking coal, when we look at actually in quarter 4, the coking coal average price is INR18,200, which has gone up in April and May. April average price is INR21,000 and May average price is INR21,800.

items.statement: Fluxes/limestone CFR cost from Dubai rising from $23-24 to ~$35; impact on saleable steel only INR100-200/t; securing supply via diverted routes
items.quote: so far as Steel Authority is concerned, we will have some impact with respect to the fluxes, limestone, etcetera, which we are buying from Dubai. So there, the landed cost, the CF R cost is going to go up, because it was around, say, $23, $24, now it will be around $35

items.statement: Fuel constraints in Q4 resolved by using PNG and creating LPG banks; not a major challenge for Q1
items.quote: So fuel concern was there in quarter 4, but we have come out of it by using PNG in certain locations and creating LPG banks in other locations. So that's not going to be a major challenge for us in quarter 1.

items.statement: Targeting zero inventory increase in Q1 FY27; Q2 challenging; inventory reduction in Q3-Q4
items.quote: we are personally looking at no increase in inventory during quarter 1, but that is a wish list. It again depends on the market conditions and Steel Authority of geopolitical situations. We are looking at zero-zero in quarter

items.statement: Debt reduced by INR3,200 crores in Q4 FY26 and INR8,150 crores in FY26; borrowing cost fell from 7.3% to 6.2%; net debt/equity 0.37, targeting further reduction in FY27
items.quote: The borrowings have also come down by around INR8,150 crores in FY '25-'26, which has given sterling advantages in terms of finance cost to us. Even the cost of borrowings has also come down from a level of 7.3% in the previous year to 6.2% this year.

items.statement: Capex funding priority from internal accruals; incremental debt only if needed; net debt/equity at 0.37 with room for future capex
items.quote: Our net debt to equity right now is around 0.3 3, how much? Right now it is 0.37. And as you said, in this year, we are trying to improve our profitability by various actions and debt level should not increase in this year.

items.statement: Employee count down to 49,752 as of Apr 1, 2026 from 53,159; targeting further reduction of 3,400-3,500 per year for next 2 years plus VRS of 500-1,000; pay revision from Jan 2027 pending guidelines
items.quote: So as on 1st April 2026, the numbers are 49,752 as compared to 53,159 opening of this year. So a reduction of around 3,400 numbers. So this is giving us advantage in terms of salary wages numbers.

items.statement: Employee cost INR11,392 crores in FY26, down INR200-300 crores YoY; expected to decline further in FY27 despite VRS impact
items.quote: In '25-'26, it is actually INR11,392 crores, it has come down. I'm expecting that it will further come down in '26-'27 despite having VRS impact also, because the overall strength will come down by 3,000-odd.

items.statement: Coke rate reduced by ~20 kg/t over 2 years via higher PCI and oxygen injection; targeting further 20 kg/t reduction in FY27
items.quote: The reason is actually reduction in coke rate is because of increase in PCI as well as by increase in oxygen in the blast furnace s. So these are the 2 vices we are using, whereby we are trying to reduce the coke rate

items.statement: Blast furnace productivity improved by closing inefficient smaller furnaces and ramping up larger ones
items.quote: The reason is because of the operational efficiency in the furnaces as well as by closing down the inefficient furnaces and ramping up production from the bigg er furnaces. These are the 2 reasons

items.statement: Salem stainless steel plant: targeting CR mill yield improvement from 84% to 90%, switching LPG to PNG, cheaper power, and feeding imported slabs to utilize spare capacity
items.quote: So in CR mill, where the yield right now is only 84%, 83%, we are trying to increase it to 90%. We have taken a couple of other actions like replacing LPG with PNG, which has given quite good benefit.

items.statement: BISL (Bhadravati) on disinvestment list; awaiting government clearance before deciding on specialty steel plans
items.quote: BISL, right now, it is in that list of disinvestment. So we are looking at getting a comfort from the government. After that, we'll have some plan for specialty steel.

items.statement: Iron ore mine renewals not a major issue; Chiria mine new lease being pursued to enhance capacity; target iron ore production 56 mt in FY27, ramping to 80 mt
items.quote: We don't have major problems, risk to our mines, and the productions are going to go up, because last year we produced 38 million tons, while this year, we have kept a target of 56 million tons, out of which some quantity will be sold.

items.statement: Rail price revision for FY25 to be finalized in FY27; provisional prices currently lower; uncertain if positive or negative impact
items.quote: So far as '26-'27 is concerned, we can't say anything about whether we'll get an advantage from rail price revision or we'll get a negative on rail price revision. So things are not very clear at this point of time.

items.statement: Middle East geopolitical situation creating uncertainties for raw material movement and fuel via Strait of Hormuz
items.quote: the geopolitical situation in the Middle East has set the otherwise stabilizing e conomic scenario, again, bringing uncertainties and volatilities to all of

items.statement: Balance sheet clean of audit qualifications for first time in many years after addressing provisions and developments
items.quote: After a pretty long time, many years and decades, you can say, that the balance sheet of '25-'26 is totally clean from the qualifications. There are no qualifications in the balance sheet after a pretty long time.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 11% to 13% for the long run with EBITDA growth slightly ahead of revenue growth
items.quote: And we are guiding in the long run that we will continue to delive r low double-digit growth. Having said that, there will be quarters where if the pricing -- I mean, costs go up, pricing is much higher. There could be some change from -- there could be a variation from that. But I think we just want to make sure that we are guiding for the long run. And in the long run, we are guiding that we wil

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin at 20.2%, seventh consecutive quarter above 20%
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 20.2% with all regions within our guided operating range, marking the seventh consecutive quarter of 20% plus margins.

items.statement: Full year FY26 EBITDA margin improved 50 bps to 20.4%
items.quote: We have improved from 19.9% to 20.4%, right, which is a 50 basis point expansion in a year on an already high base.

items.statement: Full year FY26 EBIT margin expanded 50 bps to 12.3%
items.quote: Our revenue has grown at 13%. Our EBITDA has grown at 15.8%. EBIT has grown at 18% and EBIT has moved from 11.8% to 12.3%. So even in EBIT, we see 50 basis point expansion.

items.statement: Beauty & Cosmetics grew 30% YoY in Q4 FY26, fourth consecutive quarter above 20% growth
items.quote: The momentum was led by Beauty & Cosmetics, which delivered a record 30% year -on-year growth, aligned with our strategic focus on this segment.

items.statement: Oral Care grew 10% YoY in Q4 FY26 showing healthy recovery
items.quote: Oral Care also showed a healthy recovery, growing 10% year -on-year.

items.statement: All four regions delivered double-digit growth in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Growth during the quarter was broad-based wi th all 4 regions delivering double-digit performance.

items.statement: EAP grew 25% and Americas 24.1% in Q4 FY26 driven by Beauty & Cosmetics and new customers
items.quote: EAP and the Americas led the way, growing 25% and 24.1%, respectively, driven by a focused push in Beauty & Cosmetics, new customer additions and strong pipeline conversions.

items.statement: Europe grew 15.5%, AMESA 10.4%, India standalone 11.5% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Europe also delivered a robust performance, growing 15.5%. AMESA grew by 10.4%, w hile India stand-alone recorded a healthy 11.5% growth.

items.statement: FY26 capex of INR 480 crores-plus, driven by Beauty & Cosmetics investments ahead of curve
items.quote: If you look at our c apex for this year, we have spent INR 480 crores-plus, which reflects the investments that we are making in B&C.

items.statement: FY27 capex to remain slightly elevated to capture growth opportunities
items.quote: For FY '27, I think we will continue at a slightly elevated level of c apex because we are seeing the opportunity in the marketplace gain market share, and we will continue capturing that.

items.statement: Thailand plant set up in November, certification and validation ongoing, volumes to start in next couple of quarters and scale gradually
items.quote: FY27, we will start seeing volumes from Thailand in the next couple of quarters. And it will scale gradually.

items.statement: More than 50% of business under contractual pass-through arrangements covering landed cost plus power
items.quote: More than 50% of our business comes from contractual customers, where there is a clear agreement on pass-through. On the other customers, we've been very proactive by being in the market and making sure we are able to get price increases.

items.statement: Pass-through model covers raw material, logistics, currency and freight via landed cost plus power approach
items.quote: Our model right now is a landed cost plus power pass -through model. And therefore, it covers a lot of things which you've spoken about.

items.statement: Confident of recovering full cost impact from Middle East crisis with no lag even on non-contractual customers
items.quote: We are making sure that our price increase is proactive, and we do not have a lag. So we remain confident that the full cost will be recovered.

items.statement: Raw material availability secured till at least mid-July, expanding inventories weekly
items.quote: We've made sure that availability is adequately covered till at least at this point in time till middle of July, and we continue to increase that on a weekly basis.

items.statement: Net debt to EBITDA improved to 0.52x
items.quote: Strong EBITDA and PAT performance, combined with healthy cash flow generation have enabled a further deleveraging of our balance sheet with net debt to EBITDA improving to 0.52x.

items.statement: Proposed merger with Indovida announced, creating nearly $1 billion consumer packaging platform, margin and value accretive
items.quote: We announced our proposed merger with Indovida, a transformational move that will significantly enhance our scale and strengthen our position as a leading player in emerging markets. Together, the combined entity will create a nearly $1 billion consumer packaging platform with a broader product portfolio, stronger manufacturing and innovation capabilities and an expanded presence across high -grow

items.statement: Merger expected to complete by Q4 FY27, regulatory filings done for SEBI, CCI and antitrust approvals in multiple countries
items.quote: We are hopeful that we will have the approval within a year of us filing for it. But till such time, as per the regulation, we have to remain extremely careful that there is no sharing of information of any kind between the two companies because we remain independent companies till such time as we get approval.

items.statement: Actively seeking acquisitions in Beauty & Cosmetics for new geographies or capabilities, must be growth and margin accretive
items.quote: We are very actively looking for acquisitions. We've said this in the past that inorganic growth is a clear part of our strategy. Having said that, we always say that when we are looking for a new acquisition, it should get us either into a new geography or get us a new capability.

items.statement: No dividend declared due to merger; both companies cannot declare dividend until merger completed
items.quote: On the dividend, the di vidend is actually because of the merger. We are doing a share swap as per the proposed merger announcement. And both the companies cannot declare dividend till the merger is completed, which is common in these kind of mergers to ensure that the valuation construct remains.

items.statement: Dividend payout to resume post-merger completion as per Board guidance
items.quote: Basis what lawyers are guiding us, we believe that Q4 FY '27 is a fair timeline post which we will operate as a merged entity and then dividend payout will happen as per the Board guidance and approval.

items.statement: Personal Care and Beyond mix at 53%, Beauty & Cosmetics now larger than Oral Care in most key markets
items.quote: Our Personal Care and Beyond mix now stands at 53% and Beauty & Cosmetics is now larger than Oral Care in most key markets, marking a clear shift towards a more balanced and diversified po rtfolio.

items.statement: Sustainable tube formats contributed 38% of total sales
items.quote: During the quarter, sustainable tube formats contributed 38% of total sales, reflecting steady progress in customer adoption.

items.statement: Achieved EcoVadis Platinum rating, placing in top 1% globally on ESG performance
items.quote: We are also proud to have achieved the EcoVadis Platinum rating this year, placing us among the top 1% of companies globally on ESG performance.

items.statement: Certified as Great Place to Work across seven countries
items.quote: EPL was certified as a Great Place to Work across seven countries this year, a reflection of our consistent efforts to build an inclusive, engaging and high-performance workplace.

items.statement: Middle East crisis affecting availability and cost of key raw materials; managing with agility and financial discipline
items.quote: Looking ahead, let me first address the impact of current Middle East crisis on our business. The crisis has affected both the availability and cost of our key raw materials. We are proactively navigating the situation with a clear and structured approach.

items.statement: Consolidated order book at INR 83,004 crores as of 31 March 2026, up 16% YoY, highest ever, with book-to-bill ~4x across seven verticals
items.quote: Our consolidated order book as of 31st March '26, stood at INR 83,004 crores, which is about 16% increase over the last year, and highest in the company's history.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 order inflows totaled INR 31,884 crores; Q4 inflows were INR 9,573 crores
items.quote: The fourth quarter contributed INR9,573 crores of fresh consolidated inflows and full year inflows totaled INR31,884 crores.

items.statement: Management declined to give FY27 guidance for revenue, margin, order inflow, capex, working capital or net debt, citing too many variables and uncertainty; will revisit after Q1 FY27
items.quote: We have decided not to give any guidance for FY27. However, we will revisit this decision, maybe when we will have -- we have some clarity after conclusion of the first quarter.

items.statement: Standalone revenue fell 1% YoY in Q4 to INR 5,382 crores and 9% YoY for FY26 to INR 17,669 crores; consolidated revenue rose 1% YoY in Q4 to INR 6,251 crores but fell 6% YoY for FY26 to INR 20,944 crores
items.quote: For the full year, the turnover stands at INR 17,669 crores as against INR 19,393 crores of the previous year, a decline by 9%.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin 8.44% in Q4 FY26 vs 9.21% YoY; consolidated EBITDA margin 8.83% vs 9.07% YoY
items.quote: At consolidated level, we achieved EBITDA of 8.83% and PBT of 4.70% before exceptional items and PAT of 3.3% in the current quarter.

items.statement: Gross debt reduced by INR 729 crores in Q4 FY26 to INR 2,251 crores; net debt INR 1,667 crores; debt-to-equity 0.30x
items.quote: At the end of quarter 4 of FY26, it stood at INR 2,251 crores and net debt at INR 1,667 crores. And at the end of Q4 FY25, the same is at INR1,484 crores and net debt of INR706 crores. There is a decrease of debt by INR729 crores in Q4 FY26.

items.statement: Working capital (excl. cash & margin money) INR 4,847 crores (28% of turnover, 97 days); trade receivables down to INR 3,336 crores (73 days) from INR 3,505 crores (87 days); unbilled revenue down to INR 6,675 crores (38%) from INR 7,129 cr
items.quote: Working capital, excluding cash and margin money deposits at the end of Q4 FY2 6, it stands at INR4,847 crores, which is 28% of the turnover. In terms of working capital days, it is 97 days.

items.statement: FY26 capex INR 912 crores (incl. INR 320 crores TBM CWIP) vs budgeted INR 1,050 crores; FY27 capex plan INR 500 crores (INR 100-150 crores for mining, rest regular)
items.quote: FY27, the capex plan is INR500 crores.

items.statement: TBM for Mumbai GMLR project (INR 3,000 crores execution share of INR 6,000 crores total) being lowered, expected to start in 2 months, full depreciation over ~3 years
items.quote: The TBM machine is specifically designed for this project, and the total capex will fully expensed in about 3 years' time. By the time we complete the whole depreciation, we will book.

items.statement: 74% of contracts have escalation clauses; uncertain if price increases fully covered; material availability/logistics/fuel may cause issues; buying materials just-in-time
items.quote: About 74% of the contracts, we have escalation clauses. But I'm not very sure whether the increase in the prices will completely get covered under the escalation clauses. There may be some impact. There is no doubt in that.

items.statement: Order book ~95% government (state, central, PSUs), ~5% private; no payment pressure or cancellations from private clients
items.quote: No, we have not seen any kind of pressure from the private lines because our private lines orders comprises about 4% to 5% -- yes about 5% in the entire order book.

items.statement: UP JJM receivables (trade + unbilled) down to INR 3,015 crores; trade receivables alone INR 695 crores vs INR 1,700 crores in Dec; collected ~INR 1,000 crores in Q4 and INR 400-450 crores in April

items.statement: FY2027 volume growth of at least 2 million tons vs FY2026, mostly from India Kalinganagar ramp-up
items.quote: The volume will be at least 2 million tons better in this financial year compared to the previous financial year with most of it coming in India , largely because the Kalinganagar ramp up is pretty much complete .

items.quote: India continued with its industry leading performance, with EBITDA growing 17% YoY to Rs 34,272 crores. EBITDA margin was 24% and similar to the 10 -year average even in a challenging year.

items.quote: Downstream business including Tubes, Wires and Colors achieved best‑ever sales while Tinplate witnessed record annual sales of PAXEL edible oil cans.

items.quote: Retail for us is far more attractive than projects. So, over the years, we have increased or pretty much doubled our sales to retail, which used to be at one point in time, 100,000-120,000 tons a month, is today over 200,000 tons a month.

items.statement: UK system EBITDA ~Rs 12,000/t on slab transfers (Rs 7,000-8,000/t from India slab supply + Rs 4,000-4,500/t UK conversion); post-EAF target 6-8% EBITDA margin with value-added upside

items.quote: Whether it has the affordability to make a large investment to transit or not is a question that we are testing at this point of time. Apart from the affordability is obviously whether the goal post on regulatory standards keep changing.

items.statement: Construction demand struggled in last 2 months due to elections and labour migration; auto demand strong; retail channel growing, project channel declining
items.quote: Construction has struggled a bit in the last couple of months simply because of the elections and labour going home to vote , and things like that.

items.statement: HIsarna pilot in Netherlands doing well; commercial scale plant (~1 Mt) planned in India with Nucor collaboration; engineering underway for game-changing raw material flexibility
items.quote: when we set up a commercial scale plant in India, which may be close to a million tons, Nucor will work very closely with us, and the engineering is bein g done for that.

items.statement: JLR achieved FY26 EBIT of 0.7% within 0-2% guidance and full-year cash loss just over GBP2.2bn within minus GBP2.2bn to minus GBP2.5bn range
items.value: 0.7% EBIT; cash loss just over GBP2.2bn
items.quote: So we ended up with 0.7% EBIT, within our 0% to 2% guidance. And we ended up at the better end of our cash guidance, with full year cash loss just over GBP2.2 billion versus a minus GBP2.2 billion to minus GBP2.5 billion range.

items.statement: JLR targeting GBP1.7bn savings over two years to bring breakeven volume back towards 300,000 units annually
items.quote: Together, we're targeting GBP1.7 billion of savings over two years to bring our breakeven volume back down towards 300,000 units a year.

items.quote: Capex for the year stood at about Rs. 4,300 Cr that translated to about 7.5% of revenues, well within the guidance range that we gave from the combined Capex for PV and EV.

items.quote: For the full year, the PV industry touched a new high of 4.7 million units, which was 8% year -on-year growth.

items.statement: TMPV expects industry to grow around 10% in FY27 with high double-digit growth in H1 on low base, moderating in H2
items.quote: I am pegging the number around 10% because the first half of last financial year was a low base. And therefore, in H1, you are going to see very strong double-digit growth coming on the back of that.

items.statement: TMPV EV bookings jumped 25-30% since Middle East crisis began in February; monthly run rate of 9,000 units, targeting beyond 10,000 from current month
items.quote: Demand is extremely strong, especially after the Mid dle-East crisis unfolded. Hopefully, we'll start ramping up further beyond 10,000 from this month onwards

items.statement: TMPV has healthy order book across models with lean channel inventory and strong sustained traction
items.quote: We have a healthy order book across models, lean channel inventory and are seeing strong sustained traction across models, which will serve us well in the coming quarters.

items.statement: JLR has 78,000 expressions of interest for Range Rover EV; no pre-bookings yet
items.quote: We don't have pre-bookings. We have expressions of interest, and there are 78,000 of those at the last count.

items.statement: TMPV Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 9.4%, EBIT margin 4.7%; full year EBITDA and EBIT margins muted due to adverse pricing and commodity increases
items.quote: We ended the year with 9.4% EBITDA margin for the quarter and 4.7% EBIT margin.

items.statement: JLR Q4 FY26 EBIT 9.2%, slightly lower than bumper Q4 last year but same as two years ago; full year EBIT 0.7%
items.quote: We had 95,000 wholesales, revenue of nearly GBP7 billion and EBIT of 9.2%. That's only a little lower than our bumper Q4 last year , and is actually the same EBIT level as we achieved two years ago.

items.statement: TMPV FY27 intense product action year with two new nameplates and four facelifts each for ICE and EVs; focus on ramping production and enhancing capacities
items.quote: This year also, it's going to be an intense product action year for us. These two new nameplates and four facelifts that we are going to launch, both four facelifts each for ICE and EVs.

items.statement: JLR FY26 investment GBP3.57bn (GBP2.6bn engineering) across three new architectures, UK plants, Wolverhampton BEV powertrains; 64% capitalization rate
items.quote: On a full year basis, we spent GBP3.57 billion, of which GBP2.6 billion was engineering as we progressed three new architectures towards their launches.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt Rs. 30,000 Cr at March 2026 (Rs. 25,000 Cr cash burn + Rs. 2,200 Cr dividends); PV cash positive Rs. 7,000 Cr; JLR net debt Rs. 33,000 Cr

items.statement: TMPV Q4 FCF Rs. 1,700 Cr from strong operating profits, favorable working capital, Rs. 500 Cr tax refunds; FY26 FCF Rs. 1,900 Cr

items.statement: Geopolitical splintering creating protectionism, differing electrification appetites, ADAS duplication costs, commodity inflation, supply chain rules of origin challenges, regulatory volatility
items.quote: The splintering and volatility of geopolitics creates challenges from increasing protectionism, differing electrification appetites and technology concerns that, for example, mean we have to duplicate large parts of our ADAS developments.

items.statement: JLR relying on brand strength to compete with Chinese OEMs in Europe/UK; operating in space where Chinese imports are not present

items.statement: Upcountry expansion grew 45%; strong adoption of digital and platform-led distribution in India
items.quote: There was continued traction in upcountry expansion initiatives. We grew 45% in the up-country part of the business and strong adoption of digital and platform-led distribution.

items.statement: In TSG data center space, competing with existing distributors but performing better in neo cloud segment; focus on ROCE and risk-adjusted deals
items.quote: In the neo cloud and the data center, we are also new to the picture. And we are actually, I would say, doing better than a lot of our competitors. But it's a matter of like what Krishnan said, getting the right deals with the right ROCE and the right risk levels.

items.statement: War risk insurance coverage withdrawn unilaterally with 7 days notice in Middle East; managed via alternative warehouses and new coverage
items.quote: As the war started, the insurance companies joined together with 7 day's notice removed this risk coverage, and it was an unilateral decision. So we had to manage. We did manage in the form of getting some additional cover from other insurance companies.

items.statement: Middle East contributes 30-35% of revenue and profit; UAE cluster most impacted by crisis
items.quote: In terms of revenue and profits, about 30 to 35 percentage of our business happens from this market.

items.statement: Targets 10-12% EBITDA margin for FY27 and beyond
items.quote: So I mean -- so our trajectory is definitely 10% to 12%. So 10% is our first big milestone from the company perspective, given that the expansion which has been taking place. So yes, I mean, we are looking at a range of 10% to 12% in the coming years, starting with FY '27.

items.statement: Targets 12-14% revenue CAGR over next 2 years
items.quote: So, 12% to 14% is something like we have been talking about as a CAGR that we have planned.

items.statement: Targets INR6,000 crore revenue by FY28 with 100 million pieces shipped
items.quote: By 2028, what we had foreseen is that we should be having established capacity of anywhere between 125 million to 130 million, and we should be shipping around 100 million pieces to get to that target of INR6,000 crores that we spoke about.

items.statement: Committed INR250 crore capex to be completed by H1 FY27
items.quote: A capex of INR250 crores has already been committed and is expected to be completed by H1 FY '27.

items.statement: Planning INR200-250 crore capex for FY27 across geographies
items.quote: We are in the process of outlining capex commitment of INR200 crores to INR250 crores for FY '27 across geographies.

items.statement: Approved acquisition of 10% stake in PT Pinnacle Apparels Indonesia for $1.4 million
items.quote: The company through its step-down subsidiary company, DSSP Global Limited, Hong Kong will be acquiring an additional 10% stake from minority shareholder in PT Pinnacle Apparels Indonesia for a consideration of $1.4 million.

items.statement: Identified land parcel in Vietnam for purchase at $2.5-3 million
items.quote: We have also identified a land parcel in Vietnam and are at advanced stage of concluding the purchase. The purchase consideration could be in the range of $2.5 million to $3 million.

items.statement: Installed capacity reached 101 million pieces per annum as of March 2026
items.quote: Our installed capacity reached 101 million pieces per annum.

items.statement: Bangladesh capex to add 6-7 million pieces capacity by H1 FY27
items.quote: With Bangladesh ongoing capex expected to be completed by H1 FY '27, this will further increase capacity by 6 million to 7 million pieces during FY '27, only from this capex.

items.statement: Vietnam capacity utilization improved to 80%+ in FY26 from 63% in FY25
items.quote: Capacity utilization improved to 80% plus in the current year compared to 63% of last year.

items.statement: Indonesia capacity utilization increased to 47% in FY26 from 39% in FY25
items.quote: Indonesia capacity utilization has increased to 47% of its total established capacity that we have there in this year. Last year, it was about 39%.

items.statement: Targets 125-130 million pieces established capacity by FY28
items.quote: By 2028, what we had foreseen is that we should be having established capacity of anywhere between 125 million to 130 million.

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin 9.3% in FY26 (10.3% excluding tariff and new facility losses)
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA margin stood at 9.3%, excluding tariff impact of INR36 crores and incremental loss in Bihar and Guatemala, approximately INR13 crores, adjusted EBITDA margin stands at 10.3% for the full year.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin 10.3% (10.9% excluding tariff and new facility losses)
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA, excluding ESOP expenses at INR135 crores, up by 13.7% year-on-year with a margin at 10.3%, which has been the highest ever EBITDA margin in any quarter so far.

items.statement: Standalone adjusted EBITDA margin 6.2% in FY26 (8% excluding tariff cost)
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA, excluding ESOP expense stands at INR67 crores with a margin at 6.2%, up by 60 bps year-on-year, mainly due to cost restructuring efforts done in the organization.

items.statement: Expects India standalone to deliver high single-digit EBITDA for full year FY27
items.quote: And our effort is to have high single-digit EBITDA for the full year.

items.statement: Guatemala operations expected to breakeven in FY27
items.quote: And given that strategy, as we are in the first quarter of FY '27, I see that it is working out, and we should be able to have breakeven in FY '27.

items.statement: US consumer sentiment resilient despite inflation; no significant slowdown seen yet
items.quote: What we see as of now, both these things are workable and manageable. In terms of demand trend that we are talking about in U.S. because of the current inflationary environment that U.S. is undergoing, surprisingly, like the resilience that we are seeing f rom the co nsumers and the buying pattern

items.statement: EU and UK FTA driving customer interest in shifting sourcing to India
items.quote: Equally important for India would be the FTA, which is signed between India and U.K. and between India and EU. Although we still await the implementation date, customers have started visiting and are excited about this opportunity to diversify their sourcing into India more and from the overdependence on duty-free countries like Bangladesh and Cambodia.

items.statement: India order book showing good traction post tariff removal and FTA prospects
items.quote: So, that's -- keeping that in mind, we are seeing a good traction in the order books of India so far, whatever we have seen.

items.statement: Realization per garment at INR635-640; targets sustaining INR600+
items.quote: We are already at INR635, INR640 per garment. And I think it should continue it should sustain.

items.statement: Raw material cost increases passed through to customers within 1-2 months
items.quote: So generally, that impact is suddenly like if you have booked the business and after that, some increase happens, then it impacts us. Otherwise, that also at a maximum of about 1 to 2 months.

items.statement: Working capital days at 43 days as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: Working capital days stood at 43 days as on 31 March 2026.

items.statement: Long-term credit rating upgraded to A+ stable from BBB stable in 2021
items.quote: the company has achieved a notable improvement in its credit profile with th e long-term credit rating upgraded from BBB stable in 2021 to A+ stable for a long term in 2026

items.statement: Declared total dividend of INR14.50 per share (290% face value) for FY26, highest ever payout at 25% of group PAT
items.quote: The total dividend for FY '26 stands at INR14.50 per share, 290% of the face value. This is the highest ever dividend payout ratio by the company, which represents 25% of the group PAT of FY '26.

items.statement: Design team headcount increased from 70-75 to over 100
items.quote: Yes. Design stuff, if you talk about, yes, we are almost like we used to be in the range of 70, 75. Now it's almost crossing 100.

And now businesses in U.S. are starting to file legal cases for refunds, though it may not be so easy as it sounds, and currently, a 10% tariff under the Section 122 is in place till the month of July for

items.statement: Construction segment grew 44% YoY in Q4, driven by CEV BS-V emission transition
items.quote: Our construction segment specifically grew 44% year-over-year, validating the strength of our products under the new emission standard and the capability of our engineering team.

items.quote: Yes, I mean, our full intention is to maximize on operating leverage, yes.
