items.statement: Some material cost inflation will be passed on to market; pricing policy evaluated regularly with price increases at regular periods
items.quote: I think some of the material cost inflation is such that it's going to be hard for players to absorb all of it themselves. So, some of it will certainly get passed on to the market.

items.quote: While the overall annual diesel generator market grew 18% to approximately 179,000 units, including telecom, KOEL grew by 41%, selling upwards of 50,000 units in FY26.

items.quote: The standalone loans stands at INR 1,64,000 crores and the highest ever standalone profit after tax of INR 10,134 crores. It is up by 95% year-on-year.

items.quote: Muthoot Finance declared the highest dividend of 300% or INR 30 per share and this is the 14th year of consistent dividend declaration since our IPO in 2011.

items.quote: Our EBITDA has grown from ₹ 33 crore to ₹ 69 crore, which is more than 112% growth.

items.statement: BTS book-to-bill ratio healthy with ~INR 250 crores revenue vs ~INR 400 crores orders booked in FY26; BTS order book ~INR 800 crores entering FY27
items.quote: And with -- so that's one point. items.statement: No major supply disruptions from Middle East war; only short-term logistics delays at end of Q4
items.quote: No, we don't see any short -- we had certain short-term impacts at the end of Q4 because of some logistics delays as a result of the war. But I would say we are not seeing any major supply disruptions directly as a result of the Middle East war right now.

items.statement: European subsidiary losses may continue in Q1 FY27 but deconsolidation expected by end of Q1 or Q2; no further exceptional items expected in consolidated financials
items.quote: But we don't expect any exceptional items or one time losses coming and hitting in the next fiscal year as far as European subsidiaries are concerned in the consolidated financials.

items.statement: EMS completed more than 80 new product introductions in FY26 supporting faster customer ramp-ups and new business wins
items.quote: Capability enhancem ent and customer diversification continue to remain key focus areas for us. And during the year, we completed more than 80 new product introductions, supporting faster customer ramp-ups and new business wins

items.statement: Continued investments in manufacturing capability expansion including additional lines, process automation and systems integration capabilities
items.quote: We also continued investments towards manufacturing capability expansion, including additional manufacturing lines, process automation initiatives and systems integration capabilities to support future growth.

items.statement: French subsidiary entered redressement judiciaire (court-supervised restructuring) in March 2026; asset sale process underway with court approval expected by July 2026
items.quote: In Europe, the French subsidiary entered the redressement judiciaire or the legal restructuring process during March 2026, and we are currently progressing through a court-supervised asset sale process.

items.statement: EMS business export-oriented with global quality standards enabling wins from global customers indigenizing production in India
items.quote: I would say, a differentiating point is that from a long time, we ha ve been an export -oriented business. And so the levels of quality, reliability, performance and internal systems and processes that we maintain and run are at a global standard

items.statement: Moving up value chain in defense may involve competing with current customers (HAL, DRDO, BEL) but viewed as natural ecosystem evolution
items.quote: It's -- it depends on the program, I would say. I mean, in many cases, our customers, I would say, in many cases, are basically HAL, DRDO and in certain cases with BEL. So this is -- it's an evolving scenario. There are programs that we are collaborating. There are certain programs where we will compete. And I think that's a natural process of evolution of the ecosystem in the country, and it's no

items.statement: Management bandwidth freed from overseas restructuring to focus on core India ESDM platform; impact on BTS order booking visible over longer term
items.quote: So the management bandwidth that could get focused on the BTS will only yield more results in the near future in terms of order booking for the year or the next year and the further growth on a long-term basis.

items.statement: Standalone exceptional item of INR 203 crores in FY26 for overseas subsidiary provisions/impairments; INR 153 crores capital loss available for future capital gains set-off
items.quote: Out of that, the investment-related impairment, that INR 153 crores that will be -- that's a capital loss. So that will be available for us for the future for, any capital gains set off, whereas the other items have been used to offset against the profits made during the current year.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance INR925-1,000 crores, conditional on Middle East stabilization
items.quote: So the guidance on the revenue, we've said INR925 crores to INR1,000 crores. That's the kind of band which we are looking at. And we feel fairly confident of being able to achieve it provided the geopolitical situations improve.

items.statement: FY27 growth 12-15% if Middle East remains at zero, 30%+ if normalizes
items.quote: In terms of growth, then over our financial year '26, we would look at growth of about 12% to 15% overall. Shialditya Chaudhury: 12% to 15%. Bimal Thakkar: If the Middle East remains at 0 level, right

items.statement: INR124 crores spent over last 2 years on greenfield and brownfield; INR20-25 crores more in FY27
items.quote: There will be some bit of capex still as Bimal was saying, the new line for pizza base will be coming up. So those payments will be coming up. This will be roughly around INR20 crores to INR25 crores this year, we will be still spending on capex.

items.statement: Surat facility expected INR40-50 crores revenue in FY27; INR200-250 crores at full capacity
items.quote: So we expect in terms of revenue around INR40 crores to INR50 crores contribution from the Surat facility in this fiscal year. At its full capacity, the Surat plant will give us upwards of INR200 crores in top line.

items.statement: Expect to maintain high-teen EBITDA margins in FY27 despite Surat ramp-up
items.quote: Well, as the Surat facility would not be fully utilized, but we feel fairly confident that we will maintain these high-teen EBITDAs, which we've been giving guidance for.

items.statement: Surat plant at full capacity expected to maintain similar margins as existing facilities
items.quote: So at its full capacity, we expect to maintain the similar kind of margins that we are getting from our existing facilities.

items.statement: Truly Indian brand targeting INR75-80 crores revenue in FY27; driven by distribution expansion and repeat orders
items.quote: Truly Indian brand has grown more than what we had expected in this last fiscal year. This year also, we are hoping for a much higher growth. I mean our estimate is if everything goes well, we are looking at anywhere between INR75 crores to INR80 crores on Truly Indian for this year.

items.statement: Plans to pitch Truly Indian to Costco in UK, Canada, Australia after US success
items.quote: So we are -- based on the success we've had in the U.S., our team in the U.K. is connecting with the Costco buyers and presenting the products there. So yes, we do have plans. We have already entered in Costco in Australia. We are also pitching for Costco in Canada.

items.statement: Q4 growth 60-65% volume-driven; mix improvement and rupee depreciation also contributed
items.quote: So I would say the growth is more 60%, 65% towards the volume growth. There has been some benefit with the devaluation, but majority of the growth has come through with volume growth. And the Middle East business, as I mentioned, I mean, March was literally -- we didn't have any shipments go into the Middle East in the month of March.

items.statement: No price increases taken; growth from volume, mix, and currency
items.quote: So it's again product mix. And no, we haven't increased the price. So it's volume growth, product mix and some benefit towards the rupee depreciation, yes. So a combination of these.

items.statement: Freight costs up 3-4% of revenue in March; sharing 50-50 with distributors for Middle East
items.quote: The increase has been roughly about 3% to 4% at the moment. Of the total revenue, yes. Markets like the Middle East, which have just started operating, there the freight costs are very high. And it's -- as I mentioned, it's just 1 or 2 ports that are currently operational. So in those markets, we are sharing the cost with our distributor on a 50-50 basis.

items.statement: Net debt-free with INR78.2 crores cash surplus as of FY26 end
items.quote: The company's financial position remains strong with a net debt-free balance sheet and a robust cash surplus of INR78.2 crores, thereby providing strong financial flexibility for future growth initiatives.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend 30% of face value; total FY26 dividend 60%
items.quote: The Board has recommended final dividend of 30% of face value, making the total dividend amounting to 60% for FY '26.

items.statement: Middle East (GCC) ~15% of revenue; March-April shipments near zero due to shipping disruption
items.quote: The GCC overall accounts for about a little under 15% of our overall revenues. So that's the markets which we are struggling with at the moment. So they haven't contributed at all for March and April. And we hope the situation improves because then that will help us feeding these markets back again.

items.statement: GCC business impacted 80-85%; other markets only face longer transit and slightly higher freight
items.quote: So I would say the GCC business has been impacted by at least about 80%, 85% for us. All the other markets, what has happened is we have containers going -- I mean, ships are accepting cargo there. It's just that the transit time is longer and the freight rates have increased a little bit. But all these other markets, we've not had any imp act. The main impact has been in the GCC for us

items.statement: Consolidated FY26 revenue INR683.2 crores (+15.9% YoY); EBITDA margin 19.1% (+240 bps)
items.quote: Coming to the full year performance, consolidated revenue stood at INR683.2 crores, up 15.9% year-on-year. EBITDA increased 32.8% to INR130.7 crores, while EBITDA margins improved to 19.1%, an expansion of 240 basis points.

items.statement: Management expects poultry division to grow at industry rate of 7-8% in FY27
items.quote: With regard to poultry growth, our growth is coming to 7% to 8% as an industry. And we do expect that, that growth is likely to happen in Venky's also.

items.statement: Layer chick sales target of 5 crore plus for FY27 vs 4.57 crore in FY26
items.quote: In case of poultry segment, particularly like layer segment, we sold 4.57 crores chicks during last year '25-'26. We are planning to sell almost 5 crores plus chicks during this '26-'27.

items.statement: Broiler chicks and contract broiler farming targeting 2-5% volume growth in FY27
items.quote: We are likely to repeat this number at least 2%, 3% more, 4%, 5% more in the broiler chicks as well as CBF numbers.

items.statement: Animal Health Products division expected to grow at double-digit rate in FY27
items.quote: Yes. I think the Animal Health business will definitely grow in the double digit. And even from the first month of this financial year in that direction only.

items.statement: Oil Seed division expects to maintain or improve Q4 FY26 performance through Q2 FY27
items.quote: Yes, I think next 2 quarters, we definitely expect so. Third quarter, when new crop comes in. So that depends on the availability and the crop size in all India.

items.statement: Poultry segment Q4 FY26 operating margin ~14% driven by broiler realization and input costs
items.quote: With regard to quarter 4, the main attributing factor was broiler realization and, of course, input costs. So that is the reason why the percentage and the overall absolute profit was higher.

items.statement: Animal Health Products FY27 full-year EBIT margin expected to sustain 22-23%+ despite Q2-Q3 raw material pressure
items.quote: But for whole year, I think it will sustain 22%, 23% and above, and we are likely to see the improvement in the top line also.

items.statement: Oil Seed division targets 65%+ outside sales to improve margins and reduce group dependence
items.quote: So that means our dependence on the group will become lower and our 60% to 65% revenue will be coming out from the outside the group only. And that will ensure a better margins.

items.statement: Oil Seed capacity utilization currently 65-70%, targeting 80% in FY27
items.quote: Capacity utilization today is around 65% to 70%. And this year, we expect to be around 80%.

items.statement: Animal Health Products new therapeutic plant at 35-40% utilization, older plant at 75-80%
items.quote: A new plant which we have built, so which is still at -- because this is for specialty product and the therapeutics. So this is still at the 35% to 40% of the capacity utilization.

items.statement: SPF egg capacity utilization improved to 48% in FY26 from 45% in FY25
items.quote: As far as the capacity utilization is concerned, it is to the extent of 48% in this year and the total capacity is 1.88 crores for the whole year. But for the SPF egg, it is 48% against last year of 45% utilization.

items.statement: Broiler realization INR 102.67/kg in Q4 FY26, currently INR 97-100/kg in April FY27

items.statement: Layer chick realization stable at INR 45-49 in Q4 FY26 and April FY27
items.quote: As far as the layer segment is concerned, prices are stable, the price is INR45 to INR49 is the price, which is same in the last quarter, fourth quarter as well as the coming quarter, that is April, May, June.

items.quote: In this last quarter, I mean, yearly 2025, '26, the average price is INR31,658 per ton for the feed prices, broiler feed prices -- total feed prices.

items.quote: As for raw material prices are concerned, I think it's going to be a little bit volatile in coming months. for one thing, the crude oil prices are very high. So one of the major ingredient corn, the government is working on the ethanol production.

items.statement: India corn and soya supply sufficient; domestic prices higher than international (Brazil/Argentina)
items.quote: India is more than sufficient as far as the corn and soya both are concerned. Today, corn, we are not able to export even to our neighboring country, Bangladesh, because Bangladesh is able to import much cheaper price from Brazil.

items.statement: Poultry demand growing; poultry share of non-veg segment increased from 35-40% to 55%+
items.quote: If you see overall pie graph of non-veg segment, earlier, poultry was having 35% to 40% in non-veg segment. Now it is crossing more than 55%. So definitely, there is a growth in demand also.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 productivity expected 10-12% lower due to summer heat in open farms
items.quote: Traditionally, if you see the productivity gets hampered in Q1, usually because of -- we have more than 95% of the farms which are open. So because of these conventional farms in India, usually, the productivity is comparatively 10% to 12% less.

items.statement: Receivables decreased from INR 553 cr to INR 554 cr despite INR 150 cr higher Oil Seed turnover
items.quote: See, as far as the receivables are concerned, it was INR553 crores in the last year, which has come down to the level of INR544 crores. This includes external as well as the group associates.

items.statement: Working capital availability of INR 160 cr sufficient; no plans to increase debt
items.quote: On the working capital front, we are having the sufficient working capital in place. It is almost INR160 crores is the working capital -- I mean, availability, which is sufficient to meet the requirement of all the segments.

items.statement: Oil Seed division debt-free; no plans to increase term loans or working capital borrowings
items.quote: We are debt free. We are not using any money for the capex. We are not using money for any working capital. There are absolutely no loan for the division.

items.statement: Animal Health Products shifting to natural solutions, therapeutics, and expanded distribution
items.quote: In Animal Health business, in last 3, 4 years, there were 3, 4 changes have been made in the product mix. As you know, there's a lot of talk on the antimicrobial resistance. So we started developing a lot of products for the natural solutions.

items.statement: Oil Seed targeting 33% soya meal external sales (from 20%) to reach 65%+ outside revenue
items.quote: We are targeting 33% of the soya meal to sell outside. So our outside part of our operation will be 65% plus and in-house, it will be 35%.

items.statement: Animal Health Products expanding distribution to reach customers nationwide within 6-7 days
items.quote: And third thing was that we have deployed a lot of distribution channel all across the country with a lot of clearing and forwarding and our warehousing system where we can reach to our customers in a different nooks and corners.

items.statement: Poultry industry expansion 75%+ from existing players, 25% from new entrants
items.quote: If you would like to bifurcate the expansion of the industry, we are seeing that more than 75% of expansion comes from existing players because they are better off and they are already having the infrastructure.

items.statement: CCI investigation relates to parent breeding farms; Venky's India Limited not affected as it doesn't deal in those products
items.quote: This CCI investigation is regarding certain practices in the parent companies or the parent breeding farms in which Venky's as such, do not deal in those products. However, being a group as a part of legality, we have received the notice.

items.statement: El Nino may impact soybean/maize crop from October FY27; monitoring for Q3 FY27
items.quote: Third quarter, when new crop comes in. So that depends on the availability and the crop size in all India because El Nino is affected, though the soybean and maize doesn't need much of the water.

items.statement: Commercial broiler production volume 8.69 cr kg in FY26 vs 9.17 cr kg in FY25
items.quote: The volume of commercial broiler birds is 8.69 crores in '25-'26 against the previous year, it was 9.17 crores birds. There was a reduction of almost 49 lakh kgs during this financial year.

items.statement: Layer chick volume 4.57 cr in FY26 vs 4.38 cr in FY25 (+19 lakh)
items.quote: In regard to the layer chicks, the volume was 4.57 crores in this year, whereas last year, it was 4.38 crores. So there is an increase of 19 lakh chicks during the year.

items.statement: Broiler chick volume 11.46 cr in FY26 vs 10.77 cr in FY25
items.quote: In case of broiler chicks, it is 11.46 crores chicks during the year, whereas in the last year, it was 10.77 crores chicks.

items.statement: Capex for FY27 expected in range of INR 1,000-1,200 crore including approved and pipeline projects
items.quote: So that should be in the range of around INR1,000-INR1,200 crore including the normal capex as of now, which has been let us say approved by the board, but we have few projects in the pipeline as well.

items.statement: Board approved INR 217 crore for additional renewable power supply at Bharuch plant, raising RE capacity from 50.4 MW to 98.4 MW peak
items.quote: Our Board has approved capital expenditure of INR 217 crore towards obtaining approximately INR 48 crore of additional renewable power supply for our Bharuch plant and related infrastructure development, thereby taking the total RE power provision for Bharuch plant from the present peak of 50.4 megawatts to 98.4 megawatts.

items.statement: Board approved INR 101 crore to expand epoxy formulated resins capacity by 36 KTPA to 50 KTPA total
items.quote: The Board has further approved INR101 crore for the expansion of epoxy-led formulated resins capacity by 36 kilotons per year, increasing the total formulated resins capacity to 50 KTPA.

items.statement: ECH plant fully commissioned in April 2026, currently running at 60-70% utilization with steady ramp-up expected
items.quote: Now actually the plant is running at close to 60% to 70% capacity utilization and we a re ramping up the capacity.

items.statement: Aluminium extrusion project at Kota progressing on schedule to enhance aluminium fenestration capabilities
items.quote: The aluminium extrusion project at Kota is progressing on schedule. This facility will meaningfully enhance our capabilities in the rapidly growing aluminium fenestration and building material segment.

items.statement: Fenesta order book up 15% year-on-year with record order book levels
items.quote: The order book is up by 15%.

items.statement: Chemicals PBDIT flat at INR 163 crore in Q4 FY26 due to elevated fixed costs from expansion and stabilization
items.quote: PBDIT for the quarter was flat at INR163 crore due to elevated fixed costs associated with business expansion and stabilization.

items.statement: Vinyl PBDIT improved 68% to INR 39 crore led by higher prices, lower energy costs and better operating efficiencies
items.quote: PBDIT for the segment improved by 68% to INR39 crore led by higher prices and further supported by lower energy costs and better operating efficiencies.

items.statement: Sugar and ethanol PBDIT down 18% to INR 207 crore due to 8% higher cane cost
items.quote: PBDIT for the segment came in at 18% lower at INR207 crore owing to the higher cost of production of sugar due to the increased cane price by 8%.

items.statement: Fenesta PBDIT up 6% to INR 37 crore led by volumes, partially offset by increased fixed costs for capacity enhancement and new platforms
items.quote: PBDIT for the quarter was up 6% at INR37 crore led by volumes, partially offset by increased fixed costs towards enhancing capacities, higher sales promotion, setting up of new business platforms like facade, wooden doors, and acquisition -related costs.

items.statement: Fertilizer PBDIT INR 28 crore vs INR 9 crore last year, includes one-time gain of INR 33 crore from retention price revision
items.quote: PBDIT was INR28 crore as against INR9 crore last year. There was a one -time gain of INR33 crore on account of revision of retention price of the previous years.

items.statement: Current ECU (excluding flakes) in range of INR 32,000-33,000 per metric ton for lye
items.quote: The current ECU is in the range of INR32,000 to INR33,000 per metric ton. Amit Agarwal: And just to add, this is ECU without including the flakes element because some of the peers include flakes element as well. So this is for lye

items.statement: PVC prices currently ranging between INR 81-82 per kg, volatile due to China dumping and West Asia crisis
items.quote: Our prices are ranging between 81 -82 in that range right now. But you know China dumping can come in at any time. We do not know at what price and what is their policy behind it. So it is very uncertain.

items.statement: Domestic caustic soda demand grew ~5% driven by alumina capacity expansions and sustained paper/detergent consumption
items.quote: Domestic demand grew at about 5% driven by capacity expansions among major alumina players alongside sustained consumption from paper and deter gent industries.

items.statement: Fenesta seeing good demand with record order book, no demand fallback despite metal price increases
items.quote: I think we are seeing good demand even now. If you see our Q4 numbers also, they were pretty good. So, we have had record order book. So, demand is pretty good right now.

items.statement: Shriram Farm Solutions delivered double-digit growth in FY26 anchored by research wheat segment with 22% growth
items.quote: This performance was anchored by a research wheat segment which achieved a record sales and a 22% growth despite headwinds from extended monsoon.

items.statement: SFS launched 13 new products in crop protection and specialty nutrition in FY26, including 4 from own R&D
items.quote: Notably, in the current financial year, SFS has launched 13 new products in crop protection and specialty plant nutrition verticals, including four new products from our own R&D.

items.statement: New products contribution to chemicals revenue increased from 14% to 34-35% in FY26
items.quote: before the start of this last financial year, the new products were contributing about 14% to the total revenue. Now the new products contribute about 34% or 35% and going forward this will increase.

items.statement: Fenesta retail customers difficult to pass on cost increases; institutional contracts have tolerance levels for cost pass-through
items.quote: In retail customer it becomes a little difficult to pass on the cost if, you know, although the contracts also are of a shorter value and of shorter tenor, but then it is difficult to pass on the cost there. However, in institutional clients, a lot of our contracts are made in such a way that there is a tolerance level post which the cost is passed on, you know, to the builder.

items.statement: China dumping PVC at aggressive prices; 50% of India's PVC imports from China in last year
items.quote: In the last year, 50% of India's imports were from China.

items.statement: Ethanol sector needs policy intervention: align sugar/ethanol prices with cane cost, prioritize sugarcane ethanol allocation, expand beyond E20 blending
items.quote: Ensuring the sector's long-term viability requires calibrated policy interventions, specifically aligning sugar and ethanol selling prices with sugarcane costs, prioritizing sugarcane-based ethanol allocation and expanding targets beyond E20 blending.

items.statement: Sugar inventory lower at 32.2 lakh quintals vs 39.9 lakh quintals last year, valued at INR 3,876 per quintal
items.quote: Sugar inventory was lower at 32.2 lakh quintals as against 39.9 lakh quintals last year. The inventory is valued at INR3,876 per quintal.

items.statement: Outstanding fertilizer subsidy increased to INR 189 crore from INR 161 crore last year
items.quote: Outstanding fertilizer subsidy was INR189 crore as against INR161 crore last year.

items.statement: Net debt at INR 1,767 crore as on March 31, 2026 vs INR 1,395 crore on March 31, 2025
items.quote: Our net debt remains at a comfortable level of INR1,767 crore as on 31st March '26 versus INR1,395 crore on 31st March '25.

items.statement: Raised funds via sustainability-linked NCDs from IFC in March 2026, integrating ESG targets into capital structure
items.quote: Further, in March 2026, we have raised funds through the sustainability -linked non -convertible debentures from the International Finance Corporation, IFC. This partnership is more than a financial transaction. It is a global validation of our ESG roadmap.

items.statement: Announced JV with Teknor Apex B.V. by selling 50% stake in Shriram Polytech Limited for technology-driven partnership
items.quote: we have announced a joint venture with Teknor Apex B.V., a global leader in plastic material science solutions, by selling 50% stake in our subsidiary Shriram Polytech Limited , which is a leading plastic compounding player in India.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of 200% (INR 62.38 crore); total FY26 dividend 560% (INR 174.66 crore)
items.quote: The Board has recommended a final dividend of 200% , amounting to INR62.38 crore in this Board meeting. The total dividend for the year is 560% amounting to INR174.66 crore.

items.statement: Chemicals EBITDA margin ~20% in FY26; revenue up 38%, EBITDA up 50% for full year
items.quote: if you see the last full year numbers, our revenue went up by about 38%, EBITDA went up by about 50%. So that shows that one, the volumes that are getting added are helping the overall profitability of the co mplex.

items.statement: West Asia conflict creating supply chain uncertainty for energy, fertilizer, shipping routes and export markets
items.quote: The escalation of conflict in West Asia emerged as a material external risk. Although India is geographically insulated from the conflict, its economic ecosystem is closely intertwined with the region through energy, fertilizer supply chains, shipping routes, and export markets.

items.statement: CEO targets 25% revenue growth for FY27 but cites high uncertainty and will monitor month-by-month
items.quote: What we want to achieve is 25%. But to tell you specifically where we will end up is quite difficult. Even all the uncertainty is in front of us.

items.statement: CEO expects operational EBITDA margin between 12% and 14% for FY27
items.quote: So we are positive that we will be able to operate between 12% to 14%.

items.statement: April and May demand remains good with growth in both tractors and tillers
items.quote: Looking at April and May so far the demand is continuing to be good. The company has done well in last month. April normally is a lower month compared to the other months of the year. However, we have grown both in the tractors and the tiller space in April.

items.statement: Monsoon predicted at 92% LPA; spatial distribution and timing critical for volumes
items.quote: The prediction is for 92% LPA kind of monsoon and over the long period average it will be at 92%. However, if the spatial distribution and the timing of the rainfall is reasonable and with the current comparative better levels of the reservoirs, the volume s would be

items.statement: Full-year operational EBITDA margin improved 220 bps to 13.4% in FY26
items.quote: Also on the operational EBITDA there's a strong improvement of 220 basis point from 11.2% to 13.4%.

items.statement: Q4 operational EBITDA margin improved 80 bps to 14.2%
items.quote: So if we exclude that number we are at a strong 14.2% of operational EBITDA against 13.4%, which is roughly 80 basis points of improvement.

items.statement: Zetor tractor target of 1,000 units for FY27 and 5,000-6,000 by FY30
items.quote: We are targeting thousand numbers this year.

items.statement: Retail finance share grew to 10% in FY26; target 20% in FY27
items.quote: I am very happy to say today last year we concluded with about 10% retail finance. We want to grow it to 20% retail finance this financial year.

items.statement: US market entry restarted; product launches targeted by end of 2027
items.quote: The work that we had stalled to enter the US market considering the tariffs that was there has been restarted. So by the end of 2027 we will be launching the products in the market.

items.statement: Netherlands-based Europe operation launching in June-July 2025
items.quote: We are also doing a Netherlands based operation in Europe, which we said that we will be launching in June, July of this year which is going as per plan.

items.statement: FENTM tractor series and front/rear rotary weeders launched in FY26
items.quote: Some of the new product launches which we have done during the year is FENTM series of tractors, both in red and black color. For our SFM business, we have launched front rotary weeders. These are India made weeders and also the rear rotary.

items.statement: Electric weeder and tiller all-India launch planned for early Q2 FY27
items.quote: We are intending to do a all India wide launch across India in early Q2 of this year.

items.statement: Price increase taken in late April across tractors and power tillers; full cost pass-through uncertain
items.quote: We have taken a price increase towards end of April. We are watching this closely. If this continues to grow or inflation continues to sustain, it will be difficult to pass on the entire inflation to the consumer.

items.statement: Inventory at 36 days; receivables reduced from 75 to 51 days in FY26 with further improvement targeted
items.quote: We have maintained inventory levels in a disciplined manner, I would say. We are at about 36 days of inventory. In FY25 we had taken receivables to about 75 days. items.statement: Music vertical revenue CAGR guidance of 20-23% medium-term with annual EBITDA margin of 60-65%
items.quote: For the music vertical, which is licensed music, artist management and retail, all combined, we continue with our medium-term guidance of 20-23% CAGR in terms of revenue with our annual EBITDA guidance for this vertical being anything between 60-65%.
