items.quote: We will be targeting to similarly monetize the SNRP or Sattanathapuram -Nagapattinam Road project once it is complete an d we have received the first annuity. So it may go into the FY28

items.statement: 4% year-on-year reduction in attrition; diversity ratio improved from 6.3% to 7.9%
items.quote: These efforts led to a 4% year-on-year reduction in attrition. We continue to invest in talent development, succession planning and leadership readiness, further improving organizational agility and developing bench strength. Our diversity ratio also improved from 6.3% in FY25 to 7.9% in FY26.

items.statement: Certified as Great Place to Work for second time
items.quote: All these efforts have been recognized externally with the company being certified as a Great Place to Work for the second time, reflecting the stre ngth of our culture and our core LITE values, learning, innovation, trust and transparency, and endurance

items.statement: WMEL targeting CAGR growth of over 25% over next 3 years
items.quote: It is targeting a CAGR growth of over 25% over the next 3 years.

items.statement: WMEL FY27 revenue growth guidance at 20%
items.quote: We expect our revenue bas e to be growing at a rate of 20%. We have said CAGR of 25% over the next couple of years, but 20% is what we are predicting for the FY27 season

items.statement: Geopolitical disturbances and supply chain disruptions could create near-term cost and execution challenges
items.quote: Prolonged disturbances in geopolitical situations and disruptions in global supply chain could create certain near-term cost and execution challenges, we remain confident in the resilience of our business model and execution capabilities.

items.statement: Management targets breakeven for digital business in FY27 and expects 15% CAGR subscriber growth to continue for next 2-3 years
items.quote: The way we look at, as I said, FY '27 is a year where we look at breakeven and then go forward to keep looking at more and more profitability.

items.statement: Management expects 15% CAGR subscriber growth to continue for next 2-3 years
items.quote: We believe the way in the last 2 years, we have seen almost a 15% CAGR on subscriber growth should stay put for the next 2, 3 years also.

items.statement: Radio industry demand remained subdued in FY26 due to macroeconomic uncertainties and geopolitical tensions
items.quote: FY '26 continued to be a challenging year for the overall radio industry with demand conditions remaining subdued amid persistent macroeconomic uncertainties that continue to weigh on advertisers' sentiments.

items.statement: Non-FCT segment saw strong growth for first 9 months but Q4 impacted by geopolitical challenges and event disruptions
items.quote: For FY '26, revenues for the non-FCT segment stood at INR148 crores. The segment performed well for the majority of the year, delivered healthy growth during the first 9 months, reflecting strong underlying demand across our offerings.

items.statement: Digital business reduced spending by 23% in FY26 reflecting improved unit economics and cost discipline
items.quote: Digital spending during the year was reduced by 23%, reflecting improved unit economics and tighter cost management, even as the business continued to scale meaningfully.

items.statement: Variable content cost for music streaming remains in 60-70% range with tech and people costs expected to leverage as subscribers grow
items.quote: Yes, there is a variable content of the music label cost to be given, which always remains in the range of 60% to 70%, depending on how you put it up.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue for FY26 was INR565 crores with 3.9% YoY growth; domestic revenue INR548 crores up 4%
items.quote: For FY '26, we delivered consolidated revenues of INR565 crores, representing a year -on-year growth of 3.9%. Domestic revenues grew by 4% to INR548 crores, primarily driven by the strong momentum in our digital business.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 digital revenue INR21 crores with 42% YoY growth; FCT revenue INR74 crores, non-FCT INR38 crores
items.quote: So overall digital business for Q4 was about INR21 crores and a year -on-year growth of about 42%.

items.statement: Gaana annual subscription price increased from INR499 to INR799; management sees headroom to reach INR1,200 annually
items.quote: The price what we've been charging earlier when we started the business, INR300 or maybe last year at INR499, we have now gone at to INR799 an annual pack.

items.statement: Management believes significant pricing headroom exists as India is value-driven market and willingness to pay depends on value delivered
items.quote: So, we believe there is a lot of headroom on the price. So that's for sure.

items.statement: Radio volume market share maintained at 25.2% for FY26, with slight gain in Q4 to 25.6%
items.quote: Despite these challenging conditions and industry headwinds, the company continues to maintain its leadership position with a volume market share of 25.2%.

items.statement: Music streaming industry at 15 million paid subscribers per EY FICCI report, up from 8 million two years ago; target addressable market 100 million
items.quote: EY recently reported during the FICCI report, the EY FICCI report, which came in, in March, talks about the Indian music subscription numbers at about 15 million, which was about 8 million two years back.

items.statement: Received income tax demand notice of INR113 crores for FY2023-24; company confident of successful appeal
items.quote: However, ignoring all the submissions, order was passed, and that resulted in a demand of INR113 crores. The company is completely confident that it can go to the next level to CIT appeal and other courses of getting the justice.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR2 per share for FY26
items.quote: Lastly, I'm pleased to share that the Board has recommended a dividend of INR2 per share for FY '26.

items.statement: Consolidated cash balance of INR424 crores and standalone cash of INR404 crores as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: As on March 31, 2026, the company maintained a consolidated cash balance of INR424 crores, while the standalone cash balance stood at INR404 crores.

items.statement: Digital business now contributes 48% of radio revenues, representing significant structural shift in business mix
items.quote: Digital revenues now contribute to our radio revenues by about 48% for FY '26, making a significant structural shift in our business mix.

items.statement: Gaana subscriber growth at 15% CAGR over last 2 years; Q4 FY26 digital revenue INR29 crores with 61% YoY growth
items.quote: The numbers of subscribers have been increasing at 15% CAGR and we believe that should continue.

items.statement: Management focused on profitable growth only, not burning cash; evaluating inorganic opportunities while maintaining dividend consistency
items.quote: So, we are very clear we will chase profitable growth only. We will not just chase numbers. So that's one part that it's not about we can't burn. Whatever we believe is the right amount to be invested, we'll always do that.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions in West Asia impacted Middle East operations and non-FCT business with event cancellations
items.quote: Our international operations were particularly impacted, especially in the Middle East, which was directly affected by the ongoing conflict. This market witnessed disruption and slowdown in economic activity, leading advertisers to adopt a more cautious and conservative spending approach.

items.statement: Radio effective rates remain at post-COVID levels with no improvement; volume growth flat in Q4
items.quote: It's not much change. It's almost similar levels. As I said, post -COVID, the ERs have not gone up, and they remain at the same levels.

items.statement: Gaana tech and product development continuous process; major changes completed over last 2 years but ongoing improvements needed
items.quote: To answer yes, whatever large thing which we large changes which we had to change in the last two years, we have taken care of that. But as I said, technology keeps changing, keeps evolving. So, you have to be on toes rather than just sitting on your laurel that you have come to a certain level of your product.

items.statement: International expansion strategy shifted to Gaana-led approach rather than radio
items.quote: The way we look at now is with Gaana as a critical product and with the critical mass, I think, and now being present in many countries, in any international market, we would want to go with Gaana, rather than radio.

name: ZF Commercial Vehicle Control Systems India Ltd

items.statement: FY27 margin expected flattish with single-digit small growth; cautious due to macro uncertainty
items.quote: I would expect it to be more or less flattish with maybe single - digit small growth for the next year. As we are going in, there are challenges which are being called out on the Middle East war front and caution from the government also to look at o ur expenses and consumption. So very difficult to call out on -- given the macroeconomic situation, I would be cautious on the call out for financial

items.statement: FY27 capex outlook INR 180-190 crores for new products, replacements and upgrades
items.quote: We're looking at about a spend of about INR 180 crores to INR 190 crores. Mumuksh Mandlesha: And which area, ma'am, this would be? Sweta Agarwal: Some of it is new product -- capex for new products. Others would be replacements and regular

items.statement: Q4 FY26 M&HCV production 151,000 units (+26.9% YoY); FY26 production 463,000 units (+16.6% YoY)
items.quote: with production reaching a record 151,000 vehicles in quarter as compared to 119,000 of previous year same quarter, reflecting a growth of 26.9% and this contributing to an overall vehicle growth of 16.6% in FY '25-'26, which is 463,000 vehicles versus 397,000 vehicles.

items.statement: Aluminum price rose from INR 233/kg to INR 274/kg (~18% increase); major raw material for products
items.value: INR 233 per kg to INR 274 per kg
items.quote: Aluminum as a commodity has been increased from almost INR 233 per kg to INR 274 per kg approximately. It varies from grade to grade. So that is around close to around 18% as a commodity. And that is a major commodity for our products.

items.statement: New launches: exhaust brake valve, OPL compressor with power reduction, EBS, eCars for EV buses, hydraulic/pneumatic ESC ramp-up, e-compressor for domestic, higher capacity compressor for Europe, new actuator variants for global trailer
items.quote: New launches su ch as exhaust brake valve, OPL compressor with a power reduction feature, and solutions such as EBS, eCars for EV buses. The company also accelerated ramp - up of hydraulic and pneumatic ESC and expanded e - compressor supplies for the domestic market, while scaling exports through higher capacity compressor for Europe and new actuator variants for global trailer customers

items.statement: Aftermarket outreach: 6,000+ retailers, 4,000+ distributors, 1,800+ fleets, 200+ workshops; 51 new distributor branches, 14 new service centers
items.quote: extensive aftermarket team outreach covering 6,000 - plus retailers, 4,000 - plus distributors, 1,800 - plus fleets and 200 - plus workshops continue to be key drivers of growth. Network expansion through 51 new distributor branches and 14 new service centers strengthened presence across B and C class cities, particularly in high consumption markets

items.statement: Mahindra World City plant at peak utilization; further expansions planned at Oragadam
items.quote: World City, I would say the overall plant utilization is at almost peak level. And further expansions, we will be doing in Oragadam

items.statement: 14 national awards, 16 regional awards in FY26; 21 awards in Q4 FY26 (3 regional, 2 international)
items.quote: in FY '25, '26, our teams won 14 national awards and 16 regional awards in competitions organized by CII, ACMA, QCFI and with many more awards at regional levels. This included 21 awards, including 3 regional awards and 2 internatio nal awards in quarter 4 of financial year '25 - '26

items.statement: Commissioned 1,730 MW in FY26: 660 MW Buxar thermal Unit-1, 1,000 MW Bikaner solar, and Dhubri solar; total installed capacity now 4,196 MW
items.quote: With these additions in operating assets, SJVNL achieved a total capacity addition of 1730 Megawatt during '25-'26, comprising of 1070 solar and 660 Megawatt of thermal. With this, the total installed capacity of SJVNL stands at 4196 megawatts.

items.statement: FY27 capacity addition guidance: 660 MW Buxar Unit-2, 69.5 MW Dhaulasidh hydro, ~1,555 MW solar (May'26–Mar'27); FY28: ~650 MW solar
items.quote: If you see the capacity addition for '26-'27, there will be a capacity addition of Buxar Thermal Power plant, 660 Megawatts thermal. Then we are going to commission 69.5 Megawatt of Dhaulasidh Hydro Electric Project in March '27, both the units. And there will be addition of around 1,555 Megawatt of solar capacity by March '27.

items.statement: Capex plan: INR 9,400 crore FY27, INR 7,800 crore FY28, INR 7,500 crore FY29
items.quote: Regarding CAPEX, which you asked about our plan for CAPEX, so this year we have a CAPEX plan of around 9,400 and for FY '28 and FY '29, we have a plan of 7,800 and 7,500 respectively.

items.statement: REIA awarded 16 GW renewable projects; signed PSAs for ~6 GW; 4 GW awarded in FY26 alone; 2,000 MWh BESS awarded
items.quote: As a Renewable Energy Implementing Agency, SJVNL has awarded 16 Gigawatt renewable energy projects across solar, wind, hybrid and storage segments. During '25-'26 alone, SJVNL awarded 4 Gigawatt capacity and signed power sale agreement of approximately 2,177 Megawatt.

items.statement: Renewable tender demand weak; DISCOMs signed only 25-30% of tendered capacity; unsigned PPAs ~9 GW for SJVN; demand shifting to solar+BESS and FDRE
items.quote: The problem what is happening that there are a lot of tenders which came out simultaneously in the market. And the demand is not that much, frankly speaking, because ultimately, this power has to be purchased by the DISCOMs, distribution companies.

items.statement: Buxar Unit-1 loss INR 93 crore on revenue INR 522 crore (3 months) at 60% PLF; expects profit in FY27 at 70%+ PLF; SGEL loss INR 258 crore on revenue INR 510 crore
items.quote: STPL, that is Buxar Unit-1, that earned a revenue of around INR 522 crores in this year, in the last three months. And the total expenses were around INR 644 crores. So post tax, that turns to a total comprehensive income of around minus 93 crores.

items.statement: Trade receivables INR 1,299 crore (Mar'26) vs INR 262 crore (Mar'25); unbilled debtors INR 906 crore including INR 776 crore from tariff orders
items.quote: The trade receivables, which is very important for us as a generating company, as on 31st March '26 stands at INR 1,299 crores as against INR 262 crores on 31st March '25. This includes INR 906 crores as unbilled debtors as on 31st March '26.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend 3.5% (Rs 0.35/share) plus interim 11.5% (Rs 1.15/share) = total 15% (Rs 1.5/share) for FY26
items.quote: The Board of Directors has recommended the payment of final dividend at the rate of 3.5% i.e. Rs.0.35 per equity share in addition to interim dividend at a rate of 11.5% i.e. INR 1.15 per equity share resulting into total dividend at the rate of 15%, Rs.1.5 per equity share.

items.statement: Arun-III Nepal hydro (900 MW) targeting commissioning by Dec'28 after resolving dam right bank geological issues and government approvals
items.quote: We have a plan to commission the entire plant, all the four units, by December '28.

items.statement: Bikaner 1,000 MW solar facing 120 MW curtailment due to SVR (shunt reactor) delay; SVR commissioning expected Oct'26; Khavda Gujarat projects may face 300 MW curtailment due to transmission delay
items.quote: We are facing curtailment in Bikaner. We have commissioned 1,000 Megawatt, but there is a curtailment of around 120 Megawatt. So, that is due to the SVR requirement.

items.statement: Hydro generation FY26: 13,302 MU (+25% YoY); NJHPS 7,506 MU, Rampur 2,108 MU; Buxar design energy 9,828 MU annually
items.quote: During the financial year, total generation from all our power stations stands at 13,302 million units as compared to 10,646 million units during '24-'25, which is reflecting increase of growth of 2,656 million units, approximately 25% higher than the previous year.

items.statement: Finance cost up INR 184 crore to INR 910 crore in FY26 mainly due to INR 206 crore exchange rate variation
items.quote: During FY '26 there has been increase in finance cost by INR 184 crores from INR 726 crores to INR 910 crores, which is mainly due to increase in exchange rate variation during the year by INR 206 crores.

items.statement: Impairment loss INR 174 crore recognized in FY26 (Ind AS 36) driving depreciation up INR 178 crore to INR 632 crore
items.quote: During FY '26 the depreciation, amortization and impairment expenses have gone up by INR 178 crores from INR 450 crores to INR 632 crores, which is mainly due to recognition of impairment losses amounting to INR 174 crores as per AS36.

items.statement: Received SCOPE Eminence Award in HR management from President of India on 29 Aug 2025 for progressive employee-centric HR practices
items.quote: I am pleased to share that SJVNL received the prestigious SCOPE Eminence Award in HR management from Honorable President Smt. Droupadi Murmu on 29th August 2025 for its progressive employee centric HR practices.

items.statement: Dhubri Assam solar (commissioned Feb'26) to supply at tariff Rs 3.92/unit to Assam PDCL; some solar tariffs at Rs 2.53-2.54 vs new tenders at Rs 2.8-2.9
items.quote: The project is expected to generate around 141 million units annually and it will be supplied to Assam Power Distribution Company at a tariff of 3.92 per unit.

items.statement: Long-term 25 GW by 2030 and 50 GW by 2040 targets under review; new business plan coming soon based on realistic assessment
items.quote: These projections were done based on certain market assessment and our growth, which was supposed to happen with RE as well as hydro projects. Unfortunately, due to one or the other reason, which is like unavoidable, which is beyond the control of the SJVNL, the projects did not come in time.

items.statement: Under-construction portfolio: 3,926.5 MW (4 hydro 1,561.5 MW, Buxar Unit-2 660 MW, 10 solar 1,705 MW); 15 operational projects 4,196.5 MW
items.quote: We are currently constructing four hydro projects with a total capacity of 1561.5, second unit of Buxar Thermal Power Plant 660 and 10 solar projects totaling 1705 Megawatt. This brings our total under construction portfolio to 3926.5 Megawatt.

items.statement: Buxar thermal: 85% power to Bihar; Dhubri solar: 100% to Assam PDCL; REIA PPAs pending with various DISCOMs based on their adequacy plans
items.quote: Buxar power plant, when it will be commissioned fully, will generate about 9,828 million units annually, of which 85% shall be supplied to the state of Bihar.

items.statement: All RE implementing agencies (NTPC, SECI, NHAI, SJVN) facing similar PPA signing challenges; only 25-30% capacity tied up across sector
items.quote: So, all have this issue that all have almost signed 25 % to 30% of their capacity which has been tied up as of now. Balance is pending and there is a possibility that all the PPAs may not be done.

items.statement: CCT revenue target of $200 million revised from 2030 to before 2028
items.quote: Earlier, our expectation to touch $200 million was something in 2030. However, I think that should not take so long now. It should be definitely before 2028.

items.statement: CCT EBITDA margin target of around 15%
items.quote: So going forward, I think comfortably, we should be at EBITDA of 15% more or less.

items.statement: Consolidated blended EBITDA margin target of 18% to 20%
items.quote: On a blended level, we would always look at getting to an easy EBITDA of around 18% to 20%, and that's what we are heading to.

items.statement: Topline could grow 3-4x in next 4 years from current base
items.quote: I don't feel a challenge that it can go another 3, 4 times in the next 4 years o r something like that

items.statement: Acquired 53% stake in CrudeChem Technologies (CCT) in December 2025; further 25% to be acquired by January 2028
items.quote: So, yes, we have already signed with the founders that further 25% has to be sold by them to Finotech's in January '28. It's part of the agreement.

items.statement: Evaluating further inorganic opportunities in US and Middle East, focusing on semiconductors, database, water treatment chemicals
items.quote: There is a lot of excitement coming in the semiconductors businesses, database, water treatment chemicals in U.S. This is something which is already on the cards.

items.statement: $7 million capex already deployed in CCT post-acquisition for capacity expansion
items.quote: In fact, after the acquisition also, the Fineotex has already done a capex of around $7 million.

items.statement: Doubling manufacturing capacity at CCT underway; machines ordered and being installed
items.quote: This month also, we are seeing a great increase in the capacity, a lot of machines have been ordered, and we are just installing it maybe in a couple of weeks, things should also be increased to a great extent.

items.statement: CCT order book described as very strong; Q4 baseline for next step
items.quote: Right now, what has been experienced in the quarter four is something, which is the base what is already done. But already, as I see even now and going times, I think the order book is too strong enough even to comment right now.

items.statement: Healthy demand across textile specialty chemicals globally and in India; US oilfield activity growing
items.quote: Demand trends remain healthy across specialty oilfield chemical categories. Customers globally are increasingly focused on operational efficiencies, production optimization, water management, sustainability and high-performance formulations.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin at 14%; historical Fineotex range 18-28%
items.quote: Firstly, the consolidated EBITDA margin is 14% for Q4.

items.statement: CCT run rate annualized at $90-100 million in Q4
items.quote: if you see the run rate at what we are in quarter four, if you annualize it, it's already touching almost $90 million to $100 million

items.statement: Oil & Gas specialty chemicals now 55-60% of revenue; textile contribution down to 35-36% despite volume growth
items.quote: At the moment, almost oil is 60%. Oil Specialty Chemicals is contributing to almost 55% to 60% in terms of value and revenue for the quarter 4.

items.statement: Textile volumes up 15% YoY in Q4; home textiles and technical textiles driving growth
items.quote: So it's 15% volume has gone up in textile, just to answer that -- complete that question over there, okay?

items.statement: CCT serves marquee global oil service and E&P companies including Halliburton, Schlumberger, Baker Hughes; wallet share potential 5x with existing customers
items.quote: The wallet share increase with the kind of customers we have right now, forget about adding more customers, can easily go to 5x.

items.statement: Consolidated working capital cycle at 79 days; CCT cycle at 80-85 days; comfortable up to 90 days
items.quote: Further, our working capital cycle remains healthy at 79 days despite the significant scale-up in international operations and business integration activities.

items.statement: CCT working capital cycle currently 80-85 days due to raw material shortages and logistics challenges
items.quote: But right now, the number -- the working cycle is almost 80, 85 days, and that's what it is going on right now to answer that question.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with cash on books over INR300 crores post-acquisition and capex
items.quote: Right now, we are looking at certain more opportunities. And so there is a good cash -- cash on bank in Fineotex is more than INR300 crores even as we speak after doing the acquisition and things like this.

items.statement: International revenue contribution increased to 70% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Additionally, our international revenue contribution increased significantly to 70% in quarter four financial year '26, demonstrating the growing scale, traction and the growing global diversification of our business.

items.statement: ROIC at 31% reflecting efficient capital allocation
items.quote: From a return ratio perspective, the company continues to maintain healthy financial metrics with ROIC at 31%, reflecting efficient capital allocation and disciplined execution.

items.statement: Passing on raw material cost increases to customers; maintaining margins through chemistry adjustments and value-based pricing
items.quote: As soon as there is an increase in the prices, we start talking to our customers to pass on the increase. This is something which we have been doing in CCT also and in Fineotex also. That's going very well.

items.statement: Overall plant utilization at 60-62% in Q4; improving in Q1
items.quote: So overall, we are at 60%, 62% broadly at the moment on the quarter 4 numbers. And that's also getting -- in the quarter 1, I can see again there that has been going up.

items.statement: India-US trade deal and UK/EU FTAs expected to boost textile export competitiveness
items.quote: Expanding on to India-US trade deal, its key point, its effect on the textile sector. It has the potential to significantly strengthen Indian textile export competitiveness, which adds further excitement in the domestic textile and garment producers, particularly along with the evolving trade, framework and partnership with the UK and European market.

items.statement: Global logistics and freight challenges easing; worst behind us
items.quote: I think the worst is behind us. I think the last quarter and also the April month was something which was a bit of a challenge to realign, readjust our inventory levels, readjust our pricing.

items.statement: Yusuf Contractor appointed as M&A business head and investor relations lead; PhDs and R&D team expanded at CCT
items.quote: In fact, Mr. Yusuf has also been introduced. He is the M&A business head and also taking care of the investor relationships.

items.statement: No seasonality in CCT oilfield business; drilling and production activity continuous
items.quote: Not at all, actually. This is something which there is no seasonality in this business. It's like drilling and completion, production keeps going on and on.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated top-line growth targeted at low double-digit range
items.quote: This will translate into an overall top line consolidated growth to be in the low double-digit range .

items.statement: FY27 R&D investment guided at INR750-800 crores
items.quote: R&D investments are likely to be around INR750 crores to INR800 crores as we calibrate our portfolio and structurally move towards higher value opportunities

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR300-350 crores for capacity, debottlenecking and replacement
items.quote: We expect capital expenditure for the year to be in the range of INR300 crores to INR350 crores, primarily towards capacity, debottlenecking and replacement capex.

items.statement: International generic business expected to grow low to mid-teens in FY27
items.quote: The international generic business are also likely to grow at a decent amount by low to mid-teen range

items.statement: API business expected to grow high single to low double-digit in FY27
items.value: high single or low double-digit growth
items.quote: and the API business to grow in the high single or low double -digit growth.

items.statement: U.S. business expected to grow 10-15% in INR terms in FY27
items.quote: I expect the U.S. business to grow between 10% to 15% at least.

items.statement: ROW business expected to grow 15%+ in FY27
items.quote: The ROW will continue the growth at 15 -plus percent.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA before R&D margin at ~25% vs 24% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA before R&D stood at INR455 crores, up by about 8% year-on-year with core margins at almost at 25% compared to 24% in the previous year, same quarter.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 gross margin at 71%, within 70-75% range
items.quote: This reflects better business mix with slightly better gross margins at 71%, but staying in the previously mentioned range of about 70% to 75%.

items.statement: Pivya branded business drag estimated at 100-150 bps on margins in FY27
items.quote: from a modeling point of view, I would take about 100 to 150 basis points of impact coming from Pivya, from the branded business in U.S.

items.statement: Core EBITDA margins expected to offset Pivya drag in FY27
items.quote: we believe that the margin trajectory for FY '27, the core EBITDA margins that comes from the generic formulations and API business should be more than sufficient to offset this impact.

items.statement: Management expects margin improvement in FY27 over FY26 levels
items.quote: We will see -- definitely see an improvement in the margins this year.

items.statement: Peptide facility capex completed; no major new capex for peptides
items.quote: So capex is all done. We've already completed the capex of the peptides.

items.statement: F3 ophthalmic line at full capacity; expansion underway
items.quote: In fact, we're doing an expansion of the ophthalmic line, because it's already at full capacity in terms of the other 2 lines.

items.statement: F2 injectable and OSD lines at decent utilization; limited competition opportunities coming
items.quote: In terms of F2, the injectable line and OSD, they are both working at a decent amount. We have a few limited competition opportunities coming, which is what is going to enable them and use these facilities.

items.statement: Contract manufacturing and licensing deals for F2/F3 already generating revenue in FY27
items.quote: No, it's already started. Some of the licensing and some of the contract manufacturing is in progress. So we'll see part contribution from that in FY '27 itself.

items.statement: 6 new U.S. launches in Q4 FY26; further ANDA filings and approvals
items.quote: During the quarter, we had 6 new launches in the U.S. further ANDA filings and approvals and progress on partnership-led opportunities.

items.statement: Peptide portfolio of 5-6 products; 2 filed, rest in progress
items.quote: We've got a couple. The portfolio is about 5 to 6 that we had. Two of them are filed already and the rest are going on.

items.statement: India business grew 4% YoY in Q4 FY26; 5% for full year
items.quote: The business delivered 4% year-on-year growth. The quarter was supported by price-led growth and new launches.

items.statement: Ex-U.S. markets grew 20% for full year FY26; Q4 muted due to high base
items.quote: The ex U.S. markets also continued doing well and grew 20% for the year, whilst the quarter was muted, but the full year grew 20%.

items.statement: API pricing remains premium; solvent cost increases not yet passed on but inventory buffers in place
items.quote: Have we passed it on? No, it's still not a materially big issue for us. As you know, we generally do carry a higher bit of inventory, and that's helped us out right now.

items.statement: Net working capital near INR3,000 crores; up INR50 crores QoQ due to receivables not yet due
items.quote: net working capital stood at -- almost close to INR3,000 crores, an increase of about INR50 crores versus the December levels, mainly driven by receivables that are not at due.

items.statement: Gross debt at INR1,361 crores, broadly flat QoQ
items.quote: Gross debt was at INR1,361 crores broadly in line with the December levels.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA before R&D at INR1,846 crores (25% margin), up 20% YoY
items.quote: For FY '26, EBITDA before R&D and exceptional items stood at INR1,846 crores, representing 25% of revenue and a 20% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: FY26 reported PAT grew 16% to INR675 crores
items.quote: Reported profit after tax grew at 16% to INR675 crores.

items.statement: No major easing assumed in pricing pressure, competition or supply chain volatility for FY27
items.quote: We are not assuming any major easing in pricing pressure, competition or supply chain volatility.

name: S H Kelkar and Company Ltd

items.statement: Management expects adjusted EBITDA margin of 13-14% for H1 FY27, with confidence in maintaining at least 12-13% as a floor
items.quote: We believe that we have taken adequate steps to keep close to this number at least for the first half of this year and we will wait and watch and see and take corrective steps as necessary to ensure that we do not fall below the 12%, 13% EBITDA level which we want to keep as a minimum.

items.statement: Management targets Rs 300 crore+ EBITDA for FY27, at least matching FY25 levels
items.quote: I am actually confident that we will hit the Rs. 300 crore plus EBITDA for this year. Very much so for the first half where we have more visibility, but I am confident that we can do better than '25 or at least at the '25 level for this year.

items.statement: Management expects gross margins around 42% for H1 FY27 despite inflationary pressure
items.quote: We will see that the margin continues to be under pressure, but we will be able to maintain 42% and thereabout for the first half of the year.

items.statement: FY27 capex estimated at Rs 140 crore, front-loaded in first two quarters
items.quote: FY27 capex will be around Rs. 140 crore of capex. This is all the capex, most of it is in front-ended first two quarters.

items.statement: Almere factory in Netherlands fully operational; Vanavate facility expected to start in coming months; Vashivali rebuild by Q3 FY27
items.quote: The Almere factory at Netherlands, a greenfield facility, is now fully operational, thus debottlenecking our European growth, which was approaching full capacity utilization. The Vanavate facility in Maharashtra is expected also to go on stream in the coming months.

items.statement: European capacity doubled with Almere factory and Germany CDC; targeting double-digit growth restoration
items.quote: We have now the new capacity in Europe that will allow us to grow rapidly and restore the double-digit plus growth rates that we want to achieve in the next few years because we have doubled our capacity and I think we can grow that business aggressively.

items.statement: US CDC has $1 million contracted revenue already converting; $200k revenue recognized in FY26
items.quote: We have also already seen b usiness in the US upwards of 1 million contracted, so we are on track for these markets

items.statement: Q4 FY26 adjusted EBITDA at Rs 83 crore, 13.5% margin, steady sequentially
items.quote: From a profitability perspective, adjusted EBITDA stood at Rs. 83 crores, with margins at 13.5%, remaining steady on a sequential basis.

items.statement: CDC opex of Rs 80-85 crore annually for three centres (Germany, Manchester, US) treated as capex-like investment with 3-year breakeven
items.quote: It is roughly when you look at all these three combined in the range of Rs. 80 crore to Rs. 85 crore annually.

items.statement: Raw material inflation 12-13%+ across the board; 40% directly crude-linked, 30% indirectly linked
items.quote: I think the inventory prices are going up, it is very difficult to put an exact number, but upwards of 12%, 13% plus. Pretty much across the Board, there is inflation in operations, in power and fuel, and we expect further inflation on these operating parameters.

items.statement: Company passes on RM price increases; exited Rs 35 crore (Rs 50 crore annualized) low-margin business
items.quote: We have transitioned out of Rs. 35 crore, which is roughly translating about Rs. 50 crore of annual business, which was low-margin or negative-margin in the new environment. We have transitioned out of that business with a one-time sale to these clients.

items.statement: Overall demand muted due to inflation; company expects market share gains to deliver normal growth despite industry slowdown
items.quote: I think yes, overall demand will be muted. I do not see the same kind of growth rate as is normal years. Demand will be muted. There will be a transition phase probably first half of the year while the demand the new sort of post-inflation scenario plays out.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle at ~140 days; expected to remain elevated until inflation stabilizes due to higher inventory strategy
items.quote: So, the cash conversion cycle is around 140 days at the moment. We see that remaining like this till the time that the inflation sort of steady becomes a steady state because in the high inflation we are keeping higher inventory levels.

items.statement: Gross debt Rs 851 crore at March end; may rise temporarily in next 3-6 months for inventory build; target 10% annual reduction thereafter
items.quote: Gross debt end of March we had a Rs. 851 crore and temporarily we do see that it is going to go up a little bit because we are just ensuring a supply security and, in that bargain, we might have to build some inventory. But when you look at a long-term horizon for sure that we are expecting every passing year we should reduce our debt by 10%.

items.statement: Borrowings expected around Rs 800 crore mark in FY27
items.quote: Borrowing should remain around the Rs. 800 crore mark.

items.statement: FX contributed 3-3.5% to revenue growth in Q4 and FY26; revenue transactions FX-neutral but dollar loan creates margin pressure
items.quote: So, it is in the range of 3% Abhijit when we look at either in quarter or in the full year. So, 3% to 3.5% is the revenue gain due to the FX impact.

items.statement: Gross margin at 42.3% in Q4 FY26 (ex-one-off); maintained 40%+ gross margin in H1 FY27 outlook
items.quote: I believe for the first half, we will be able to maintain this margin. As of now, we are covered the raw material and unless there is anything further, we will be able to continue the business at 40% plus gross margin.

items.statement: No full-year guidance given due to Iran-USA standoff uncertainty on raw material supply and pricing; visibility only for H1
items.quote: We are faced with an uncertain future on what is the raw material supply situation, what is the pricing and inflation as a result of the Iran-USA standoff. And given that, we are not really in a position to give you a full-year view.

items.statement: Flavours growth driving margin improvement via operating leverage; no specific MNC order update but plant audited and approved
items.quote: No, I think the Flavours growth has kicked in, so the margins are accordingly better. We also have, operating leverage as a result of the rapid growth in the volumes.

items.statement: Large global accounts confirmed commitment with price increases; monthly monitoring system implemented for cost pass-through
items.quote: I must say that we are pleased that even the large global accounts have sort of responded and confirmed their commitment to the supply with price increases to us.

items.statement: Gaining market share in India as smaller players lack inventory buffers during RM volatility
items.quote: I think first few weeks of this quarter also we believe that we have gained market share in the Indian market especially. So yes, I think the smaller you are the less inventory buffer you hold, the more exposed you are to this volatile situation.

items.statement: Anti-trust judgments against large F&F companies creating buyer interest in alternative suppliers; SHK doing some tolling in Europe but not core
items.quote: On the bit on the anti-trust, there is no further work that or nothing that we are doing, but we do see that as an effect on some of the buyers so that they look at alternative suppliers.

items.statement: Employee cost normalized at Rs 94-95 crore/quarter; Q4 had Rs 6 crore MTM one-off; depreciation up Rs 5-6 crore due to reclassification
items.quote: Our normal employee cost in the range of Rs. 94 to Rs. 95 crore on a quarterly basis at this point of time, which is more or less in line with what we have in December quarter.

items.statement: Organic US expansion preferred over inorganic (12-13x EBITDA multiples imply 5-6 year breakeven vs 4 years organic)
items.quote: When we talk about inorganic, we end up paying 12x, 13x of EBITDA, which translates to roughly 5 to 6 years of break-even time. On an organic strategy, what we are investing in the US, we will have a break-even of roughly 4 years or earlier.

items.statement: Holding 2-3 months RM inventory; committing client prices based on stock-in-hand to avoid mismatch
items.quote: We are more or less looking at 2 to 3 months of inventory raw materials in hand and communicating and committing to the clients the prices based on those raw materials.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target INR650-700 crore, PAT INR100 crore; FY28 revenue INR800-850 crore; FY29 revenue INR1,000 crore with 30% EBITDA margin
items.quote: we remain confident of achieving our FY27 goals of INR650 crores in revenue and INR100 crores PAT in FY27, while continuing our journey toward long-term aspiration of INR1,000 crores revenue by FY29

items.statement: FY27 revenue could exceed INR650 crore by up to INR50 crore if LatAm registrations accelerate
items.quote: we believe that INR650 crores is a very, very achievable number, but this number could increase considering if we get more registrations or queries from the ministry and the registration happens in the timely manner. So, probably this number could go plus/minus -- sorry, not minus but plus INR50 crores

items.statement: Oncology EBITDA margin ~32% (peptide 40%, routine 25%, peptide 40% of oncology sales)
items.quote: So, the mix of peptide products in the overall oncology products will be 40%. So, overall, you can say the EBITDA margins will be roughly around 30% to 32% in case of onco products.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin target 26-27% at INR650-700 crore revenue
items.quote: So, probably the EBITDA margins at INR650 crores should be around 26% to 27% and INR800 crores to INR850 crores, it should be around 28%.

items.statement: Gross margin expected to improve to 52-53% in FY27 from ~49% in FY26 as regulated market sales increase
items.quote: As I told the previous investor also that once the regulated sales revenue come into play from the second quarter of FY27, the gross margins will be roughly around 52% to 53%.

items.statement: Oncology revenue ~INR100 crore in FY26, targeting INR150 crore in FY27 and INR300 crore by FY29
items.quote: the revenue was roughly close to INR100 crores in FY26 for oncology. So, this number we are projecting to increase by up to INR300 crores by FY29. And next year the contribution will increase to INR150 crores.

items.statement: Total capex INR260-270 crore for hormones, oncology expansion, biosimilars clinical trials, R&D and BE; INR46 crore spent in FY26, INR90 crore planned FY27, INR90-100 crore FY28
items.quote: for hormones, oncology expansion, biosimilar with clinical trials and the R&D and the bioequivalence what we have to do, all these four projects roughly the capex was around INR260 crores to INR270 crores, out of which INR46 crores capex we have already done in FY26. So, FY27, we would do roughly around INR90 crores and another INR90 crores to INR100 crores in FY28.

items.statement: Unit 6 hormones capex ~INR65 crore, 50% spent in FY26, targeting WHO GMP and commercialization in ROW before November
items.quote: So, roughly around INR65 crores of capex was to be done and roundabout we have already spent 50% of the total capex in FY26. So, we believe that before November, we'll try to get the WHO GMP and do the commercialization in the ROW market.

items.statement: Oncology capacity utilization rose from 30-35% to 65% due to Annexure 1 guideline changes; INR50 crore expansion adding one line with three lyophilizers underway
items.quote: the capacity utilization came down from, I mean, from 35% to 40% to 65%. So, we had to make an immediate expansion in our facility and we have made an allocation of roughly around INR50 crores to make those expansions

items.statement: Oncology to contribute 25-30% of FY29 revenue (INR300 crore), non-onco 70% (beta-lactam, cephalosporin, general injectables, oral solids BE); biosimilars and hormones excluded from base INR1,000 crore
items.quote: So, 25% to 30% contribution will be from onco, and 70% will be contribution from beta-lactam, cephalo, general injectables, and other oral solids where we are conducting the bioequivalence studies. This will not include the revenues from the biosimilar and hormone.

items.statement: Geographic mix for INR1,000 crore: LATAM 30% (Mexico 70%, Colombia 30%), Algeria 15-16%, French West Africa 10%, GCC 10-15%, Russia/Eurasia 5-7%, Southeast Asia remainder; domestic only peptide ~INR50 crore
items.quote: overall, LATAM will contribute roughly around 30% in INR1,000 crores revenue, 15% shall be from Algeria and other MENA countries, French West Africa will have a 10% contribution and GCC shall have a roughly around 10% to 15% contribution. And remaining is from Southeast Asia and Eurasia.

items.statement: Annual interest cost ~INR11 crore to remain flat as borrowings unchanged; working capital not expected to increase with revenue scaling
items.quote: Annual interest cost will roughly remain the same, sir, it won't change because we have not increased our borrowings. Even the borrowings have almost remained the same. And working capital probably shouldn't be increasing considering that the cash conversion cycle is going to improve quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Four major European registrations expected by May-June 2025; targeting 7-8 regulated market registrations by end CY2027; Russian GMP audit passed
items.quote: we have almost got four registrations now, major registration in European countries. However, the certificate is yet to be announced so that we have not made it public, but probably by end of May or June, we'll get the registration. So, now we are slowly moving towards the regulated markets and we expect at least seven, eight registrations before end of calendar year 2027.

items.statement: Key risk: geopolitical disruptions (Strait of Hormuz, war) delaying payments/deliveries; contingency: hormones/biosimilars can add INR200 crore to ensure INR1,000 crore target
items.quote: if this situation doesn't arise, Kwality can smoothly reach a INR1,000 crores mark. However, to our investors and for our own, I mean, as a keeping biological and hormone as a contingency plan, we believe that if something goes wrong even then we can reach INR800 crores, INR850 crores mark, and additional revenues from hormone and biosimil ars can help us cross that INR1,000 crores mark

items.statement: Plan to appoint KPMG as auditor, announcement expected in next 1-2 quarters
items.quote: probably we are closing with KPMG, sir.

items.statement: Alteplase dropped due to patient recruitment difficulty; replaced by Pembrolizumab (Keytruda biosimilar) targeting pre-patent expiry launch
items.quote: Alteplase has been replaced by Pembrolizumab, which we believe that Keytruda is a blockbuster molecule and Kwality can launch it before the patency get expired.

items.statement: 85% raw material from India, 15% from China; API cost increases offset by USD/EUR appreciation; no plan to pass cost increases to customers
items.quote: majorly our 85% of material is from India, 15% is from China and there has not been much increase in our case, the API prices, and it has been replaced by the increase dollar price.

items.statement: GCC sales to shift from legacy products (20-25% margin) to BE products (30-35% margin) in next 2-3 quarters, replacing revenues with same partners
items.quote: we are going to reduce the current sales revenues in those GCC countries, and we are going to replace it with the bioequivalence product first, wherein, the margins and EBITDAs are roughly around 35%.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue ~INR150-160 crore (similar to Q4 FY26); Q2 FY27 INR160-170 crore; Q4 FY27 target >INR200 crore; quarter-on-quarter growth 15-20%
items.quote: So, probably the Q1 for FY27 will be the same as Q4 of FY26. It will be around INR150 crores -- between INR150 crores to INR160 crores. But the second quarter of FY27, we believe the numbers would increase to INR160 crores, INR170 crores. So, I think quarter -on-quarter, there will be increase of 15% to 20% increase in sale. And quarter four, our target is that we should cross INR200 crores mark.

items.statement: FY26: 55 regulatory submissions, ~10 approvals; Q1-Q2 FY27: 6 more approvals expected; all 55 by end CY2027; 25-30 new submissions planned FY27
items.quote: FY26, we made total 55 submission, sir, out of which we got roughly around 10. And in Q1 and Q2 FY27, we might get six more. And all these 55 registration we will get before end of calendar year '27. And we are in the process of making 25 or 30 more submission this financial year.

items.statement: FY27 standalone revenue target 30-40% growth over FY26 INR7,005 cr
items.quote: if we look at FY26 number, we mentioned it will be a 30% to 40% growth from this number. So we're in line with that because we have the order.

items.statement: FY27 standalone EBITDA margin target 11-12%
items.quote: Now in terms of our EBITDA, we are targeting that same 11%, 12% EBITDA that we have mentioned. That will be in line with that.

items.statement: FY27 order inflow target INR10,000-12,000 cr
items.quote: Now more than that, we are also targeting about INR10,000 crores, INR12,000 crores of new order inflow to come in this financial year, which will provide us good visibility extending up to FY '30.

items.statement: FY27 debt reduction target INR600-800 cr
items.quote: We anticipate somewhere between INR600 crores to INR800 crores of debt will be reduced in this financial year.

items.statement: Net debt-free target by FY28
items.quote: our agenda is to be a net debt-free balance sheet by FY28. We are very confident of this because of the continued cash generation from our EPC operations, our MDO operations and the growing income from our InvIT holdings.

items.statement: MDO revenue FY27 ~INR2,500 cr, FY28 ~INR3,100 cr, FY29 ~INR4,000 cr
items.quote: what we anticipate from the current INR1,600 crores of revenue in this year, we expect revenue to increase to about INR2,500 crores or so in FY27, which will further increase to about INR3,000 plus INR100 crores in FY28. And eventually, I think in FY29, we should be somewhere in the range of around INR4,000 crores of revenue coming from this sector.

items.statement: Coal production target 57 million metric tons by FY29
items.quote: Now we remain committed to achieving our annual coal production of around 57 million metric tons by FY29, which at its full capacity would represent a significant part of India's total coal output and positioning DBL as a critical partner in the nation's energy security.

items.statement: FY26 order inflows INR18,548 cr, exceeding guidance
items.quote: I'm also very happy to report that for the FY26, DBL has secured total order inflows of INR18,548 crores, which is much higher than our original guided figure.

items.statement: Current order book ~INR28,000 cr, diversified across segments
items.quote: The order book is very healthy right now at almost INR28,000 crores. So we are very confident of the revenue that we should be able to get.

items.statement: Bid pipeline INR80,000 cr+ across sectors
items.quote: Our current bid pipeline stands at INR80,000 crores plus across sectors.

items.statement: INR169 cr incremental investment for 11 HAM assets to InvIT
items.quote: Sir, for the 11 assets in total, it is less than INR200 crores, INR169 crores to be exact right now, which is there on in the presentation Slide number 24, you will find it there.

items.statement: Transmission and solar equity requirement INR1,600 cr total, DBL 15% (INR240 cr)
items.quote: let's say, in solar, about INR1,200 crores of equity and in transmission about INR400 crores of equity has to go, now what we are doing is of the INR1,600 crores of equity, we are looking to find a solution that 85% of the capital that has to be invested as equity comes from the investor, while 15% is put by on DBL's own balance sheet.

items.statement: Consolidated FY26 EBITDA margin 19.6%
items.quote: The consolidated EBITDA stood at INR1,766 crores with an EBITDA margin of 19.6%.

items.statement: MDO margin stabilised 24-25%, improvement expected with scale and coal handling plant
items.quote: You're right, sir. You're right. That range is the right range to take, and there will be improvement on that, yes.

items.statement: Transmission EBITDA margin upward of 24%, IRR high teens
items.quote: In terms of EBITDA margin, in transmission, it is upward of 24%. IRR would be high teens in both the projects.

items.statement: Raw material cost escalation not fully passed through; government indexation partial
items.quote: So it's not completely passed through, and we will be facing those challenges as well as will be the rest of the industry. The -- I guess the saving grace here is the government is aware of this issue.

items.statement: Receivables up INR400 cr due to JJM uncertified 10% pending hydro testing
items.quote: Jal Jeevan Mission, the last 10%, which is basically uncertified one, which will be paid once we will do the last hydro testing. So that INR400 crores will be paid once we will do the hydro testing.

items.statement: Standalone debt INR1,880 cr, consolidated INR7,082 cr as of Mar 31, 2026
items.quote: Outstanding debt as of March 31, 2026 stood at approximately INR1,800 crores at the stand-alone level and INR7,082 crores at the consol level.

items.statement: InvIT units worth INR1,600 cr on balance sheet; net debt ~INR300 cr if sold
items.quote: Now against our stand-alone debt of INR1,880 crores today, we hold nearly INR1,600 crores of InvIT units on the balance sheet. Had we chosen to sell all these units, our net debt would have been roughly INR300 crores or so.

items.statement: Average cost of borrowing ~9%
items.quote: So, our cost of borrowing around 9% on average basis.

items.statement: 11 HAM assets to Anantam InvIT by Q1 FY28; InvIT units value INR1,800 cr, net equity creation INR1,500-1,600 cr
items.quote: The next tranche of 11 assets is expected to require less than INR200 crores of incremental investment while generating InvIT units valued at around INR1,800 crores, implying a net equity value creation of INR1,500 crores to INR1,600 crores.

items.statement: Total InvIT units value after 11 assets transfer: INR3,000-3,300 cr
items.quote: Sir, about INR3,000 crores, INR3,300 crores in between that will be total InvIT value that we'll have including the seven assets that we've done and these 11 that will go, so I mean, against the total 18 assets that we have that we will be putting in the InvIT, we will have InvIT units worth between INR3,000 crores to INR3,300 crores.

items.statement: FY26 coal production 28.72 million metric tons (Siarmal 22.35, Pachhwara 6.37)
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, DBL coal production for FY26 stands at 28.72 million metric tons.

items.statement: FY26 standalone revenue INR7,005 cr (-22.2% YoY), PAT INR841 cr (+170% YoY)
items.quote: On a stand-alone basis, the revenue for FY26 stood at INR7,005 crores as compared to INR9,004 crores in FY25, reflecting a Y-o-Y change of approximately 22.2% negative. EBITDA for the year stood at INR734 crores against INR903 crores in the previous year, representing a Y-o-Y change of negative 18.72%, while the profit after tax stood at INR841 crores as against INR311 crores in FY25.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated revenue INR8,984 cr (-20.6% YoY), PAT INR1,398 cr (+66% YoY)
items.quote: On consol basis, FY26 revenue stood at INR8,984 crores as compared to INR11,317 crores in previous year, reflecting a Y-o-Y change of negative 20.6%. The consolidated EBITDA stood at INR1,766 crores with an EBITDA margin of 19.6%, while profit after tax stood at INR1,398 crores as against INR840 crores in FY25.

items.statement: FY26 InvIT distribution income ~INR100 cr; dividend+interest INR64.5 cr
items.quote: Total dividend and interest income during FY26 from both the units are INR64.5 crores. And the distribution was higher. So the total distribution was close to INR100 crores.

items.statement: MDO Q4 margin hit by 6 mt coal stockpile due to delayed government evacuation and rack shortage
items.quote: See, the margin that you are talking about that has come down in the mining business temporarily right now is primarily because the evacuation by the government could not be done on time. So there is at the Siarmal mine, right now, we have about 6 million metric tons of stock, which is lying at site because of delayed evacuation by the government and because of unavailability of racks.

items.statement: Transmission and solar projects commissioning timeline 2 years from start
items.quote: 2 years from April '26? Rohan Suryavanshi: Yes. that is broad line, whenever we start the project, so 2 years from there, it will go

items.statement: Order book stood at INR1,432 crores as of 31 March 2026 on a consolidated basis
items.quote: Our order book as of 31st March stood at INR1,432 crores on a consolidated basis providing strong visibility for future growth.

items.statement: Management expects to continue growing at a similar pace in FY27 and FY28 backed by large ticket orders due this financial year
items.quote: We will continue to grow at a similar rate, in this particular financial year and the subsequent financial year backed by the size of the order book that we are going to have.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated PAT margin expanded 185 bps to 12%, EBITDA margin expanded 114 bps to 24%
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded by 114 basis points to 24% in FY26, while PAT margin expanded by 185 basis points to 12% in FY26.

items.statement: Unit 3 phase one civil work complete, machinery received and installation ongoing, MEP and facade works in progress
items.quote: Unit 3 civil work is already complete for phase one. So, phase two civil work is still taking place. Some of the machinery, which we have ordered, we have already received those machinery and installation process going on.

items.statement: Inventory holding days improved in FY26 and will improve further as production orders increase and in-house test facilities come online
items.quote: There is an improvement in this financial year and this is something, which is going to be in the subsequent financial years as well.

items.statement: Additional acquisition by subsidiary Apollo Defence Industries expected to complete before end of FY27
items.quote: We are pleased to announce that an additional acquisition by our subsidiary Apollo Defence Industries Private Limited is expected to be completed before end of this financial year, which will significantly complement our organic growth and overall strengthen our business.

items.statement: Entering land systems including armament electronics, fire control systems, battle tanks, ICVs, artillery platforms, vehicle-mounted counter-drone systems with trials in upcoming quarters
items.quote: FY26-'27 will mark our serious entry into key defense domains including armament electronics, fire control systems, and battle tanks, infantry combat vehicles, and artillery platforms, vehicle-mounted counter-drone systems with trials scheduled in the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Received DPIIT lifetime license covering UAVs, INS systems, radars, torpedoes, underwater mines, ATGM, decoys, chaffs and flares, aerial bombs, rockets, missiles, and loitering munition
items.quote: We have received a DPIIT license covering UAVs, INS systems, radars, torpedoes, underwater mines, ATGM, decoys, chaffs and flares, aerial bombs, rockets, missiles, and loitering munition. This is a remarkable achievement, which are a lifetime license for the company.

items.statement: R&D expenditure at 8% of revenue (INR72 crores) in FY26 with zero attrition in R&D team
items.quote: We made the highest investment in R&D within the industry during FY26 with R&D expenditure amounting to 8% of revenue, which is around INR72 crores in absolute terms. Notably, we recorded zero attrition within our R&D team during this year.

items.statement: Expecting large ticket orders to materialize in FY27, order book size to increase significantly on standalone and consolidated basis
items.quote: We are expecting a large ticket projects, which we have been quite vocal about for last one year. And the time has come, and the clocking of these large ticket orders are due to come, and anytime in this financial year we would be getting and our order book size also will cumulatively increase both on standalone, as well as on a consolidated basis.

items.statement: Export audits by interested customers have started, new facility readiness will enable firm commitment on export opportunities
items.quote: The audits by some of our -- the customers of interest, you know, who are interested to work with us and place orders which are export opportunities, you know, the audits have already started actually.

items.statement: Mine variants alone represent immediate market size of INR4,000-4,500 crores, with orders expected this financial year and beyond
items.quote: All these -- only these variants of mine alone would be a cumulative, you know, a market, you know, in very immediate market size of something like INR4,000 crores to INR4,500 odd crores, you know, that that we are expecting, which -- out of which some of the, you know, orders, you know, which we will be getting in this financial year, some maybe next-next after financial year on a continual basis

items.statement: IDL Explosives FY26 revenue around INR380 crores, undergoing transformation with operational losses reduced significantly, guidance from Q3 FY27
items.quote: IDL last year performance stood at around INR380 crores, little less than INR380 crores. So, it will continue to maintain a similar level of performance. So, this is primarily a huge shift of management, which have been there for decades. Now, our outlook towards IDL is totally different.

items.statement: TNT 500 tons and HMX 50 tons expansion for industrial explosive requirements, larger defense expansion DPRs getting ready
items.quote: The capacities are not limited to that. For higher capacities for the defense explosive requirements, you know -- and you know, we would be doing a very large expansion. So, the DPRs are have -- are getting ready and as and when, you know, we feel it to be, you know, necessary that, you know, it has to be opened in the market, you know, we will keep, you know, disclosing.

items.statement: Standalone revenue growth was 36% in FY26 vs 45-50% guidance due to delayed approvals, but management will maintain similar momentum
items.quote: Certain projects which we expected to be, you know, executed in the last quarter of, you know, previous financial year, that couldn't happen because of the certain approvals, you know, which got pending actually from our customer, okay, which was still lying. That's how the holding, you know, inventory is all about actually. That's something that we would be getting eventually, you know, the gener

items.statement: DAC approval for large Navy order (mines/torpedoes) expected any moment
items.quote: So, we are expecting the DAC approval any moment. As and when we receive, we'll definitely keep you posted, but this is something which is going to happen very shortly.

items.statement: Developed Mini Torpedo, sensor suits for underwater autonomous vehicles, fiber optic gyro-based INS systems in FY26
items.quote: In FY26, our focused and rigorous R&D efforts culminated in successful development of products such as Mini Torpedo, sensor suits for underwater autonomous vehicles, fiber optic gyro-based INS systems, and several other advanced solutions.

items.statement: Setting up specialized RF seeker testing facility in upcoming Hardware Park unit
items.quote: And the programs are -- these are our internal R&D programs and we are investing heavily on that, and we are setting up a specialized RF seeker testing facility in our upcoming unit in Hardware Park.

items.statement: Presence across every indigenous missile program of the country, equipment going into all programs that go into production
items.quote: Any indigenous missile program which is going for production which you hearsay, you know, through the news, social media or, you know, the defense news or any other, you know, media, you know, all those programs we will be having our, you know, equipment going in it actually. items.statement: Company maintains net debt-free position with INR782 crores cash and equivalents as of March 31, 2026

items.statement: Solapur greenfield planned for regulated markets after initial ROW focus; FDA inspection timeline key for ramp-up
items.quote: Yes, yes, that is the plan very much.

items.statement: R&D spend at 3.6% of sales in FY26; expected to reach 4% in next 1-2 years then settle
items.quote: As far as settling down, I don't think we'll cross 4%, right? We'll probably be at 4% in the next year or 2. And then it should settle down.

items.statement: Solvents (12-13% of cost) increased significantly; freight costs impacted from Feb 2026; moved from gas to briquette boilers stabilizing operational costs

items.statement: Added 49 new customers in FY26, total base ~900; CDMO contracts longer-term, generic API contracts typically 1-2 years

items.statement: Actively evaluating inorganic opportunities to enhance platform and extract more value from API pipeline via allied platforms
items.quote: So we are actively looking and the direction is to basically enhance the platform that we already have. So our goal is to extract more value from our pretty large and diverse pipeline of APIs.

items.statement: Geopolitical conflicts and tariff uncertainties disrupt supply chains, elevate logistics and energy costs; fire at Dahej intermediate facility caused INR20 crore loss
items.quote: From an expense perspective, yes, we have booked a loss due to fire in our other expenses to the extent of INR20 crores.

items.statement: Net exporter benefiting from rupee depreciation; FY26 forex gain of INR31 crores on P&L (INR11 crores in Q4)
items.quote: For the entire year on the P&L, we have seen a net gain of about INR31 crores on the P&L. There is about INR11 crores of gain that we have booked for Q4 and about INR20 crores for the full year that we have booked.

items.statement: Employee cost increase due to accrued performance bonuses linked to strong company performance
items.quote: So on the employee cost side, we have accrued performance bonuses since the performance for the company is good. There are certain performance bonuses which are payable to the employees, and those have been accrued in the last quarter.

items.statement: High potent API pipeline: 28 products (12 validated, 7 advanced, 9 in development); commercial revenue expected from FY28
items.quote: The high potent API portfolio remains on the development path with 28 products in the pipeline. 12 of these products are validated, seven products are in advanced stages of development and the remaining Nine products are progressing well through land development stages.

items.statement: Fully settled Right of Recompense obligation with INR101 crore payment to consortium lenders on March 31, 2026, clearing all legacy dues and covenants.

items.statement: Board approved buyback of 1 crore shares at INR180 per share aggregating INR180 crores in April 2026; promoters not participating.
items.quote: In April 2026, our Board approved a buyback of 1 crores shares at INR180 per share, aggregating to INR180 crores.

items.statement: Expects mid-teen revenue growth of 15-17% in FY27 and high-teen growth in FY28 based on won orders and ramp-ups, excluding potential recovery of lost US business.
items.quote: for fiscal 2027, what we expect as on date is maybe a mid-teen growth, 15% to 17% growth, something like that. And again, same kind of growth would be there or maybe a bit on a higher -- a high-teen growth in the fiscal 2028.

items.statement: US exports declined ~30% in FY26 due to tariffs peaking at 53%; expects recovery from Q1 FY27 as tariffs normalized to 25% and customers re-engage.

items.statement: European revenue grew ~25% in FY26; 60% of new nominations from European customers; structural tailwinds from China+1 sourcing and Tier 1 relationships.
items.quote: Revenue from Europe grew by almost 25% during the year compared to previous fiscal. And out of that, 60% of our new business nominations came from European customers only.

items.statement: Domestic revenue grew 50% YoY in FY26 with both bearing rings and auto components contributing; early contributions from EV and industrial programs expected to grow over 2-3 years.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded from 49.4% to 51.5% in FY26 due to favorable product mix shift to higher-value auto components and better raw material management.
items.quote: our gross margin expanded meaningfully from 49.4% to 51.5% in fiscal 2026, reflecting the positive shift in product mix towards higher-value machine auto components and a better raw material management.

items.statement: Auto components now ~50% of revenue; targets maintaining 50% share; machined components constitute 85% of revenue.

items.statement: Current utilization at 62-63% of achievable capacity; certain product ranges at 80-85% utilization requiring incremental capex.

items.statement: Monthly dispatch schedule of INR115-125 crores for H1 FY27; FY26 order wins ramping from 10-20% to 50-60% peak levels over FY27; new customer programs may materialize in FY28.

items.statement: Container availability delays of 2-3 weeks and extended transit days; managing via premium payments and warehouse/consignment inventory.

items.statement: Exploring inorganic opportunities in hot forging/value-added processes in US/Europe at preliminary stage; open to acquisitions with surplus cash.

items.quote: Our business generated INR190 crores in our operating cash flow and spent hardly INR36 crores on capex, leaving substantial free cash for the company to deploy.

items.quote: In line with our long-standing pricing philosophy, all of these incremental costs, including higher freight, energy, and other ancillary costs, have been transparently passed on to all our customers with effect from 1st April 2026 itself.

items.statement: Zinc dross supply secured despite geopolitical disruption; March saw import freeze from Middle East and Europe delays, forcing domestic procurement at higher LME
items.quote: During the month of March, there was a complete freeze in imports from the Middle East and also there were huge delays in shipments from Europe. Hence, raw materials during the month of March had to be procured from the domestic market at a much higher LME.

items.statement: 90+ specialized zinc oxide grades (up from 80+ in FY25); non-rubber share to grow materially after Dahej commissioning; ceramics, pharma, specialty chemicals targeted
items.quote: As we close FY26, we are now offering more than 90 specialized grades of zinc oxide to our customers, up from the 80 plus grades we had at the end of FY25.

items.statement: 200+ domestic, 50+ international accounts; supply to all major Indian tire makers and 9 of top 10 global tire companies; wallet share zero at some customer plants in Gujarat
items.quote: Today, our customer franchise now extends to more than 200 domestic customers and also perhaps 50 plus international accounts. And we are proud today to supply to every major Indian tire manufacturer and also to nine out of the world's top 10 companies.

items.statement: Exports 10-15% of sales; EU and US trade agreements opening export opportunities for tire customers
items.quote: As we've mentioned, yes, so the export to sales is roughly between 10% and 15%.

items.statement: Rolling inventory on FIFO basis; no separate inventory gain quantification; March supply disruption forced spot purchases at higher prices
items.quote: Ours is a rolling way of inventory valuation and a FIFO basis of consumption. So, every quarter on quarter the inventories keep coming in and the sale price gets established every month on month.

items.statement: Strong balance sheet and financial strength enabled raw material security during supply chain disruption
items.quote: Our scale, our financial strength, our balance sheet, our two-decade plus track record of honouring every commitment to our suppliers, and our unmatched relationships with the dross suppliers across India and different parts of the world have made us the preferred customer.

items.statement: Zinc oxide ~3.5-5% of tire compound by weight, ~1-1.5% of tire cost; tire industry utilization healthy; ATMA welcomes Budget 26-27 for long-term demand
items.quote: On the quantitative terms, roughly 3.5% to 5% of the compound is zinc oxide. And in terms of cost, how much zinc oxide contributes to a tire, it's roughly about 1% to 1.5% of the tire cost.

items.statement: Zinc oxide utilization ~77%, can reach 86-87%; zinc sulphate ~60%; Naidupeta brownfield debottlenecking complete by Dec 2026; Dahej Phase 1 utilization 35-40% in H2 FY27, 65-70% in FY28
items.quote: for zinc oxide, as Anuj just mentioned, the capacity utilization currently is about 77%. We can easily take this up to 86% to 87%, so we still have about 10% of the spare capacity. The zinc sulphate business, which has gradually been growing, is today running at approximately 60% of the installed capacity

items.statement: Solar Phase 1 at Naidupeta commissioned FY26 (~INR2 cr, 3-3.5 yr payback); further renewable investments planned at Naidupeta and Dahej

items.statement: Healthy order book and demand projections for May-June; June projections at par with April-May levels
items.quote: Even as we speak the months of May, June, we have a very, very healthy order book and a very healthy demand projection. So, currently we are not witnessing any slowdown from the tire industry.

items.statement: Top 3-4 players control 60-67% market share; long tail of 30-40 small players; JG largest by significant margin; Dahej capacity largest in Western India
items.quote: Yes, the top three-four people would be controlling about 60% to 67% share in the market, but there in there is a long tail of smaller-smaller zinc oxide players prevalent in most regions, maybe 30-40 of them.

items.statement: Geopolitical conflict disrupting supply chains (zinc dross imports, energy prices); ceramic sector in Morbi facing gas shortage plant shutdowns (temporary)
items.quote: There is no denying the fact that the war has impacted virtually every industrial supply chain across the world, and zinc dross, our primary raw material, has been no exception.

items.statement: Recycled rubber pilot trials positive; commercial scale project under development with adjacent products; will share capex, capacity, timelines, revenue potential later
items.quote: The pilot trials have just not continued, the feedback we have received from our customers has been extremely positive and validating. On the back of this strong customer endorsement, we are now actively working on a detailed commercial scale project for this product.

items.statement: Naidupeta facility only IATF-certified zinc oxide plant globally; also WHO GMP and pharmacopeia certifications; multi-year process to achieve
items.quote: Our Naidupeta facility continues to be a structural differentiator for us. It remains the only IATF certified zinc oxide facility anywhere in the world, and it also carries the WHO GMP accreditation along with several pharmacopeia certifications.

items.statement: Break-even utilization 60-65%; prefer operating above 75%; Dahej startup costs small, volume growth to compensate
items.quote: Our facilities would break even above 60%, 60% to 65%, but ideally, we like to operate our capacities above 75%. And the moment we reach 80%, 85%, 80 plus we start looking at more expansions.

items.statement: Government working on mandates beyond E20 including E85 and E100; draft notification issued

items.statement: Ethanol prices under juice and B-heavy route not revised for 3 years despite higher cane costs

items.statement: Positive conversations started on ethanol price revision given crude at Rs 111 and currency at Rs 96

items.statement: Target 35% EBITDA margin for PLA business excluding incentives
items.quote: We have not considered the benefit of incentive while guiding 35% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Integrated sugar and bagasse availability gives significant logistics and energy cost advantage for PLA

items.statement: PLA plant designed for multiple grades across packaging, 3D printing and other applications
items.quote: Our plant is built well to handle different grades, different applications, etc.

items.statement: Central and UP government mandates on non-plastic alternatives progressing; three-pronged approach with customers
items.quote: There is also a mandate being worked on by the UP Government. They have already formed a committee and are taking steps to move forward with the non-plastic mandate as well. So, to summarize, there are three fronts: the Central Government mandate, the UP Government mandate, and customers.

items.statement: Sugar season 2025-26 net production estimated at 28 million tonnes after 3 million tonnes diversion; closing stock 4.3 million tonnes
items.quote: After accounting for 3 million tonnes of diversion, net production is expected to be around 28 million tonnes.
