items.statement: UP sugar recovery 11.24% in FY26 vs 11.28% prior year; cane crushed 1,043 lakh quintals up 5.2%
items.quote: The Company crushed 1,043 lakh quintals of cane during the season, which is up 5.2%, while the gross recovery remained broadly around the same range, marginally lower at 11.24% vis-a-vis 11.28%.

items.statement: Sugarcane price increased INR 30 from INR 370 to INR 400 per quintal in FY26
items.quote: Against this backdrop, Balrampur concluded FY26 on a stable note, with the sugar segment delivering resilient performance despite an increase of INR30 in sugarcane price from INR370 to INR400 per quintal.

items.statement: PLA customers require committed volumes and supply schedules before switching from existing suppliers
items.quote: Because customers are saying, You need to come in with production, commit your volumes to us, and specify when and how much you will supply.

items.statement: PLA cost advantage from integrated sugar and bagasse; peers with sugar assets would have similar basic advantages
items.quote: Yes, they will have that same sugar available and same bagasse available. But, ours is a group, so we have more advantages than anyone. Also we are located close to each other in two plants, but yes definitely, if a sugar factory owner with a large size wants to do it, he would have the same basic advantages except whatever, this 2 years of research which has gone into this PLA business.

items.statement: Cane yield impact from fertilizer availability uncertain until September-October assessment
items.quote: If you want an honest answer to this question, do not ask anybody before September. But yes, if there is a negative tenor to the crop yield, probably some rainfall quantum etc, best assessed in August, mid-August.

items.statement: Promoters participated INR 193 crore in preferential issue proportionate to holding
items.quote: There is no dilution and promoters have participated to the extent of INR193 crore, which is proportionate to their current holding.

items.statement: Next PLA expansion timeline estimated at 15 months
items.quote: 15 odd months is very possible. 15 months is very possible.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance for FY27 is more than 15%
items.quote: So, we are retaining our revenue growth of more than 15%. So definitely, we are going to have more than 15% as a revenue growth for '26-'27.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY27 is more than 28%
items.quote: EBITDA margins will be more than 28%.

items.statement: Order inflow guidance for FY27 is more than INR 55,000 crores including QRSAM
items.quote: The order inflow we are expecting this year more than INR55,000 crores. That includes, of course, QRSAM, which we are expecting very soon.

items.statement: R&D investment target for FY27 is around INR 2,200 crores
items.quote: So, this year, we have targeted a value of around INR2,200 crores investment in R&D.

items.statement: Capex target for FY27 is more than INR 1,200 crores with 20%+ growth
items.quote: And same thing is the capex also, again, 20%-plus growth. So, we are targeting more than INR1,200 crores as a capital investment for this year.

items.statement: Defense to non-defense revenue ratio guidance for FY27 is 90:10 +/- 1%
items.quote: And defense to non-defense ratio, more or less, it will be 90% to 10%, maybe plus/minus 1%.

items.statement: INR830 crores capex in FY26 mainly for grain distilleries in Gorakhpur and Kashipur (~INR400 crores)
items.quote: Actually, there are two distilleries largely, which are the main capital expenditure. One is the grain distillery in Gorakhpur, and one is the grain distillery in Kashipur. items.statement: Prepaid INR804 crores debt in Q4 FY26 (INR467 crores via equity issue, rest from cash flow), saving INR20 crores interest cost
items.quote: One point is that the company has prepaid almost about INR804 crores in this quarter, which has been funded by INR467 crores through equity issue, which we did in November '25 and rest of the funds has been put in through the cash flow. So, this INR804 crores include the long-term debt, the working capital, and the short-term loans resulting in INR20 crores saving in the interest cost.

items.quote: This year we have a normal liability of say about INR268 crores, which in liquor, it is INR168 crores, and INR100 crores in Chemical. Anand Singhal: Both we will pay, and apart from this, we will try to make some of the prepayments

items.statement: Debt-to-equity improved from 0.7x (FY23) to 0.5x (FY26); interest coverage from 2.3x to 3.0x; ROCE from 7.7% to 11.9%; RONW from 7.7% to 11.3%
items.quote: Similarly, if you look at some of our ratios, our debt-to-equity ratio has gone down from 0.7x in FY23 to 0.5x this year. Our interest coverage ratio has gone up from 2.3x in FY23 to 3.0x in FY26. And if you look at ROCE over the last few years, it has gone from 7.7% in FY23 to 11.9% in FY26, and RONW has gone up from 7.7% in FY23 to 11.3% in FY26.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded to 15.5% in FY26 (up 162 bps); PAT margin 6.9% (up 84 bps)
items.quote: EBITDA has been INR654 crores, which is up 24.5% over last year. And the EBITDA margin itself is up to 15.5%, up 162 basis points. And we have seen EBITDA growth more or less across the business.

items.statement: Chemicals EBIT margin improved to 11.7% in FY26 despite 10.4% revenue decline; Q4 Chemicals EBIT margin 12.2%
items.quote: In the Chemicals business, we've had a net revenue of INR1,203 crores in FY26, which is down 10.4%, but our EBIT at INR141 crores is up 12.5% and our EBIT margins are up to 11.7%.

items.statement: Bio-Fuels EBIT margin reached 7.8% in FY26 with EBIT up 103.3%; grain prices stable, DDGS prices improving
items.quote: For the Bio-Fuels business, an excellent year with the 40.9% growth delivering a top-line of INR1,470 crores in FY26 and an EBIT of INR115 crores, which is nearly double, which is up 103.3% and an EBIT margin of 7.8%.

items.statement: Potable Spirits Q4 EBIT margin 22.1%; IMFL contributes 31% of segment revenue (5-6% Amrut), up from mid-teens last year
items.quote: For the Potable Spirit segment, I think I've already shared the number, which for Q4 were 22%, the EBIT margin. Now, I think the point that we made is we made certain assumptions in terms of ethanol, the growing market premiumization, as well as strengths of IGL.

items.statement: India achieved 20% ethanol blending ahead of 2030 target; discussions ongoing for 21-22% blending and flexi-fuel vehicles
items.quote: India reached 20% blending as far as Bio-Fuels is concerned, which drove quite a lot of growth, both in terms of profits as well as sales. And as we will talk later, there is talk about how and whether the Government of India can increase the blending to 21% to 22% or even looking at flexi vehicles.

items.statement: Performance chemicals value up 40% in FY26; targeting more than doubling in FY27 with new products (dibasic esters, wire enamels, personal care, flavors/fragrances)
items.quote: We've seen excellent growth in terms of performance chemicals, which in terms of value itself is up 40%, and contribution is up 40+%. And we are hoping, that I'm not projecting, but we are hoping for in excess of doubling this business this year.

items.statement: Potable Spirits premiumization drive: IMFL now 31% of segment revenue (5-6% Amrut), up from mid-teens; 7 new brands launched, CSD/paramilitary approvals progressing
items.quote: So, Akash, the total freight revenue percentage, whatever we have declared, it is around 31% of the total Potable section, and Amrut share is likely to be around 5% to 6% out of it.

items.statement: Chemicals shifting to high-value performance chemicals (green amines for L'Oreal, glycols, oilfield chemicals with BASF/New Park/Dow); letting go of low-margin glycol ethers and gases
items.quote: We've seen good growth in terms of glycols, we've seen excellent growth in terms of performance chemicals, which in terms of value itself is up 40%, and contribution is up 40+%. And we are hoping, that I'm not projecting, but we are hoping for in excess of doubling this business this year.

items.statement: Grain prices stable at INR21-22/kg (down from INR24/kg mid-FY25); maize now 46% of ethanol feedstock vs 0% in FY20; DDGS prices improving
items.quote: In the middle of last year, grain prices were running close to INR24 a kilo. And then in the last quarter of last year, they were running close to between INR21 and INR22 or, INR21 plus minus. And the good thing was that the DDGS started to fetch a better price.

items.statement: Ethanol capacity now exceeds Bio-Fuels consumption; 3x3 strategy (grain, molasses, import flexibility) enables in-house ethanol for Chemicals
items.quote: Now, given the fact that we have good ethanol capacities in-house, we talked about a 3x3 strategy and the fact that we have grain, molasses-based, as well as the option to import, it allows us to also use in-house ethanol for our Chemicals as an intermediate without worrying too much about excess ethanol capacity.

items.statement: EO competitiveness vs Reliance improved due to higher crude prices and ample domestic ethanol; crude expected to stay firm due to war and US policy
items.quote: So, we saw a period and for the last couple of months, we have been competitive as far as Reliance's EO price is concerned and that is because of rising crude prices and also ample availability of ethanol within India.

items.statement: New CSD approvals for Soulmate Whisky and Zumba Lemoni (lifetime registration); Zumba Black cleared preliminary screening; Amrut distribution rights acquired in North
items.quote: Two of our key brands, that is Soulmate Whisky, which is a Millionaire Case Brand, also our Zumba Lemoni, which is very popular in the market have been introduced in the CSD and we've already started supplies in the entire country.

items.statement: Ennature Biopharma: first commercial supplies of green bio-based amine to L'Oreal after 3-4 years co-development; expanding US presence with new office
items.quote: We spoke about bio-based amines, we had a slow start but we did mention to you that IGL became the first manufacturer of a green bio-based amine for certain applications, and our first customer, we are proud to say, is L'Oreal with whom we also did some co-development over the last three-four years, and we've started commercial supplies for them.

items.statement: Plant shutdown 17 Mar - 2 Apr for catalyst change (15-20 days); silver sale INR98 crores (cost INR51 crores) not booked as profit due to catalyst consumption accounting
items.quote: Third point, that there was a plant shutdown for the change of the catalyst from 17th March till 2nd April. So, this has also resulted the reduction in the production as well as some sales.

items.statement: Ethanol feedstock mix shifted dramatically: grain now 73% of production (5% damaged + 22% FCI rice + 46% maize) vs 9% in FY20
items.quote: Now come to '25-'26, grain is contributing 5% plus 22%, 27% plus 46%, which is close to 70-plus-percent, 73% of ethanol production is coming from grain.

items.statement: NCLT hearing for demerger scheduled 21 May; order expected early June; ROC filing to follow
items.quote: 21st May, we are hopeful that we will get the order for the demerger of the division. And another hope is that in first 10 days of the June we will get the order. So, once we get the order, we will start working for filing that in ROC and the other matters, which is related.

items.statement: War impact mixed: positive for ethanol-based competitiveness (higher crude, MEG/ethanol constraints); negative for oilfield chemicals exports to Middle East (New Park business on hold)
items.quote: Now, the reason it has had mixed impact probably overall a little positive is that what it has led to, it has led to sharp increases in the crude price and also some availability constraints as far as MEG or ethanol is concerned. Which means that our relative competitiveness for products, which are based on ethanol is somewhat better, or significantly better in some cases.

items.quote: The amount of INR38.38 crores, which we have received from our JV Clariant has been adjusted against the investment, which is there.

items.statement: FY27 cement demand expected to grow ~6%
items.quote: Overall, we see that FY26-'27 cement demand is going likely to grow at about 6% or so.

items.statement: National effective installed capacity reached 712Mt at end of March 2026 after 64Mt addition in FY26
items.quote: Supply side witnessed highest ever annual capacity addition of 64 million tons. The national effective installed capacity reaching now to 712 million tons at the end of March 2026.

items.statement: Industry capacity addition estimated at 45-50Mt in FY27 vs 64Mt in FY26
items.quote: So '26 -'27 estimated to be about -- again, our estimation is about around 45 million to 50 million tons, right? Last year, it was about 64 million tons.

items.statement: Pet coke prices up ~40% QoQ to ~$160/t; global coal prices up ~30% QoQ
items.quote: Fuel costs surged sharply because of the geopolitical situation, pet coke prices up by about 40% quarter-over-quarter to about $160 per ton level, and that is again quite fluctuating.

items.statement: Energy costs expected to rise by at least INR300/t and packaging cost by INR80-100/t in coming quarters
items.quote: Energy costs are expected to rise by about at least INR300 and packaging cost about INR80 to INR100 per ton, and that is going to impact maybe in coming quarters because of this geopolitical situation.

items.quote: So, what I see maybe the INR 300 impact would come somewhere around quarter 2. But this quarter, definitely, I see somewhere around maybe INR100 to INR120 or INR130 a ton.

items.quote: And I'm sure that it is going to reduce at least by another INR50 to INR75 for sure.

items.statement: Non-cement margin in Q4 FY26 was 4%

items.statement: Clinker utilization at 93% in FY26; Q4 CC ratio 1.44; power cost INR5.79/kWh in Q4 vs INR5.37 in Q3

items.statement: Industry closed FY26 at ~480,000 vehicles, 16% above FY25; Q4 was a record quarter for all OEMs.

items.statement: FY27 expected to be another good year at 400,000+ vehicles, though exact level uncertain.
items.quote: And whoever the OEM partner, it is not just one. I think most of the OEMs are expecting this year, FY27, should also be a good year. So when I say good year, it is 400 plus, but whether it is 420, 450, 480 that is probably too early to say.

items.statement: Aspirational top line target of INR4,000-5,000 crores over next 4-5 years with exports as a key lever.
items.quote: So overall, as you rightly mentioned the forecast with the domestic market growth, export and all other initiatives that we are taking up, the top line should grow in the order of rough order of INR4,000 crores to INR5,000 crores with export being a large -- better than the current contribution what we have today.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin at 12.4%; full year EBITDA margin 12.4% (10.6% after exceptional item), up 40-50 bps YoY.
items.quote: Overall, our EBITDA for the full year is at INR2,692 million at 12.4%. And then we had the exceptional item, the annualized impact what we discussed last time of about INR120 million. Netting of that, our EBITDA stood at 10.6% for the year. When you compare to previous year, we had 10.1%. So we are about 40 to 50 basis points above there.

items.statement: Technical fee to Meritor HVS is 4-4.5% of total revenue depending on mix; already factored into reported margins.
items.quote: So see, overall, see the technical fee is anywhere in the range between 4% to 4.5% depending on the mix of revenue that we have. So I think that's the broad percentage in which the technical fee operates.

items.statement: Spent ~INR70 crores in FY26 (60-70% of committed capex); generated INR30 crores net cash after investments.
items.quote: So when compared to last year -- sorry, in the last financial year, we spent more than INR70 crores of capex. So whatever investments that was committed, most of -- about 60% to 70% was spent in the last year. And instead of all that, we were able to generate net of investments, INR30 crores of cash that we have generated in the last financial year.

items.statement: Phase 1 and 1A capacity expansion to complete by December 2026; next capex phase to be finalized in 6-12 months based on domestic and export outlook.
items.quote: So as we committed to you, the Phase 1 and I would say, Phase 1 and 1A, that's what we call is that capacity will be completed by end of December '26. And then that's what we were telling to earlier question that in next 6 to 9 months, we'll be coming and forming up our next phase of capex -- capex investment based on both the domestic and export market outlook

items.statement: FY27 capex expected to be similar to FY26 (~INR70 crores) to complete ongoing phases.
items.quote: So, I'll take the question. So, on the capex part, first piece of -- I think last year to now, I think last year, we spent about INR30 crores vis a vis INR70 crores in the coming year also, we are expecting because the major spend are we going to complete the phases that we had already spoken about. So, we'll be almost similar range of capex spend will be there in the upcoming year as well.

items.statement: No current capacity constraints unless market exceeds Q4 FY26 volumes; new capacity aimed at meeting peak domestic and export demand.
items.quote: At this point of time, unless the market really goes beyond the volumes what we have seen in the last Q4, I don't think we have any capacity constraints at this point of time.

items.statement: New product launches (e.g., 185 axle for tractor-trailers) ramping up well; tractor-trailer share rising, partially cannibalizing rigid multi-axle but overall TIV growing to 500,000+ by 2029-30.
items.quote: And that is probably the highest axle number of -- in terms of capacity also that we are creating and expecting that this trend will continue for some time. But on the other side, there is enough headroom in the industry where even the multi-axle rigid vehicle will also grow.

items.statement: LCV/ICV revenue share low single digits (<5%); focus remains on medium/heavy-duty core.
items.quote: LCV, ICV, it's a very small portion of the revenue that we have. Maybe I would say somewhere in the single digits at this point, maybe low, less than 5%.

items.statement: Supply to Tata Motors primarily brakes; axle discussions ongoing but no confirmation of increased wallet share.
items.quote: There are continuous discussions. But right now, I don't -- I can -- I'm not in a position to confirm there are different discussions at different levels.

items.statement: Ashok Leyland share maintained per agreement; product mix varies monthly so focus on healthy annual average.
items.quote: On an average, the whole year, we have maintained as per our agreement with Ashok Leyland, like Nagaraja mentioned earlier, it is very difficult to speak one particular day or a week or a month because the product mix changes so much.

items.statement: Exports limited to assemblies/sub-assemblies/child parts due to regional customization needs; not fully dressed axles.
items.quote: So the product line as such in Europe and North America don't allow us to supply the fully dressed axle because the products are different. So it is largely going to be limited to the assemblies, subassemblies and probably child parts.

items.statement: Commodity cost increases passed through via back-to-back agreements with customers; financials trued up to latest increases.
items.quote: We always have a back-to-back agreement with most of the customers when it comes to commodity changes. And this is a standard industrial practice. There may be a little bit of a lag or lagging in that adjustment. But definitely, the business is always protected and it is a standard industrial practice.

items.statement: Productivity improvements and new technology capex aimed at offsetting inflationary pressures and protecting bottom line.
items.quote: So while there is always an inflation, if you look at the last several years of our results, we have been able to always bring in the efficiency and then productivity improvements and both in internal operation and from our supply chain. So we always have to work on that, and that is one of our strength.

items.statement: Net cash generation of INR30 crores in FY26 after INR70+ crores capex spend.
items.quote: And instead of all that, we were able to generate net of investments, INR30 crores of cash that we have generated in the last financial year.

items.statement: Industry tonnage carrying capacity rose to 9.4 million tons in FY26 from 8.7 million tons in FY19 at similar vehicle volumes, driven by heavier vehicles.
items.quote: And just to give you a comparison of this versus the previous peak, which was FY19, where we also did the similar vehicle production of 476,000, was 8.7. 8.7 to 9.4 with the same industry level, that addition is coming from that heavy-duty or higher tonnage vehicles.

items.statement: No major regulatory changes expected for axles; brake regulations may shift niche segments to disc brakes but drum brake demand to continue.
items.quote: Axle side, we are not seeing any major changes in the regulation. There was one where the overload has been, to some extent, regularized. But that's a typical overload that we see on Indian roads all the time. So, it has not changed anything in our product portfolio.

items.statement: Smart axle/ADAS products exist in global portfolio but not yet applicable to India; will industrialize when market demands.
items.quote: Yes, we have couple of axles that we qualify as smart axle in the global portfolio but they're not applicable for Indian markets as of now. So, if it moves in that direction, the products are available. It's more of licensing them and industrializing them.

items.statement: Employee benefit expense included ~8% one-off (leave encashment settlement) in Q4; normalized run-rate lower.
items.quote: So, that's had a bit of one-offs this time. So, we had some leave encashment settlement and all that happened. So, about 8% of it was a one-off. So, -- but on a like-for-like, it should be lower by around 8%.

items.statement: Q1-Q2 historically softer; diesel price impact on demand too early to assess; FY27 volume dependent on post-monsoon recovery.
items.quote: Historically, it's been like that and we think it will continue that. And then how we come out of monsoon and how we end Q4, that will probably define whether it is a 400 plus 20%, plus 5%.

items.statement: e-Axle ready but India market not yet transitioned; content per vehicle would be 100% of current mechanical parts plus power electronics.
items.quote: The technology or the architecture that we have in the e-axle that is an add-on to the traditional mechanical axle. That means what we are currently manufacturing in terms of the mechanical parts, gears and other things plus the electric motor and other electronics, power electronics.

items.statement: Bus low-floor regulation evolving; current product portfolio meets most requirements, some OEM strategies still developing.
items.quote: Yes, there is more clarity on that. And it looks like the current product portfolio, what we have can meet most of the requirements, but then there are also some OEMs have a different strategy and is actually evolved. So it is still something that is evolving.

items.statement: Pre-sales growth target of 25-30% CAGR for FY27
items.quote: So, we expect to grow by 25% to 30% CAGR.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 25-27% for FY27
items.quote: However, we expect in this FY27 to increase our EBITDA margin and take it to 25%-27% range because the contribution from the new projects will add on to the P&L going further.

items.statement: Revenue target of around Rs. 700 crores for FY27
items.quote: And because of this, we will be able to jump forward from the 500-550 crores top line to around Rs. (+700) crores this year.

items.statement: Free cash flow positive expected from FY27 onwards
items.quote: I think next financial year onwards, we should turn free cash flow positive.

items.statement: Delivery volume target of upwards of 2,000 units for FY27
items.quote: But we are expecting a big number this financial year as well with respect to deliveries. It will go upwards of 2,000 very easily.

items.statement: Total construction CAPEX target of around Rs. 400 crores for FY27 including Rs. 75 crores for hotel and gymkhana
items.quote: CAPEX, we intend to spend around (+400) crores in construction this financial year across all the projects. So, that's our target for CAPEX.

items.statement: Hotel and gymkhana CAPEX of Rs. 75 crores for FY27 to be debt funded
items.quote: So, debt will be taken for the gymkhana and th e hotel development, which will, I mean, this financial year, we should do a CAPEX of around 75 crores for these two assets

items.statement: FY26 collections of Rs. 539 crores
items.quote: Collections for this financial year stood at Rs. 539 crores.

items.statement: Average selling price increased 27% YoY to Rs. 7,769/sq ft in FY26
items.quote: The average price per square foot achieved for the entire financial year stood at Rs. 7,769 per square feet versus Rs. 6,082 per square feet in the year FY25, reflecting a year-on-year increase of 27% in the average price achieved.

items.statement: Construction cost increase of 3-5% expected due to geopolitical situation

items.statement: World Villas price increase of ~Rs. 1 crore per unit from launch
items.quote: So, price increase for World Villas has happened by almost (+1) crore at realization levels from what we had started off.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin improved to 23%, up ~200 bps YoY

items.quote: So, as a company, whenever we look at taking on a project, we expect a EBITDA margin of 33% across all the segments, and PAT margins to the tune of 24%. items.quote: We should finalize our brand by this 1st Quarter and work has already started off, we have completed the excavation. And that will involve an investment of around Rs. 60 crores in total.

items.statement: No demand slowdown seen despite geopolitical tensions; transactions continuing at pre-war levels
items.quote: So, yes, the situation is being witnessed by all with respect to some panic from some customers, but we are not seeing any stoppage with respect to decisions. There is obvi ously more time, which some customers may require, but we are not seeing any slowdown in transactions

items.statement: ABS expansion on track for second half of FY27; no change to earlier timeline
items.quote: We are still saying in the second half of this year, we will have additional volumes and capacities coming in line. So, there is no change.

items.statement: ABS capex commitments made and on track; no cost escalation currently
items.quote: The commitments are already -- have been made. And we do believe, given current timelines, we are on track to what -- we are on track with regards to whatever we have mentioned in the past with regards to our capex and volume -- incremental volume that we will get.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 India volume dip due to GPPS decline from imports and unorganized market; ABS and HIPS grew YoY
items.quote: been a dip in our GPPS sales for the quarter. There has been a muted demand and also there has been a lot of pricing pressure on account of certain imports. items.quote: We were again shifting from INEOS' brand to our brand, and we had started intimating to all the customers that we would be discontinuing and we were also wanting them to switch to our brand. items.statement: Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA margin 19.2% (+734 bps YoY); PAT margin 12.8% (+524 bps)
items.quote: EBITDA margin for Q4 FY '26 improved by 19.2%, an increase of 734 basis points. Profit after tax for Q4 FY '26 stood at INR84.3 crores, a growth of 58.6% and profit after tax margin for Q4 FY '26 stood at 12.8%, a growth of 524 basis points.

items.statement: Q4 profitability higher due to product mix (less GPPS) and opportunistic spot pricing; not sustainable long-term
items.quote: the profitability in the last quarter has probably been a little bit higher on account of 2 things. One is, of course, the product mix. Like I mentioned that we sold less GPPS in that quarter, and that has changed. Now going forward, what happens, we'll have to see. And the other thing was in terms of certain prices that we could get for certain segments were higher on account of certain shortages

items.statement: HIPS margins better than GPPS due to organized OEM demand and specialized grades; GPPS more unorganized and price-sensitive
items.quote: for HIPS, a larger market is actually driven by air conditioning, refrigerators and some packaging industries. And a lot of this is kind of organized and is growing well in India. There also a lot of specialized grade requirements by these customers, which are not easy to switch from one supplier to the other. And hence, there is a greater value that customers see in buying a specific product from

items.statement: Short-to-medium term prices likely to remain above pre-war levels due to supply chain lag; long-term normalization uncertain
items.quote: I would say in the short to potentially short -- medium-term, prices will tend to remain a little bit higher from what we can assess at this stage as opposed to what they have been in the past.

items.statement: Raw material procurement diversified globally; no significant disruption despite Middle East crisis; minor disruptions only
items.quote: We have obviously not faced any significant disruption to our manufacturing. We may have had minor disruptions, but nothing that requires significant reporting or worry. So, we have covered for all the raw materials that we need. We are buying from multiple sources globally.

items.statement: Korea structurally worse affected by Middle East crisis; Styrenix better positioned to supply specific ABS grades, gaining spot margins
items.quote: Korea and certain countries have had structurally worse problems than, say, India or Thailand or even China for that matter, have had. And we are better positioned to supply those specific grades. And in those grades, we are able to get better margins.

items.statement: Korean competitor vertically integrated into styrene but stopped production 1-2 years ago; now imports styrene, no advantage
items.quote: One of the big competitors who is positioned in Korea and probably has the largest share in the import substitution market was actually vertically integrated into styrene and they stopped producing styrene, in fact, I think, a year or 2 ago. And they chose to now import or buy styrene from outside even into that country.

items.statement: Thailand well-positioned geopolitically; not severely affected in procurement/production; critical for global customer access
items.quote: As far as Thailand is concerned, if I look at a broader, more longer-term geopolitical view, it is very well placed. We -- in spite of all these challenges which have happened, Thailand has not been affected so severely in terms of its ability to procure and produce. So, we see that as a very big positive.

items.statement: Power sourcing agreement expected to start next month; savings depend on production volumes, difficult to quantify currently
items.quote: We have been advised that hopefully, by next month or so, we would start receiving that power. But again, it is hazarding a guess or hazarding an opinion from a third party. So, I would take that with a pinch of salt. So hopefully, that does happen, and we are able to start accruing gains from next month, which would reflect in this quarter.

items.statement: Healthy return ratios: standalone ROE ~25%, ROCE ~32% for FY26; strong prudent balance sheet
items.quote: We have maintained a healthy return ratio with strong and prudent balance sheet. ROE and ROCE stood at nearly 25% and 32%, respectively, for FY '26 on a stand-alone basis.

items.statement: India ABS market 350-370 KT; domestic sales ~160-170 KT pre-new entrant; ~200 KT imports; new entrant reduces shortfall to >100 KT
items.quote: Indian demand last year was about 350,000 tons, as we know, 350,000 to 370,000 tons. And I think between the Indian players prior to the third now player, which has entered the field, the total sales were about 160,000, 170,000 tons. So close to 200,000 tons were still being imported. Even with the new player coming in, we are still talking about a shortfall of more than 100,000 tons.

items.statement: Consolidated other income INR11.8 crore in Q4 FY26 includes Thailand forex gains, services income, scrap sales
items.quote: So, it has income from both India as well as our Thailand operations. So maybe some forex gains in Thailand, which comes into this. Then we have some services also in Thailand, which we give from our facilities. And maybe other than that, scrap sales and all other things overall will come into other income.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 expected to be better than Q4 FY26 on consolidated and standalone basis
items.quote: I can say that our Q1 looks on track for numbers, which are better than Q4, whether it is on standalone or on a consolidated basis. So we anticipate Q1 to be better than Q4, which was, of course, better than Q3.

items.statement: Polycarbonate project commissioning expected by June 2028
items.quote: So we've clarified earlier, and we are, by and large, remaining kind of in line with that, and we are expecting it to be commissioned by June 2028.

items.statement: MIBK and MIBC projects scheduled for commissioning in Q2 FY27
items.quote: We witnessed a steady progress of our multipurpose agrochemical intermediates and MIBK, MIBC projects, which are scheduled for commissioning in Q2 FY27.

items.statement: FY27 expected to show stronger margin profile for standalone business vs FY26
items.quote: Therefore, in FY27, we expect a stronger margin profile, even for the standalone business, compared with

items.statement: Polycarbonate project total capex INR11,000 crore funded 60:40 debt-equity
items.quote: So, the total project, what we have announced is around INR11,000 crore. The funding is for all the projects together. We have tied up with the banks for d ebt. It will be in the ratio of 60 -40

items.statement: Nitric acid plant utilization at ~45% in Q4 FY26 due to technical issues
items.quote: But during this quarter under review, we were roughly at about 45% of utilization.

items.statement: Nitration and hydrogenation plants at Dahej fully commissioned and operational
items.quote: So on your first question on nitration and hydrogenation, those plants are already commissioned and they are operating with the right productivity and efficiency as expected.

items.statement: Phenolics plant operating at high efficiencies after brief April maintenance
items.quote: Just to clarify, the maintenance was only in the beginning of April, maybe for about 10 days or so, not for the month of April. And we are operating at this moment, at high efficiencies.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 18% from 11% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA margins improved significantly to 18% during the quart er under review compared to 11% in Q3FY26

items.statement: Phenolics segment EBIT margin improved to 20% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: EBIT margins improved significantly to 20% during the quarter.

items.statement: Structural margin benefits from backward integration and by-product valorization
items.quote: This was underpinned by strategic combination of proactive feedstock procurement, improved core product realization and the structural margin benefits of backward integration and by-product valorization.

items.statement: Domestic demand stable across automotive, infrastructure, pharma, electronics, polymers
items.quote: While global demand conditions remain mixed, domestic demand in India continued to witness relatively stable momentum across several end industries, including automotive, infrastructure, pharmaceuticals, electronic, polymers and other downstream sectors.

items.statement: New products (6-7 plus fluorinated molecules) commercial production expected from Q3 FY27
items.quote: So in all of these, as we said earlier, we anticipate commercial production on a regularized basis from Q3 onwards because this will reach our export customers towards the end of Q3 in time for their CY 2026 requirements.

items.statement: Secured feedstock inventory at enviable prices through Q4 buying on dips
items.quote: We ended up with a much larger inventory than we would traditionally have had in Q4. So this was because we saw an unusual movement and we did not actually anticipate a hot war, but we did anticipate volatility. And that position has held out quite well for us, whether it is in Q4 or in subsequent quarters.

items.statement: Passing on price increases balanced with market participation and wallet share
items.quote: In terms of passing on the same price increases equivalent to the market conditions, that is an ongoing exercise. What we do is we balance out that as well as market participation and wallet share.

items.statement: China's constraints on nitration chemistries creating structural tailwind for Deepak
items.quote: China will administer significant constraints on certain key chemistries, including production, storage and transportation. So there, we find that there will be some uptick in the demand as well as the profitability for nitration products.

items.statement: Sulfur downstream facing heightened cost headwinds globally
items.quote: But like I said, the important thing is to check what the delta between international prices and Indian prices are. And there, if we are able buy to maintain par for the course, we anticipate no significant net impact to the Company and the benefit as it comes from nitration chemistries, which Deepak has a considerable market position as well as a technological strength.

items.statement: Domestic to export revenue mix 86:14 in Q4 FY26 and FY26
items.quote: Our domestic to export reven ue mix stood at 86:14 reflecting the resilience of our domestic franc hise while continuing to maintain meaningful engagement across export markets

items.statement: Receivable days increased due to shift to dealership and CSA model to secure outstandings
items.quote: In some cases, we have changed the model, because today we are passing through a very volatile situation, and we do not want to risk our outstanding. So, instead we have gone into a dealership and CSA model. That is helping us in at least securing our outstanding.

items.statement: Finance costs INR19 crore in Q4 FY26 reflecting growth investments
items.quote: Finance costs for Q4 FY26 stood at INR19 crore, reflecting borrowings associated with ongoing growth investments and strategic expansion projects.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend INR7.5 per equity share for FY26
items.quote: The Board has recommended a final dividend of INR7.5 per equity share for FY26, reaffirming our commitment to delivering consistent shareholder value, continuing to invest in strategic growth and long-term value creation.

items.statement: China's CCP guidelines on hazardous chemistries audit creating tailwind for responsible players
items.quote: To clarify, my comment was not linked to one or the other province because this is a general CCP guideline with regards to the chemistries as well as the safe material movement as well as the transport, which includes, of course, also product at port and transport over oceans.

items.statement: Near-term volatility from geopolitical tensions, Chinese supply dynamics, US tariffs, feedstock volatility
items.quote: Near -term industry conditions are expected to remain influenced by geopolitical developments, Chinese supply dynamics, U.S. tariff policies and feedstock volatility.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue INR7,947 crore, EBITDA INR1,041 crore, PAT INR551 crore for FY26
items.quote: For FY26, consolidated revenue stood at INR7,947 crore, while EBITDA and PAT stood at INR1,041 crore and INR551 crore, respectively.

items.statement: New downstream products in agrochem and non-agrochem space significantly margin accretive

items.statement: Aluminum pass-through impact roughly 4-5% on casting revenue growth in Q4

items.statement: Green mobility segment created consolidating EV, CNG, hybrid; Q4 revenue INR 423 crores (25% YoY), 8% of consolidated
items.quote: Showing immediate momentum, the green mobility segment achieved a robust 25% year-on-year revenue growth in the quarter, reaching INR 423 crores and contributing 8% to the company's total consol revenues.

items.statement: Sunroof manufacturing facility commissioning expected by end of FY27

items.statement: Increasing share of business with leading Indian PV OEMs in switching; new EV customers onboarded
items.quote: we witnessed furthe r increase in share of business with leading Indian passenger vehicle OEMs, further strengthening our leadership position in the domestic market

items.statement: Final dividend of INR 1.75/share recommended; total FY26 dividend INR 2.65/share (~INR 153 crores)
items.quote: Reflecting our strong financial performance and robust cash flow generation, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR1.75 per share for shareholder approval. items.statement: INR 2,500 crores enabling resolution for fundraising (mix of instruments) approved; no specific plan currently
items.quote: So Neel, if that's the only question, I'm assuming, this is only an enabling resolution we take every year. Even last year, we have done it. And this is a mix of all the instruments. It is not necessarily equity. It also covers NCDs and some other borrowings.

items.statement: 2-wheeler alloy wheel capacity ~9.5 million/year; 4-wheeler alloy wheel capacity ~7 million/year after expansions

items.quote: Additionally, the company has incurred a cash flow of INR 200-odd crores towards the acquisition of shares in UMEVSPL and associated technologies from FRIWO.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty, commodity price volatility, and labor cost spikes identified as key near-term risks
items.quote: While external uncertainties, particularly on the geopolitical and commodity front continue to warrant close monitoring, the underlying demand environment and long-term growth drivers remain firmly intact.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of INR 6,000+ crores and EBITDA margin of 24-25% at current market levels
items.quote: revenue, we should, top line should be 6,000 plus with our new pellet plant operating at close to 80%, 90% capacity. So, there will be the additional volume and additional revenue coming from there as other volumes remains almost constant. And FY '27 guidance, see at current market level, we should be able to do somewhere about 24%-25% at EBITDA levels, at current market levels

items.statement: FY27 iron ore mining guidance of 4-4.25 million tons production, 3.4 million tons net usable ore for pellets

items.quote: So, the actual iron ore mining production will be about 4 million to 4.25 million tons. But the guidance we have given is the net usable iron ore coming to the plant for making pellets, which is about 3.4 million tons.

items.statement: FY27 pellet production guidance of 4 million tons with captive consumption of 0.9-1 million tons and merchant sales of ~3 million tons
items.quote: No, no, no, there is a confusion. So, pellet guidance for this year is 4 million tons. The iron ore volume, net usable iron ore for the pellet is at 3.4 million tons.

items.statement: FY27 capex estimated at INR 1,500-2,000 crores for balance CRM, battery storage and solar; FY28 and FY29 capex ~INR 3,000 crores each for steel plant
items.quote: Yes, including the balance of CRM, balance of your battery storage and little bit of solar, you can consider CAPEX of close to about INR 1,500 crores to INR 2,000 crores for FY '27.

items.statement: 1 million ton integrated steel plant capex revised to INR 7,000 crores from earlier INR 4,000 crores estimate; construction to begin October 2026
items.quote: The current CAPEX given as INR 7,000 crores is very much on the practical side. We have done a thorough study with the equipment suppliers and basis that we have shared the details with the stakeholders.

items.statement: 2 million ton pellet plant commissioned December 2025 using natural gas-based grate-kiln technology; total pellet capacity now 4.7 million tons
items.quote: GPIL commissioned its 2-million-ton iron ore pellet plant in December '25, taking total pellet capacity from 2.7 million to 4.7 million tons. The plant is India's first to use advanced natural gas-based grate-kiln technology, marking a shift from conventional carbon intensive processes.

items.statement: CRM Complex (0.7 million tons) on track for commissioning by March FY27; 50% utilization targeted for FY28, 90% from FY29
items.quote: GPIL is progressing on its 0.7-million-ton CRM Complex project with on-site construction expected to commission by July FY '26. Order for key equipment lines have been placed and advance payments have been released for all major process lines. The project is targeted for commissioning by March FY '27.

items.statement: 20 GW BESS project: soil testing done, compound wall construction underway; long-term agreements with EVE Power for cells and Shanghai Shenyi Roche for BOS; first line commissioning by March 2027
items.quote: GPIL is setting up a 20-Gigawatt BESS project for which soil testing has been completed and construction of the compound wall is currently underway. We have signed long-term agreements with EVE Power for Grade-1 628 Ah LFP cells and with Shanghai Shenyi Roche Energy Technology for BESS Balance of System supply securing the project supply chain. BESS project is expected to commission from March '27

items.quote: FY '26 EBITDA stood stable at INR 1,253 crores whereas Q4 FY '26 EBITDA increased by 38% Y-o-Y basis and 91% Q-o-Q basis to INR 439 crores.

items.quote: We expect EBITDA of more than 20% once the plant is operating at full capacity, because we are into value-added steel and currently there is not much competition from the Indian market.

items.quote: See, this quarter, we are very well covered within the limits. So, our average pricing should be somewhere about INR 12,000, INR 13,000. But Q2 onwards, because of the war impact, the sea freight has gone up substantially from $15-$16, it is almost crossed $22. Dollar is up from 93-94 levels to 97 levels. So, there is a substantial impact on the imported coal price from Q2 onwards, at least by 15%

items.statement: Domestic pellet demand positive due to steel capacity expansion and low-carbon focus; global pellet market projected 5-6% CAGR; export market viable if domestic demand weak
items.quote: Supported by increasing adoption of cleaner steelmaking technologies, looking ahead, India's pellet demand outlook also remains positive, supported by ongoing steel capacity expansion and the industry's growth focus on low-carbon and high-grade raw materials.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 prices softened ~10% across supply chain post-April due to war/heatwave; Q4 FY26 saw sequential realization improvement
items.quote: Q1, the pricing was pretty much at the same levels of Q4 for the first half of Q1. But the second half of Q1, say, end of April, early May, the prices have softened a bit almost by 10% across the supply chain.

items.statement: RR Ispat rolling mill has healthy order book of almost 6 months; structural rolled products capacity ~3.75 lakh tons for FY27
items.quote: And now you can see this production happening on a continuous basis quarter-on-quarter, because the mill is now quite stable and there is activity of the product in the market. So, we have a healthy order book of almost six months on RR Ispat.

items.statement: Operating cash flow improved 29% to INR 1,157 crores in FY26 driven by strong operations and efficient working capital management; cash position INR 837 crores
items.quote: Cash flow from operating activities improved by 29% to INR 1,157 crores, driven by a strong operational performance and efficient working capital management. GPIL continues to maintain a healthy balance sheet with a cash position of INR 837 crores.

items.statement: Steel plant debt funding to begin FY28 onwards; CRM and BESS projects 40-50% invested; self-funded from internal accruals until then
items.quote: So, FY '28, FY '29 will be the major money flow into the steel plant. Apart from that, we are self-funded to afford everything from internal approval. So, whatever debt you have to take on will be happening from FY '28 only on account of steel CAPEX.

items.statement: Received environment approval and CTO from CECB for Ari Dongri mine expansion (2.35 to 6 MTPA) and sponge iron/HB wire/waste heat recovery expansions in February 2026

items.statement: Export parity for pellets viable: domestic ~INR 9,500 ex-plant vs export ~INR 13,000 delivered China (INR 3,000 freight); delta <$10/ton currently; may export if domestic demand remains weak
items.quote: But today, the Indian prices are about INR 9,500. And with the dollar inflation, today, if you want to export, we can easily achieve more than INR 9,000 ex-plant. So, the delta is now hardly less than $10 between domestic pricing and the export pricing.

items.statement: New pellet plant uses natural gas (7-year GAIL MoU) vs coal gasification; saves INR 100 crores capex and enables export readiness for CBAM
items.quote: Plus, we also saved close to about INR 100 crores of CAPEX on the coal gasification side to generate the same kind of fuel. So, INR 100 crores CAPEX was saved on the CAPEX side, plus we are future ready whenever export opportunity is there.

items.statement: Beneficiation at mine saves ~INR 150/ton freight by removing 10-15% waste before transport; 6 million ton beneficiation plant targeted Q3 FY27
items.quote: See, so currently the freight is about INR 1,000. So, if you are able to remove 10%-15% of wastage inside the mine, so straight away, INR 150 of saving, you will be doing on the freight side.

items.statement: EV fleet transition for mining transport: 300-350 trucks needed at full capacity; ~INR 350 crores capex with charging infra; 10 dumpers, 24 loaders, 15 excavators already deployed
items.quote: See, the amount of iron ore we need to move at the full capacity, we need to deploy more than about 300 trucks or about 350 trucks at the full capacity. Aman Kothari: 300, okay. Abhishek Agrawal: Yes, 350 trucks. So, at a full site CAPEX should be more than about INR 350 crores

items.statement: FY26 production achievement: sponge iron, structural rolled products, ferroalloys >100% of target; mining 92%, pellets 95%, billets 96%
items.quote: Sponge iron, structural rolled products and ferroalloys surpassed their targets with production exceeding 100% of planned levels. Meanwhile, mining, pellets and billets achieved 92%, 95% and 96% of their targeted production level respectively.

items.statement: Iron ore prices expected to remain above $100/ton supported by China demand and India's high-grade ore shortage; new low-cost supply from Simandou (Guyana) a medium-term risk
items.quote: Looking ahead, the medium-term outlook for iron ore prices remains costly, balanced, ensuring steel demand in China and expected ramp-up of new low-cost supply from Shandong project in Guyana. However, rising steel consumption in India and increasing preferences for high-grade iron ore are expected to provide structural support to demand going forward for pellets in high-grade iron ore.

items.statement: Management expects FY27 revenue growth at least in line with the 9% order book growth, with H2 back-ended execution similar to FY26
items.quote: we do have is a growth in the enquiry closing order book by about 9%. And so that gives you an indication of the minimum growth that we would like to anticipate

items.statement: Closing order book grew 8% YoY to ₹20.54 billion with export orders contributing 51%

items.statement: Enquiry book nearly doubled YoY to ~18 GW for product segment, driven by broad-based growth across geographies and sectors including data centres, geothermal, biomass, and thermal power
items.quote: The overall order book mix also witnessed a meaningful improvement, supported by a strong scale -up of the aftermarket business, which improved during the year.

items.statement: US enquiry book grew ~1000% to ~3 GW driven by data centre combined cycle, biomass, pulp & paper, geothermal and small modular reactor enquiries
items.quote: we've see n, I would say, a near 1 ,000% increase in our enquiry book in North America, but this is driven by the fact that we had very low visibility. The enquiry generation in that market is somewhere in the range of about 3 GW odd

items.statement: Commodity price increases (copper, aluminium, steel) mitigated through rate contracts, diversified supplier base, and partial pass-through to customers
items.quote: we have rate contracts for all our large components. And so there has been movement in material prices. You're very right. Everything from copper to aluminium to steel has actually increased in price. But we do not see that impacting both our supply chain procurement or therefore, our margins.

items.statement: Trade receivables at ₹6.39 billion (84 days vs 49 days YoY) due to March-skewed billing on large projects; significant portion already collected, but FY27 year-end receivables may remain elevated due to back-ended execution
items.quote: receivables at the end of March 31, 2026, stood at ₹6.39 billion, primarily reflecting the execution profile of certain large projects as well as the billing, which was skewed towards the end of March, which will be liquidated in the subsequent quarters.

items.statement: Export revenue grew 30% YoY to 58% of total revenue in FY26; Q4 exports grew 46% YoY to 60% of revenue; ₹8.5 crore MTM loss from rupee volatility
items.quote: Export revenue remained a key growth driver, increasing 30% year -on-year and contributing 58% of our overall revenue compared to 48% in the previous year.

items.statement: Aftermarket share declined to 25% of Q4 revenue (vs 33% YoY) due to lower spares execution; refurbishment driving aftermarket growth in Africa
items.quote: the aftermarket as a percentage of sales was actually at 25%, which is lower than about 33% for the previous year.

items.statement: API turbines expected to revert to 10%+ of order booking and revenue; geothermal and ORC seen as large future markets; CO2 energy storage awaiting pilot validation
items.quote: we believe in the coming quarters and years, it will revert to having a meaningful 10% plus number in our order booking as well as in revenue.

items.statement: Investing significantly more in AI readiness for technological disruption across industries and markets
items.quote: We will be investing significantly more into the movement into AI. We think that we need to be technologically ready for any disruption that will occur both within industries, within companies as well as in the market in general.

items.statement: US subsidiary turned profitable in Q4 FY26; full-year FY26 loss of ~₹8 crore; expected to be profitable in FY27 driven by aftermarket execution
items.quote: this Q4 was a profitable quarter for the U.S. subsidiary. Though the full year itself, as you will see from the annual report when it's out and the subsidiary accounts still had a loss of about ₹8 odd crores in that subsidiary.

items.statement: African aftermarket refurbishment orders growing sustainably with both lower and higher value-add projects including repair parts manufacturing
items.quote: As we are getting more entrenched into the African continent, we see good orders coming from that market. These include both lower value -add and higher value addition-based projects

items.statement: Geopolitical conflicts (India-Pakistan, West Asia, US tariffs) impacted FY26 order booking and revenue; similar disruptions anticipated in FY27 but with improved processes
items.quote: we anticipate certain conflicts to continue in our projections, we are confident of growth in the business, confident in growth in our bottom line as well as the fact of the visibility that we have in the enquiry pipeline

items.statement: Domestic market grew ~35% in FY26 to ~3,400 MW addressable market for sub-100 MW turbines
items.quote: Marketwise, domestic market around 35%, it has grown. That is the one data point when it comes to domestic market.

items.statement: R&D workforce at 7.5%+ and engineering at 8%+ of total; 35%+ in servicing for customer satisfaction

items.statement: No M&A discussed; organic growth through new product development (geothermal, ORC, CO2 storage, MVR, heat pumps) and geographic expansion
items.quote: we are also then have new technology innovation, and new technology introductions, which allow us to provide a longer -term growth path for the company.

items.statement: US permitting timelines for water (combined cycle) longer than air (simple cycle), causing phased project execution; not a direct risk for Triveni as supplier to EPC/developer
items.quote: the permitting that is required for water is different than what is required for air. And those are different regulations in the United States, and they take different time.

items.statement: Negative working capital maintained on non-balance sheet dates; disciplined capital deployment and liquidity management
items.quote: The company continues to maintain its negative working capital on non -balance sheet ending days, which is March 31 st and 30th of September, given the way that it is conducting its business.

items.statement: NTPC strategic order (subcritical CO2 energy storage) ~2/3 executed at ~3% PBT margin; cost increases absorbed but project marginally profitable
items.quote: whatever the increase in cost in this order we've already taken, this order is probably at a PBT level of about 3 -odd percent. And we've taken over two-thirds of the order already into revenue.

items.statement: Long-duration CO2 energy storage technology validation ongoing; Indian cost appetite very low; evaluating round-trip efficiency and per MWh cost vs pumped hydro and flow batteries
items.quote: Long -duration energy storage, where the CO2 comes in is evaluated in the same form like pumped hydro because of the availability. And the costing of it is actually significantly higher than pumped hydro.

items.statement: Management guides for 40-50 bps gross margin improvement and 50-75 bps EBITDA margin improvement in FY27

items.statement: Management maintains mid-single-digit revenue growth outlook for FY27 and targets profit growth of ~10%

items.quote: Net debt reduced sharply to around ₹105 crores as of March 2026 from ₹374 crores in March 2025, despite the consolidation of approximately ₹91 crores of debt from Knit Gallery acquisition.

items.statement: Capex during FY26 reduced by more than half compared to FY25, reflecting disciplined capital allocation
items.value: more than half reduction vs FY25
items.quote: Capex during the year was almost reduced by more than half compared to FY 2025, reflecting disciplined capital allocation.

items.statement: Proposed dividend payout of ₹3.3 per share for FY26, of which ₹1.65 per share paid as interim dividend amounting to ~42% of FY26 PAT
items.quote: we have proposed a dividend payout ₹3.3 per share, of which ₹1.65 per share was paid as interim dividend amounting to around 42% of FY 2026 PAT, maintaining our capital return track record.

items.quote: in the later part of the year, we took measures to in case we had to take some calls for redundancies. We took that and provided for that in the later half of the year as well.

items.value: ₹1,034 crores revenue; ₹57 crores EBIT; 5.5% EBIT margin
items.quote: The Manufacturing segment also delivered strong performance during FY 2026, with revenues growing 31% year-on-year to approximately ₹1,034 crores and EBIT increasing to ₹57 crores, translating into EBIT margins of approximately 5.5%.

items.statement: Medium-to-long-term mid-teens growth outlook remains intact; FY27 focused on profitability restoration before scaling growth

items.statement: No new vertical investments initiated in past 12 months; expect to maintain similar approach with no new investments over next 12 months

We've actually brought it down by 27%, and we had said we will be able to bring it down to about ₹80 crores in FY 2027.

items.statement: New Lobster (Ted Baker) business impacted by retail partner bankruptcies; in discussions with ABG for financial contribution ($2-2.5M for 12 months) or new retail partner; resolution expected in 4-6 weeks
items.quote: we are in close discussion with ABG, the brand owner and discussing with them either they have to give PDS financial contribution every year for us to be able to maintain and run the head office of the business or they have to then find a new retail partner who will then be able to ramp up the volumes and give us adequate turnover required to be able to maintain the infrastructure of the entire bu

items.statement: Sourcing-as-a-service model gaining traction with retailers outsourcing procurement operations; PDS and Li & Fung are final two in RFQs for global sourcing contracts
items.quote: the sourcing as a service business model that we had started on two years ago is having some very large active conversations with retailers who are talking about cutting the overhead in their social operation in Asia and giving PDS option to run those businesses. items.statement: Retailers consolidating vendor base; PDS positioned as one of few platforms (with Li & Fung) capable of professional large-scale sourcing-as-a-service engagements
items.quote: the good thing is if there are any global source contracts coming up, it's only PDS and Li & Fung, which are actually in the RFQ stage at the end. So I think overall, we are remaining quite confident.

items.statement: BCG-led procurement efficiency savings of ~₹40-50 crores annually and similar opex savings targeted; well on track
items.quote: As I recall, we had foreseen on that annually about ₹40 crores to ₹50 crores, we should be able to save in our procurement and a similar number in our opex as well. So I think we are well on track.

items.statement: Global apparel industry grew modestly and remained value-led; PDS delivered 5% GMV growth to ~₹19,666 crores and 4% revenue growth to ₹13,110 crores in FY26
items.quote: we delivered GMV growth of 5% to approximately ₹19,666 crores and a revenue growth of 4% to ₹13,110 for FY 2026. Importantly, this growth came in during a period where the broader apparel industry globally grew only very modestly and remained highly value-led in nature.

items.statement: Krayons (U.S.-focused) has stable order book with Costco; expected to return to top-line and profitability growth in H1 FY27; Klieder may take 1-2 more quarters
items.quote: Krayon is largely serving the U.S. markets. And there have been, as you know, the turbulence due to the tariff impact and otherwise. But structurally, beyond t he U.S. impact, Krayon is looking fine both in terms of top line and profitability. So these two, we are very positive that in H1 itself, you should see them posting both top line growth as well as profitability growth. Our vertical Klieder

items.statement: Effective tax rate for FY26 was 13.5% vs 10.1% in FY25 due to full impact of Pillar 2; India stand-alone impairment of ~₹14 crores on DBS lifestyle investment reduced Q4 ETR to ~7.9%
items.quote: Effective tax rate for FY 2026 was 13.5% compared to 10.1% in FY 2025. As guided earlier, we have full impact of Pillar 2 now in our ETR. At India stand-alone level, we have taken an impairment of about ₹14 crores on investment in DBS lifestyle vertical. DTA on account of this and other losses have reduced our Q4 ETR to almost 7.9%.

items.statement: Venture tech portfolio moving towards self-sustaining model; new investments only from cash realized from exits; other income doubled to ₹99.7 crores driven by FX gains and ~₹19 crores mark-to-market gains on venture investments
items.value: ₹99.7 crores other income; ~₹19 crores MTM gains
items.quote: Other income almost doubled to ₹99.7 crores in FY 2026, primarily driven by FX gains and mark-to-market gains of around ₹19 crores on PDS venture investments. We are witnessing positive traction across our venture tech investment portfolio with improving value realization, and it is now moving towards a self-sustaining model with new investments will only be done from cash realized from exits.

items.statement: Expects 6-7% tonnage growth for FY27 and at least 2% sequential quarterly growth
items.quote: In terms of volume growth, we are expecting to grow at least around 6% to 7% for the full year basis. And we are expecting that at least around 2% quarterly growth on a sequential basis even for the financial year '27.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA margin around 21% plus for Q1 FY27 and 20% plus going forward
items.quote: For the month of April also, we have -- we saw that the year-on-year volume growth is around 8%, and we are maintaining the EBITDA percentage in the range of around 21% plus.

items.statement: Plans INR300-350 crore capex for FY27 with INR100 crore for vehicles and INR200+ crore for land and building
items.quote: So, on a full year basis, we are expecting around INR300 crores to INR350 crores capital expenditure.

items.statement: Will add 500 vehicles in FY27 with 100+ already added and remaining 400 by December
items.quote: As we planned this year around 500 vehicles addition, out of that, around 100-plus vehicles have been already added. So, the remaining 400 vehicles are going to be added till December.

items.statement: Plans to open 100+ net new branches in FY27 after opening 110 and closing 60 in FY26
items.quote: Net branches itself, we are expecting at least around 100 numbers in the coming year.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin at 21.4%, down 190 bps YoY due to higher lorry hire, salary and maintenance costs
items.quote: On profitability, the EBITDA margin stood at around 21.4%, down by around 190 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 190 bps to 20.8% driven by 10% realization improvement and cost efficiencies
items.quote: The EBITDA margin stood at around 20.8%, expanded by nearly 190 basis points year-on-year, supported by a 10% improvement in realizations and sustained cost efficiencies.

items.statement: Passing on fuel cost increases via selective route rate hikes, chargeable weight changes and fuel surcharge clauses
items.quote: So, for example, earlier, we used to charge a 1 cubic feet equal to 8 kgs. Now for certain routes, we increased from 8 kgs to 9 kgs. So straight away, the quantity will increase in such routes.

items.statement: Fuel cost as percentage of revenue declined to 24% from 25.7% despite per litre cost rising from INR84.52 to INR85.54
items.quote: Fuel cost as a percentage to total income declined by -- to around 24% from 25.7%, due to decline in fuel consumption quantity and cost has increased to some extent on account of increase in the fuel procurement cost per liter from INR84.52 to INR85.54.

items.statement: Reduced direct refinery fuel purchase from 41% to 36% due to higher bulk purchase rates
items.quote: The quantity directly purchased from the refinery is reduced from 41% to 36%. We restricted the bulk purchasing quantity on account of increase in the bulk purchase rate.

items.statement: Petrochemical and oil-linked commodity demand constrained due to crude price impact
items.quote: Say, for example, the products which are related to the petrochemicals and oil, which are directly related to the crude oil, say, for example, plastic products and all. We are already seeing -- acknowledging in the market that the demand of such product is coming down.

items.statement: New customers contributed 17% of Q4 tonnage, lost customers returning contributed 14%, existing customers grew 1%
items.quote: For example, in Q4 year-on-year basis, our quantity -- around 17% of the quantity is contributed by the new customers year-on-year, I'm saying. And the left customer share is around 14% and existing customer growth year-on-year is around 1%.

items.statement: Door-to-door delivery mix increased to 38-39% from 33-34% with INR1-1.5 per kg premium realization
items.quote: Door-to-door, earlier it was around 33%, 34%. Now, I think, it increased to arou nd 38%, 39%, close to 40% of the commodities are door-to-door

items.statement: Spot bookings (TO PAY/PAID) contribute 80%, account customers 15-16%, FTL 6-7%
items.quote: Spot booking, again, see, TO PAY booking, what we call, TO PAY and PAID booking, which is a spot payment what we are getting from the customer. That is again contributing in the range of around 80%. And ACCOUNT customers are contributing in the range of around 15% to 16%.

items.statement: Trade receivables turnover at 36x implying ~10 debtor days among lowest in industry
items.quote: The trade receivables to turnover ratio is at around 36x, of the revenue, which will work out the receivable days around 10 days, among the lowest in the industry.

items.statement: Paid INR175 crore dividend in FY26 from operating cash flows
items.quote: The cash flow of INR175 crores was also utilized for the payment of dividend in the current year.

items.statement: Realization per ton at INR8,147 in Q4 FY26, up ~3% YoY from freight rationalization and route mix
items.quote: The realization per ton stood at around INR8,147 increased by approximately around 3% year-on-year, reflecting freight ra te rationalization and route mix

items.statement: Average lead distance 270-280 km across vehicle categories with 15-18 ton capacity
items.quote: The lead distance is in the range of around 270 to 280 kilometres. I'm telling you about across all the vehicle categories. And the capacities are in the range of around 15 to 18 tons.

items.statement: Vehicle life restricted to 15 years by government driving replacement cycle
items.quote: The government has put a restriction of the life of the vehicle for 15 years. Even though it is not mandatory, but there are a lot of restrictions to operate the vehicles which are crossing more than 15 years.

items.statement: Geopolitical developments may cause fuel rate and input cost volatility
items.quote: We are actively managing the risk posed by current geopolitical developments and potential thereof to caus e volatility in fuel rates and other input

items.statement: Western DFC not a risk as commodities carried not directly linked to railway services
items.quote: DFC is directly related to the full truckload. So, the commodity what we are carrying is not directly linked with the railway services. So that's the reason the impact of DFC will not be much on our commodity or our quantity.

items.statement: Targeting over 20% year-on-year EBITDA growth for FY27
items.quote: we will be able to maintain year-on-year EBITDA growth of over 20% for FY27

items.statement: Entered FY27 with about 20,000 open positions, 15-20% higher than previous quarter
items.quote: We entered the new fiscal year with about 20,000 open positions

items.statement: Planned exit of about 10,000 headcount in Q1 and Q2 FY27 from low-margin mandates
items.quote: there is a planned exit of about 10,000 headcount between our staffing and DA businesses in Q1 and Q2 of FY27

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 1.5%, up 10 bps sequentially; full year 1.34%, up 10 bps YoY
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin for Q4 was 1.5%, up 10 basis points over Q3 FY26. For the full year, EBITDA margin came in at 1.34%, about 10 basis points higher than FY 2025

items.statement: General staffing PAPM improved to INR689 in Q4 from INR669 in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Sustained PAPM improvement in general staffing, which moved to INR689 in Q4 from INR669 in Q1

items.statement: Employment outlook report shows net employment change improving to 4.7% for H1 FY27 with 58% employers planning to expand workforce
items.quote: Our own employment outlook report published in March confirms this po sitive sentiment showing the net employment change improving to 4.7% for H1

items.statement: BFSI in-sourcing impact largely behind; growth from wallet share gains at private banks, SFBs, mid-sized NBFCs and Tier 2/3 shift
items.quote: We believe the BFSI drop is largely behind us, though the shape of recovery will vary by segment

items.statement: Specialised Staffing PAPM realization up 17% YoY; GCC segment contributes 60% headcount and 67% revenue
items.quote: our PAPM realization has gone up by 17% and our year-on-year PBT has grown by 15%

items.statement: Specialised Staffing expanding into bot model, RPO, hire-train-deploy and AI-led hiring for higher margins
items.quote: today, we are partnering with many of them on bot models, which give us higher margins. And along with that, we are also doing models such as RPO

items.statement: Investing in technology, talent and adjacencies; HCM platform not expected to drag group margins in FY27
items.quote: we are very keen on investing in the future in the technology, in talent, the adjacencies that will make TeamLease the absolute default partner

items.statement: Labor codes to create transition costs in FY27 but long-term tailwind for formalization; Shram Suvidha Portal expected in 18-20 months
items.quote: the 4 labor codes while a clear long-term tailwind for formalization and organized staffing will create some transiti on costs across the industry through FY27

items.statement: DSO at 6 days, funding exposure at 14%, TDS receivable INR149 crores
items.quote: DSO and staffing business stands at 6 days and funding exposure is at 14%, bo th consistent with prior periods

items.statement: Board approved buyback up to 25% of free reserves at INR1,600 per share funded from free cash
items.quote: the Board has approved a buyback of up to 25% of free reserves at a price of INR1,600 per share to be funded from our existing free cash

items.statement: Suparna Mitra took over as MD & CEO; transition going well
items.quote: Now we've had Suparna join us to take over the MD and CEO role. And the transition has been going well

items.statement: General staffing underlying business added 14,000 associates in FY26 adjusting for NBFC in-sourcing
items.quote: adjusting for that Q3 transition reveals that the underlying business actually added about 14,000 associates

items.statement: Specialised Staffing added 85 new logos in FY26 contributing INR20 crores annualized revenue
items.quote: We added 85 new logos in the last year, 24 of them in Q4, co ntributing nearly about INR20 crores in annualized revenue

items.statement: HR Services full year revenue and EBITDA grew 22% and 23% respectively; built 42 universities in EdTech in Q4
items.quote: In HR Services, full year revenue and EBITDA grew at 22% and 23%, respectively. We built 42 universities in our EdTech segment in the quarter

items.statement: RegTech combined digital and services MRR at INR3.6 crores per month
items.quote: Combined digital and services MRR of RegTech verticals stood at INR3.6 crores per month

items.statement: Labor codes and Shram Suvidha Portal to drive shift from unorganized to organized staffing players
items.quote: with the new labor codes and the digital infrastru cture going live, there will be a lot more shift from unorganized to organized

items.statement: Recruiter productivity improved 20% YoY in Specialised Staffing via AI-enabled ATS and upskilling
items.quote: Our recruiter productivity has improved by 20% year-on-year, reflecting the positive impact of our investments in upskilling our recruiters, building AI-led efficiencies

items.statement: Added 120 new logos in general staffing in FY26, two-thirds under variable markup model
items.quote: adding about 120 new logos over the full year with almost two-thirds of those coming in under variable market structures

items.statement: AI impact creating new roles (AI developers, integrators, data engineers) offsetting traditional IT hiring decline
items.quote: there are newer jobs that are getting created. Also, apart from the IT services companies, there are jobs for these roles, which is AI integrators, AI developers, data engineers

items.statement: Income tax refund of INR143 crores received in Q4 including INR13.1 crores interest; underlying PBT growth ~20% YoY excluding refund
items.quote: There is INR143 crores income tax refund pertaining to assessment year 2024-'25 received during this quarter, which includes INR 13.1 crores of interest income

items.statement: FY27 capex expected to remain similar to FY26 (~₹800 crores)
items.quote: Our India capex in FY 26 was approximately ₹ 800 crores compared to ₹ 600 crores in the previous year, and was driven by new plants and investments in new growth areas. We expect capital expenditure in FY 27 to remain similar to FY 26.

items.statement: FY26 standalone capex was ~₹800 crores vs ₹600 crores in FY25
items.quote: Our India capex in FY 26 was approximately ₹ 800 crores compared to ₹ 600 crores in the previous year, and was driven by new plants and investments in new growth areas.

items.statement: ABS capacity expansion of 12 lakh units/annum underway, SOP expected September 2026
items.quote: Work has commenced on this expansion of 12 lakh units per annum, with SOP expected in September 2026.

items.quote: The Chennai plant will have a capacity of 3 million disc brake assemblies per annum and 4 million discs per annum, which is part of our total 7.6 million disc brake assemblies and 8.6 million brake discs per annum planned at Endurance.

items.statement: Inverted front fork monthly capacity rising from 60k to 75k by June 2026, 100k by end FY27
items.quote: With increasing OEM offtake, we are adding assembly lines which will take our monthly sales of inverted front forks from 60,000 units to 75,000 units per month, by June 2026 and to 100,000 units per month by the end of FY 27.

items.statement: 3W brake assembly volumes to double from 0.6M to 1.2M units/annum by end FY27
items.quote: We are also progressing with the planned increase in our 3W brake assembly volumes, which will double from 0.6 million to 1.2 million units per annum by end of this year.

items.statement: Alloy wheel total capacity now 48 lakh wheel sets/annum across Chakan and AURIC Bidkin
items.quote: The total capacity in these plants is now 48 lakh wheel sets of front and rear wheels per annum.

items.statement: New aluminium forging press (5th) SOP Q3 FY27 at new Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar plant
items.quote: We are progressing with the addition of a fifth aluminium forging press. All our presses will be set up in a new forging plant at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, which will start SOP in Q 3 of this financial year.

items.statement: AURIC Shendra cumulative orders ₹513 crores peak annual potential by FY29
