items.statement: Solar damper ₹118 crores & actuator ₹227 crores orders won (total ₹345 crores)
items.quote: The total business won is ₹118 crores for solar dampers, and ₹227 crores for solar actuators, totalling ₹345 crores of business.

items.statement: Europe FY26 orders booked €15.8M including VW, Porsche castings & EV plastic parts
items.quote: In our Europe business, we have booked orders worth €15.80 million in FY 26. This includes large machine casting orders from Volkswagen and Porsche and certain plastic injection molding parts for EVs.

items.statement: Maxwell FY26 new business ₹56 crores; cumulative orders ₹247 crores/annum peaking Q2 FY28
items.quote: At Maxwell, we have won ₹56 crores of new business in FY 26, which has taken the total cumulative orders won to ₹247 crores per annum, which will peak in Q 2 of the next financial year.

items.statement: Battery pack plant order ~₹300 crores/annum, could reach ₹350-360 crores, then ₹600 crores by FY28
items.quote: This is a n order which is approximately, as I've said ₹ 300 crores but I think could go to ₹350- ₹360 crores per annum. And of course, this order will go up to ₹ 600 crores per annum by next financial year based on the outlook of the customer.

items.statement: Standalone FY26 EBITDA margin 12.6% (would be 13.3% excluding ₹73.7 cr non-value-add RM cost)
items.quote: If I just take the ₹73.7 crores impact of alloy and steel, which is completely a non-value add, if you see the numbers from that angle, our EBITDA margin instead of 12.6% should have been 13.3%.

items.statement: Europe Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 20.5% (€21.9M), full year 18.5% (€72.4M)
items.quote: Speaking about energy, for sure we have had an increase in the las t 2 months due to the war in Iran, but the situation was bad in the previous year as well due to the war in Ukraine. So, everyday we face this kind of problem. But despite the increase of energy cost in the previous quarter in Eur ope, due to the important increase of volume, we have been able to optimize EBITDA and we closed with

items.statement: Raw material cost up ₹160 crores (1.5% RMC increase) in FY26; aluminium alloy & steel up ₹73.7 crores
items.quote: If I see the whole year, the raw material increased by ₹160 crores, which is in absolute terms 1.5% RMC increase. So if you see our RMC percentage went up from 65.3% to 66.82%. ₹73.70 crores out of this was for aluminium alloy and steel increase, which is a non -value add increase.

items.statement: Pass-through of commodity cost increases with ~1 quarter lag for some customers; seeking spot increases
items.quote: Due to the continuous inflationary trend in the commodity prices, RMC costs were higher due to cost increases yet to be passed on, as pass-on is with a lag of a Quarter for some customers.

items.statement: Europe: quarterly price adjustment based on prior quarter aluminium average; supplier indexed similarly
items.quote: As you know, we have a clear rule with our customer and we change the price quarter per quarter considering the average of the price of the previous quarter. And so it means that in our profit and loss we have an impact only if the price of aluminium continues to grow.

items.statement: India 2W sales Q4 FY26: 7.2M units (+25.4% YoY); EV scooters 339k (+53.9%); PV 1.6M (+14.4%); 3W 0.3M (+32.2%)
items.quote: In the Indian automotive sector, as per SIAM, 2W sales reached 7.2 million units in Q4 of FY 26, up 25.4% year -on-year, with motorcycles at 19.8% growth and scooters at 37.1% growth. The 2W EV scooters grew 53.9% from 220,000 units to 339,000 units in Q4 FY 26.

items.statement: Europe new car sales Q4 FY26 +4% YoY; BEV 19.4%, PHEV 9.5%, HEV 38.6% share
items.quote: In the European Union, new car sales saw a year-on-year rise of 4% in Q4 FY 26, with Italy and Spain recording high single percentage growth, while France recorded a degrowth. In Q4 FY 26 new car volumes in Europe, there was a 19.4% share of battery electric vehicles, 9.5% share of plug-in hybrids, and 38.6% share of hybrids.

items.statement: 4W revenue ~6% of FY26; target to reach 10% soon driven by AURIC Shendra, Chennai, Vallam, proprietary
items.quote: Our plan is to reach 10% soon, but the question in the 10% is because it may look as a lower number, but the sales in 2W are also growing. If you see the sales growth which we have planned in the next 3 to 5 years is very large. Definitely you will see with the AURIC Shendra, with Tata Mahindra, with our plants in Chennai and Vallam, and the proprietary business, you will see a very good traction

items.statement: EV business wins: ₹1,185 crores conventional products (ex-Bajaj), ₹1,724 crores including Maxwell & battery pack
items.quote: Cumulative India business wins for electric vehicles in the conventional product areas stand at ₹1,185 crores without considering Bajaj Auto wins. This reaches ₹1,368 crores per annum of orders if we include the Bajaj Auto EV business. The total electric vehicle business win is ₹1,724 crores per annum if we add Maxwell and the battery pack business.

items.statement: New alloy wheel OEMs: Honda, Suzuki, Ather, Piaggio added to Bajaj, RE, TVS, Yamaha
items.quote: In addition to Bajaj, Royal Enfield, TVS, and Yamaha, we would be also now serving new OEM customers such as Honda Motors and Scooters India, Ather, Suzuki, and Piaggio, from our alloy wheel plants both in Chakan and AURIC, Bidkin.

items.statement: AURIC Shendra: US EV OEM, JLR, Yazaki, Valeo (Mahindra/Tata EV platforms)
items.quote: These orders are from a large US EV OEM for automotive as well as non -auto applications, from Jaguar Land Rover, as well as from Yazaki and Valeo for electric platforms of Mahindra and Tata Motors.

items.statement: Chakan die-casting: Tata Motors & Mahindra demand up 35-40% this year
items.quote: We are seeing strong traction at this plant, with demand from these OEMs increasing by approximately 35% to 40% in this year.

items.statement: Maharashtra PSI 2019 incentive increased from ₹600 crores to ₹858 crores via addendum
items.quote: Under the Maharashtra Package Scheme of Incentives 2019 scheme, we had received an addendum taking our incentive up from ₹ 600 crores to ₹ 858 crores. These incentives will be availed through the Industrial Promotion Subsidy by way of a state GST refund, broadly over a seven-year period.

Work has commenced on this expansion of 12 lakh units per annum, with SOP expected in September 2026. This project is being implemented irrespective of t

items.statement: ABS volumes FY26: 280k single-channel; FY27 target 100-150% growth with dual-channel SOP June 2026
items.quote: In FY '26 we did about 280,000 ABSes, which were single-channel. This year we are doubling, but we feel this figure will go up also, looking at the line of sight and looking at the dual-channel which we are starting from July. So I think the growth can be 100% to 150% compared to last year.

items.statement: Europe outperformed market: FY26 turnover +28.9% (+2% organic ex-Stöferle); parts sales +6.4%

items.statement: Q1 FY27 margin volatility expected due to rising oil, gas, alloy costs from Middle East conflict
items.quote: Well, I would say that Q1 will still be a bit volatile because as the war goes on, the prices are not going down, whether it's oil, whether it's gas, whether it's alloy. They continue to rise. So we will se e a bit of volatility.

items.statement: Electronics division expected to grow around 40% in FY27 with margins of 9.5-10%
items.quote: Continuing the strong growth momentum, this division is expected to grow by around 40% in FY '27.

items.statement: Railway division expected to grow 30-35% in both FY27 and FY28
items.quote: backed by strong order book visibility of INR2,600 crores plus and product portfolio expansion, we remain optimistic of division's growth of 30% to 35% for both FY '27 and FY '28.

items.statement: Consolidated margin pressure of 50-100 bps expected, temporary in nature

items.statement: Industry volume growth estimated at 12-13% for FY27, Q1 expected around 20%
items.quote: On the complete year side, we are estimating a growth of somewhere around 12% to 13% on the complete year.

items.statement: FY28 cash outflow for capex expected INR1,400-1,500 crore
items.quote: So it will be same because in '28, our new Ascent-K circuit larger capex will happen. There also we'll have a better -- much larger pay terms from the capex suppliers. So you can expect a similar or a little higher around INR1,400 crores, INR1,500 crores of cash outflow for the capex in terms of cash.

items.statement: Ascent-K Circuits HDI PCB facility construction to start by June 2026, trial production Q3 FY28

items.statement: Ascent Hosur multilayer PCB trial production by Q3 FY27, commercial by Feb 2027
items.quote: We expect that the trial production will start by Q3 and commercial production will start by February, mid of February of next 2027.

items.statement: Sidwal Greenfield facility in Faridabad ready, trial production underway, commercial production from current quarter
items.quote: Sidwal's Greenfield fac ility of HVAC, Pantry, Doors and Gangways in Faridabad is now ready and trial production is underway, and commercial production is expected to begin from current quarter

items.statement: Consumer Durable division operating EBITDA grew 6% to INR593 crore in FY26
items.quote: Operating EBITDA for the year increased by 6% year-on-year and stood at INR593 crores compared to INR562 crores in financial year '25.

items.statement: Electronics division operating EBITDA grew 89% to INR287 crore in FY26
items.quote: Operating EBITDA for the year recorded growth of 8 9% year-on-year and stood at INR287 crores compared to INR151 crores in financial year '25.

items.statement: Railway division operating EBITDA grew 8% to INR90 crore in FY26
items.quote: the resulting operating EBITDA stood at INR90 crores, a growth of 8% year-on-year.

items.statement: PCBA margins ~5%, PCB margins ~12-13% (target 16-17%), Power-One ~15%
items.quote: So PCB -- in PCBA, we are at about 5% , in PCB, we are at about 12%, 13%. This generally business is about 16%, 17% business, but because of CCL and because of gold prices and currency, that is, but they are taking price increases from the customer that's underway.

items.statement: Railway division margins expected 16-17% in FY27
items.quote: But the margins in the railway side, we expect in the range of 16% to 17%.

items.statement: Copper clad laminate prices increased >60% in last year, gold prices up ~60%
items.quote: For bare PCB businesses, there has been increase in input cost of copper clad laminate. Prices has increased by more than 60% in last 1 year and still increasing. Gold prices have also increased by approximately 60% in last 1 year and prices still continue to increase.

items.statement: Minimum wage increased 35% in Haryana, ~22% in UP
items.quote: Basically, first factor is the minimum wage increase, which happened of 35% in Haryana, which led to riots in Noida and UP government also in turn increased minimum wages to about 22%.

items.statement: PCB business has 2-quarter lag in passing cost increases vs 1-quarter in Tier 1
items.quote: in the PCB business, we are Tier 2. We don't supply directly to Maruti or Hyundai, we supply to Tier 1 guys, and that's where the inventory has to be taken care at 2 levels. And hence, the lag in the PCB business to increase the cost is about 2 quarters.

items.statement: RAC industry flattish in FY26, Amber outperformed with 14% growth
items.quote: Owing to weather conditions, room AC industry has remained largely flattish during the year. In line with our guidance, the division outperformed the industry, recording a growth of 14% over previous year.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 industry volume growth expected ~20% due to low base and heat wave
items.quote: Against last year because the base was very weak, the industry expects to grow by somewhere around 20% in quarter 1.

items.statement: Net debt INR511 crore as of March 2026 vs INR780 crore March 2025
items.quote: On the balance sheet front, net debt stood at INR511 crores as of March '26 against INR780 crores in March '25.

items.statement: Net debt expected to increase to INR700-800 crore by FY27 end due to capex
items.quote: you can expect around INR700 crores to INR800 crores of net debt by year-end.

items.statement: Antidumping duty of 30% on PCBs up to 6 layers protects domestic demand
items.quote: you would have seen that there is an antidumping duty imposed by government to a tune of 30%. So despite of this commodity increase of CCL and gold has been a global phenomenon. It's not particularly to India. So even Chinese import or Taiwanese PCB imports have gone expensive. So it's just -- and it is from -- up to 6 layers, it is protected through the antidumping duty.

items.statement: Quality control order on compressors allows 30% import of last year volumes for <2 tonne category
items.quote: And that's why the quality control order says that, but there is still a shortage in terms of the capacity built up versus the growth in the country for the room AC. And that's the reason why government has allowed to import 30% of last year imported volum es to cater to the shortage.

items.statement: Increased stake in Unitronics Israel to 50.4%, achieving majority ownership
items.quote: Further, strengthening our foothold in the promising and fast -growing industrial automation space, we have now increased our stake in Unitronics, Israel to 50.4%, achieving the majority ownership.

items.statement: Electronics revenue mix: PCBA INR2,281 crore, PCB ~INR600 crore, Power Electronics/Industrial Automation balance
items.quote: PCBA is INR2,281 crores, almost INR2,300 crores and then total on the other side is about INR596 crores, which is Power-One, Unitronics and Shogini and Ascent clocks crossed INR402 crores. So almost about INR1,000 crores is the other, out of which if you see Shogini plus PCB will be about INR500 crores -- around INR600 crores is PCB.

items.statement: PLI incentive received INR49.5 crore for FY25, expect INR78 crore for FY26
items.quote: On the incentive front, we have received a PLI amounting amount of INR49.5 crores in April pertaining to financial year '25. In the current year, we expect to receive INR78 crores under the PLI scheme for the financial year '26.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin expected to improve by 2-3% over FY26's 17.4% driven by higher utilization
items.quote: I think we are -- I have already mentioned that we are looking for the better margins compared with this year. So yes, we are expecting at least 2%, 3% higher EBITDA compared to the what we had, purely because of the operational efficiencies when we are driving up the utilization beyond 70%, we should able to rationalize a lot of cost.

items.statement: FY27 capacity utilization target over 75% from above 60% in FY26
items.quote: Our plant facilities operated at above 60% utilization in FY '26 due to the various challenges what we have faced. With improving sentiment and enhanced customer engagement, we target over 75% utilization in FY '27, supporting EBITDA margin expansion.

items.statement: FY27 volume growth expected 35-45% with 15% utilization increase
items.quote: We already said that we will grow by about 15% on capacity utilization and volumes are between 35% to 45%, volume growth also will happen in FY27.

items.statement: FY28 revenue target INR1,500 crores driven by 85-90% utilization and long-term contract commercialization
items.quote: First and foremost, we are expecting to utilize our assets by FY '28 by optimal, when we say optimal, 85% to 90% that will drive us. Also in FY '28, the special project where we got the advance which will come in commercial operation. So that will also add to it, and that gives us confidence.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at INR125 crores fully funded by internal accruals at Pakhajan plant
items.quote: For FY '27, the company has planned a capex of INR125 crores, which will be completely funded through internal accruals.

items.statement: FY26 capex was INR75 crores split across R&D, Pakhajan and Vapi
items.quote: Well, FY '26, we spent about INR75 crores, INR25 crores we spent on R&D, about INR40 crores, INR42 crores on Pakhajan and about INR7 crores, INR8 crores into the Vapi.

items.statement: 15-year long-term agreement secured with INR51.4 crores advance received; revenue from FY28
items.quote: A key milestone was securing a 15-year long-term agreement. This reinforces our capabilities and enhance revenue visibility for us in the long term. Advanced funding of INR51.4 crores has already been received, reflecting strong customer confidence.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin improved to 17.4% from product mix, operating leverage and cost optimization
items.quote: Consolidated revenue reached INR830 crores, up 22.7% year-on-year, while EBITDA stood at INR144 crores with margin improving to 17.4%, supported by product mix, operating leverage and cost optimization.

items.statement: Gross margin guidance 40-42% for coming years; fixed cost leverage from higher utilization to improve margins
items.quote: I think 40% -- anything between 40% to 42% should be the right guidance. What will help us as we are going to do more utilization of our -- all the assets that will help us to leverage all our expenses, fixed expenses and that will come down drastically, which will also help us to improvise the margins.

items.statement: FY26 volume growth 33% YoY driven by industrial chemicals segment; domestic demand growing from new and existing customers
items.quote: For FY '26, volume growth was 33% year-on-year, supported by stronger customer traction and scale up across categories. Industrial Chemicals contributed 87% of revenue for both the quarter and the full year.

items.statement: Americas market performing well; Europe slowdown offset by Asia expansion and Americas growth
items.quote: Yes. Definitely, the tariff has helped us to expand our sales in Q4. And that comes in the results. And we believe that the Americas market is doing very well for us even in this quarter.

items.statement: Supply chain disruptions: import delays 8-12 weeks vs normal 3-4; US export transit 60-70 days vs 25; sulfur availability challenging but manageable
items.quote: are getting delayed, which generally typically takes 3 to 4 weeks, at times it's taking more than 8 to 12 weeks to get the product. So that's one of the biggest challenge. At times, we don't know where our import contents align. And then those are the challenges when we are exporting earlier days to the U.S.A. was only 25 days. Today, it takes more than 60, 70 days to reach the container to U.S

items.statement: Working capital days reduced from 215-216 in FY25 to ~190 in FY26; target 170-175 days in 6-12 months
items.quote: I think we were at the 200-odd days in FY '25, was 215, 216 days. We are broadly down to 190 days today. Our debtors are constant that has not increased. On the stock has dropped to some extent. That will help us.

items.statement: Debt-to-EBITDA improved to 3.75x from 4.70x; prepaid INR23.3 crores of FY27 liabilities; target 2.5x comfort zone
items.quote: Financial discipline remains strong with debt-to-EBITDA improving to 3.75x from 4.70x in FY '25. We also prepaid INR23.30 crores of FY '27 liabilities, leaving only INR15.6 crores due, easing repayment pressure and enhancing flexibility.

items.statement: Absolute debt may rise but debt-to-EBITDA ratio to remain at 2.5x comfort zone
items.quote: t assure that. What we are assuming is that debt-to-EBITDA ratio to come down and our comfort zone will be in the 2.5x. That's what we want to draw. So first, let's achieve that and then we talk about the debt. Till that we don't want to talk about increasing the debt. Absolute number could rise. But when you look at the ratio point of view, it will remain that

items.statement: Pakhajan plant has 2 production buildings; can add 4 more as demand ramps up
items.quote: Honestly speaking, I don't know what is my current capacity. But I can tell you in Pakhajan, we have made 2 production building, and we can build additional 4 production building. So that four building will be start construction one by one as we see the ramp-up or the additional demand coming in.

items.statement: Industrial chemicals 87% of revenue; rubber and lube additives all performing well; no formulation business
items.quote: Industrial Chemicals contributed 87% of revenue for both the quarter and the full year, while exports accounted for 62%, underscoring resilience despite global challenges.

items.statement: 40% revenue from quarterly/half-yearly pricing contracts; 60% from spot/relationship-based orders
items.quote: Long term, when you say long term, we have customers who buy on a regular basis, they buy either quarterly pricing or 6 monthly pricing. So that is about 40% of the revenue and balance 60% come from spot what you call or customer with whom we have relation over time and they buy as and when they require.

items.statement: Chinese competition very strong in lubricant additives and industrial chemicals
items.quote: Strong, very strong. They are very, very competitive and they do come hard.

items.statement: India-EU FTA expected by early January 2026; Europe team maturing after 1 year on ground
items.quote: Well, number -- first and foremost, India, Europe and treaty FTA will come in place only by early January, hopefully, we are hopeful that it will come in by early January.

items.statement: Exports 62% of revenue; currency depreciation minor benefit offset by import costs
items.quote: There was a very, very minor. As you know, we also import equivalent quantity of raw materials from overseas. So that will always nullify. There will be a slightly more edge on export side. But if you look at net to net, there is import export and a little bit extra on export side.

items.statement: Geopolitical supply chain disruptions causing raw material delays and price volatility; no visibility on normalization timeline
items.quote: Well, I can give any number of points. Number one, a lot of our imports are getting delayed, which generally typically takes 3 to 4 weeks, at times it's taking more than 8 to 12 weeks to get the product. So that's one of the biggest challenge.

items.statement: R&D facility completed October 2025 fully operational; focusing on performance chemicals beyond traditional rubber/lube additives
items.quote: Our R&D facility completed in October '25 is now fully operational, accelerating innovation and strengthening our portfolio.

items.statement: Not pursuing CDMO model; minimum 500-1,000 metric tons per molecule; each new molecule must add at least INR50 crores revenue
items.quote: Well, CDMO is something which is done in API segment and those kind of segments. We are not in that segment here. We are not here to cater for a smaller volume kind of thing. Somebody wants 20 metric ton-100 metric tons. I don't think so Yasho is there to do that kind of a model. We have a design Pakhajan looking into the molecule, which we can produce at least 500 to 1,000 metric tons minimum and

items.statement: Planned capex of approximately INR30 billion over FY27 to FY29 across hospitality and commercial real estate portfolio, largely funded through internal accruals
items.quote: Looking ahead, we have outlined a planned capex of approximately INR30 billion over FY '27 to FY '29 across our hospitality and commercial real estate portfolio. This includes announced acquisition and committed investments and importantly, is expected to be largely funded through internal accruals, underscoring our focus on maintaining balance sheet discipline.

items.statement: Fit-out cost for Hyderabad Ritz-Carlton project close to INR5,600 million, largely back-ended after possession in Q4 FY28
items.quote: Our fit-out cost shall be close to INR5,600 million and largely after we get the possession in quarter 4 FY '28, so it is back ended.

items.statement: Added 2 major projects to pipeline: Udaipur Resort (144 keys) and Hyderabad Ritz-Carlton (330 keys), total pipeline now 1,655 keys across 7 assets
items.quote: During the quarter, we added 2 major projects to our pipeline, both in high-demand destinations with strategic advantage and potential to deliver high returns over the long term.

items.statement: Signed LOI for additional 66,000 sq ft at Bangalore, taking overall CRE occupancy to over 83%; Powai CRE occupancy at 90%
items.quote: During the quarter, we signed LOI for an additional 66,000 square f eet at Bangalore, taking the overall occupancies to over 83

items.statement: Hospitality EBITDA margin declined 81 bps YoY to 43.9% for FY26 due to resort assets at early stabilization stage (avg 43% occupancy) and incremental Bangalore inventory costs
items.quote: EBITDA increased 12% year-on-year to INR7,603 million with EBITDA margins at 43.9%, a decline of 81 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: Q4 RevPAR declined 3% YoY driven by 7.7 pp occupancy drop, primarily from Mumbai underperformance and West Asia geopolitical tensions causing ~9,000 room night cancellations in March
items.quote: RevPAR declined 3% year-on-year in quarter 4, largely driven by a 7.7 percentage point drop in occupancy.

items.statement: Athiva Khandala ADR sustaining north of INR15,000; Ritz-Carlton Hyderabad expected to achieve INR25,000 ARR easily given market positioning
items.quote: The pickup in occupancy with ADR sustaining north of INR15,000 gives us confidence for the upcoming monsoons, which will be followed by the wedding season.

items.statement: Monthly CRE rental exit run rate touched INR280 million in March 2026; expect to scale to INR300 million during FY27
items.quote: Our March '26 run rate of rentals touched INR280 million, as indicated in the last call. While growth in FY '26-'27 would be driven by improvement in occupancies at Powai and Bangalore, commissioning of CIGNUS II in FY '27-'28 will bring a major growth in this business.

items.statement: Net debt reduced from INR25 billion (Mar'24) to ~INR19 billion (Mar'26) despite ~INR19 billion deployed in growth capex/acquisitions; ~INR15 billion funded through internal accruals
items.quote: Over the last 2 years, we have deployed approximately INR19 billion towards growth capex and acquisitions. Despite the significant investment phase, net debt has reduced from INR25 billion as of March '24 to approximately INR19 billion as of March '26.

items.statement: Enabling approval for debt raise up to INR10 billion; purely enabling with no immediate plan to raise incremental debt
items.quote: We have also taken an enabling approval for debt raise of up to INR10 billion. To clarify, this is purely enabling in nature, and there is no immediate plan to raise incremental debt.

items.statement: Completed acquisition of Udaipur Resort for INR1,710 million (144 keys, 8.2 acres); announced Hyderabad Ritz-Carlton greenfield project on long-term lease from Mindspace REIT
items.quote: We completed the acquisition of Udaipur Resort, marking our entry into this fast-growing and deep leisure market of Udaipur. We have paid a total consideration of INR1,710 million for 144 key resort spread over 8.2 acres of land.

items.statement: Hospitality RevPAR for FY26 up 5% to INR9,226; Q4 RevPAR declined 3% YoY
items.quote: RevPAR for the year was up by 5% to INR9,226.

items.statement: Foreign tourist arrivals contributed ~40% of mix; lost ~9,000 room nights in March from FTA cancellations; domestic group segment grew from 20% to 22% in last month
items.quote: Just to give you a number, we lost almost 9,000 room nights from foreign tourist arrivals and some attached business, as I had referred to in my speech from the domestic side, which was a much smaller number, but still an attached number.

items.statement: West Asia geopolitical tensions caused ~10-12% business disruption in Q4; monitoring foreign travel recovery; crew displacement and MICE impact from CIGNUS II construction at Powai
items.quote: Overall, I think the political tensions have caused about a 10% to 12% disruption in our business.

items.statement: Targeting 20% revenue from leisure segment (drivable distance 1-1.5 hrs from key airports, deep markets like Goa, Udaipur, Jaipur); diversifying from business-heavy portfolio
items.quote: On the leisure side, we have always said that we wanted to diversify our portfolio to get to at least 20% of our revenue from the leisure segment.

items.statement: No specific regulatory changes mentioned; operating in standard hospitality and CRE regulatory environment
items.quote: We continue to focus on disciplined execution, operational excellence and prudent capital allocation as we move forward.

items.statement: Foreign tourist arrivals impacted by West Asia tensions; domestic leisure demand strong; weddings shifting from Middle East back to India
items.quote: Already, I think the Middle East image has taken a bit of a beating. And therefore, we expect the marriages to move from Middle East back to India.

items.statement: No management changes or key hires mentioned; focus on asset management team for margin stability
items.quote: We remain focused on ma intaining cost - efficient operating structures, project productivity and exercising disciplined asset level cost control as the portfolio scales

items.statement: Not applicable - non-lender/insurer business
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains strong. Our asset portfolio is well positioned, and our growth strategy is aligned with lo ng-term demand drivers

items.statement: No dividend or buyback announcements mentioned
items.quote: We continue to maintain comfortable liquidity position with a cash buffer of around INR4 billion as of year-end.

items.statement: Mumbai ADR growth 0-2% vs India 6-8%; Chalet's micro-market variance starker; supply continues to lag demand supporting confidence
items.quote: As per industry reports, Mumbai saw ADR growth of only 0% to 2% and an occupancy decline of 0 to 2 percentage points during January to March '26 compared to last year. In contrast, India overall average recorded ADR growth of 6% to 8% with a limited occupancy decline of 0 to 2 percentage points.

items.statement: Green energy consumption increased to 65%; Dow Jones Sustainability Index score improved from 67 to 82 (2nd globally among hospitality peers)
items.quote: Also, I would like to highlight that our green energy consumption has now moved up to 65%.

items.statement: CIGNUS II Powai on track for FY27 end substantial completion; Taj Delhi Airport 70 rooms launch by Q4 FY27; Mindspace excavation begun at Hyderabad and Airoli
items.quote: Work is at full swing at the CIGNUS II Powai, and we are on track for a FY '27 end substantial completion, although the West Asia crisis has put some pressure on labour availability.

items.statement: April stronger and surprised on YoY trend; May very strong (benefiting from weak base due to Operation Sindoor); June looks steady; expect fairly strong quarter overall
items.quote: April has been stronger and actually has surprised us also on a year-on-year trend. And May is really strong. But to give you a full picture, May last year at this time was very weak because of Operation Sindoor. So, we are getting a bit of advantage for that. June looks steady. So, this quarter will be fairly strong overall is our expectation.

items.statement: City hotel margins stable at flow-through = margin level; leisure portfolio margins expected to grow to mid-40s; CRE margins at 83-84% with some growth scope; asset sweating to add revenue streams
items.quote: But on the leisure side, we still have some growth because we have not stabilized on the margins in our leisure portfolio. And we expect that to grow to at least mid-40s, thereby overall continuing to grow the margins of the portfolio.

items.statement: DIAL project minority equity partnership is a one-time project-level trial, not a capital decision; balance sheet strength confirmed
items.quote: This is not a capital decision for us, Jinesh. Let me clarify that. This is not a capital decision. We are trying out a project level partnership that we have not tried before.

name: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation Ltd

items.statement: Management declines to give formal FY27 volume or margin guidance due to geopolitical uncertainty, but aims to grow volumes at or above market pace and maintain or improve margins.
items.quote: However, given the uncertainty around the war in the Middle East, I will be optimistically cautious at this point of time. items.statement: Domestic MDF demand expected to grow at early double-digit to mid-teens pace in FY27.
items.quote: Domestic demand, MDF demand is expected to continue at a healthy pace of early double digit to mid-teens.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 operational EBITDA margin was 8.8%; Q4 FY26 operational EBITDA margin was 9.1%.
items.quote: Consolidated operating EBITDA, excluding the impact of currency movement on the Euro borrowing for the new plant and the one-o Ưs impacting the results, was INR35.4 crore or 9.1% of revenues in Q4FY26, while the full year number was INR132.7 crore or 8.8% of revenues.

items.statement: Reported EBITDA margin for FY26 was 6.3% after forex loss, new line inefficiencies, and higher interest and depreciation.
items.quote: Counting these in, our reported EBITDA for the full year was INR94.2 crore or 6.3% of our revenues.

items.statement: 15% price hike taken in two phases (5% + 10%) across the industry to absorb chemical cost inflation of 40-45%; slight discounting already seen in market.
items.quote: Like others, we too have announced price increase of 15% to reduce the impact on our margins.

items.statement: Chemical costs (40-45% of raw material) have risen 40-45% and are volatile; timber costs stable for 3-4 months and expected to remain stable in FY27.
items.quote: Supply chains have been impacted adversely leading to signiﬁcant escalation on cost front, especially in case of chemicals which is 40% to 45% of our raw material cost

items.statement: Operated at 60% capacity utilization in Q4 FY26; significant headroom for organic growth in FY27 without material capex.
items.quote: On our side, we operated at 60% capacity utilization in quarter four FY '26 and thus have a signiﬁcant headroom available for organic growth next year without any additional material investments

items.statement: FY27 capex limited to sustenance capex of INR20-30 crore; no significant growth capex planned for FY27 or FY28.
items.quote: The capex, in terms of what we are planning to do is just sustenance or, the basic capex that is required. So I think it would be something between INR20 crore-INR30 crore, not more at this point in time.

items.statement: MDF domestic volumes grew 29.5% YoY in Q4 FY26 and 16.9% for full year; total MDF volumes (incl. exports) grew 27.8% YoY in Q4 and 12.9% for full year.
items.quote: we achieved MDF domestic volumes growth of 29.5% year-on-year in quarter 4, while the full year growth was 16.9%.

items.statement: High-value MDF product mix was 43% by volume and 55% by value in FY26; includes Pre-lam, HDWR, thin MDF, fire-retardant, and Boil Black.
items.quote: The high-value MDF product mix for the year being 43% in volume terms and 55% in value terms.

items.statement: B2B sales to large OEMs are 7,000-8,000 cubic meters per month (~15-20% of volumes); majority sold through retail channel.
items.quote: The only B2B sales that are happening are to large format OEMs. And, that would be to the tune of maybe 7,000 to 8,000 cubic meters every month, not more than that. So I would say about 15% to 20%.

items.statement: DSOs at 21 days in FY26 (up from 11 days in FY25) due to higher OEM/export sales and March stocking; core cash conversion cycle at 38 days.
items.quote: Our DSOs at 21 days is the best in the wood panel industry and reﬂects our very strong brand positioning. Our core cash conversion cycle is at 38 days for the full year

items.statement: Reported net debt INR156 crore at end of March 2026, increased due to adverse FX on Euro borrowings; core leverage comfortable and debt reduced.
items.quote: Our debt has further reduced this year, although because of the unfavourable FX change, the reported net debt was INR156 crore at the end of March.

items.statement: Industry MDF capacity estimated at 4-4.5 million cubic meters per annum; FY26 industry demand estimated at ~3 million cubic meters (15% growth), thin MDF ~25% of market.
items.quote: On the supply side, the overall MDF capacity in the country is 4 to 4.5 million cubic meter per annum, depending on the actual product mix oƯered by the suppliers.

items.statement: Industry-wide 15% price hike taken; some competitors offering targeted discounts (4.5-5%) but management expects limited long-term margin impact.
items.quote: Yes, I would say this price increase in two phases which we took, 5% plus 10%, has been across the industry.

items.statement: EPCG benefit of INR25 crore recognized in FY26 (vs INR35 crore in FY25); remaining ~INR26 crore benefit linked to export volumes and may spill to FY28 if exports don't recover.
items.quote: Quarter one was ﬁve, the next quarter was six, quarter three was eight and this quarter we have taken INR6 crore as EPCG. So overall INR25 odd crore have been accounted for as EPCG in the year against 35 which were accounted one shot in quarter four last year

items.statement: Geopolitical situation in Middle East biggest variable; export business halted due to freight issues; chemical cost volatility and competitive discounting create margin uncertainty.
items.quote: The ongoing geopolitical situation in the Middle East is the biggest variable at play right now. Supply chains have been impacted adversely leading to signiﬁcant escalation on cost front, especially in case of chemicals which is 40% to 45% of our raw material cost

items.statement: New hires: Prakash (domestic sales head, joined March 2025) and Himanshu Jindal (CFO, joined Q1 FY26).
items.quote: On the people front, we brought in Prakash last year in March to lead domestic sales and got Himanshu on board later in Q1 to lead

items.statement: Plywood volumes grew 18% YoY in Q4 FY26; full year plywood volumes nearly flat YoY.
items.quote: On the plywood side, we had a strong growth of 18% in volumes in quarter 4 as a result of which on a full year basis, we closed the year almost ﬂat over last year

items.statement: 6% price increase taken on plywood starting Q1 FY27.
items.quote: We have taken a 6% price increase on plywood starting this quarter.

items.statement: Plywood capacity expansion possible at existing location with minimal investment, but only after existing capacities fully utilized; trading volumes limited to dealer support.
items.quote: We already have certain plans in the pipeline subject to our existing volumes being fully utilized. This could be an addition of capacity at our existing location with a very minimal investment and going forward an additional investment in another location.

items.statement: New competitor MDF capacities of ~400,000 cubic meters expected in H2 FY27 (Madhya Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh), ramping gradually.
items.quote: So, there are two capacities that we are aware of which are going to come in in the second half. One is in Madhya Pradesh, the other is in AP. I think the total size that we are looking at is 400,000 for the full year.

items.statement: Export volumes significantly impacted in March 2026 due to Middle East war; freight issues preventing export order fulfillment currently.
items.quote: Counting in exports, which were signiﬁcantly impacted in March after the onset of the war in the Middle East, the total MDF volumes for quarter 4 grew by 27.8% year-on-year in the quarter and by 12.9% year-on-year for the full year FY '26

items.statement: Plywood segment EBITDA margin ~4% in FY26; expected to improve above 5-6% with higher volumes and operating leverage.
items.quote: We did something like 4%. Yes, if we are able to do more volumes, automatically, the operational eƯiciencies kick in, So the advantage on operating leverage, operating eƯiciencies, all of that get kick in. Yes, so we should

items.statement: Raw material mix rationalization ongoing: shifting from Eucalyptus to cheaper species; South India Eucalyptus 20-25% more expensive than alternatives; North India higher Eucalyptus usage due to proximity.
items.quote: Well, I think that is reﬂected, for example, in the South of India, Eucalyptus continues to be about 20% to 25% more expensive than other species. But again, availability and how far you have to transport the other species also come into play

items.statement: MDF realizations down 3.6% YoY in FY26 due to higher OEM sales and product mix change post AP plant addition.
items.quote: MDF realizations were lower by 3.6% over the last year in FY '26. Some portion of this was also attributable to the increase in OEM sales, apart from the change in product mix post addition of the new plant at AP.

items.statement: Thin MDF capacity fungible across three lines; not a dedicated line; production allocated based on efficiency, freight, and grade optimization.
items.quote: We set up a plant which was capable to produce thin MDF in a very optimal way. But it is not just a thin MDF plant. Now, what we are doing is our capacities are sort of fungible across the three lines.

items.statement: Management expects Telangana cluster EBITDA growth of 10%-12% in FY27 despite Kondapur and Kompally expansions
items.quote: With the cluster, I think there should be a healthy growth rate. It won't be soft, maybe around 10%-12% EBITDA growth we should look at for Telangana cluster.

items.statement: Management targets net debt to EBITDA ratio of 1:2 and plans to retire INR 1,000 crore debt from QIP proceeds

items.statement: Management expects new unit EBITDA losses to be less than half of FY26's INR 128 crore drag in FY27
items.quote: But obviously, it will be less than half the number.

items.statement: Kondapur new facility Phase 1 to commission 400-500 beds in June 2026, remaining 300 beds later; INR 50-75 crore capex for two additional floors in FY28-29
items.quote: So, the new hospital will have 800 beds, of which in Phase 1, because we are already at an occupancy of 200 beds and we need headroom for growth, we will commission at least 400 to 500 beds in Phase 1.

items.statement: Management plans greenfield expansions in Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra, Telangana over next 24-36 months
items.quote: We will also use the next 24, 36 months to get the greenfield projects going. So, we obviously have plans to expand in Karnataka, in Kerala, Tamil Nadu, we are going to add one hospital.

items.statement: Kondapur new 800-bed facility transition starting first week of June 2026, old facility to shut down after 1-3 months overlap
items.quote: So, we will shift into the new Kondapur facility starting in the first week of June. So, the new hospital will have 800 beds in total.

items.statement: Bangalore hospitals to operationalize more beds at 60% occupancy on current operational beds
items.quote: 60% on the current occupancy, on the current operational beds, we will operationalize the other beds.

items.statement: FY26 mature units revenue INR 3,335 crore with 29.5% EBITDA margin; new units revenue INR 597 crore with INR 128 crore EBITDA erosion
items.quote: So, from the mature units for the entire financial year, we did a revenue of INR 3,335 crores, to be exact, out of that INR 3,931 crores of revenue which we have reported.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 mature units EBITDA margin 28.5-29% on INR 862 crore revenue; new units EBITDA erosion INR 32 crore on INR 224 crore revenue
items.quote: Whereas the EBITDA, which we have reported almost INR 216 crores in this quarter, out of that INR 250-odd crores is from the mature unit. So, to say that almost 28.5% or 29% of EBITDA margin from matured unit we continue to maintain.

items.statement: Thane EBITDA neutral at March and April 2026 exit; Mahadevapuram expected EBITDA positive before October 2026; PES expected EBITDA positive by March 2027
items.quote: As far as Thane is concerned, March exit number, we were EBITDA neutral. April also, we were EBITDA neutral. But also, we added some doctors now again in the month of May.

items.statement: Bangalore Mahadevapuram doing INR 17 crore monthly revenue with visibility to reach INR 25-30 crore over next 12 months
items.quote: Now it is 8 months old, 8-9 months old. We are doing an average of INR 17 crores a month based on Q4 numbers. And we have very clear visibility of how it will go to INR 25-30 crores over the next 12 months.

items.statement: Bangalore ARPOB normalized at INR 75,000 annually; Andhra Pradesh ARPOB normalized at INR 26,000-27,000
items.quote: But you should fairly assume, for all models, we should assume 75,000 as a base and work on it.

items.statement: Insurance empanelment delays due to new GIC common empanelment initiative causing confusion; Nashik pending STAR, Medi Assist, GIPSA; Thane got GIPSA, STAR and Medi Assist almost through; Bangalore 3-4 more months for empanelment
items.quote: I think there is a new council, GIC, which also got introduced in the same financial year. And because of that, there led to a lot of confusion as to who empanels hospitals, will GIC do it, will companies do it directly.

items.statement: Planning QIP of INR 1,500 crore in 1-2 months to retire debt and fund greenfield expansions; debt peaked at INR 3,000+ crore
items.quote: So, the change is only because of we are coming up, we are planning for a QIP in a month or two.

items.statement: Current debt INR 3,000+ crore; target net debt to EBITDA 1:2; QIP proceeds to retire INR 1,000 crore debt
items.quote: Right now, we have a debt of almost INR 3,000 plus crores. We want to use the capital raised from the QIP to retire debt.

items.statement: Exploring small acquisition opportunities of 400-500 beds combined in home markets over next two quarters
items.quote: There are one, two small acquisition opportunities that can potentially come up over the next two quarters, but they are not significantly big. They are around 400, 500 beds, both put together.

items.statement: Palakkad 300-bed hospital acquisition consolidated; current revenue INR 6.5-7 crore monthly with 5% negative EBITDA; expected break-even June-July 2026, potential INR 12-15 crore monthly
items.quote: It is like how we have in Kollam. It is a 250 bedded hospital, sorry, 300 bed hospital. The revenue potential would be around INR 12 to 15 crores per month over a period of time.

items.statement: No significant doctor attrition despite competition; same doctor compensation model extended to new geographies
items.quote: We have not seen any doctor, significant doctor acquisition. We lost one or two doctors, but nothing material that we are worried of.

items.statement: FY26 operational highlights: ARPOB grew 14% YoY, ARPP grew 11.4% YoY, IP volumes grew 15.4% YoY, OP volumes grew 25.4% YoY
items.quote: Average revenue per operating bed grew by 14% on year-on-year basis. Average revenue per patient grew by 11.4% on year-on-year basis. IP and OP volumes grew by 15.4% and 25.4% respectively on year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 operational highlights: ARPOB grew 13.7% YoY, ARPP grew 14% YoY, IP volumes grew 17.9% YoY, OP volumes grew 30.1% YoY
items.quote: Average revenue per operating bed grew by 13.7% and 1.7% on year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter basis respectively. Average revenue per patient grew by 14% and 3.5% on year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter basis respectively.

items.statement: Key challenge across all new geographies is insurance empanelment delays; ramp-up trajectory similar to mature markets otherwise
items.quote: Right now, the only challenge I see is the insurance empanelment. Whatever we have learned in Thane, Bangalore, Nasik, all new clusters, we have not seen it any different from how things are in AP and Telangana.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated revenue INR 3,931 crore (+28.2% YoY), EBITDA INR 828 crore (+1.6% YoY), EBITDA margin 21.1% vs 26.6% FY25, PAT INR 242 crore vs INR 415 crore FY25
items.quote: Total revenue of INR 3,931 crore, a growth of 28.2% on year-on-year basis. EBITDA of INR 828 crore, a growth of 1.6% on year-on-year basis. EBITDA margin of 21.1% versus 26.6% in Financial Year '25.

items.statement: Targets revenue growth of 20-25% short term with EBITDA margins of 38-40% and net cash status
items.quote: We continue to target revenue growth of around 20%, 25% over the short term while maintaining healthy EBITDA margins of 38% to 40% and preserving our net cash status.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR 2,062 crores including negotiated orders
items.quote: The order book as on date stands at approximately INR2,062 crores, including orders negotiated, which provides a strong revenue visibility over the coming years.

items.statement: Additional single vendor contracts based on already supplied products stand at INR 1,900 crores
items.quote: than the order book, additional single vendor contracts based on already supplied products, which can fructify into contract this financial year stands at INR1,900 crores

items.statement: Negotiated orders of INR 1,090 crores expected to convert in 1-2 months
items.quote: I think in the next 1 to 2 months' time, we should expect the contracts to happen.

items.statement: Export order book at INR 53 crores with expectations of meaningful improvement starting this year
items.quote: The export order book as on date stands at approximately INR53 crores, and exports remain an important strategic pillar of our long-term growth road map.

items.statement: Expect contracts from global OEMs in Europe and US within 2-4 months
items.quote: I think in the next 2, 3 months' time or 4 months' time, we should start getting some contracts from these global OEMs.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin at 56% driven by in-house developed full systems with no bought-out components
items.quote: And since th ere is no bought-out in those last quarter revenue. And it is all our own full systems, which has been developed by us was sold, the margin profile was different

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 63% in FY26 from 61% in FY25 due to favorable product mix

items.statement: Building nine floors of factory space and infrastructure for seekers and scaling to multi-thousand crore company
items.quote: We are building something about nine floor of factory space to build in additional capacity to see that the larger -- as we -- the program size has increased and the volume of contracts increase to scale to multi thousand crore company.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle improved to 365 days in FY26 from 428 days in FY25, targeting 320-340 days going forward
items.quote: Our cash conversion cycle improved meaningfully to 365 days in FY26 from 428 days in FY25, reflecting strong execution, better inventory management and continuous focus on disciplined working capital control.

items.statement: Expect cash conversion cycle to settle at 320-340 days going forward

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with strong balance sheet and healthy liquidity

items.quote: Once there the execution is completed, I think in the next 4, 5 months' time, the production orders would start coming in.

items.statement: Order inflows of INR 1,121 crores in FY26, up 216% year-on-year

items.statement: Products economically priced with superior support systems compared to foreign OEMs
items.quote: Our products should be far more economically priced and support systems are going to be far superior as long as the product meets world-class specifications.

items.quote: Tejas one is part of -- some inquiries have come, we quoted for whatever products are going, avionics is going into Tejas. So this -- hopefully, the orders should come during the course of this year.

items.statement: Nearly 1,200 engineers with deep domain expertise and 15-25 year tenure driving technology development
items.quote: We have a strong in-house technology development team. We are nearly about 1,200 engineers working with us.

items.statement: Free cash flow turned positive at Rs 89 crore in FY26, one year ahead of plan
items.quote: We have 89 crores of free cash flow this year and we're really happy about this. A couple of things, this is one year ahead of plan.

items.statement: CapEx intensity target of 4% of revenue; currently at 4.7% and motoring ahead of plan

items.statement: Express business at upper end of normative margin guidance of 16-18%

items.quote: PTL margins expanded again successively and have reached… [inaudible] …on the back of a reduction in capital intensity to less than 5% of revenue and a massive reduction in net working capital days.

items.quote: As we bundle all of this performance into our segment P&L, you'll find that the transport adjusted EBITDA has expanded 260 basis points to 6.3%.

items.statement: Overall adjusted EBITDA margin at 4.4% for FY26 (Rs 457 crore on Rs 10,486 crore revenue)
items.quote: All of this translates to an overall percentage margin of about 4.4%. That gives us 457 crores of adjusted EBITDA on a revenue base of 10,486 crores.

items.statement: Core transport ROIC reached 16%, up from 5.2% earlier

items.statement: Steady-state transport ROIC potential of 25%+ driven by EBITDA margin expansion to 10%+ and capital intensity improvement
items.quote: The steady state ROICs, currently we are at 16%, but in a steady state, this number for our transport business can certainly go to 25% plus.

items.statement: Delivered over 1 billion packages in FY26; 306 million in Q4 FY26 with sequential growth

items.statement: No broad pricing increase planned; 1-2 rupee increase seen on air shipping network due to ATF cost
items.quote: I suspect the 1 to 2 rupees increase that you're seeing would have been immediately on our air shipping network. So, we continue to monitor this. There will be some impact, as pump prices have obviously gone up right now by about 3 rupees.

items.statement: E-commerce industry growth anticipated at 15-20% medium term
items.quote: We anticipate that they should see nothing less than 20% kind of growth rate, 15 to 20% growth rates for the industry as a whole.

items.statement: Net working capital days reduced to 11 days from 38 days three years ago; considered sustainable
items.quote: On the left side, ….[inaudible].. that's come down to 11 days, a very sharp drop in receivables.

items.statement: Working capital improvement driven by billing efficiency, client selection, and more frequent billing cycles
items.quote: What we're doing, of course, is being able to bill extremely fast and extremely accurately, which we're able to do now, b ecause our counter really begins, from the moment that a parcel is delivered

items.statement: Company extremely well capitalized with over Rs 4,500 crore cash on balance sheet
items.quote: The company continues to be extremely well capitalized with over 4,500 crores of cash on the balance sheet.

items.statement: Market structure more settled with three listed players; no space for additional players like Xpressbees
items.quote: I don't think Xpressbees has any structural advantages compared to the three listed players, and I don't see a reason for them to exist.

items.statement: Amazon 3PL opening not a strategic threat; first-party logistics more expensive and prioritizes own orders
items.quote: I think this is just an old product in a new wrapper.

items.statement: Single largest customer below 35% revenue threshold; currently higher than 16% but not concerning
items.quote: I think if any single customer were to cross 35% of revenues, and I don't really have a very scientific basis for that, to be honest, Aditya, but I think, let me put it this way, at the moment, while it's h igher than the 16% that we were at last year, we are absolutely nowhere close to even my made up 35% threshold at this point in

items.statement: Neelam Dhawan appointed Chairperson; Kabir Ahmed Shakir added to Board; Romesh Sobti stepping down after 5 years

I'd also like to welcome Mr. Kabir Ahmed Shakir to the Board of Directors of Delhivery

items.statement: Fuel price volatility may create consumption headwinds but benefits market leader with cost advantages
items.quote: A more volatile, expensive environment is generally better for the market leader and generally better for Delhivery. Because what happens is that our relative cost advantages are larger.

items.statement: Delhivery Direct intracity service live in 6 cities; targeting Rs 200+ crore external GMV run rate
items.quote: This gets us to north of about a 200-crore run rate in terms of on-demand intracity logistics.

items.statement: Management reaffirmed top-line growth guidance of approximately 25% plus for FY27 and on a multiyear basis.

items.statement: Order book stands at approximately INR6,500 crores net of FY26 deliveries, providing 11-12x revenue visibility.

items.statement: Order book split: ~$400M Energy, ~$200M+ Aerospace & Defence, ~$100M+ Oil & Gas.

items.statement: Management expects continued margin upside from operating leverage as new plants ramp up.
items.quote: We always say 33% to 35% plus, and that plus can be anything. So keep expecting some kind of -- definitely a growth is always because we just don't make -- we just don't produce. We do a lot of improvements, continuous improvements on the floor.

items.statement: Global OEMs across aerospace, defense, energy and oil & gas are scaling platforms; supplier base meeting technical thresholds remains small.
items.quote: Overall outlook, looking ahead, the demand backdrop of the product we make remains strong. Global OEMs across aerospace, defense, energy and oil and gas are scaling their platforms and the supplier base capable of meeting the technical threshold we operate at remains small.

items.statement: Awarded single-source 8-year contract by Mitsubishi Heavy Industries for hot section nozzle vane segments.

items.statement: Inaugurated dedicated facility for Baker Hughes in April 2026, marking deepest form of customer integration.
