items.quote: We expect the occupancy level to move up, and we are hopeful that by early next year, we should be hitting the 60% mark.

items.statement: Expect ARPOB to grow around 8% in FY27 through tariff increase and specialty optimization
items.quote: We expect the ARPOB to grow by around 8% through a mix of tariff increase as well as specialty optimization.

items.statement: Targeting to add 150 beds through Jamshedpur hospital commissioned by Q4 FY27
items.quote: So this year, we are targeting to add around 150 beds through our Jamshedpur hospital, which is expected to be commissioned by quarter 4 of FY27.

items.statement: Capex per bed for Jamshedpur hospital around INR 70 lakhs, similar to Raipur
items.quote: The capex per bed for the Jamshedpur hospital would be around INR70 lakhs per bed. That is very similar to the capex we've incurred in Raipur as well.

items.statement: Majority 90% of Jamshedpur capex to be deployed in FY27, rest 10% in FY28 for creditors
items.quote: And we expect the major ity, almost 90%, of the capex requirement to be deployed in this financial year as well. Whatever will be left will be on account of creditors because we commissioned, we are looking at commissioning the hospital in this FY. So whatever will be left for next year will only be on account of creditors to the extent of around 10% of the capex cost.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin excluding Raipur was 23.06%, up 94 bps from 22.1% in FY25
items.quote: Similarly, the EBITDA margin, excluding Raipur is 23.06%, which is a 94 basis point improvement as against our overall EBITDA margin of 22.1% in FY '25.

items.statement: Overall FY26 EBITDA margin including Raipur was 18.84%
items.quote: However, the overall EBITDA margin, including the Raipur Hospital, has come down to 18.84%.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margin to improve by around 100 bps to ~20.2% in FY27
items.quote: The EBITDA for this FY will be growing because as you correctly said, there will be an improved contribution from the other hospitals. So the impact of Jamshedpur shall be nullified, and we expect the EBITDA to move by around 100 basis points.

items.statement: Raipur Hospital FY26 EBITDA loss was INR 13.8 crores; mature hospitals EBITDA was INR 103.9 crores
items.quote: The FY '26 EBITDA from the Raipur Hospital was negative INR13.8 crores, and the EBITDA from mature hospitals is INR103.9 crores, making the overall EBITDA INR90.1 crores.

items.statement: Raipur Hospital Q4 FY26 EBITDA loss was around INR 3 crores
items.quote: We expect the hospital to breakeven around the 25% mark, you're right. And we incurr ed an EBITDA loss of around INR3 crores for the last quarter.

items.statement: Expect Raipur Hospital to breakeven at around 25% occupancy
items.quote: We expect the hospital to breakeven around the 25% mark, you're right.

items.statement: Raipur Hospital ARPOB may reduce 4-5% after insurance empanelment completes
items.quote: With the empanelment complete and the corporates coming onboard, the AR POB might reduce a bit by around 4% or 5%.

items.statement: Expect Agartala ARPOB to increase 7-8% YoY but remain intentionally lower than Kolkata units
items.quote: We expect the ARPOB to increase on a Y -o-Y basis by around 7% to 8%, but that will not mat ch up to the ARPOB of our Kolkata units or other locations. We will keep it at -- intentionally keep it at lower compared to the other hospitals.

items.statement: Jamshedpur 150-bed tertiary care hospital progressing per planned timelines for Q4 FY27 commissioning
items.quote: The upcoming 150-bed tertiary care hospital remains aligned with our strategy of expanding high-quality health care infrastructure across underserved yet high potential markets in Eastern India.

items.statement: No real estate to expand beds in Kolkata hospitals; Agartala can add ~100 beds after reaching 70% occupancy
items.quote: Across the older hospitals, at this point, there is no real estate available to expand beds, especially in the Calcutta hospitals. In Agartala Hospital, once we reach the optimum occupancy of around 70%, we are in a position to add beds. There is vacant land in the complex where we can add beds.

items.statement: Revenue mix: ~90% cash and insurance (50-50 split), ~10% corporate and scheme patients
items.quote: We work more on a cash and insurance business. We have almost 90% of our revenues coming from cash and insurance patients only. Our corporate and scheme patients combined are giving us around 10% revenues, of which Corporate might be around 5% and 5% woul d be scheme patients of Ayushman Bharat, etcetera.

items.statement: Bangladesh patients contributed ~10% of Agartala revenues earlier, now ~3%, expected to recover to 10%
items.quote: The Bangladesh hospital -- Bangladesh would contribute around 10% of our volumes in Agartala earlier. At this point, it is down to around 3%. We expect it to move again towards the 10% mark hopefully soon once the process eases out a little more.

items.statement: Ayushman Bharat replacing Swasthya Sathi in West Bengal not expected to notably impact ARPOB or scheme patient volumes
items.quote: So we do not expect a lot of change with regards to the number of scheme patients we cater to. So therefore, the impact on the ARPOB also should not be anything notable.

items.statement: Insurance empanelment delays (typically 15 months) slowing Raipur ramp-up; expected to complete next quarter
items.quote: The performance could be much better, but there has been a delay in the insurance empanelment's, which was expected. Insurance empanelment's generally take around 15 months for any new hospital. And with insurance becoming such a predominant factor in the running of any hospital, they are critical to the success of the hospital. We expect the empanelment's to be complete in the next quarter, post

items.statement: Bengal elections caused slight impact in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 but not significant
items.quote: slight bit of impact in the last quarter of FY26, but it was nothing very significant. Abhishek Maheshwari: Okay. So no impact during Q1 this year? Management: In Q1 in April, there was an impact. But in last FY, there was very little impact

items.statement: Some nursing attrition risk with new hospitals entering Raipur market, but confident in clinical and paramedical team retention
items.quote: There might be some attrition with regards to the nursing fraternity, which generally happens across the country. But apart from that, we are very confident with our team.

items.statement: Constantly evaluating M&A and greenfield opportunities in Eastern India; targeting 150-200 bed hospitals
items.quote: We are constantly evaluating suitable M&A opportunities in this part of the country. This part of the country being underserved from a corporate health care point of view, M&A opportunities are also -- we have to be very choosy in selecting good real e state assets. So, we are evaluating opportunities. Once the suitable one does come in, we would take it.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of INR13,500 crores with EBITDA margin 7-7.5% and PAT margin 4%
items.quote: maintaining a guidance of INR13,500 crores revenue along with an EBITDA margin of 7% to 7.5% and a PAT margin of 4% for FY27

items.statement: Retail segment FY27 target of INR9,800 crores representing 23% growth over FY26
items.quote: the next year targets and the guidance for the retail, which we have taken under in our AOP, is around INR9,800 crores, which is a 23% increase.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 gross margin declined 230 bps YoY to 9.7% due to higher gold bars/coins mix, lower studded ratio, and promotional discounts
items.quote: Gross margin stood at 9.7%. The moderation in Q4 FY26 was primarily driven by higher share of gold bars and coins, a lower stud jewellery mix in the overall sales mix, and a target customer acquisition discounts in the new markets and a bit of the gains on the unhedged portion which are coming in the sales.

items.statement: Full year FY26 gross margin expanded 280 bps to 12%, EBITDA margin improved 180 bps to 6.6%, PAT margin expanded 100 bps to 3.8%
items.quote: Gross profit grew 83% year-on-year to INR1,302 crores with gross margin expanding by 280 bps to 12% on a yearly level, reflecting structural improvement in the product mix. EBITDA grew 90% year-on-year to INR704 crores with EBITDA margin improving by 180 bps to 6.6%.

items.statement: Gold bars/coins gross margin 0.5-1% vs gold jewellery 12.5-13%, franchise gross margin 2.5-3%
items.quote: So, the we on the gold bar and coins we operate on a very thin margins in the range of half a percent to 1%. And on the normal jewellery on the gold jewellery which is not studded, which is not non-studded jewellery is in the range of 12% to 13%. 12.5% to 13% is the right number to place on the margins for the gold jewellery.

items.statement: Gold bars/coins share rose from 28% in Q4 FY25 to 40% in Q4 FY26 (INR450 cr to INR1,400 cr), full year FY26 at 32%
items.quote: The share of gold bars and coin sales in the overall revenue mix rose 28% in Q4 FY25 to 40% in Q4 FY26. In value terms, it rose from INR450 crores to INR1,400 crores.

items.statement: Gold bars/coins contribution expected to normalize to ~25% in FY27 from 40% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: But I think this year it should again stabilize back to the 25% or even lower levels, and that is what we have been always saying that, you know, this year is going to be a year of a lot of new jewellery being bought using old jewellery and bars and coins as a category this year will see a slowdown.

items.statement: FY26 same-store sales growth 43% driven by wedding/festival demand, improved mix, and new stores
items.quote: reporting a revenue growth of 51% year-on-year to INR8,131 crores, led by healthy same-store sales growth of 43% driven by wedding and festival demand, improved product mix, and contribution from newly added stores.

items.statement: Old gold exchange currently 40% of business, expected to rise to 50%+ in FY27; make-to-order 30-35% of sales
items.quote: So old gold today is around 40% of our entire business, and we expecting that this the old gold trend picks up, we should be at around 50% plus, as far as old jewellery to new jewellery is concerned. Make-to-order again is at around 30%, 35% and I think that should continue at the same level.

items.statement: Total store count reached 78 as of March 31, 2026 (25 added in FY26: 12 in Q4 including 8 COCO and 4 FOCO)
items.quote: During Q4 FY26, we added 12 new stores, 8 COCO, in which 3 legacy and 5 LiteStyle, and 4 FOCO, 1 legacy and 3 LiteStyles, taking our total store count to 78 as of March 31 st, 2026. On a full year basis, we added 25 new stores.

items.statement: Inventory turnover 3.8x for FY26, decline attributed to new stores opened in H2 FY26 not yet matured
items.quote: if you'll see, most of our stores are opened in Q4. We have opened roundabout 8 stores in COCO category for the - in itself Q4 itself. That has what is not matured into the sales right now, and that's why you see an impact on the stock turnover for the year. But having said that, 3.8x in this industry is a healthy stock turn.

items.statement: New stores outside Maharashtra achieving annualized stock turns of 1x in first year vs guidance of 0.8x
items.quote: So these are very healthy for the new stores outside Maharashtra. And this gives us encouragement to also venture into these geographies. Saurabh Gadgil: So, like our guidance we had projected around 0.8x stock turn for the year one, so we have we have surpassed the guidance and all the stores in primary UP, Bihar, and MP are doing annualised stock turns of 1x in the first year itself

items.statement: Gold hedging increased from 57% in Q4 FY25 to 67% in Q4 FY26 (1,300 kg hedged), FY26 average ~60%, target 80% for FY27
items.quote: We at the end of March '26, we are covered for 1,300 kg of gold on the hedging through various GMLs and MCX and other instruments. So this is 67%. When I talk about last year FY25 quarter four, we were at 57%. So there is an improvement of 10% year-on-year on the quarterly basis.

items.statement: Unhedged gold gains: Q4 FY25 INR7.4 cr, Q3 FY26 INR45 cr, Q4 FY26 INR20 cr; monthly sales ~600 kg, inventory ~2,000 kg
items.quote: the gain from unhedged portion of sales in Q4 FY25 was INR7.4 crores, in Q3 FY26 was INR45 crores, and in Q4 FY26 was INR20 crores. So, this was another reason why we have seen the dip in the margins.

items.statement: Import duty hike passed to consumers, not impacting margins; may reduce gold bars/coins demand and boost jewellery via old gold exchange
items.quote: As far as import duty is concerned, it's directly passed on to the consumer. So, it will not have an impact on the margins, but what it may have a positive rub-off is it may induce people to buy less of bars and coins, which are which typically carry lower margins, and may push the interest further to gold jewellery by exchanging old jewellery for new.

items.statement: Advance authorisation for gold import applies only to exporters, not applicable as business is purely domestic
items.quote: See, as far as the advance authorisation is concerned, it is mainly for exporters, people who are importing gold for exporting jewellery. We don't fall in that category, so it's not applicable to us. Our business is purely domestic.

items.statement: Long-term credit rating upgraded to A+ stable from A, short-term reaffirmed at A1; reflects stronger business profile and disciplined capital management
items.quote: We are also pleased to share that during the quarter, our long-term credit rating was upgraded to A+ stable from A, while the short-term rating was reaffirmed at A1. The rating upgrade reflects the continued strengthening of the company's business profile, healthy financial position, and disciplined approach towards capital and debt management.

items.statement: QIP enabling resolution valid till August 2026; not currently pursuing as business is self-sufficient; promoter shareholding compliance deadline September 2027
items.quote: See, I mean, in terms of progress, like I said, there is an enabling board resolution which is till end of August. So that is where we are. We haven't really thought on, you know, going ahead on that front at this point of time. We've got we had a good year, so as we move ahead now, there's something which we would want to explore, but it's not a QIP is not an impediment for us to grow our busines

items.statement: A&P spend guidance maintained at 1.5% of revenue (ATL+BTL), may go lower in FY27 due to import duty driving old gold exchange
items.quote: Guiding on the on the A&P spend, both ATL and BTL, 1.5 is what we would stick to or in fact we would try to go a little lower, considering the year wherein we are seeing the import duty, where the focus will move more towards exchanging old gold for new gold.

items.statement: FY26 operational metrics: ATV >INR1 lakh, revenue per store INR137.7 cr, revenue per sq ft INR4.51 lakh, net profit per store INR5.25 cr
items.quote: Our average transaction value, ATV, for FY26 stood at over INR1 lakh, reflecting both premiumization in our basket and the rising aspirational quotient of our customer base. Our key P N Gadgil Jewellers Limited May 15th, 2026 operational metrics include average revenue per store of INR137.7 crores, revenue per square feet of INR4,51,000, net profit per store of INR5.25 crores, and an inventory tur

items.statement: FY27 guidance may be updated next quarter depending on market evolution post import duty hike; volume outlook uncertain due to recent policy changes
items.quote: While it is still early to fully assess the overall impact of the evolving situation and we continue to calibrate our strategy accordingly, we are currently P N Gadgil Jewellers Limited May 15th, 2026 maintaining a guidance of INR13,500 crores revenue along with an EBITDA margin of 7% to 7.5% and a PAT margin of 4% for FY27. However, depending on how the market situation evolves during the ongoing

items.statement: FY26 consolidated revenue INR10,739 cr (+40% YoY), crossed INR10,000 cr milestone; Q4 FY26 revenue INR3,544 cr (+123% YoY)
items.quote: FY26 has been truly a defining year for PNG, a year in which we crossed several meaningful milestones, expanding into new geographies and reinforced the depth of our 194-year-old legacy. Most importantly, FY26 marks the year in which we crossed INR10,000 crores of revenue, a milestone for the first time, reporting a full year consolidated revenue of INR10,739 crores, a growth of 40% year-over-year

items.statement: Management targets debtor days below 120 in FY27 and expects EBITDA margins to recover toward 7%+ from current 4.6-4.7%
items.quote: We are targeting to bring our debtor days to below 120 in this current financial year.

items.statement: Capex of INR 100 crores planned for FY27, calibrated to market conditions and EXIM normalization pace
items.quote: Seeing better opportunities, our intention is a further capex of INR100 crores in this FY27, which remains linked to strong customer demand and will be calibrated to market conditions as year goes on, including the pace of EXIM normalization.

items.statement: EXIM container volumes dropped 10.96% QoQ in Q4 FY26 due to Middle East crisis, but full-year FY26 EXIM volumes grew 5% YoY
items.quote: the 34,404 EXIM numbers are compared to the 38,638 containers in Q3 of this year, which shows a reduction of 4,234 containers, an absolute reduction of 10.96%.

items.statement: Domestic container volumes held steady QoQ in Q4 FY26 with less than 1% decline despite tiles/steel weakness, pivoting to chemicals and FMCG
items.quote: our numbers are 23,350 compared to 23,565 an absolute decrease of just 215 containers, which is less than 1%.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 total container volumes grew 6.14% YoY to 2,26,578 containers
items.quote: In overall numbers, 2,26,578 boxes compared to 2,13,475 the year before, an absolute increase of 13,103 containers and a percentage increase of 6.14%.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin declined to 5% from 5.6% in Q3 FY26; PAT margin fell to 1.7% from 2.3%
items.quote: EBITDA margins showed a slight decline from 5.6% to 5%. Similarly, the PAT decreased slightly from INR10.8 crores in Q3 to INR8.3 crores in Q4 and the margin decline was minimal from 2.3% to 1.7%.

items.statement: Management expects sequential EBITDA margin improvement from current 4.6-4.7% back toward 7%+ levels as geopolitical disruptions ease
items.quote: The EBITDA margins which are 4.6%, 4.7%, we hope to bring it back to where we were starting FY25 which is around almost 7% and even higher the year earlier.

items.statement: Strong order book with pedigreed customers for rest of the year; EXIM pipeline especially on East Coast is very robust
items.quote: Your company has a very strong order book with pedigreed customers for the rest of the year giving us additional confidence.

items.statement: FY26 capex deployed over INR 70 crores including 161 specialized containers, reach stackers, commercial vehicles; FY27 capex planned INR 100 crores for similar specialized assets
items.quote: Total capex deployed in FY26 was over INR70 crores, including in specialized TEUs, handling equipment such as reach stackers, commercial vehicles, all completely aligned to our customers' requirements and operating needs.

items.statement: Own fleet of specialized containers now exceeds 1,000 units, one of the largest private sector fleets in India
items.quote: Our own fleet of specialized containers now stands at over 1,000, making it one of the largest specialized container fleets in the country in the private sector.

items.statement: Devaliya MMCT fully operational on 32 acres serving Morbi tiles/chemicals cluster; fixed services to North, South, East India running at lower frequencies
items.quote: So, we are fully operational now, sir and the Devaliya MMCT is right outside Morbi, sir. We are smack in the middle of the tiles industry and the tiles industry is a natural customer for us.

items.statement: War risk surcharges and insurance premiums up USD 1,200/20ft and USD 2,400/40ft; ocean freight costs nearly doubled on some routes
items.quote: The war has resulted in insurance premium going up by USD1,200 for 20 feet and 2400 USD for 40 feet in some cases. Add to that the shipping lines imposing war risk surcharges and cargo, which in many cases are nearly doubling the ocean freight costs.

items.statement: Operating cash flow negative in FY25 and FY26 due to rising working capital needs; improvement expected as EXIM realizations recover
items.quote: The cash flow remains negative, like I said, due to the increasing working capital requirements, but we expect it to improve as realization increases, especially on our EXIM side.

items.statement: Debt increased from INR 172 crores to INR 217 crores YoY due to working capital requirements for new MMCT operations; INR 92 crores of IPO funds remain for capex deployment
items.quote: The working capital requirements has been constantly going up as we've operationalized our new multimodal cargo terminal and so whatever working capital requirements we've taken has gone into our working capital requirement, sir.

items.statement: Industry EXIM volumes shrank ~40% in March 2026; Western Carriers EXIM volumes dropped only 11% showing resilience
items.quote: The import-export EXIM volumes for the logistics industry are said to have shrunk by about 40% in the month of March, with reductions in heavy fluctuations in both export and import volumes. Luckily for our company, we have been very resilient in this regard, with our EXIM container movement dropping less than 11% compared to the 40% overall.

items.statement: Rake stabling increased 10x to 50+ rakes in March vs normal 4-5; empty wagon running up 4x to 15-20% from normal 5%
items.quote: the requirements for stabling of rakes idling for want of cargo in the month of March has already crossed 50 rakes, 50 trains, which is a dramatic increase from an industry standard of four to five rakes that are stabled on a normal situation to deal with cargo fluctuations. So that's a 10x.

items.statement: Government launched INR 1.5B Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool; Customs permitted export returns; JNPT waived 100% ground rent and 80% reefer plug-in costs
items.quote: GOI has launched 1.5 billion Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool to shield shipping from global risks. BMIP will provide coverage across key segments of maritime risks including hull and machinery, cargo, protection and indemnity (P&I) and war-related risk for Indian flag vessels and those with India linkages.

items.statement: Western Dedicated Freight Corridor completed and commissioned on 31 March 2026 including final 102 km JNPT to New Rewari stretch
items.quote: On 31st March 26, DFCCIL announced the completion and commissioning of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor, including the final 102 kilometers which were pending from JNPT to New Raphale stretch.

items.statement: Middle East crisis blocking Strait of Hormuz since 28 Feb 2026; 40,000-45,000 Indian containers stranded; capacity on US/Europe routes at 30-35% of normal
items.quote: Due to all of this, the capacity currently on key routes to US and Europe is about 30% to 35% of normal levels, putting extreme pressure on the EXIM trade.

items.statement: Tiles industry in Morbi facing propane/natural gas shortage impacting 700 units; 70% of ceramics units run on propane
items.quote: 700 units are facing propane and natural gas supply shortages. As most of you know, almost 70% of Morbi's ceramics units run on propane.

items.statement: Pivoted from corporate to retail customers growing 25-30% YoY; new retail business at MMCT driving receivables increase
items.quote: since we've grown our retail side of the business from corporate in the last 2 years almost I would say 25% to 30% year-on-year, Western Carriers ( that's where the funds have gotten stuck up

items.statement: Domestic volumes steady via pivot to industrial chemicals, FMCG, aggregates, salt as tiles/steel weakened; specialized containers for niche cargo
items.quote: by pivoting to other industries like industrial chemicals, FMCG, aggregates, etcetera your company has managed to keep its domestic volume steady with a minimal decline of less than 1% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: India merchandise exports fell 7.4% YoY in March; West Asia shipments down 58%; US/Europe routes account for 195B of 437B projected exports
items.quote: India's merchandise exports have fallen 7.4% year-on-year in March to 38.92 billion, with shipments to West Asian region particularly down 58%, both largely driven by the Middle East crisis.

items.statement: Revenue from operations INR 496 crores in Q4 FY26, up 4% QoQ; fourth straight quarter of revenue growth
items.quote: Revenues from operations was INR496 crores, climbing steadily further up by about 4% from INR478 crores in Q3, recording a fourth straight growth quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth expected above 20% with gradual EBITDA margin improvement
items.quote: Looking ahead to FY27, we remain optimistic about the demand environment across key industry user base. We expect revenue to grow by more than 20%, supported by capacity additions and strong order inflows, and increased contribution from high-margin engineered products.

items.statement: Long-term target of INR650 crore+ revenue with 15-16% EBITDA margins in 2-3 years
items.quote: Our long-term inspiration remains to build a INR650 crores plus revenue platform with sustainable EBITDA margins in the range of 15% to 16%.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to improve by 80-100 bps in FY27 despite raw material volatility
items.quote: For this financial, we expect our EBITD A margins to go up by around 80, 100 basis points considering the increase in our operation size and considering the consolidation of our cost for a higher revenue

items.statement: Order book at INR200 crore as of 30 April 2026, 80-90% executable in FY27
items.quote: Our order book remains healthy at approximately INR200 crores as of 30th April 2026, providing strong visibility for the coming quarters.

items.statement: Order book doubled from INR100 crore to INR200 crore year-on-year
items.quote: If you compare our order book of what it was on 31st March 2025, it was INR100 crores and now we have an order book of INR200 crores.

items.statement: INR100 crore IPO-funded capex (INR70 crore for Unit 4, INR30 crore for B33 facility)
items.quote: So, total capex of the IPO we had mentioned our objects was close to INR100 crores, INR70 crores going in the facility where we have our wear part, wear plate and heavy engineering capabilities and INR30 crores in our facility where the B33 facility where we have the sli tting line and electrode manufacturing

items.statement: Unit 4 heavy engineering facility (170-180k sq ft) commissioning by end of Q1 FY27
items.quote: In addition to our new wear plate manufacturing and heavy engineering facility is progressing well and as planned and is expected to be commissioned by the end of Q1 2027.

items.statement: New 10 TPD electrode plant, 25% wear plate capacity expansion, and in-house strip-slitting line commissioned in FY26
items.quote: We successfully commissioned a new 10 -ton-per-day electrode plant, expanded wear plate capacity by approximately 25%, and installed an in -house strip-slitting line for manufacturing flux-cored wires.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization at 85-90% for wear plates, heavy engineering, and wires; will drop to 50-60% after new capacity comes online
items.quote: For wear plates, heavy engineering, we are -- as we speak, close to 85%-90% utilization. So, of course, as soon as these new shop floors get ready and available for manufacturing, these capacities will -- utilization will drop to around 50% to 60%.

items.statement: Consolidated FY26 EBITDA margin at 14.05%, standalone at 13.25%
items.quote: EBITDA margin, excluding other income, for FY26 stood at 14.05%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin volatility (13-14%) due to raw material price pass-through lag on fixed-price contracts
items.quote: Because of that reason, the EBITDA margin fluctuates between 13% to 14%.

items.statement: Price hikes ongoing as raw material costs rise; some volatile items (cobalt, nickel, tungsten) have very short quote validity
items.quote: Yes, yes. Price hike is an ongoing activity depending upon raw material prices. The customers in the industry are also aware with the raw material situation. So, as and when our input cost increases, we are doing upward revision of prices.

items.statement: Healthy demand from cement, steel, power, mining, engineering; no project delays despite West Asia crisis
items.quote: We don't see any slowdown happening as of now. So, none of the projects have gone under hold. There are major coal -based power plants coming up in India. So, we've got orders coming in from there.

items.statement: Revenue mix roughly 30% welding consumables, 30% wear plates/parts, 30% heavy engineering, 10% services; heavy engineering and wear plates to grow faster
items.quote: We have always indicated that it's roughly 30 % products, 30% wear plates and wear parts and 30% heavy engineering and 10% of services. So, this is how the breakup is.

items.statement: Over 80% revenue from repeat customers; heavy engineering orders from L&T Power, private steel, cement players
items.quote: We continue to derive over 80% of our revenues from repeat customers, which reflects the trust placed in our product quality, engineering capabilities, and long-standing customer relationships.

items.statement: Exports to 35+ countries; targeting 15% international revenue share in FY27, growing faster than 20% YoY
items.quote: So, right now, we think as the revenues and as we are growing at 20 % plus year on year, we expect the international revenue to go up to 15% in the next, in this year and the next year.

items.statement: FY26 debtor days 98 (target 80-90), inventory days 66 (target 60-65); heavy engineering items 60-90 days, welding consumables cash-and-carry
items.quote: And we are hopeful that we will be able to bring it down to around anywhere between 80 to 90 days which was at the same levels of FY25.

items.statement: Strong liquidity position maintained; no specific debt numbers disclosed
items.quote: The company c ontinues to maintain a strong liquidity position, which provides us with the flexibility to future growth opportunities confidently

items.statement: Investment in Tejorup Sunmay Systems for VSHORADS defense systems; prototype stage, PSO for 200 launchers and 1,200 rockets
items.quote: Tejorup has a project sanction order from DRDO where post-prototype development, there is already a mention of a requirement of 200 launchers and 1,200 rockets.

items.statement: UAE subsidiary operational for service/overlay work; revenue contribution expected from FY27
items.quote: So the UAE facility has been handed over to us. And we've already sort of set it up for doing service and service repairs and overlay work in UAE and the region, not just UAE. So that is up and running now.

items.statement: Railway developmental orders execution in 6-9 months; substantial revenue from FY28
items.quote: we expect the execution to take anywhere between six to nine months. And post they are delivered, then we will become or we will come in the approved vendor list for those particular components. And by the end of the year, we can start seeing some substantial orders coming in for from these initiatives

items.statement: Welding consumables: <3% conventional, >97% special hard-facing/repair electrodes
items.quote: So, Diffusion is identified with special electrodes, which are used in maintenance and repair and hard facing. Very small portion of our business is conventional. I would imagine less than 3% -- 2%-3% is conventional business.

items.statement: Raw material volatility (tungsten, nickel, cobalt, molybdenum, chromium) impacts margins with pass-through lag

items.quote: You can see in our balance sheet also the consolidated results, you have got INR139 crores of exchange difference.

items.quote: The international, as we have said, on a yearly basis, the revenues jumped up from INR668 crores to INR1,133 crores. And the EBITDA went from INR88 crores to INR152 crores.

items.statement: Geopolitical issues causing demand postponement in Europe and MENA regions; time frame is the only challenge

items.statement: Sulfur price rising dramatically due to Indonesian nickel smelter demand and Middle East crisis disrupting Gulf of Hormuz supply routes
items.quote: In fact, about 50% of global sulfur trade is through Hormuz. So that has affected availability and therefore the price of the product not only in India but also in other parts of the world including China.

items.statement: Boron ore supply disruption from Turkey in H1 FY26 caused production loss; resolved in H2 with adequate stock now

items.statement: Non-boric acid products (ceramics, glass) face demand reduction due to natural gas crisis in consuming centers like Morbi

items.statement: All raw material price increases passed to customers; absolute margin maintained despite percentage margin compression
items.quote: we did manage to pass on all the price increase to our customers. Mathematically, it looks in percentage terms as if the margin has come down. But in absolute terms, even in a quite turbulent and difficult supply chain situation, we were ab le to maintain the absolute margin

items.statement: Dahej and Roha sulfuric acid plants each ~350 tons per day capacity; both similar in size

items.statement: Land monetization proceeds could be used for capex or debt reduction

items.quote: So, we are working on a couple of specialties in the boron business. And we are working on one particular product which is used in making a polymer which goes int o enhanced oil recovery and some other applications like that. So currently we have started some commercial

items.statement: Forex mark-to-market loss in Q4 due to dollar at all-time high on March 31; notional entry to reverse if rupee doesn't depreciate further
