items.statement: Targets FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin around 22-23%
items.quote: Yeah, that's the target. But as I said, let's wait for a quarter or so, and then we can be confident of giving the guidance on the numbers.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin improved 200 bps to 19.3%; CDMO Q4 margin 18.7% vs 23.9% YoY; Marketable molecules margin up 940 bps to 18.8% for FY26
items.quote: All of this resulting into an EBITDA of INR 565 crores, equating to 19.3% for the full FY26 as compared to 17.3% in the previous financial year. So, we have been able to increase our EBITDA margins by 200 bps in the current financial year that concluded.

items.statement: ADC linker-payload project has purchase orders for next years; co-investment phase 1 complete, phase 2 in progress
items.quote: Yeah, so starting with the first part, yeah, so the molecule has been performing quite well. And it has been getting more and more approvals as well. And we supply the linker as well as the payload. So yeah, I mean, we have the purchase orders in hand for the next years.

items.statement: Tech transfer of CHF 20-25 million annual revenue product from Switzerland to India agreed by big pharma customer; another CHF 20-25 million opportunity from innovator inspection
items.quote: Basically, for this molecule that I mentioned about, for the tech transfer, the annual revenue that we currently do is close to about CHF 20-25 million per annum. For the other project, if everything goes well, it could be at least another CHF 20-25 million of opportunity for the India business.

items.statement: FY26 CapEx CHF 22.4 million; no major CapEx planned except maintenance and digital transformation; Japanese partner funds 100% of co-investment CapEx
items.quote: Regarding the CapEx that was done for the full financial year, that stood at roughly about CHF 22.4 million.

items.statement: French facility revenue EUR 8M with EBITDA loss EUR 9M in FY26; targets EUR 11-12M revenue and EUR 6M loss in FY27; aims breakeven in FY28
items.quote: Yeah, so the French facility did a revenue of close to about EUR 8 million. And we had a loss of close to about EUR 9 million for that particular entity. What we expect is that in the current year, it should get up to close to about EUR 11-12 million of revenue. And the losses should come down to close to about EUR 6 million.

items.statement: Net debt (ex-leases) CHF 146.8M vs CHF 157.6M YoY, down CHF 11M; India debt ~INR 800 cr at 10.5-11% to be refinanced via promoter ECB at ~4% for 10 years unsecured
items.quote: Our net debt, excluding the lease liabilities for the year ending March 31, 2026, stood at about CHF 146.8 million as compared to CHF 157.6 million at the end of the last financial year, representing a decrease of close to about CHF 11 million.

items.statement: Targets net debt reduction of CHF 10-15M (~INR 150 cr) annually; could be higher from cash flow after CapEx and working capital
items.quote: So, that would be at least to the tune of about CHF 10-15 million. So, roughly about INR 150-odd crores every year is what the target is.

items.statement: Optimized supplier base for wool grease in Specialties; negotiated new contracts, added suppliers, got better prices, improved cost base
items.quote: We have optimized our supplier base, specifically on wool grease. We have negotiated new contracts. We have more suppliers on board. We got better prices. So, the cost base has been improved as well.

items.statement: ADC contributes ~25% of CDMO revenue in FY26; share expected to increase with Celonic partnership for MAb conjugation and drug product formulation
items.quote: So FY26, that would be close to about all molecules put together on the ADC side would be close to about 25%.

items.statement: Sprint initiative attracting early-phase projects from big pharma, mid and small pharma; multiple late-phase projects ready for FDA inspection; Celonic collaboration enables combined linker-payload, conjugation, drug product offering
items.quote: We have some multiple late-phase projects where we're also ready for FDA inspection. We're just waiting for FDA popping up, so which is always a good sign. And the collaboration with Celonic is a milestone because there, we have the possibility to have a combined offering, starting from the linker-payload synthesis to the conjugation with the Celonic antibody, and then also do the drug product for

items.statement: Onerous contract provisions increased other expenses by ~INR 50 cr in Q4 FY26 vs reversal in Q4 FY25; continuously assess actual vs budgeted hours
items.quote: The other expenses stood at about INR 147 crores as compared to INR 92 crores in the comparable quarter of the last financial year. This deviation of about INR 50-odd crores is largely represented because of certain additional provision that we had to make in the quarter ending March 31, 2026, on account of the onerous contracts.

items.statement: Board approved promoter entity ECB to parent: 10-year unsecured loan at ~4% to refinance INR 800 cr India debt at 10.5-11%; also for working capital and CapEx; interest capitalized first 2 years, bullet repayment
items.quote: Apart from this, I would like to highlight one of the points that was also approved as part of the Board meeting yesterday, obviously subject to the necessary regulatory and the shareholders' approval, which was in regards to one of the promoter entities providing a long-term external commercial borrowing to the parent entity, with the objectives that we are able to pay off the high-cost debt in I

items.statement: Interest cost to reduce to INR 30-35 cr/quarter from Q2/Q3 FY27 post refinancing; FY28 net interest cost not more than INR 100 cr consolidated; FY27 could be ~INR 70 cr
items.quote: Yeah. It could go even lower than that. But, yeah, on a conservative basis, INR 30-35 crores should definitely be doable.

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected ~40% in FY27, ~30% in FY28, approaching 15-20% in 3 years as loss-making entities turn profitable and utilize accumulated losses
items.quote: I would say, it would gradually keep on coming down. So, for FY27, it could be close to about 40% for the full financial year. The year after, it could be close to about 30%. Because if you see right now, the most profit-generating units that we have, majorly the Swiss entity as well as the Dutch entity.

items.statement: Revenue mix target 85% CDMO / 15% Marketable Molecules (Vitamin D analogs, cholesterol) in next 2-3 years
items.quote: Yeah. So, the CDMO business will keep on growing. And as far as the mix is concerned, I would say it would be somewhere like 85-15. So, 85% being the CDMO part of the business and 15% being the marketable molecules.

items.statement: Increased sales force at both Carbogen (Europe) and Dishman Carbogen (India) sites to attract more products and customers
items.quote: Specifically on the sales activities, we have increased our sales force. We have increased on both sites, on the Carbogen site, but also on the Dishman Carbogen site in India. We have increased the number of salespeople, which is the condition to attract more products and more customers to feed our pipeline.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainties noted; cautious on near-term guidance but confident on 3-year growth path
items.quote: The overall growth looks quite promising. And yes, I mean, right now, because of the geopolitical situation, there are certain uncertainties as well. We do see that, overall, from a business perspective, things should look up, but we are continuously assessing the market situation as well. Hence, we would remain cautious as far as the guidance for the year is concerned.

items.statement: Strong Vitamin D analog demand drove Marketable Molecules growth; ADC and linker-payload demand high; late-phase project inquiries increasing
items.quote: There we see a strong Vitamin D and analog sales. These are the products with high margins. The demand has increased, which had a big impact on the strong numbers there.

items.statement: Combined drug substance-drug product offering and Celonic partnership for ADC conjugation seen as competitive differentiator attracting market interest
items.quote: We have started now to offer this entire package to the market, so that the customer can come in the drug substance side and take the materials through the drug product. So, he has only one supplier to deal with, which is Carbogen Amcis.

items.statement: French facility received ANSM approval; aggressively bidding for Phase 3 and commercial projects
items.quote: We already received the ANSM approval, that is where we are trying to get more and more projects for Phase 3. We are also aiming for projects for commercial supplies as well.

items.statement: 90% of India revenue in foreign currency; Swiss franc debt acts as natural hedge against CHF/EUR/USD/GBP revenues; CHF depreciation vs INR boosts INR-reported EBITDA
items.quote: No, because if you see from India, 90% of our revenue also comes in foreign currency. We have equivalent amount of foreign currency that would be coming in, which kind of negates any adverse foreign exchange fluctuation risk.

items.statement: Celonic partnership for MAb supply enables combined ADC offering from linker-payload synthesis through conjugation to drug product formulation
items.quote: And the collaboration with Celonic is a milestone because there, we have the possibility to have a combined offering, starting from the linker-payload synthesis to the conjugation with the Celonic antibody, and then also do the drug product formulation in Saint Beauzire.

items.statement: Goodwill increased from INR 4,053 cr to INR 4,798 cr due to foreign exchange restatement; no additions; ~INR 550 cr from 2017 India merger, rest consolidation goodwill from Swiss/Netherlands subsidiaries
items.quote: This increase is largely on account of the foreign exchange fluctuation that we have seen in the last one year. These assets get restated at the closing exchange rate. But, otherwise, there is no additions, so to say, as far as the goodwill is concerned.

items.statement: FY26 order inflow was INR4,446 crores, exceeding full-year guidance of INR3,500 crores
items.quote: Order inflow during FY '26 stood at INR4,446 crores, exceeding our full year guidance inflow of INR3,500 crores.

items.statement: FY27 order inflow guidance is INR4,500-5,000 crores
items.quote: I'll give you a range of INR4,500 crores to INR5,000 crores, and we are well on track to achieve that.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance is 20% year-on-year
items.quote: Over the next 2 years, we are seeing that -- we are giving a guidance of 20% revenue growth year-on-year.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance is 15.5%-16.5% if geopolitical issues persist, 16.5%-17.5% if they cease
items.quote: Considering the current situation, the EBITDA guidance for the full financial year '26, '27 will be in the range of 15.5% to 16.5%. However, if the global uncertainties cease over the next few weeks, a couple of months, the guidance will be restored to 16.5% to 17.5%.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin was 16.3%, within guided range
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the full year FY '26 stood at 16.3%, around our guided range.

items.statement: Working capital days reduced by 43 days in FY26 due to improved debtor collection
items.quote: The year saw a significa nt reduction in working capital days by 43 days on back of improved debtor collection

items.statement: Net cash from operating activities increased to INR224 crores in FY26 from INR52 crores in FY25
items.quote: Net cash from operating activities stood at INR224 crores in FY '26 as compared to INR52 crores in FY '25.

items.statement: Bank rating upgraded to BBB+; net debt to equity at 0.10x; net debt less than INR170 crores as of call date
items.quote: The company's bank rating has been upgraded to BBB+, signifying overall improving credit profile. The assessed working capital limits, fund-based and non-fund-based, stand fully tied up, providing clear headroom to boost execution in the coming year.

items.statement: FY27 capex target is INR165 crores, mainly for aluminum formwork and jump-form
items.quote: For the current financial year, our target towards capex, mainly coming from aluminum formwork, jump-form will be close to about INR165 crores.

items.statement: Commodity prices rose ~18% for electrical and aluminum items Feb-Apr 2026; escalation indices up only 2% in Feb-Mar, 8% in April
items.quote: The company has witnessed nearly 18% rise in the prices of electrical items, aluminum product items over the last 3 months, starting February 26 to April 26. While electrical commodities are lower as a total input cost and while they are covered under escalation, the upward movement in escalation was only 2% in February and March '26.

items.statement: Provision of INR10 crores made in FY26 for procurement cost increases; may reverse if escalation matches price rise over next 2 quarters
items.quote: the company, as a prudent measure, has factored INR10 crores in procurement cost in FY26. If the escalation receivable from the cli ent matches this increase overall over the next 2 quarters, the provisions so made will be reversed

items.statement: Standalone order book INR13,498 crores as of 31 Mar 2026; 57% public, 43% private
items.quote: Order book on standalone basis stood at INR13,498 crores as on 31st March '26. Public sector accounts for 57%, while private sector accounts for 43% of the total order book.

items.statement: FY26 capex additions: INR67.81 crores in Q4, INR147.33 crores full year
items.quote: Last year, the addition was INR67.81 crores in quarter 4, right? And the additions for the full year was INR147.33 crores.

items.statement: Finance cost expected to reduce by INR6-8 crores in FY27; interest rate down from 12.65% to 9.65% over 15 months; BG commissions nearly halved
items.quote: Going forward, if the RBI main tains their margin rates, we further see a reduction in that. The commissions on bank guarantees have nearly halved. So the current year, you will see an absolute drop in , on an absolute level, a drop in the overall finance cost, including the advances on which interest is payable, all right? So yes, you can take it from us that on an absolute basis, the company wil

items.statement: Target net working capital days of 56-60 days over next 8 quarters (excl. retention down 50+ days, incl. retention down 42-43 days)
items.quote: Over the next 8 quarters, you will see we achieving that what we were talking about net working capital of 56 to 60 days. Now what will this do? Obviously, this will reduce the debt as well, considering that we maintain our creditor levels and reduce our debtor levels, okay?

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty and commodity price volatility may impact margins; labor shortage of ~3,000 workers across 30 sites; execution impacted by elections and environmental stoppages
items.quote: the current geopolitical conditions, what are surrounding all of us, do not allow me to gi ve you an upward number. On a Lower base say if we were at INR1,200 crores, giving 30% was logical. At INR2,700 crores, giving 30% in such situations, which have been declared as emergency by the Central Government of India, I don't think it would be appropriate

items.statement: Labor requirement ~14,000+; currently at ~11,000 (down to 9,000 in Mar-Apr); expect to reach optimum by May end
items.quote: So the per day is never a count. It is always at the requirement at project site. So the average requirement should be 14,000 -plus. Maybe we are at 11,000 -odd. This had depleted to nearly 9,000 in the March and some part of April. We have seen reinforc ements coming back after the elections, and we hope to be at the optimum by the end of this month

items.statement: NCR/Haryana/Gurgaon/Noida private order backlog INR1,500 crores; public sector INR800 crores (NBCC)
items.quote: So, Haryana -- the total NCR, Haryana, Gurgaon, Noida, UP put together, in private sector, we have close to INR1,000 crores -- sorry, INR1,500 crores order backlog. And in public sector, we have close to INR800 crores, NBCC.

items.statement: FY27 order inflow phasing: Q1 >INR1,000 crores, Q2 similar, Q3+Q4 INR2,500-3,000 crores
items.quote: So we do expect in the quarter 1 orders closed in excess of about INR1,000 crores. Quarter 2 will be a similar number. Quarter 3 and quarter 4 will be about INR3,000 crores, so between INR2,500 crores to INR3,000 crores, thereby -- which we will be achieving the full year guidance of about INR4,500 crores to INR5,000 crores.

items.statement: Net turnover ratio of core assets 5.2x in FY26, same as FY25
items.quote: Net turnover ratio of core assets stood at 5.2x for FY '26, in line with 5.2x for FY '25.

items.statement: Other income reduction due to one-time write-backs in FY25; FY27 other income expected ~INR3-4 crores per quarter (+/-10%)
items.quote: So, it was some write -backs which we received as one -off, which was recorded in the last financial year. Generally, the other income includes interest income, all right . So last year, the interest income and this year, the interest income -- this year, o n the contrary, the interest income has increased a little bit. However, the other income has not been there because it was a onetime, as we e

items.statement: Bidding for data center projects; management declined to discuss margin differential vs residential/commercial on call
items.quote: Sir, you are taking away my competitive advantage by asking this. You can ask me this offline. I can explain. But let us not discuss the pricing of tenders on the con call

items.statement: Escalation clauses vary by contract; aluminum formwork falls under WPI all commodities; electrical items under specific electrical index or WPI all commodities
items.quote: No, every contract is unique. There are escalation clauses. Wherever the escalation clauses are there, a certain portion is towards the labor that is 30%. A certain portion is there towards reinforcement steel. A certain portion is for cement. A certain portion is for POL that is oil component. And the remainder -- or the other thing is WPI all commodities, all right? So, aluminum would generally

items.statement: Targets INR500 crore revenue in 4-5 years requiring slightly over 30% CAGR; SaaS ARR growth target ~35%
items.quote: This is something we mentioned in the previous financial year, and we stick to this number. This is our aspiration, and we are setting the conditions for reaching this target. At this point, we believe this will require a growth rate of slightly over 30%over the next 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: Targets ~35% ARR growth for SaaS business; SupTech to grow at lower rate but with potential surprises
items.quote: For our SaaS business, we are targeting an ARR growth rate of approximately 35% and we expect the SupTech business with a combination of one-time revenues plus recurring revenues to move a at a lower rate, but there could be surprises as we go forward.

items.statement: IRIS CARBON ARR grew 33% in FY26 on disclosure management wins; opened ESG reporting module account
items.quote: For the previous year, IRIS CARBON ARR, the annual recurring revenue grew at 33% on the back of several wins in the disclosure management space. We also opened our account in the ESG reporting solution area, which is an additional module on IRIS CARBON.

items.statement: IRIS iDEAL ARR grew 17% in FY26 despite H1 delays in Indian BFSI purchase decisions
items.quote: On our BFSI automated regulatory reporting solution, IRIS iDEAL, the ARR grew at 17% despite the fact that we faced some delay, especially in the first half of the previous financial year in purchase decision-making at customer end, especially in Indian market.

items.statement: Added 3 new SupTech logos in FY26 including Government of Qatar for tax reporting; expanding into deposit insurance management
items.quote: We added 3 new logos in FY26, which included the government of Qatar for tax reporting. This industry is a new area and combined with our deposit insurance management segment this opens new markets for our iFile SupTech reporting platform with new regulators.

items.statement: FY26 total revenue grew ~23%; EBITDA margin ~14%; balancing SaaS acquisition costs with SupTech profits
items.quote: Coming to our financial performance, our growth has been steady for the full year with total revenues growing at about 23%, while the EBITDA margin came in at about 14%. We have mentioned before, our endeavor is to partially balance customer acquisition expenses in the SaaS business with profits emanating from the SupTech business so that EBITDA numbers are not severely impacted.

items.statement: Plans measured, well-thought-out spending increases in sales, marketing and product enhancements for RegTech growth
items.quote: And we have articulated before, we plan to spend in a measured and well-thought-out manner as we increase investments in key areas such as sales and marketing, along, of course, with product enhancements.

items.statement: Expanding SupTech iFile platform beyond data collection into risk-based supervision, licensing, decision management modules
items.quote: We are also expanding this product suite to offer more end-to-end features for the regulatory customers, which include risk-based supervision, licensing and decision management and a few other modules as well.

items.statement: Embedding AI technologies in product stack and software development process; investor presentation includes AI product initiative slides
items.quote: We see it as being critical for us to embed AI technologies in both our product stack and in the software development process itself, and we are doing that assiduously with speed and focus. Our investor presentation also includes a couple of slides, which talks about our product initiatives on the AI side.

items.statement: Broke into large enterprise accounts for IRIS CARBON, gaining confidence to compete with market leaders
items.quote: We have also been able to break into large enterprise accounts, and which gives us a lot of confidence in competing with the best in the market.

items.statement: SaaS business predominantly Europe and US focused with smaller India presence; SupTech pipeline linked to Middle East regulators
items.quote: the SaaS business part, which is enterprise-oriented business, we don't see much of an impact, because our SaaS business is predominantly Europe and U.S. focused and to some smaller extent, India as well. So, we don't see much of an impact. On the SupTech side, to some extent our pipeline is linked to the Middle East with ongoing discussions with Middle East regulators as well

items.statement: Regulators cautious on AI/cloud adoption for confidential data; exploring small/sovereign LLMs and private cloud structures
items.quote: I think you are absolutely right. We have been speaking to regulators. In fact, we have actually one regulator already on the cloud, which is PFRDA in India. That's the private cloud which we are using. But when you talk about AI services and cloud-based architecture, there is reluctance on part of the regulators to embrace that completely.

items.statement: Receivables trending down due to enterprise mix shift and prompt regulator payments; comfortable at 75-80 days
items.quote: I would say that 75 to 80 days is what we would be comfortable. But if the enterprise SaaS revenues really gallop going forward, it could further improve, but we need to wait for that.

items.statement: Post TaxTech divestment, cash ~INR155 crore and net worth ~INR200 crore as of March 31; book value ~INR98 from INR37
items.quote: Post the TaxTech divestment, our balance sheet has strengthened considerably and cash right now in the books is at around INR155 crores as on March 31st, while the net worth has moved to INR200 crores from INR76 crores as at March 31st, 2025, and the book value has gone up as well to about INR98 from INR37.

items.statement: Open to evaluating inorganic opportunities in RegTech adjacencies but disciplined; wait-and-watch mode given AI volatility
items.quote: On the inorganic side, nothing is off the table, but we'll be disciplined. And there's a lot of volatility in the market. We don't know how it is shaping up in terms of AI impact on enterprise software. So we don't want to do a deal just because we have the capital. We'll be open to evaluating opportunities, particularly in adjacencies that could enhance our RegTech footprint.

items.statement: Plans to deepen sales/marketing presence with on-ground hires in developed markets (US/Europe)
items.quote: Hiring, certainly yes. We have plans to deepen our presence in sales and marketing, including on ground hires in these markets. Clearly, yes. We have started looking at that activity now.

items.statement: SaaS sales/marketing spend at 1.1-1.2x net ARR vs industry benchmarks of >2x; may increase slightly but stay EBITDA positive
items.quote: We are well below the SaaS benchmarks where people spend at times more than $2 for $1 of net ARR. We are at about 1.1, 1.2 levels. We might go a little higher than that, but we don't want to be spending indiscriminately.

items.statement: Prolonged Middle East crisis beyond Q1 FY27 could adversely impact SupTech pipeline and government regulatory budgets
items.period: if crisis goes well beyond the first quarter of this financial year
items.quote: It is possible that a prolonged Middle East crisis might have a possible adverse impact on the SupTech pipeline. Having said that, so far, we have not seen any indications along these lines, but it will be fair to factor in this possibility if the crisis goes well beyond the first quarter of this financial year.

items.statement: SupTech wins could delay if Middle East crisis prolongs post June; targeting 3-4 wins annually as usual
items.quote: I would start getting worried post June, I would say. We are looking at 3 to 4 wins on the SupTech side as usual every year. This could be more or less given the situation.

items.statement: Moved to new office in Navi Mumbai near Turbhe station
items.quote: And finally, I want to say that we are pleased to mention that we have moved to a new office, which is in Navi Mumbai itself, which is near Turbhe station, and you are welcome to visit us when you get an opportunity.

items.statement: FY27 standalone revenue guidance INR 875-950 crore excluding battery chemicals
items.quote: We remain confident of achieving revenues in the range of INR 875 to INR 950 crore in FY27 on a standalone basis, considering full production from MPP-5 from Q2 FY26 onwards.

items.statement: Battery chemicals revenue guidance INR 300 crore plus for FY27, mostly H2
items.quote: The electrolyte salt and electrolyte, the Neogen Ionics revenue potential we had mentioned last year to be INR 300 crore plus. The same remains the current guidance also. We expect to have a INR 300 crore plus kind of revenue from our NIL business.

items.statement: FY28 standalone revenue target INR 1,100 crore plus at full utilization
items.quote: Our FY28 tentative target is around INR 1,100 odd crore. And if we maintain the same growth rate, by FY29, we should be INR 1,200 crore plus, between INR 1,200 to INR 1,400 crore plus revenue just based on the regular demand in the existing business.

items.statement: FY29 consolidated revenue projection INR 3,700-4,200 crore
items.quote: With the existing capacity, we can have revenue of around INR 3,700 to INR 4,200 crore plus based on the projections which we have made till now.

items.statement: Dahej Phase 1 budgeted INR 428 crore, completion by February 2027; Pakhajan Phase 2 revised cost INR 1,367 crore, completion by March 2027
items.quote: Under this updated schedule, the Dahej Phase 1 project is budgeted at INR 428 crore and is firmly on track for completion by February 2027. Concurrently, the revised cost for Pakhajan Phase 2 stands at INR 1,367 crore and expected completion is by March 2027.

items.statement: FY27 capex outflow estimated INR 800 crore including balance battery projects and standalone
items.quote: FY27 we would complete with the balance CAPEX which could be around INR 600 crore/INR 700 crore. Plus maybe about INR 100-odd crore in Neogen. So, total together at around INR 800 crore.

items.statement: Provisional approvals from additional global customers for lithium electrolyte salts; final site audits completed for multiple US electrolyte makers awaiting commercial clearances
items.quote: Encouragingly, we have received provisional approval from additional global customers for lithium electrolyte salts, while final site audits for multiple US-based electrolyte makers have also been completed and are currently awaiting final commercial clearances.

items.statement: Domestic giga customer scaling from 1 to 5 GWh in H1 FY27, Neogen sole qualified supplier; second customer pilot line in Q2 FY27, commercial 2027
items.quote: One of the customers has already been buying from us small volumes for last one year. And they have now also increased their capacity which is coming online. Within the first half, their capacity is increasing from 1 giga to 5 giga.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin sustained at 17.8% despite expansion overheads and Dahej replacement costs
items.quote: EBITDA margin sustained at 17.8% despite expansion-related overheads, geopolitical-led supply chain disruptions, and temporary costs associated with the Dahej replacement facility and toll manufacturing arrangements.

items.statement: Battery chemicals ROCE target 18-20% maintained after revised capex
items.quote: So, when we put together the revised model also, the return remains at 18% to 20% - 20% being the base target on the salt side and with electrolyte, as I said, we are finalizing it, but effectively we should be targeting 18% to 20% ROCE, even after the revised capex.

items.statement: Lithium carbonate prices around USD 24-25/kg, considered slightly above long-term stable range of USD 20+/-5; bromine prices stabilized at elevated levels
items.quote: Even now lithium prices are around USD24/USD25 lithium carbonate prices, which as per me is the kind of a normal price because USD15 to USD20 is what I consider as a long-term stable lithium price. So, it is only slightly above.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 revenue growth 22% YoY driven mostly by volumes (2-3% value impact); Inorganic Chemicals up 145% YoY on volume
items.quote: Most of this is basically by volume. There was hardly any impact of may be 2% or 3% which was because of value. Rest of it was completely through volumes.

items.statement: Improving demand visibility for India giga-scale ACC battery ecosystem and international non-FEOC compliant supply chain interest
items.quote: We continue to witness improving demand visibility for India's giga-scale ACC battery manufacturing ecosystem, alongside strong international interest for non-FEOC compliant supply chain.

items.statement: H2 FY26 net cash from operations positive INR 14.6 crore vs H1 outflow INR 246.1 crore; inventory built for Q1-Q2 sales due to Dahej delay
items.quote: H2 FY26 reflected a significantly stronger cash flow performance compared to H1 FY26, supported by improved operating efficiency and better working capital management. Net cash from operating activities turned positive at INR 14.6 crore in H2 FY26 versus an outflow of INR 246.1 crore in H1 FY26.

items.statement: Trade payables extended via supplier negotiations and factoring during fire-related disruption; target to balance debtors and creditors over 2-3 years
items.quote: we were able to negotiate longer credit terms with them and some of them were also able to get factoring against Neogen's payment lines. So, we were able to get longer credit terms. So, we have basically used longer credit terms with them. And our long-term target as we said is to balance our debtors with our creditors

items.statement: FY26 consolidated total debt INR 1,330 crore, net debt INR 1,295 crore; peak debt unchanged after promoter equity INR 160 crore and Morita USD 20M
items.quote: Consolidated total debt reached INR 1,330 crore in FY26, bringing the net debt to INR 1,295 crore. Increase in debt was driven by targeted funding for the Dahej facility rebuild and ongoing capital deployment at Neogen Ionics.

items.statement: One-year principal moratorium from commercial operations start date for Pakhajan and Dahej; interest starts immediately after COD
items.quote: The moratorium is for the period of one year from the revised start of commercial operations. So, whenever we have the first start of stable commercial operations, there will be one year moratorium from that date.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend INR 1 per equity share for FY26
items.quote: Reflecting our strong performance and long-term growth confidence, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR 1 per equity share for FY26.

items.statement: Insurance claim INR 60 crore received February 2026; cumulative on-account INR 140 crore plus salvage INR 7 crore; net claim receivable INR 203 crore
items.quote: On the insurance front, we received a recent tranche of INR 60 crore in February 2026, which provides additional liquidity comfort during our ongoing transition. This brings our total cumulative on-account insurance claims received to INR 140 crore plus a salvage realization of INR 7 crore. Our net claim receivable stands at INR 203 crore.

items.statement: Organic Chemicals revenue split: bromine derivatives 40-45%, advanced intermediates 30%, organolithium and lithium balance
items.quote: I think bromine derivatives was about 40-45% of the revenue. The advanced intermediates was about 30% of the revenue. The organolithium and lithium together were the balance.

items.statement: Organolithium capacity increased 2.5x to 300 MT/year; achieved highest monthly production in March 2026; targeting 80-90% utilization
items.quote: As compared to the installed capacity which was around 120 metric tons, we had increased 2.5x to 300 metric tons per year. So, this year and last year was somewhere in between. So, this year we are very strongly looking at a potential to achieve almost 80%, 90% of our increased capacity.

items.statement: Lithium price volatility and geopolitical supply chain disruptions remain key risks; commodity price increases are pass-through with no EBITDA impact
items.quote: I normally do not factor in commodity price increase into how it will change our topline significantly because most of it is a pass-through and it is anyway something which is difficult to predict. So, for us more focus is on what we consider as a normal price revenue potential.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guided at low to mid-teens with 8-9% organic India growth, OSAM full-year contribution, and Africa trajectory
items.quote: We expect revenue growth to be in the low to mid -teens, supported by OSAM's full year contribution, Africa continuing on its current trajectory, and an 8% to 9% organic growth in our India business.

items.statement: FY27 gross margin recovery of 50-100 bps over FY26 as procurement normalizes and pricing actions take effect
items.quote: are expecting a gradual gross margin recovery of 50 to 100 basis points over FY26 levels as procurement normalizes and our pricing actions take effect

items.statement: Effective tax rate to normalize to 25-27% range post FY26 favorable tax orders
items.quote: Effective tax rate will return to the normal 25 to 27 range post completion of the favorable tax orders we received in FY26.

items.statement: FY27 capex budget: INR130 cr standalone regular, INR180 cr Maharashtra expansion, plus Uganda and OSAM
items.value: INR130 crores standalone regular, INR180 crores Maharashtra
items.quote: So INR65 crore s for the regular capex what we consider, around INR33 crore s we have concerned for the Q3 and hardware around INR7 crores and overall standalone we are expecting around INR 130 crores of capex. Q4 -- yes, that's what we're projecting, Abhishek. Dodla Sunil Reddy: Without considering the Maharashtra project.. Management: Maharashtra out of INR280 crores, INR20 crores we have spent

items.statement: Uganda greenfield expansion: 70 acres acquired, INR60 cr total capex budget, phased completion by end-2029
items.quote: On the Uganda expansion plan, we acquired 70 acres of land parcel for a greenfield expansion. Total capex budgeted for this project is currently around INR60 crore s, including land as well as the plant. It will be executed in a phased manner and will be completed by year-end of '29.

items.statement: Bihar land allocated: 7 acres, INR4.4 cr investment, project under consideration pending Board approval
items.quote: We were also allocated a 7-acre land parcel by the Bihar Industrial Area Development Authority for a dairy project, which will call for additional investment of around INR4.4 crore s towards the land. The project is presently under consideration and further details shall be disclosed after Board approval.

items.statement: Maharashtra plant commercial operations expected by end of FY27, INR106 cr deployed cumulatively across FY25-26 against INR280 cr envelope
items.quote: Our Maharashtra project is progressing as per the scheduled timelines and is expected to start commercial operations by the end of FY27. The work is under progress and INR106 crore s worth of capex has already been deployed cumulatively across '25 and '26.

items.statement: Maharashtra procurement currently 3 LLPD, targeting minimum 5 LLPD by end of FY27
items.quote: So right now, the average procurement Maharashtra what we are procuring is 3 lakh average right now for the last couple of months onwards. So once season comes by end of this year, we are targeting minimum 5 lakhs.

items.statement: Africa revenue target 15-18% of consolidated by FY28, supported by Uganda Phase 2 expansion into pasteurized milk
items.quote: We see Africa scaling towards 15% to 18% of consolidated revenue by FY28, supported by a Phase 2 expansion in Uganda, which will include pasteurized milk and milk products that will be sold in Uganda.

items.statement: Africa FY27 revenue guided ~INR600 cr (20% growth on FY26 ~INR500 cr base)
items.quote: So basically, last year we've done around INR500 crores, on that --- talking about 20%, INR600 crores approximately. Dodla Sunil Reddy: That is the guiding number

items.statement: Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin 5% due to elevated procurement costs and calibrated pricing; standalone India EBITDA margin ~6-7% for full year
items.quote: The EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 5% and PAT margins stood at 6.5%. Margins remained under pressure due to elevated milk procurement costs and a calibrated pricing strategy.

items.statement: Packaging material costs up 30% YoY; small corrections passed to consumers; expecting prices to hold at elevated levels
items.quote: So I think packaging material as a number has gone up by 30%. Most of the plastics that are there and we use a lot of the plastic, it's gone up by 30%. That small corrections is what we have passed on to the consumers in terms of the price corrections that we have taken.

items.statement: Fuel price increase INR3/litre currently; absorbing for now; will wait 2-4 weeks for stability before deciding pass-through
items.quote: So the current INR3 I think currently for a month or so we will have to look at it and we will absorb because a portion of it will be passed on to the transporters itself because we take price corrections only periodically and we normally try to keep it for that period.

items.statement: Milk procurement cost Q4 FY26 INR41/litre vs INR37.4 in Q4 FY25; sales price INR58.4 vs INR57.7 previous quarter; INR1/litre of inflation passed through so far
items.quote: The average procurement cost in Q4 FY26 stood at INR41 per liter as against INR38.7 per liter in the previous quarter and INR37.4 per liter in Q4 FY25. However, we did not entirely pass on this increase in cost to the consumers. Our average milk sales price for the quarter stood at INR58.4 per liter, which was INR57.7 per liter in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Cooperatives (Amul, Mother Dairy) raised consumer prices INR2 in May; Dodla had already hiked in mid-March; no further major hikes planned, only minor corrections
items.quote: See, we have -- they have increased the selling prices. Amul and Mother Dairy has just come in the paper to increase the INR2 selling price. We have already taken that price increase in the month of March itself, mid-March itself we had taken the increase.

items.statement: VAP mix target 32-34% long-term; Q4 VAP revenue INR2,969 mn (ex-bulk 21% YoY growth); curd 15.4% volume growth, paneer strong
items.quote: Once our planned expansion fully stabilizes, our planned expansion directionally we are confident that the VAP mix will improve further. This growth will be delivered by curd, paneer, and ice cream, and broadly we are targeting closer to 32% to 34% in terms of VAP contribution.

items.statement: Seasonality reduction strategy: extend buttermilk/lassi/curd consumption from 2-3 months to 6 months; paneer and flavoured milk growing steadily
items.quote: We're trying to extend that to a six months period to see that people start using it as a refreshment rather than worrying about it as a summer product. On the other hand, products like paneer have improved for us. Paneer has seen a significant growth that has come in the local consumption once placements are in place.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 volumes strong: liquid milk 4.5-5% growth, VAP 16-17% growth; summer driving higher VAP mix and realization
items.quote: Yes, our milk growth rates have maintained around that 4.5% 5% even in the current scenario, but we've seen a significant increase in the VAP growth. Like we normally say that our summers of VAP will be higher, so our VAP rates have been -- VAP growth rates have been significantly higher. We are around 16% 17% VAP growth rate.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend INR5 per equity share for FY26
items.quote: For FY '26, the board has recommended a final dividend of INR5 per equity share.

items.statement: Ms. Dodla Silpa Reddy appointed as senior management personnel for strategy and transformation
items.quote: I also would like to welcome Ms. Dodla Silpa Reddy, who got appointed by the Board as a senior management personnel for strategy and transformation.

items.statement: Key uncertainties: fuel price trajectory (USD60-120/bbl could mean 25-30% fuel cost increase), plastic prices, weather/El Niño, war-related commodity volatility
items.quote: None of us are certain about where this price of fuel will be stopped becau se if you look at it and people and this is my view and please correct me if I'm wrong USD60 to USD 120 in my simple mathematics for barrel means it's a 100% price increase, which should translate even to a 25% or 30% increase for us on fuel, which is not yet shown

items.statement: FY27 organic revenue growth guidance of 12-13% with high visibility, targeting 18-20% with pipeline additions
items.quote: right now, the way we are looking at our current order book as well as pipeline, we have a reasonable level of confidence in terms of high visibility pipeline and order book to deliver about 12% to 13% of growth, and that is, of course, at the beginning of the year.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 21-22% at INR 92/USD planning rate, with currency benefit at current rates
items.quote: when we've done the planning at INR 92-odd levels, what we planned for is an EBITDA between 21% to 22% for the revenue growth that we will deliver primarily on account of some of these upfront investments that we are making in the leadership hires on the AI CoE side as well as the side

items.statement: Technology vertical expected to grow 5-8% YoY in FY27 after adjusting for losses
items.quote: technology vertical for this year, our sense is that it should be between 5% to 8% growth on a year-on-year basis. This is adjusting for the loss.

items.statement: CPG vertical expected to grow 18-22% YoY in FY27
items.quote: Consumer should, our sense is right now, should grow anywhere between 18% to 22%. So that's the sort of range that we're looking at.

items.statement: BFSI vertical expected to grow at least 40% YoY in FY27
items.quote: BFSI, obviously, the growth rates for the next year will come down compared to the previous year. But our sense is they should grow at least at about 40% for the next year, based on where we stand right now.

items.statement: Databricks revenue expected to grow 60%+ in FY27
items.quote: the expectation is that the Databricks portfolio of work will continue to grow at about 60% plus.

items.statement: FY26 full year business EBITDA 23%, in line with 23-24% guidance
items.quote: on a full year basis, again, in line with what we had guided before, our business EBITDA for the full year came in at 23%, in line with what we had guided.

items.statement: AI project gross margins 55-58% vs company average 50.8% in FY26
items.quote: When you compare this with the gross margins that we are seeing on the AI-led projects, we are seeing gross margins in the range of 55% to 58%.

items.statement: Three large deal conversations in top tech account: one $3M+ near closure, two at $1M and $1.5M
items.quote: I was able to participate in three fairly large deal conversations. And one of them is almost at the point of fructifying, which will be a $3 million-plus deal in total, but the other two are also $1 million, $1.5 million in size.

items.statement: Planning senior leadership hires including potential CTO for AI CoE and Databricks practice
items.quote: there will be some senior level hiring that we will continue to make specifically in the AI space, right, including a potential hiring of a Chief Technology Officer.

items.statement: Fixed-bid revenue 18-20% of total, managed services 65-68% of T&M, pure T&M remainder; targeting shift to milestone/outcome-based models
items.quote: the ratio of fixed-bid to T&M for us will be closer to about 18% to 20%. So, 20% from fixed-bid, fixed type of work and then T&M would be about 80%. But within that 80%, almost 65% to 68% of that would be in a managed services construct.

items.statement: Top tech client consolidation and insourcing caused revenue loss; new leader prefers internal employees over vendors
items.quote: The nature of the decline is twofold. One is a consolidation where they have decided to work with one of several partners. This has led to some amount of the decline. The second part of it is taking the work in-house. Specifically in this account, there was a new leader who came in to head up a big chunk of the work that we were doing. And their preferred model is to work with internal full-time e

items.statement: Pursuing nearshore/offshore shift for top tech client to improve margins on new work
items.quote: One of the things that we are actively pursuing with the client is as we open new threads with the client, we want to do a lot more work either offshore or nearshore.

items.statement: OpenAI/Anthropic services arms validate need for strong services layer; models alone cannot deliver value without orchestration, governance, transparency
items.quote: While there have been concerns around that in terms of what it means for services companies, I think it's also a validation that a very strong services layer is required. And just the models by themselves cannot deliver value until the services layer is available to take care of a lot of the orchestration, not just the business process and the decision-making and the embedding within the workflow,

items.statement: No debt or fund raise mentioned; intercompany forex gain of ~INR 4.5 Cr in FY25 not repeated
items.quote: for the last year, there was almost INR4.5 crores forex gain that we had recognized in relation to some intercompany loans and advances that were given out.

items.statement: Evaluating inorganic acquisitions to strengthen Databricks professional services partnership
items.quote: We are also evaluating potential inorganic acquisition opportunities where these firms come with a much stronger professional services partnership with Databricks.

items.statement: FY26 revenue crossed INR 1,000 Cr milestone; ~2.2x USD growth since IPO over 3 years
items.value: INR 1,000 Cr, 2.2x USD growth since IPO
items.quote: One of the, I would say, big positives for this year as we close the year was going past the INR1,000 crores mark, which is a fairly significant milestone for us. Even in dollar terms compared to the year in which we IPOed, we've roughly grown about 2.2x in about the 3-year time frame.

items.statement: FY28 revenue target of INR1,000 crores remains but timing may shift

And the road map showed that in FY28, we will try to achieve it, okay? But for the last 1 year, we have been saying that while INR1,000 crores number has no t changed, the question is only could be of timing

items.statement: Open order book of over INR1,750 crores provides revenue visibility for FY27
items.quote: We are encouraged by this shift and remain op timistic that this renewed upward trajectory will sustain through FY26-'27, supported by a str onger order pipeline of over INR1,750-plus crores, improved visibility and growing demand across our businesses

items.statement: Government open order book significantly past INR200 crores with strong pipeline
items.quote: If you see we closed the government with an open order book of more than INR200 crores, significantly more than INR200 crores and I think for the first 9 months, we had already explained in Q3, what were the dynamics across the different segments.

items.statement: FY26 order book conversion rate was 17-18% from opening INR1,500 crores
items.quote: From that INR1,500 crores, around 17%, 18%, I guess, 18% got converted into revenue. So that makes it from INR1,500 crores and 18%, you can calculate, it is something like INR270 crores.

items.statement: INR780 crores of new orders booked in FY26, INR200 crores converted to revenue
items.quote: INR780 crores we booked new orders in FY26. Out of that, INR200 crores got converted into revenue itself, leaving behind INR580 crores for the future.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 460 bps YoY to 44.6%
items.quote: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin has expanded 460 bps year-on-year to 44.6% and PAT margin has expanded 230 bps year-on-year to 31.3%.

items.quote: over the course of the year, that was the objective that how do we optimize the cost and increase the efficien cy and productivity. We still see opportunities for cost efficiency which we are focu

items.statement: Strong Q4 sequential recovery with revenue up 54.8%, EBITDA up 141%, PAT up 171%
items.quote: Compared to Q3 FY26, the fourth quarter delivered a strong sequential improvement with revenue growing by 54.8%, EBITDA increasing by 141% and PAT also growing by 171%.

items.statement: Government business saw significant growth in Q4 with deferred orders expected in FY27
items.quote: We saw a strong Q4, that's the inflection point that we have seen. And so the government business itself should see a significant growth in this year. And also the IoT business, which is basically underpinning or being driven across government, but also automotive and the corporate, that is also going to see a significant growth.

items.statement: FY27 priority is organic growth investment in IoT and government working capital needs
items.quote: Our first priority, which we believe is the right way to do is to provide organic growth. Now remember, there are three verticals market segment-wise, government, auto and corporate. In terms of segments, you can think we already are giving you map-led and IoT-led. So investments in IoT part of it because IoT also requires capital.

items.statement: IoT margin expansion driven by operating leverage and better SaaS mix, not inventory gains
items.quote: I don't think that's the reason I wish that's not -- the reason for margin expansion is simply operating leverage yes, operating level revenue went up, the mix was better, more SaaS, that mix was better. And yes, that's where the margin went up. Inventory is just a function of what our future demand is.

items.quote: One of the most encouraging developments for us continues to be in growing adoption. And engagement of the Mappls App ecosy stem, which has recorded 45-plus million downloads till date and 10-plus million downloads during the year

items.statement: Final dividend of INR3.50 per share (175%) declared for FY26
items.quote: The Board was pleased to express its gratitude to all the shareholders by declaring a final dividend for FY26 of INR3.50 per equity share of INR2 each at the rate of 175%.

items.statement: IoT automotive order delayed due to regulatory requirements now fulfilled
items.quote: Now that INR20 crores that got delayed for certain, not the execution capability of ours, but there were certain regulatory things which we had to fulfil. And now we ha ve fulfilled that. So that will start reflecting in Q1

items.statement: Plan to restructure reporting segments from Q1 FY27: Auto & Retail, Corporate, Government
items.quote: Going forward, from Q1, we are thinking of changing that reporting of C&E and A&M to auto and retail as one, corporate as a second one and government as a third one. So we are thinking on those planning for it. And if we go ahead with that, then we will break up for FY26, Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4 also so that you can have a comparison.

items.statement: IoT hardware treated as fixed asset depreciated over 3 years, requires ongoing capital
items.quote: When we get the IoT business, it is done on an opex model for the customers, which has -- where hardware and software are put together. And that's where we get the subscription on a monthly basis. That -- when the hardware goes in to -- goes to the customer, it is treated as a fixed asset in the company's books and gets depreciated over the next 3 years.

items.statement: Government payment delays may persist but collection flow remains strong with near-zero bad debt
items.quote: One of the reasons we are actually moving on two fronts in the government. One part, as Rohan has been saying, we have almost -- if not really fully, but almost zero bad debt in the government. That is very important for us to note. The collection period might be higher. But that's again a nature of that beast.

items.statement: Aim to at least hold adjusted EBITDA margins in FY27 while stepping up revenue growth
items.quote: Our key focus in FY27 is on stepping up revenue growth while at least holding margins.

items.statement: Expect acceleration and step-up in growth in FY27 versus FY26, targeting long-term FY30 goals
items.quote: FY27, as we see today, short of any black swan events coming our way, we do see an acceleration and a step-up in growth of what we delivered in FY26.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 13.2% in Q4 FY26, highest ever, and 12.2% for full year FY26, up 55 bps YoY
items.quote: For the full year, adjusted EBITDA stood at INR 332 crores with margin of 12.2%, up 55 basis points over the previous year.

items.statement: Implemented calibrated price increase of 6-7% on average in April 2026 to address input cost inflation
items.quote: In response to rising costs, we implemented a calibrated price increase of 6% to 7% on an average in April, and we will re main agile as the situation

items.statement: Early indicators show price increase landed well with no material impact on sell-outs or down-trading observed so far
items.quote: The early indicators that we have seen is that the price increase has landed well, and we do not see any impact as of now on sellouts or on tertiary sales.

items.statement: Water purifier category growing at 3-year CAGR over 12%; rising consumer awareness driving traction despite drought concerns
items.quote: Water purifiers saw a temporary moderation after strong growth in FY25, the category has grown at a 3-year CAGR of over 12%, and we remain confident of its growth trajectory stepping up as we go forward.

items.statement: Emerging categories scaling: robotics strong growth, air purifiers grew 2.7x in FY26, water softeners double-digit growth
items.quote: Air purifiers gr ew 2.7x in FY26, albeit on a low base, and we see this as a significant future growth opportunity

items.statement: AMC bookings grew double-digits for fourth consecutive quarter in FY26; multi-year mix increased significantly
items.quote: We've had the fourth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth in bookings, in AMC bookings. And therefore, that momentum has sustained.

items.statement: Capex increased to INR 84 crores in FY26 from INR 55 crores in FY25; free cash flow INR 237 crores (148% of PAT)
items.quote: This is despite a step-up in capex from INR 55 crores in FY25 to INR 84 crores in FY26. We have consistently targeted an FCF to PAT conversion above 100%, and this trend has continued in FY26.

items.statement: Balance sheet strengthened to net cash surplus of INR 443 crores from net debt of INR 193 crores in June 2022
items.quote: Our balance sheet also strengthened significantly, and we have moved from a net debt of INR 193 crores in June 2022 to a net cash surplu s of INR 443 crores

items.statement: Robotics manufacturing shifting from imported FG to SKD assembly at Dixon partnership over next 3-4 months as QCO deadline extends to September
items.quote: about manufacturing SKDs. And as you're aware, the quality control order, the Q4 FY26 Earnings Conference Call May 20, 2026 QCO of BIS has got pushed out to September of this year. And as we come closer to September, you will start seeing the manufacturing and assembly migrate to Dixon over the next 3-4 months

items.statement: Uncertain macro environment with geopolitical tensions, input cost inflation, currency pressure, and potential consumer demand impact
items.quote: The evolving geopolitical situation, input cost increases, currency pressure and the potential impact of inflation on consumer demand all warr ant close observation

items.statement: Employee cost grew 7% to INR 328 crores (12.1% of revenue vs 12.6% YoY); headcount additions aligned to growth
items.quote: Employee cost for FY26 grew by 7% to INR 328 crores and came in at 12.1% of revenue versus 12.6% of revenue last year.

items.statement: Launched influencer-led marketing campaign generating over 1 billion views to drive filter sales and consumer awareness
items.quote: During the quarter, we launched major influencer-led marketing campaign that has already generated over 1 billion views.

items.statement: Company confident of growing around mid-teens in FY27

items.statement: EBITDA margin target to sustain current level and improve gradually
items.quote: Our aim is to sustain current level of EBITDA margins and continue our efforts to improve gradually in the subsequent quarters, depending upon the growth of the two-wheeler industry and geopolitical environment.

items.statement: Export revenue expected to grow 20% in FY27 if geopolitical situation remains reasonable
items.quote: This year we are very confident of growing at 20%, provided the geopolitical situation remains reasonable, which we are as an optimist, which we feel that it shall be sorted out soon rather than later.

items.statement: Alloy wheel revenue expected Rs. 90-100 Cr in FY27 and Rs. 220 Cr in FY28
items.quote: FY27 we are expecting revenue of around Rs. 90 - Rs. 100 Cr and FY28 will be about Rs. 220 Cr.

items.statement: Capex plan of Rs. 400 Cr for FY27 funded from internal accruals

items.statement: Capex breakup: Rs. 40-50 Cr maintenance, rest for new plant capacities
items.quote: Capex breakup is very little is the maintenance budget, that's about Rs.40 to Rs. 50 Cr, rest is all the capex for the new plant capacities, which we keep on adding.

items.statement: Bangalore plant reached 90% capacity utilization, all capacities full
items.quote: Very, very happy to share that Bangalore we have reached 90% capacity utilization that we set up last year, our 18th plant and the third plant in Bengaluru. The Bangalore all capacities are full now.

items.statement: Karoli plant at 65% utilization, alloy wheel supplies to Japanese customer starting H2 FY27
items.quote: In the Karoli plant, the capacities utilization is still 65%, that is the reason that we have made investment for the alloy wheels. The alloy wheel supplies to the Japanese customer in the beginning of the H2, so this current year you'll see much higher capacity utilization in the Karoli plant also.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 12.1%, impacted 80 bps by aluminium pass-through
items.quote: We achieved EBITDA of Rs. 140 Cr with 31.1% year-on-year growth. EBITDA margin at 12.1%, however, this EBITDA percentage was impacted due to pass-through alloy prices as mentioned earlier. For this impact, EBITDA percentage would have been higher by 80 basis points.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin 13.1%, impacted 40 bps by aluminium pass-through
items.quote: We achieved EBITDA of Rs. 551 Cr with 24.1% year-on-year growth. EBITDA margin at 13.1%, however, EBITDA percentage was impacted due to pass-through alloy prices. For this impact, EBITDA percentage would have been higher by 40 basis points.

items.statement: Aluminium price surge in March caused conscious loss of Rs. 5 Cr in aftermarket as daily price increases could not be passed on immediately
items.quote: There was a conscious loss by us of Rs. 5 Cr because every day we cannot increase the prices and the prices were rising actually every day. items.quote: Whatever the aluminium prices, the customer is already compensating us. items.statement: Alloy wheel supplies to Japanese customer started on schedule from Karoli plant, supplies beginning H2 FY27
