items.statement: Sunroof plant audited by system suppliers, supplies starting H2 FY27
items.quote: Yes, very much on track. The plant has been audited by the sunroof system suppliers and I think again the same time H2, all the previous ventures shall bring fruit, and the supplies will start.

items.statement: Second alloy wheel partnership under testing, expected to fructify before H2 FY27
items.quote: The second partnership is also as I've already mentioned under testing and we are very confident that something should come out before H2.

items.statement: GTD cable JV production started, plant audited, supplies to begin H2 FY27
items.quote: GTD cable holding, the production has come out and to the system suppliers have audited the plant and the supplies again will start in

items.statement: Two-wheeler industry production grew 11.8% YoY in FY26 to 26.7 million units, surpassed FY19 peak
items.quote: The two-wheeler industry closed FY26 with a strong production volume of 26.7 million units, up from 23.9 million units in FY25. In Q4 alone, production touched 7 million units as compared to 5.8 million in the same quarter last year. I am happy to share that this year the two-wheeler industry production volumes have surpassed the previous peak of FY19.

items.statement: OEMs maintaining original production schedules showing nice growth for FY27, no supply disruptions
items.quote: As far outlook of the two-wheeler industry is concerned, our all our OEM customers they are carrying on with their original production schedules which shows a nice growth in this year also and none of the supplies have been affected by the raw materials or anything.

items.statement: Independent aftermarket grew 24.7% in FY26 driven by GST reduction from 28% to 18%, enabling market share gain from grey market
items.quote: Since all our products were under the category of 28% GST, hence the reduction of GST rate from 28% to 18% is helping us to outgrow in the Indian aftermarket and capture more market share from grey market operators and duplicators. Happy to share that our independent aftermarket has grown by 24.7% in FY26.

items.statement: EV segment growing at single digit, company growing with it, supplies to almost every EV manufacturer
items.quote: The EV segment is growing still at single digit, and we are also growing with the EV segment. As you are aware, we are supplying to almost every EV manufacturer in the country, so we are growing as they are growing.

items.statement: Advanced braking system revenue grew 32% in Q4 FY26 and 17% in FY26 YoY
items.quote: Our advanced braking system revenue grew by 32% in Q4 FY26 and 17% in FY26 on year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Aluminium light-weighting precision solutions revenue grew 47% in Q4 FY26 and 30% in FY26 YoY
items.quote: The aluminium light-weighting precision solutions revenue grew by 47% in Q4 FY26 and 30% in FY26 on year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Safety control cable revenue grew 26% in Q4 FY26 and 14% in FY26 YoY
items.quote: The safety control cable revenue also recorded growth of 26% in Q4 FY26 and 14% in FY26 on year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Export revenue Rs. 141 Cr in FY26 vs Rs. 147 Cr in FY25 due to trade disruptions, higher tariffs, geopolitical tensions
items.quote: Our revenue from exports were at Rs. 141 Cr in FY26 against Rs. 147 Cr last year because of the trade disruptions due to higher tariff rates, geopolitical tensions, supply chain issues, logistic costs and other bottlenecks. We could not achieve our target on the export front.

items.statement: Negative working capital in FY26 due to sudden aluminium price increase in March causing receivables buildup before pass-through
items.quote: This is due to sudden increase in aluminium prices in the month of March and the impact is on the balance sheet date. That's why it's looking like that because the pricing to the customers takes time to pass on in the terms of invoices. So, there is increase in receivables share and I think that is the only reason.

items.statement: Working capital expected to normalize in coming quarters as aluminium price pass-through completes
items.quote: Yes, yes, it will normalize, you know.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of 92.5% (Rs. 1.85 per equity share of face value Rs. 2) for FY26
items.quote: The board has recommended a dividend of 92.5%, that is Rs. 1.85 per equity share of face value of Rs. 2 each.

items.statement: ROACE 26.9% and ROE 25.3% delivered in FY26
items.quote: We have delivered strong returns in FY26 with ROACE at 26.9% and ROE at 25.3%.

items.statement: 9.9 MW solar plant at Sirsa, Haryana fully operational since April 2025; 11.55 MW Bikaner plant expected commissioning Q2 FY27
items.quote: I am happy to update that our 9.9 megawatt solar plant at Sirsa, Haryana has been fully operational since April 2025 and is delivering the sustainable operational economies on the expected lines. Our second captive solar plant of 11.55 megawatt in Bikaner, Rajasthan is progressing well and is expected to be commissioned in Q2 FY27, this reflects ASK's special focus on green energy.

items.statement: Geopolitical conflict in West Asia disrupting supply chains, creating volatility in energy, commodity, currency; aluminium alloy prices phenomenally increased
items.quote: After 28th February, 2026, geopolitical conflict in West Asia has disrupted the global economy, posing an unprecedented challenge in supply chain, creating undue volatility in energy, commodity and currency across the globe and it has started affecting Indian economy as well. The phenomenal increase in aluminium alloy prices in particular have affected our industry.

items.statement: Deficient monsoon could affect agriculture income and two-wheeler demand, but impact not quantifiable
items.quote: This monsoon if it is deficient, it certainly affects the agriculture income, that everyone knows. But we can't quantify the impact that it will have, let the time come.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 orders expected at 40,000-45,000 and consolidated revenue at 500-550 crores, nearly double Q4 level
items.quote: Looking ahead to Q1 FY27, we expect 40,000 to 45,000 orders and consolidated revenue of 500 to 550 crores, nearly double of the Q4 level.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 consolidated gross margin reached 38.5%, up from 34.3% in Q3 and 13.7% in Q4 FY25; excluding PLI gross margin was 33.5%
items.quote: In Q4 for 2025-26, consolidated gross margins reached 38.5%, up from 34.3% in Q3 and 13.7% in Q4, similar quarter as last year. Excluding PLI gross margins was 33.5%.

items.statement: Management expects gross margins to remain a strong structural advantage and incrementally increase over the long term, despite short-term commodity pressures and growth investments
items.quote: And over the longer term also, we can actually expect gross margins to incrementally keep going up. Obviously, in the short term, there will be commodity pressures, as well as some of this gross margin in the last month or two we've invested into aggressive growth.

items.statement: Auto business requires only ~50 crores annual maintenance capex; Cell business capex for 6 GWh largely done with payouts in Q1/Q2 FY27, no further capex until separate capital raise for expansion beyond 6 GWh
items.value: ~50 crores annual maintenance capex for Auto
items.quote: Vipul, again, I will tell you rule of thumb maintenance CapEx will be some ₹50 crores annually. I'll just add one more nuance. We do have some R&D which we capitalize, about 20% -30% of our overall R&D expenses. That will keep coming in. But in terms of PPE CapEx, that'll be below ₹50 crores a year.

items.statement: Auto capacity of 1 million units/year and Gigafactory Phase 1 infrastructure for 6 GWh in place; asset base can support 15,000-20,000 crores annual revenue without meaningful incremental capex
items.quote: The core Auto CapEx is already in place for up to one million. Bhavish just spoke about it for the Auto business of annual capacity, and 4 Gigafactory phase 1 infrastructure is in place for 6 GWh of scale up. Together, the asset base can support approximately 15,000 to 20,000 crores of annual revenue scale across Auto and Cell without needing meaningful incremental CapEx

items.statement: Bikes (Roadster) contributed 15% of April gross orders with 50%+ market share in electric motorcycles; bike portfolio offers up to 500 km certified range using Bharat 4680 cell
items.quote: Motorcycles are India's largest two-wheeler category and EV penetration remains very low. Ola now has 50% market share in electric motorcycles, and bikes contributed 15% of April gross orders. With products going up to 9.1 kWh battery capacity and 500 plus kms certified range, Roadster is built around the core motorcycle customer needs of range, performance and reliability.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 first operating cash flow positive quarter with consolidated CFO of 91 crores; Auto business delivered 213 crores CFO and 173 crores free cash flow
items.value: 91 crores consolidated CFO; 213 crores Auto CFO; 173 crores Auto FCF
items.quote: Q4 was the first operating cash flow positive quarter. Consolidated CFO was 91 crores, supported by strong gross margins, PLI inflows, lower OpEx and tighter working capital discipline. The Auto business delivered 213 crores of CFO and 173 crores of free cash flow in Q4.

items.statement: Plan to raise capital at cell subsidiary level to fund expansion from 6 GWh to 20 GWh; significant inbound interest from private equity players
items.quote: And we are actually going to be expanding that 6 to 20 GWh by next year, but only by raising capital separately at the cell entity, which also we have a lot of inbound interest from private equity players, given the leadership of this asset that we have created.

items.statement: Adjusted operating EBITDA breakeven achievable at 20,000-25,000 units/month at current gross margin (~35%+) and OpEx (~300-350 crores/month) structure
items.quote: With the reset OpEx base and current gross margin structure, adjusted operating EBITDA breakeven is ach ievable at around 20,000 to 25,000 units per month, subject to pricing mix and commodity conditions

items.statement: Government policy shifting toward domestic battery supply chain (ALBM/ALCM mandates), BESS procurement mandates, potential ACC PLI extension; Ola well-positioned with domestic cell IP and Gigafactory
items.quote: There will be more... just like ALMM in solar, there will be ALBM, ALCM. There will be hopefully some extension in the ACC PLI. There will be domestic procurement for BESS deployments mandates coming soon. And our battery business is actually right in the centre of that potential for growth.

items.statement: Near-term commodity cost pressures and aggressive growth investments may pressure gross margins in short term; supply chain ramp-up constraints for both auto and Shakti production
items.quote: Obviously, in the short term, there will be commodity pressures, as well as some of this gross margin in the last month or two we've invested into aggressive growth. But still, gross margins will remain fairly healthy for u s in the short term

items.statement: No dealership model planned; company-owned stores strategy maintained despite past execution slip-ups; focused on improving frontend experience over next 1-2 quarters
items.quote: We don't plan to have any dealerships in our auto business, we believe our strategy is correct. We had some execution slip -ups through last year but now the company has meaningfully overcome that. That said, there is still some work to be done, like you correctly pointed out, and the good thing is our volumes are ramping up in parallel

items.statement: Capex for FY27 is about Rs 1,700 crore for cell expansion; FY28 capex around Rs 1,800-2,000 crore for ingot project
items.quote: So, for FY27, our capex requirement for this expansion is about 1,700 crores. So it will be a mix of debt -equity. Partly that will be funded -- the equity will be funded from accruals and debt we are already working on. So that will be our requirement for FY27.

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio expected to remain between 1 and 1.5 times over next two years
items.quote: Yes. Our current debt-equity is 0.65, but we feel that our debt -equity will remain at around 1.1 -- between 1 and 1.5 times ratio, not more than that.

items.statement: 2.4 GW cell line equipment move-in starts July, production ramp-up in H2 FY27; Phase II 3.6 GW civil work from August, commissioning by mid FY28 (June-July 2027)
items.quote: So 2.4, we are already. If you see our investor presentation, our civil and our building are ready, and we are getting our equipment move-in, which is going to start. Module equipment move-in will start from June, and cell equipment move-in will start from July. So we believe that in the second half of the year beginning, we'll be able to start our cell production and then ramp up.

items.statement: Encapsulant capacity expanded from 2 GW to 5 GW roadmap; currently operating at ~80% utilization
items.quote: Building on this progress, we have now expanded our encapsulant manufacturing roadmap from 2 gigawatt to 5 gigawatt, further strengthening supply chain control, operational resilience, and long-term integration capabilities.

items.statement: Confirmed order book robust at ~5.89 GW (~Rs 8,000 crore) as of March 2026; execution timeline 3-18 months
items.quote: Our confirmed order book remains robust at approximately 5.89 gigawatt, as of March 2026, providing strong forward revenue visibility for the coming quarters.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 margins compressed due to commodity price spikes (silver, aluminum, copper), rupee depreciation, and fixed-price contracts preventing immediate pass-through
items.quote: Also, the depreciation of the Indian rupee against the dollar results in higher import and procurement costs for key components. Also, you know, this war started on 20th February, so last quarter you have orders which are at fixed price contracts and, you know, it was not possible for us to pass on the increase in the input cost and the dollar cost immediately and, you know, that compressed our ma

items.statement: Margins expected to be stable and healthy in FY27, significantly better in H2 as cell production starts and war situation eases
items.quote: Yes. So in overall '27 we see that margins are going to be stable and good because firstly we feel that from the second quarter of this year, the industry is going to be back because we see that the war should ultimately come to a halt. And also , our cell production is starting, which will give a good bump to our bottom line.

items.statement: Input cost pressure from silver, aluminum, copper, oil, and rupee depreciation; pass-through varies by order type (utility pass-through vs C&I fixed price)
items.quote: So the major reasons for the decrease in EBITDA are, as you rightly mentioned, correct, because there was an increase in commodity pricing, which really impacted our input costs across the value chain. You know, solar cell procurement cost was driven by a high increase in silver prices. Aluminum frame cost also risen due to rise in aluminum prices. Copper and other key raw material also, because o

items.statement: Cash conversion low (17-18%) due to PSU orders with 90-120 day recovery cycles and Q4 dispatches concentrated in last 30-45 days; creditor days normalized to secure better pricing
items.quote: So I mean, as far as the cash conversion goes on, I mean, there are many factors to it. So , in the past year, I mean, we have had many orders which are from large-scale PSU orders. So the recovery cycle on those are about 90 to 120 days. And we also had, particularly in quarter four, a good amount of PSU orders where the recovery cycle is 90 to 120 days, so the recovery comes approximately in the

items.statement: Debt-equity improved to 0.65 in FY26 from 1.34 in FY25; FY27 capex funded via mix of accruals and debt
items.quote: Our debt -equity ratio improved significantly to 0.65, as compared to 1.34 in FY2 5, reflecting prudent financial management, reduction in leverage, and improved financial flexibility even as we continue to invest towards future expansion and initiatives.

items.statement: ALMM-II effective from June 1, 2026; ALMM-III declared starting June 2028 requiring 3 manufacturers with 15 GW cumulative capacity
items.quote: ALMM -II is just around the corner, which is coming from 1st onwards. So that is there. And ALMM -III has already been declared, which is really good for the industry, because we have a clear path on how the ecosystem is built up commitment from the government, and we are also aligned with that. And, you know, that's going to start from June 2028.

items.statement: EPC contribution ~3-4% of top line (150 MW); solar pumps ~1% of top line (Rs 50 cr); both expected to stay in same range in FY27
items.quote: Our EPC contribution was about 150 megawatt, which is about 3% -4% of our bottom line. We only take EPCs that are profitable and have a high margin, because that is not our core business. In terms of the breakup of our other part of EPC, which is the solar pump projects, also, that was 1% of our top line, which was about 50 crore of our revenue came from solar pumps.

items.statement: Acquired 80% stake in Melcon Transformers for entry into power transmission segment
items.quote: We entered the transformer manufacturing segment by acquiring an 80% stake in Melcon Transformers and Electricals Private Limited, marking Saatvik's strategic entry into the broader power transmission and energy infrastructure segment.

items.statement: FY26 revenue Rs 45,484 mn (+111% YoY), EBITDA Rs 5,811 mn (+62% YoY, 12.78% margin), PAT Rs 3,571 mn (+64% YoY, 7.85% margin)
items.quote: For the full year FY2 6, revenue from operations increased to 45,484 million, registering a strong growth of around 111% year -on-year and representing the highest ever annual revenue achieved by the company. EBITDA for FY2 6 stood at 5,811 million, reflecting a growth of around 62% year -on-year. EBITDA margin for FY2 6 stood at 12.78%. Profit after tax increased to 3,571 million, registering a g

items.statement: FY26 production 3,162 MW (+117% YoY), sales 3,138 MW (+126% YoY), capacity utilization >84%
items.quote: Operationally, as well, FY26 was our strongest year to date. Total production during the year stood at 3,162 megawatt, as compared to 1,459 megawatt in FY25. Total sales volumes increased significantly to 3,138 megawatt during FY2 6, as against 1,389 megawatt in FY2 5. Capacity utilization remained healthy at over 84% during the year, demonstrating strong operational efficiency and demand visibili

items.statement: Order book split: ~65% large utility (mostly pass-through), rest C&I (fixed price)
items.quote: In the order book, the large utility customers, is almost 65% wherein we will be able to -- most of it will be pass-through and the rest C&I customers will be on a fixed price basis.

items.statement: War-driven commodity, freight, and currency volatility compressing margins across industry; first quarter FY27 expected softer due to ongoing fluctuations
items.quote: But what we are seeing now is a war situation, a force majeure situation right now. And we expect that the first quarter, because this war still continues. The first quarter will be a little softer, because there's high fluctuation, which is really extraordinary fluctuations both in, you know, the US dollars and commodities and oil prices, and all these are key components in manufacturing.

items.statement: Strong domestic demand driven by PM Surya Ghar, PM-KUSUM, ALMM, and 500 GW non-fossil target by 2030; India added ~44.6 GW solar in FY26
items.quote: The country crossed nearly 150 gigawatt of installed solar capacity during FY2 6 and added approximately 44.6 gigawatt of solar capacity during the year, which is amongst the highest annual additions globally.

items.statement: Long-term contracts use dollar-denominated pricing with pass-through clauses for dollar, silver, and change-in-law fluctuations
items.quote: So when you have a long-term order, which is going to be executed in 18 months' time, to ensure that it's a fair business for both parties, what we normally do is we plug three types of possible fluctuations. One is the dollar fluctuation. The other is the silver cost. So normally, now that we will have our own cell , you will have the wafer cost plus kind of a contract. When you have only a modul

items.statement: Technical staff coming with cell equipment to stabilize efficiencies quickly; targeting C&I/utility qualification by end of Q3 or early Q4 FY27
items.quote: So we are very confident that we'll be able to stabilize our efficiencies in a very short period of time , wherein we'll be able to get into C&I and the large utility segment also by the end of the third or beginning of the fourth quarter of this year.

items.statement: Normalized copper EBITDA per ton guided at INR30,000-32,000 on steady-state basis, excluding Q3 tailwind and Q4 headwinds
items.quote: So, for forward guidance, I'm sure about excluding the exceptional tailwind of quarter three FY '26 and a confluence of one-time headwinds in quarter four FY '26, the management expects normalized EBITDA to stabilize at approximately INR32,000 to INR30,000 on a steady state basis.

items.statement: Lead volume growth guided at 10-15% for FY27; copper volume growth expected at good double-digit, potentially beyond 15%
items.quote: Lead and copper, as we see the trends coming in and if we don't let the international disturbances overpower the trends, a regular growth in two digits is always expected.

items.statement: FY27 capex estimated at INR115-120 crores covering antimony project, plastic recycling plant, Ahmedabad JV, Kuwait project, and copper value-added phase 2
items.quote: So, this all put together plus the phase two of the copper value-added project will be around INR115 to INR120 crores.

items.statement: Copper anode capacity 800 MT/month started March 2026; second furnace 800 MT/month expected Q1 FY27; cathode phase 1 Q2 FY27, phase 2 Q3 FY27 to 1,500 MT/month; wire rod 600 MT/month by Aug 2026; bus bar 1,500 MT/month by Sep 2026
items.quote: I am pleased to share that copper anode production has already commenced in March 2026 with an initial installed capacity of 800 metric ton per month. The second furnace with an additional 800 metric ton per month capacity is currently in the advanced stag e of installation and is expected to be commissioned during quarter one financial year '27, taking the total anode capacity to 1,600 metric ton

items.statement: Ahmedabad JV processing of electric motor and cable scrap to start Sep 2026; machinery installation completion targeted Dec 2026
items.quote: Processing of electric motor scrap and cable scrap is expected to commence from September 2026 onwards. Installation of the planned machinery and equipment is targeted for completion by December 2026.

items.statement: Dedicated plastic recycling plant on 6 acres land targeted operational by Q3 FY27 with INR15 crore capex
items.quote: The new unit is targeted to become operational by quarter three financial year '27 and will entail an estimated capex of around INR15 crores.

items.statement: Kuwait battery recycling project civil construction complete; machinery ready at supplier; shipment delayed 30 days due to Iran shipping disruption
items.quote: Civil construction at the site has been completed and the ordered machinery is ready at the supplier's facility. However, due to disruption in shipping routes arising from Iran-related geopolitical situation, dispatches have been temporarily delayed.

items.statement: Copper downstream value-added projects (anode to bus bar) have potential to increase EBITDA margin by 2-4% and add INR22-45 per kg incremental EBITDA
items.quote: Copper downstream project has potential to further increase the EBITDA margin from 2% to 4%.

items.statement: Shipping disruptions eased considerably entering Q1 FY27; logistics costs normalizing and realization formulas recalibrating with stabilizing LME prices
items.quote: Entering Q1 FY '27, shipping disruptions have eased considerably, logistics costs have started normalizing, and realization formulas are also witnessing gradual recalibration with stabilizing LME prices.

items.statement: Management implementing long-term hedging formula mechanism for copper to eliminate formula volatility impact on sale price
items.quote: So in the future we will be working on a long-term hedging formula mechanism where the price of the formula which varies up and down won't affect our sale price.

items.statement: FY26 working capital cycle at 66 days (inventory 62 days, debtor 18 days, creditor 14 days); target to reduce below 60 days
items.quote: As at March 2026, inventory days stood at approximately 62 days, debtor days stood at around 18 days and the creditor days stood at approximately 14 days. Accordingly, the overall working capital cycle stood at around 66 days.

items.statement: Operating cash flow negative INR600 crores in FY26 due to volume/price-driven working capital increase; expected to turn positive from Q2 FY27 as inventory reduced
items.quote: So once that is achieved, hopefully we can see some positive working capital coming positive into the CFS from the Q2 onwards.

items.statement: IPO proceeds INR500 crores: INR375 crores used for debt repayment, INR16.4 crores for IPO expenses, balance for general corporate purposes
items.quote: From the primary issue of around INR500 crores, approximately INR375 crores was utilized towards repayment of the debts, while the balance amount was earmarked for general corporate purposes including the IPO expenses.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 volume decline across copper, lead, aluminium due to raw material supply constraints from Middle East geopolitical conflict; containers stuck at UAE ports
items.quote: Yes, it is because of the geopolitical war. There is a supply of the raw material has been constrained and a lot of containers got stuck in Dubai port.

items.statement: China-driven exceptional buying in Q3 FY26 created tailwind; formula normalized as LME stabilized; structural demand outlook positive for recycling
items.quote: In the quarter three, we had tailwind where we have got benefited from the elevated buying and driven by exceptional demand from China.

items.statement: FY26 revenue mix: copper/copper alloys 55%, lead/lead alloys 40%, aluminium 5%; geographic mix: exports 62%, domestic 38%
items.quote: From a segment contribution perspective, copper and copper alloy products has contributed approximately 55% of the total revenue, while lead and lead alloy ingots contributed 40%, and the aluminium and aluminium-related products has contributed approximately 5% of the revenue during FY '26.

items.statement: Capacity utilization FY26: copper 65%, lead 97-100%, aluminium 35%; copper utilization to rise over 2-3 years with new capacities
items.quote: So the copper, presently we are utilizing around 65% of the total installed capacity, while lead we are almost close to 97% to 100%, and aluminum is around 35% of the installed capacity.

items.statement: FY26 ROE 30.4%, ROCE 25.3%; EBITDA margin 5.9%, PAT margin 3.6%; revenue INR9,543 crores (+48% YoY), volume +26.5%
items.quote: Coming to the return ratios as at March 2026, the return on equities stood at approximately 30.4%, while return on capital employed stood at approximately 25.3%.

items.statement: Global sourcing network across 120+ countries; domestic sourcing improving with EPR-led policy initiatives and recycling formalization
items.quote: We continue to maintain one of the strongest global procurement networks in the industry, with sourcing capabilities across more than 120 countries, and domestic sourcing also improving steadily, supported by India's evolving recycling ecosystem, increased formalization, and EPR-led policy initiatives.

items.statement: Geopolitical shipping disruptions (Iran-Israel conflict) caused temporary logistics cost spike and raw material delays; future shipments rerouted bypassing Middle East ports
items.quote: Secondly, the geopolitical disruptions arising from the Iran-Israel conflict impacted the global shipping routes and increasing logistic and fuel-related costs during March '26.

items.statement: Antimony extraction project (INR20 crores) to recover critical metal from lead-acid battery scrap for higher value realization
items.quote: Antimony is a critical metal present in the lead which we use in the batteries, lead acid battery. And if you are able to separate antimony from the lead, then the free antimony has better value realization.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target INR 210 crore, 45%+ growth on FY26
items.quote: Our FY27 revenue target is INR 210 crores, a 45% plus growth on FY26.

items.statement: FY27 PAT target INR 24-25 crore on INR 210 crore revenue
items.quote: So, it will be around INR 24-25 crores on INR 210 crores of business.

items.statement: INR 159 crore assured recurring revenue at FY27 entry, INR 13.5 crore monthly run rate
items.quote: We entered FY27 with INR 159 crore in assured recurring revenue at INR 13.5 crore per month, a 35% MRR step-up before even we won a single new deal.

items.statement: INR 190 crore visibility from contracted base and pipeline for FY27
items.quote: Current outlook based on contracted base and visible pipeline is INR 190 crores.

items.statement: INR 80 crore locked in contracted recurring revenue for H1 FY27
items.quote: For half year Financial Year '27 specifically, around INR 80 crores is already locked in contracted recurring revenue.

items.statement: FY26 gross margin 32.8%, EBITDA 16.2%, PAT margin 11.1%
items.quote: Gross margin was 32.8% versus 33.9% in FY'25. EBITDA was 16.2% versus 17.7%. PAT was INR 15.92 crores at 11.1% compared to INR 13.9 crores at 13% in FY'25.

items.statement: Underlying PAT margin 14-15% adjusted for Dubai contract, gaming client exit, headcount investment
items.quote: Adjusted for these three items on a like-for-like basis, underlying PAT margin was approximately 14% to 15% above FY '25 and consistent with our track record.

items.statement: FY27 margin recovery via mix shift to AI/security, utilization 84% to 88%, operational leverage
items.quote: Our FY '27 margin recovery plan is built on three levers. First, improving our services mix towards higher margin, AI and security work. Second, driving billable utilization from 84% towards 88%. And third, operational leverage as new hires reach full productivity.

items.statement: AI to be meaningful contributor in FY27, primary growth engine from FY28
items.quote: AI will be a meaningful contributor in FY27, and our primary growth engine from FY28 onwards.

items.statement: AI services revenue INR 2 crore in FY26, targeting 5% of revenue from AI and cybersecurity combined in FY27
items.quote: Our target for this year, both AI and cybersecurity put together, we are targeting about 5% revenue from this.

items.statement: Billable utilization rose from 72% to 84% in FY26, target 88% in FY27
items.quote: Second, driving billable utilization from 84% towards 88%.

items.statement: Headcount 170 with 120+ AWS certified professionals, added INR 6 crore annual cost in FY26
items.quote: Simultaneously, our headcount investment added approximately INR 6 crores in annual cost, again with the revenue benefit that will flow in the current year FY '27 and not FY '26.

items.statement: Debtor days improved 14% from 72 to 62 days, FY27 target below 55 days
items.quote: Debtor days, we have improved 14% from 72 days to 62 days with the FY '27 target below 55.

items.statement: No cost surprise on GPU/hardware as AWS Bedrock prices stable; on-prem hardware costs doubled
items.quote: No, there is no cost surprise.

items.statement: Managed services pricing pressure in India; customers negotiate heavily on services vs cloud consumption
items.quote: India is a very funny country to be in, in this case, because in India, come what may, people would buy the product, but they would crib about the services.

items.statement: Top 20 accounts contribute 73% revenue; 10-12 customers near $1M annual billing
items.quote: Our top 20 accounts contributed 73% of revenue. This is an evidence of relationship depth.

items.statement: DPDP Act and RBI cloud guidelines accelerating cloud migration in India
items.quote: Regulation is accelerating it. Digital India, the DPDP Act, and the RBI cloud guidelines are all forcing the move.

items.statement: US billing entity setup in progress; no US/UK revenue included in FY27 INR 210 crore target
items.quote: So, in this INR 210 crore that we are projecting, we have not considered any U.S. or U.K. turnover, top line in that.

items.statement: Global expansion via light model using fractional consultants/partners; delivery from India centers
items.quote: So, what we are going to do is we will keep it light model in each of the global cities or global geographies where we will start our operation. So, it will be based on fractional consultants as well as partners who will be involved in acquiring businesses for us.

items.statement: Employee cost INR 16.91 crore for 170 employees (~INR 9-10 lakh/head); may rise to INR 12 lakh with AI hiring
items.quote: It's about, see, we have got INR 16.91 crore is our employee cost, and we have got around 170 employees. So, it's about INR 9-10 lakhs.

items.statement: Recurring revenue 82.5% of FY26 revenue; project implementation billing grew 56.3% to INR 25 crore

items.quote: Monthly run rate - MRR grew from INR 7.58 crores at FY'26 entry to INR 10 crores at exit. We opened FY'27 at INR 13.5 crores.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target of INR450-500 crores

items.statement: Target to reach INR1,000+ crores revenue in three years

items.statement: EBITDA margin sustainable at 15%+, targeting above 15%

items.quote: For this year's target, we can comfortably complete it with existing capacity, just by adding some machinery for automation and faster production.

items.quote: For copper and steel, we pass on the costs because it depends on the situation at the time of supply. We pick orders based on the rates at that time.

items.statement: 3-month glass fiber stock; resin and petroleum products affected by geopolitics

items.quote: The FRP market for exports is worth 79 billion. We started exports last time, and it was our first experience in Oman and Gulf countries. We are starting there now.

items.statement: Working capital cycle improved to 40-45 days per MSME rules, sustainable
items.quote: Actually, 40 to 45 days is the government rule, and we have followed that. As I mentioned, we now choose our orders, so our payment terms are also better.

items.statement: No immediate funding need; IPO proceeds cover working capital; future debt/equity depends on order requirements
items.quote: Actually, right now we have improved our working capital cycle. Mostly our performance will be from that. And right now we have a cash fund because the IPO has just happened.

items.statement: Railways clearance expected by end of next month; lab expansion completed

items.quote: Right now, in market competition, actually approvals are held by very few people in this. There are, but we are working in 11 kV and 33 kV only.

items.statement: Developing system house capabilities; back-to-back work for ABB, Crompton
items.quote: We are also creating many system houses ourselves which we have put in approvals in many labs. So they should come in almost two or three months.

items.statement: Aerospace/automotive trial orders in 2-3 months via hand mold development
items.quote: Basically, that is why we are developing hand molds. Actually, hand mold products are used quite a lot in industrial vehicles now. So, we are developing it in the next two or three months.

items.quote: The performance for the Consumer Products vertical was mixed across subsegments. This is not just a structural integration but the creation of one integrated global metals business with India at the center of the opera tion, execution, and manufacturing

items.statement: US business consolidation under evaluation, targeting completion by end of year or slight delay
items.quote: USA is we are still here also we are still investigating. There are some technical issues on incorporating, not incorporating, on consolidating USA. items.statement: Board exploring fundraise options, another board meeting in 2-3 weeks to evaluate

items.statement: Disciplined cash management remains key focus as business scales
items.quote: As the business scales, disciplined cash management will remain a key focus area for the company.

items.statement: Order pipeline positive trend expected over next 24 months, driven by India, China, and green steel/JVD interest

items.statement: Consolidated order book executable over 3 years for major projects, 12-18 months for value services
items.quote: Our last project which is a majority of this order book is over three years. We have the value services, which is a smaller portion of this is more kind of revamping or spare parts and this is more over 12 to 18 months. But the vast majority is more over three years.

items.statement: Cost structure gradually aligning from West to East (India and China) to drive operational synergies and margin improvement
items.quote: Going forward, the cost structure is gradually aligning from the West towards India and China, which is expected to drive operational synergies and efficiency improvements over time, improving the margin trajectory.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions in Middle East creating uncertainty in energy markets, logistics, and commodity flows, could lead to short-term volatility
items.quote: At the same time, geopolitical tensions in the Middle East are creating uncertainty across energy markets, logistics, and commodity flows, which could lead to short-term volatility in the industrial sectors globally.

items.statement: Volteron technology ready for commercialization only in recent weeks; strategy under evaluation with promoter who owns IP
items.quote: So Volteron has no revenue yet due to the fact that it is ready for commercialization only since few weeks. items.statement: Novelis long-term EBITDA per ton guidance of $600 remains intact
items.quote: Importantly, our long-term guidance of $600 per ton remains intact, supported by accelerated execution of our $350 million to $400 million structural cost reduction program.

items.statement: Novelis targets $350-400 million structural cost reduction by FY28 exit
items.quote: Back in April 2025, we set an FY26 exit savings run rate target of $75 million, which we raised last quarter to $125 million. With another quarter of solid execution behind us, that run rate is now $200 million as we accelerate all cost efficiency initiatives. Looking ahead, we remain committed to our 3-year goal of permanently reducing our cost structure by $350 million to $400 million by FY 28 e

items.statement: India capex FY27 ~INR12,000 crores; Novelis capex FY27 $2.3-2.4 billion
items.quote: In FY 27, the India capex will be about INR12,000 crores, and the Novelis capex will be between, I think, Dev has already announced on the call about 2.3 billion to 2.4 billion, largely Bay Minette.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt peak expected INR80,000-90,000 crores over next 2 years
items.quote: So consolidated net debt peak should be between INR80,000 crores and INR90,000 crores over the next 2 years.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated capex INR31,619 crores, up 47% YoY
items.quote: At the same time, we continue to invest aggressively in future growth with capital expenditures of INR31,619 crores, up 47% year-on-year.

items.statement: India capex FY28 expected INR15,000-17,000 crores; Novelis capex to drop sharply post Bay Minette
items.quote: India capex, Pinakin, INR 12,000 crores this year, next year will be, I don't know, INR 15,000 crores to INR17,000 crores, but it's not going to be at the same level as Bay Minette was. So, I do think the consol capex of the two will be lower.

items.statement: Aditya Aluminium smelter first 180 pots by Dec 2027, next 180 by Dec 2028
items.quote: So, calendar year December '27, the first 180 pots of Aditya will get commissioned. And calendar year December '28, the next 180 pots of Aditya will get commissioned.

items.statement: Novelis Bay Minette 600 KT greenfield rolling and recycling facility completion this year
items.quote: In parallel, we continue to invest for growth with our 600 KT greenfield rolling and recycling facility at Bay Minette scheduled for completion this year.

items.statement: India upstream aluminium EBITDA $1,756/ton, margin 48% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: This helped us deliver an EBITDA of $1,756 per ton this quarter. EBITDA margins were at 48% and continued to be among the best in the global industry.

items.statement: Novelis adjusted EBITDA $543/ton in Q4 FY26, up 5% YoY
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA for the quarter stood at $498 million or $543 per ton, reflecting a 5% year-on-year.

items.statement: India aluminium cost of production up 2.5% QoQ in Q4; expect 5% increase in Q1 FY27 driven by furnace oil
items.quote: In Q4, the costs were up 2.5%, 2.4% versus Q3. And in Q4, we were just starting to see the impact of the war. So I think in Q1, we are anticipating a 5% increase over Q4, and the majority is driven by furnace oil.

items.statement: Copper EBITDA INR907 crores in Q4 FY26, up 48% YoY, record quarter
items.quote: Our quarterly copper EBITDA stood at a record INR907 crores, up 48% year-on-year on account of better realization in byproducts and operational efficiencies.

items.statement: Sulfuric acid prices up due to Middle East conflict; Q1 prices slightly higher than Q4 but may correct if Strait of Hormuz opens
items.quote: So, Pinakin, the sulfur prices are up largely because of the conflict in the Middle East. So Q1 prices are looking slightly higher than Q4 as well. But I wanted to caution that the moment any Strait of Hormuz opening or thing comes, then you will have to see there will be a correction in the sulfur prices because they're really high right now.

items.statement: India aluminium demand ~1.6 MT in Q4 FY26, up ~9% YoY, broad-based across auto, electrical, packaging
items.quote: In Q4 FY26, aluminium demand is estimated around 1.6 million tons, reflecting an approximately 9% year-on-year growth. This growth remains broad-based, supported by structural drivers in automotive, continued strength in electrical demand and stable packaging demand.

items.statement: India copper demand up 10% YoY to 402 KT in Q4 FY26 driven by infrastructure, electrical, white goods
items.quote: In the domestic copper market demand this quarter, including domestic supply, scrap and imports and imports excluding rose by 10% year-on-year, reaching 402 KT compared to 364 KT in the same period last year.

items.statement: Aluminium hedges FY27: 29% at $3,013/ton; currency 14% at INR90.13/$
items.quote: Our hedged position for aluminium in FY27 stands at around 29% of the commodity at $3,013 per ton and 14% in currency at INR90.13 per $1.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 alumina sales 211 KT; Q1 FY27 expected ~170 KT
items.quote: Yes. The fourth quarter alumina sales were 211 KT, and in Q1, we expect to sell about 170.

items.statement: FY26 operating cash flow INR21,858 crores, up 11% YoY
items.quote: In FY26, our businesses continued to generate healthy cash flows amounting to INR 21,858 crores. This represents a strong 11% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Global growth vulnerable to geopolitical escalation, energy shocks, inflation persistence, financial tightening
items.quote: Global growth remains vulnerable to a combination of geopolitical escalation, energy shocks, inflation persistence and financial tightening with risk reinforcing each other.

items.statement: Renewable capacity 470 MW end FY26; adding 53 MW next quarter; 30 MW storage-based power this quarter taking total to 523 MW by end Q1 FY27
items.quote: At the end of this year, our renewable energy capacity stands at 470 megawatts powered by solar, wind and idle sources. items.statement: INR 500 crore capex planned from FY26 to FY28, with INR 200 crore in FY27

items.quote: Moving to our net working capital. It increased by about 4.6% due to one -off factors and this same is expected to normalize as we move forward.

items.statement: Full year net working capital improved 3.7% YoY
items.quote: For the full year, net working capital improved by 3.7% year-on-year.

items.statement: FY26 cash flow INR 4.05 billion, cash conversion ratio 85%, impacted by demerger one-offs
items.quote: Our cash flow for the year stood at INR 4.05 billion, which represents a cash conversion ratio of about 85%. Cash flow during the year was also impacted by certain one -off factors related to the demerger and these are expected to smoothen as we move forward.

items.statement: EV revenue share: 2W ~6%, PV ~4%; EV product performance much higher than ICE
items.quote: the current 2 -wheeler is about 6% and then the passenger vehicles is about 4%. Krupa, specific to what you mentioned, certainly the performance of the electric vehicle products is much, much higher than the ICE vehicles.

items.statement: Wins driven by OEM redesign for BS-VII and CAFE emission norms
items.quote: The character of the wins that we are having in quarter 1 is reflecting the market shift to EVs as well and the OEMs going back to the drawing board to redesign their drivetrain subsystems to new emission norms that are coming in, mainly the BS-VII and the CAFE norms as well.

items.statement: No pure-play listed automotive bearing peer for benchmarking post-demerger
items.quote: Even if you want to compare, there is not a single listed company, which is bearing purely for automotive. There is no such company exist where we can compare.

items.quote: this is a kind of transition, which is happening, onetime cost sitting here and there slowly, so maybe you may be seeing, but we are very hopeful and we are confident about going forward, maybe after a couple of quarters, we will become stable and we will be back to normal.

items.statement: RACE strategy: portfolio shift to energy efficiency/emission norms, focus on PV/CV premiumization, amplify value selling via R&D partnerships
items.quote: the focus is basically to shift portfolio significantly to energy efficiency and the emission norms addressing value propositions to the customers across vehicle segments. items.statement: Committed to consistent shareholder returns

items.statement: Management emphasizes transparency and investor communication improvement
items.quote: we would like to remain transparent as it was earlier, and we are very committed to that. SKF as a company always value our investors, our customers, our community and everything. So, we have no intention to hide anything.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,450-1,500 crores

items.statement: Yarn capacity utilization at 78% in Q4 FY26 and 77% for FY26
items.quote: The capacity utilization stood at 78% during quarter four FY26 and 77% for the full year.

items.quote: The capacity utilization overall in the Garment business went up to 72% for FY26 compared to maybe 50% or so in FY 2025.

items.statement: Healthy order book supporting Garment division growth
items.quote: The strong performance is supported by a healthy order book, improved execution, and we are hopeful for a strong business momentum towards the final quarter of the new financial year.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 garment demand subdued due to geopolitical developments and raw material costs
items.quote: Recent geopolitical developments and elevated raw material costs have impacted just the near-term demand visibility, particularly in quarter one FY 2027 in our Garment orders. Customers and retail brands continue to remain cautious.

items.statement: Expect garment business momentum to improve from Q2 FY27 onwards
items.quote: While quarter one may remain relatively subdued, we do expect business momentum to improve progressively in the Garment business from the second quarter onwards.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA at INR144 crores, up 22.5% YoY with 11% margin
items.quote: During FY26, our EBITDA stood at approximately INR144 crores with a year-on-year growth of 22.5%, translating into the EBITDA margin of around almost 11%.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA up 46% YoY to INR46 crores

items.statement: Polyester raw material costs up ~25% due to Middle East conflict

items.statement: Wool fiber prices increased sharply, more than synthetic
items.quote: And in particular, the worsted sales has become a little bit more. So, we are seeing that the entire increase in prices of wool, this has been the biggest challenge in terms of the price increases, even more than synthetic, the wool prices have increased even more.

items.statement: Price pass-through lag of 6-12 months for wool cost increases

items.statement: Targeting 70% revenue contribution from Fabric and Garment over medium-term

items.statement: Debt-to-equity ratio comfortable at 0.8x as of March 31, 2026

items.statement: Long-term debt reduction expected from FY28 onwards

items.statement: One-time exceptional expense of INR9 crores for new labor code implementation

As far as the commodity is concerned, yes, there is a

items.statement: Royal Enfield grew ~37% in April; top 10 cities grew ~24%+; rural growth continues; urban also showing growth after income tax savings
items.quote: In fact, in the month of April, we grew by almost about 37%. That's what I mentioned. And if I have to tell you about top 10 cities, in top 10 cities, we have grown almost about 24% plus. And even in the rural market, the growth is continuing.

items.statement: First-time buyers increasing; 30% of consumers below age 25; replacement cycle yet to kick in but growing double-digit on low base
items.quote: First-time buyers are going up. In fact, as I mentioned, 30% of our consumers are below the age group of 25. So the first-time buyer percentage is also going up.

items.statement: Current declared capacity 1.4 million; adding 500 per day module from July to reach ~1.6 million for festive season
items.quote: Our capacity declared was about 1.4 million, and we said with the 500 module, which we started off anticipating the growth, that's going to kick in from July because we had to be prepared for festive season. So, with that, our capacity will go to almost about 1.6 million.

items.statement: INR 958 crore investment started in April to expand Cheyyar facility from 1.6M to ~2M capacity by Q2 FY28
items.quote: The investment which was also clear INR958 crores in April, that has started, and that will take us the overall capacity in phases to 2 million for future because the growth momentum is continuing.

items.statement: Greenfield project MoU signed for 261 acres in Andhra Pradesh; new plant expected fully operational in 24-30 months for capacity beyond 2 million
items.quote: Typically, it will be somewhere around 24 to 30 months window, that's where we will come out with a new plant fully operational.

items.statement: Focus remains on 250-750cc middleweight segment across 350cc, 450cc, 650cc platforms; Bullet 650 dispatch started; Flying Flea S6 and other EICMA products on track
items.quote: A bullet 650 is on the cards. It's just going to come because that I can share it with you because the dispatch is already started. Remaining products, you will see one by one, which will come into the market.

items.statement: Flying Flea electric launched in Bangalore single store; City/City Plus won Red Dot Award; media reviews very positive; city-by-city rollout planned
items.quote: Our electric mobility products, which is Flying Flea during this quarter, we actually launched and it's a City, City Plus motorcycle, which won the Red Dot Award even before it was even launched, we have launched the product. Now booking has just started.

items.statement: Brazil grew ~71% YoY; now #2 in middleweight; Guerrilla 450 won Motorcycle of the Year; Himalayan 450 won Style Bike of the Year; Bear 650 launched in March; focusing Brazil as next big market after India
items.quote: In fact, last year, we grew by almost 71% compared to the previous year. And in Brazil, we have become the number 2 in the middleweight and our product, Guerrilla 450 has won the motorcycle of the year.

items.statement: Europe degrowing; maintaining share in degrowing market; OBD2B pre-registered vehicles not yet cleared; cautiously optimistic on international overall
items.quote: Europe continued to degrow. In a degrowing market, we are maintaining our market share. But I must tell you, in Europe, I call it as market adjustment year.

items.statement: Vehicle financing JV with Volvo Financial Services formed; up to INR 750 crore capital infusion; existing net worth ~INR 500 crore; debt-equity ~3x; target AUM INR 9,000-10,000 crore in 5 years; no further capital needed for 5 years
items.quote: We are now going to put up to INR750 crores into the balance sheet and they already have net worth of around INR500 crores and their current debt equity is only around 3. So with INR750 crores -- up to INR750 crores additional and existing net worth and in the finance companies, if you can go up to debt equity of 5 is to 1. I think we are adequately capitalized for the medium term.

items.statement: VECV announced ~2% price increases from 1st April to offset 3-3.5% commodity inflation; also pursuing value engineering, commodity optimization, transaction price improvement
items.quote: We also announced appropriate price increases for that, which is to tune of 2% various vehicles. So that has been announced from 1st April. And we also work on a lot of initiatives of cost reduction, whether it is value engineering, whether it is optimizing the commodity use and also improving the transaction prices in the market.

items.statement: Commodity pressure expected 3-3.5% in Q1 and similar for year; supply disruptions from elections, manpower, LPG, commodity, power issues now settling
items.quote: I think the commodity pressure is exactly same as what Govind has mentioned. I think we are sailing the same boat. So, which is expected to be in the range of 3% to 3.5% and that's in the first quarter. So that continue to be in the similar lines for the year.

items.statement: Labour shortages due to election-related migrant worker movement and LPG availability caused 2-3 week production disturbance in both businesses; production numbers now recovering
items.quote: Two things I think in both the businesses, we are also hearing more from that is because of the election there is migrated workmen movement from here and there. That has caused a disturbance and LPG availability was causing an issue. Things are settling down. As I mentioned, it was almost about 2, 3 weeks disturbance were in both the businesses.

items.statement: VECV sees good market traction; no formal FY27 forecast yet; April industry sales extremely well; consumer sentiment good; diesel price hikes passed through via indexing
items.quote: As far as demand is concerned, I think there is no forecast expected at this moment. But however, right now, the traction in the market is quite good.

items.statement: VECV electric bus portfolio covers 9m, 12m, 13.5m for public and private demand; reasonably good order book; competing for emerging orders
items.quote: We are there in 9 meter, we are there 12 meter, we are there in 13.5 meter buses. It covers a large spectrum of buses Eicher Motors Limited May 22, 2026 which are required, both public and the private demand. And we go by the current order book, our current demand, but we have a reasonably good order book business right now

items.statement: Royal Enfield expanded to ~400 cities, ~710 dealerships; digital platform for replacement traction showing double-digit growth on low base
items.quote: In the last year, if I have to tell you, we have gone to almost about 400 cities, about 710 dealerships. We have created a digital platform, the traction is slightly better. If I had to tell you in terms of growth, it's in double digit, but it is still the base is lower.

items.statement: Tariff issues/confusions in US (~3% of market) getting settled; Europe degrowth continues; cautiously optimistic on international markets
items.quote: Currently, what is happening in the macro, most of the markets, especially United States, you all know, and there are tariff issues, confusions, which are all getting settled, but that's only about 3% of the total market for us.

items.statement: Digital business achieved positive EBITDA in FY26, meeting guidance given at start of year
items.quote: With a balanced cost structure, it resulted in delivering a positive EBITDA in FY26 compared to a loss of INR5,480 million in the previous year. This also marked the first year in which our digital business has delivered a positive EBITDA on a comparable basis, achieving the guidance which we had given at the start of the year.

items.statement: Digital revenue grew 71% YoY in Q4 FY26 to INR4,700 million, highest ever quarterly revenue
items.quote: We witnessed continued momentum in our revenues, which grew 71% year-on-year basis for Q4 FY26 to INR4,700 million. This quarter has also marked our highest ever revenues in the digital business.

items.statement: ZEE5 achieved breakeven in FY26, operationally profitable for second quarter in a row with 53% YoY growth
items.quote: I'm glad to share that ZEE5 achieved breakeven during the previous fiscal. The platform was operationally profitable for the second quarter in a row, delivering 53% year-on-year growth in FY26.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin stood at 6.9% in Q4 FY26, would have been similar to Q3 excluding one-offs and lower ad revenue
items.quote: With a 7% decline in operating revenue and optimizing our other fixed costs during the quarter, our adjusted EBITDA margin stood at 6.9%. Further, we had higher costs due to legal expenses in quarter 4. Excluding these one-offs and lower advertising revenue on account of the Middle East conflict, our margins would have been similar to quarter 3.

items.statement: Full year FY26 EBITDA margin finished at 8-9%, management aims to improve towards high teens over time
items.quote: We have finished at 8%, 9% on the full year basis. Start of the year, we had ambitious plans on the margin front, but what needs to change? And how do we get to that high teens' kind of a margin, if at all?

items.statement: Content inventory advances and deposits stood at INR67.6 billion as of March 2026, down INR2.8 billion YoY
items.quote: As a result of the above and optimized fresh acquisitions, the content inventory advances and deposits as of March '26 stood at INR67.6 billion, down by INR2.8 billion on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Board approved investment of INR20 crores in CORE Private Limited for Live business and up to INR116 crores in Phantom Digital Effects Limited for AVGC capabilities
items.value: INR20 crores and up to INR116 crores
items.quote: Firstly, an investment of INR20 crores was approved in respect of CORE Private Limited, CORE stands for Culture of Real Experiences. So, this will help drive our Live business. Secondly, an investment of up to INR116 crores was also approved, as Punit mentioned, in Phantom Digital Effects Limited.

items.statement: Revised pricing strategy for digital business aided improved performance alongside enhanced content offering across 7 languages
items.quote: The enhanced content offering across 7 languages, coupled with revised pricing strategy aided in an all-round improved performance.

items.statement: Digital offerings more than doubled with over 120 shows and movies released including 34 originals across 7 languages
items.quote: Our digital offerings were more than doubled by releasing over 120 shows and movies, including 34 originals. The enhanced content offering across 7 languages, coupled with revised pricing strategy aided in an all-round improved performance.

items.statement: Monthly unique reach crossed 800 million across platforms as part of omnichannel strategy
items.quote: Further, I'm pleased to inform you that as a part of our omnichannel strategy, ZEE's monthly unique reach has crossed 800 million across platforms.

items.statement: Advertising revenue declined 4% YoY in Q4 due to Middle East conflict impacting March spends, would have been low single digit growth otherwise
items.quote: On the advertising front, we did witness healthy traction in the initial months of Jan and Feb. However, March was severely impacted with the ongoing Middle East conflict where advertisers have held back their spends in the end of the quarter. As a result, our overall advertising revenues declined 4% year-on-year.

items.statement: Network share increased 80 basis points to 17.4% in Q4 FY26, Zee TV GRP growth 40% YoY with 21% stronger performance than closest competitor for 26 weeks
items.quote: The positive outcome of this strategy reflects in our network share, which increased by 80 basis points to touch 17.4% during the quarter. Our flagship Hindi GEC, Zee TV continued to display robust GRP growth of 40%. Strong character-led storytelling, coupled with culturally rooted narratives enabled the channel to garner peak engagement during the prime-time slots.

items.statement: Changed movie rights amortization policy from straight-line over 5 years to 50% in first 2 years and balance 50% over next 3 years, resulting in INR4,084 million charge
items.quote: We've had a look at the various patterns of consumption, and we have changed that estimate to make it more front-ended to increase it to 50% in the first 2 years and then the balance in the next 3 years. So that's the impact which we have taken, which is reflected in the notes.

items.statement: Provision for doubtful debts of around INR70 crores made on conservative basis at year-end based on age of debtors, considered collectible
items.quote: These are made on a conservative basis, Umang, and they are all collectible, but we make these provisions especially at the end of the year, taking into account the age of the debtors and receivables, and we make these provisions. And they will be collected subsequently.

items.statement: Cash and treasury investments stood at INR27.6 billion as of March 2026 comprising cash, fixed deposits, and mutual funds
items.quote: Cash and treasury investments as of March 2026 stood at a healthy INR27.6 billion, comprising of cash balance of INR7.5 billion, fixed deposits and other treasury investments of INR7.8 billion and mutual fund investments of INR12.3 billion.

items.statement: Employee cost down 16% in Q4 and 9% for full year FY26 through manpower optimization and omnichannel strategy, targeting pre-pandemic 9% people cost to revenue ratio
items.quote: As Mukund mentioned in his speech that we have done a lot of optimization in manpower through our omnichannel strategy. A lot of people have taken on a lot more responsibility towards achieving their KPIs and all those things. So that's how we've opti mized it. If you go back 4, 5 years before the pandemic, we used to operate at 9% people cost to revenue, and we are trying to bring it back to that

items.statement: West Asia crisis and geopolitical uncertainty impacting advertiser sentiment and consumer spending in near term
items.quote: The uncertain geopolitical environment and macroeconomic headwinds disrupted consumer sentiments during the quarter. The continuing ambiguity in the global economic landscape is a result of the conflict in the Middle East, and that has impacted overall growth across sectors and the industry at large.

items.statement: Music business garnered over 217 billion total video views with 176 million YouTube subscribers, driven by new age catalog and 20,000+ song library
items.quote: During the year, we have garnered over 217 billion total video views with more than 176 million subscribers on YouTube. This performance was driven by our new age music catalog and a rich library of over 20,000 songs.

items.statement: Digital advertising revenue growing extremely handsomely quarter-on-quarter and YoY, moving toward 50-50 balance with subscription in medium term
items.quote: the good news, which is what I can tell you is it continues to grow extremely handsomely on a quarter-on-quarter basis, and it is moving into the territory of us with our aspiration of becoming ad and subscription more like balance of 50-50 in the medium term.

items.statement: Open to value unlocking for music business through demerger or strategic partnership if right offer comes, but currently focused on expanding catalog
items.quote: No. As I mentioned in my opening remarks and in the earlier question somebody asked me that if I get the right offer, why would I not be open to considering and demerging Zee Music from ZEE to a separate entity and bringing in a strategic partner there. Why not?

items.statement: Micro-Drama app Bullet gaining steady traction with gamified viewing experience, market size estimated at INR3,000-3,500 crores
items.quote: I believe that already the Micro-Drama market or short-form content market has reached almost, correct me, Mukund if I'm wrong, INR3,000 to INR3,500 crores.

items.statement: Live events business opportunity estimated at INR50,000 crores in organized segment, complementing current business with talent marketing and advertising synergies
items.quote: In live events business on an organized manner, in our estimate is close to INR50,000 crores in this country. And I'm not even including the segment, which is your B2B and what happens in small towns and all those things.

items.statement: No specific FY27 margin guidance given, but management optimistic about improvement once macro stabilizes, focusing on revenue growth with cost prudence
items.quote: Once the current macroeconomic environment stabilizes, our focus will continue to remain on driving revenue growth while maintaining a cost prudence, ai ding operating leverage, resulting in profitability improvement and cash generation

items.statement: ZEE5 at optimum investment level, may increase slightly but not enough to impact EBITDA line significantly
items.quote: I believe that we are at optimum level of investments on the ZEE5 or the digital front. At some point in time, we may choose to up our investments, but they will not move the needle to the extent that it will start impacting our EBITDA line.

items.statement: Subscription revenue grew 4% YoY primarily driven by digital business
items.quote: Moving to subscription revenues , i t has registered a 4% year -on-year growth, primarily driven by our digital business

items.quote: During the quarter, we released 13 movies, 7 in Hindi and 6 in other languages, of which 9 were our own productions and 4 were distribution deals.
