items.quote: at least in the first 2 years, we are clearly seeing growth of around 15% in a single year

items.statement: Domestic stationery revenue growth expected at ~15% in FY27 including new category launches
items.quote: In domestic stationery business, we are expecting growth of 1 -5, 15%, including our new category in launches that we have already done so far

items.statement: Export stationery revenue growth guided at high single-digit 8-9% for FY27 due to global uncertainty
items.quote: I would say single higher-digit growth will be an estimation, around 8% to 9%.

items.statement: Stationery segment EBITDA margin expected ~9% in FY27 and 9.5-10% in FY28 after brand investments
items.quote: So we should be making around 9% margin in the current year post these expenses. And in the subsequent year, around 9.5% to 10%

items.statement: Publication EBIT margin expected to improve by at least 200 bps in FY27 vs FY26 due to double-digit revenue growth
items.quote: there will be at least 200 basis points better margin than the current year -- than the last year

items.statement: Capex for FY27-28 limited to INR25-30 crores at India level; UAE project on hold
items.quote: at a company level in India level -- at India level, at present, we don't have big plans to invest either in land building or in machinery. So it would be just hardly INR25 crores, INR30 crores of investments

items.statement: Paper stationery capacity utilization ~80% annually; non-paper to be outsourced initially except plastic products from new Gujarat plant
items.quote: On paper capacity, I would say we are quite highly utilized. So on an annual basis, I can say around 80%

items.statement: South Gujarat plant invested INR65 crores including land; asset turnover expected 1x in year 1, 2x in year 2, 2.5x thereafter
items.quote: altogether, we have invested INR65 crores, including buying of a land

items.statement: Export stationery EBITDA margin compressed 3% in FY26 due to US tariffs; deliberate price cuts to protect market share
items.quote: our export stationery revenue saw a 10% decline, which compressed our divisional EBITDA margin by 3%

items.statement: Domestic stationery margins to be impacted short-to-medium term by INR30 cr (FY27) and INR40 cr (FY28) brand spend under YOUVA
items.quote: in the first year, we have planned around INR30 crore s the brand expense. And in the subsequent year, around INR40-odd crores to spend on brand

items.statement: Paper prices jumped ~8% from lows in Q4 FY26; further increases uncertain due to competitive pressure
items.quote: the paper that we use in last 1 quarter, we have seen around 8% jump from its lowest level that it had gone down last year

items.statement: GST exemption on paper stationery prevented input tax credit claims on inventory and vendor confusion for ~2 months
items.quote: paper stationery became exempt from GST. So it prevented us claiming the input tax credit on the inventory that we were holding as on that date as well as in the initial almost 2 months of period

items.statement: Scaling up higher-margin non-paper stationery portfolio and expanding digital commerce footprint
items.quote: we are rapidly scaling up our better margin non-paper stationery products as a portfolio and expanding our footprint in digital commerce

items.statement: Export customers are large and negotiate pricing considering currency moves; volume guaranteed but margin expansion not allowed
items.quote: our customers are quite big, smart. They also understand the currency fluctuations and currency rates of the respective country. So when they negotiate i n the subsequent years, they always consider -- keep these currency rates also in mind

items.statement: Intense pricing pressure from unorganized regional players in domestic stationery; brand investment to build moat
items.quote: intense pricing pressure from unorganized regional players

items.statement: Curriculum changes confirmed in Maharashtra and Gujarat starting FY27 over 3-4 years; new books already in market
items.quote: both respective state governments have announced and accordingly, the new curriculum books have already started coming in the market

items.statement: Indiannica merger with Navneet filed; awaiting authority approvals to realize cost synergies from overlapping sales, tech, content, logistics
items.quote: we have decided to merge it with Navneet and the major reason being that a lot of cost that are duplicated at both the locations and both the companies individually gets reduced

items.statement: Combined CBSE revenue (Navneet + Indiannica) ~INR65 crores in FY26 vs ~INR70 crores in FY25
items.quote: So it's about INR65 crores at present

items.statement: Indiannica FY26 net sales INR42 crores, PAT loss INR16 crores; revenue down from INR55 crores due to halted new product development and higher returns
items.quote: Indiannica had a net sale of INR48 crores -- sorry, INR42 crores for the year, and it had a negative profit of -- loss at PAT level at INR16 crores

items.statement: Global inflation in developed markets may reduce export growth by 5-7% on conservative basis
items.quote: we all may discount by around 5% to 7% impact, which we have to reduce from our growth expectation on a conservative basis

items.statement: UAE manufacturing project on hold due to geopolitical tensions; limited investment to date
items.quote: have kept it on hold due to ongoing geopolitical tensions. So very limited investment has gone till date

items.statement: Three buybacks done in last 5 years; may consider again at right time
items.quote: in last 5 years, we have already done, if I am not wrong, around 3 buybacks already in the last 3 -- 5 years. At the right time, we will -- we may again decide on the same

items.statement: One-time provision for leave encashment due to new labor law impacted H2 FY26 margins; positive impact expected Q1 FY27
items.quote: we have created a provision for leave encashment, so that has also created some negative impact on our margins

items.statement: Domestic stationery volume grew 6% in FY26 despite 4% value growth due to paper price declines and GST exemption
items.quote: we have achieved a volume growth of 6%. This growth was achieved despite a downtrend or downward trend in the paper prices

items.statement: Transitioning from curriculum provider to diversified digital/AI and non-paper stationery consumer brand
items.quote: we are transitioning from just a curriculum provider through textbooks or through paper to various areas of digital AI as well as stationery, including non-paper

items.statement: Internal target for FY27 revenue growth is upwards of 20% and closer to 30% if all goes well
items.quote: our targets internally are to remain in this, you know, on the lower side also, upwards of 20, and closer to 30, if all goes well.

items.statement: 5-year internal target aims to return to 30%+ PAT growth levels in a more structured and sustainable manner
items.quote: we want Produced & transcribed by - 16 - that our, you know, over the next 5-year period, our growth levels come back to those 30-plus kind of numbers

items.statement: FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin expanded ~250 bps to 22.9% driven by better realisations, improved product mix, operating leverage and cost discipline
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded by around 250 basis points to 22.9%, which demonstrates that growth was supported by better realisations, improved product mix, operating leverage and continued cost discipline.

items.statement: Contacts business revenue grew ~60% in FY26; ~31-32% was actual volume growth, rest was silver price pass-through with minimal margin impact
items.quote: if we have, an approximate growth of about... roughly about 60% on revenue basis in the contacts business, out of which nearly about 31 or 32 is actual business growth

items.statement: Q4 FY26 standalone gross margin improved 329 bps YoY to 49% from 46%
items.quote: the quarter-to-quarter, we have improved by 329 BPS, as for the standalone result. So, there is no decline in gross margin. Gross margin earlier in quarter 4- 2025 was 46%, which grew by 49%.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin declined QoQ due to higher revenue share of contacts business which has lower gross margin because of precious metal raw material input
items.quote: the contact's revenue has grown more as a percentage, as compared to the other product, so that's why it's, probably showing in a consolidated basis.

items.statement: Shunt revenue from energy meters grew 33% to ~70 crore in FY26; contact portion of smart meter relays expected to grow significantly in FY27 as new capacity comes online
items.quote: almost 33% growth in shunt, from the energy meters, which is around, 70 crore odd rupees.

items.statement: US key customer (shunt resistors) revenue expected to return to peak levels in FY27 and surpass in FY28; all new business in higher-margin component form
items.quote: we expect that in this year and the year after, we expect numbers to reach, and then probably in the year after that, to go beyond what its highest numbers were when we used to supply those larger volumes of strip two or three years ago to them.

items.statement: US customer revenue concentration peaked at 38-39%, fell to 13-14%, expected to stabilize at 16-18% as component volumes recover
items.quote: From its peak, it's come down from nearly 38-39%, It came down to about 13-14%. And now, when it goes back to those levels, it will come back to an 18-19% level, at the most.

items.statement: Pune facility Phase 1 nearly complete for PCBA and busbar assemblies; revenue potential of 250-350 crore in 2-3 years from this standalone unit
items.quote: we expect that this standalone unit, this new standalone unit could bring in revenues, you know, anywhere in the 250 to 350 crore, range.

items.statement: No substantial growth capex required beyond maintenance and automation capex of 10-15 crore per year; existing capacity supports 1300 crore revenue
items.quote: We have enough capacity in all three segments, and that will continue.

items.statement: Current consolidated capacity utilization ~60% on practical basis (theoretical ~43-45%); expected to reach 75-80% in FY27 without incremental capex
items.quote: even at that point, we should be at about, maybe around 75%, 80%, - 75% of our capacity utilization, assuming we haven't done those incremental capex.

items.statement: Contacts division added capacity in new plant over last 7-8 months; was capacity constrained for 1.5-2 years during construction
items.quote: We have moved into a new plant. That plant has been, you know, sort of partially ready for the last 7 or 8 months, so we've added some capacity.

items.statement: Shunt realization per kg improved 10-12% as component mix shifted from 55% to 65% of supply
items.quote: earlier we used to supply regarding 55% in component, which goes up to 65% in year-on-year. And that is yielding almost 10-12% improved realization, as per the previous, per kg shunt realization.

items.statement: Silver price surge in last 5-6 months of FY26 contributed ~21-22% to contacts revenue growth; minimal margin impact due to low silver content and surcharge mechanism
items.quote: out of this, nearly 21, 22%, or so is simply because of the precious metal jumping extremely high in, to high levels in the last, 5 or 6 months of the financial year.

items.statement: Strategy shifting from strip-led supply to engineered components and assemblies; standalone revenue grew despite stable volumes due to better average realization
items.quote: On a standalone basis, revenue grew despite broadly stable product volumes, indicating better average realisation and increasing contribution from higher-value components.

items.statement: EB-welded busbars/CCS for 2W EVs offer safety and copper savings; premium pricing sustainable due to 5-6 year technology barrier and safety criticality
items.quote: our EB-welded bus bars are actually acting, providing an extra layer of security. On top of that, what it does is also saves on certain materials.

items.statement: Europe thermostatic bimetal strong traction from deeper engagement via local presence; US developments restarted after tariff-driven pause
items.quote: Europe delivered strong traction, supported by deeper customer engagement from our local presence and export momentum.

items.statement: EMS Bimetal (US division of German parent) not bankrupt but shifting capacity; Shivalik gaining share from their supply disruptions to marquee customers
items.quote: they have not been able to supply properly to some of their old marquee customers as a result of that, and that is where an opportunity for Shivalik arises.

items.statement: Inventory days elevated due to Pune PCB assembly copper consumption and geopolitical supply safeguarding; domestic sourcing development in second stage to reduce import dependency
items.quote: this inventory level has gone up due to this, Pune, or the additional PCB assembly business, where we are consuming copper at large.

items.statement: No specific debt metrics discussed; focus on converting growth into stronger cash generation in FY27
items.quote: focus on converting growth into a stronger cash generation.

items.statement: Metallor JV converted to 100% subsidiary in 2023 after partner exited parent business; no longer a JV
items.quote: this is no longer a JV, it's a 100% subsidiary of Shivalik, and this used to be a JV until 2023

items.statement: Shunt component mix increased from 55% to 65% of supply, driving 10-12% per kg realization improvement
items.quote: earlier we used to supply regarding 55% in component, which goes up to 65% in year-on-year. And that is yielding almost 10-12% improved realization

items.statement: Smart meter growth considered bonus, not core growth story; could plateau in 4-7 quarters if installation slows to <50% of plan
items.quote: growth coming from smart meters good, or bad,- we consider it to be more of a bonus for us, and we don't want to rely or make our growth story, as I mentioned in the previous question also, related to any one particular industry

items.statement: Management confident of improved top-line and bottom-line in FY27 subject to no further Middle East conflict impact
items.quote: I am further confident of an improved result both in top-line and bottom-line in FY'27.

items.statement: Order backlog stood at approximately INR593 crores as of March 2026
items.quote: As of March 2026, our order backlog stood at approximately INR593 crores, and we recorded an order inflow of almost INR990 crores in FY'26.

items.statement: Cumulative capex of INR27 crores incurred in FY26 with additional INR10 crores planned for FY27
items.quote: We have incurred a cumulative capex of INR27 crores in FY'26 and plan to close FY'27 with an additional capex of around INR10 crores.

items.statement: Quickmill plant expansion planned at approximately CAD 4 million (INR25-30 crores) pending municipal permissions

items.statement: Vyom Agarwal (President) participated in call; no management changes mentioned

items.quote: Most probably we should be hopeful that it would get back in the range of anywhere between INR20 crores to INR35 crores, right Luthra?

items.statement: Impairment losses on financial assets reflect expected credit loss provisions on slightly delayed receivables, not actual losses

So as a prudent accounting policy, actually, this is not a real loss, but we have to be provided keeping in view the -- any expectation or any risk coming going forward.

items.statement: Defense NOC approvals received; rough terrain forklift/telehandler execution to start next quarter; QRSAM missile program prototype work underway for material handling (not firing systems)

items.quote: As intimated to you in the Q3 call, we had signed the SPA for purchase of an EPC signaling business based out of New Delhi, Alcon Builders and Engineers Private Limited at a cash consideration of INR151.83 crores.

items.quote: In the current Board meeting, the Board has also approved a draft scheme of amalgamation of Alcon with GPT and also one of our earlier erstwhile subsidiaries, Jogbani Highway Private Limited, so as to fully integrate the business with the parent and also provide them the enhanced network and other credentials to bid for larger contracts.

items.statement: Highest ever annual order inflow of INR2,422 crores in FY26, surpassing INR2,000 crores projection; total order book stands at INR4,476 crores, approximately 3.5x FY26 revenues

We achieved our highest ever annual order inflow of INR2,422 crores, surpassing our projections of INR2,000 crores for the year. Our total order book stands at INR4,476 crores, which is approximately 3.5 times our FY '26 revenues.

items.statement: Key order wins include INR1,201 crores Northern Railway rail-cum-road bridge (40% share = INR481 crores) and INR1,805 crores MCGM flyover (26% share = INR470 crores)

items.statement: Secured first HAM contract in Rajasthan for Jodhpur elevated bypass from NHAI, contract value INR669 crores, 51% share in SPV

This marks GPT Infra's entry into the HAM segment, which further diversifies our project portfolio and strengthens our positioning in the road and highway space.

items.statement: Commercially operationalized Ghana facility with first supply and invoice in March 2026; started steel girder fabrication factory in Singur, West Bengal with ~10,000 tons per annum capacity, looking to enhance further

As also intimated to you earlier, during the year, we have also started a factory for fabrication of steel girders in Singur in West Bengal with a capacity of almost 10,000 tons per annum. And we are also looking at enhancing that capacity further.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of 100% (INR 10 per share), ~40% payout on PAT
items.quote: The Board has recommended a final dividend of 100%, which means INR10 per share and approximately 40% payout on our PAT, reflecting our commitment to sharing profits -- sharing wealth and profits with shareholders.

items.statement: Tax Services revenue grew 17.5% to INR 498 crores with 59% market share, issued 4.7 crore PAN cards
items.quote: Our Tax Services business continued to deliver strong performance during the year with revenue growing 17.5% year-on-year to INR 498 crores. We continue to maintain our leadership in this segment with a 59% market share, issuing more than 4.7 crore PAN cards during FY26.

items.statement: CRA Services revenue grew 7.5% to INR 304 crores
items.quote: Our CRA Service business continues to show resilient growth with FY26 revenue growing by 7.5% to INR 304 crores.

items.statement: Identity Services revenue at INR 92 crores with volume growth across foundational ID products
items.quote: Coming to Identity Services segment, revenue for FY26 stood at INR 92 crores. We continue to see volume growth across most foundational ID products.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated revenue INR 998 crores (19% YoY), EBITDA INR 188 crores (27% YoY), margin 17.6%
items.quote: During the year, the company delivered consolidated revenue from operation of INR 998 crores, which is the highest in the history of the company, registering a healthy growth of 19% Y-o-Y. EBITDA for FY26 stood at INR 188 crores as against INR 149 crores in FY25, which reflects a robust growth of 27% on a Y-o-Y basis. EBITDA margin expanded by 125 basis points to 17.6%.

items.statement: Acquired 4.95% stake in NSDL Payments Bank for INR 30.2 crores
items.quote: During the year, we acquired 4.95% of strategic stake in NSDL Payments Bank with an investment of INR 30.2 crores.

items.statement: Geopolitical situation causing slowdown in international business decision-making
items.quote: the current geopolitical situation happening around Middle East and some part of the world, there has been a slight slowdown, which we have seen in this month, but we hope that this will start picking up

items.statement: PFRDA introduced reforms including NPS Sanchay to improve pension inclusion for informal sector
items.quote: During the year, PFRDA introduced several progressive reforms aimed at improving pension inclusion and accessibility. Initiatives such as NPS Sanchay are expected to significantly improve participation from India's informal sector, which constitutes nearly 90% of total workforce.

items.statement: Bima Sugam platform in WIP stage, health and motor products mandated to go live in 3-4 months
items.quote: The mandate from the regulator for that to happen is within the next 3 to 4 months and this needs to be done prior to that.

items.statement: CRA charge revision may dip margins short-term but accretive long-term as AUM grows
items.quote: In short run, we see some dip in margins. But in long run, I think it will help industry and company because the charges become dynamic with your AMC growing, your subscriber base growing, you will get more and more revenues.

items.statement: Employee cost to increase with ~2,000 hires for 190 Aadhaar Seva Kendras
items.quote: What I can say is we will add about 2,000-odd employees for these Aadhaar centers. These are mostly entry-level jobs or those kind of people.

items.statement: Storage charges INR 44 crores recognized in Q4 for 2-3 years of document storage
items.quote: This INR 44 crore is for 2 to 3 years. As I said, because of collectibility, we recognize revenue only on the receipt basis.

items.statement: International revenue from Ethiopia agri platform and Africa DPI engagements
items.quote: there are certain wins which we have already got, on the agri business in Ethiopia and those revenues will start flowing in. O ther parts are all going on. There are a lot of engagements happening in various places across Africa

items.statement: PAN 2.0 distribution model expected to continue for 1.5 years, no change in position
items.quote: We believe that the same model for our kind of demographics and geographies stand a very good chance to keep continuing. This is what during last quarter also, the assessment that we had, and we continue to believe the same.

items.statement: Data Stack products (eSignPro, RISE, KYC) showing healthy traction with revenue expected in 2-3 quarters
items.quote: At least in next 2-3 quarters, we see a very good amount of revenue should come from these data products, which is either eSign Pro or RISE with Protean or Protean or some of those new age initiatives.

items.statement: Management expects mid-single-digit growth in FY27 and flat store count with ~20 new stores and ~20 closures

items.quote: FY27 may be slightly lower, may be around 23%, 24% because the marketing spend is going to go up in the next year.

items.statement: Gross margin expected to remain in 56-58% range but uncertain due to raw material costs

items.statement: Capex per new store is INR 40-45 lakhs depending on location and format
items.quote: So, capex per store is around INR40 lakhs to INR45 lakhs depending on the location and whether it is high street or mall.

items.statement: Plan to open ~20 new Mufti 2.0 stores and close ~20 underperforming stores in FY27, keeping store count flat
items.quote: We are looking to open about 20 new stores and also shut down approximately 20-odd stores which are underperforming during the year.

items.quote: No, no, they can pass on the price. It's not on a fixed price. It's the overall latency and the demand in the brand that is able to absorb the cost rises, etcetera, that happen, and we are able to pass them on to the customers.

items.quote: And it is very unpredictable going forward. But these are very difficult to predict today whether it will be 56% to 58% or it could even go down to 55%.

items.quote: In the current situation in West Asia, we are still able to derive a utilization in the range of 85% to 90% and a yield which is upwards of 4.5%.

items.statement: 50% of clients provide free fuel supply; for balance 50%, advanced discussions underway for price increase to pass on diesel cost
items.quote: No. So 50% of our clients give us free supply of fuel. And for the balance 50%, we are already in advanced stage of discussions with the client for a price increase.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA margin 40.1% in FY26; core crane rental maintains high EBITDA margin while renewables E&C is asset-light, high ROCE (~70%), lower EBITDA margin business
items.quote: The core business has still grown at 30% and has contributed significantly to both the EBITDA and the PAT and all the other financial ratios. The incremental growth beyond 30% in terms of the top line, which has allowed the company cross and historical revenue of INR 1,100 crores is coming from the new business engine, which was carved out in 2024 as a wholly owned subsidiary Sangreen Future Renew

items.statement: KSA EBITDA profile benchmarked at 40-45%; management targets 45-48% through technical operating efficiency and lean cost structure
items.quote: But we believe because of our 3.5 years -- of decades, our technical operating and efficiency factors that we can deliver in the country and our capability to operate as a leaner cost structure, we can push that EBITDA profile to 45% to 48%.

items.statement: India wind capacity addition 6.1 GW in FY26 (46% YoY); trajectory to 100 GW by 2030 and 156 GW by 2036; company delivered 2 GW of 6 GW added
items.quote: India added a record 6.1 gigawatt of wind capacity in FY26 alone, and that's a massive 46% jump over the previous year. Total capacity stands at 56 gigawatts, and we have the clear trajectory to 100 gigawatts by 2030.

items.statement: KSA crane rental market estimated at INR 1 billion with INR 2 trillion investment pipeline; inquiry pipeline of $50 million over 24 months
items.quote: KSA's infrastructure sector is witnessing a strong momentum with the crane rental market estimated at around INR 1 billion, supported by massive INR 2 trillion investment pipeline. We have built a strong revenue visibility with a pipeline of around INR 50 million over the next 24 months.

items.statement: Net debt INR 612 crores, net debt-to-equity 0.47x, average borrowing cost 8.12%; leverage to increase slightly due to capex but maintained below 0.5x historically
items.quote: As of 31 March 2026, net debt stood at INR 612 crores with a net debt-to-equity ratio of 0.47x, reflecting a comfortable leverage position. The average cost of borrowing remained stable at 8.12% per annum with net worth stood at INR 1,310 crores.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity to increase slightly due to recent capex but will be maintained at certain levels; historically managed below 0.5x
items.quote: So you have seen that in last 5 years, we are able to manage below 0.5%. But we are doing more capex in recent years, and we have planned to do it. So definitely, it will go up, but we'll maintain it at certain levels.

items.statement: Engineering & Construction business working capital cycle 50-60 days; very high ROCE due to asset-light model
items.quote: capital days is around ranging 50 to 60 days in this business for Engineering & Construction. And what about... Pradeep Mehta: Ratios. Pradeep Mehta: Ratios, on ROCE, is improving like we again earlier call -- in the call already that these are very high ratio on ROCE side as compared to other business because this is a less capital - intensive business

items.statement: FY26 revenue mix: crane rental 65%, renewables 31%, project EPC 4%; renewables revenue doubled YoY
items.quote: In terms of segment contribution for FY26, the crane rental business contributed 65% of operating revenue and the renewables segment accounted for 31% and the project EPC contributed remaining 4%.

items.statement: Wind E&C revenue doubled FY25 to FY26; company selective on contracts to maintain healthy margin profile; opportunity exceeds current delivery capacity
items.quote: Our revenue for FY '24-'25 to '25-'26 has almost doubled. We believe that in the coming years, there is a sizable opportunity in this segment. And we will take in through those orders that we believe will help us maintain a minimum threshold in terms of profitability as well as coupled with our ability to execute and deliver.

items.statement: KSA customers are regional/country-specific contractors (shutdown, EPC); no Indian clients currently working in Saudi
items.quote: As far as the customers are concerned, we do not, as of today, have a single Indian client who is working in Saudi. We have multiple customers who are regional or country -specific contractors, shutdown, EPC contractors, so on and so forth.

items.statement: KSA yields at upper pricing spectrum due to track record, brand recognition, and brand-new equipment supply
items.quote: We believe that we are at the upper pricing spectrum as far as yield is concerned, and largely, we are able to derive this pricing because of our track record, brand recognition and the fact that we are supplying brand-new equipment's in the country.

items.statement: India crane rental yield 2.12% per month for FY26; management foresees maintaining same with +/-5% deviation
items.quote: So, our yield in the last financial year has been around 2.1%. And we foresee maintaining the same with a plus/minus 5% deviation.

items.statement: Supply chain disruption risk for KSA crane deliveries due to shipping congestion and cost hikes; Jeddah port also facing severe congestion
items.quote: is also facing severe congestion. And also, there is a figure hike in shipping cost due to congestion. Prashant: okay. thank sir, thank you very much. Rishi Sanghvi: It is possible, but it is costly and

items.statement: Employee cost rose 103% YoY in FY26 due to E&C business doubling and strategic leadership hiring for ELEVATE 2030 plan
items.quote: So we have also been aggressively valuing leadership talent, both in India and in Saudi Arabia because we have a stated vision ELEVATE 2030, which is our 5-year strategic model plan, which talks about building up the capabilities of the organization.

items.statement: Order book at all-time high of Rs.15,109 crores as on 31st March 2026
items.quote: Company order book position has reached its all-time high and stands at Rs.15,109 crores as on 31st March 2026, as compared to Rs.11,717 crores as on 31st March 2025.

items.statement: Order inflow for FY26 was Rs.7,979 crores vs Rs.8,214 crores in FY25
items.quote: Order inflow during the Financial Year '2 5-26 stands at Rs.7,979 crore s against the previous year figure of Rs.8,214 crores.

items.statement: Management targets order inflow around Rs.8,000 crores for FY27
items.quote: Order inflow will stick to the existing numbers, which we have achieved around Rs.8,000 crores. We will try to maintain and sustain the same.

items.statement: Consultancy margin maintained at 20-25%, LSTK margin at 5-7% for FY27
items.quote: We are continuously maintaining our consultancy margin in the range of 20% to 25% percent and in the LSTK business around 5% to 7%.

items.statement: Expect minimum 10-15% revenue growth in FY27
items.quote: Just now only two months have been passed and we are expecting minimum 10% to 15% increase in the revenue.

items.statement: Middle East seeing slowdown in greenfield projects, focus on revamp; Saudi Aramco long-term agreement signed
items.quote: The big -ticket jobs are a bit on the slower side, which were to start immediately somewhere in April or May. The decision -making from the client side is delayed, because naturally, the focus has shifted on the revamping of the damaged facilities and awarding of the new projects is a little bit slower on the side.

items.statement: Middle East constitutes 10-15% of current order book
items.quote: You can say 10% to 15%, around.

items.statement: Africa emerging as alternative; Dangote refinery expansion ($360M) and fertilizer ($70M) orders secured
items.quote: In Africa, in the month of last January, we have secured the biggest order from the Dangote Refinery. This expansion project is 3,000-plus crores, and a fertilizer project, which we have also secured from them.

items.statement: Dangote projects execution timeline around 4-5 years, site activities starting end of FY27 or early FY28
items.quote: It is around four years. Right now we are in the initial stage of engineering and ordering, supporting clients and ordering of the equipments and facilities. Gradually, in a short period of time, initial site facilities would be started as well as retail engineering and other activities would start.

items.statement: Coal gasification opportunity emerging with VGF increase; private and PSU projects moving; consultancy opportunity Rs.300-400 crores per project
items.quote: It could be consultancy, Rs.300, 400 crores, depends on what size of project and what services they want to take it and which mode they would like to take.

items.statement: Interim dividend Rs.2.5/share paid, final dividend Rs.2.5/share proposed for FY26 (100% dividend)
items.quote: During the Financial Year '2 5-26, the company paid an interim dividend of Rs.2.5 per share , amounting to Rs.140 crores. Further, the Company has proposed a final dividend of Rs.2.5 per share in addition to the interim dividend and against the face value of Rs.5.

items.statement: Q4 consultancy EBIT margin 29% due to Rs.221 crore change order; normalized margins 20-25%
items.quote: In the current financial year, we have got the orders from our client, and in fact, that change order was Rs.221 crores for which we have already incurred the expenditure. So, that was the major change.

items.statement: IOCL Paradip Phase-II award expected by Q4 FY27 after feasibility completion
items.quote: It is expected by the end of this financial year it should be able to be done because the first phase is about to be finished, because which is the feasibility phase , they will be going for the investment decision from the organization and then proceed with the second phase.

items.statement: Andhra Pradesh refinery feasibility study ongoing; Phase-II implementation expected to start in FY27
items.quote: Andhra feasibility study is on. There would be licensor selection to be done or it would start shortly. And thereafter, probably towards the end of the financial year, they should be able to start the three project activities and all.

items.statement: No immediate impact from 8th Pay Commission; applies to central government first, PSUs later
items.quote: We do not see anything. That is for the central government as of now. Public sectors will come later.

items.statement: Infra business ~25% of order inflow in FY26; niche projects with ONGC, NTPC, IIMs, data centers
items.quote: For this year, it is around 25% in the order inflow. In the order book, I do not have the figures right now, I will have to check specifically.

items.statement: Middle East conflict creating uncertainty; resolution in 1-2 months critical for order flow
items.quote: If gets resolved in the Middle East then everything would be fine and we would be able to have control of it. But as of now we have to be very cautious about what is happening out there.

items.statement: Associate plant (CEIL) running at 100% capacity in FY27 after maintenance resolution
items.quote: And we expect that plant will run on 100% capacity in this year.

items.statement: AI initiatives for internal engineering processes and costing optimization, not for sales
items.quote: AI initiatives are generally used for our internal, like, engineering processes and costing purposes, not specifically for the selling purposes, but our internal processes, we are trying to improve like the costing system is there, we have generated AI utilizing this, we can extract the data quite fast.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target INR 2,600-2,800 crore with 10-12% EBITDA margin and 5-6% PAT margin
items.quote: For FY27, we are definitely looking at about INR 2,600 to INR 2,800 crores of revenue, which I am expecting that about INR 1,800 crores to INR 1,900 crores should come from the ethanol segment, based on further allocations, about INR 800 crores we are targeting to get from the grain segment, and about INR 100 crores from the mineral segment.

items.statement: Grain processing FY27 target 5% EBITDA margin on INR 800 crore revenue
items.quote: So, in FY27, I definitely have a target of being able to achieve about 5% EBITDA on this segment, which will amount to about INR 40 crores at the EBITDA level on a revenue of INR 800 crores.

items.statement: Current ethanol order book 18 crore liters (INR 1,250 crore) for ESY 25-26, targeting 22 crore liters by FY27
items.quote: We had an order book of about 18 crore liters, which translates into revenue of around INR 1,250 crores. So that is the current order book status for the ethanol segment. We are, however, looking to increase this allocation in the subsequent tenders, which are expected to be released in the month of June. As the next tender cycles, namely C2 and C3, come in, we are confident that we will be able t

items.statement: Long-term OMC off-take agreements for 13 crore liters annually through 2032
items.quote: We currently have an order book of about 18 crore liters, providing healthy near to medium-term visibility alongside long-term off-take agreements for approximately 13 crore liters annually with OMCs extending through 2032.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin 10% (up 504 bps), Q4 FY26 11.9% (up 612 bps)
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded by 612 basis points year-on-year to 11.9% in quarter four. This is an important development for us and it reflects a structurally stronger earnings base as our new capacity is stabilized. EBITDA margin for FY26 was 10%, up by 504 basis points.

items.statement: Maize price outlook: INR 19-22/kg range expected to continue through year with seasonal/regional variation
items.quote: So, currently, prices are ranging between INR 19 and INR 22, depending on the region. Right now, in the north, we have the Rabi crop season. So, we are getting more favorable prices in the northern plants from crops sourced from Bihar, UP, and Assam. In those regions, prices are around INR 19 to INR 20, while in MP, prices are around INR 22. However, in the second half of the year, when the Kharif

items.statement: FY28-29 capex to use mix of debt and equity; may require fundraising; evaluating options
items.quote: It is going to be a combination of everything. We still have to finalize those details and obtain Board approval. The capex will likely be spread across FY28 and FY29, over a period of two to three years, since it is going to be a mega project. So yes, it is going to be a combination of both debt and equity funding. It may also require some fundraising, and we are currently evaluating all availabl

items.statement: Ethanol demand strong with government blending push; industry capacity >2,000 crore liters; no supply constraint foreseen
items.quote: Ethanol industry has been supporting the government's demand over the last three years, and government wants 20, ethanol industry is ready with 25. So, I don't ever see that demand will be more than supply. That problem of the government is over. So, the ethanol industry has come out in a very strong way, and is able to produce more than 2,000 crore liters with existing capacities and the capaciti

items.statement: Ethanol margin sustainability dependent on continued FCI rice supply and soft maize prices for next 2-3 years
items.quote: We remain confident that the government will continue supplying FCI rice to the ethanol industry, and as long as that continues, the overall grain ecosystem should remain balanced, while maize and broken rice prices are expected to remain soft. So, as long as this situation continues, we are confident that we will be able to sustain these margins over the next two years.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; 25 years grain procurement experience cited as competitive advantage
items.quote: In agribusiness, we are very used to these things. We have been actually producing, procuring maize for the past 25 years. We have always been a grain processing company. First, we were making sorbitol, then starch, then fructose, now ethanol.

items.statement: Good demand seen in BFSI and warehouse/logistics for products; IT products, Auto and Power Electronics for Customer Support Services
items.quote: We are seeing good demand in BFSI and warehouse and logistics sector for our product business. And for our Customer Support Services, it is the IT products and the Auto and Power Electronics segments.

items.statement: Margin improvement is structural, supported by operational efficiencies, volume growth and disciplined execution; quarterly volatility may continue
items.quote: But, however, we believe the margin improvement is structural rather than temporary, supported by the operational efficiencies and volume growth and disciplined execution. However, the quarterly volatility may continue due to industry dynamics.

items.statement: Handheld devices and 2D scanners seeing good demand growth in manufacturing and logistics as manufacturing grows in India
items.quote: It is mainly the handheld devices and 2D scanners which are used in the manufacturing and logistics sector. We are seeing that as the entire manufacturing is growing in India and subsequently there is a resultant growth in the logistics sector as well, we are seeing a good demand growth in this segment.

items.statement: SMT lines utilization currently 30-40%, expected to go up in FY27; a few customers already onboarded
items.quote: Currently, the utilization is in the range of 30% to 40% and we expect this to go up in the coming year. That is the current year, FY27.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity increased due to higher inventory from supply chain challenges and memory price increases, plus minor receivable delays; better payable terms helped stretch payables
items.quote: So, to address those things, we have to increase our inventory levels from our normal plan and even on the receivable side, we are seeing that there is a minor delay or that the customers take a little longer time to pay than what we observed in the earlier period.

items.statement: EMS external customer revenue started in FY26, pipeline of customers and prototype orders expected to fructify in FY27
items.quote: Revenue from external customers has already started coming in from this year. So, we expect this to grow further in next year because we have a pipeline of customers with whom we are working closely and we have got a few prototype orders also from a few customers. So, all this will fructify in FY27.

items.statement: Revenue growth slowed in FY26 due to focus on sustainable profitable growth and letting go of low-margin orders; management focusing on profitability
items.quote: Company's focus is to grow on a sustainable, profitable manner. So, this focus, we have to take decisions on few low -hanging fruits either on Product side or Customer Support Service side. That is why you are seeing the revenue growth has slowed down a little bit.

items.statement: All three businesses (Products, Customer Support Services, EMS) to contribute to FY27 growth via new customer acquisition and deep sell to existing customers
items.quote: See, all the three businesses will contribute for growth with acquisition of new customers as well as deep sell in the existing customer space. So, we expect all the three businesses to contribute for growth in FY27.

items.statement: PSG growth impacted by letting go low-margin customers and supply chain disruptions with memory price increases delaying customer orders
items.quote: I think as I already mentioned, we need to let go few customers or customer orders with a lower margin. And in addition to that, as I mentioned, there is a supply chain disruption and the price increases in memory and all those things. So, which delayed onboarding few customer orders in hand.

items.statement: CSS grew 12.7% YoY driven by new customers in Infra-Management and Solar-Management; solar base expanded from 1 GW to 3 GW
items.quote: In solar, we increased our base from 1 gigawatt to 3 gigawatt. The total number of sites we increased in the last one year, which has helped us to increase the total site, which we are handling from 1 gigawatt to 3 gigawatt.

items.statement: EMS targeting 50:50 revenue mix with Products over time but no specific timeline given; confident of reaching it
items.quote: I think it will happen over a period of time. But, the exact timelines, as I mentioned earlier, we can't give an outlook statement. So, we won't be able to exactly mention that. But yes, we are working towards that, and we are confident of reaching that.

items.statement: TCM initiatives focused on optimizing manpower cost, facility cost and other costs to improve efficiency and productivity across businesses
items.quote: Based on that, we took a few calls on optimizing the manpower cost and related facility cost and all other related costs, w hich has helped us to improve the cost and keep the cost under control

items.statement: EMS customers onboarded in Auto, Industrial Electronics, Power Electronics and Defense Systems
items.quote: We have got customers in Auto and Industrial Electronics, and our focus is Auto, Power Electronics, Industrial Electronics, and Defense systems.

items.statement: Memory price increases (double/triple) impact short-term order conversion; long-term customers will absorb price increases as they need products for business growth
items.quote: See, in the short run, it has the impact on converting order into execution. But in the long run, I think customers will have to take the bite and buy the products at whatever market price, because that is what is happening in reality also.

items.statement: Product prices increase proportionately to memory cost share in product (e.g., 20% memory cost share leads to proportionate product price impact)
items.quote: Memory may not be the entire cost of the product. So, our product will increase proportionately, accordingly, like based on how much it constitutes the total product cost. If it is 20%, then to that extent, it will have an impact on the product cost of the specific product.

items.statement: TVS Aikya and AIDC platforms seeing traction; a couple of customers onboarded on Aikya, existing customers being converted; AIDC handheld devices seeing good demand in warehousing/logistics
items.quote: Yes, we have already onboarded a couple of customers on using this platform. And even our existing customers, we are working with them to convert this platform because it will give us the benefit of utilizing the platform and scaling and improving our prof itability.

items.statement: E-auctions (scrap disposal) business running 10+ years, consistently contributes to revenue and profitability; no sub-segment revenue disclosed
items.quote: This business, we are there for a longer period of more than 10 years. So, this is one of strategic business as we are an entire value chain of like products, services and end -to-end scrap solutions as well.

items.statement: Authorized service partners reduced from 700+ to 500+ due to exit from non-profitable geographies (e.g., remote Northeast locations) as part of consolidation initiative
items.quote: On an overall basis, when we are consolidating a few customers, we had to exit from a few of the non-profitable geographical areas. So, when we were implementing this initiative, this is one of the resultant of that initiative.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned for business-as-usual requirements and product development tools/molds; Rs. 40 crores already invested in factory expansion for EMS
items.quote: As I mentioned in the earlier calls, we have already invested Rs. 40 crores in all our expansion projects, which is the factory expansion EMS. In addition to that, we will have a regular CAPEX, which will keep on continuing year-on-year.

items.statement: Management expects double-digit revenue growth in FY27; no specific margin guidance given as per company policy
items.quote: Yes, we are looking at double-digit growth, obviously.

items.statement: Other income spike of Rs. 2 crores in Q4 FY26 from regular mark-to-market of FOREX forwards per accounting standards; not export-related as company predominantly imports
items.quote: It is a regular mark-to-market of FOREX forwards, which is as per accounting standard, you have to do a tender every quarter. So, it is a regular activity, which is done as per the accounting standard requirement.

items.statement: Company does not have significant exports; predominantly imports products for PSG and EMS
items.quote: Not exports. We import predominantly most of our products, which are used in the PSG as well as the EMS, Electronic Manufacturing Services.

items.statement: Short-term impact from memory price increases on order conversion; customers may postpone purchases 1-2 quarters but cannot delay longer as their business grows
items.quote: Only in the short run, it has an impact because the customers have a choice of postponing it. They can't postpone it for a longer time than one or two quarters, because their business is also growing. They need those products to grow the business.

items.statement: Management declined to provide FY27 guidance due to fluid geopolitical situation
items.quote: Actually, the present situation is so, I think, fluid, it will not be right on our part to give you anything right now, but maybe by next time, we will be in a better position to -- till now whatever we have projected, we have been able to mostly achieve.

items.statement: Plywood demand continues post price increase with no drop in secondary sales
items.quote: we are not seeing any drop in our secondary. So that, to me, shows that there might be some holding with the big dealers. But because we have such a wide expansion, and we actually run routes on a daily basis when it comes to feeding smaller dealers, I feel that demand is continuing even post the price increase currently for ply.

items.statement: MDF demand stable and healthy post Q4 exuberance
items.quote: Look, for us also, demand has been quite stable. Usually, April, May as compared to Q4, of course, there's a little bit of correction that happens from the Q4 exuberance. But in general, we don't see any fundamental weakening of demand. So it's quite stable and healthy.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin ex-forex improved to 13.6% in Q4 FY26 from 12.6% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: At the profitability level, consolidated EBITDA margin, excluding forex losses improved to 13.6% compared to 12.6% in the previous quarter and 12.1% in the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin ex-forex improved to 13% from 11.1% in FY25
items.quote: For the full year FY '26, the company achieved top line growth of 19.2%, while EBITDA margin, excluding forex loss improved significantly to 13% from 11.1% in FY '25.

items.statement: MDF steady-state EBITDA margin target is high-teens
items.quote: our strong belief is that this is a high-teens EBITDA business in steady state. And there are 2, 3 reasons for it.

items.statement: MDF Q4 margin declined 1% QoQ due to chemical disruptions and one-off ATL spend
items.quote: if you compare our Q4 versus Q3, there has been a margin erosion of about 1%, a marginal margin erosion. This is on account of 2 factors. One, some production-related disruptions linked to the chemical availability and prices. And secondly, some one-off spend.

items.statement: MDF and industry took 15% price increase to cover chemical cost disruption
items.quote: given the disruption in chemicals and supply chain, so on and so forth, we and the industry have taken a 15% price increase, which barely actually covers the cost that has gone up on account of chemicals disruption.

items.statement: Plywood took 7% price increase in April due to imported timber and chemical cost increases
items.quote: prices have increased, and we have taken a 7% price rise already in the month of April due to these reasons because we are so import heavy as well as our chemicals, which are imported as well. They too faced a lot of increase.

items.statement: Particle Board price pass-through similar to MDF range
items.quote: the raw material prices on account of chemicals have taken a hit similar to MDF, and our price pass -on has also been in the same range.

items.statement: Raw material cost increase higher than price increase percentage due to cost structure
items.quote: The raw material increase will be higher because of the ratio of the raw material to the pricing is -- it's not 100%, right? So obviously, the raw material price would be higher, obviously, but we pass on the exact, right? We do not let our EBITDA get hit.

items.statement: Plywood capacity 406,000 CBM as of March 2026; adding 48,000 CBM Hoshiarpur plant in H2 FY27 plus 20% brownfield expansion
items.quote: current capacity at Plywood is 4,06,000 as on March '26. And we are coming up with new capacity of Hoshiarpur, which is 48,000 CBM, which is going to come up in the second half of this year. Apart from that, we are having a brownfield expansion at our different factories, which is Kandla, Chennai and Guwahati, which will add another 20% of this particular capacity

items.statement: Plywood Q4 FY26 capacity utilization at 99%; planning 30% capacity increase in FY27
items.quote: in Q4, we had a capacity utilization of about 99%. We are increasing our capacity by about 30% within this year. Part of it is -- about 20% is the internal plant expansion. And another, the Hoshiarpur plant is supposed to come up in October this year. So that would make it a 30% expansion.

items.statement: MDF capacity 530,000-540,000 CBM; adding 60,000-70,000 CBM via brownfield expansion in South plant by end of Q1 FY27
items.quote: For MDF, the current capacity is about 5,30,000, 5,40,000 CBM per year. And with the brownfield expansion, we will add another 60,000 to 70,000. So we'll make about 6,00,000 cubes a year.

items.statement: MDF current utilization 80-85% of rated capacity
items.quote: With the current numbers, we are at about 80% to 85% capacity utilization, give or take for our full capacity. And this is against the rated capacity.

items.statement: Major FY27 capex directed towards Hoshiarpur plywood plant; UP plant capex to start late FY27 or Q1 FY28
items.quote: The basic capex that we are going to incur, the majority of it is going to be towards our new Hoshiarpur plant. Other than that, once we are online in Uttar Pradesh, once the land is in hand, we should be looking at commissioning Uttar Pradesh over the course of the next 2 years. Other than these 2, we have no major frozen capex as yet. So the capex will be predominantly directed towards plywood.

items.statement: No frozen capex for MDF or Particle Board; using internal cash flows to strengthen balance sheet
items.quote: Currently, there's no frozen capex for MDF or Particle Board, which are large substantial capexes. We are going to be using our internal cash flows predominantly to strengthen our balance sheet.

items.statement: Long-term debt not to exceed 1:1 EBITDA going forward
items.quote: long-term debt, I don't think we'll exceed 1:1 EBITDA going forward.

items.statement: Total forex exposure INR 600 crores, mark-to-market on long-term debt for imported machinery
items.quote: our total forex is within INR600 crores. Over the course of the past 2 decades, we have benefited substantially because of a natural interest hedge, as you are aware. One year, yes, there's been a start loss. This is predominantly due to the fact that currencies appreciated beyond what anyone could have imagined. Having said that, I think our total forex expenditure to our total forex exposure is

items.statement: Timber prices stable with marginal correction; no supply challenges but prices increased due to freight
items.quote: timber has remained a lot more stable this year, while -- it's marginally corrected. I won't say it's corrected by 10%, but it's remained stable. And there are some regular seasonal variations that happen any which ways in timber.

items.statement: Chemical and resin input costs under inflationary pressure due to geopolitical conflicts and supply chain disruptions
items.quote: During the quarter, the industry witnessed inflationary pressure in certain chemicals and resin -related input costs due to ongoing geopolitical conflicts and supply chain disruptions in global markets.

items.statement: MDF focusing on value-added products and product mix improvement for margin uplift
items.quote: a lot of effort is being made just in terms of product mix and value-added products, which we want to push further and further.

items.statement: Plywood moving Sainik MR outsourcing in-house; target 100% in-house production by April next year
items.quote: we want to actually make it a complete 100% in -house production. We are hoping that by the time there is an internal expansion next year, April, and Hoshiarpur. So once Hoshiarpur comes, we will start moving a lot of our Sainik MR, which is the only product we outsource in-house. And by the time we are here next year, we would probably make it 100% in-house.

items.statement: Some MDF peers doing selective rollbacks on 15% price increase; industry in flux
items.quote: Some peers in the industry have done selective rollbacks on this. So right now, it's in a bit of a flux given that the global tensions are again at play.

items.statement: ROE improved from 10.6% to 15.2% and ROCE from 12.5% to 14.6% in FY26 ex-forex
items.quote: Excluding forex losses, ROE improved from 10.6% to 15.2%, while ROCE increased from 12.5% to 14.6%, reflecting stronger operational performance and improved capital efficiency.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty (Iran war, chemical supply chain) creating fluid situation for guidance and pricing
items.quote: the situation is really, really -- and we do not know what will happen to this war because they have given 60 days for that uranium, something, they will again sit down. So it may or may not -- the war may again start. So you really don't know what is going to happen. So that's why we are reserving.

items.statement: FY27 capacity addition target of 9,557 MW: thermal 1,070 MW, hydro 250 MW, renewable 8,237 MW
items.quote: as far as FY27 is concerned, on a totality basis, we are planning around 9,557 MW of capacity. If I break down it into thermal, hydro and renewable, thermal would constitute 1,070 MW, hydro will be 250 MW, and renewable total would be 8,237 MW.

items.statement: FY28 capacity addition target of 10,039 MW: thermal 1,460 MW, hydro 444 MW, renewable 8,135 MW
items.quote: The year next, FY28, the total plant capacity addition is 10,039 MW, comprising of thermal 1,460 MW, hydro total will be 444 MW and renewable total will be 8,135 MW.

items.statement: FY29 capacity addition target of 11,478 MW: thermal 3,070 MW, renewable 8,408 MW, no hydro
items.quote: In a similar way for FY29, we are planning 11,478 MW total capacity. 8,408 MW would be renewable. We don't expect any hydro addition during that year. Thermal total will be 3,070 MW.

items.statement: NGEL FY27 capex INR 35,800 crore, FY28 INR 46,000 crore, FY29 INR 48,000 crore at 80:20 debt-equity
items.quote: For NGEL, for current year it would be c apex of INR 35,800 crores. Next year, it would be INR46,000 crores and the year next, it would be INR48,000 crores. So we'd be implementing a debt equity of 80-20

items.statement: Group capex INR 6.22 lakh crore till FY32, half allocated to renewables via NGEL
items.quote: We have a broad c apex for the group of INR 6,22,000 crores till the financial '32 and we have allocated roughly half of that, around INR3 lakh crores for renewable energy, which should broadly be done by NGEL

items.statement: NTPC Group renewable capacity target 60 GW by 2032, supported by GOI investment limit increase to INR 20,000 crore for renewable subsidiaries
items.quote: Government of India enhanced investment approval limit for renewable subsidiaries up to INR20,000 crores, supporting NTPC's target of 60 GW renewable capacity by 2032.

items.statement: NTPC Group installed capacity 89,108 MW as of 31 March 2026, added 9,618 MW in FY26 (highest ever), crossed 90 GW as of call date
items.quote: As on 31 March 2026, NTPC Group installed capacity stood at 89,108 MW. During the year, we have added 9,618 MW of capacity. NTPC contributed 1,823 MW and JVs and subsidiaries contributed 7,795 MW, making the highest ever annual capacity addition since inception.

items.statement: NTPC Group RE capacity 12,068 MW as of call date (4,738 MW added in FY26, 490 MW added in FY27 to date)
items.quote: During FY26, NTPC Group added 4,738 MW of RE capacity. Out of this, NGEL added 4,225 MW compared to 2,977 MW added in FY25. In addition, 490 MW have been added in FY27 till date, taking the total installed renewable energy capacity of NTPC group to 12,068 MW.

items.statement: NTPC Group has over 34 GW under construction: 16.5 GW coal, 2.6 GW hydro, 15 GW renewable
items.quote: NTPC Group currently has over 34 GW of capacity under construction, comprising 16.5 GW of coal-based capacity, about 2.6 GW of hydro capacity and 15 GW of renewable energy capacity providing a strong foundation for near- to medium-term growth.

items.statement: NGEL pipeline reduced from 32 GW to 30 GW after normalizing JV/subsidiary progress; MoUs and activities ongoing to increase pipeline
items.quote: We had earlier shown 32 GW up to Q3 of last year. However, now we are seeing in which of the JVs or the subsidiaries the progress is being made and normalize the numbers, so that is why the numbers have come down from 32 GW to 30 GW.

items.statement: PPA tie-up for next 3 years: FY27 79%, FY28 71%, FY29 66% of planned capacity
items.quote: Over the next 3 years, broadly for an average 72% to 75% capacities, PPA already in place. For FY27, it is 79%. FY 28 CODs of 8,069 MW we are already covered with 71% PPA. And the year next around 8,400 MW, it is 66%.

items.statement: Transmission connectivity for RE: FY27 firm 57% + T-GNA 38%, FY28 firm 88% + T-GNA 3%, FY29 firm 84%
items.quote: as far as FY27 is concerned, we have the firm connectivity of 57% and T-GNA of 38%. As far as FY28 is concerned, whatever CODs are expected in FY28, we have a projected firm connectivity of 88% and 3% would be coming from the T -GNA, remaining 9% is so mething which we are yet to tie-up. FY29, 84% we have firm connection and remaining 16%, we'll have to work on the connectivity

items.statement: NGEL EBITDA margin sustained at 87% in FY26; revenue up 29% to INR 2,858 crore, EBITDA up 29% to INR 2,475 crore
items.quote: Consolidated revenue from operations increased by 29% to INR2,858 crores in FY26, while operating EBITDA grew by 29% to INR2,475 crores. EBITDA margin remains at 87%.

items.statement: NTPC standalone PAT up 18% to INR 23,162 crore in FY26; adjusted PAT up 8% to INR 19,530 crore
items.quote: NTPC profit after tax for FY26 is INR23,162 crores as against INR19,649 crores in the previous year, registering a growth of 18%. Adjusted PAT for FY26 is INR19,530 crores against INR 18,016 crores in the previous year, registering a growth of 8%.

items.statement: Group PAT up 15% to INR 27,546 crore in FY26; subsidiaries profit INR 3,312 crore, JV share INR 2,864 crore
items.quote: Profit after tax of the group for FY26 is INR27,546 crores as against INR23,953 crores in FY25, registering an increase of 15%. During FY26, our subsidiaries earned a profit of INR3,312 crores. NTPC's share of profit in JVs was INR2,864 crores in FY26.

items.statement: Weighted average interest rate on borrowings improved to 5.98% in FY26 from 6.61% in FY25 due to proactive financing and loan restructuring
items.quote: The weighted average interest rate on borrowings during FY2 6 stood at 5.98% compared to 6.61% in FY25, reflecting the benefits of proactive financing and strategic restructuring of the company's loan

items.statement: Q4 FY26 executed US$150 million JPY loan with Mizuho at 0.98% over TONA, 7-year average maturity, 8-year door-to-door tenor
items.quote: During Q4 of FY2 6, loan agreement for US$150 million, JPY denominated was executed with Mizuho Bank Limited. The loan carries an interest rate of 0.98% per annum over 6 months compounded Tokyo overnight average rate, TONA, and has the average maturity of 7 years. The door-to-door tenor of the loan is 8 years

items.statement: Outstanding receivable days improved to 15 days as of 31 March 2026 from 29 days previous year
items.quote: Outstanding receivable days improved to 15 days as on 31st March '26 compared to 29 days for the previous year.

items.statement: Coal production from captive mines up 8.5% to 47.88 MMT in FY26; Pakri Barwadih Northwest mine commercial from 1 April 2026; mining business transfer to NTPC Mining Limited completed
items.quote: Coal production from group captive coal mines under commercial operation increased to 47.88 million metric ton, registering a growth of 8.5% vis-a-vis previous year. Coal production started from Pakri Barwadih Northwest mine in December '25, and mine was declared commercial operation with effect from 1st of April 2026.

items.statement: Coal stock at comfortable 18 days across stations; 18% of coal requirement met through captive mines
items.quote: The coal position across all our power stations remains at comfortable levels, sufficient for nearly 18 days, ensuring stable generation and supply reliability. Further, with nearly 18% of our coal requirement being met through captive mines, fuel security for our stations is more assured than ever before.

items.statement: NTPC coal PLF 72.04% vs all-India average 63.20% in FY26; group generation 432.2 BU vs 438.7 BU in FY25; NVVNL trading up 13%; NGEL generation up 114% to 14.6 BU
items.quote: NTPC Group generation stood at 432.2 billion units in FY2 6 as compared to 438.7 billion units in FY2 5. Generation from NGEL stood at 14.6 billion units as compared to 6.8 billion units in FY25, registering a growth of 114

items.statement: Biomass co-firing doubled to 15.19 lakh MT in FY26 from 7.03 lakh MT in FY25
items.quote: During FY2 6, our group thermal station co-fired 15.19 lakh metric ton of biomass, more than double as compared to 7.03 lakh metric tons used last year

items.statement: Technical minimum of 55% PLF for thermal plants mandated by regulator; below 55% plant can take reserve shutdown and still recover fixed charges
items.quote: Accordingly, there has been a very favorable pronouncement wherein we have been assured a technical minimum of 55%. I mean if it goes down, we are not obligated to then keep the unit live and we'll be compensated further for our availability under fixed charges.

items.statement: Final dividend INR 3.50 per share recommended for FY26; total dividend INR 9 per share (INR 5.50 interim + INR 3.50 final)

This is in addition to the interim dividend of INR5.50 per share already paid during FY26. Total dividend for the FY26 will be INR 9 per share, in line with the company's commitment to delivering value to its shareholders.

items.statement: Acquired 1,350 MW Sinnar Thermal Power Station in partnership with MAHAGENCO in FY26
items.quote: This also includes the acquisition of the 1,350 MW Sinnar Thermal Power Station in partnership with MAHAGENCO.

items.quote: Yes, we have started coal gasification, we have taken up a pilot project at one of our mines, Talaipalli. And we are going to EIL, and this has a capacity of 4 lakh tonnes per annum. And this is basically for synthetic natural gas production. It's a pilot project.

items.statement: FY27 business growth guided at ~15%, deposit growth 10-15%, advance growth 15-20%, CASA ratio 33%+, CD ratio 80%
items.quote: The overall position I ha ve given, I will stand firm on it with the overall business growth of around 15% and maintaining we want to have the deposit growth between 10% to 15% and advanced growth of 15% to 20

items.statement: FY27 ROA guided at 1%+ with improvement bias
items.quote: ROA, I was telling 1% plus. 1% plus may be anything. So 1% plus, I will still hold on to it. Right now, I am not in a position to tell, but when the ROA was less than 1%, I was telling that 1% plus.

items.statement: FY27 cost-to-income ratio guided at 52-53%
items.quote: it further. It wil l be between 52% and 53%. Once the costs are under control and the business is running smoothly, we will certainly work on further improvements

items.statement: PCR target to increase ~1% per quarter
items.quote: We want to increase 1% every quarter. That number still I'm holding on. But last quarter, we have done more.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 NIM 3.07% vs 2.92% Q3; yield on advances 8.78% (+7bps QoQ); cost of funds 5.38% (-8bps QoQ)
items.quote: Net interest margin stood at 3.07% for Q4 FY '26, versus 2.92% in Q3 FY '26 and 2.98% in Q4 FY '25. Improvement in net interest margin was driven by the bank's focused initiatives in the RAM segment with an emphasis on enhancing yield, alongside a calibrated improvement in CASA and retail term deposits aimed at optimizing the cost of funds.

items.statement: NIM outlook: bottomed out, no further downside expected unless EBLR moves up
items.quote: Unless there is a movement in EBLR it is at the lowest now , if it is moving upward and all and it gets compensated. Otherwise, if the trend is continuing, we will be on the same trend. I feel it has bottomed out. There may not be any chance it is coming down further.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 gross advances INR83,340 cr (+8% QoQ); RAM INR51,197 cr (+4% QoQ); mid-corporate +13% QoQ; housing, agri, gold, vehicle loans added INR1,547 cr
items.value: gross advances INR83,340 cr; RAM INR51,197 cr
items.quote: Gross advances stood at INR83,340 crores as on 31st March '26, reflecting a Q-on-Q growth of 8% from INR77,283 crores as on 31st December '25. Our overall strategy is to continue our focus on growing ; Retail, Agri and MSME, that is RAM, which has grown from INR49,152 crores as on December '25 to INR51,197 crores as on March '26.

items.statement: IBPC & Food Credit portfolio reduced from INR4,057 cr (Mar'25) to INR1,707 cr (Mar'26); INR2,350 cr replaced with higher-yielding loans in FY26
items.quote: IBPC and Food Credit portfolio, which was at INR4,057 crores as of March 31, '25 has been brought down to INR1,707 crores as of 31st March '26. Accordingly, around INR2,350 crores have been replaced during FY '25-'26.

items.statement: INR2,000 cr of sanctioned loans pending disbursal as of Mar'26; disbursements started post-April
items.quote: As of March, we had INR2,000 crores of sanctioned but pending for disbursal. It has not happened for various reasons. It started happening post April.

items.statement: ECL implementation impact ~1-1.5% on net worth, spread over 4-5 years (~25-30bps per year); capital adequacy sufficient
items.quote: I believe the guidelines which has now come, which is available to spread over to the next 5 years and we have studied the impact also maybe around 1% to 1.5% overall will be there. Even that also available for the next 4 years or 5 years, that will be spread over to 25 basis points, 30 basis points. And we have sufficiently taken care of that.

items.statement: Cost of funds improved 8bps QoQ to 5.38% driven by bulk deposit reduction and CASA buildup; further improvement expected
items.quote: Cost of Funds stood at 5.38% for Q4 FY '26, as compared to 5.46% for Q3 FY '26, registering an 8 basis points improvement. The sequential Q-on-Q improvement in cost of funds is expected to be supported by our continued efforts t o reduce the dependence on bulk deposits and replacing them with retail deposits at card rates and focus on CASA

items.statement: New product launches planned: agri input loans for tobacco (digital onboarding), programmable CBDC, NFC QR tap-and-pay, surrogate-based housing/mortgage lending, dropline OD & LAP for MSME
items.quote: Launches planned during the coming quarters: Agri input loans for tobacco crops, short-term agri input loans are extended to registered tobacco growers to meet the cultivation requirements, with digital onboarding and faster sanctioning under a tobacco board tie- up. Programmable CBDC enables the funds to be used only for predefined purposes within a s pecified time or through designated beneficia

items.statement: Headcount declines monthly due to superannuation (~50-60/month); recruitment only as needed; 31 branches opened last year; IT investments to absorb workload
items.quote: the number of staff is always going down. Every month, it wil l go down, with the superannuation. As and when required, we will recruit people. In between, last year, we have opened around 31 branches, staffs are required. In between, we recruit also. That during the first H1 or up to Q3, we have recruited some people. Again, Q4, there was no recruitment rather. Rather, people retired in 3 months.

items.statement: Employee cost control assured; expansion may require added manpower but will be compensated by business growth
items.quote: Yes, it will be under control, that is my assurance. But sometimes, see certain business expansion and other things, we may require additional manpower also. Taking that into account, it will be duly compensated from the business. Need not worry. While expenditure quantum may go up, it will be duly compensated for by the increase in the business.

items.statement: Loan book mix: base rate 0.31%, MCLR 5.59%, EBLR G-Sec 2.31%, EBLR T-bill 55% (Mar'26)

items.quote: To be very frank with you, base rate is 0.31%, MCLR 5.59% at the end of March '26. Then EBLR linked to G-Sec 2.31%, EBLR linked to T-bill rate 55%. This is the component.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20-25% YoY
items.quote: So, from a guidance perspective, I would try to give anywhere between 20% to 25% growth. But internally, we have a more aggressive growth. But for the outside world, it is anywhere between 20% to 25% kind of a growth that we are looking at year-over-year because our long-term target is to do 10x in 10 years is what we are trying to achieve.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 12.5-13% near term, 15% long term
items.quote: So, margins currently due to all these one -offs, our margins were in the tune of about 11% EBITDA. We want to target it to anywhere between 13% to 15% on the long term. So short term, we should be able to do 12.5%, 13% and on the longer term, we should be able to be 15%.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 new orders and renewals of Rs. 166 crore
items.quote: We secured around Rs. 166 crore in new orders and renewals during this period, reflecting continued demand for our capabilities across digital transformation, infrastructure modernization, managed Services and AI-led Solutions.

items.statement: Mumbai government project expected Rs. 150-200 crore, announcement in 2-3 weeks
items.quote: It should be to the tune of about anywhere between Rs. 150 crore to Rs. 200 crore. We are still figuring out and the final signing one is going on. We should be able to come up with a number very soon.

items.statement: FY26 adjusted EBITDA Rs. 112 crore at 11% margin, up 14% YoY
items.quote: On the profitability front, adjusted EBITDA increased by 14% year-on-year basis to Rs. 112 crore, while EBITDA margins were resilient at 11%.

items.statement: AI and automation expected to reduce resource count 20-25% in 6-12 months, driving margin improvement
items.quote: So, we see definitely a reduction on the resource count for any customer close to 20%, 25% in a matter of 6 months or a year.

items.statement: Enterprise revenue grew 31% YoY in FY26, Government revenue declined 6% YoY
items.quote: In terms of customer mix, revenues from Enterprise customers grew strongly by 31% year -on-year during FY '26, while Government revenues were lower by 6% during the year.

And eventually, we had to go out of those deals. And that is one of the

items.quote: So, in this quarter, our multiple projects were on. Because of that, our direct expenses, supply of equipment got increased by around 3%, 4% in comparison to the standard or direct expenses level. So that impacted.

items.statement: RBI approval pending for FEMA compliance on US subsidiary loan conversion; expected in 1-2 quarters
items.quote: There are certain procedures that we have to get done through the RBI and get the approval of the RBI. The process for that has started. items.statement: One-time additional ECL provision of Rs. 36 crore taken in Q4 FY26 per auditor advice and policy change
items.quote: And secondly, other expenses also you will find in this quarter is higher because that onetime provision is also taken under that, the Rs. 36-odd crore that ECL provision, that is also part of this quarter's expenses.

items.statement: Services revenue grew 21% YoY, Solutions revenue grew 17% YoY in FY26
items.quote: From a segment perspective, our Services business continued to perform strongly, reporting a 21% year -on-year growth in FY '26, while Solutions revenue increased by 17%.

items.statement: Domestic revenue grew 17% YoY in FY26, Q4 domestic up 37% YoY; International revenue grew 22% YoY in FY26
items.quote: From a geographic standpoint, both our domestic and international business delivered healthy double -digit growth during FY '26. International revenues grew 22% year -on-ye

items.statement: Dividend maintained at 30% (Rs. 1.50 per share, face value Rs. 5)
items.quote: Recognizing the resilient performance , the Board of Directors has maintained the dividend at 30% equivalent to Rs. 1.50 per equity share with a Rs. 5 face value.

items.statement: Target Services mix 75-80% of revenue for consistency; Solutions act as entry point converting to annuity Managed Services
items.quote: But if you ask me personally, I would want our Services business to keep on growing and take about 75% to 80% of our top line revenue because that gives a lot of consistency from a growth perspective because most of the Services contracts are signed for 5 years.

items.statement: No clients lost to insourcing; AI adoption increasing outsourcing demand for vendors with AI adaptability
items.quote: Not so far Pratik. We have not seen any customers taking anything in -house. items.quote: There are, of course, major margin pressures that are happening across the industry, and we are also facing the same. But we look at that as an opportunity because a lot of our service delivery, we have started using AI. And with AI getting implemented, AIOps getting implemented, we are seeing that there is a cost reduction that is happening across the line.

items.statement: Investing in AI resources, technology, and training as three key aspects of AI journey
items.quote: Allied Digital is constantly investing into AI more and more in terms of resources, in terms of technology and in terms of training. So, all these three are our key aspects of our journey this year also.

items.statement: Management targets 230-250 new restaurant openings in FY27
items.quote: we would open similar to about 230 to 250 kind of restaurants this year.

items.statement: Long-term like-for-like growth target remains 5-7% annually

items.statement: Long-term margin improvement target of 200 bps over 2 years maintained

items.statement: Energy cost inflation hitting P&L by 100-120 bps

items.statement: Gross margin improvement driven by wastage reduction, premium product launches, mix changes and calibrated price increases
