items.statement: Price increase of ~1.2% passed on to consumers to offset energy cost inflation

items.quote: our capex per store has actually reduced year-on-year, and almost nearly 3 years in a row by 20%, right? So it has come down by 20%.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 like-for-like growth tracking better than Q4 FY26's 0.2%

items.statement: Delivery mix at 76% creating labor cost headwind; premium product launches (Big Big Pizza, Sourdough) improving mix
items.quote: We've had a 76% delivery mix, and that is another inflation headwind on the labor cost.

items.statement: Aggregators growing faster than Domino's delivery, indicating broader QSR basket not growing as fast; Domino's gaining share among tracked QSR peers
items.quote: the aggregators have grown faster than the delivery of Domino's, that bit I agree, which would only indicate that the QSR as a basket has not grown as fast.

items.statement: Near-term margin pressure duration uncertain (1-3 quarters) due to volatile energy, labor and commodity inflation; recalibrating numbers every few days
items.quote: Now will it be for a quarter, 2 quarters, 3 quarters, I think, at this stage, is anybody's guess, right? items.statement: Long-term vision of INR 17,500 crores revenue by FY30 with 12.5% EBITDA margin on consolidated group basis
items.quote: Yes. So we have kept the long-term vision in mind for 2030 to deliver INR 17,500 crores top line with 12.5% EBITDA margin. And the whole group is working towards achieving those stated numbers.

items.statement: Expect FY27 capex of INR 400-450 crores, similar to FY26 range of INR 350-400 crores
items.quote: So our capex has been in the range of INR 350 crores to INR 400 crores. And this year also, we expect to be in that range, maybe 10% plus of that, close to about INR 400 crores, INR 450 crores capex we are expecting for fiscal year 2026-27.

items.statement: Lifetime order book of INR 10,000 crores for FY26 with 20% from exports; Q4 FY26 order book of INR 3,500 crores
items.quote: We recorded a lifetime order book of INR 10,000 crores, contributing about 20% from exports order.

items.statement: Order book execution timeline typically 48-60 months across products and customers

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 11.9%, up 37 bps YoY; FY26 EBITDA margin 11.7%, up 29 bps YoY

items.statement: FY26 capex of INR 413 crores, highest ever; acquired land parcels in industrial clusters for future expansion

items.quote: When it comes to the Minda Instruments' second plant, which is under commissioning, we expect it to be ready by Q1 of next year, and that will house all our advanced electronics technologies from the instrument cluster and cockpit point of view.

items.statement: PV revenue share to accelerate to 25% from 14% after Minda VAST consolidation from FY27
items.quote: With the consolidation of Minda VAST business with Minda Corporation from FY 27 onwards, it will certainly accelerate our vision to achieve 25% revenue from Passenger Vehicle segment, which currently stands at about 14%.

items.statement: Multiple platform-level instrument cluster orders won from leading OEMs; TFT clusters 3-15 inch across PV, CV, 2W domestic and export

items.statement: Minda VAST to be consolidated into Minda Corporation from FY27 after shareholder agreement change; enhances 4W system solutions

items.quote: Overall, the auto industry grew by 20% and closed Q4 FY26 on a firm footing with a stable macroeconomic conditions and policy-led affordability gain.

items.statement: CV outlook positive driven by infrastructure build-out (highways, airports) and logistics demand; regulatory changes (safety, TPMS, AC) adding content
items.quote: CV is again expected to continue the growth largely by, again, the exports that are being driven by the India, India is growing, extreme amount of roads and transportation is being built across, the number of highways that are being built is phenomenal.

items.statement: Minimum wage hikes in UP and Haryana effective April 2026 addressed via productivity, controlled headcount, workload management

items.statement: Final dividend 40% (INR 0.80/share); total FY26 dividend 70% (INR 1.40/share)
items.quote: In recognition of our shareholders, the Board of Directors have recommended a final dividend of 40% that is INR 0.80 per equity share on the face value, taking the total dividend for the year to 70%, that is INR 1.40 per equity share.

items.statement: 42 plants, 23,000+ associates globally; 950 engineers; 330 patents filed (147 granted) in FY26
items.quote: We have a manufacturing footprint, which includes 42 plants with over 23,000 associates and employees across our plants and offices all over the world. We remain focused on innovation which enabled us to file 330 patents during the fiscal year, of which 147 have already been granted.

items.statement: Flash Electronics PAT improvement driven by lower interest cost and higher capacity utilization; export orders from metallics business
items.quote: Yes. So PAT is mainly to do with the interest cost. I think their overall interest cost has gone down, which has resulted in a better PAT performance.

items.statement: Commodity cycle volatility (copper, zinc, aluminum up 30-40%) not expected to cool off next quarter due to geopolitical tensions

items.statement: TPMS orders across multiple segments entering mass production soon; safety regulations driving adoption
items.quote: Tire Pressure Monitoring System is one such key critical sensor, which is in the portfolio of Minda Corporation as well as we have multiple orders in place, also getting into start of production.

items.quote: Q4 FY26 witnessed a meaningful improvement in theatrical momentum, supported by a stronger content pipeline and better audience engagement across markets.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated revenue grew 15% to ₹4,864 million, EBITDA increased 36% to ₹803 million, net profit grew 161% to ₹249 million

items.statement: Trade receivables increased to INR 162 crores from INR 115 crores, driven by higher ad revenues and Dhurandhar release timing

items.statement: Revenue sharing with exhibitors increased to 59.5% from legacy 33% due to higher multiplex mix and non-DCI investment model

Using this tool, we are now able to demonstrate to advertisers that we deserve a better share of advertising revenues because we deliver a disproportionate impact.

items.statement: Off-screen advertising and activation initiatives initiated but at early stage, progressing in phases

items.quote: Our net cash has improved from INR 48.3 crores to INR 59 crores during the year, despite nearly INR 11 crores getting further tied up in working capital.

items.statement: Company maintains cash and debt deliberately; debt funds expensive equipment via LCs converted to loans, not tracked linearly quarter-on-quarter

items.statement: Adequate provisions made for receivables; current DSO of 147 days not materially out of line with pre-COVID FY19 level of 134 days
items.quote: There is nothing concerning from a provisioning standpoint. Adequate provisions have been made wherever required. The increase of roughly 12–14 days over normal DSO levels is largely attributable to the higher revenues booked from Dhurandhar.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance of 10-12% for FY27 on FY26 base of ~5.3 million tons cement

items.quote: So current year, we have done INR184 crores of subsidy. So what Tushar ji is saying INR40 crores to INR50 crores, somewhere in the INR145 crores to INR150 crores sort of thing you can estimate for the coming year.

items.statement: FY27 capex revised to INR600-700 crore; FY28 capex estimated at INR1,500 crore for Nimbol, Haryana and Bihar grinding units

items.statement: Rajasthan clinker plant (3.3 mt) with split grinding in Haryana (2-2.5 mt) targeting commissioning H1 FY29; Jorhat grinding (2 mt) and Umrangso clinker later

items.statement: Q1 FY27 fuel cost increase of INR0.10-0.15/GCV due to coal shortage from railway rake diversion to power plants; expected to normalize by Q3-Q4

I don't think it should be a long-term structural increase, but there will be increase because of all the rakes being diverted and then we have to arrange coal from elsewhere and then that increases the cost.

items.statement: Cement prices improved slightly in April-May: Northeast up INR6-7/bag, outside Northeast (West Bengal, Bihar) up INR10/bag vs March exit
items.quote: Northeast, I think it may be about INR6 to INR7. Outside Northeast was about INR10.

items.statement: EBITDA/ton guidance INR1,500-1,700 for Northeast operations until Rajasthan commissioning; long-term blended target INR1,300-1,400 after Rajasthan ramp-up
items.quote: I think for the next 2, 3 years till when we get the Rajasthan project, I think the EBITDA is -- because it is only in Northeast sales, the EBITDA should be between INR1,500 to INR1,700, right, at least. And once we get the Rajasthan, of course, for the first 1 year, because we'll be absorbing fixed costs and because we'll be ramping up our sales, the EBITDA per ton may fall. But I think in the lo

items.quote: For FSA, this quarter, it is 78.5% and biomass is 21.5%.

items.statement: New entrant timeline unchanged at 3-4 years; Northeast market small so entrants must consider impact on own profitability; some price pressure expected for 1-2 years then normalization

items.statement: Board approval for fund raise obtained in Q3 FY26; QIP decision pending, will depend on market conditions and net debt/EBITDA reaching 1.5x

items.quote: I would anticipate at this point in time a mid and early double -digit growth would be a good number to look at and as we progress forward, I think we would be in a better position to see how things progress.

items.statement: Export revenue growth target of 20-25% for FY27, lower than the 40% achieved in FY26, due to global uncertainty.
items.quote: I think a growth of about 20% to 25% should be a good number to look at given how the world order is.

items.statement: Working capital target of 25-30 days for FY27, with 30 days seen as a good normalized number.
items.quote: I would say that, you know, anywhere in the range of about 25 days to 30 days of working capital is a good number, an aggressive number to look at.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin target remains 13-15%, but near-term focus is on sustaining current margins until volumes recover.
items.quote: Our longer -term outlook of trying to get back to the 13% to 15% range is something that we will continue to drive and focus.

items.statement: Udaan volume target for FY27 is 2-3x the FY26 level of 202 units, depending on demand recovery.
items.quote: If we can manage to do two times to three times that number, I think I'd be delighted given the current demand conditions in the country.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin declined to 12.6% from 15.3% due to CEV5 transition costs, lower volumes, and calibrated pricing; Q4 margin improved to 15.1% from 14.7% YoY.
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the year came in at 12.6% versus 15.3% in the previous year. This performance is broadly in line with our consistent guidance indicating an approximately 200 basis points to 250 basis points decline in margin driven primarily by higher production costs and the calibrated approach that we have adopted towards pricing actions.

items.statement: Gross margin in Q4 FY26 rose 170 bps YoY to 25.8% as higher production costs are now in the base and cost reduction initiatives took effect.
items.quote: Gross margins of Q4 FY26 stood at 25.8% compared to 24.1% in Q4 FY25, an increase of 170 bps on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Management intends to continue calibrated price increases to recover commodity cost inflation (steel, fuel) as market conditions allow.
items.quote: There is obviously an indication of the fuel increases which have an impact for us as well. So I think directionally, our intent is quite clear and we would walk the path of making sure that whatever we can recover from the market, we will continue to do so.

items.statement: SLCM revenue flat despite volume decline due to favorable product mix (higher 4-Series share) and Q4 price hike; non-SLCM revenue grew 7% on volume growth in pumps and batching plants.
items.quote: SLCM revenue for FY26 stood at INR1,758 crores, remaining largely flat versus FY25 despite a decline in volumes. Revenue was supported by a favorable product mix and a marginal benefit from the price increase taken in Q4.

items.statement: Net working capital fell to 21 days in FY26 (lowest in 5 years); EBITDA to operating cash flow conversion at 142%.
items.quote: Our EBITDA to operating cash flow stood at a robust 142% in FY26. With liquidation of inventory, our net working capital has come down to 21 days, which is the lowest in the last five years.

items.statement: Cash balance of INR 1,121 crores as of March 2026; strong cash generation expected to continue (INR 200-300 crores annually).
items.quote: Our cash position continues to be extremely strong with a cash balance of INR1,121 crores, as of March 2026.

items.statement: Dividend policy exists; board will decide on payouts; growth remains priority, M&A considered if it drives growth.
items.quote: The other facet, Prolin, if you're asking me that, you know, does the company have a dividend policy? The answer is yes. Are we going to look at something like this? I cannot answer because that's a consideration that the board will take.

items.statement: Non-SLCM B2B team completed first full year of operations; higher-capacity batching plants (4-series, 7-series) and 38m/44m boom pumps gaining traction.
items.quote: We've witnessed that our 4-series and 7-series pumps have done very well, our 38-meter and 44-meter boom pumps have done well. So I think these combinations are doing well, and we do believe that this year the benefit will accrue on the work that has been done in the last full year.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 revenue growth expected at 15-17%
items.quote: Full year, we expect to grow by 15% to 17%.

items.statement: Firm FY27 guidance deferred to next quarter due to geopolitical uncertainty
items.quote: We are closely monitoring these dynamics and will provide firm guidance as our visibility improves and we are better positioned to assess the impact of student flow, conversion rate and our revenue profile.

items.statement: Aggregate demand for overseas education steadily increasing despite visa policy shifts
items.quote: Importantly, aggregate demand for overseas education around the world continues to steadily increase. It is just that supply has tightened in some particular destination markets while still continuing to loosen in others.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 172 bps to 27%; Q4 FY26 margin expanded 467 bps to 24%
items.quote: EBITDA for FY26 came around 2,824 million, growing around 31% year-on-year. With margin expanding 172 basis points to 27%, a clear demonstration of operating leverage embedded in our business model.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 margin boost partly from favorable GBP/INR movement, deemed transitional
items.quote: At the same time, because of positive currency movement in our favor, the pound has gone up substantially. This has resulted in a higher profit in Q4, which we feel is transitional in nature and it will even out gradually.

items.statement: Normalized gross margin steady state 28-30%; EBITDA margin guidance deferred to next quarter
items.quote: We are talking about the gross margin between 28%-30%.

items.statement: Applications processed grew 43% YoY to 3.94 lakh; active agents up 36% to 5,389; enrollments up 14%
items.quote: Application process grew 43% YoY to 3,94,000 plus applicants. Our active agent base expanded the 36% year-on-year to 5,389 agents and student enrollment grew 14% year-on-year, reflecting sustained operating momentum across our global education platform.

items.statement: Committed USD 2.5 million over five years to EduMentor AI platform
items.quote: In March 2026, we committed USD 2.5 million over five years roadmap to the EduMentor project, an AI-driven platform for student university matching, mentorship and decision support, led by Mr. Dishant Kharbanda, a distinguished Edtech leader and IIM Calcutta alumnus.

items.statement: Onboarded entire Medway Educational Consultant team to operationalize New Zealand business at scale
items.quote: In April 2026, we operationalized our new New Zealand business at scale through onboarding of the entire Medway Educational Consultant Team, bringing dedicated on-ground leadership and admission capabilities to one of our new destination markets.

items.statement: 67-70% of agent commissions paid in GBP, limiting FX gain to repatriated portion
items.quote: 67% to 70% of our expenses, agent commission, we pay directly to the agent in pounds only. So, the FOREX gain comes only of the part which part we bring it to India.

items.statement: Expanding ancillary services: accommodation, student loan, visa, insurance and FOIAs
items.quote: Expanded ancillary services including accommodation, student loan, visa, insurance and FOIAs.

items.statement: Top 10 university partners contribute 66% of revenue; 400+ institutional partnerships with 5+ year tenure for top 30
items.quote: Our top 10 university partners account for 66% of our revenue, reflecting both the depth of those relationships and the importance of trust and track record in how universities allocate recruitment resources.

items.statement: UK Agent Quality Framework raises regulatory barriers, favoring mature platforms like Crizac
items.quote: The UK recently introduced a comprehensive regulatory regime for student recruitment platforms, such as Crizac, known as the Agent Quality Framework. It's quite a burdensome, heavy regulatory regime. And this means that only mature, sophisticated platforms are in a position to comply with it and operate at large scale.

items.statement: Visa policy tightening in Canada and US redirecting demand to UK, Ireland, Germany, New Zealand
items.quote: Canada and the United States have both tightened their immigration and study visa frameworks and this has caused visible shifts in student flow patterns globally. This has created displacement in some corridors while simultaneously redirecting demands to the UK, Republic of Ireland, Germany, New Zealand and other markets where policy remains welcoming of international students.

items.statement: Revenue primarily GBP-denominated; average FY26 GBP/INR rate 116 vs 105 in FY25
items.quote: We have taken 116 as the average while preparing the financials.

items.statement: Cash conversion 56% of EBITDA in FY26, moderated by INR 55 cr termination fee
items.quote: Our net cash flow from operating activity as proportion to EBITDA stood at 56% for FY26, moderated by one of termination fees payment of around INR 55 crores.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with net cash of INR 4,674 million as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: I am pleased to report that Crizac remains debt-free with healthy net cash flow position of 4674 million as on 31st March 2026.

items.statement: No fund raise mentioned; strong cash generation funds inorganic pipeline
items.quote: The company is generating more cash than the investment which is required for its growth.

items.statement: Four acquisitions in FY26: StudiesPlanet (LATAM), Global Tree Careers (51% stake, B2C), EduMentor (AI), Medway (New Zealand)
items.quote: Taken together, these four transactions expected within a year demonstrate our deliberate use of acquisition to compress timelines for geographical entry and capabilities built out.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 dividend of Rs 8/share declared, payout ~64% vs committed 40%
items.quote: Anchored by our cash generation, the board declared a dividend of Rs. 8 per equity share in Q4 FY26, representing a dividend payout of approximately 64% which is higher than our committed 40% what we have said earlier.

items.statement: Board open to evaluating buybacks alongside dividends
items.quote: For sure. We would be looking at all the pros and cons, and we will do whatever it is for the beneficial of all our shareholders.

items.statement: Promoter holding ~80%; two years to meet SEBI 75% minimum public shareholding
items.quote: We still have two more years. So, whenever we find that the market is right, we will look into it. But we are not in a hurry to get it diluted as we have two years more with us.

items.statement: Student enrollment growth 14% YoY in FY26; targeting similar or higher growth ahead
items.quote: We have been growing around 10% to 20% year-on-year. This year, the student number has grown by 14%. Going forward, we look to grow by the similar or higher percentage.

items.statement: UK revenue concentration ~97% currently; target to reduce below 60% in two years via Australia, Canada, US, New Zealand
items.quote: Based on the diversification to multiple new geographies as a destination market, we believe our concentration for UK will go down. And in next two years, we will prefer the numbers of a percentage of contribution from UK to go below 60% while that of rest of the world should go roughly 40% for us.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty and visa policy changes create near-term visibility challenges; 6-9 month revenue visibility
items.quote: We get a visibility of roughly between 6 to 9 months. So, currently we are wrapping up with September intake and we will get a visibility more of Jan intake in the next couple of months, which are two major intakes for overall recruitment.

items.statement: Australia university contracts require multi-year negotiations; meaningful recruitment expected in 3-6 months
items.quote: We believe we have already done most of the work. We have started getting some of the contracts from Australia and we believe over the next three to six months, we should be able to start recruiting and become a reasonable recruiter for all the Australian institutions.

items.statement: UK graduate visa reduction to 18 months already baked into student plans; UK remains competitive with 1.5:1 study-to-work ratio
items.quote: The UK remains extremely attractive because a master's degree can be completed in 12 months, and then the graduate visa is 18 months. So, what students look at is the ratio of time from time studying to time to work or look for finding a job. And on that basis, the UK still has a ratio of 1.5:1. So, it remains extremely competitive globally.

items.statement: Management expects FY27 to deliver stronger growth than FY26 but declines to provide specific numerical guidance.
items.quote: While we would prefer not to provide a specific guidance at this stage, we believe FY'27 has the potential to deliver strong growth -- stronger growth in comparison to '26.

items.statement: Management projects better revenue growth in FY27 than FY26, citing strong order books from key customers like Hitachi, ABB, Siemens, GE, and Toshiba.
items.quote: So, it is very difficult to give you in figures, but as I said, it will be -- we are projecting better than the last year growth also.

items.statement: Demand environment remains supportive with structural tailwinds from infrastructure, electrification, and renewable energy investments.
items.quote: The demand environment remains supportive, our capability continues to strengthen, and our team is fully aligned towards delivering consistent and sustainable growth.

items.statement: Key customers are reportedly booked for at least the next five years, and the company is expanding into railways, defense, and government tenders via GeM portal.
items.quote: I think all my current customers are booked for the next at least five years. This is what I have been told. And plus other we are also trying to enter into other sectors wherein we are adding more portfolio in railways, in other places.

items.statement: Margins are considered sustainable and expected to improve with scale, capacity utilization, operating leverage, and cost optimization.
items.quote: Looking at the current scenario, we believe our margins are sustainable and also improve as we achieve greater scale in the business. The volumes increase and capacity utilization improves as it is done.

items.statement: Management is very optimistic about margin improvement driven by operational efficiency, productivity, and operating leverage from expansion.
items.quote: So, in this scenario, we see good business in front of us and we also continue to focus on productivity improvement and cost optimization initiatives also in the business.

items.statement: New expansion commissioned in March FY26 provides enhanced capacity for FY27; near-term benefits visible, larger financial impact expected medium-term.
items.quote: Financial Year '27 will be our full year where we will have the benefit of enhanced capacity available and throughout the year this provides us a very strong platform for growth.

items.statement: Capex expansion machinery commissioned in March FY26; strategic inventory built to feed new machines; benefits starting near-term, larger impact medium-term.
items.quote: We have commissioned all our machinery in the month of March, the expansion of capital -- the capex. And we wanted to keep inventory so that that also continues to feed our new machines and everything.

items.statement: Price variation clauses with most customers pass through raw material and fuel cost changes monthly, limiting margin impact.
items.quote: We have this -- clause with them, wherein the price variation, all the raw material prices that are increasing is price passed on to them on monthly basis currently.

items.statement: Added two prominent export customers in FY26: QAG (Australia) and Trench (Europe); also expanded supply to additional Hitachi factories.
items.quote: Last year we had added two new customer in export front. One is QAG, it is an Australian-based multinational, and one is Trench from Europe.

items.statement: Key customers include Hitachi, ABB, Siemens, GE, Toshiba; strategy focuses on long-term relationships and expanding share of wallet within existing accounts.
items.quote: I would also like to mention our customers such as we have good customers such as Hitachi, ABB, Siemens, GE, Toshiba. So, they are also having good orders and the same will translate to us.

items.statement: Export presence in Europe, Mexico, US, and Australia improving; meaningful potential seen; actively discussing with more multinational customers.
items.quote: On the export side, we believe that there is a meaningful potential going forward and we are actively exploring opportunities. We are in discussion with few customers.

items.statement: Operating cash flow turned negative in FY26 due to strategic working capital build: advanced vendor payments, higher inventory, and March collection delays.
items.quote: While the company delivered healthy revenue last year, our operating cash flow was impacted mainly due to higher working capital during the year.

items.statement: Collection efficiency improving post-March; supplier payment cycles normalized; initiatives underway to optimize inventory and improve cash conversion.
items.quote: We have taken multiple initiatives also in the company, improving the collection efficiency, optimizing inventory management also, we are already working on it, and better planning, I would say.

items.statement: Proactive vendor management with advanced payments secured raw material availability and locked pricing amid geopolitical supply chain uncertainty.
items.quote: We took a very proactive approach with our vendor ecosystem. We worked closely with them and supported them through faster and advanced payments to secure raw material availability, lock pricing wherever is possible.

items.statement: FY26 total income grew 19.50% to INR 36.19 crores; EBITDA INR 6.22 crores; profit after tax not fully stated in transcript.
items.quote: For FY'26, our total income grew by 19.50% to INR36.19 crores, reflecting steady business momentum. EBITDA stood at INR6.22 crores, and our profit after tax was at

items.statement: Growth driven primarily by volume increase from strong customer demand and improved execution; pricing impact very limited.
items.quote: The growth was because of volume, which supported from strong customer demand, improving our executions also, execution capabilities also. The pricing impact was relatively very, very, very limited.

items.statement: Varun Sharda is second-generation promoter, working in the factory for 18 years; father started the business.
items.quote: So, no, my father started this business and I am the second generation in the business, but I am working in this factory since last I think now 18 years.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty and war-related disruptions affected supply chains, raw material availability, pricing, and delivery schedules in FY26.
items.quote: One of the most important factors during the year was uncertainty in the global environment, including geopolitical situation and war-related disruptions.

items.statement: Company listed on BSE SME platform in FY26; listing improved visibility, governance, and positioning for larger opportunities.
items.quote: Our recent listing has given us a stronger platform for our next phase of growth. It has improved our visibility, strengthened our governance framework, and positioned us as large opportunities with greater confidence.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guided at 25-30%, EBITDA margin 18-21%, PAT margin 8-10%, rent-paying area addition 1.5-2 million sq ft annually
items.quote: And that would translate to the same occupancy EBITDA. So, the top-line growth, you can again see in the range of 25% to 30%. And my CAPEX would also be in the range of the same factors, as I said if I am adding so my per square feet of the CAPEX is about 1650.

items.statement: FY27 CAPEX per sq ft ~INR 1,650; solar CAPEX INR 125-150 cr for 30-35 MW addition
items.quote: So, next year, we plan to give you some kind of bifurcation of the solar so that it is much clearer on how much CAPEX or what kind of investment we are doing on the solar and sustainability initiative.

items.statement: FY26 CAPEX INR 414 cr: interiors INR 248-256 cr, design-build INR 50 cr, solar INR 73 cr, vendor payments INR 30 cr
items.quote: So, INR 256 crores to INR 248 crores is about the CAPEX interior s. Your design-and-build, we spent about INR 50 crores. Our solar investment was about INR 73 crores, which is for the captive use and is generating close to INR 22 crores to INR 23 crores of savings per year

items.statement: Added ~1.6 million sq ft rent-paying area and 15 new centers in FY26; steady-state occupancy improved 87% to 88%
items.quote: During the year, we have added close to 1.6 million square feet in rent-paying area and launched 15 new centers.

items.statement: Area under management 9.66 million sq ft to convert to operational over next 18-24 months
items.quote: So, the area under management is about 9.66. So, it is under different stages, and it should get into the operational stage in about the next 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 18% to 21%, PAT margin 5% to 9% in FY26
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded from 18% in FY25 to 21% in FY26. PAT margin improved from 5% to 9% over the same period.

items.statement: Revenue per occupied seat ~INR 192/month in FY26; expect 5-10% increase in FY27 from 5-6% contractual escalation and premium space mix
items.quote: So, typically, about INR 192 is the kind of average revenue realization we have for the last year. And most of our contracts come with 5% to 6% rental inflation built in.

items.statement: Fit-out cost per sq ft rose from INR 1,550 to INR 1,650 due to 5-7% material cost increase; absorbing cost, not passing to clients
items.quote: So, what was INR 15.50 is now trending towards INR 16.50. But it is a small increase and that too it is a CAPEX kind of increase. So, we are pretty much at this point in time absorbing it.

items.statement: CY2025 gross office absorption 82.5M sq ft; Q1 CY2026 20.7M sq ft; expect 5% higher absorption in CY2026; Flex operators 23%, GCCs 44% of absorption
items.quote: And the way last year has gone, I think we'll see a repeat of that happening this year also. And within this, Bangalore leads the pack with about 29%-30% market share. And the absorption that we are seeing for this year looks like 5% higher than last year's absorption.

items.statement: No AI impact seen yet; campus hiring robust; premiumization driving demand for managed offices; GCC diversity expanding beyond BFSI
items.quote: So, far, we have not seen the impact. And when I talk about GCC, one thing we have to appreciate is that, for example, US banks. The US has 6,000 banks. As of date, I don't think even 60 banks have come into India.

items.statement: VAS revenue share rose from 12% to 15% in FY26; guided to 17-18% in FY27; VAS margins 10-15% vs 18-20% for space
items.quote: We expect the contribution of VASP revenue to be total now, we cannot predict what is one-time or recurring, but we expect the total contribution of VASP revenue to increase by 2% to 2% in the coming year. So, from 15% we see the going up till about 17% to 18%.

items.statement: Tenant mix stable: IT/ITES ~49%, Indian Enterprises ~58%; GCCs diversifying into manufacturing, logistics, healthcare; hub-and-spoke model with MNCs
items.quote: So, I think this will broadly remain the same, honestly speaking, in terms of vertical split. As I mentioned to you, the GCCs are throwing up a lot more diversity in terms of manufacturing, logistics, healthcare, and all of that.

items.statement: Solar capacity: 20 MW Karnataka operational, 4 MW Maharashtra operational, 2.7 MW Tamil Nadu by next quarter; targeting 30-35 MW addition in FY27 across same three states
items.quote: So, about 30-35 megawatts is what we see will be the addition. And predominantly, we are focused on three states, as I mentioned to you, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Maharashtra, for the coming year.

items.statement: Solar savings INR 22-23 cr/year from current plants; accelerated depreciation (40%) to benefit PAT
items.quote: Our solar investment was about INR 73 crores, which is for the captive use and is generating close to INR 22 crores to INR 23 crores of savings per year.

items.statement: Lease payments to grow in line with revenue (25-30%); security deposits for new leases increased; IPO proceeds reallocated INR 187 cr to design-build, solar, deposits, adjacent ventures
items.quote: It is in line with the revenue growth. I said, yes, it would be definitely, Adhidev, in line with the revenue growth. The top line would be in line with 25% to 30%, I said.

items.statement: CRISIL A+ Stable rating maintained; IPO debt repayment unchanged; security deposits for landlord LOIs now part of capital allocation
items.quote: Backed by expanding profitability, stronger cash generation, continued sustainability progress, and our CRISIL A+ Stable rating, we remain confident in our ability to grow with scale, discipline, and profitability.

items.statement: IPO primary raise INR 610 cr; INR 462 cr earmarked for CAPEX; INR 187 cr reallocated to design-build (INR 55 cr), solar (INR 16 cr), security deposits (INR 52 cr), adjacent ventures (INR 64 cr)
items.quote: Now, in that, the biggest chunk was INR 462 crores towards CAPEX. So, what we have now done is we have basically looked at that reallocation of that CAPEX.

items.statement: Occupancy: portfolio 80-85%, mature centers 85-90%; Q4 FY26 end-month 81%, full-year average 84%
items.quote: But if you see, the more relevant metric is the average occupancy during the year, which is about 84%. Therefore, the actual dip is only 1%, not 4%.

items.statement: Rent-paying area additions ~1-1.25 lakh sq ft/month; rent-yielding area ~1-1.25 lakh sq ft/month at 80% occupancy
items.quote: If you look at, say, we are adding 1.25 lakh, 80% of that is 1 lakh. So, that is what you are seeing, that between about 1 lakh and 1.25 lakh per month will be additions in the RYA.

items.statement: Geopolitical volatility, AI impact uncertainty, Tier-2 supply quality and landlord maturity risks; disciplined growth in key micro-markets only
items.quote: In a year marked by geopolitical volatility and broader uncertainty around the impact of AI on businesses and workspaces, our performance demonstrates the resilience of our business model.

items.statement: Institutional supply share rose from 16% to 18% of portfolio; focusing on Grade A tech parks in core micro-markets; avoiding high-vacancy areas like Manesar, North Bangalore, Navi Mumbai
items.quote: And most of these global capability centers prefer to go to tech parks and larger office spaces. So, our institutional uptake, which was about 16% of our portfolio, has now become 18%.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; team includes CEO, COO, CFO, Head IR, AVP Marketing
items.quote: From the Management, we have with us Mr. Rishi Das – CEO, Ms. Meghna Agarwal – COO, Mr. Pawan Jain – CFO, Mr. Vikas Agarwal – Head (IR) and Mr. Vamsi Chatrathi – AVP (Marketing).

items.statement: MiQube platform recorded 1.4M transactions; new space management and vehicle pooling modules gaining traction
items.quote: Over the last year, MiQube recorded 1.4 million transactions, reflecting growth adoption across our client base.

items.statement: FY27 volume growth guided at 30-40% and value growth at 60-70%
items.quote: So this year, i.e current coming year, it will be around 30% to 40% growth in terms of volume and around 60%-70% growth in terms of value

items.statement: Sustainable PAT margin guided at around 4%
items.quote: This margin would be around 4% and all, which we've been maintaining that 4% plus and all.

items.statement: Revenue guidance of INR 3,000-3,500 crores for FY27 with 35-40% growth
items.quote: So next year like around we expecting a turnover of around INR 3,000 crores to INR 3,500 crores and with 35% to 40% growth.

items.statement: Export share targeted to increase from 10% to 20%
items.quote: So I told you like this year will be like from 5% to we are going to go up to 10% or maybe more. Sorry, from 10% to 20%.

items.statement: Marol facility adding ~4,000 kg/annum capacity, Jaipur facility adding ~1,200 kg/annum
items.quote: Our existing Andheri manufacturing facility with an installed capacity of approximately 2,700 kilo per annum has been operating at healthy utilization levels in line with the growth of our new Marol facility in Mumbai, which will add approximately 4,000 kilo per annum of manufacturing capacity. In addition, the 1,200 kilo per annum capacity addition announced during an IPO at Jaipur, continues to

items.statement: Marol facility expected to start in ~1 month, ramping to 100 kg/month initially; Jaipur facility expected by Sep-Oct
items.quote: So see, our new factory is almost ready, which is going to be like in a month or so for Marol factory, and I guess Jaipur factory should be starting by around September, October now. So initially to start with, like I expect this Marol factory initially few months to start with, it's going to be around 100 kgs per month and reaching very soon we'll be reaching till 4,000 kilos.

items.statement: Total installed capacity to reach ~7,900 kg/annum after expansions
items.quote: Once operational, this addition will take our total installed manufacturing capacity to nearly 7,900 kilogram per annum, positioning us strongly for the next phase of scalable growth.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization at ~65%
items.quote: Our present capacity is around 65%.

items.statement: Current monthly volume at 145-150 kg
items.quote: So we have given out our volumes on a quarterly basis in our presentation around 145 kilos to 150 kilos.

items.statement: Demand resilient across key markets and segments despite elevated gold prices; strong traction in wedding and occasion-led jewellery
items.quote: Despite elevated gold prices during the year, overall demand trends remained res ilient across key markets and customer segments. We continue to witness healthy transactions, particularly in wedding and occasions-led jewellery categories

items.statement: Structural shift from unorganized to organized jewellery retail creating outsourcing opportunities
items.quote: The structural shift from unorganized to organized jewellery retail continues to gather pace, which is creating meaningful outsourcing opportunities for manufacturers with proven execution capabilities

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 10.17% (+306 bps YoY); FY26 EBITDA margin 9.86% (+173 bps YoY)
items.quote: EBITDA margins for FY26 stood at 9.86% as compared to 8.13% in FY25, improving by 173 basis points.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 PAT margin 7.88%; FY26 PAT margin 6.94% (+205 bps YoY)
items.quote: PAT margins for FY26 stood at 6.94% as compared to 4.89% in FY25, improving by 205 basis pointsY-o-Y.

items.statement: Core business PAT margin ~3.5-4%; FY26 PAT included inventory gains from gold price appreciation
items.quote: See basically my core margin is around 3.5% to 4%, that's for sure. We are not speculating on the gold market price movement whether it goes North or South. So we don't want to speculate where we wi ll head to. The 7% that we have projected last year, it had an element of a surge in the gold price, additionally, maybe 3% to 3.5%, which we are not considering as of now.

items.statement: Entered machine-made plain gold jewellery segment; launched Mangalsutra and Turkish jewellery categories
items.quote: We entered the machine -made plain gold jewellery s egment, which opens a meaningful growth opportunity for the company. We also introduced Mangalsutra, as a new product category and we are witnessing encouraging customer response. Additionally, we also developed Turkish jewellery to be produced at our Marol facility and have onboard skilled professionals directly from Turkey to ensure authenticit

items.statement: Do not supply to Titan/Tanishq; plan to approach them with new factories
items.quote: No, we don't supply jewellery to Titan. Anshul Saigal: Is that a customer Pankajkumar Jagawat: New factories are coming up, so we are going to approach Titan and lot of new clients who are not on our Board. So they are on our list now, which very soon we are going to be on

items.statement: Import duty restored to 15% from 6%; management sees no demand impact as 15% was long-standing rate
items.quote: So one year back also there was 15% duty. So it didn't affect the consumer deman d. So government had reduced it from 15% to 6% last year only, and again they have come up to 15%. So I don't think so there would be any problem in demand and all. For many years it was 15%.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions (Iran-Israel-US) driving gold price volatility; Dubai subsidiary delayed; gold price decline could reduce margins
items.quote: Due to again Iran war with Israel and US and all, so things are not good, means lot of volatility is there and things are not good across the world. So that is what we are expecting. We are not giving any hopes to the shareholders because there is lot of issues throughout the world, geopolitical things. items.quote: In this calendar year, we have two contracts that we are expecting to come for renewal. One is a small contract for just two clinics in Uttarakhand. That's in the process. And then later part of the year, we should get Andhra Pradesh, one of the phases for renewal.

items.statement: Operates in 5 countries (India, Nepal, Philippines, Uzbekistan, Saudi Arabia JV); Philippines peso +5%, Uzbek currency +7% favorable forex impact on RPT
items.quote: Philippines peso moved favorably by 5%, Uzbek currency moved favorably by 7%, helping our RPT.

items.statement: Saudi Arabia JV in investment phase; first clinic in Riyadh to launch within 2 months; large MoH/Ministry of Defense tender at EOI stage, moving to RFP in a couple of quarters
items.quote: Our first clinic in Saudi Arabia at Riyadh Hospital is all set to be launched within two months to showcase our clinical excellence. Overall, we are optimistic about creating a large dialysis business in Saudi Arabia, but we need to be patient as things sometimes do not move as fast as we expect.

items.statement: FY26 guests (active patients) 36,981, up 11.8% YoY; treatments 38.4 lakh, up 16.6%; RPT INR2,598, up 13.3%
items.quote: As of March 2026, our active guest counts stood at 36,981 compared to 33,076, as of March 2025, representing a healthy growth of 11.8%. Moving to treatment volumes, which represent the total number of dialysis sessions performed during the period. For FY '26, treatment volumes reached 38,44,658 sessions compared to 32,97,447 sessions in FY '25, registering a growth of 16.6%.

items.statement: Adjusted PAT grew 74.6% to INR128.3 cr; PAT margin improved 310 bps to 12.8%
items.quote: Adjusted PAT for the year stood at INR128.3 crores compared to INR73.5 crores in the previous year, reflecting a strong growth of 74.6%. PAT margin also improved by 310 basis points from 9.7% to 12.8%.

items.statement: One-time ECL provision of INR10 cr in Q4 on two aged accounts (4-5 years old) from abundant caution; money still expected to be recovered
items.quote: At the end of the year, we identified two accounts where we wanted to take a one-time provision out of abundant caution. These two accounts still we believe the money will come, but from an ECL model point of view, we took a provision just to prevent the likelihood of a future profit surprise.

items.statement: Saudi Arabia expansion dependent on tender outcomes and regulatory timelines; NUPCO tender did not translate to business; MoH/Ministry of Defense tender at EOI stage
items.quote: A NUPCO tender came out a year ago, in which we participated and came out strong, but NUPCO was not the end user of the service, hence it has not translated into business yet. This takes time. The good news is the large Ministry of Health and Ministry of Defense dialysis tender has recently been issued with clear visibility of patient volume. Right now, it is on the EOI stage, but it will soon mov

items.statement: First global dialysis network to effectively use AI in core operations; Reformmed.AI deployed in 50 clinics, expanding to full network
items.quote: We are happy to state that we are the first global dialysis network to effectively use AI in its core operations. Our team at NephroPlus has created Reformmed.AI application to effectively monitor numerous core operational elements across a distributed dialysis network. This has already been implemented successfully in 50 clinics at NephroPlus as of today, and of course, we'll be expanding this to

items.statement: Committed to 100% focus on dialysis; not exploring adjacencies; CKD prevention platform in early stages as funnel for dialysis
items.quote: we'll stay focused on dialysis services delivery. So, we are not looking at exploring any of the adjacencies right now and we would stay 100% focused on dialysis delivery and expanding our footprint

items.statement: Management targets 40-50 gross new clinics in India and 12-15 in Philippines for FY27, excluding large PPP or M&A.
items.quote: As I said that in India, we are fairly confident of delivering a 40 to 50 range of gross new clinics and Philippines of 12 to 15 range.

items.statement: FY26 capex was INR165 crore, up 50% YoY; no specific FY27 capex guidance given, but INR500 crore cash available for disciplined ROCE-accretive deployment.
items.quote: I think in terms of capex, in FY 2026, we had a capex of INR165 crores compared to INR116 crores the year before. So, our capex almost grew by 50% in FY 2026 compared to FY 2025.

items.statement: Capex per bed: India INR10-11 lakh (3.5-4 yr payback), Philippines INR40-45 lakh (1-1.5 yr), Uzbekistan INR18-20 lakh (1-1.5 yr).
items.quote: The capex per bed in India is about INR10 lakhs to INR11 lakhs with a payback period of about three and a half, four years. Philippines, it is INR40 lakhs to INR45 lakhs with a payback period of one, one and a half years.

items.statement: Philippines market has ~900 centers; organized players hold ~250, leaving a long tail of 550-600 unorganized clinics for roll-up acquisitions.
items.quote: Philippines is a 900 dialysis center market with 250 if you take out which are with the organized player. It has a long tail of unorganized, 550-600.

items.statement: India treatment volume grew 17% YoY; management emphasizes volume over center count due to opening/closing variability.
items.quote: And as we can see, the treatment volume has grown by 17% year-on-year and that's the metric that you should look at because the center has too much variability both in terms of the number of beds and the dynamics of opening and closing.

items.statement: Dialysis pricing is stepwise, not annual; last CGHS increase was 35% after 11 years, PhilHealth ~58% after a decade; no large price increase expected in FY27, RPT changes driven by geography mix.
items.quote: So, in this coming year, we are not expecting any large price increase, but RPT change will be a factor of geography mix. If our international geography as we keep expanding, that would translate to the net RPT increase at the platform level.

items.statement: Consolidated RPT rose 13.3% YoY (INR2,292 to INR2,598) driven by international mix shift (32% to 42%), favorable forex (PHP +5%, UZS +7%), and full-year impact of 58% Philippines price hike.
items.quote: The RPT went from INR2,292 to INR2,598, which is about 13.3% increase. As I mentioned in my opening remarks, there are three key drivers. One is obviously the international mix going from 32% to 42%.

items.statement: Other expense spike in Q4 FY26 driven primarily by INR10 crore ECL provision; yearly increase also from IT/platform investment and R&M accounting change from capex to opex.
items.quote: The other expense has predominantly moved by the ECL provision of INR10 crores that I previously mentioned. That was the primary driver of the other expense movement this quarter.

items.statement: Uttarakhand PPP contract at renewal tendering stage; decision expected in 2-4 months if normal pace, but extensions possible.
items.quote: If it goes with the normal pace, we could expect the tender to be kind of reaching a conclusion in a two to four months' time period. But if it gets postponed due to any reason, then there could be extensions that one can expect.

items.statement: Recent Philippines acquisition: mid-size center with 600-800 sessions/month and ~15 beds; plan 12-15 roll-ups in Philippines in coming year.
items.quote: We had done as I said we would be looking at doing a 10 -- anything between 12 to 15 roll-ups in the Philippines in the coming year as well.

items.statement: GLP-1 drugs cause ~0.25% drop in new dialysis patients in developed markets; no impact on emerging markets for 10-15 years; NephroPlus TAM unaffected.
items.quote: When I talk to the nephrologists in the US and UK and let's say European countries, they are talking about a 0.25% drop in new patient additions because GLP-1s are managing the CKD early stage more effectively and hence the delay of onset of dialysis is happening.

items.statement: Philippines price hike attracts more competition (global and Indian), but 600-clinic unorganized tail supports multi-decadal roll-up runway; regulatory complexity is a barrier to entry.
items.quote: So, we expect more competition, there will be more competition, but it wo n't dampen our growth plans by any means in the long run

items.statement: India added 21 net clinics in FY26 (468 vs 447); majority captive, 5-6 greenfield; no large PPP signed.
items.quote: So we had majority of them captive while there were five to six standalone greenfield units that we started, but majority of them were captive units only and we did not sign any large PPP project last year too.

items.statement: Saudi JV in investment phase; INR3 crore quarterly loss run-rate continues until new tender (at EOI stage) materializes in a few quarters; line-by-line consolidation blocked by partner participative rights.
items.quote: Saudi, as we mentioned, we are on the in the investment phase and there is just recently a new contract or new tender which has been just released and it's at the EOI stage, which will take couple of quarters to take shape.

items.statement: Enpidia training academies replicated in Philippines; India-Philippines talent pipeline is strategic advantage vs global peers for nurse/paramedic supply.
items.quote: And now given that we are operating in India and in Philippines with a comfortable scale, a large scale, I think that puts us in a good competitive edge over our other global peers because globally, India and Philippines are the supplier for nurses and the paramedic staff.

items.statement: Nepal: 6 centers reclassified from branch to subsidiary; economics unchanged, same dynamics as India.
items.quote: Nepal, we have about six centers currently and I think the dynamics of Nepal are very similar to India. So, I think in terms of modeling or in terms of sort of baking it into the model, you can assume the same dynamics as there are in India.

items.statement: Targets INR200 crore turnover in FY27, implying 40-45% growth over FY26
items.quote: We are targeting a turnover of INR200 crores in FY27, which will translate into a growth of approximately 40%-45% over FY26 figures.

items.statement: Expects turnover of more than INR300 crores in FY28
items.quote: So, in the next financial year, we are expecting turnover of more than INR300 crores.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin to improve by 1-2 percentage points in FY27
items.quote: The margin profile will be slightly better than the last year. We can also scale from a larger turnover and expecting 1 or 2 percentage points higher margin this year.

items.statement: Current order book stands at approximately INR200 crores
items.quote: Our current order book stood at approximately INR200 crores, which provides strong revenue visibility for the coming period and reflects continued customer confidence and deep business momentum.

items.statement: Order book split 50% product and 50% project
items.quote: 50% is product and 50% is project.

items.statement: Expects almost 90% of current order book to be executed in FY27
items.quote: Most of the, almost 90% will be completed this year only, because the order book, now, the new projects we are getting, we are going to complete, we are now planning to complete all of them quickly.

items.statement: Booked INR44 crores of new orders in FY27 so far (as of May)
items.quote: the order booking for the current financial year so far, we have booked order of INR44 crores already.

items.statement: FY26 capex of INR4 crores from internal accruals and bank loan; further INR2 crores ongoing
items.quote: The capex in '26, we have done around INR4 crores of capex we have done, which has been from our own internal accrual as well as bank loan. And there is a further capex ongoing of INR2 crores

items.statement: Total capex since last year approximately INR8 crores, including INR1 crore from IPO proceeds
items.quote: So, the total capex since last year would be approximately INR8 crores. Nishita Shanklesha: Okay. Madhusudan Sarda: After which only INR1 crores is from the IPO

items.statement: Manufacturing capacity to reach 18,000 metric tons by September 2026 from current 12,000
items.quote: our production capacity currently is 12,000 and 3,000 metric tons of machinery already is on the way. So, 15,000 will be there and then 18,000, our capacity will become 18,000 by September 2026.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization around 80%
items.quote: We have a high-capacity utilization of around 80 %, supported by more than 170 old machineries and strong project execution capabilities

items.statement: Long-term demand outlook for geotechnical and infrastructure solutions remains strong
items.quote: We believe the long -term demand outlook for geotechnical and infrastructure solutions remains strong, and we are well-positioned to participate in this growth opportunity.

items.statement: H2 FY26 EBITDA margin improved to 15.91% from 12% in FY24
items.quote: EBITDA margins improved to 15.91 %.

items.statement: Insulates from steel and polymer price fluctuations by booking large orders with suppliers and customers
items.quote: what we do to safeguard us from price fluctuations is by booking large orders with our customers and with our suppliers. That ensures that they also have a continued business because it is, the manufacturing process is a continuous line for them.

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio around 0.7; finance cost INR4.7 crores in FY26, expected to remain at similar level in FY27
items.quote: Actually, our debt equity ratio has become very less now. Around 0.7 is our debt equity ratio. And the finance cost this year has been INR4.7 crores. And we expect it to be around this level only.

items.statement: Directly deals with customers through qualified engineer marketing team; no dealers or distributors
items.quote: We directly deal with the customers. We do not believe in having a line of -- another line of people, because they will not be able to technically understand the requirements of the customer.

items.statement: FY26 total income INR115.58 crores, up 14.15% YoY; EBITDA INR17.79 crores, up 15.75%; Net profit INR8.11 crores, up 31.04%
items.quote: For FY26, total income stood at INR115.58 crores, registering a growth of 14.15 % year-on-year. EBITDA for the year increased to INR17.79 crores from INR15.37 crores, reflecting a growth of 15.75%. Net profit grew to INR8.11 crores compared to INR6.19 crores in registering a strong growth of 31.04 %.

items.statement: H2 FY26 total income INR74.87 crores, up 29.44% YoY; EBITDA INR11.91 crores, up 72.09%; Net profit INR5.69 crores, up 62.53%
items.quote: Total income for H2 FY26 stood at INR74.87 crores, as against INR57.84 crores in H2 FY25, registering a growth of 29.44 %. EBITDA increased to INR11.91 crores, reflecting a strong growth of 72.09%, while EBITDA margins improved to 15.91 %. Net profit for the half -year stood at INR5.69 crores, registering a strong growth of 62.53%.

items.statement: INR15 crores work-in-progress could not be billed in FY26 due to customer measurement delays, muting revenue growth
items.quote: There is a work in progress in our project amounting to approximately INR15 crores, which could not get built during the financial year. So, that revenue loss has resulted in this muted growth from our estimated 20% to around 15%.

items.statement: Built up engineering team and machinery fleet over past years to support growth; new factory in Assam operational
items.quote: We have built our factories. We have put up a new factory in Assam. So, we have now built up the required infrastructure to be able to drive the business that we need to do. We have similarly built our number of engineers that are required.

items.statement: Management aspires to continue the trajectory of the last three years with durable growth, operating leverage, and cash conversion, but declined to give prescriptive FY27 revenue or margin guidance.
items.quote: It's hard to kind of give prescriptive guidance at this point, but our aspiration is to kind of continue on the trajectory that we have been in the last 3 years.

items.statement: Net revenue retention remained best-in-class at 126% in FY26, marking the third consecutive year above 115%.
items.quote: Net revenue retention is a very important metric for us because it captures how existing customers expand with us over time. For starters, this is similar to the same-store sales metric, which is typically used. It has remained pretty healthy in the last 3 consecutive years, 122% in FY24, 127% in FY25 and 126% in FY26.

items.statement: Million-dollar customers grew 25% year-over-year from 28 to 35, indicating deepening enterprise relationships.
items.quote: Customers contributing more than $1 million in annual revenue for us increased from 28 to 35 during the year, which translates to roughly a 25% growth.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 800 basis points to 10% in FY26, with Q4 margin doubling to 10% from 5% a year ago.
items.quote: On the left, if you see adjusted EBITDA improved 800 basis points from 2% in FY25 to about 10% in FY 26. In Q4, the margin doubled from 5% to 10%.

items.statement: Total cost as a percentage of revenue declined 28 percentage points over two years to 90% in FY26, driven by sales & marketing and R&D leverage.
items.quote: Total cost as a percentage of revenue declined from about 118% in FY24 to 90% in FY26. So that's a 28-percentage point improvement over 2 years, while maintaining revenue growth at about 30%.

items.statement: Gross margin held steady at ~69% for the full year despite quarterly lumpiness; AI costs were a minor contributor to sequential compression.
items.quote: If you look at our gross margin over the last 3 years, we've got lumpiness in quarters, but full year is held steady at about 69%, with minor improvements.

items.statement: Management expects volume growth to offset modest CPM pressure, viewing gross margin compression as a speed bump, not a recurring signal.
items.quote: I think the way at least internally, when we are looking at our modelling, there is enough of a tailwind on the volume side to offset modest sort of compression on price. So, we believe that it will net out as a net tailwind.

items.statement: No material capex guidance given; operating cash flow improved 80% to INR 60 crores and free cash flow rose 29% to INR 38 crores in FY26.
items.quote: On the left, we've covered adjusted EBITDA, so I don't want to get into too much detail on that one. But if you see in the center, adjusted operating cash flow, excluding onetime items relating to IPO and share buyback went up from INR 34 crores to INR 60 crores, up 80% year-over-year.

items.statement: All three segments grew over 25% and each exceeds INR 250 crores: Streaming Unification 26% to INR 838 cr, Monetization 36% to INR 381 cr, Cloud Modernization 32% to INR 286 cr.
items.quote: Streaming unification grew 26% to INR 838 crores. Monetization and marketplace grew 36% to INR 381 crores and cloud modernization grew 32% to INR286 crores.

items.statement: NEWSPULSE, the first agentic AI product, signed its first paid customer and is running tens of POCs with traditional news networks globally.
items.quote: NEWSPULSE, our first agentic product, signed our first paid customer. It's early, but it is the first data point that AI work has been talking about is starting to convert and not just trials.

items.statement: NEWSPULSE pricing is outcome-driven, mixing fixed and transaction-based models; early indications show no gross margin impact.
items.quote: Having said that, we have not seen any major impact at this point in time, largely the way that's really working with customers today is on outcome-driven pricing models a nd having said that, today, the way customers are starting to engage is a mix of fixed plus some sort of an outcome-driven approach from a transaction standpoint

items.statement: Customer count rose to 492 in FY26 from 463 in FY25; net additions positive over three years despite quarterly churn from small-account cleanup.
items.quote: if you look at our customer count over the last 3 years, right, like it's been 396 in F Y '24, roughly 463 in FY '25 and about 492 in FY’26. So, the trajectory is positive

items.statement: Management sees no credible platform competitor targeting the glass-to-glass stack with comparable AI strategy and financial health; only single-point solutions observed.
items.quote: We are not seeing anybody specifically coming to what's Amagi's staple today as we see it, right? And again, this might change, it's dynamic market. But today, we don't see anybody really credible in the whole system.

items.statement: Revenue is largely USD-denominated; ~50% of costs are USD-denominated, creating a structural net tailwind; hedging is occasional and transactional.
items.quote: From a cost lens, the direct cost, which is roughly 30% and about another sort of 20% is sort of USD denominated for the sales teams. So, on $100 revenue you're talking about $50 of U.S.-denominated sort of cost.

items.statement: Cash conversion improving; adjusted operating cash flow up 80% YoY to INR 60 cr, free cash flow up 29% to INR 38 cr; intra-quarter timing variations noted.
items.quote: On the right, you see that free cash flow improved from INR 29 crores to INR 38 crores, up 29% as well. There will be intra-quarter movements in cash flow because of working capital timing.

items.statement: Cash balance INR 1,664 crores (INR 907 cr pre-IPO + IPO proceeds + operating cash); no debt details discussed.
items.quote: If you look at the cash in the bank, it's about INR 1,664 crores. And out of which INR 907 crores was FY25 exit, the rest of it is what is the IPO proceeds plus continued operating cash generation that we're doing.

items.statement: Actively scanning for capability-driven acquisitions to fill glass-to-glass gaps or accelerate AI; no size or valuation targets fixed; approach remains rational and conservative.
items.quote: We're looking at where are the gaps that we could actually look at from an acceleration standpoint instead of us it's a buy-build partners sort of decisions that we are actually going through. And obviously, with the AI, there are new opportunities that's coming along.

items.statement: Monetized impressions grew ~62% YoY while Monetization segment revenue grew 36%, implying modest CPM pressure more than offset by volume.
items.quote: If you saw the impression growth that was roughly 62% year-over-year, revenue growth was still 36% year-over-year in the segment. So that's obviously, like Baskar said, two dynamics playing out.

items.statement: Serviceable addressable revenue for cloud modernization grew 11% to $1.9 billion; US streaming share at 48% of TV viewing, FAST viewership now equals Netflix.
items.quote: We've seen that our serviceable addressable revenue is kind of starting to grow, and we saw it grew almost 11% a year this year to $1.9 billion.

items.statement: Sales headcount declining over 2-3 years while accounts grow; efficiency driven by high NRR, sublinear account management, and product-led growth.
items.quote: Account management at some point is sublinear in scale. You're not going to add just because a customer of ours is spending $1 million today and then they're gone to do $10 million more. It doesn't mean we need 10 more people to solve a particular problem.

items.statement: Macroeconomic advertising environment has not impacted yet, but management acknowledges geopolitical climate could change that.
items.quote: Macroeconomic environment today has not impacted, as you see it today, but I can never say never with all this geopolitical climate that we don't control.

items.statement: Revenue phasing: Q1 ~22% of full-year revenue and 11% of EBITDA; H1 ~45% revenue / 37% EBITDA, H2 ~55% revenue / 63% EBITDA based on FY25-26 average.
items.quote: On the right-hand side, we've added some historical context to educate this audience on phasing based on FY'25 and '26 average, Q1 represented about 22% of full year revenue and about 11% of adjusted EBITDA.

items.statement: Management says it is not possible to make any forward statements given overall uncertainty and volatility
items.quote: Given t he overall uncertainty and volatility, it is not possible to make any forward statements

items.statement: Capex of INR200-300 crores planned over next two to three years focused on Performance Solutions, contract manufacturing, and YP derivatives
items.quote: you last call you had mentioned doing about INR200 crores to INR300 crores capex over the next three years

items.statement: Expected fixed asset turnover of 1-1.5x and ROI of 15-20% on planned capex
items.quote: the fixed asse t turnover for this would be 1 to 1.5 times, and expected ROI could be 15% to 20

items.quote: Capacity addition of 2,530 tons per annum of our existing product in the biocides range, announced in March 2025, is operational in the second half of FY26.

items.statement: Contract manufacturing dedicated line expected to come on stream in July 2026
items.quote: The capacity for catering to this agreement is expected to come on stream in July 2026.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization levels range 65% to 85% depending on product
items.quote: typically our current capacity utilization levels are in the range of 65% to 85%, depends on the product.

items.statement: Contract manufacturing long-term agreement with multinational company announced May 2024 progressing well; validation batches dispatched
items.quote: The contract man ufacturing long-term agreement with a multinational company, which we announced in May 2024, is progressing well. The validation batches for the same have been dispatched

items.statement: Another contract manufacturing agreement announced November 2025 on track; capacity expected July 2026
items.quote: The agreement we announced in November 2025 is going well and on track. The capacity for catering to this agreement is expected to come on stream in July 2026.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin 8%; FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin 10.1%
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA stood at INR112 crores with margins of 10.1%.

items.statement: Largely able to pass on raw material price increases in April and May; using shorter pricing windows
items.quote: we have been largely able to pass on the input price increases in the month of April and May.

items.statement: Sourcing yellow phosphorus from multiple players including Kazakh Phosphate and multiple producers in Vietnam; no over-dependence on single source
items.quote: we source yellow phosphorus from multiple players: Kazakh Phosphate as well as multiple producers in Vietnam. Yes. And we are not just dependent on one source, I can confirm that much.

items.statement: Phosphonates domestic market share 50-55%; applications in water treatment, soaps, detergents, cleaners, textile auxiliaries
items.quote: Our domestic market share varies; it's in the range of 50% to 55%.

items.statement: Biocides identified as fastest growing area within Performance Solutions; planning new biocide product launch in H2 FY27
items.quote: biocides is something that we are continuing to invest. You know, biocides is something that was a relatively small and newer business for Excel in the past, and we believe t hat this opportunity, you know, is

items.statement: Strong market position in THP for polycarbonate inputs; significant global market share
items.quote: we have a strong market position in THP particularly, and you know, in the global polycarbonate market, wherever THP is consumed, we do have a significant market share and global positions on THP.

items.statement: Contract manufacturing funnel driven by inbound customer inquiries based on Excel's known strengths and R&D capabilities
items.quote: It's typically the inbound that comes in from a customer, you know, seeking a specific query.

items.statement: China VAT refund withdrawal and global input cost increases leading to higher Chinese export prices to India
items.quote: the prices have gone up. In general, we are seeing an increase in prices of products from China, and you know, this is due to a combination of factors, which is withdrawal of VAT refund as well as the input costs are globally increasing, including in China.

items.statement: DGTR anti-dumping investigation for HCDP and ATMP initiated September 2025; preliminary findings expected by September 2026
items.quote: considering that the investigation was initiated in September 2025, in normal course, we should expect some findings to be released by September 2026.

items.statement: India-EU FTA and India-US treaty seen as positive; exploring EU market opportunities
items.quote: these are generally quite positive, particularly for us, you know. We are exploring opportunities in the EU market

items.statement: Balance sheet exceptionally strong with zero long-term debt and net cash position
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains exceptionally strong with zero long-term debt and a net cash position. We continue to be a net cash positive company.

items.statement: Board declared final dividend of INR13.75 per equity share (275% of face value INR5)
items.quote: the Board has declared a final dividend of INR13.75 per equity share, which is 275 % of the face value of INR5 per share.

items.statement: Uncertainty about agrochemical intermediates demand due to possibility of suboptimal monsoon per El Nino forecasts
items.quote: there is uncertainty about agrochemical intermediates demand going forward on account of the possibility of suboptimal monsoon as per the El Nino forecasts.

items.statement: Geopolitical developments causing challenges in raw material availability and prices for Q1
items.quote: Due to the geopolitical developments, we are seeing challenges in raw material availability and prices for Q1.

items.statement: FY26 net operating revenues INR1,094 crores, up 11.8% YoY; adjusted EBITDA INR112 crores; PAT INR73 crores at 6.7% margin
items.quote: For FY26, the company reported net operating revenues of INR1,094 crores, as against INR978 crores in FY25, reflecting a growth of 11.8%.

items.statement: H1 FY26 difficult due to extended monsoon disrupting sowing/harvesting and channel inventory build-up; recovery in Q4 FY26
items.quote: The third quarter usually is a lean season for agrochemical intermediates. However, the demand environment had begun to turn in Q4 FY26.

items.statement: Inorganic opportunities evaluated for strategic technology or market access; organic focus on Performance Solutions, contract manufacturing, YP derivatives
items.quote: wherever there is a strategic opportunity for us to either acquire some kind of technology or market access or a combination of these two. That's the sort of way we would look at any kind of inorganic opportunities.

items.statement: Management targets 15% consolidated EBITDA margin in medium term, currently at 11.5%
items.quote: So, our company of us, in engineering, we believe that a 15% EBITDA margin, if you look at some of our peers, that should be something that we should definitely aspire to.

items.statement: Order intake up 20% YoY to INR 3,714 crores; opening backlog up 34%
items.quote: The good news is that the order intake continued to remain strong this quarter as well, but on a year-on-year basis, order intake is up 20%. We have an order intake this year of INR 3,714 crores versus INR 3,100 crores in the previous year.

items.statement: Full-year EBITDA margin improved 1 percentage point; Q4 margin dip attributed to product mix and cost increases
items.quote: So, again, I think the foundation is in place. It's been a tough year for us. There has been a lot of multiple different issues that have impacted our performance.

items.statement: Poland facility at full capacity; need to build two more sheds soon
items.quote: It is full. It is completely full. We need to build another two sheds as soon as possible.

items.statement: Poland facility commissioned as low-cost manufacturing hub for Europe
items.quote: Our Poland facility is now up and running, so that should also help as a low-cost source for Europe.

items.statement: Gas and metal price increases impacted margins but have now stabilized
items.quote: Number two is that we probably had a little bit of increases in some of our costs, which were a result of the gas prices going up and metal prices and stuff like that. But that has now stabilized, so we should be okay.

items.statement: Nearly 50% of order intake from non-traditional industries (semiconductors, defense, oil & gas, petrochemicals, metals & minerals)
items.quote: Nearly 50% of our order intake this year has come from non-traditional industries. So, when I say non-traditional, these are non-chemical and non-pharma.

items.statement: Edlon business works with Micron, Intel and other semiconductor majors; now USD 25M high-margin business

items.value: 9% to 11% revenue growth; 50-100 bps EBITDA margin improvement
items.quote: Looking ahead to FY '27, we remain confident in our growth trajectory and currently expect revenue growth of 9% to 11%, along with an improvement in EBITDA margin of 50 to 100 basis points.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 140 bps to 10.8%; Q4 EBITDA margin 10.3%
items.quote: For the full year FY '26, consolidated revenue was INR3,691 crores with EBITDA margin expanding by 140 basis points to 10.8%.

items.statement: Management expects gradual margin improvement toward peak 15% level over coming years
items.quote: But it will continue to improve. And for the foreseeable future, we don't see that we should not achieve the peak margin of 15% we have achieved.

items.statement: In-house brands crossed 50% of B2C sales, nearly a year ahead of target; 85% jewelry, 15% lifestyle within in-house
items.quote: One of the most encouraging structural shifts during the year was a rising share of our in-house brands, which crossed 50% of B2C sales. This was achieved almost a year ahead of the plan.

items.statement: Lifestyle products at 35% of total sales, targeting 50% medium-term
items.quote: Our product mix, lifestyle products now contribute around 35% of total sales, and we continue to target a medium-term share of 50%.

items.statement: Lab-grown diamonds contribute 11% of retail revenue at ~$250 ASP, lifting realizations and gross margins
items.quote: Lab-grown diamonds are another important new lever. LGD now contributes 11% of retail revenue at an average selling price of around USD 250.

items.statement: Digital contribution at ~44% of B2C sales in FY26, targeting 50% by end of FY27
items.quote: Digital contribution stood at around 44% of B2C sales for the year, supported by better quality customer acquisition, improving retention and stronger AI-led targeting and personalization.

items.statement: Digital mix target of 50% by end of FY27
items.quote: We remain on track to reach 50% digital mix towards the end of FY '27.

items.statement: New lease signed for U.K. premises in February; consolidating 4 buildings into 1, operational by end of FY27
items.quote: So we have taken one lease -- signed a lease in U.K. around February. So that result in a higher ROU. But the existing building that we have, we will vacate and move in the new buildings by the end of -- during this financial year.

items.statement: In-house jewelry casting line operationalized in U.S. during FY26, mitigating tariff impact on shipments and product gross margins
items.quote: Importantly, the in-house jewelry casting line we operationalized in U.S. during the year continue to help us to mitigate tariff impact on our shipments and product gross margins.

items.statement: U.S. and Germany grew 1% and 7% YoY in Q4 local currency; U.K. degrew 1%; total 3% growth in USD terms
items.quote: In Q4 FY '26, U.S. and Germany grew by 1% and 7%, respectively, and U.K. degrew by 1% in local currency terms, resulting in total growth of 3% Y-o-Y in U.S. dollar terms.

items.statement: Germany achieved EBITDA breakeven for FY26, expected to contribute positively to group profitability from FY27
items.quote: The most important milestone in our international footprint this year has been Germany achieving EBITDA breakeven.
