items.statement: Management sees better digital traction in U.S. and U.K. in April-May; TV audience stressed by inflation and gas prices
items.quote: We are seeing better digital traction in both the geographies, but the television audience is still a bit stressed owing to the inflation. The gas price is high and interest rates are getting higher.

items.statement: Maintained pricing discipline and product profitability despite elevated precious metal prices and geopolitical tariff tensions
items.quote: Despite elevated precious metal pricing and geopolitical tariff tension, we maintained pricing discipline and product profitability.

items.statement: Highest ever free cash flow of INR272 crores in FY26; operating cash flow INR305 crores; net cash position INR296 crores
items.value: INR272 crores FCF; INR305 crores OCF; INR296 crores net cash
items.quote: We delivered operating cash flow of INR305 crores and free cash flow of INR272 crores, which is our highest ever free cash flow generation in a year. Net cash position stood at INR296 crores as of 31st March 2026.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR1.5 per share; total FY26 payout INR6 per share (~37% of free cash flow)
items.value: INR6 per share total; 37% of FCF
items.quote: On dividend, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR1.5 per share, subject to shareholders' approval. Including the interim dividend already paid, our total FY '26 payout works out to around 37% of our free cash flow.

items.statement: Tax rate expected to remain steady around 22% for upcoming years
items.quote: So our tax rate will be steady around 22% for the upcoming years.

items.statement: All group entities across India, U.S., U.K., Germany and China now Great Place to Work certified
items.quote: And I'm pleased to share that all our group entities across India, U.S., U.K., Germany and China are now Great Place to Work certified, reflecting our human resources engagement.

items.statement: India-U.K. and India-EU free trade agreements, India-U.S. trade discussions, and easing U.S.-China tariff tensions create favorable environment
items.quote: The India, U.K. and India EU free trade agreements, the ongoing India-U.S. trade discussions and the easing of U.S.-China tariff tensions all create a favorable environment for a vertically integrated retailers like us.

items.statement: Tariff uncertainty remains under current U.S. administration; company relies on agile multi-country operations and logistics to manage
items.quote: With the current administration, Mehul, we can never be certain. -- but I can only say that is whatever the circumstances, we are very agile and pretty multi-country operations and logistics that we'll deal better than competitors.

items.statement: AI integration across marketing, operations, supply chain and content creation improving conversion, customer spend and operational efficiency
items.quote: Number one is AI is now completely integrated into our digital efforts, from scanning the competitor environment or Meta library or other data or what is working, what angles are working.

items.statement: Unique customer base 6.8 lakh; retention stable at ~38%; average 23 pieces purchased per customer on trailing 12-month basis
items.quote: Our unique customer base stood at 6.8 lakh customers. Retention remained stable at around 38% and customers purchased an average of 23 pieces from us on a trailing 12-month basis.

items.statement: ROCE improved to 24% and ROE to 15% in FY26
items.quote: ROCE improved to 24% and ROE to 15%, reflecting much better profitability and disciplined capital allocation.

items.statement: Mindful Souls acquisition: INR25 crore write-off due to conservative impairment testing; recovery period extended from 5 to 7 years; business profitable with high cross-learning benefits
items.quote: Mindful Souls current business, initially, we structured based on the higher growth and we forecasted based on the double-digit growth basis, the initial impairment testing that we have done it. Though conservatively, we have taken this year that, that number -- however, that number growth percentage not coming, but the business is still good profitable business for us.

items.statement: Constant currency guidance not provided due to macro and business transition; INR revenue guidance of 9-11% for FY27
items.quote: At this time, because of the macro and business transition, we are not giving that constant currency guidance.

items.statement: Recruitment margins expected to sustain if topline grows at 10%+; may dip if growth slows to 7-8%
items.quote: If we are able to grow our topline in double digits, margins should remain the same. If you're able to grow at 10% or more, you should be able to maintain margin in Naukri.

items.statement: 99acres targets 60% traffic share, aims to double billings to ~Rs.1,000 crores in 3 years with 25-30% EBITDA margin
items.quote: Our goal in 99acres should be, if you ask me, given where we are today, because we made substantial gains in share over the last few quarters, we should now be aiming to get to 60% share.

items.statement: Hiring sentiment stable but subdued; premium segment growing faster than mid-level; non-IT hiring slowed
items.quote: I would say it's bee n stable. If you look at JobSpeak also, I think it's been in that four, five, six percent range. I would say it's been stable

items.statement: Standalone operating margin 40% in Q4 FY26, 37% for FY26; recruitment margin 58% in Q4, 57% for FY26
items.quote: Operating profits at a standalone level grew by 39% YOY to Rs.323 crores, and the operating margins stood at 40%.

items.statement: Standalone billings Rs.1,057 crores in Q4 FY26 (7% YoY), Rs.3,178 crores in FY26 (10% YoY)
items.quote: For the standalone business in Q4 FY26, billing s were Rs.1,057 crores, a YOY growth of 7%.

items.statement: Recruitment billings Rs.811 crores in Q4 FY26 (10% YoY), Rs.2,374 crores in FY26 (10% YoY)
items.quote: In Q4 FY26, the standalone recruitment billings grew by 10% to Rs.811 crores.

items.statement: 99acres billings Rs.163 crores in Q4 FY26 (2% YoY), Rs.497 crores in FY26 (10% YoY)
items.quote: In Q4 FY26, billings grew by 2% to Rs. 163 crores.

items.statement: Jeevansathi billings Rs.39 crores in Q4 FY26 (21% YoY), Rs.142 crores in FY26 (28% YoY)
items.quote: In Q4 FY26, Jeevansathi billings grew by 21% to Rs.39 crores.

items.statement: Shiksha billings Rs.45 crores in Q4 FY26 (-13% YoY), Rs.164 crores in FY26 (1% YoY)
items.quote: In Q4 of FY26, billing was Rs.45 crores, a YOY decline of 13%.

items.statement: Marketing expenses lowered 13% YoY in Q4 FY26 despite JobHai investments
items.quote: Marketing expenses were lowered by 13% YOY in Q4, despite continued investments in JobHai and other smaller businesses as they scale up their monetization efforts.

items.statement: Naukri 360 shifted online revenue mix from 27% to 53% in 15 months; paid users rose from 1.2% to 2.2% of MAU
items.quote: The shift to a self -serve online-first model has driven the online revenue mix from 27% to 53% in the last 15 months, while monthly ac tive users have been growing.

items.statement: AI-Rex onboarded 1,000 clients with 30,000 job mandates; Talent Pulse generated Rs.30-35 crores revenue in FY26
items.quote: With over 1,000 clients onboarded and 30,000 job mandates already on AI -Rex, early adoption is encouraging.

items.statement: 99Shorts launched in NCR as video-first new home discovery; expansion to other major cities planned in FY27
items.quote: The recent rollout of 99Shorts in NCR aims to drive deeper engagement in this segment with expansion to other major cities planned in for FY27.

items.statement: 99acres now traffic leader in almost every major city; supply share crossed 50% in residential resale
items.quote: In every city now, earlier we used to be leaders in two or three of the big cities, but now in Delhi, Mumbai, Bangalore, Chennai, Hyderabad, in almost every big city now we are traffic leaders.

items.statement: Competitors Housing and MagicBricks facing leadership changes and high burn; Housing burn ~Rs.250 crores/year
items.quote: Housing gives out the numbers publicly. I think their burn is now close to Rs.250 crores a year. They've lost a lot of ground in my view, in India.

items.statement: JobHai model similar to Apna and WorkIndia but more freemium; now monetizing in Delhi NCR and expanding to Mumbai, Bangalore
items.quote: Our business model in JobHai is not very different from Apna and WorkIndia except that perhaps we are more freemium than they are.

items.statement: Naukri platform hosts ~115 million resumes, adding ~21,000 resumes/day in Q4 FY26
items.quote: On the jobseeker front, the Naukri platform now hosts approximately 115 million resumes and added an average of around 21,000 resumes per day during Q4 FY26.

items.statement: 99acres web traffic share 49% in Q4 FY26 (up from 46% prior quarter); app traffic share 54%, iOS 67%
items.quote: 99acres continues to strengthen its traffic leadership with its web traffic share growing to 49% in Q4 FY26 from 46% i n the prior quarter.

items.statement: AI-powered mock interviews used by 1.5M users/month; AI-generated resumes powering 3M profiles/month
items.quote: AI-powered mock interviews are used by 1.5 million users monthly. AI-generated resumes are now powering 3 million profiles monthly.

items.statement: Standalone cash from operations before tax Rs.621 crores in Q4 FY26 (16% YoY); Rs.1,469 crores in FY26 (12% YoY)
items.quote: The standalone business generated cash from operations before taxes of Rs.621 crore s in Q4 FY26, a YOY growth of 16%.

items.statement: Cash balance including wholly owned subsidiaries Rs.4,963 crores at end of March 2026
items.quote: The cash balance of InfoEdge, including wholly owned subsidiaries, at the end of March 2026 stood at Rs.4,963 crores.

items.statement: Board approved final dividend Rs.3.6/share; total FY26 dividend Rs.8.4/share (40% increase YoY)
items.quote: the board has also approved a final dividend of Rs.3.6 per share for the year. This adds to the total dividend payout of Rs.8.4 per share for FY26, a 40% increased dividend payout versus last year.

items.statement: Headcount dip driven by AI efficiency gains; no layoffs, focus on productivity; every new hire scrutinized for value addition
items.quote: We've implemented a lot of, there are hundreds of AI projects going on in the company right now, as we speak. I'm sure we're getting some efficiency because of what we're doing inside the company.

items.statement: AI-driven search changes hitting Shiksha traffic and billings; headwind expected to persist near term
items.quote: AI -driven changes in search behaviour have been affecting Shiksha's traffic for several quarters. In Q4, this translated into a more direct billing impact as reduced referred search traffic from Google affected client deliveries.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty and tariffs impacting hiring sentiment; GCCs and non-IT sectors cautious
items.quote: The year was impacted by geopolitical headwinds, tariffs related to uncertainty, and a generally cautious hiring stance amongst corporates both in global demand linked sectors such as IT, as well as domestically oriented ones.

items.statement: Heavy forward investments in 99acres completed in FY26; expect business to turn cash-generative in FY27
items.quote: In FY26, we cautiously made forward investments in 99acres to strengthen its competitive position and become a clear market leader. With the heavy lifting now behind us, we expect growth to accelerate, operating leverage to play o ut and the business to turn cash -generative in FY27.

items.statement: Open to M&A in 99acres at right price for right asset
items.quote: Yeah, I mean, at the right price for the right asset, why not?

name: Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Ltd

items.statement: Demand trends in Q4 FY26 were broadly in line with prior quarters; wedding calendar was weaker YoY; geopolitical disruptions emerged late in quarter.
items.quote: demand trends during the quarter remained broadly in line with what we have seen over the past quarter. The wedding calendar was relatively weaker compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: March saw marginal demand impact slowing momentum; April demand nearly normal; inflationary pressures may play out over next 3-4 months with potential demand compression in H2.
items.quote: we have seen demand nearly normal for most part of April and going into this quarter. So, as of now, while we feared a significant sort of risk on demand, as of now, we have not seen it play out.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA grew 29% YoY excluding one-offs; margin at 11.5% in Q4 FY26.
items.quote: Excluding both of these impact, EBITDA grew 29% year-on-year with margins at 11.5%.

items.statement: Ethnic business EBITDA margin expanded 390 bps YoY in Q4 FY26 due to reduction in TCNS losses.
items.quote: Within overall EBITDA, our ethnic business margin, specifically saw a big expansion of 390 basis points year-on-year, mainly due to reduction in TCNS losses.

items.statement: Pantaloons EBITDA margin at 15.5% in Q4 FY26, up 40 bps YoY despite OWND ramp-up.
items.quote: Profitability also improved during the quarter with EBITDA margin at 15.5%, expanding by 40 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: Ethnic portfolio FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 560 bps to 10.8%.
items.quote: Profitability improved significantly with FY '26 EBITDA margin expanding by 560 basis points to 10.8%.

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 11% in FY26 from 10% in FY25.
items.quote: EBITDA adjusted for the demerger gain and the revaluation gain in TMRW's associates grew by 23% Y -o-Y to INR903 crores with margin at 11% versus 10% last year.

items.statement: Added ~70 new stores in Q4 FY26; total FY26 additions over 180 stores.
items.quote: During the quarter, we added around 70 new stores, taking the total additions for the year to over 180 stores.

items.statement: OWND store network expanded to 79 stores with 12 added in Q4 and 34 in FY26.
items.quote: OWND continues to strengthen its presence with its store network expanding to 79 stores. This included 12 new stores added during the quarter and 34 stores added in FY '26.

items.statement: TCNS added 23 new stores in FY26; launched first W flagship store in Mumbai in Q4.
items.quote: The business has also kick started its expansion journey this year in a calibrated manner, adding 23 new stores during FY '26. During the quarter, we also launched the first W flagship store in Mumbai.

items.statement: Tasva network stands at 94 stores; will continue selective expansion in high-potential wedding markets.
items.quote: The network now stands at 94 stores, and we will continue to expand selectively in high potential wedding markets.

items.statement: Jaypore network at 44 stores; strengthening position in premium artisanal ethnic wear.
items.quote: The brand now has its network of 44 stores and continue to strengthen its position in the premium artisanal and craft-led ethnic wear space.

items.statement: Luxury retail collective and mono-brands network at 49 stores; Galeries Lafayette flagship commenced operations Nov 2025.
items.quote: luxury retail, the collective and mono-brands business continued to grow profitably with its total network, including mono-brand stores at 49 stores. Galeries Lafayette, India's first flagship luxury departmental store commenced operations in November 2025

items.statement: TMRW portfolio omni-channel presence at 120 stores including WROGN.
items.quote: The portfolio also continued to build its omni-channel presence, closing the quarter with 120 stores, including WROGN across key markets nationwide.

items.statement: FY26 capex ~INR500 crores including INR150 crores for Galeries Lafayette; FY27 capex guidance INR250-300 crores at console level.
items.quote: Next year, this one-off type of thing will not come. So, we have -- in our plan, I already conveyed roughly INR300 crores capex, INR250 crores to INR300 crores at console level.

items.statement: Overall retail network at 1,273 stores spanning ~7.9 million sq ft; added 0.6 million sq ft net in FY26.
items.quote: Our overall retail network stood at 1,273 stores, spanning almost 7.9 million square feet. During the year, we added 0.6 million square feet of retail space on a net basis.

items.statement: Experiencing 3-4% raw material inflation; may need 5-8% price increases in H2 depending on category; evaluating pass-through.
items.quote: We are experiencing something like 3% to 4% sort of inflationary pressure as far as raw materials is concerned. Obviously, this is not the entire cost. Raw material is a part of the cost. And therefore, effectively, it would sort of put pressure in the second half of the year to take -- to fully counter it, take price increases between 5% to 8% depending on the category.

items.statement: Pantaloons growth driven by women's western, menswear, non-apparel categories each growing >20% in Q4; highest ever sell-throughs in autumn/winter season.
items.quote: We've seen growth in excess of 20% in each of these categories in quarter 4. Our sell-throughs, which is again a very important metric of the success of our merchandising strategy, we've seen the highest ever sell -throughs in our autumn/winter season.

items.statement: Pantaloons online business ~3-4% of revenue; basket size increase is biggest growth lever; footfalls increased in H2 FY26.
items.quote: Today, it's about 3%, 4% of our business. It's not very large. But with all the shifts we have made this year, we feel confident of scaling up this business. To your third question in terms of the customer KPIs -- the biggest one, which we feel very good a bout is our increase in our basket sizes.

items.statement: Pantaloons Q4 pricing marginally negative; growth largely volume-driven; footfalls up in Q3-Q4.
items.quote: as pricing is concerned, our price increased through the year was negligible. We've hardly taken any price increases. And in fact, in quarter 4, our pricing Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited (ABFRL) May 26, 2026 would have been, in fact, marginally negative. So, a large part of the growth has come from volume

items.statement: Ethnic wear category crowded with low entry barriers; no significant new competition; focus on distinctive branding. Men's ethnic more consolidated.
items.quote: I don't think new competition is entering this space because it's already pretty crowded with very low entry barriers and large number of players. I think the challenge is to create a distinctive brand where you can stand out and charge a reasonable premium.

items.statement: TMRW growing 30%+ for 3rd consecutive year; online players established, not many new entrants; some older players falling out.
items.quote: As far as TMRW business is concerned, you've seen consistently, we report every quarter the growth numbers -- we're still growing on a full year and a quarterly basis at 30% plus. This is the third consecutive year and about 10, 12 quarters with the exception of 1 or 2.

items.statement: Consolidated gross cash INR1,545 crores, gross debt INR1,695 crores as of Mar 2026; standalone gross cash INR1,144 crores, gross debt INR748 crores.
items.quote: As of March 2026, ABFRL had gross cash of INR1,545 crores at the consolidated level, while gross cash at the standalone level stood at INR1,144 crores. The gross debt at consolidated level is INR1,695 crores and standalone level is INR748 crores.

items.statement: Standalone cash utilization plan: INR1,000 crores FY26, INR600 crores FY27, INR500 crores FY28; target FCF positive FY29.
items.quote: As stated, we are planning to utilize it INR1,000 crores in FY '26, INR600 crores in FY '27 and INR500 crores in '28, post which we aim to be FCF positive in FY '29.

items.statement: TMRW raised INR440 crores equity and tied up INR500 crores NCDs; will have INR800 crores cash to fund growth.
items.quote: As you are aware, with equity issuance of INR440 crores during the year and more recent fund tie-up of INR500 crores through NCDs, TMRW is now adequately funded with INR800 crores cash to pursue its aggressive growth plans.

items.statement: TCNS cash losses more than halved in FY26; expect breakeven by end FY27, profitable by FY28. Tasva in investment phase; cash breakeven expected FY28.
items.quote: We'll probably towards the end of FY '27 is when we would expect to breakeven. And on a full year basis, definitely be profitable by FY '28 onwards. All this I'm giving you are still their IndAS profitabilities are positive in both cases. I'm talking of cash profit.

items.statement: Pantaloons store addition plan FY27: 20-22 stores; OWND: 20-35 stores; TMRW portfolio profitability target FY29.
items.quote: the plan for this financial year is about 20, 22 stores, I think as we get more confident, we will look at some point of time to step up this agenda and accelerate our store expansion.

items.statement: Standalone revenue guidance of 30% growth to INR 6,000 crore in FY27 and 25% growth to INR 7,500 crore in FY28; EBITDA margin guidance of 12% for FY27
items.quote: So, we are proposing a guidance of around 30% for F Y27, which will be around INR 6,000 crores top line, and then for FY28, from there we are looking at another 25% guidance, so that will roughly translate into INR 7,500 crores. The EBITDA will continue to be around 12% for FY27

items.statement: Unexecuted order book stands at over INR 22,000 crore including newly secured 2 HAM and 2 EPC bridge projects; highways 62%, water/canal/rail/airport 25%, coal mining 13%
items.quote: Company's unexecuted order book stands at over INR 22,000 crores, which includes the value of newly secured 2 HAM projects and 2 EPC bridge projects. Highway contracts contribute 62% of total unexecuted order book, while water, canal, area development, railway and airport contracts contribute around 25%, and coal mining contract contributes 13%.

items.statement: FY27 order inflow guidance of INR 15,000 crore; INR 3,957 crore already won in highways, INR 2,000 crore solar; INR 14,000 crore bids submitted awaiting opening
items.quote: See, we are expecting an overall new order book of around INR 15,000 crores in FY27, out of which we got INR 3,957 crores new orders in the highways sector. And as you said, if you consider again order book from the renewable energy, so it will be around INR 6,000 crores. So, INR 9,000 crores to INR 10,000 crores further orders we are expecting in FY27.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 12% for FY27; margin pressure expected in H1 due to bitumen/fuel cost spikes but MoRTH compensation mechanism from April 2026 provides partial relief; FY28 margin uncertain due to commodity volatility
items.quote: The EBITDA will continue to be around 12% for FY27. So, we will see what the EBITDA will be in FY28 going forward, given the geopolitical tensions and the volatility in the commodity prices.

items.statement: MoRTH introduced cost escalation compensation for EPC/HAM/PBMC projects from 1 April 2026 and reduced price adjustment cycle from 3 months to 1 month to address bitumen price spikes; SPV passes through WPI/CPI index and bitumen compensation
items.quote: Ministry of Road Transport & Highways introduced cost escalation compensation mechanism for national highway projects executed on EPC, HAM, PBMC modes, payable from 1st April 2026 and reduced price adjustment cycle from 3 months to one month to address the adverse impacts due to steep increase in bitumen prices.

items.statement: FY27 capex target of INR 150 crore; coal mining project capex INR 350 crore (INR 250 crore spent in FY26); solar equity investment INR 400 crore (INR 120 crore in FY27)
items.quote: CAPEX for Financial Year '27, we are targeting INR 150 crores.

items.statement: 14 HAM projects with aggregate BPC over INR 17,200 crore; 5 achieved PCOD/COD, 6 under construction, 1 MPRDC achieved financial closure, 2 L1 awaiting LOA; total equity requirement INR 1,623 crore (INR 1,081 crore infused, INR 542 crore ove
items.quote: Aggregate Bid Project Cost of 14 HAM projects is over INR 17,200 Crore. ✓ Out of total 14 HAM projects, o 5 projects achieved PCOD/COD, o 6 projects are under construction, o 1 project of MPRDC achieved financial closure o 2 projects, in which Company stands L1 bidder, LOAs are expected

items.statement: Standalone net worth INR 5,811 crore, debt INR 741 crore, net debt/equity 0.13x, cash INR 1,068 crore, net surplus INR 327 crore; Consolidated net worth INR 6,813 crore, debt INR 5,151 crore, net debt/equity 0.76x, cash INR 2,856 crore
items.quote: On Standalone Basis, Our net worth as on 31st March 2026 is INR 5,811 crores, whereas standalone debt from Banks/Financial Intuitions and Inter Corporate Deposit is INR 741 crores. This translates to net debt to equity of 0.13 times. Total cash & bank balance including current investments is INR 1,068 crores. Thus, we have a net surplus of INR 327 crores as on 31st March 2026.

items.statement: Equity infusion of INR 542 crore for HAM projects over FY27-28 (INR 350 crore in FY27, balance in FY28); solar equity INR 400 crore (INR 120 crore in FY27); internal accruals adequate to meet requirements
items.quote: Out of INR 542 crores, around INR 350 crores will be infused in current Financial Year ‘27 and the balance will be in Financial Year ‘28. Shravan Shah: Okay. And for solar, sir, BESS mean. Pankaj Agarwal: Actually, the total equity requirement we have told earlier was INR 400 crores , o ut of that, approximately INR 120 crores will be infused in this financial

items.statement: Completed final tranche of 12-asset divestment to Vertis Infrastructure Trust in March 2026; received full payment; evaluating monetization options for remaining 5 PCOD-achieved HAM assets
items.quote: In March 2026, the Company successfully completed the sale of its equity stake in PNC Challakere (Karnataka) Highways Private Limited to Vertis Infrastructure Trust. This transaction marked the completion of the final tranche of the strategic divestment of 12 assets announced in January 2024.

items.statement: NHAI awarding subdued at 3,124 km vs 4,500 km target in FY26; FY27 budget INR 2.9 trillion (+8%); expect accelerated land acquisition and approvals improving HAM/BOT pipeline; new opportunities in renewables, transmission, water, railways,
items.quote: Union Budget for FY27 reflects the Government's commitment to faster infrastructure development. Capital expenditure for the road sector has been budgeted at approximately INR 2.9 trillion for FY27, representing an increase of around 8% over the previous year. With increased focus on expressways, access controlled greenfield alignments including 4 & 6 lane economic corridors, the expansion in lane

items.statement: EPC competition remains cutthroat; HAM and BOT-Toll see less competition, especially larger HAM projects; won two INR 1,700 crore HAM projects with fewer bidders; direct bidding for BOT-Toll subject to due diligence and NHAI structure final
items.quote: See, what we see, the competition in the EPC segment will continue to be very sharp, and I would say, a cutthroat kind of competition will be there. But NHAI, if you see, they came out with a list of projects they proposed to do over the next one year. So, the majority of them are HAM and BOT Toll where we are seeing less competition compared to EPC.

items.statement: Management team includes MD Yogesh Jain, Director (Infra) T.R. Rao, VP Finance Pankaj Agarwal; no changes mentioned
items.quote: Today, I have with me Mr. T. R. Rao, Director (Infra), Mr. Pankaj Agarwal, Vice President, Finance and Accounts and Strategic Growth Advisors - our Investor Relations Advisors.

items.statement: Order book mix: highways 62%, water/canal/rail/airport 25%, coal mining 13%; FY27 order inflow target 60-70% highways, 30-40% non-highways (renewables, transmission, water, area development); solar BESS under PBMC model, mining as EPC item-
items.quote: 60% to 70%, we are still targeting the highways sector because NHAI has declared that they are coming out with a large number of highways projects, both on HAM and as well as BOT Toll apart from the EPC. So, 60% to 70% we are targeting from the highway s sector, and the remaining we are targeting from the non-highways sector

items.statement: NHAI and MoRTH remain primary highway clients; MSRDC (Maharashtra) two EPC packages progressing well; MPRDC (MP) one HAM project; UP State Bridge Corp bridge project in JV; Lucknow Development Authority flyover EPC; Andhra Pradesh irrigatio
items.quote: All the remaining highway projects are of the Government of India's NHAI and MoRTH, and two more state projects are there from MSRDC. Since the beginning, we have been getting the payments regularly. So, there are also two packages that are EPC; here, there is no investment risk, and we are getting payments regularly for what we are progressively doing the work.

items.statement: No material impact on EBIT margin for current year after closure and next year; plans in place to improve revenue and margin
items.quote: So for us, the contribution to the value come from the three aspects of deal one, deal two, and deal three and in summary, I just want to say, there is going to be no material impact to the margin, for this year, even after closure and for the next year, we have plan in place to make sure that there is no material impact.

items.statement: Minimal sales investment needed; overlay sales team for cross-sell of SAP, Oracle, cloud, data, AI capabilities; treated as BAU investment
items.quote: The investment will be very minimal and will be more on the overlay sales. As part of this transaction, we are getting a lot of good talented sales people who have a very deep client relationship.

items.statement: Five-year GCC partnership with Randstad Group starting at $55-60M TCV for AI transformation of Hyderabad GCC
items.quote: Look, I think the initial scope that we will ramp up will be closer to 50 to 60 million TCV, because it is a five-year relationship, but you have to start with some scope to begin with. So we have identified a scope, which will start ramping up.

items.statement: Acquired business DSO profile regular for IT services, in line with LTM's own DSO profile, no abnormality
items.quote: As far as the DSO profile is concerned, it is regular DSO profile, which is there for any IT services kind of a company. There is no abnormality out there. It is more or less in line with our own DSO profile as well.

items.statement: Acquisition consideration 10-15% of cash on balance sheet; no cash debt expected from transaction
items.quote: If you look at the cash on our balance sheet and the consideration that you are going to be paying for this transaction, it is not going to be more than 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Intend to keep acquired business as separate subsidiary; minimal integration beyond finance/HR; focus on retaining deep domain talent with 7-8 year account tenure
items.quote: We intend to keep this as a separate subsidiary of LTM so that we do not spend time on integration or anything and as I said, since it is completely white space, both from the market standpoint, as well as from the capability standpoint, there is no need for any sort of an integration as such.

items.statement: Short-term revenue haircut possible from further tail account trimming; focus on scaled marquee accounts with multi-billion dollar tech/AI spend
items.quote: My view is that I would assume a little bit more haircut in the short term just to transform, the scaled accounts, I mean, these are marquee accounts. Our focus should be a lot more on those accounts and they are like, customers with their multibillion dollar tech spend and AI spend.

items.statement: No conflict with group company LTTS; capabilities complementary in AI-led software engineering, digital engineering, enterprise platforms, interactive practices, industrial AI
items.quote: There is absolutely no conflict with any of our group companies. We are very conscious about it. We are focused significantly on AI-led software engineering, AI-led digital engineering. We are very focused on bringing our data capabilities, cloud capabilities, focused on our business AI capabilities.

items.statement: Clients have global aspirations and huge need for global delivery model; significant headroom for cross-sell/upsell of LTM capabilities (SAP, Oracle, Cloud, data, Business AI) into acquired accounts
items.quote: All these customers are the ones who have global aspirations, and these clients have a huge need for the global delivery model and that is the huge headroom that we see in the growth over here.

items.statement: Subcontractor spend efficiency gains via Randstad MSP capabilities; contract covers savings realized through subcons as third value lever
items.quote: We are going to leverage the parent company, Randstad Groups, MSP capabilities, for managing our subcons, and most importantly, the contract covers the savings that will be realized through the subcons.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth target of 10%-15%
items.quote: Firstly, we are looking to grow Operating revenues by 10%-15% for the year.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 17%-19%
items.quote: Secondly, we are giving an EBITDA margin band guidance of 17%-19%.

items.statement: FY27 operating cash flow target over Rs1,000m
items.quote: We expect to deliver OCF of over Rs1,000m for FY27.

items.statement: Content licensing revenue target over Rs400m for FY27
items.quote: Fifth, We are looking to target revenues more than Rs400m in the Content Licensing opportunities of our text, images and videos repositories and growing the number of clients.

items.statement: FY26 gross margin sustained at approx 68% despite 6% GST hike on paper
items.quote: We sustained our high Gross Margin levels of approx. 68% this year despite a 6% GST hike in Paper on the back of better product mix.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA Rs1,449m at 18.1% margin meeting guidance range
items.quote: We achieved the Highest EBITDA of Rs. 1449 Mn and EBITDA Margin of 18.1% which meets the guidance range of 18%-20%,

items.statement: Paper prices expected to increase 10%-15% in FY27; selling price hike limited to 6%-8%
items.quote: Paper prices, definitely, we expect to grow by 10% to 15% this year at least, maybe more also. But right now, we are in negotiation stage with all the paper mills, and we have not finalized our rates for this year. But we expect a 10% to 15% increase, which surely be there not only in paper, but on chemicals, glue, plates etc. And even with the new Labor Code coming in the cost for the labour will

items.statement: Selling price hike expected in range of 6%-8% for FY27
items.quote: We expect that the price hike would be in the range of 6% to 8%. That's only maximum we can take. We can't take beyond that because then ther e is a pushback from the customers from the market

items.statement: AI dataset content licensing revenue grew over 60% YoY in FY26
items.quote: On the AI Dataset content licensing revenues, we had a great year with over 60%+ YoY revenue growth during FY26.

items.statement: Curriculum products adopted in over 1,500 schools
items.quote: Curriculum sales adoption grew faster for the all new Mylestone, My Zen, SmartK and Solid Steps being adopted in over 1500 schools.

items.statement: Content licensing client count grew from 2 to 5 in FY26; adding 2 more in FY27
items.quote: In our first year of this business we had 2 clients. In the year gone by we had 5 clients. During this year, we are picking up 2 more clients.

items.statement: Acquired CPD Singapore in January 2026 for international curriculum capabilities
items.quote: We have completed our 1st International acquisition in January 2026 when we acquired CPD Singapore which gives us Curriculum capabilities for the India and Asia markets.

items.statement: CPD Singapore acquisition valued at potential US$8-10m business in few years
items.quote: We believe this has the potential to be an US$8-US$10 Mn business in a few years.

items.statement: FY26 capex Rs362m; FY27 capex ~Rs200m for new printing plant near Delhi
items.quote: Considering we have a capex of about Rs20 crores coming up, I would say, we should be around Rs130 crores, Rs135 crores.

items.statement: New printing plant near Delhi to add capacity, digital printing machines, improve efficiency and working capital
items.quote: That's mostly capital expenditure towards building a new printing plant, state -of-the-art near Delhi. And for that, we require to invest money there.

items.statement: Currently 80%-85% printing in-house, 15%-20% outsourced
items.quote: Almost, I would say, 80% to 85% is done in-house and 15% to 20% is outsourced.

items.statement: Receivables and inventory expected to normalize in 1H FY27
items.quote: We expect Receivables and Inventory to normalize during the 1H of FY27.

items.statement: Net debt-free at end of FY26 with net cash Rs1,048m
items.quote: The company continues to build on its net debt free status company at the end of FY26 with a net Cash balance of Rs1,048m, despite a Capex of 362 Mn and Acquisition Outgo of 107 Mn, which gives us ample headway to look at potential M&A and/or Buyback from internal accruals as well.

items.statement: Interim dividend of Rs4/share declared for FY26
items.quote: We have announced an Interim dividend of Rs4/share

items.statement: Buyback under consideration but deferred due to geopolitical uncertainty and cost volatility
items.quote: Yes, yes, we are considering that. Unfortunately, because of the war situation, we are waiting for things to settle down because it's best to have cash in books for this uncertain period. Once this gets over, then of course, we'll definitely consider.

items.statement: School publishing market share estimated at 10%-15% of private school market
items.quote: We anticipate our market share of the school business to be in the range of 10% to 15% of the private school publishing market approximately.

items.statement: School segment revenue up 20%-25% over 8 years; higher education segment degrown from 20% to 8% of mix
items.quote: Just to add to that, pre -COVID, higher education constituted almost 20% of our market. Currently, it's about 8%. So, the degrowth has happened in the higher education segment. The school segment continues to still grow. So, we are higher by about 20% to 25 % in the school segment.

items.statement: Content licensing revenue mix shifted from 80% in-house/20% sourced to 30%/70% in FY26
items.quote: Last year it was 80% ours, 20% sourced. This year, it's 30% ours and 70% sourced.

items.statement: Content licensing margins near 90% for in-house content; lower for sourced content
items.quote: Yes. So wherever our content is going, that is almost 90% margin for us.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty (Middle East war) impacting collections and cost visibility; buyback deferred
items.quote: Unfortunately, because of the war situation, we are waiting for things to settle down because it's best to have cash in books for this uncertain period.

items.statement: Guided for over 15% consolidated revenue growth in FY27, excluding potential pricing retrigger
items.quote: I do expect that even on a conservative level, I am happy to give a guidance of over a 15% growth in the overall revenue. This is without taking a price retrigger, which is likely to happen

items.statement: Targets doubling revenue every 3-4 years with consistent margin and ROIC improvement
items.quote: We expect to double our revenues every three to four years with consistent improvements in margins and return on investments.

items.statement: Aims to improve consolidated EBITDA margin by ~0.25% in FY27 for existing businesses, new projects to dilute near-term margin
items.quote: excluding the new projects that would be coming up, yes we could expect a growth of 0.25% in EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Overseas subsidiaries turned around to 14.6% EBITDA margin and break-even EBT in Q4 FY26, expect continued improvement
items.quote: in Quarter 4, the business has turned around and registered an EBITDA of 14.6% and has come to neutral or break-even at EBT level.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR 275-310 crore for FY27 (5-7% of projected ~INR 5,500 crore revenue)
items.quote: taking our 15% growth on the current year's revenue, which is roughly INR 5,500 crores, you can expect somehow capital outlay of INR 275 crores to around INR 310 crores for the upcoming financial year

items.statement: CWIP of INR 115 crore to be largely capitalized by end of Q2 FY27 as Sundaram-Clayton, Khed City, Sanaswadi projects complete
items.quote: major portion will be done away in terms of capitalization by the end of 2nd Quarter.

items.statement: New projects (INR 342 crore investment) generated INR 468 crore revenue in FY26, expected to reach INR 700-750 crore in FY27 (2-2.5x asset turnover)
items.quote: 2.5x, which can be 2x to 2.5x basically, I would say. So, around INR 750 crores of revenue these projects can do.

items.statement: EV business revenue INR 20 crore in FY26 (41,000 battery chargers, 5,500 MCUs), targeting 2x revenue in FY27 but profitability only in FY28
items.quote: We are expecting now to double this revenue in the current financial year. During Financial Year 2026, 41,000 battery chargers were sold and 5,500 motor control units were sold.

items.statement: Smart Key locksets reaching ~5,000 units/month with growing volumes
items.quote: we have reached a level of about 5,000 locksets per month. And it is growing. The volumes are growing every month.

items.statement: Sundaram-Clayton die-casting shift to own premises by end Q2 FY27, EBT turnaround from Q3 FY27
items.quote: by the end of Quarter 2, we would be able to shift the entire business to our own premises. I think from Quarter 3 onwards, we will start a turnaround in the units with our new EBT levels.

items.statement: Khed City aluminum die-casting (PV segment) and Pune cabins/fabrication to start EBT turnaround from Q2 FY27
items.quote: From Quarter 2 onwards, it will start generating EBT level margins. So, this is a turnaround time for this project.

items.statement: Aluminum/commodity price pass-through lag of ~3 months in India (June pass-through for April hikes), 180 days overseas; negotiating shorter cycles
items.quote: April pass-throughs will start from the month of June, in that quarter. Yes, so it can take a lag of three months, typically, as to how it happens in India.

items.statement: Expect pricing retrigger in FY27 due to higher input costs (gas, oil, manpower, power tariffs) across industry
items.quote: there will be a pricing retrigger mechanism that will be activated, and sometimes this becomes positive for the company because many costs or pricing that has been done by the customer was done years ago

items.statement: Net debt INR 897 crore, gross debt INR 948 crore (INR 564 cr WC, INR 384 cr term loans); INR 103 cr term loan repayment due in FY27
items.quote: This year we have a repayment commitment of around close to INR 103 crores with various banks. So, term debt will start pairing as the repayment schedule comes in

items.statement: Overseas debt increase from €41M to €46.9M largely due to reclassification of bill discounting to borrowings and FX translation (€/INR 90→111)
items.quote: majority of the portion that we have shifted from bill discounting to a clean debt. So, largely, we are regrouping in the balance sheet heads itself.

items.statement: Consolidated receivables 44 days (standalone 51 days), inventory 54-55 days (India only 12-13 days, overseas higher); targeting 40-45 day collection
items.quote: at the consolidated level, it is 44 days, standalone 51. There is some one-time receipts that we got. Because of that, the cycle has gone up.

items.statement: Strong demand across all 2W OEMs (three leaders competing fiercely); robust order book in sheet metal, casting, proprietary products
items.quote: there are now three leaders who are fighting bitterly amongst each other to become number one. Having said that, we as a company continue to get very, very robust orders in some of the new businesses

items.statement: Integrated aluminum casting capability (HPDC, LPDC, machining, zinc, magnesium, engine blocks) is key differentiator; consolidation of supplier base favors Sandhar
items.quote: now we do both high-pressure die casting, we do low-pressure die casting, we do machining, and the entire context of not just small components, but from small to extremely large, including engine blocks.

items.statement: India business revenue grew 28% YoY to INR 4,384 crore vs industry 12.7%; 2W segment grew 35.1% vs industry 12.9%
items.quote: the industry has achieved a growth rate of 12.7%, whereas Sandhar has achieved 28%. In terms of two wheelers, industry has achieved a growth rate of 12.9%, whereas Sandhar has achieved 35.1%.

items.statement: Consolidated FY26: Revenue INR 4,852 cr (+25%), EBITDA INR 513 cr (+28%, 10.6% margin), PAT INR 199 cr (+40%)
items.quote: the revenue for '25-'26 is INR 4,852 crores, which is up 25% on a consolidated basis, EBITDA at INR 513 crores, higher by 28% year-on-year, at the rate of 10.6%

items.statement: Manpower shortages (20% absenteeism post-Holi/elections, 30-50% minimum wage hikes in states) caused industry loss of 200-300k vehicles in April; improving in May/June
items.quote: according to my understanding, would have lost somewhere in the region of almost 200,000 to 300,000 vehicles. And that reflects in the inventory which has come down dramatically.

items.statement: Overseas business strategic review pending after FY27 turnaround; currently drags ROCE but provides customer reference for India business
items.quote: Now that we are hopeful that this particular year we would have all those sins washed away, we will relook at this business, but at this point of time it is very difficult for me to comment

items.statement: Not pursuing new JVs; focusing on technology transfer/royalty collaborations using existing infrastructure for faster ROCE
items.quote: We are not looking at joint ventures at this time. We are considering transfer of technology or collaborations, which will be on the royalty basis rather than in the form of joint ventures.

items.statement: Overseas revenue degrew ~8.5% in Euro terms in FY26; €46M revenue vs €46.9M debt; FX translation impact significant (€/INR 90→111)
items.quote: it has degrown by around 8.5% in Euro terms. €46 million revenue, a similar amount of debt.

items.statement: Telematics/connected vehicle products in advanced discussions with partners; customer POCs underway; targeting production within 12 months
items.quote: we are very, very ahead of those discussions with the partners for those technologies and also in-house development of those products in our R&D center.

items.statement: Management committed to enhancing revenue by 15% to 20% year-on-year and achieving EBITDA closer to 20% in the medium term.
items.quote: We are, as a team, fully committed to enhancing the revenue by 15% to 20% year-on-year, and achieving EBITDA of closer to 20-odd percent in the medium term, and we continue to work on that journey.

items.statement: FY27 capex estimated at INR110 crores including INR90+ crores for approved projects and INR20-25 crores maintenance capex.
items.quote: Yes. INR110 crores -- I mean, broadly, yes. Yes, broadly. It can go -- maybe it can go up depending on more projects through the year. But at the moment, yes, that's correct.

items.statement: Board approved furnace capacity expansion from 25 to 32 tonnes per day with third forming line at ~INR50 crores, likely in FY27 or FY28.
items.quote: One is to expand our furnace capacity from 25 tonnes per day to 32 tonnes per day with the addition of a third forming line, and this will likely happen in the year '27 o r '28, depending on when the furnace life is over. The cost of this capex is roughly INR50 crores

items.statement: Glassware manufacturing at Bharuch plant via Borosil Scientific to commence by end of Q3 FY27 with capex ~INR42 crores.
items.quote: The company is looking at a high growth p otential in these categories, and we expect this facility to be commenced by the end of Q3 FY27 with a capex of approximately INR42

items.statement: Vacuum-insulated stainless steel flask plant: 2 lines commercial production before end of Q1 FY27, third line by end of Q2 FY27.
items.quote: I'm happy to say that the commercial production from the first 2 lines is expected to commence in the next few days before the end of Q1 FY27, and the third line is expected to commence by the end of Q2 FY27.

items.statement: Opalware utilization at 90-95%; no major capex planned, only debottlenecking.
items.quote: Opalware, look has been on a -- I mean, we're close to 100%, I would say, between 90% and 95% utilization, depending on the month.

items.statement: 20 MW ground-mounted solar plant with battery storage expected to be commissioned in Q1 FY27, covering ~61% of power requirements.
items.quote: The company is further investing INR75 crores towards setting up a 20-megawatt ground-mounted solar plant with a battery energy storage system, which will further reduce the overall power cost, and the same is expected to be commissioned in this quarter, Q1 FY27.

items.statement: FY26 operating EBITDA flat at INR176.7 crores vs INR177.7 crores; margin declined from 16.3% to 15.1% due to lower Hydra sales and reverse operating leverage.
items.quote: In FY26, the company achieved an operating EBITDA before exceptional and one-time income of INR176.7 crores as against INR177.7 crores in FY25, which is basically flat for the year. And in fact, the operating EBITDA margin has reduced from 16.3% the year before, to 15.1% in this year.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 11.5% vs 14.2% in Q4 FY25; impacted by gas cost increase and price hike lag.
items.quote: The EBITDA margin before exceptional and onetime items was 11.5% in Q4 FY26, as against 14.2% in Q4 FY25.

items.statement: Solar plant estimated to save INR28 crores at EBITDA level in FY27.
items.quote: Yes. So that will be -- that is estimated to be about INR28 crores at EBITDA level, for FY27.

items.statement: In-house vacuum bottle manufacturing expected to increase gross margin by at least 10% over trading margins, but not in first couple of quarters.
items.quote: But my sense is on the gross margin side, 10% at least we should get an increase. Otherwise, there's no benefit of manufacturing in India, so -- but I don't think that will be realized in like the first couple of quarters.

items.statement: Power and fuel costs fell from INR82.4 crores to INR78 crores in FY26 despite per-unit cost increases.
items.quote: Power and fuel costs saw sharp reduction falling from INR82.4 crores to INR78 crores.

items.statement: Opalware demand growth muted; management expects muted growth for next year until R&D yields differentiated products.
items.quote: But at the moment, I think we are -- for the next year or so, I think we are going to expect to see muted growth. And hopefully, our R&D efforts will play off and lead to something nice, which can then be kind of ignite this category.

items.statement: Glassware grew 17.3% in FY26 to INR295.5 crores; Larah opalware grew 7.3% to INR411.9 crores; non-glassware grew 2.4% to INR463.7 crores.
items.quote: In our glassware segment, which includes borosilicate microwavable products, serving ware, glass tumblers, lunchboxes, we recorded a year-over-year growth of 17.3% in FY26. Revenue stood at INR295.5 crores compared to INR252 crores in FY25.

items.statement: Hydra inventory from last year's QCO buildup mostly depleted; new appliance inventory built up for QCO 2025; glassware inventory elevated due to production exceeding sales.
items.quote: The Hydra inventory, whatever we built up last year is more or less all depleted. But on the flip side, we had to build up a lot of appliance inventory this year because of this QCO, which has come on a large range of appliances.

items.statement: Anti-dumping investigation for borosilicate glass only; preliminary outcome expected in 6-9 months.
items.quote: At present data is under the investigation, but we hope that it at least it will take 6 to 9 months from now

items.statement: QCO 2025 for electrical appliances effective 19 March 2026; remediation timelines extended to 1 October 2026; company built advanced inventory to mitigate sales impact.
items.quote: Recently, in QCO 2026, the remediation time lines have been extended to 1st October 2026 from its trial date, I think, sometime in March. Accordingly, the company has built up advanced inventory to mitigate potential sales reductions as non-certified products will not be permitted for sale in India beyond the prescribed time lines.

items.statement: China dumping borosilicate glass products below cost; rupee depreciation partially offsets but cost differential remains; anti-dumping petition filed.
items.quote: China is a major irritant and challenge because they rout inely are selling products lower than the cost of production and dumping because of over capacity or whatever reason they may have

items.statement: Glassware ~66% own manufacturing (pressware), 34% outsourced; percentage unlikely to change significantly in FY27 without policy support.
items.quote: Now, I mean see -- if we define our own manufacturing as just pressware, it's roughly two-thirds, but if we define it including -- two-thirds. Two-thirds would be Borosil Limited manufacturing.

items.statement: Net debt INR49.7 crores as of 31 March 2026; short-term debt may rise with capex timing but funded by INR120 crores operating cash flow and inventory drawdown.
items.quote: As of the end of 31st March '26, at the consolidated level, Borosil Limited maintained a strong balance sheet with a net debt position of INR49.7 crores.

items.statement: Vacuum flask plant investment financed through mix of equity, debt and internal accruals; no immediate equity raise planned.
items.quote: This investment is being financed through mix of equity, debt and internal accruals.

items.statement: FY26 revenue INR1,195.9 crores, up 8% YoY; PAT INR74.7 crores vs INR74.2 crores; 8-year revenue CAGR 21.4%, EBITDA CAGR 29.4%.
items.quote: Borosil has delivered a reasonable performance in FY26 with revenue from operations reaching INR1,195.9 crores, up from INR1,107.8 crores during the last year. This represents an 8% year-over-year growth.

items.statement: Inventory up for 2 consecutive years due to Hydra QCO, appliance QCO, and glassware overproduction; management expects reversal in FY27 as Made in India reduces inventory needs.
items.quote: So overall, yes, it's been 2 years consecutive of inventory growth, but I do see a stop to that, hopefully this year itself, and then from next year, we should see a reversal of that because being more Made in India should logically give us leverage to red uce our inventory, not have to increase it

items.statement: West Asia crisis caused LPG supply restrictions impacting Jaipur furnaces in Q4 FY26; no sales impact due to inventory but margin hit from fixed cost absorption.
items.quote: During the quarter ended March 31, 2026, the production activities at the company's borosilicate glass furnace for pressware products and its opal glass furnace located in Jaipur were also impacted temporarily due to the restrictions in supply of LPG arisi ng from a force majeure situation caused by the West Asia crisis

items.statement: Certified as Great Place to Work; ICRA reaffirmed AA- stable long-term and A1+ short-term ratings.
items.quote: Borosil Limited has continued to be certified as a Great Place to Work, reflecting its commitment to fostering a positive workplace culture, a high-trust work environment and strong employee satisfaction across its operations.

items.statement: Revenue target of INR 3,000 crores by March 2031 (FY31) reaffirmed
items.quote: No, no. We are very much intact, and we have a plan to achieve this INR 3,000 crores by March 2031. So that plan is already in place, and we are working very rigorously on that plan.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15-20%
items.quote: Sir, we are expecting a revenue increase of about 15% to 20%, as we have given the earlier guidance also. So that expectation we are having even for this year.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 18-20%
items.quote: Our margin ranges we have projected 18% to 20% EBITDA margin. So margin will be in that range only.

items.statement: FY27 capex of INR 45 crores for standalone and INR 90 crores for subsidiary, funded mainly through internal accruals
items.quote: Our capex plan for India Pesticides is INR 45 crores and for our 100% subsidiary, it is INR 90 crores. And mainly, it will be funded through internal accruals. We may take a small loan in our 100% subsidiary.

items.statement: Shalvis facility second block expected operational by September-October 2026
items.quote: Yes, I'm assuming that it will be operational by September, October. So including that, it will be around INR 70 crores to INR 80 crores, including the second block.

items.statement: Pretilachlor/PEDA facility utilization at 70-75% due to seasonal three-month shutdown (Aug-Oct)
items.quote: The capacity utilization, because this is a seasonal product, we may have to stop the plant for about three months' period. So roughly, it will be around 70% to 75%.

items.statement: Formulation capacity scaled to 10,000 metric tonnes across 24 depots in 18 states
items.quote: Formulation capacity has now scaled up to 10,000 metric tonnes, enabling the company to better leverage its in-house technical capabilities and strengthen responsiveness towards domestic demand.

items.statement: Shalvis facility revenue expected at INR 70-80 crores in FY27 including new block
items.quote: So we expect Shalvis revenues to be in the range of at least INR 70 crores to INR 80 crores.

items.statement: Japanese partner forecast 30% volume increase for FY27 and discussing one additional molecule
items.quote: Actually, we are having regular discussions with our Japanese friends, and they have given the forecast for this year and for the next year, which is almost 30% more than last year.

items.statement: Domestic demand strong for herbicides and intermediates; export demand stable despite geopolitical pricing pressure
items.quote: Domestic sales during Q4 FY26 increased significantly by more than 50% to INR 183 crores compared to INR 118 crores in the corresponding quarter last year, largely driven by strong demand for herbicides and intermediates. Exports remained stable despite selective pricing pressure in certain products arising from geopolitical factors.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin improved to 18% from 15.9% in FY25
items.quote: EBITDA for the year was INR 194 crores, registering a growth of 44.7%, while EBITDA margin improved to 18% from 15.9% in FY25.

items.statement: Successfully passing on raw material cost increases to customers, particularly for sulphur-based products
items.quote: We have to take, because the raw material costs have already increased, so that price increas e we have to take, and we have been successful. In some of the cases, our customers have agreed as the price differential, so that we are able to maintain the same ratio of margins roughly

items.statement: Two new molecules at Hamirpur facility for FY27, one being first in India production, targeting export markets
items.quote: No, no. They will be entirely new molecules, and we are not producing in our Sandila or Dewa Road unit. They will be in addition to these molecules.

items.statement: Japanese partner providing 30% volume forecast increase and evaluating additional molecule
items.quote: Actually, we are having regular discussions with our Japanese friends, and they have given the forecast for this year and for the next year, which is almost 30% more than last year. And we are also discussing one more molecule with them.

items.statement: Net working capital days improved to 223 in FY26 from 254 in FY25; further 10-12 days improvement possible in FY27
items.quote: Our net working capital days has now improved to 223. There is a slight scope for further improvement, maybe by 10 to 12 days less by FY27.

items.statement: Term loan of INR 27 crores for subsidiary at ~8% cost; working capital blended cost ~7.2-7.3%
items.quote: We have taken term loan for our new 100% subsidiary. It is around INR 27 crores. And our cost is around 8% for this term loan.

items.statement: Dividend policy of 5-15% of net profit maintained; INR 0.75 dividend continued despite higher profits
items.quote: I mean we have a dividend p olicy, which is providing 5% to 15% of net profit. As you know, we have a lot of capex plan for our subsidiary, and our turnover is growing, so we have to fund a lot of increased working capital through our internal accruals

items.statement: Antidumping duty on PEDA/Pretilachlor supporting domestic production; import replacement achieved
items.quote: I think it is mostly catered by domestic players, maybe some small import may be there in very, very small quantity. Some time back, some people might have imported long back, so they may be there. But otherwise, it is primarily by domestic production.

items.statement: Export revenue 39% of total in FY26; Q4 exports INR 84 crores vs INR 89 crores YoY due to geopolitical issues
items.quote: Export revenues contributed approximately 39% of total revenues during FY26 despite temporary pricing challenges in select exported products arising from geopolitical developments.

items.statement: ROCE improved to 16.8% in FY26
items.quote: Net working capital days improved to 223 days in FY26 from 254 days in FY25, while ROCE improved to 16.8%.

items.statement: Geopolitical supply chain disruptions managed through long-term supplier arrangements and customer price discussions
items.quote: We have done some long-term arrangements with some of our suppliers who are able to bring the material to us in time. Plus for the local supplies where we don't keep long inventories, there, we are able to sustain because of the continuous supply, though at a slightly higher price.

items.statement: Hamirpur facility development progressing with infrastructure established and operational blocks moving as planned
items.quote: Development work at the Hamirpur facility continued during the year with supporting infrastructure and operational blocks moving ahead as planned. The facilit y provides a strong pathway for future capacity expansion and specialty product manufacturing

items.statement: Plant 6 commercialization on track for H1 FY27
items.quote: Plant 6 has achieved mechanical completion, and we remain on track for commercialization by H1 of FY '27.

items.statement: No organic capex expected in FY27 beyond maintenance; next capacity addition possible in FY28 if utilization reaches ~60%
items.quote: We don't expect FY '27, any organic capex other than the maintenance capex. And if we are able to deliver very good numbers, maybe FY '28, we go for additional capacity.

items.statement: Capex philosophy targets 1.5-2.5 year capacity increments rather than 5-year builds
items.quote: We do not want -- or we do not see ourselves doing a capex, which is like 5 years kind of we're creating capacity for the next 5 years. We want to do it more like 1.5 to 2.5 years kind of chunk.

items.statement: Plant 6 enables ~INR1,000 cr revenue (ex-injectables); 10-15% further efficiency upside expected
items.quote: Excluding injectables, which is about 100 cr, we can deliver about 1,000 cr revenue with Plant 6. However, as mentioned earlier, there is an upside potential in terms of efficiency, which always we have been able to bring in through tweaks in the system.

items.statement: Operational EBITDA (ex-ESOP) improved; long-term expectation of overall EBITDA growth
items.quote: The operational EBITDA, as you must have seen, if we exclude the ESOP expenses has actually improved a lot. And in the long run, we maintained that we expect the overall EBITDA level to grow.

items.statement: 13 consecutive quarters of record revenue; CDMO vertical grew 20% YoY to INR664 cr in FY26
items.quote: Q4 FY '26 revenue stood at INR238 crores, up 18% Y-o-Y, while the company extended its track record to 13 consecutive quarters of record revenue. In Generic Formulations CDMO vertical, we achieved revenue of INR664 crores and INR176 crores in FY '26 and Q4 FY '26, reflecting 20% Y-o-Y growth.

items.statement: Customer concentration low: top customer 6.5%, top 10 ~32%, top 20 ~40-41% in FY26
items.quote: Our highest customer is at 6.5% for the year. And top 10, we are at about 32%. Top 20 would be around 40%, 41%.

items.statement: Export revenue grew 40% YoY to INR46 cr in FY26; Q4 up 67% to INR17 cr; Philippines GMP received for injectables
items.quote: Our export vertical revenue grew by 40% to INR46 crores in FY '26, while Q4 FY '26 increased by 67% Y-o-Y to INR17 crores, given the longer lead time. Associated with export markets, we view this as an encouraging validation of efforts towards regulatory approvals and product registrations over the past few years.

items.statement: API price increases passed through via transparent cost sheets in CDMO; evaluating price hikes for trade generics and exports
items.quote: In our CDMO vertical, we have an open, transparent cost sheet. So the price increases are discussed with the customers, the customer then validates them and then continues. On the trade generic side and other -- our own brand side, we are looking at where we may need to also do the price increase.

items.statement: Trade generics impacted by codeine syrup exit (~INR50-60 cr annualized); replacing with alternate liquid products and Ayurvedic cough syrups
items.quote: As you rightly mentioned, our Q3 and Q4 got affected with trade generics by mainly two factors. One, as we mentioned, codeine. So it has impacted the trade generics vertical. We are trying to fill in that portion of codeine business lost with alternate.

items.statement: Injectable facility can fill GLP-1 vials; positioning as CDMO partner for vial filling as volumes scale
items.quote: With respect to the vial format for GLP-1, our facility can fill those vials already, okay? So that is one important thing. And our question is that as the volume picks up and the people who have done the launches so far have done it from their in-house facilities. And as the volumes pick up, they have to go out to CDMOs like us.

items.statement: Completed INR47 cr buyback without promoter participation; proposed dividend INR13 cr (INR6.3/share) for FY26
items.quote: The completion of the INR47 crores buyback without promoter participation were considered reflections of the Board's confidence in the intrinsic strength and future potential of the company. In addition, in line with our dividend policy, the company has proposed a dividend of INR13 crores, INR6.3 per share for FY '26.

items.statement: Regulatory oversight on codeine syrups led to exit of two largest multinational brands; company replacing with non-codeine and Ayurvedic alternatives
items.quote: It is very difficult for government to monitor who is taking it and whether they are taking it on prescription or not. So in our case, as some of the -- like 2 large, very, very large, in fact, 2 of the largest brands in the Indian pharma market owned by multinationals have now exited the market.

items.statement: Indian pharma market volume growth 2.7% YoY in FY26; Windlas revenue grew 19% to INR904 cr
items.quote: The Indian pharma market registered a Y-o-Y volume growth of 2.7% in FY '26. Despite moderate industry volume growth, we are pleased to report another year of strong performance, with revenue growing 19% Y-o-Y to INR904 crores in FY '26.

items.statement: Dosage form expansion opportunities identified: ointments, steroids, beta-lactams, soft-gel hormones, protein powders, nutra, eye drops; no immediate organic plans
items.quote: We don't have anything in ointment. We don't have anything in steroids, beta-lactam antibiotics. We don't have anything in soft-gel hormones. And even on the protein powders and nutra side, our capacities are very, very small. So there is a lot of eye drops, right? There is a lot of dosage forms, which we currently don't have.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected similar to FY26 at INR 5,097 million
items.quote: On the capex front, during FY '26, we incurred a capex of INR5,097 million, and we expect a similar level of investment in FY '27 as well.

items.statement: Additional INR 250 crore capex planned for ADS to clear INR 4,500 crore order backlog by 2031
items.quote: It is very clear right now, the asset turn ratio in the ADS space is very clearly 1:2. And we have given an indication that we would be incurring another INR 250 crores of capex, more or less to clear the current order backlog of INR4,500 crores.

items.statement: Board approved purchase of 10 acres land near aerospace park for ADS expansion
items.quote: yesterday, in fact, at the end of the Board meeting, we have taken an approval to acquire about 10 acres of land very near to the international airport, which is closer to the aerospace park.

items.statement: INR 50 crore capex allocated for Nichidai JV in FY27 including forging press procurement
items.quote: This year, we have kept about 50 cr as our contribution, the thing towards the JV. That would -- we have already procured one forging press, which has come into India currently on part of that -- as a part of that capex.

items.statement: New ADS factory building construction to complete by July-August 2026, already fully occupied visibility
items.quote: we have just taken up the expansion of our new factory building. And as we speak -- we expect it -- to complete the construction by July, August. And as we speak, we have a visibility of the entire factory to be fully occupied already.

items.statement: ADS component size capability expanded from 1.5m to 4-5m with 5-axis machining
items.quote: From earlier, it used to be limited to 1.5 meters was the maximum component si ze we could handle. Now we can handle up to 4 meters, 5-axis machining

items.statement: Auto ICE facilities operating at max peak utilization, expanding forging and machining at Plant 6 and Plant 12
items.quote: part of this outlay is directed towards expanding our ICE capabilities as our existing facilities are currently operating at max peak utilization. In addition, we are setting up new ADS facilities to support growing demand backed by our strong order book. Further, we continue to invest towards adding capacities into forging and machining in our existing facilities of Plant 6 and Plant 12, respecti

items.statement: Cumulative unexecuted lifetime order backlog for 5 years stands at INR 44.6 billion, especially for ADS
items.quote: If we look at the cumulative unexecuted lifetime order backlog for 5 years, especially for the ADS business, it stands at INR 44.6 billion.

items.statement: ADS confirmed order backlog of INR 4,500 crores by 2031
items.quote: we have given an indication that we would be incurring another INR 250 crores of capex, more or less to clear the current order backlog of INR4,500 crores.

items.statement: Order book visibility of INR 8,000-8,200 crores for execution by end of decade, targeting INR 10,000 crores
items.quote: as we go towards the end of this decade, we already have a visibility of closer to, as you said, about INR 8,000 crores, INR 8,200 crores on the order book front for the execution. We still have a couple of years where we can fulfill the order book and take the company towards INR10,000 crores.

items.statement: Auto ICE Q4 FY26 revenue INR 6,426 million, up 21.6% YoY driven by PV and CV with Swedish subsidiary strength
items.quote: our core Auto ICE business delivered its highest ever quarterly revenue of INR6,426 million, registering a healthy Y -o-Y growth of 21.6%. The growth was primarily driven by strong momentum in the passenger vehicles and commercial vehicles with passenger vehicle being broad -based across OEMs and commercial vehicles, led by the strong growth in Swedish subsidiary.

items.statement: Auto Tech-Agnostic and xEV Q4 FY26 revenue INR 1,217 million, up 19.8% YoY
items.quote: At the same time, our Auto -Tech Agnostic and xEV segment also registered its highest ever quarterly revenue of INR 1,217 million in Q4 FY '26, reflecting a healthy growth of 19.8%.

items.statement: Non-Auto Q4 FY26 revenue INR 1,736 million, up 70.5% YoY with ADS more than doubling
items.quote: Our Non -Auto business sustained its strong momentum, delivering a record revenues of INR1,736 million, registering a robust growth of 70.5% year -on-year. Within this segment, the ADS business more than doubled on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Domestic 2-wheeler EV offtake momentum to continue in FY27 with hybrid and energy storage opportunities
items.quote: We see a momentum to continue this year on the 2-wheeler EV offtake improvement. We are also quite excited to see the hybrids working well where we have a lot of offering on the hybrid components into the system.

items.statement: Energy storage program expected to generate INR 80-100 crores annual revenue, mass production starting FY27
items.quote: Currently, for this program, it is anywhere between INR 80 crores to INR 100 crores is the annual revenue that we expect out of this program that has come to us.

items.statement: US export demand improving after tariff reduction, no one-time inventory refill, order inflows may take 1-2 quarters to convert
items.quote: No, there is no onetime refilling that has happened. In fact, we would see that because a lot of our -- some of our clients -- U.S.-based clients had a rough -- especially on the EV segment had a rough year. So we would see that going forward, I think we will have a better offtake from the exports.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 19.3%, up 306 bps YoY from 16.3% due to positive product mix shift to higher ADS revenue
items.quote: Due to a positive product mix shift towards higher ADS revenue contribution, we witnessed margin improvement during the quarter, leading to a 306 basis points increase in the operating margins. EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 1,929 million, registering a strong growth of 52% year -on-year, while the EBITDA margin has improved to 19.3% as compared to 16.3% in the fourth quarter of FY'25.

items.statement: ADS margins expected to move towards 25-30% as new facility ramps up and utilization improves
items.quote: I think it is -- the margin profile should move towards the number that you indicated.

items.statement: Inflationary pressures across steel, aluminum, energy, tooling, consumables and freight
items.quote: Despite the strong structural tailwinds underpinning the business, the operating environment remains fluid with inflationary pressures across steel, aluminum, energy, tooling, consumables and freight, et cetera.

items.statement: Operating cash flow 11% of revenue in FY26 vs 12% in FY25 due to ADS working capital buildup, expected to optimize as flow normalizes
items.quote: We are down from 12% last year to 11% this year. We believe that this is the initial capital buildup in this segment. As we move forward, as the flow becomes more normal, we will have opportunities to further improve or optimize the overall working capital.

items.statement: Semiconductor raw material localization underway to reduce holding periods and lead times significantly
items.quote: The customers are working to localize a few component -- raw material sources, and that is underway. And the moment that happens and we are directed to buy from that source, there will be a nice significant impact on the reduction. Holding periods will come down significantly. Lead times will shrink, and that will help a lot.

items.statement: Healthy cash position of INR 3,972 million provides flexibility for expansion without significant leverage dependence
items.quote: With a healthy cash position of INR3,972 million, our balance sheet provides ample flexibility to support future expansion without significant dependence on leverage.

items.statement: Nichidai JV facility machinery installation to commence September 2026, production by Q3 FY27
items.quote: As we speak, the facility is getting ready and machinery installation should commence September time frame. And then the normal process will follow of the sample execution and production.

items.statement: Labor availability and attrition a key challenge, increasing automation to 80% on new lines and women workforce diversity
items.quote: So we are trying to increase our diversity. So one of our second plant in Pantnagar is intended to be 100% women employed. Today, we have about 65%, 70% women employees there. ADS, we have increased significantly the number of women employees. While we are working towards more and more automation, I think this is going to be one critical component where the availability and the attrition of the la

items.statement: FY26 ROCE 18.0% vs 16.2% in FY25, ROE 11.1% vs 10.5%
items.quote: We also see an improvement in our return ratios with ROCE at 18.0% as against 16.2% in FY '25 and ROE at 11.1% against 10.5% during last year.

items.statement: Geopolitical volatility, tariff uncertainty, and labor availability/attrition identified as key execution risks
items.quote: Despite the strong structural tailwinds underpinning the business, the operating environment remains fluid with inflationary pressures across steel, aluminum, energy, tooling, consumables and freight, et cetera. We are proceeding towards FY '27 with caution.

items.statement: FY27 volume guidance of 350,000 to 360,000 tonnes, subject to market conditions
items.quote: For this year, we are having around roughly you can take 3,50,000 to 3,60,000.

items.statement: EBITDA per tonne guidance to maintain current blended EBITDA of around INR 7,200-7,800 per tonne
items.quote: EBITDA, current year we are having around, blended EBITDA is 7,200 and we have taken into the consideration which is a very good EBITDA, blended EBITDA and the product mix, if you are taken, then this product mix also at far from the market level.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of sustainable 12.5-12.6%
items.quote: EBITDA margins are sustainable, basically, whatever is being shown in the numbers are there. So, these are the sustainable things and this will continue as we are focusing only on our profits.

items.statement: Existing capacity can support 30% volume growth but will not compromise profitability for volume
items.quote: Yes, we have the capacity, Still, whatever the existing capacity we are having, we can manage whatever we have achieved aro und 288,000 sales volume, we can go around 30%.

items.statement: Solar power project total cost INR 241-245 crores with INR 195 crores debt, equity investment INR 25-30 crores
items.quote: project cost is around INR241 crores and the bank term loan will become around INR195 crores. So, remaining our investments are there and that is totally backed by capital subsidy from the central government

items.statement: B2B contribution increased from 15% to 20%, targeting gradual increase
items.quote: Earlier it was 15% now it has become increased up to 20%.
