items.statement: Q4 FY26 blended EBITDA INR 7,800 per tonne vs INR 6,583 in Q4 FY25
items.quote: In the Q4 , ou r EBITDA was, blended EBITDA was INR7,800.

items.statement: Full year FY26 EBITDA margin 12.56%, Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 12.59%
items.quote: Full year EBITDA margin 12.56% . Margin remained broadly stable despite competitive market conditions.

items.statement: Full year operating cash flow INR 192 crores, EBITDA to OCF conversion 92%
items.quote: Full year operating cash flow INR192 crores, strong improvement in cash generation from operations. Full year EBITDA to OCF conversion 92%

items.statement: Net debt to EBITDA 1.65x, debt to EBITDA 0.4x, solar project net debt ~INR 160 crores after completion
items.quote: Full year net debt to EBITDA 1.65x, leverage improved and remains comfortable. Debt to EBITDA 0.4x, indicates control leverage with adequate net worth support.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu plant closure due to pollution board notice during election period, awaiting reopening order within 2-3 working days
items.quote: We are waiting for the order, everything, formalities and compliances are c ompleted and the pile was already moved. We are waiting to the opening order from the department at any point of time, maybe another two to three working days, within two to three working days.

items.statement: Value-added products 98% of revenue, focus on B2B and dealer network expansion
items.quote: Full year value -added product contribution , 98%

items.statement: Q4 volume growth 20% QoQ, revenue growth 40% QoQ, realization up 15-16%
items.quote: Volume growth is coming around 20% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: ROCE 21%, ROE 12% for FY26
items.quote: Full year ROCE 21%, return profile improved during this year. Full year ROE 12%, return on equity remained healthy.

items.statement: Solar project 38 MW under construction, 10 MW to start production next month, 60 MW total by FY27 end
items.quote: out of 60 megawatt we have started commencement of the construction and the power plant for 38 megawatts, out of 38 megawatt , 10 megawatt is coming to production, commencement in next month.

items.statement: Solar power PPA rate INR 3.21 per unit fixed for tenure
items.quote: So, per unit we are getting around INR3.21paise, apart from capital subsidy. So, as and when it will be generated that is the fixed tenurity and fixed revenue will be coming.

items.statement: No dealer losses from Tamil Nadu closure, dealer network loyal and supportive
items.quote: Our dealer network is very truly loyal with us and are continuously supporting the company.

items.statement: No impact from gas supply disruption, own suppliers and storage intact
items.quote: Touchwood we have not been impacted by the gas which means we were having our own the suppliers and other things are intact basically.

items.statement: Focus on profitable growth over volume-led growth, improving capacity utilization and operating efficiencies
items.quote: Our key priorities from FY27 will be improving capacity utilization, strengthening the value -added product mix, maintaining working capital discipline, improving operating efficiencies, optimizing financial costs and generating healthy cash flows.

items.statement: Market share by first year premium income was 56.6% for FY26 vs 57.05% in FY25
items.quote: Our market share by first premium income by first year premium income for the year ending 31st March 2026, is 56.6% as per IRDAI as compared to 57.05% for a similar period ended 31st March 2025.

items.statement: Individual business market share was 36.6% and group business market share was 70.11% for FY26
items.quote: On a comparable basis, for the year ending 31 st March, 2025, the respective market share for individual and group business were 37.46% and 71.19% respectively.

items.statement: Total premium income grew 9.8% YoY to Rs 5,35,984 crore in FY26
items.quote: For the year ended 31st March 2026, we have reported a total premium income of 5,35,984 crore rupees as compared to total premium income of 4,88,148 crore rupees, for year ending 31 Life Insurance Corporation of India May 21, 2026 March, 2025, registering a growth of 9.8% on a year-on-year basis

items.statement: Individual new business premium grew 8.29% YoY to Rs 67,676 crore in FY26
items.quote: The individual new business premium income for the year ended 31st March, 2026, was 67,676 crore rupees as compared to 62,495 crore rupees for the similar period ended 31st March, 2025, thereby registering an increase of 8.29% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Group total premium grew 16.26% YoY to Rs 1,96,609 crore in FY26
items.quote: Therefore, for the year ending 31st March, 2026, the total group premium has increased by 16.26% as compared to previous year ending 31 March, '25.

items.statement: Total APE was Rs 66,961 crore in FY26 with individual APE at Rs 43,335 crore and group APE at Rs 23,626 crore
items.quote: The total annualized premium equivalent (APE) for the year ended 31 st March 2026, is 66,961 crore rupees, which comprised individual APE of 43,335 crore rupees and group APE of 23,626 crore rupees.

items.statement: Non-par share of individual APE rose to 35.11% in FY26 from 27.69% in FY25, a 43.78% YoY increase
items.quote: Since then, our non-par APE has increased from 10,581 crore rupees to 15,214 crore rupees, reflecting an increase of 43.78% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Profit after tax grew 19.25% YoY to Rs 57,419 crore in FY26, the highest in history
items.quote: The PAT for the year ended 31st March 2026 was 57,419 crore rupees as compared to 48,151 crore rupees for the last year, registering a growth of 19.25% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Net VNB grew 41.63% YoY to Rs 14,179 crore in FY26, the highest ever
items.quote: That net VNB has registered a growth of 41.63% on a year-on-year basis to 14,179 crore rupees for the year ended 31st March, 2026, from 10,011 crore rupees for the previous year.

items.statement: Net VNB margin improved 360 bps YoY to 21.2% in FY26, the highest ever
items.quote: Further, net VNB margin has improved by 360 basis points on a year-on-year basis to 21.2% for the year ended 31 March, 2026 from 17.6% for the previous year.

items.statement: Solvency ratio improved to 2.35 as of March 31, 2026 from 2.11 a year earlier
items.quote: The solvency ratio as on 31st March 2026 improved to 2.35 as against 2.11 on March 31st 2025.

items.statement: Indian Embedded Value grew 1.58% YoY to Rs 7,89,185 crore as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: The Indian embedded value as on 31st March 2026 has been determined as 7,89,185 crore rupees as compared to 7,76,876 crore rupees as on 31st March 2025. Therefore, the IEV has registered an increase of 1.58% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Assets under management grew 5.08% YoY to Rs 57,29,396 crore as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: The assets under management as on 31st March 2026 was 57,29,396 crore rupees as compared to 54,52,297 crore rupees as on 31st March 2025. Therefore, our AUM has registered a growth of 5.08% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Offered 58 products as of March 31, 2026 (36 individual, 13 group, 1 common) plus 7 individual riders and 1 group rider
items.quote: As on 31st March 2026, we had a comprehensive suite of 58 products excluding the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana available for new business including 36 exclusive individual products, 13 exclusive group products and one common product which is eligible for group as well as individual business.

items.statement: Number of policies sold grew 3.7% YoY to 1,84,41,175 in FY26
items.quote: The number of policies sold during the year ended 31st March 2026, we sold 1,84,41,175 new policies as compared to 1,77,82,975 new policies in the previous year, registering a growth of 3.7% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Individual agent count declined to 14,57,045 as of March 31, 2026 from 14,86,851 a year earlier; market share by agents fell to 44.25% from 47.61%
items.quote: Agency workforce as on 31st March 2026 the total number of individual agents was 14,57,045 as compared to 14,86,851 as on 31st March 2025. The market share by number of agents as on 31st March 2026 stands at 44.25% as against 47.61% for March 31st 2025.

items.statement: Agency channel sold 98.42% of policies and contributed 91.75% of new business premium in FY26
items.quote: Further, 98.42% of our policies in the year ended March 31st 2026 were sold by our agency force. When seen on premium basis, 91.75% of the new business premium came from our agency channel in the financial year ending of 2025-26.

items.statement: Bancassurance and Alternate Channels new business premium grew 45.19% YoY to Rs 5,076 crore in FY26, crossing Rs 5,000 crore for the first time
items.quote: Bancassurance and Alternate Channels collected a new business premium income of 5,076 crore rupees for the year ended 31st March 2026 as compared to 3,496.10 crore rupees for the previous year, registering a growth of 45.19% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Overall expense ratio improved 51 bps YoY to 11.91% in FY26, the lowest since listing
items.quote: For the year ended 31st March 2026, the overall expense ratio was 11.91%, as compared to 12.42% for the last year. Therefore, there is a decrease of 51 basis points in our overall expense ratio on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Persistency on premium basis: 13th month 74.64%, 25th month 68.98%, 37th month 66.94%, 49th month 63.03%, 61st month 59.31% as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: On premium basis, the persistency for 13th, 25th, 37th, 49th and 61st month up to 31st March 2026 stands at 74.64%, 68.98%, 66.94%, 63.03% and 59.31% respectively, as compared to 74.84%, 70.99%, 66.11%, 61.51% and 63.12% respectively, up to the year ended 31st March 2025.

items.statement: Persistency on policy count basis: 13th month 64.87%, 25th month 57.65%, 37th month 55.29%, 49th month 49.78%, 61st month 46.88% as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: On number of policies basis, the persistency for 13th, 25th, 37th, 49th and 61st month up to the year ended 31st March 2026 stands at 64.87%, 57.65%, 55.29%, 49.78% and 46.88% respectively, as compared to 64.12%, 59.32%, 52.66%, 48.79% and 50.31% respectively, up to the previous year ended 31st March 2025.

items.statement: Digital ANANDA app completed 23,00,983 policies in FY26, up 56.08% YoY; active agents on app grew 29.56%
items.quote: in our digital initiative, through the agent assisted ANANDA app, we have completed 23,00,983 policies, during the year ended 31st March 2026 as compared to 14,74,208 policies on the year ended 31st March 2025, thereby registering a growth of 56.08% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Maturity claims rose 17.97% YoY to Rs 2,79,951 crore; death claims rose 1.91% to Rs 24,885 crore in FY26
items.quote: On an amount basis, during the year ended 31st March 2026, the total maturity claims were 2,79,951 crore rupees and the total death claims were 24,885 crore rupees.

items.statement: Bima Sakhi Yojana: 3,45,000 women designated as Bima Sakhis, sold 21.94 lakh policies generating Rs 2,848 crore premium in FY26; covered 59% of Gram Panchayats
items.value: 3,45,000 Bima Sakhis, 21.94 lakh policies, 2,848 crore premium
items.quote: As of 31st March 2026, a total of 3,45,000 women have been designated as Bima Sakhi's, successfully selling 21.94 lakh insurance policies and generating a new business premium income of 2,848 crore rupees in the year ended 31st March 2026.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR 10 per equity share (INR 20 pre-bonus) for FY26
items.quote: I would like to share that the Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of INR10 per equity share of INR10 each equivalent to INR20 per equity share, pre-bonus issue basis, for the financial year 2025-26 subject to approval of shareholders in the 5th Annual General Meeting of the Corporation.

items.statement: Cautious on dividend payout ratio due to upcoming risk-based capital framework; need to maintain solvency buffers given high equity exposure
items.quote: See the payout ratio will depend on how the regulatory changes also happen. So we have to be a bit cautious in releasing it because the -- there are some expected regulatory changes particularly in respect of the risk-based capital being planned to be introduced.

items.statement: Non-par IRR pricing depends on investment opportunities, competitive scenario, hedging availability, and margin protection; no commitment on FY27 rate increases
items.quote: The IRR is a factor which depends upon the available investment opportunity, not necessarily from a year-to-year basis, but for the duration for which the products are priced, as well as for the competitive reasons.

items.statement: Focus on agent quality, productivity, training, and recruiting younger agents; agency count decline of ~30,000 not seen as business impact
items.quote: Training will be our focus for the new agents as well as existing agents. Second will be young generation, new agents. Younger age group agents are going to rope in in more numbers, so that they are with us for quite some time, and they will address the requirements of the millennials.

items.statement: Bancassurance policy count decline driven by one microfinance partner; conscious shift away from low-persistency login-based sales toward higher ticket sizes; Q4 showed ~10% growth in sales count
items.quote: Coming to reduction in number of sales through bancassurance, primarily it is not bank driven or alternate channel driven performance decline. It is mainly attributed to one geographical issue where one of our corporate agency, and particularly a microfinance institution was not able to concentrate that heavily and that has impacted.

items.statement: VNB margin drivers: business mix shift to non-par (+3%), RFR changes (+3.4%), operating assumption changes (-2.8% including GST impact)
items.quote: So this business mix which has gone up has contributed to 3% to the VNB margin. Then the RFR throughout the year if you see, it is ranging, it's range-bound and then in some months it has gone up to 0.84 – 84 basis points or so. So this RFR has contributed to 3.4%. And with regard to this operating assumptions as you asked, this is mainly because some lines of business, the expense has been realig

items.statement: VNB composition: par individual 42% of APE contributes 28% of VNB; non-par individual 22.7% of APE contributes 53% of VNB; group contributes remainder
items.quote: If you look at the par individual business, which is about 42% of the APE, is contributing to the extent of 28% of VNB margin – 28% of VNB. Now if you look at that non-par business, individual non-par business contribution to the VNB, 22.7% is the proportion of APE, which is contributing to the extent of 53% of VNB.

items.statement: Future VNB margin expansion expected from ticket size increases and persistency improvement; non-par mix to consolidate; Ind AS implementation ongoing
items.quote: the focus would be on increasing the ticket size, the product mix that we are selling, though the mix may not increase too much, we would like it to consolidate or whatever it is. Two aspects, one, the ticket size of the policies going up; and two, improvement in persistency are the ones which may be -- which should be the drivers for margin expansion further.

items.statement: High equity exposure makes LIC sensitive to volatility under risk-based capital; dividend policy to be finalized after RBC framework clarity
items.quote: Now on one side, that leads to improved returns to the policy holders that's why we are seeing something like 8.9% to be the -- as compared to the previous year, something around 8.5% or so. On the other side, when the risk-based capital assessments are done, -- as of now, it is only been a quick exercise, so I will not get into details of that. But the point here is sensitivity to the volatility

items.statement: FY27 volume target 231,000 metric tons, 73% capacity utilization, 13% YoY revenue growth, EBITDA margin ~11%, BESS revenue additional
items.quote: Looking ahead to financial year 2027, we are confident of sustaining our growth trajectory, targeting a volume of 231,000 metric tons per annum with a capacity utilization of 73% and a year-on-year revenue growth of 13% alongside top line expansion. We remain equally focused on margin quality with EBITDA margins anticipated at approximately 11%, reflecting our continued emphasis on operational eff

items.statement: FY28 polymer volume growth 15% over FY27 base of 230,000 tons
items.quote: See, Arihant, this question with regard to polymer compounding. So, we are expecting 15% growth -- volume growth over what we achieved in 2026, 2027. Means in 2026, 2027, if we are targeting a polymer compound volume of 230,000 tons, then in 2027, 2028, you can add on another 15% on that 230,000 tons.

items.statement: BESS FY27 revenue INR200-250 crores, breakeven; FY28 target 1 GWh, INR800-900 crores revenue, EBITDA margin 10%+
items.quote: Current year, we are close to INR200 crores to INR250 crores because the machine will stabilize, there will be ramp-up. It will be taking some time. However, from next financial year, yes, you're right. We are targeting 1 gigawatt hour of sales and close to INR800 crores to INR900 crores of revenue, expecting EBITDA margins of 10-plus. So, INR80 crores to INR90 crores of EBITDA, which we are antic

items.statement: FY26 capex ~INR100 crores; FY27 capex ~INR175 crores including ~INR70 crores for BESS and ~INR100 crores for XLPE capacity
items.quote: During financial year 2026, we incurred a capital expenditure of close to INR100-odd crores. Looking ahead, we plan to invest further INR175-odd crores in financial year 2027, primarily towards expanding our XLPE compound capacity with investments earmarked for our diversification into BESS as well.

items.statement: Total installed capacity 268,400 MTPA end FY26; added 30,000 MTPA PVC/HFFR and 48,000 MTPA XLPE at Bhiwadi (commercial April 2026); overall capacity beyond 315,000 MTPA
items.quote: To sustain this momentum, we have strategically invested in both brownfield and greenfield expansions, elevating our total installed capacity to 2,68,400 metric tons per annum this fiscal year, adding another additional 30,000 metric tons per annum overall, another 48,000 metric tons dedicated to XLPE in operation from April 2026 onwards at a committed capex of INR80 crores. This capacity addition

items.statement: Sufficient order book, no lag in bookings; export volumes up 23% in FY26, April-May exports higher month-on-month
items.quote: As Kothari ji highlighted earlier, that cable manufacturers have diversified over a period of time. And now they have sufficient demand, not only with regards to government, but private demand, private capex as well. So, we are getting sufficient order book, and there is no lag as far as the booking is concerned.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin 11%; FY27 guided ~11% despite raw material volatility; pass-through lag 7-15 days normally, instant for sharp spikes
items.quote: EBITDA grew by 12% year-on-year with margins at 11%, a commendable outcome achieved despite multiple industry headwinds and softer trade sentiment amid the ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.

items.statement: Raw material prices up 50%+ in FY26; pass-through to selling prices done; prices now stabilized; fixed margin per kg maintained
items.quote: Yes. See, we are able to pass-through the price increases, which means we are able to maintain our fixed margins per kg basis.

items.statement: Raw materials: polyethylene and PVC polymers; sourced from domestic petrochemical majors and imports from Middle East/Europe; import share 10-15%; supply constraints normalized by mid-April
items.quote: We source from both domestic and import sources. In domestic we have all the big petrochemical players as our suppliers. Similarly, on import side, we rely on a lot of big players in the Middle East as well as in European countries. And there were issues till, I will say, mid of April, where the supply constraints were there. However, today, the supply is more or less normalized.

items.statement: Domestic wires & cables demand robust driven by renewables, T&D, data centers; localization trend benefits domestic polymer producers; no demand impact from perceived government capex cut
items.quote: India's domestic wires and cable sector continues to thrive with robust growth, fueled by surging demand across key areas. The rapid adoption of renewables expansion in transmission and distribution networks and the nationwide push for data centers.

items.statement: Exports rose 30% in FY26; MENA region strong, Europe growing, LatAm/North America flat; April-May export volumes higher month-on-month
items.quote: No, all markets have contributed well up to Europe, I would say, because it had not impacted demand sales point of view. Latin America and North America has not shown any growth, but rest of the world, say, MENA region mainly, Middle East and North Africa has contributed strongly to our numbers.

items.statement: Inventory and receivables up due to 50%+ raw material price increase; inventory comparable in volume terms; debtor days controlled
items.quote: So, the -- since we have highlighted already, the average raw material prices have gone up substantially. There is a steep increase in the prices, close to 50%-plus. So, now that is the impact of that only.

items.statement: Net worth INR1,013 crores, up INR179 crores YoY; sufficient banking limits for BESS working capital (INR200-250 crores for 1 GWh phase)
items.quote: Our net worth increased to INR1,013 crores, reflecting a growth of INR179-odd crores over the previous year and underscoring our disciplined approach to cash flow management.

items.statement: Proposed final dividend INR1.25 per share for FY26
items.quote: We are pleased to propose a final dividend of INR1.25 per share for financial year 2026 as a final dividend, reaffirming our commitment to delivering consistent returns to our shareholders.

items.statement: XLPE largest player, competition from Dow, Borealis; HFFR competition from Shakun Polymer (Orbia); entry barrier is proven performance and approval cycles
items.quote: And as far as the competition is concerned, in XLPE, we are the largest player. We are having major market share. So, in XLPE, the competition is from overseas players like Dow and Borealis. Now, the low-voltage fire-blast segment, there are a couple of Indian producers like KLJ Polymers. And in HFFR, Shakun Polymer is the -- which is now part of Orbia Group from Mexico. They are our competition.

items.statement: Supplying to cable producers for data centers, solar, T&D; BESS discussions with Tier 1 developers (Sterling, Wilson, Enrich, Orange); approval cycle 3-6 months
items.quote: We had already discussed with all the Tier 1 developer in India, including Sterling, Wilson and Enrich and Orange. So, this customer, we already started to pitching and demand is high. And just we started to have their quality parameters, validation, quality supply chains, all the documentations required.

items.statement: No significant import pressure from China; scale and capability strong enough to face competition
items.quote: No. See, China import pressure direct or indirect will always remain in every segment, but our scale and our capability is quite strong, and we are able to face it off without any challenge.

items.statement: BESS certifications required: ISO 62619, 62777, 62999, 629540, 62384; government mandates EMS made in India, BMS import allowed from China
items.quote: So, these are the base guidance the developers follow the as per ISO standard. So, because as per ISO standard, fire and safety concern. So, they are validating from documentation to reliabilities each and every parameter.

items.statement: Polymer compounding FY26 volume 201,370 MT, utilization 77% (incl. new capacity with limited operating time); HFR utilization ~50% during turbulence
items.quote: Operationally, our volumes for financial year 2026 stood at 2,01,370 metric tons per annum, translating a capacity utilization of 77%. The modernization in utilization level is attributable to the inclusion of 30,000 metric tons per annum of incremental capacities in PVC and HFFR added during financial year 2026, which had limited operating time during the year.

items.statement: Geopolitical conflict (Israel-Iran) disrupted exports, logistics, raw material availability and cost; backward integration risk from customers mitigated by scale, skill, product range
items.quote: Financial year 2026 presented challenging external environment shaped largely by the Israel-Iran conflict that escalated from 28th February, disrupting exports, transit routes, tightening raw material availability, and triggering steep input cost inflation.

items.statement: BESS entry via assembly initially, importing cells/components from China; plan to develop own BMS/EMS IP; backward integration over time
items.quote: Yes, initially for the initial period, we are going to import it from China. And over a period of time, we will be working on backward integration or just a suggestion of many components, which are easily available in the country.

items.statement: Mamaearth brand expected to deliver double-digit CAGR over next 5 years
items.quote: we're fairly confident of delivering a double-digit CAGR on the brand from the next 5 years perspective.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA at INR77 crores (11.3% margin), up 2.5x YoY; full-year EBITDA margin 9.3%, up ~100 bps YoY
items.quote: We've delivered 28% Y-o-Y growth with EBITDA scaling almost 2.5x over last year same quarter. Overall, INR682 crores in quarterly revenue, 71.4% gross margin, which has expanded by 70 basis points Y-o-Y. EBITDA at INR77 crores, which is 11.3%.

items.statement: Mamaearth and Derma Co. both double-digit EBITDA positive; expected to continue improving margin trajectory
items.quote: Mamaearth and Derma Co., both are double-digit EBITDA-positive now. And we foresee them to continue improving their margin trajectory in future, as they have done in the past, along with growth.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 revenue INR682 crores, 28% YoY growth (like-for-like); third consecutive quarter of 20%+ growth; volume-driven
items.quote: We've delivered 28% Y-o-Y growth with EBITDA scaling almost 2.5x over last year same quarter. Overall, INR682 crores in quarterly revenue, 71.4% gross margin, which has expanded by 70 basis points Y-o-Y.

items.statement: FY26 revenue grew 20% YoY; volume-driven growth; PAT INR200+ crores
items.quote: Looking back at overall FY '26, and this is a year where we have delivered 20% Y-o-Y growth, and this was our internal agenda and the team has come together and has been able to deliver it.

items.statement: Focus categories grew 35% YoY; contribution up 500 bps in 1 year; all channels growing strongly in focus categories
items.quote: the focus categories that we have chosen to double down on continue to drive growth for the company. They have grown by 35% Y-o-Y. Contribution of focus categories has increased by 500 basis points in 1 year and all the channels are growing strongly in our focus categories

items.statement: Products launched in last 1 year contributed 7-8% of growth; innovation viewed on 3-year horizon
items.quote: if we look at just the products launched in last 1 year, Manoj, that growth would be to the tune of about 7% to 8%.

items.statement: Mamaearth brand grew mid-teens in Q4; brand health at multi-quarter high; value market share up consistently in core categories
items.quote: Mamaearth continues to become stronger in terms of the consumer love it's getting which is visible in the growth as well. The brand has grown at mid-teens this quarter. The brand health is at multi-quarter high.

items.statement: Derma Co. face cleanser business almost doubled; Nielsen market share ~1% for face wash; hero products >50% of brand revenue
items.quote: the face cleanser business has almost doubled for the brand in terms of growth and it's also now visible in GT market shares, in Nielsen almost 1% market share for Derma Co face wash is visible now.

items.statement: Reginald Men (acquired) grew 100%+ YoY; crossed INR100 crores ARR; 6th brand in portfolio to do so
items.quote: the brand has actually grown by 100% plus and doubled its revenue Y-o-Y. It has also crossed INR100 crores ARR mark becoming the sixth brand in Honasa's portfolio to do so.

items.statement: Younger brands (ex-Reginald) grew 28%+ in Q4; all brands with strong product superiority and sharp consumer targeting showing strong results
items.quote: Yes, they are at 28%-plus.

items.statement: Mamaearth distribution at 200,000 outlets; target 0.5 million outlets over next 3-5 years
items.quote: the brand is only 200,000 outlets and potentially can get to 0.5 million outlets over the next 3 to 5 years.

items.statement: Direct Distributor stocks optimized at 25-30 days; strong distribution ecosystem in Top-100 cities enabling Derma Co. GT expansion
items.quote: Our Direct Distributors stocks are also optimized between 25 to 30 days. And this distribution system is helping us drive our other brands like The Derma Co also in GT.

items.statement: Calibrated price increases executed in Q1 FY27 to offset crude-driven RM/PM inflation; RPI remains competitive; no further hikes expected at current crude levels
items.quote: we have already executed some calibrated price increases in line with where we've also seen competition taking the price in crease the same, and our RPI is still remaining fairly competitive at that premium that we want to maintain

items.statement: Company remains negative working capital; continues to generate excess cash
items.quote: we continue to be negative working capital. So a call out that this growth includes our recent acquisition of BTM Ventures as well. And this is a like-for-like growth.

items.statement: Board approved first-ever dividend of INR3 per equity share (50% of FY26 PAT); total cash payout ~INR98 crores
items.quote: this is the first main year for the company where the Board has decided to reward shareholders with a dividend straight off with INR 3 per equity share. This is about 50% of the PAT that the company has generated for the full year, which is in excess of INR200 crores, And the total cash payout will be about INR98 crores as a part of this dividend.

items.statement: New senior hires: Saahil (ex-CEO cosmetic/makeup cos), Dheeraj (nutraceuticals founder), Madhur (new-age business builder) to shape next horizon of businesses
items.quote: we have recently made a few new appointments, which includes Saahil, who's been CEO at multiple cosmetic and makeup companies; Dheeraj, who has been a founder of nutraceuticals brand; Madhur who has worked across new age companies to build businesses and shape the other businesses.

items.statement: Derma Co. ARR at INR750+ crores; targeting INR1,000 crores; claims largest actives brand per Euromonitor and Nielsen
items.quote: As we disclosed, it was at INR750 crores-plus. It continues to grow on from there.

items.statement: Online channel showing double-digit growth for Mamaearth
items.quote: Online is also showing double-digit growth.

items.statement: Philosophy: pursue opportunities by building required talent/playbooks; only limits are those organization chooses to accept
items.quote: the only limits that exist for us are the ones that we choose to accept. And I think I was fairly moved by that and that has been my operating philosophy.

items.statement: Aqualogica 2-2.5 years younger than Derma Co.; investment gears shift based on consumer sentiment (actives tailwind now favoring Derma Co.)
items.quote: Rest all the brands are actually much younger, Aqualogica is 2 years later than Derma Co., actually 2.5 in terms of its birth year and month. And hence, they are actually years apart in terms of their progression as well.

items.statement: Core business like-for-like growth 21% in Q4 (ex-Reginald); EBITDA impact of Reginald ~30 bps
items.quote: from a growth perspective, 21% will be the like-for-like growth. And from an EBITDA perspective, the impact will be just about 30 basis points. Rest of all EBITDA is of the core business.

items.statement: A&P leverage: ad spend value up but % of revenue down; 3 leverage buckets - channel/performance spend, brand spend, OpEx spend - to drive 500 bps EBITDA expansion over 5 years
items.quote: In general, advertising as a value spend is something that we have talked about, will go up. But as percentage, it comes down. And hence, that's the A&P leverage that we see getting generated in the business.

items.statement: Flipkart settlement impacts revenue recognition (not bottom line); reported growth lower than like-for-like due to base effect
items.quote: the reported growth, of course, contains the Flipkart adjustment that we have been talking about over the last few quarters, where revenue recognition gets impacted, but not the bottom line and we have shared those numbers as well

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 15% maintained for FY27 despite West Asia crisis
items.quote: Despite the West Asian crisis and uncertainty looming over it, we would like to maintain the revenue guidance of 15% FY '27.

items.statement: Pens segment targeted at 5% growth, Creative at 50%, Steel Bottles at 40% for FY27
items.quote: So what we are targeting for the coming years is the writing instrument, which is Pens would be growing at 5% on an annual basis. And also to add the high -growth category, which is Creative, we are targeting 50% growth this year as well. And for Steel Bottles, we continue to grow at 40%.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin impact of ~4% from crude-linked raw material cost increase, expected to normalize by year-end
items.quote: So everything averages out and the impact will be in the -- in Q4, a total of 13%, which would net up to something like a 4% or something in Q1.

items.statement: Full year FY27 EBITDA margin target range 17-19% with 18% as base case
items.quote: Yes. So like we said that our target was towards 18%. So we might see an impact of 1% looking at the global scenario.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at INR80-90 crores including INR60-70 crores for Valsad facility capitalization
items.quote: What we see in the coming year in this quarter when we capitalize the new Valsad facility, so we have another outlay of probably INR60 -- INR70-odd crores. And the total capex for the year would go to around INR80 crores, INR90 crores.

items.statement: Valsad facility operations commenced in Q1 FY27, capacity ramp-up expected by Q3 FY27
items.quote: Operations at our new Valsad facility are scheduled to commence from Q1 FY '27 with capacity ramp-up expected by Q3 FY '27.

items.statement: Peak revenue capacity from all facilities estimated at INR1,750 crores
items.quote: What we see in the next -- the peak revenue from the assets which we would have would come to around INR1750 crores of sales which we can do from these facilities which we are building up.

items.statement: Creative segment revenue INR298 crores for FY26 (74% YoY growth), Steel Bottles INR85 crores (95% YoY growth)
items.quote: The Creative segment achieved impressive growth of 80% year -on-year growth for Q4 FY '26 and 74% year-on-year for FY '26, the whole year. The revenue contribution stood at INR86 crores for the quarter, that's Q4 at INR298 crores for the full financial year.

items.statement: Own brand sales increased to 91% of total revenue in FY26 from 87% in FY25
items.quote: Our own brand sales now account for approximately 91% of the total revenue in FY '26, marking a steady and consi stent rise from 87% in FY '25, 86% in FY '24 and 80% in FY '23.

items.statement: Pens own brand share rose to 95% of Pens revenue from 80% a year ago
items.quote: To summarize, while th e Pens business grew in FY '26 with focus on quality and our revenue mix, showing a significant shift towards own brand sales, which now represents 95% of our Pens revenue versus 80% a year ago.

items.statement: Crude-linked raw material costs increased 10-50% (weighted avg 13%), 35% of raw materials are crude derivatives
items.quote: Cost of such raw materials have gone up from 10% to 50% on an average. So we are expecting an impact of about 13% increase in the consumption ratio.

items.statement: Price increases taken in Steel Bottles and Houseware; rationalizing schemes and discounts to offset margin impact
items.quote: In household and Steelware, we have also increased the selling price for all the products. With sustained focus on premiumization with a consistently rising share of mid -premium and premium products in new product launches, we expect to further offset the negative margin impact.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 inventory days 97, debtor days 78 (down 4 QoQ), creditor days 37 (down 3 QoQ), working capital cycle 139 days
items.quote: Our inventory days s tood at 97 days in Q4 FY '26. It was similar compared to other quarters as we stocked up more inventory in advance during the quarter, anticipating further price in crude oil and its byproducts. On the other hand, our debtor days stood at 78 days. It reduced by 4 days quarter-on-quarter and our creditor days stood at 37 days, a decrease of 3 days quarter-on-quarter. Hence, our

items.statement: Expect 5-7 days inventory improvement in next 2 quarters as pre-stocking was one-time
items.quote: Going forward, obviously -- , streamline inventory. Inventory prestocking was a onetime event, which we said. This is not what we are going to -- is going to repeat. So with the entire West Asia crisis coming -- moving in a direction, we see around 5 to 7 days of improvement in inventory in the coming 2 quarters.

items.statement: Pre-stocked 4-5 weeks of raw material inventory (40% of total inventory) to hedge crude price rise
items.quote: So in my inventory, when I say raw material and packing material, which constitute -- which makes up around 40% of my inventory. And when I say stocking up of the inventory, it's around 4 to 5 weeks of inventory -- raw material inventory stock up.

items.statement: Export OEM declined due to West Asia route closure; Middle East is 25% of export revenue; own brand exports grew 31% YoY in Q4, 29% for FY26
items.quote: So the overall export to the Middle Eastern countries is about 25%.

items.statement: Domestic OEM fully phased out; new Flomaxe subsidiary creating incremental domestic OEM revenue
items.quote: As highlighted earlier, our domestic OEM business has been fully phased out with legacy OEM relationships reduced to 0. Nonetheless, we are pleased to share that new customer engagements through our Flomaxe subsidiary have created an incremental revenue stream within the domestic OEM segment.

items.statement: Creative growth driven by market share gains from competitors (DOMS, Faber-Castell, Cello, Camlin) via innovative products
items.quote: So what we expect from -- the growth is from the -- we will increase our -- grab the market share from the existing players in the category by -- and the main reason why we have been growing at such a high speed is the innovative products, what we ha ve launched in the last 2 years.

items.statement: Final dividend of INR0.50 per share (10% of face value) approved for FY26, same 20% payout as prior year
items.quote: In line with our strong performance and positive outlook, the Board of Directors have approved a final dividend of INR0.50 per share, representing 10% of face value of our equity share, aggregating 20% of FY '26 similar to previous year.

items.statement: Back-to-school demand extremely positive, no dent from price increases taken
items.quote: So the demand is extremely positive when we talk about the back -to-school season. It's very, very positive. Okay. So there is no dent on the demand post the price increases which we have taken.

items.statement: West Asia crisis causing crude price volatility; margin impact if conflict persists beyond 2-3 months
items.quote: However, the ongoing West Asia crisis has inflated crude oil prices drastically, leading to a corresponding increase in crude-linked derivatives, which are one of the important components of raw materials.

items.statement: Employee cost stable at 20-21% of revenue including job work; consistent percentage despite absolute growth
items.quote: At our -- if I do at the console level, my employee cost is same percentage -wise, same at 20% to 21%. It's consistent over there.

items.statement: Flomaxe subsidiary operationalized wooden pencil manufacturing; INR20 crores capex in FY26 for Surat facility
items.quote: We recently incurred a capex of INR20 crores FY '26 for the Flomaxe facility in Surat, mainly invested in the new building and plant in machinery and has already emerged as a revenue -accretive driver for the Creative segment. We recently operationalized wo oden pencil manufacturing at this facility, a major category expansion in Creative segment.

items.statement: Planning to add fourth production line for Steel Bottles
items.quote: We are planning to expand our Steel business by adding one more line.

items.statement: Creative growth driven by pencil category (mechanical, wooden, 2mm) and kids coloring range; new categories planned
items.quote: So the maximum revenue growth, what we have seen in the last couple of years is in the pencil category and also in the kids category. So pencil is going to grow further for next 2, 3 years. And also, we will be adding new categories in terms of the coloring range of geo boxes strengthen our position there as well.

items.statement: Expect late-teen volume growth in FY27 with EBITDA margins broadly in line with FY26 levels
items.quote: Looking ahead, our outlook for FY '27 remains optimistic. We expect late -teen volume growth for the business while maintaining EBITDA margins broadly in line with FY '26 levels.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected at Rs.450-500 crores; next 2 years planned capex Rs.800 crores including solar
items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect total capex for FY '27 to be in the range of Rs.450 crores to Rs.500 crores, primarily directed towards expanding our high -growth capabilities and creating sustainable long-term value for all stakeholders.

items.statement: New business order book stands at nearly Rs.950 crores executable over 2.5-3 years
items.quote: The order book for the new businesses today stands at nearly Rs.950 crores, which will be executed in the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 59.4% in Q4 FY26 and 59.1% for FY26; EBITDA margin 31.5% Q4 and 30.4% FY26
items.quote: Gross profit for the quarter stood at Rs.252 crores, while for FY '26, it is Rs.915 crores, registering a year-on-year growth of 21.9% and 11.9%, respectively. Consequently, gross margin increased to 59.4% for the Q4 FY '26 and 59.1% for the full year by 70 basis points and 140 basis points, respectively.

items.statement: Expect 3.5-4% selling price increase from customers for non-steel cost inflation; confirmations from few OEMs received
items.quote: besides the steel price, we are expecting around 3.5% to 4% i ncrease on selling price from our customers, for which our teams are in discussion. We have received the confirmation from a few OEMs. We are hopeful to get it from 1st of April

items.statement: Domestic CV industry mid-teens growth in FY26; FY27 outlook stable with replacement and infra-led demand
items.quote: Domestic industry outlook for FY '27 remains stable with expectations of continued replacement demand and infrastructure -led growth.

items.statement: Machining contribution increased to 89% in FY26 from 87% in FY25; heavy forgings (700kg-1.8 tons) part of new order book
items.quote: Machining contribution increased to 89% in FY '26 compared to 87% in FY '25 and 73% in FY '21.

items.statement: Forging capacity 147,000 tons FY26 to 161,000 tons FY27 to 187,000 tons FY28; machining 69,000 to 82,000 FY27 to 87,000 FY28
items.quote: Forging capacities in the last year have ramped up from 125,000 to 147,000, which is further expected to go up to 161,000 by FY '27. And further, it will be enhanced to 187,000 tons, addition of almost 26,000 tons from FY '27 to '28.

items.statement: CV market share expected to rise from 32% to 42% on MHCV; PV share from 32% to 47% with large customer; farm share 41% to 45%
items.quote: So for our product range, we are currently at 32% market share on the CV side, which we expect to go up to 42% on the MHCV side. So simply on a market share basis, we expect good growth.

items.statement: Export CV demand expected mid-single digit growth in Europe; North America PV programs ramping from Q2 FY27; industrial Europe orders from FY29
items.quote: CV as per the company and as per the recent comment ary, we are seeing that should grow this year by single digit, by mid-single digit this year

items.statement: Raw material price increases passed through to OEMs with 1 month lag domestic, 1 quarter lag export; fuel cost up 30-40% but only 1% of cost
items.quote: On the domestic side with 1 month lag and on the export side with a lag of 1 quarter. So we are not worried about the steel price pass -through.

items.statement: No management changes or key hires discussed

items.quote: We successfully completed pilot field trials of our raw effluent membrane technology, which represents a step change in wastewater treatment by enabling direct treatment of raw effluents without the need for conventional pre-treatment.

items.quote: we think it would be fair to assume an average price of around $2. We say between INR1,600 crores to INR1,800 crores is the potential for this at 100,000 tons utilization.

items.statement: Ex-battery business revenue potential INR1,000-1,200 crores with current greenfield capacity
items.quote: excluding battery, once this greenfield now that is commissioned, the business can scale to approximately INR1000 crores to INR1200 crores without any incremental capex in the existing product portfolio.

items.statement: NSS Ireland acquisition integration progressing smoothly; appointed new business head for European expansion
items.quote: the integration process across operations and supply chain continues to progress smoothly. To further strengthen the business and accelerate expansion outside of Ireland, we recentl y appointed Mr. Mattias Fredrickson, as the new business head of NSS

items.statement: Significant recruitment for greenfield facility completed in FY26; costs currently in pharma food nutrition vertical
items.quote: we have gone through a significant recruitment cycle to support the new greenfield that we have, that we are going to be operating. But because we have not entirely started generating revenue, all of those, all those expenses of employees are also sitting in the pharma food nutrition vertical today.

items.statement: Aspire to grow at least about 20% in FY27
items.quote: we aspire to grow at least about 20%. We will do our best to achieve that.

items.statement: Demand moderation continued in latter half of Q4 FY26 amid geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainty
items.quote: Following softer discretionary spending trends in Q3 FY '26 across our categories, demand moderation continued further in the latter half of the Q4 FY '26 too amid evolving geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainty.

items.statement: Gross margin for Q4 FY26 stood at 56%
items.quote: Gross margin for the quarter stood at INR192 crores with a margin of 56%.

items.statement: Reported EBITDA margin for Q4 FY26 was 10.6%
items.quote: The reported EBITDA, excluding other income for the quarter was INR36 crores with a margin of 10.6%.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin at 6.3% remains relatively soft on sequential basis
items.quote: Operating EBITDA, which is at 6.3%, remains relatively soft on a sequential basis, largely due to the better operating leverage in the quarter 3, which was the festive period with higher sales and marketing investments.

items.statement: Anticipate A&P spend to ramp up to 7-8% of sales over medium term
items.quote: we reiterate that over the medium term, we anticipate a ramp-up in our brand building efforts from the A&P spend expected to be around 7% to 8% of the sales with continuous monitoring on the success metrics.

items.statement: Expect minor gross margin impact in Q1 FY27 but hope to stay steady at March exit level
items.quote: Compared to March exit gross margin, we foresee that it will hopefully stay steady at that level for AMJ.

items.statement: Raw material prices such as polyol, TDI increased 30% to 150% in March quarter
items.quote: The March quarter saw sharp inflation across several input categories with select raw materials such as the chemicals which get used like the polyol, TDI, etcetera, registering price increases ranging from 30% to 150%.

items.statement: Implemented two calibrated price increases of 7-8% each in March and April
items.quote: we have done two measured calibrated price increases of about 7% to 8% in March and 7% to 8% in April.

items.statement: FY26 revenue reached INR14,889 million with 17% YoY growth
items.quote: With 17% year-on-year growth, we delivered our highest ever annual revenue at INR14,889 million.

items.statement: Mattress category grew 20% in Q4 FY26, contributing 61.4% of FY26 revenue
items.quote: In Q4 FY '26, the mattress category continued to lead and grew by 20%, outpacing the industry growth trends, we were able to garner this growth due to our strong omnichannel sales presence, complete product portfolio and retail conversion.

items.statement: Furniture category grew 24% in FY26 and 14% in Q4 FY26, contributing 29.3% of revenue
items.quote: The furniture category contributed about 29.3% of revenues for FY '26. The growth of this category was approximately 24% in FY '26 and 14% in Q4 FY '26.

items.statement: Furnishings category contributed 9.3% of total revenues in FY26
items.quote: Furnishings category contributed 9.3% of our total revenues in FY '26.

items.statement: 139 active COCO stores across 76 cities as of March end, total retail area ~4 lakh sq ft
items.quote: As of March end, we had 139 active company-owned company-operated stores across 76 cities. Our total current COCO retail area would be approximately 4 lakh square feet.

items.statement: Targeting more than 80 net store additions in FY27
items.quote: the target for this full year is to deliver more than 80 stores net addition.

items.statement: First Jumbo store (100,000+ sq ft) expected to open early FY28, second later in FY28
items.quote: Jumbo the first store will come up only in early FY '28, which is April, May of next year as per our today's projection where the construction is going on

items.statement: Capex for FY27 estimated at INR120-140 crores, mostly for retail including Jumbo store and 80 store openings
items.quote: we should be somewhere around INR120 crores to INR140 crores of the capex we will be spending in this year. C. Ramalingegowda: And just to clarify, most of this capex is going to be in retail, not for any manufacturing capacity increase. And this will include nearly 60%, 70% of the jumbos initial capex to have been done in this

items.statement: Proactive stocking of key raw materials and chemicals helped mitigate immediate price volatility impact
items.quote: we undertook proactive stocking of key raw materials and chemicals, which helped mitigate the immediate sharp impact of these price volatility arising from the macroeconomic factors and supply side disruption.

items.statement: Expanding into adjacent categories like live plants, fertilizers, plant nutrients to complete home portfolio
items.quote: For instance, within furnishings, we offer home decor items such as life plants. Under the extended scope, we can also offer essentials such as fertilizers, plant nutrients, soil conditioner to support plant care at home.

items.statement: Own channels (website + COCO) contributed 67.2% of annual sales and >74% of quarterly sales
items.quote: Our own channels, which comprise our website and COCO stores contributed 67.2% of our annual sales and more than 74% of the quarterly sales.

items.statement: Competition intensity increased over last 6-9 months from smaller D2C players with lower cost structures
items.quote: competition intensity has definitely gone up over the last six to nine months, where certain companies in the INR100 crores to INR300 crores annual revenue with a much lower cost structure, although they do not have a recognized brand per se, they might be very well-respected labels on marketplaces or they might be strong in specific two or three regions.

items.statement: Repeat revenue percentage and cross-category sale percentage are key tracked metrics monthly
items.quote: one obsessively tracked metric for Wakefit is repeat revenue percentage every month and cross-category sale percentage every month.

items.statement: Geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainty causing demand moderation in H2 FY26
items.quote: demand moderation continued further in the latter half of the Q4 FY '26 too amid evolving geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainty.

items.statement: Industry grew low single-digits in Jan-Mar 2026; refrigerator industry declined for the full year driven by direct cool.
items.quote: The industry continued to basically grow with very low single-digits in Jan 2026 to March 2026, so subdued industry growth. Decline in refrigerators so far for the whole year, driven by decline in direct cool refrigerators.

items.statement: Full year industry was roughly flattish; refrigerator industry declined due to delayed summer onset and early monsoons.
items.quote: Just to give you a little bit of color, this came on a backdrop of a flattish or a muted industry because the industry for the whole year was roughly flattish. And in fact, the ref industry declined largely due to the direct cool as there was delayed onset of summer and the monsoons got advanced.

items.statement: Revenue grew 7.4% YoY in Q4 FY26 to INR 2,181 crores on standalone basis.
items.quote: We're happy to see that we delivered a revenue growth of about 7.4% versus last year.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue for Q4 FY26 was INR 2,181 crores, high single-digit growth versus last year.
items.quote: In this quarter, we delivered a revenue of INR 2,181 crores, which is a high single-digit growth versus last year.

items.statement: Full year consolidated revenue crossed INR 8,000 crores at INR 8,034 crores, up 1.4% YoY.
items.quote: We crossed the INR 8,000 crores numbers from a top line perspective and delivered a top line of INR 8,034 crores, which is a growth of 1.4% versus last year.

items.statement: Elica revenue grew 30% YoY in Q4 FY26; PBT up 48%.
items.quote: Elica had a wonderful quarter. Revenue was up 30% and profit for Elica was up 48% -- PBT.

items.statement: Elica full year revenue grew 12% YoY; profit grew 15%.
items.quote: Elica continues to do well, grew revenue in double-digits at 12% and its profit on an annual basis grew ahead of revenue at 15%.

items.statement: Air conditioner business grew over 40% YoY in FY26 despite soft summer.
items.quote: Aircon continued to be a good story on an annual basis. We grew aircon business by 40% despite that the summer was pretty soft and not conducive to the aircon growth, but then we managed our business very well.

items.statement: Air conditioner quarterly volume grew over 50% YoY in Q4 FY26; crossed 100,000 units monthly sales in March 2026.
items.quote: Our air conditioner business, even in a relatively tough year, has gone up by more than 40% versus last year, following quite a strong 80%-odd growth in the previous year.

items.statement: Front load washer business grew ~60% YoY in FY26 with triple-digit basis points market share gains.
items.quote: Our total business has grown about 60% more than last year. We've had triple-digit basis points market share growth pretty much through the year.

items.statement: March 2026 marked highest-ever shipment month in company history, beating April 2019 record.
items.quote: March 2026 marked the highest-ever shipment month in the history of Whirlpool of India Limited, handsomely beating the last great record which was in April 2019.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin declined 50 bps YoY to 29.9% in FY26 due to air conditioner mix impact.
items.quote: Our overall reported gross margins stroke material margins were lower versus last year by 50 basis points, largely on account of aircon mix because at a material margins level, the profile of aircon -- the margins of aircon are relatively lower than the T2 business.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA was INR 121 crores at 5.6%, down 33.7% YoY; profit before exceptional items INR 110 crores at 5%, down 29% YoY.
items.quote: On the profitability side, we delivered an EBITDA of INR121 crores at 5.6%. The EBITDA was lower by 33.7% versus last year. And our profit before exceptional items was at INR110 crores at 5% and our profit declined by 29% versus last year.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA INR 481 crores at 6%, down 12.6% YoY; profit before exceptional items INR 426 crores at 5.3%, down ~12% YoY.
items.quote: On profit side, we delivered an EBITDA of INR481 crores at 6%. It was lower by 12.6% versus last year, roughly 100 basis points. And our profit before exceptional items came in at INR426 crores at 5.3%, lower by about 12% versus last year and 80 basis points versus -- lower by 80 basis points versus last year.

items.statement: Core T2 (refrigerator & washer) business margins improved YoY in FY26 due to P4G cost savings offsetting commodity and currency headwinds.
items.quote: Because of this P4G program, our core T2 business margins, which is ref and washers business, improved versus last year.

items.statement: Profit decline driven by incremental e-waste provisions and energy regulation upcharges not yet compensated by pricing.
items.quote: The single biggest factor which led to the decline in profits versus last year was the incremental e-waste provisions.

items.statement: Excluding incremental e-waste provision, full year profit margins would have been flat YoY.
items.quote: And outside of that e-waste impact, our profit margins were flat to last year.

items.statement: Energy regulation upcharges (BEE star rating change) permanently increase BOM cost; pricing recovery depends on competitive dynamics.
items.quote: The energy upcharge is a permanent upcharge to the BOM, right? And this is because the bill of materials cost goes up when you go -- basically what happens is last year's three-star becomes this year's two-star.

items.statement: Company chose not to fully follow aggressive competitive pricing to balance market share and profitability.
items.quote: And the secondary driver was competitive pricing, which continued to be very aggressive and we didn't follow to the same extent to balance between market share and profitability.

items.statement: Supply situation challenging due to Middle East war impacting cost and supply of components; monitoring daily with suppliers.
items.quote: We continue to closely monitor the supply situation. As everybody knows, the supply situation arising from the Middle East war is of concern to not only us but all industries across the country. Both with respect to cost and supply of components, products, etcetera, it is quite challenging and we continue to work on that very, very seriously and diligently.

items.statement: 20-35% of product components imported, exposed to forex and oil-linked raw material costs (plastics, EPS, methyl isocyanate).
items.quote: Typically between, depending on the company, between 20% and 35% of products components may be imported, right, depending on the company. And so that part of it is subject to forex.

items.statement: Refrigerator & washer business achieved negative net working capital in March 2026; overall NWC increased due to planned AC inventory investment.
items.quote: If you compare March 2026 excluding AC with March 2025, we are actually better off on networking capital on refrigerators and washing machines. The planned investment of air conditioners networking capital is what took our networking capital up in this quarter and obviously, it would be recovered in the coming quarter.

items.statement: Launching large capacity frost free refrigerators in Q2 FY27 to fill portfolio gap.
items.quote: Well, the answer is in Q2 of 2026-2027, thereby filling a significant gap in our frost free portfolio.

items.statement: Premiumization driving growth: auto-defrost 'No Tension' direct cool refrigerators, 11kg BloomWash top load with Quick Sense, Dynamix semi-automatic, Protton NXT three-door frost free, front load washers.
items.quote: Our focused interventions and our ROI-based ideas are focused on driving incremental growth in mid and premium segments of each of our categories, which again helps us driving premiumization within the category and hence driving the revenue growth.

items.statement: Achieved Silver WCM rating at Pune, Bronze at Puducherry and Faridabad; targeting Silver across all sites.
items.quote: We've achieved a Silver in Pune and Bronze in the other two manufacturing sites with our Puducherry and Faridabad, and we hope to take them to a Silver across the course of the coming quarters and years.

items.statement: New e-waste notification (Sept 2024) increased provisions; industry discussing rationalization with Ministry and recyclers.
items.quote: The new notification for e-waste came in middle of September last year -- middle of September 2024, correct. Last year had pre-September rates which were based on market-driven rates and the post-September 2024 e-waste provisions based on the new circular which came into effect.

items.statement: BEE energy regulation change from Jan 1 2026 required full SKU replacement (phase-in phase-out) for refrigerators and air conditioners.
items.quote: There's a big energy change that happened in January on both refrigerators and air conditioners. What that really means is every refrigerator and every air conditioner had to be replaced with new technical models, every single SKU that we have.

items.statement: Middle East war creating supply chain and cost uncertainty for components, oil-linked materials, and forex; managing daily with suppliers.
items.quote: We are focused on figuring out what's happening on the supply situation from two points of view. One is what's happening with respect to availability of products, right? Quite a few of the products are dependent on coming through the Straits of Hormuz.

items.statement: Market share: #2 in combined refrigerators & washing machines MBO volume share in March 2026; #1 in direct cool for 4 months from Dec 2025; #2 in top load and semi-automatic in Q4; front load volumes doubled with triple-digit bps share gain
items.quote: In March 2026, in refrigerators and washing machines combined, in the multi-brand outlets volume market share, we secured the number two position.

items.statement: Net Promoter Score (service KPI) continuing to grow strongly despite higher AC service complexity.
items.quote: As you know, the Net Promoter Score is the score difference between when consumers after installation or after service give you a score on a scale of 10. 9 plus 10, whoever gives you -- what percentage of people give you 9 and 10 scores out of 10, minus the people who give you ratings between 1 and 7. So, this is continuing to grow for us very strongly.

items.statement: Management monitors oil-dependent raw material supply and forex impact on imported components (20-35% of components imported) daily.
items.quote: So, both of these is what we are monitoring on a daily basis, making our plans against that, making sure that we're talking and working very, very closely with our suppliers on an hourly basis because what you actually have to do is make sure first of all that you have supply of components to be able to make your products.

items.statement: Pricing decisions are dynamic and competitive; management focuses on controllable factors and will modify actions dynamically.
items.quote: So, what we are doing is focusing on what we can control and what we should be delivering, which is our everyday work and staying close to the ground in terms of managing our supply, looking and taking the right decisions that we feel on costs and on pricing, and then monitoring the market very closely and we will keep on modifying dynamically our actions as we go through because it's an incredibl

items.statement: AC business is a small proportion; aspiration is to grow strongly but responsibly, focused on offtake not inventory loading.
items.quote: Our aspiration on AC I can certainly answer that. I think we would like to grow in AC across the years strongly, but responsibly. And what I mean by that is that we would obviously like to increase our market share in this very dynamic and fast-growing -- and I'm talking about the last five years, fast-growing industry of air conditioners.

items.statement: AC category working capital is heavily utilized in certain quarters; growth strategy focuses on offtake to avoid inventory buildup.
items.quote: But having said that, we are very, very conscious that this is also a category in which working capital is very heavily utilized, at least in certain quarters. And it's also not at the margin profile -- even for the most established players, it's not at the margin profile of our refrigerators or washing machine business.

items.statement: No buyback planned; cash will be deployed organically or inorganically over next 12-24 months for long-term value.
items.quote: So, buyback is something that we've not looked at, at this point in time because we think there is lot of opportunity that we can actually take. Like I was saying, especially on innovation, there is so much more that we plan to do across the next 12 to 18 months in terms of bringing innovative products to the market -- and I would say 12 to 24 months actually as we invest.

items.statement: Evaluating inorganic opportunities similar to Elica acquisition; cash sufficient for similar-sized deal; work started with board guidance.
items.quote: Now, outside of this, there are always options to go into the market and look at inorganic opportunities like we did Elica about six, seven years back. And probably just from a sheer cash point of view, it is just sufficient enough to look at a company of a similar size. So, these are some of the options. Now, do we have an exact timeline in terms of what we're doing? Ongoing business, we do it in

items.statement: No margin guidance for FY27 due to war, energy regulations, e-waste costs, and competitive pricing; long-term core margin likely high single-digit, Elica to stay double-digit but may trade some margin for growth.
items.quote: Margins, to be honest, we can't give any guidance right now. Like I said before, this is an incredibly unusual time. If it had been a normal year, even then I probably would be loath to give any guidance on margins because it's so -- it's such a competitive market, right?

items.statement: CWIP of ~INR 200 cr for premium frost-free refrigerators to capitalize next quarter; AC manufacturing decision depends on 3PL economics vs own plant; portfolio gap filling in refrigerators/washers over 12-24 months.
items.quote: The CWIP right now pertains to the premium refrigerators we spoke about. Since we've not started -- since it's going to come in the next quarter, so the capex is still lying in CWIP and has not got capitalized. Just want to clarify that piece.

items.statement: Washer market share gains in last quarter across fully automatic, semi-automatic, and front load; front load share still single-digit with high double-digit/triple-digit bps growth for 8 quarters.
items.quote: On washers, like I said, our front load washers, washers overall we've had some pretty solid results. We've had share increases in the last quarter as I said in the presentation. There's been volume market share increases and obviously value market share increases in all three categories in the last quarter: in fully automatic, in semi-automatic, and in front load.

items.statement: Energy efficiency regulations (BEE star ratings) increase costs and prices, potentially dampening entry-level demand; industry engages with ministries on balance.
items.quote: On the one hand, you know, having more energy efficient products is very good because it helps save, you know, energy, it helps conserve energy for the country. It's a wonderful thing. On the other hand, if you increase -- keep on increasing star ratings, then the cost also goes up, right?

items.statement: Refrigerators >50% of business, washing machines 25-30%, AC small but next big play alongside Elica; premium frost-free refrigeration and front-load washers are focus areas.
items.quote: As you know, refrigerators still covers more than 50% of our total business, washing machines covers about 25%, 30% of our total business. AC would be the next big play basically along with Elica. That would be the kind of thing.

items.statement: AC focus on markets where category is strong and where Whirlpool has strong refrigerator/washer share (pan-India brand).
items.quote: And the second type of area that we focus, for example, are the markets where our market shares are very strong in other categories. So, A, where the category itself is strong, and B, those markets where our market share is very strong in refrigerators and washers, which means we have very strong brand profile.

items.statement: FY26-27 challenging due to energy regulation changes, war impacts, e-waste provisions, and competitive intensity; supply chain and forex volatility monitored daily.
items.quote: I have already said to you that 2026-2027 will be difficult financially for the entire industry and also for Whirlpool because of all the energy changes, because of all the war impacts that are happening, which are very, very significant and kind of continuing to be not so clear as we go along.

items.statement: Board proposes final dividend of Rs. 15 per share for FY26 subject to shareholder approval
items.quote: We are pleased to announce that the Board proposes a final dividend of Rs. 15 per share for FY26 subject to approval by the shareholders in the forthcoming AGM.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin at 78.36%, down from 79.33% in FY25
items.quote: EBITDA margins stood at 78.36%.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin at 77.85%
items.quote: EBITDA margins were about 77.85%.

items.statement: Leasing rate at NKP north of Rs. 185 per sq ft per month at 80% efficiency in Feb 2026
items.quote: In Feb 2026, the leasing rate per square foot per month at NKP was north of Rs. 185 at 80% efficiency.

items.statement: No significant lease renewals in 2026-27; negotiations for 2027-28 renewals not yet started
items.quote: After that, there is nothing significant because there are not many renewals coming up in 2026-27.

items.statement: GCC boom in India is a positive development and tailwind for business
items.quote: I think it's a positive development for the country that various MNCs, banks, vario us global corporations are opening their GCCs in India. And we welcome that

items.statement: Capex focused on maintaining A-grade asset and sustainability; no significant capex outside the park
items.quote: The capex is of course to ensure that the park is in the best possible condition, the maintenance is to the best possible extent, whatever additional and incremental capex and capex-related modifications we have to do to maintain an A-grade asset, we are happy to do and we are going to keep doing to increase the sustainability aspect.

items.statement: Nirlon House sale involves 12-13 owners; no significant update; process takes significant time
items.quote: as far as the Nirlon house is concerned, we have nothing significant to say at this point in time. As I said in the past when there is something significant, we are going to tell you. But you must also appreciate that there are not just one or two owners, there are almost 12 o r 13 owners in the building

items.statement: No concrete plans for debt repayment from cash balances; will follow existing HSBC agreement terms
items.quote: As of now, there is nothing concrete or no concrete plans to pay back any debt from the existing cash balances. The debt to Hong Kong Bank, we have an existing agreement with them. So, we will follow the terms of the existing agreement with Hong Kong Bank.

items.statement: HSBC loan: 5% repayment in May 2027, then 5% annually for five years, then bullet payment
items.quote: As per the terms of the agreement, 5% in May 2027.

items.statement: FY26 asset valuation approx Rs. 6,650 crores vs Rs. 6,500 crores in FY25
items.quote: I think last year March 25 was 6,500, and this year it's 6,650, approximately.

items.statement: No early tenant exits visible; fully leased at 99.7% occupancy
items.quote: No, not right now. Not anything significant that we have been told.

items.statement: No data center plans or FSI increase at NKP currently
items.quote: Nothing that I can make a comment on now, no. I can't comment on that. Nothing significant or concrete.

items.statement: Moved to new tax regime under Section 115BAA from Q2 FY26; PAT growth 27% YoY excluding one-time deferred tax adjustment
items.quote: As the company decided to move to the new tax regime under Section 115BAA of the Income Tax Act 1961 from Q2 FY26, the profit after tax growth would be 27% year on year, excluding this item.

items.statement: Management commits to 20% PAT growth for FY27
items.quote: So let me say, a PAT growth of 20% is what we are committed to it, we will ensure we achieve that.

items.statement: Management guides consolidated tax rate of 25% to 26%
items.quote: We continue to guide you to a consolidated tax rate of approximately 25.5%, which is 25% to 26% -- in the range of 25% to 26% overall.

items.statement: Management guides finance cost to remain below 4% for the full year
items.quote: We have guided to Nitin, the overall below 4% in terms of the finance cost. We are at 3.71% slightly higher on the working capital at 3.03% and lower the overall long-term capital. So, we continue to guide you based on the revenue, we will be at below 4%.

items.statement: Capex plans for FY27 are sub-INR100 crores, mainly for BIW Hyundai plant completion and automation
items.quote: We don't have extremely heavy capex plans. It comes in sub-INR100 crores, I think. Most of it is Hyundai, the completion of our BIW Hyundai plant. That should happen in the next two to three months.

items.statement: PEB India capacity utilization at 70% in Q4 FY26, targeting around 80% in FY27
items.quote: I think around 80% is certainly achievable for this financial year, and that will be goal.

items.statement: PEB India order backlog at INR810 crores, PEB U.S. at $63 million, Boilers at INR145 crores, Hydraulics at INR34 crores
items.quote: The order book stands healthy for PEB India at INR810 crores, PEB U.S. at $63 millions and Boiler at INR128 crores.

items.statement: Q4 PAT margin improved to 4.44% from 3.9%; full year PAT margin at 3.83% vs 3.7% in FY25; expects positive trajectory to strengthen through 2027
items.quote: Our Q4 PAT margin stood at 4.44%, which is an improvement over 3.9%, reflection of ongoing mix shift towards high-margin businesses. This is something I guided to several times over the last few quarters, last few years, and it is well in line with our trend to have higher and higher PAT margins over the next few years.

items.statement: Gross margins guided to remain at similar 42-43% level
items.quote: Margins are sustainable. Margins have not changed while we had some ups and downs in this quarter. But overall, the margins we guide you would remain at the similar 42%, 43% kind of a thing.

items.statement: Working capital at 82 days, targeting reduction to 75 days in next few quarters via inventory and receivables improvement
items.quote: Working capital currently stands at 82 days. There has been some increase in this, and we are focused on reducing working capital days to 75 in the next few quarters.

items.statement: Gross debt-equity at 0.98x; target to reduce to 0.8x by end of FY27 via cash generation, capex gap, and equity infusion
items.quote: Our stated target and aim is that we should be below at 0.8. This has happened on account of two reasons: one, on account of the acquisition that we have done for the Telco, which was close to around 14 million that we had in terms of the long-term and the working capital, as well as yes, there is a working capital increase in the India business at the quarter end. And that's where our plan is to

items.statement: Long-term debt at 0.68x, working capital debt at 3.03x; working capital debt slightly high, will be reduced in coming quarters
items.quote: Presently, the long-term loan is at 0.68 and the working capital is 3.03. We are slightly high on the working capital and we will be reducing in the coming quarters.

items.statement: PEB U.S. sees sustained demand across data centers, warehouses, industrial; PEB India sees healthy quote activity and large order pipeline; Boilers secured highest capacity AFBC and WHR boilers
items.quote: PEB U.S. next delivered another quarter of very strong double-digit growth in revenue and profitability. It was anchored by sustained demand across data centers, warehouses and industrial end markets.

items.statement: Revenue mix shifting to higher-margin businesses (PEB U.S., Engineering Services, Hydraulics, BIW); legacy businesses at 30-35% of revenue, not allocating capital to them
items.quote: About 30% to 35% would be, and let me give to Shrikant on the exact numbers, would be the legacy businesses, about 70 -- Shrikant, would you agree with that or do you... Shrikant Bhakkad: Yes. I think we are there depending upon the month and the quarter, it changes, but we are between 30% to 35% in terms of

items.statement: Steel price increases passed through via price variation clauses; energy inflation from Iran war passed on to customers; operating margins expected to hold steady
items.quote: I think the recent issues have been with passing on the large price increase in steel. So, but that's okay. That's a temporary issue, and we pass it on. I don't -- I think the industry will always maintain the same operating margins that it always had because I don't think there's anything else that can be, any other interpretation is not possible.

items.statement: Labor issues in PEB India resolved; automation expanding in painting, surface treatment, assembly; AGT Robotics line commissioned in U.S. reducing man-hours from 20-30 to 2 people per product
items.quote: We've also increased our onboard. We've also began a process by which a lot more automation is brought in. What can get automated specifically in painting, surface treatment and assembly, we have expanded our automation deployment as well.

items.statement: ROCE at 20.23%, ROE at ~12% for FY26; focused on enhancing both via capital allocation and working capital management

items.statement: PEB U.S. order backlog includes Ascent Structural; Engineering Services billing on project outcome basis, not man-hours; AI-assisted design improving productivity
