items.statement: PEB India competitive landscape constrained by capacity; average order size ranges from INR5-10 crores (sand) to INR100 crores (rocks); pricing stable with pass-through clauses
items.quote: So, the average order size, I mean the larger orders go around INR100 crores and about INR5 crores to INR10 crores is the sand. So, there's rocks and the sand, right? So, and we need both really. So, our average order value is quite healthy.

items.statement: U.S. dollar depreciation impacted solar JV capex; forward cover used partially; no further equity investment planned in solar JV
items.quote: There's 2 things. One, I think the U.S. dollar has -- I mean the total capex for the plant and the plant is abo ut to be commissioned was made at a time when the U.S. dollar was significantly different from Indian rupee. So, as the equipment comes in the conversion, you can take forward cover in some cases, but effectively, some amount of it is left uncovered

items.statement: U.S. tariff impact on Hydraulics moderated; customers placing orders again; exploring European markets for expansion

items.statement: Iran war creates energy inflation risk; cost pass-through sometimes hard but imperative; no macro risk to business model anticipated

items.statement: Labor harder to get in India and U.S.; expanding automation to offset; U.S. engineering talent expensive but necessary for scale
items.quote: Across all of our plants right now, yes, labor is harder to come, harder to get, and then it used to be historically that's being met through an expansion of our resources in terms of how we procure labor.

items.statement: Telco acquisition completed last year; Ascent Structural integrated into combined U.S. order book; no further M&A disclosed
items.quote: Custom Design Building Solutions revenue grew from INR460 crores to INR516 crores at a consolidated level, an increase of 12.35%. Growth predominantly comes from the U.S. business driven by our Telco acquisition that we have carried out in the last year.

items.statement: Founders may bring in equity to help achieve 0.8x debt-equity target; other options under board discussion
items.quote: The way we get there through a combination of profitability, us -- The founders bringing in equity, and there are other things also which are under discussion. As and when we have those initiatives in place, we will communicate them to you.

items.statement: Debtors increased due to project handover delays; confident of collection in 6-8 weeks; inventory consciously higher due to price expectations

items.statement: Investment property revalued from INR25 crores to INR85 crores; addition shown separately, not in P&L; CWIP mainly for BIW and maintenance capex
items.quote: No, it is directly the addition that we carry out in investment property gets shown separately. There are a separate rental income and other things which will come. So hence the classification has undergone from property, plant, and equipment to investment property.

items.statement: FY27 presales target set at around INR 2,200 crores

items.quote: As a result, you will see our debt-to-equity guidance move to 1.00x.

items.statement: FY27 business development target of INR 1,800 crores

items.statement: FY26 collections of INR 1,103 crores, up 71% YoY
items.quote: Furthermore, our record-breaking collections, INR1,103 crores, which was up 71% year-on-year, reflect our strong execution capabilities.

items.statement: FY26 business development of INR 2,433 crores across 5 asset-light projects

items.statement: Unsold inventory of INR 2,200 crores as of March 2026

items.statement: Weighted average cost of debt reduced to 11.15% in FY26 from 12.20% in FY25
items.quote: Moreover, our weighted average cost of debt stood at 11.15% in FY26 versus 12.20% in FY25, highlighting our advanced credit profile and disciplined financial management.

items.statement: SPV-level equity tie-up discussions underway for Kanjurmarg conversion funding
items.quote: we are already in discussions with some funds and other people where we are trying to do a tie-up for the conversion process and we are having positive approvals for the same.

items.statement: Imperia 2 FY27 revenue recognition projected INR 130-150 cr (total project ~INR 300 cr); ~INR 47 cr recognized in Q4 FY26

items.statement: US FDA accepted BLA review for Ilumya in psoriatic arthritis with action date late October '26
items.quote: During the quarter, U.S. FDA accepted the review of BLA of Ilumya for the treatment of adults with active psoriatic arthritis with regulatory action date set for late October '26.

items.statement: Greenfield sterile-only facility in Madhya Pradesh for global supply capacity, not solely for US generics
items.quote: Yes. This is a sterile-only facility.

items.statement: Net cash of $3.2 billion at consolidated level
items.quote: Balance sheet continues to be strong with a net cash of $ 3.2 billion at the consolidated level.

items.statement: Expect effective tax rate in range of 25% for next year and beyond
items.quote: We expect the effective tax rate to be in the range of 25%.

items.statement: Compliance issues at existing sites limiting generic approvals; new facility to address future capacity needs
items.quote: No, I think part of the question you answered yourself is that because of the compliance issue, we haven't been getting approval. And as all of you are aware, generic business is a business where pricing pressure will mean existing product will lose top line every year.

items.statement: Biosimilar Stelara not impacting Ilumya due to Medicare Part B reimbursement structure
items.quote: We are seeing some impact of biosimilars changing formulary access, but we've not seen an impact on our business. Keep in mind that Medicare is one of the primary channels through which, through Part B that ILUMYA is reimbursed by, and that has no effect on the Part B reimbursement program.

items.statement: UNLOXCYT and LEQSELVI launch spends factored into base spend for FY27, not one-off
items.quote: And you should anticipate that, that just becomes part of our base spend in support of these brands versus a one-off spend.

items.statement: Ilumya launched in 40 countries ex-US, up from 35 previously
items.quote: Now it has gone to 40 countries, and it is helping us to grow.

items.statement: Rest of World formulation revenue US$ 220 million in Q4, up 10% YoY
items.quote: Formulation revenues in Rest of the World for the quarter were US$ 220 million, up 10%.

items.statement: Oral semaglutide clinical study completed in India, will launch upon approval
items.quote: So for oral, we have completed the clinical study. And once we get approval, we will launch the product at the earliest.

items.statement: MM2 partnership sought for US market; emerging markets to be marketed directly
items.quote: I think the idea is that in larger market where we will require a large field force to promote, we would look for a partner. In some of the emerging markets and in other geographies, we would look at marketing the product ourselves.

items.statement: No explicit EBITDA margin guidance for FY27; launch expenses for UNLOXCYT and LEQSELVI factored into plan
items.quote: So, as you know, we do not guide on the margins. However, the expenses relating to UNLOXCYT and LEQSELVI has been factored in the plan for the year.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 expected to reflect Q4 FY26 trends with muted corporate gifting and export demand
items.quote: Quarter 1 FY 2027 is expected to reflect the trends seen in quarter 4 FY '26. So corporate gifting orders, which typically span over quarter 4 and quarter 1, have been muted this year and will accordingly have a bearing on quarter 1 FY '27 revenues also.

items.statement: Formal FY27 guidance deferred pending better visibility after another quarter
items.quote: Given the current uncertainties, we believe it will be prudent to await another quarter to gain better visibility before providing formal guidance on our outlook for the year FY27.

items.statement: Corporate gifting orders muted due to high base effect and client preference variability
items.quote: Firstly, our corporate or institutional sales moderated due to a high base effect, as the segment had contributed meaningfully in both quarter 4 and quarter 1 of the previous year.

items.statement: Export demand affected by geopolitical environment in Middle East and Eastern Africa
items.quote: if we look at the export market performance, our quarter 4 was a degrow th because of the prevailing situation in the Middle East, as we all know. So quarter 4 definitely saw a degrowth. If we look at -- so quarter 4 was almost 25% degrowth year -on-year

items.statement: FY26 operating EBITDA margin 11%, down 89 bps YoY; Q4 FY26 margin 12.9%, up 41 bps YoY
items.quote: Operating EBITDA for FY '26 stood at INR59.49 crores with a margin of 11%, reflecting a decline of 89 basis points over the previous year. For quarter 4, the operating EBITDA stood at INR17.78 crores with a margin of 12.9% representing an improvement of 41 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: Polymer prices risen due to supply disruptions; full pass-through not feasible given competitive dynamics
items.quote: Polymer prices, our principal raw materials, have also risen due to supply-side disruptions. And given competitive dynamics, immediate full pass-through in pricing may not be feasible.

items.statement: Export pricing strategy passes portion of FX benefit to customers to maintain local market pricing
items.quote: So when we get an export -- when we get benefit from the foreign currency fluctuation, a portion of that has to be passed on to our customers because if we kind of don't do that, our pricing to the market in those countries increases.

items.statement: Significant raw materials imported; rupee depreciation increases input costs
items.quote: And even the raw materials have increased because we have a significant raw material which are imported.

items.statement: Sales team split into mass and premium verticals; 125 frontline staff added from April 2026
items.quote: So we have one vertical which is focused on more mass distribution and the second vertical, which are focused on more premium brands like Uni and Deli, which is focused towards urban distribution. So this has been one initiative, and we have actually added about 125 frontline sales team to our team.

items.statement: New Pentonic launches planned at INR20+ price points; 2-3 this year, more next year
items.quote: We have a couple of new developments in INR20 and above in the Pentonic portfolio. Probably 1 or 2 even in the -- yes, probably 2 or 3 of them, we have planned for this year and a couple of more for next financial year.

items.statement: GT channel showed double-digit growth in April 2026 from new distribution initiatives
items.quote: And if we look at GT channel growth, so if we look at our April performance, our April performance in GT channel has shown a double-digit growth, actually.

items.statement: Geopolitical disruptions outweigh currency depreciation benefits for exports
items.quote: But the overall geopolitical situations had far outweighed the benefits of the rupee depreciation.

items.statement: West Bengal manufacturing facility expected operational by Q3 FY27 for Morris subsidiary
items.quote: Subsidiary with Morris, progress remains linked to our upcoming West Bengal manufacturing facility, which is expected to become operational by quarter 3 FY27.

items.statement: Board approved additional $250,000 investment in Mitsubishi Pencil JV with matching partner contribution
items.quote: Linc's Board has approved a further investment of $250,000 with a matching contribution from the JV partner maintaining the existing shareholding structure.

items.statement: Turkish JV operations commenced, stable with gradual transition to automation
items.quote: The joint venture with our Turkish partner, operations have commenced successfully, they remain stable and have a gradual transition towards automation.

items.statement: Kenya subsidiary sales momentum improving; Linc-on subsidiary operations commenced
items.quote: Kenya subsidiary, sales momentum has started to improve, and we expect this positive trajectory to strengthen further in the coming periods. Linc-on subsidiary. Operations have commenced and the business is expected to gain meaningful traction from this financial year.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle at 64 days as of March 2026
items.quote: Our cash conversion cycle stands at 64 days.

items.statement: Net cash position of INR686 lakhs; net debt to EBITDA at -0.12x as of March 2026
items.quote: Our balance sheet remained strong throughout the year with a net cash position of INR686 lakhs as on 31st March 2026, reflecting continued financial discipline. Net debt to operating EBITDA stood at 0.12x negative.

items.statement: Board approved dividend of INR1.5 per share, same as last year, 27% payout ratio
items.quote: To reward our shareholders and reinforce our commitment to value creation, the Board has approved a dividend of INR1.5 per share, same as last year, implying a payout ratio of around 27% on consolidated profit, subject to sha reholder approval

items.statement: FY26 operating income INR543 crores, broadly stable YoY; Q4 FY26 INR137.67 crores, down 10.6% YoY
items.quote: Our operating income for the year stood at INR543 crores, broadly stable year-on-year. For quarter 4 FY 26, our operating income stood at INR137.67 crores, reflecting a decline of 10.6% compared to the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: FY26 PAT INR3,274 lakhs at 5.9% margin; Q4 FY26 PAT INR1,046 lakhs at 7.5% margin
items.quote: For FY26, PAT stood at INR3,274 lakhs, translating into a PAT margin of 5.9%. On a quarterly basis, PAT for Q4 FY '26 came in at INR1,046 lakhs with a margin of 7.5%.

items.statement: ROC 18.7% and ROE 13.3% for FY26; fixed asset turnover ~4x
items.quote: ROC and ROE stood at 18.7% and 13.3%, respectively. Asset productivity will remain healthy with fixed asset turnover at around 4x indicating efficient utilization of asset base.

items.statement: Geopolitical issues in Middle East, Russia, Sudan, Myanmar disrupt exports annually
items.quote: Every year, we actually face -- we've been facing situations in some of the other countries. Looking at tariffs. Tariffs From U.S. last year. Before that, if you look at Russia. Russia used to be one of our big markets. So when the Russia war started, our Russia market got affected. Sudan, there were geopolitical issues in Sudan. There was Myanmar in 1 or 2 years. Myanmar was affected.

items.statement: Focusing on stable markets like Indonesia to diversify export risk
items.quote: Trying to focus on more stable countries, stable economies. For example, Indonesia is one of our markets, which ha s been vacant for a very long time, and we opened -- we started exporting to Indonesia just last year

items.statement: Mitsubishi Pencil JV operations stable; recently launched product receiving encouraging response
items.quote: The joint venture with Mitsubishi Pencil Company, Japan, operations remained stab le, and the recently launched product has received encouraging response from the

items.statement: FY27 consolidated revenue guided at INR2,300-2,400 crore, up from INR1,875 crore in FY26
items.quote: On a consol basis, we are guiding a revenue of INR2,300 crores to INR2,400 crores, up from INR1,875 crores we have done in FY '26, which will include full year consolidation of PendraCare and Citieffe.

items.statement: FY27 standalone revenue guided at INR1,900-1,950 crore with domestic growth >20% and international >15%
items.quote: On stand-alone basis, we are guiding on a revenue of INR1,900 crores to INR1950 crores with domestic business growing upwards of 20% and international business growing upwards of 15%.

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR200-225 crore, lower than FY26's INR296 crore
items.quote: We expect to spend between INR200 crores to INR225 crores on capex this year. This is a guidance. This is lower than last year. Last year was INR296 crores.

items.statement: Current gross margin may erode from 68% to ~66% (200-300 bps) due to raw material inflation, but cost-saving projects aim to minimize impact by year-end
items.quote: on the current situation based on where we are today as on today, we may see some erosion on gross margin going from, let's say, 68% to maybe around 66% or maybe in that region, maybe lower by 200 bps, 300 bps

items.statement: Raw material costs up ~20% aggregate due to crude-linked plastics and packaging; freight and Haryana minimum wage revision also pressuring costs
items.quote: There has been an impact on raw materials because and plastic packaging materials all across because most of them are crude linked. And we see there was an impact of around 20% on an aggregate basis in raw materials and a meaningful headwind to the gross margin.

items.statement: Price increases of 3-5% secured from customers; rupee depreciation (60-70% export revenue) helping offset cost inflation
items.quote: We are able to get our price increase from customers between range of 3% to 5% already. And also, currency has moved -- rupee has currently depreciated against all major currencies and company's 60% to 70% business is international, export driven on a stand-alone basis.

items.statement: Pending orders intact in West Asia (6-8% of revenue) but logistics bottlenecks delaying shipments; demand remains strong
items.quote: We have pending orders, which we need to execute, but we are still waiting for supply chain and shipping routes to improve and have better pricing.

items.statement: Europe demand recovered with new distributors added in Northern Europe, UK, Germany; pipeline very strong
items.quote: We have bounced back in Europe. That's what I can tell you right now. We have added quite a few customers in Europe. And also the existing customers where we had an over inventory situation and we had a little slowdown in demand. I think that has come back.

items.statement: US business back on track after 1-year tariff setback; new FDA approvals in pipeline and active customer conversations
items.quote: Our U.S. business is picking up momentum with the conversation on multiple projects with customers, again, getting active. I think due to the scenario, which was created last year, especially because of tariffs, I think we had a setback. But now I think we are on track.

items.statement: Infusion Therapy share fell to 50% in Q4 FY26 from 57% in Q4 FY25; Renal ~11%; higher-tech segments (Cardiology, Critical Care, acquisitions) now >50% of revenue
items.quote: Infusion Therapy now accounts for 50% of the revenue, down from 57% in Q4 '25 with Renal around 11%, steadily rising, share coming from Cardiology, Critical Care and other acquisitions. In other words, our new higher technology segments are now contributing to over 50% of our revenue.

items.statement: Renal: ~450 dialysis machines placed in FY26, installed base ~1,000; Cardiology: ~11,000 stents deployed; 2,000-patient clinical registry 650 enrolled
items.quote: On the Renal platform, we have placed around 450 dialysis machines last year, taking our installed capacity to approximately 1,000 machines. On Cardiology, now we deployed close to 11,000 stents.

items.statement: Post-QIP-1 capacity utilization at 65-70%
items.quote: After the QIP-1 we are seeing a capacity utilization of close to around 65% to 70% right now.

items.statement: Acquired Medyneo in Brazil for ~$40k to fast-track ANVISA/import licenses (saves 18-24 months); Brazil market USD13-15bn, gateway to Latam
items.quote: From an acquisition standpoint, it was about $40,000. So it's a small acquisition from a cash outlay perspective, but it clearly saves us anywhere between 18 to 24 months to be able to operationalize the business.

items.statement: Working with Indian government to counter Chinese dumping via ASEAN route (0% duty) causing cost inversion; raw material duty 2.5% + 18% GST vs finished Chinese imports 5% GST only
items.quote: Many Chinese companies have set up bases in ASEAN countries where we have a 0 import duty on medical products from ASEAN countries. So that is hurting the current environment. So we are working with the government to arrest that point.

items.statement: West Asia 6-8% of revenue; demand intact but logistics nightmare disrupting shipments; rupee depreciation helping export competitiveness
items.quote: West Asia, I just want to call it out, around 6% to 8% of our revenue comes from there. And though the demand seems to be quite intact, we don't see any drop in demand. I think it's a logistics nightmare right now.

items.statement: Renal segment targeting >20% growth in FY27 despite Chinese dumping; placed 450 machines in FY26, targeting similar 20% increase in FY27
items.quote: It's 20% growth in the renal segment again. So we will not say maybe around -- earlier, we were targeting 30%, 35% growth. But I think the Chinese headwinds continue to kind of disrupt the market. So we are still seeing maybe a 20% growth or maybe over 20% growth this year also in this business.

items.statement: Long-term export customer relationships (15-20 years), hardly lost any large customer; stickiness from quality compliance, performance parity with MNCs, innovation (399 group patents)
items.quote: Most of our customer relationships outside of India have been for the last 15, 20 years. And we have hardly lost any large customer in the last 15, 20 years. That's number one. And the stickiness is created because of 2, 3 reasons. One, because of quality, which we deliver because today Polymed has almost every quality -- our products comply to every possible global quality standard.

items.statement: Crude at $100-110 baked into plan; if crude softens, margin headwinds reduce; geopolitical uncertainty (Gulf war) remains a worry
items.quote: The current business plan, we have looked at, has been made on crude levels of around $100 and I think $100 to $110, but I think in time to come, crude prices will definitely soften up. So I think this headwind will kind of go down a little bit.

items.statement: Long-term revenue mix target: 1/3 India, 2/3 Rest of World
items.quote: So ideally, I would like it to be between like 1/3 India and 2/3 RoW.

items.statement: Drug-eluting balloons launched (100% indigenous, import substitute); developing high-value products in cardiology (INR1-10 lakh), orthopaedics, oncology, renal
items.quote: We will already launch drug-eluting balloons, again, fully indigenously developed product. It's 100% import substitute product and very, very few companies are able to make that kind of product. And we are working on some high-level products, which will be around INR1 lakh or INR7 lakh, INR8 lakh, INR10 lakh products in times to come.

items.statement: Chinese dumping persists in Renal (0% ASEAN duty vs Polymed's 2.5% customs + 18% GST on raw materials); no domestic renal competitors except Polymed
items.quote: Today, Chinese are importing at 0% duty, only 5% GST pay on the finished product, whereas I'm importing -- I'm buying all the raw materials, I'm importing some raw materials, I pay 18% duty, I pay 2.5% duty custom duty on my raw materials, 18% GST. So there's a lot of cost inversion plus the dumping from the Chinese.

items.statement: Consolidated cash ~INR842 crore as strategic reserve; operating cash flows to fund regular capex
items.quote: On the balance sheet front, the equity remains strong and consolidated cash of around INR842 crores. This amount is a strategic reserve for our strategic initiatives in future, and we intend to use operating cash flows to meet regular capex requirements across the group.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target of around INR800 crores, with Motion Pictures contributing ~50%
items.quote: So FY27, if I say we will be expecting close to around, say, INR800-odd crores top line, largely driven by motion pictures. Movie will give almost 50% of it.

items.statement: Commissioned shows (TV + OTT B2B) revenue expected to grow from INR160 crores in FY26 to INR330 crores in FY27
items.quote: if my commissioned shows, which is TV plus OTT, which is B2B business, which was around INR160-odd crores in the FY26, we expect it to be around INR330 crores in the coming fiscal year.

items.statement: Motion Pictures revenue expected at close to INR400 crores in FY27 vs INR15 crores in FY26
items.quote: And we expect this year close to INR400 crores top line coming from Motion Pictures itself as compared to only INR15 crores, which was there last year.

items.statement: Balaji Studios revenue expected around INR70 crores in FY27 vs INR8.5 crores in FY26
items.quote: We had INR8.5 crores revenue last year. We believe it will be around INR70-odd crores this financial year.

items.statement: Meta revenue expected around INR115 crores in FY27 vs INR6.5 crores in FY26
items.quote: Plus, there is Meta, which we just started last year with a revenue of around INR6.5 crores. We believe that will be around -- which will be around INR115-odd crores this year.

items.statement: Balaji Hoonur talent agency revenue expected at least INR12 crores in FY27 vs INR1.5 crores in Q4 FY26
items.quote: We have clocked a revenue of INR1.5 crores last quarter. We believe this will be at least doing INR12 crores in the coming financial year.

items.statement: Balaji AstroGuide app revenue expected INR6.5-7 crores in FY27 vs INR56 lakhs wallet recharge in FY26
items.quote: We have app installed of around 1.8 mill ion with the wallet recharge FY26 was INR56 lakhs plus, and we expect close to INR6.5 crores to INR7 crores in this financial year.

items.statement: Digital business (B2C) expected to contribute around INR100 crores in FY27
items.quote: And B2C business, where we own IP, we retain everything with us and be monetize, I think that will be contributing around INR100-odd crores in this financial year.

items.statement: OTT partnership order book of approximately INR350 crores, with over INR135 crores expected to be realized in FY27
items.quote: We now have an order book of approximately INR350 crores under this line, out of which we expect to realize over INR135 crores or so within the ongoing financial year FY27.

items.statement: Commissioned order book over INR350 crores with INR50 crores added each quarter
items.quote: We have an order book of over INR350 crores plus around INR50 crores gets added each quarter.

items.statement: OTT margins significantly lower than TV due to finite series format vs long-running shows
items.quote: However, I must admit here, the margin a s compared to television and OTT vary differently and significantly, I would say. See in TV, what happens is the show is it runs for 6 months, 12 months, 18 months, 5 years. So the marginal costing and everything comes into play and you have a better yield, whereas the OTT-led platform typically will not have that kind of yield because these are all finite

items.statement: TV yield down 25-30% vs pre-COVID rates; show tenures reduced to 6-9 months norm
items.quote: In fact, if we just compare the yield to the pre -COVID year rate, we are still down by 25% to 30%. So there is a -- the investment into the content from the broadcast side has significantly slowed down and considerably reduced. As a result, all the production houses will see their margin getting depleted.

items.statement: Motion Pictures working capital investment of INR125-150 crores at any given time; digital business needs INR10-15 crores working capital
items.quote: And typically, we will have investment of around INR125 crores to INR150 crores at any given point of time because certain movies will be on floor, certain movies will be nearing release and certain movies will be in advanced stage of discussion and rolling out for the next schedule. And digital business, not more than INR10 crores to INR15 crores, we require working capital to run that stream.

items.statement: TV and commissioned OTT require ~3 months capital of INR50-55 crores; Motion Pictures 50% COP funded by presales
items.quote: television and commissioning model OTT platform because it is also funded by the platform themselves. So maybe 3 months of capital, which will be around INR50 crores to INR55 crores gets locked into these kind of segments. Whereas on Motion Pictures side, we try to presell all those movies. And what happens is 50% of the COP gets funded by the presales, which we do.

items.statement: 17 movies in pipeline over next 3 years; 4 movies releasing in FY27 with 3 already presold at 99% cost recovery
items.quote: In terms of our content slate, we have another 17 movies in the pipeline planned over the next 3 years, and we will have 4 movies released in this year, out of which 3 movies have already been presold of the cost recovered is 99%.

items.statement: Strategic shift: Motion Pictures to contribute >50% of revenue/profit in 2-3 years, followed by digital; TV to be least contributor
items.quote: I believe in next 2 to 3 years, this pyramid will shift and Balaji will be more an IP -led content creator with the movie contributing more than 50% to the top line and profitability, followed by digital business. And television will be the least contributor to the segment.

items.statement: New vertical micro-drama format with Vertigo TV for mobile-first audiences; Lock Upp and Koke releasing in FY27 on Netflix; 1 show with Amazon
items.quote: We have r ecently entered into a strategic collaboration with Vertigo TV through Balaji Telefilms studio model to produce Hindi vertical micro drama tailored for mobile-first audiences. This is a new storytelling format focused on short, immersive, high engagement content

items.statement: Inventory increase to INR207 crores from INR73 crores due to 3 movies under production (Bhooth Bangla, Vvan, Hero Ki Horroin)
items.quote: Inventory is coming out of motion pictures. So what you see as of March is largely your Bhooth Bangla, Vvan and Hero Ki Horroin . That 3 movies inventory is residing there.

items.statement: Liquid cash position of over INR165 crores in cash and mutual funds; minimum liquidity threshold for motion pictures INR125-150 crores
items.quote: With a healthy liquidity position, we have over INR165 crores liquid cash into the banks and mutual funds and a robust pipeline across television, films and digital platforms, we remain confident about the medium- to long-term growth opportunity for the business.

items.statement: GST input credit of INR117 crores from ALT/Marinating Films merger; no direct tax incidence expected for next 4-5 years
items.quote: The other major initiatives or the significant benefits which will arise for the parent company, which is Balaji Telefilms is the huge input credit from GST, which is around INR117-odd crores. So we have that asset, which remains to be utilized. And plus, I believe next 4 to 5 years, there won't be any incidence of direct tax also.

items.statement: In-house AI team created for content production, VFX, music library; won awards for AI-generated short formats
items.quote: We have set up our own AI team into the company. There is a captive team, which sits here and works on the various formats which we do. We have done many newer things using AI tools. One is the creating a short format, reels and shows, and we also won awards for it.

items.statement: TV segment EBITDA turned from INR7 crore loss in Q3 to INR4 crore profit in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Business EBITDA in the TV segment grew sequentially from a loss of INR7 crores in the previous quarter to a profit of INR4 crores in quarter 4 FY26, indicating a turnaround in this segment's performance.

items.statement: Digital business cash burn reduced from INR125-145 crores/year to INR6 crores/year; expected cash positive in FY27
items.quote: Last year, our cash burn was INR50 lakhs, thereabout per month. So it is around INR6 crores of cash loss on the total digital initiatives, including the newer launches like, say, Astro or we do whatever initiatives. So that way we ha ve brought it down to bare minimum. The turnaround is expected in FY27 with overall digital business will be cash positive.

items.statement: TV broadcasters not investing in content; show tenures shrinking to 6-9 months; IP ownership remains with broadcasters
items.quote: Earlier, the show used to run for a year, 2 years, 3 years and there was enough and more opportunities for production house also to make a decent return. With the tenure of the shows, very few shows run more than a year these days. If you just scan the -- each of these broadcast companies, you will find 6 to 9 months is becoming the norm.

items.statement: OTT platforms bleeding losses while under-investing in TV content where profits are generated
items.quote: However, they are bullish on the OTT segment. So that's another challenge for them. They bleed on OTT, but where the profit is getting generated, they are not investing so much of content.

items.statement: FY26 revenue INR210 crores vs INR453 crores in FY25; EBITDA loss INR65.8 crores; PAT loss INR49.6 crores
items.quote: For FY26, revenue from operations stood at INR210 crores as against INR453 crores in FY25. EBITDA loss for the year stood at INR65.8 crores, while loss after tax stood at INR49.6 crores.

items.statement: Targets double-digit revenue growth for FY27
items.quote: as historically that we always look for a double -digit growth in our revenues, and that's what we would also say today.

items.statement: Expects margins to remain stable in FY27
items.quote: would say it would remain stable. And we would -- like it's also with the situation we are currently in, we wouldn't want to throw a figure on that

items.statement: Capex for FY27 expected to be constant unless major new CS project arises
items.quote: I would say the capex for the following year, unless we see any major custom synthesis project or any new project that's in our way, it would be a constant capex.

items.statement: Capitalized assets worth ₹1,544 crores in FY26, ~₹800 crores in Q4
items.quote: During the year, the company capitalized assets worth ₹ 1,544 crores, out of which approximately ₹800 crores is capitalized in the last quarter.

items.statement: Capital work in progress stood at ₹2,113 crores as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: Capital work in progress as of March 31, 2026 stood at ₹2,113 crores.

items.statement: Kakinada expansion of ₹1,500 crores underway, ₹600 crores capitalized
items.quote: at Kakinada, we did mention earlier that we are going to do a ₹1,500 crores expansion plan, out of which ₹600 crores has been capitalized.

items.statement: Unit 3 operations progressing steadily, supporting backward integration and freeing GMP space at Units 1 & 2
items.quote: operations at Unit 3 have been steadily progressing, and the facility is now playing an increasi ngly important role in our overall operations by supporting our backward integration capacity.

items.statement: Peptide capacity includes several 3,000-liter SPPS reactors, targeting to be one of the largest global players
items.quote: We have several 3,000-liter SPPS, which by far in India nobody has. We are quite strong and committed towards this segment, and we are targeting to be one of the largest global players in the world.

items.statement: Gadolinium contrast media still in qualification stage (Phase II/III), commercialization awaits customer approvals
items.quote: we are still at qualification stage because these are new molecules which are in Phase II, Phase III. Yes, we are basically tagging along with our customers. As and when they start getting approvals, we will start seeing revenues from that side

items.statement: Generic volumes stable with steady demand across markets; CS project pipeline active across development stages
items.quote: Volumes across our key products have maintained and remained stable through the quarter and full year. While the pricing environment remains competitive, we have seen steady demand across markets and healthy volume traction in our products.

items.statement: Long-term contracts with variability clauses protect against raw material cost increases in generic segment
items.quote: most of our APIs on the generic segment are backed by long -term contracts, which have variability clauses, which protects us from such situations.

items.statement: Freight and raw material cost pressures expected to continue near term; incorporated into planning
items.quote: Freight-related cost pressures are expected to continue in the near term, and we have incorporated these factors into our planning for the coming quarters.

items.statement: Cash and equivalents ₹3,414 crores, receivables ₹2,984 crores, inventories ₹3,954 crores as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: As on March 31, 2026, the Company's Cash and Cash equivalents stood at ₹3,414 crores, Receivables at ₹2,984 crores and Inventories at ₹3,954 crores.

items.statement: Constant currency revenue growth 6.82% for FY26
items.quote: Constant currency growth for the year was 6.82%.

items.statement: Product mix FY26: Generics 45%, Custom Synthesis 55%
items.quote: The product mix between generics and custom synthesis for the year was at 45% and 55%, respectively.

items.statement: Nutraceuticals revenue ₹946 crores in FY26 vs ₹781 crores prior year
items.quote: Revenue from nutraceuticals business for the current financial year amounted to ₹ 946 crores compared to ₹781 crores in the previous financial year.

items.statement: Management guides FY27 realization at INR165 per kg, considering product mix and currency effects
items.quote: Next year, INR165 is a fair realization to consider.

items.statement: Maintenance capex and renewable balancing investment of INR100-150 crores for FY27; INR30 crores remaining for renewable project completion
items.quote: So total, we don't expect more than between INR100 crores and INR150 crores of outflow on accounts of maintenance capex and the renewable balancing investment left for the renewable part.

items.statement: Ghana and China plants under paperwork approval; no spend yet; timing uncertain
items.quote: This year, other than our investments in Ghana and China which as we speak are under paperwork approval procedures, there is no spend have done.

items.statement: New generation discharge system solution proven at large mine; delivers 15%+ throughput improvement and power reduction; solution includes linings and grinding media as integrated package
items.quote: At least 15% of throughput improvement, at least. Otherwise, it's not material. And throughput is inversely linked to power. So, 15% throughput improvement is 15% power reduction, plus other benefits of down process and other things.

items.statement: Global shipping uncertainty and protectionist measures persist; but solution efficacy transcends commodity pricing concerns
items.quote: Shipping remains to be a proxy for global geopolitical uncertainty and hence, the shipping uncertainty and that plays a role where people are -- customers that migrate to our solution will be exposed to the global supply chain.

items.statement: Inventory up 25% due to South American order from Oct-Nov and billing cycle change shifting invoicing to consumption basis; all stock against orders
items.quote: So, 100% of our stock is built against orders. There is the South American order that got introduced, I think, from October, November this year. And there was a change in billing cycle for another lot where the billing shifted from when it moved from India to actually when they consume.

items.statement: Short-term borrowing of INR485 crores reduced to zero; cyclical treasury arbitrage using export credit limits
items.quote: So, it's very momentary or functional what we were doing earlier that we were trying to sort of utilize lower cost credit and trying to work out on a little bit of arbitrage that is all cyclical.

items.statement: Currency benefit INR65 crores in Q4 EBITDA (4-5% margin impact); rupee depreciation benefit partially passed through over 1-2 quarters
items.quote: There is INR65 crores currency that's sitting in the EBITDA for this quarter and which is about 4% or 5% in EBITDA or operating margins coming from the currency as other income.

items.statement: Most customers pay in local currencies (not USD); rupee depreciation gives temporary benefit until dollar prices reset in 1-2 quarters
items.quote: Most customers, except U.S., are importing in a local currency, Canadian dollars, reals, euro, South Africa, whatever the currency is. So generally, I think there is a disconnect where now where rupee has weakened more than other currency.

items.statement: Antidumping and protectionist measures in multiple countries; status quo continues; viewed as business as usual
items.quote: We have seen duty measures. We've seen antidumping measures. We've seen Trump and U.S. bringing measures to protect local industry. I think every country is going to look for their own interest cost

items.statement: Full year sales volume 258,000 tons (mining 160k, non-mining 98k); Q4 volume 70,000 tons (mining 45k, non-mining 25k)
items.quote: We've done 70,000 tons of sales for the quarter for a full year sales of 258,000 tons, largely flat from full year last year, which was 255,000 tons.

items.statement: Full year revenue INR4,355 crores; Q4 revenue INR1,251 crores; full year PAT INR1,270 crores; Q4 PAT INR393 crores (highest ever)
items.quote: INR1,251 crores of top line for the quarter. And INR4,355 crores for the full year. EBITDA of INR502 crores for the quarter. And INR1,744 crores for the full year translating into a profit after tax of INR393 crores and a full year profit after tax of INR1,270 crores.

items.statement: Renewable power to reach 60-65% of consumption by June-July; 100 MW rated capacity targeting 20 crore units annually at INR5-5.5/unit vs grid INR6.5-7
items.quote: The renewable about 60% of our power or 65% of our power once that comes online, which is by June or July will come from renewable sources.

items.statement: Geopolitical shipping uncertainty and global protectionism are key risks; solution strategy aims to transcend commodity pricing volatility
items.quote: There is extreme uncertainty as far as global shipping is concerned. There is -- just bizarre events happening where prices are volatile, availability is volatile and customers' anxiety around global shipping.

items.statement: Claims unique global position: only company offering integrated discharge system solution for ball mills; IP protected through design patents and causal engineering knowledge
items.quote: There is nobody in the world offering a similar solution, is a very tall statement, and I think we are very proud about it.

items.statement: Marquee South American mine win validates solution; 15 other mines across countries using parts of solution; Brazil volumes 6-8k tons but not scaling as hoped
items.quote: We should be doing 6,000, 8,000 tons in Brazil, but it still needs to scale up. It is not gone through the scale-up, we had hoped for.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; team focused on solution engineering and global mining customer engagement
items.quote: We have been putting our full force, I would say, over the last 1 year on this new solution and the new system on which we are now offering the global mining customers something unique on the platter.

items.statement: Management declined to give FY27-28 revenue and EBITDA guidance due to geopolitical uncertainty and rising costs, stating they will be in a better position after Q1.
items.quote: keeping the geopolitical issues in place, how it is going, it has become very, very difficult for us to give any guidance. However, we are pledged to improve our performance

items.statement: Signed pipeline comprises 52 hotels with 3,600 rooms, including ~522 keys on revenue-share model expected to open within the year.
items.quote: There are 52 hotels which are signed and comprising of 3,600 rooms and we have beefed up our development team also now.

items.statement: Hampton by Hilton partnership targets 125 hotels over 10 years, part of the 22,000 keys Vision 2030 roadmap.
items.quote: Yeah, that's a long-term 10-year partnership for the Hampton by Hilton brand in 6 states in India where we are going to be opening about 125 hotels with them.

items.statement: Capex for FY27 limited to 5 revenue-share hotels requiring INR5-10 crores total; maintenance and renovation capex ongoing for existing properties.
items.quote: CapEx, as we have mentioned, our business model is very, very, you know, asset light. So we don't anticipate large CapEx only in the revenue share hotels, which are, I can see about five of them coming up in the next one year.

items.statement: Existing hotels (ex-ICONIQA) delivered INR103 crores EBITDA; ICONIQA Mumbai EBITDA was INR7.3 crores in FY26.
items.quote: Other than ICONIQA, the EBITDA was INR103 crores and ICONIQA EBITDA was INR7.3 crores.

items.statement: ADR grew from ~INR5,800 to ~INR6,000; occupancy flat year-on-year; F&B cost percentage rose due to ICONIQA pre-opening write-offs.
items.quote: The average rate has grown in our presentation I have given. So from 5,800, we have grown to 6,000 and odd. However, the occupancy remained the same for last year.

items.statement: Consolidated cash equivalents ~INR100 crores; bank borrowings ~INR91 crores including INR45 crores for ICONIQA; company can be debt-free but retains debt for flexi-lease growth.
items.quote: If you look at our borrowings actually, the bank borrowings is around INR91 crores including the INR45 crores of the new ICONIQA Bombay.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR2.5 per equity share for FY26.
items.quote: In line with this confidence, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR2.5 per equity share.

items.statement: Portfolio strategy: Regenta (80+ keys), Regenta Place (40-80 keys), Z by Regenta franchise (~50 keys), plus flexi-leases; minimum fee thresholds set per hotel.
items.quote: The Regenta brand, which will be typically 80 keys and 60, 80 keys and upwards. The Regenta Place brand, which is what this hotel opened under, which is going to be typically 40 to 80 keys.

items.statement: Geopolitical conflict, rising labour costs under new labour codes, fuel price hikes, and construction delays (e.g., tile supply from Morbi) cited as key risks.
items.quote: This new labour code and the fuel prices have added to this thing and the labour code expenses are very, very high. And in fact, today, there is a news article in the Bangalore paper that they are planning to increase the minimum wages.

items.statement: International travellers accounted for ~19% of guests in Q4 FY26; Middle East carrier disruption impacted inbound travel.
items.quote: Q4FY26, 30,000 means almost 19% guests were international travellers as against 80.8% guests in domestic.

items.statement: ICONIQA Mumbai Q4 occupancy 62% (Jan 80%, Feb 73%, March hit by war cancellations); pre-operating expense write-off of INR7.5 crores taken in FY26.
items.quote: So the occupancy of ICONIQA during Q4 was around, one second, I'll just tell you. 62%. Yeah. So the occupancy of ICONIQA was 62% in Q4.

items.statement: Consumer sentiment and retail demand improved meaningfully across all categories and channels in Q4 FY26.
items.quote: During the fourth quarter, we witnessed a meaningful improvement in overall consumer sentiment and retail demand. This was reflected across all our categories and channels.

items.statement: Sales volume grew 10.8% YoY to 54.5 million pieces in Q4 FY26.
items.quote: Sales volume in the quarter was 54.5 million pieces, growing by 10.8% year-on-year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin was 20.8% in Q4 FY26 and 22% for FY26; management targets 19-21% for FY27.
items.quote: We're still confident that we will operate between 19% to 21%. This year, '25-'26, has been a year of very good performance in terms of margin. We closed the year with 22%. But our range, we believe, will be between 19% and 21%, and that's what we'll be targeting for the coming year as well.

items.statement: A 2% weighted average price increase was implemented in mid-January for product enhancements; a further hike is planned in Q1 FY27 to cover input cost inflation.
items.quote: We took a price increase. I mean, we initiated it in the month of January, sometime mid-January as far as production is concerned. But I think the benefit of that has flown in only from mid of March. That's because of the FIFO model that we operate with. And that is to the tune of about 2% weighted average.

items.statement: Inflationary pressure seen in cotton and other raw materials; fresh purchases show elevated inflation.
items.quote: We continue to witness inflationary pressure across key input costs during the quarter, particularly in cotton, along wi th increase in certain other raw materials and operating

items.statement: Odisha and K.R. Pet plants are still on learning curve; maturity expected to improve production efficiency and margins.
items.quote: As you are aware, some of our plants are ne w, still going through the learning curve and operating at suboptimal levels today. But once we hit maturity with Odisha, once we hit maturity with K.R. Pet, our overall efficiencies -- prod uction efficiency for the company will be much higher than what we are delivering today, which should bring in margin expansion opportunities

items.statement: Inventory days rose to 73 at end of Q4 from 64 at start of year; net working capital days 56 vs 54; inventory build-up was a conscious hedge against raw material price increases.
items.quote: Inventory days were 73 in the end of quarter 4 as against 64 days in the beginning of the year. Net working capital days were 56 days as against 54 days in the beginning of the year.

items.statement: Expect INR 40-50 crores of subsidies in FY27 from Odisha (wage, power, capital investment subsidies spread over multiple years).
items.quote: On the subsidy part, yes, we didn't plan to realize any subsidy in FY26. But yes, in FY27, we have plans to start realizing the subsidies. So over the year, I think we are expecting we should be getting around INR40 crores to INR50 crores of subsidy and that will happen.

items.statement: E-commerce contributes 15% of revenue, up a couple of percentage points YoY; Jockey ranks #1 on major platforms in men's and women's innerwear.
items.quote: As we stand today, 15% of our top line is contributed by the e-commerce business. As this -- the reduction in intensity helped us, definitely because the lesser money is going into brands in terms of activating consumer, the more stable brands or market-leading brands tend to gain.

items.statement: Competitive intensity has reduced vs 1.5 years ago; several D2C brands exited or consolidated offline presence; marketing and discounting spend by rivals has come down significantly.
items.quote: There have been many players who operated in the offline space, who were traditionally D2C players, moved in and operated in the offline space, who, in a way, wound up operations offline, exited general trade, consolidated their presence, either exited completely or consolidated distribution to operate in lesser number of geographies or shrunk their distribution to operate with lesser number of st

items.statement: Premiumization driven by Bonded collection and outerwear; JKY Groove sold out faster than expected, expanding to 500 EBOs and select MBOs.
items.quote: In terms of the Bonded line, I think a lot of our numbers in terms of ASP increase and premiumization is thanks to the Bonded collection, both in men's innerwear wear as well as bras, very, very well accepted all through quarter 3 and quarter 4.

items.statement: Targeting double-digit volume growth in FY27; value growth to exceed volume growth; EBITDA margin target 19-21%; marketing spend to rise to ~5% of sales.
items.quote: Our intent in the year going forward is a volume growth intent. And of course, anything that reflects because of price increase would be largely driven by input cost-related measures but not as a means to increase top line.

items.statement: Marketing spend was a little over 4% of sales in FY26; targeting close to 5% in FY27 with shift to performance-led marketing.
items.quote: For the bygone year, it's about a little over 4%. We target to take that up to close to 5% in the next year.

items.statement: Exited one large-format store due to commercial negotiations to maintain channel harmony and margin parity; store count reduced.
items.quote: There was one key large-format store where we have exited because of commercial negotiations, which led to Jockey having to exit a large-format store in terms of presence.

items.statement: Volume elasticity closely monitored; will absorb input cost inflation in margins rather than risk volume loss from price hikes.
items.quote: If it comes to a stage where we will need to touch prices to the extent that it's going to affect volumes, we would rather refrain from doing that given the healthy margins that we operate with and absorb that in the margins temporarily.

items.statement: Revenue grew 14.1% YoY in Q4 FY26; PAT grew 9% YoY; FY26 revenue growth 6.3%, PAT growth 4.8%.
items.quote: For the quarter, revenue grew by 14.1%, while the profit after tax increased by 9%. For FY26, revenue growth was 6.3% and PAT increase was 4.8%.

items.statement: FY27 presales guidance of INR6,000 crores from own projects and INR2,000 crores from DM projects, total INR8,000 crores
items.quote: On the FY '27 outlook, based on our launch pipeline, ongoing inventory sales and market momentum, we are providing the following FY '27 guidance. A presales of INR6,000 crores from our own projects, representing a 30% year -on-year growth, along with an additional INR2,000 crores from the DM projects totalling INR8,000crores.

items.statement: FY27 collections guidance of approximately INR3,000 crores, reflecting around 75% year-on-year growth
items.quote: Collections of a pproximately INR3,000 crores, reflecting around 75% year -on-year growth driven by the milestone -linked inflows from existing launches and ongoing projects

items.statement: FY27 new launch GDV guidance of approximately INR19,400 crores across 11 owned projects and 2 DM projects
items.quote: New launch GDV of approximately INR19,400 crores across 11 owned projects and along 2 DM projects, Juhu and Sky Terraces in Bangalore, with the combined GDV of DM projects is approximately INR6,100 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 presales of INR2,632 crores, up 89% quarter-on-quarter, strongest quarter in company history
items.quote: Q4 FY '26 was the strongest quarter in our company's history. Q4 presales stood at INR2,632 crores, up 89% quarter -on-quarter.

items.statement: FY26 collections from operations of INR1,673 crores, Q4 collections of INR577 crores up 39% quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: Q4 FY '26 collections stood at INR 577 crores, reflecting a 39% quarter -on-quarter growth and FY '26 collections from operations were INR1,673 crores.

items.statement: FY26 construction spend of INR1,182 crores, representing approximately 71% of collections
items.quote: Construction spend dur ing FY '26 stood at INR1,182 crores, representing approximately 71% of collections, reflecting a capital deployment that's disciplined

items.statement: FY27 construction spend planned at approximately INR2,500 crores
items.quote: So, while we are expecting collections of roughly INR3,000 -odd crores this year, we also want to spend approximately INR2,500-odd crores on construction.

items.statement: FY26 launched projects with cumulative GDV of approximately INR16,300 crores across 6 launches
items.quote: During FY '26, we launched projects with a cumulative GDV of approximately INR16,300 crores across 6 different launches.

items.statement: FY27 launch pipeline of 11 owned projects with GDV of INR13,300 crores plus 2 DM projects with GDV of INR6,100 crores
items.quote: Our FY '27 launch program consists of 9 projects, which are owned with a cumulative GDV of INR13,300 crores. And this is supplemented by 2 DM projects, taking our total launch GDV to approximately INR19,400 crores.

items.statement: FY27 launch pipeline weighted towards luxury residences, villas, premium apartments and lifestyle second homes across Bangalore, MMR and NCR
items.quote: This pipeline is geographically balanced across our 3 core markets, Bangalore, MMR and NCR and is weighted towards product categories where we have demonstrated strong absorption, which is luxury residences and villas, premium apartments and lifestyle second homes.

items.statement: Bangalore luxury portfolio (INR10 crore+ ticket size) accounted for over 65% of all FY26 sales in that segment, roughly INR2,000 crores
items.quote: Our Bangalore launches in the INR10 crore s ticket size accounted for over 65% of all FY '26 sales in Bangalore in that segment, which was roughly INR2,000 crores.

items.statement: Embassy Citadel positioned as value proposition in South Mumbai luxury with intentionally smaller ticket sizes and pricing lower than top developers
items.quote: And honestly, if I have to tell you about Worli and all the supply there, we are positioned as a value proposition there, also given that the ticket size is intentionally smaller. And from a pricing point of view, we are coming in much l ower than what I think the top developers are

items.statement: Gross institutional debt of INR4,100 crores, cash of INR1,100 crores, net institutional debt of INR3,000 crores, net debt to equity 0.3x as of March FY26
items.quote: As of March FY '26, our gross institutional debt stood at approximately INR4,100 crores with cash and cash equivalents of around INR1,100 crores, resulting in net institutional debt of approximately INR3,000 crores. Our net debt to equity ratio stood at 0.3x while gr oss debt equity was at 0.4x

items.statement: Target to reduce cost of debt from current 14.8% to 10% over next 12-18 months
items.quote: Our expectation is to bring it to 10% over a period of time, but this will be a gradual decrease over the next 12 to 18 months.

items.statement: Comfortable with net debt to equity of 0.3x; progressive reduction in net debt levels expected from FY28 onwards
items.quote: We want to keep our net debt levels to 0.5x or less. And as Aditya said, this year, we want to spend all the collections or most of the collections on construction, so not a great reduction in the net debt numbers. But starting from the next financial year, there will be a progressive reduction in the net debt levels. And we are comfortable with the net debt levels of 0.3x.

items.statement: Karnataka High Court set aside KIADB resumption order relating to 78 acres at Kadugodi, Bangalore, based on company's undertaking to comply with lease terms
items.quote: Second, the Honourable High Court of Karnataka set aside the KIADB resumption order relating to 78 acres at Kadugodi, Bangalore, held by Embassy East Business Park based on the company's undertaking to comply with the lease terms and obtain KIADB's NOC pri or to any third -party interest creation

items.statement: Presales to collection conversion is a structural lag; FY26 collections marginally lower than FY25 despite 128% presales growth due to 80% of presales concentrated in H2
items.quote: With over 80% of FY '26 presales concentrated in H2, the corresponding milestone- linked collections will largely flow through FY '27 and FY '28. This is the principal reason why FY '26 collections of INR1,673 crores were marginally lower than FY '25 collections of INR1,852 crores even as presales grew 128% ye ar-on-year. The presales to collection conversion is a structural lag and not an operati

items.statement: Net surplus margin expected to be close to 50% over next several years as launched projects get delivered
items.quote: And we expect that to be close to 50% over the course of the next several years as these projects get delivered. And so we're really focusing on that kind of cash coming into our system that will eventually help us to do more projects, do more BD as well as kind of service our debt.

items.statement: OC received portfolio is 98% sold with FY26 presales of INR573 crores and collections of INR645 crores
items.quote: Our OC received portfolio is now 98% sold with FY '26 presales of INR573 crores and collections of INR645 crores from this portfolio, reflecting a healthy monetization of completed inventory.

items.statement: No additional legacy regulatory agreements identified that could harm the company; NCLAT matter caught management by surprise but resolved
items.quote: Look, we don't know of anything else that's out there today that can harm the company and the stock. This did catch us a little bit by surprise. But I think we've overcome it and we're looking forward out here, but there is nothing else out there.

items.statement: Promoter pledge increased from 47% to 68% due to share price dip; no additional debt taken; plan to reduce pledge to 48% and fully unpledge over 2-3 years
items.quote: pledge -- had pledged about 47 -odd percent of the promoter shares has pledged before this entire NCL AT matter came up. And because the share price dipped, we had increased that 47% pledge to 68% pledge. And no additional debt was taken, mind you. The promoter had not taken any additional debt. It was only because the share price fell that additional shares were pledged. And now that the share pr

items.statement: Shareholder debt of INR1,121 crores (including Blackstone) to be converted to equity over time, waiting for share price improvement
items.quote: We have a shareholder debt today along with Blackstone, we have a shareholder debt of INR1,100 crores, which we will convert to equity over a period in time, but we're waiting for the market to correct, both the market to correct as well as our share price to correct, which will take a little more a few more months maybe. And then we will up our equity in the company along with Blackstone.

items.statement: Evaluating options to dispose Sohna land (500+ acres, only 75 acres developable) as it suits only resort/farmhouse development with limited FSI
items.quote: At the same time, we are evaluating options of even disposing this land because only 75 acres of developed portion that we can do only suits really a resort or some type of a farmhouse, bungalow. There's not a whole lot of FSI we can consume here. So while the land size is high, management does not feel that there's a whole lot of value attributed to that.

items.statement: Revenue recognition under Ind AS 115 on completed contract basis; over 80% of FY26 presales from projects with target OC dates FY28-FY32; revenue recognition to normalize from FY28 onwards
items.quote: Over 80% of our FY '26 presales were concentrated in H2, predominantly from launches such as Embassy Citadel, Embassy Greenshore, Embassy Eden and Embassy Verde Phase 2. These projects have target OC dates ranging from FY '28 through FY '32. Revenue from these projects will be recognized from FY '28 onwards in the respective years when the OC for these projects are received.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance INR2,200-2,400 crores with EBITDA margin 12-14%
items.quote: So the way we are seeing it is that on the top line, we should be in the region of between INR2,200 crores to INR2,400 crores. And EBITDA margins would be between 12% to 14% on an overall basis.

items.statement: FY27 guidance unchanged despite Middle East crisis impact
items.quote: And -- we are not changing our guidance -- and we are not changing our guidance for FY 2027. We are guiding on the same line.

items.statement: Q4 sales impacted ~20% due to shipment delays, lack of ships, increased freight time
items.quote: This quarter, the sale was impacted by around 20% due to delay in shipments, lack of ships and increased freight time to our markets across the globe.

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA INR21 crores at 5% margin; Middle East crisis and Vinpai loss reduced EBITDA by ~INR30 crores
items.quote: Resultantly, the quarter EBITDA has been INR21 crores, it's 5%. I think it's -- in the given circumstances, it's not a bad performance.

items.statement: Vanillin realization improved from sub-$11 to >$12.5 in Q4; FY27 blended realization expected $13.5-14
items.quote: Our realization moved from sub $11 in the last quarter to almost $12.5 plus in this quarter. And naturally, the realizations are better. Realizations will increase in the next quarter.

items.statement: Ethyl vanillin campaign 600 MT with 50% order book covered; US vanillin target 2,200-2,400 MT for FY27
items.quote: We started with the ethyl vanillin campaign and the campaign is for 600 ton, and we already have an order book covering 50% of that.

items.statement: Blends business FY26 exit rate INR1,050 crores; FY27 target >INR1,400 crores
items.quote: This year, we are looking at anything an upwards INR1,400 crores for the FY27 in the Blends business.

items.statement: Diphenol plant fire contained; evaluating repurpose or shutdown due to high phenol prices (INR85 to >INR150/kg)
items.quote: We were able to contain it. There will be some loss, but we will be -- we have adequate insurance cover. In fact, we were -- we had reduced the -- or planning to close down the plant or shut down the plant of diphenol.

items.statement: Ethyl vanillin plant running well; 600 MT campaign planned; methyl vanillin inventory 300 MT in channel
items.quote: We'll be taking a campaign of around 600 metric ton of ethyl vanillin. So we have enough methyl vanillin to -- not enough, but a fairly good stock of ethyl vanillin to not allow the market to dry.

items.statement: Phenol raw material price rose from INR85 to >INR150/kg; switching to imported hydroquinone from China
items.quote: As you know, our basic raw material prices INR85 is now being quoted at more than INR150 per kg and the availability is also not consistent.

items.statement: Vanillin raw material cost increased from $7.5 to ~$9/kg post-war; caustic costs doubled
items.quote: The total cost of -- raw material cost itself is $7.5 pre-war, it's around $2 of catechol. So you can just imagine there are a lot of other raw materials which are going, which can really get impacted by the geopolitical situation.

items.statement: Longer delivery times impacted working capital cycle; freight costs 3x pre-war levels; logistics uncertainty to persist at least a quarter
items.quote: The cost as far as we are concerned, where we put almost a lot of material across the globe in the American continent, both north and south of it, the costs are almost three times.

items.statement: Consolidated debt INR670 crores (incl. INR30 crores escrow); annual repayment INR60-70 crores; seeking structured/bank debt for growth
items.quote: So at the end of this year, we have around INR670 crores loan. Out of that, we are carrying INR30 crores in escrow, which is for the Vinpai open offer.

items.statement: Equity infusion last resort; authorized capital increased in March; pursuing debt financing (structured/bank combo)
items.quote: Capital infusion is the last resort. We are in the market for debt at this moment. So that looks like a better option.

items.statement: CFS Europe liquidated; INR100 crores gain on derecognition; INR50-60 crores annual cash burn eliminated
items.quote: There is a gain booked on loss of control of the company, which is around INR100-odd crores, which we have booked this quarter.

items.statement: Vanillin US volume target 2,200-2,400 MT for FY27; Europe 1,500-1,600 MT
items.quote: Our estimate for FY 2027 in the U.S. will be around the 2,200 to 2,400 metric ton. And we are on stream to achieve that number.

items.statement: Catechol inventory ~3,000 MT (8-9 months vanillin production); 1:1 yield for methyl/ethyl vanillin
items.quote: So it's about in the region of about 3,000 ton.

items.statement: US tariff reduced to 15.5% (5.5% base + 10%); INR9-10 crores duty paid till Feb claimed as refund (50-50 cash/adjustment)
items.quote: So there's a base 5.5% duty and then there's 10% tariff across the board. So it's 15.5%.

items.statement: Vinpai acquisition added INR10 crores first month, only INR17 crores last 3 months due to liquidity issues
items.quote: We missed the target of 20% primarily because the projections of Vinpai, which did INR10 crores in the first month was only able to do around INR17crores in the last three months.

items.statement: Syensqo pricing vanillin at $17-18 to saturate market; expected to raise to $19-20 when capacity full
items.quote: Syensqo is selling at about $17 to $18, so there is -- cost, there's a holding cost and the tariff cost and some channel financing costs.

items.statement: Geopolitical conflict causing freight cost 3x, raw material inflation, logistics unpredictability; H1 FY27 likely impacted
items.quote: I feel that even a stable growth of 10% to 15% over these two quarters is great. Really great.

items.statement: Employee cost increased for Blends growth investment; Vinpai added 4 months costs; peak hiring reached, no significant further increase
items.quote: We have been saying that we'll be investing in human capital to help us grow the business, especially in the Blends sector, and we are really looking at exponential growth in Blends business.

items.statement: Vinpai and Vitafor EBITDA breakeven at INR14-16 million annual revenue each; both expected above breakeven in FY27
items.quote: Vitafor is at 16 million for the whole year. And so is Vinpai is also at the same level, 14 million to 16 million.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR1 per share (10% of face value) for fourth consecutive year, subject to shareholder approval
items.quote: I'm pleased to inform you that our Board has recommended a dividend of INR1 per share, which is equivalent to 10% of the face value for the fourth consecutive year, subject to the approval of shareholders.

items.statement: Hospital business guided for 15%+ revenue growth and 150 bps EBITDA margin improvement in FY27; Diagnostics guided for 23-24% EBITDA margin and double-digit revenue growth in FY27
items.quote: So revenue-wise, we are well poised to see on hospital side, 15% plus revenue growth. And EBITDA side, we expect another 150 basis point margin improvement for the current financial year.

items.statement: Diagnostics business guided for 23-24% EBITDA margin and double-digit revenue growth in FY27 with 70% volume and 30% value contribution
items.quote: For the coming year as well, we'll be around 23% to 24% kind of EBITDA margins. We are making further investments into new centers and all this year. In terms of revenue, I think from where we were, we have improved quite well, and we have come to about 8.5% now. And we'll definitely improve and touch about double digits this year is what we are hoping.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR900 crores annually for FY27-FY29, split 60% maintenance and 40% growth capex
items.quote: As regard the capex guidance, we expect to incur around INR900 crores annually on the capex, which may include 60% towards maintenance capex and balance is the growth capex.

items.statement: Plan to add 1,800 beds over next 4 years via brownfield expansion; FY27 target of 400+ beds including FMRI tower operational within weeks and additions at Noida, Manesar, Amritsar, FHKI Kolkata
items.value: 400+ beds in FY27, 1,800 beds over 4 years
items.quote: Over the next 4 years, we plan to ramp up bed capacity further through brownfield expansion by adding around 1,800 beds. Of these in financial year '27, we expect to add capacity of more than 400 beds with a new tower at FMRI expected to be operationalized within weeks and balanced bed addition at Noida, Manesar and Amritsar as well as FHKI Kolkata coming during the year.

items.statement: FMRI tower to be operationalized in phased manner starting with ~100 beds in FY27; current occupancy at 85-90% with bed shortage
items.quote: We expect to operationalize this new tower in a week time. Our initial plan is to operationalize in a phased manner. We don't want to open all the beds immediately because it is having impact on the cost also. And as we move on the occupancy ramp-up curve, we will open the further beds. In the current financial year, our target -- our plan is to open around 100 beds.

items.statement: Acquired ~800 beds in FY26 via brownfield and inorganic: People Tree Hospital (125 beds) in Bengaluru Jan 2026, 200-bed lease in Greater Noida Sep 2025, Shrimann Hospital (228 beds) in Jalandhar Jul 2025
items.quote: The year gone by has also been marked by significant progress and strategic development across the company, including the addition of approximately 800 beds to our network through a combination of brownfield expansion and inorganic acquisitions.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 22.8% in FY26 from 20.4% in FY25; Hospital EBITDA margin improved to 22.2% from 20.5%; Diagnostics EBITDA margin (ex-one-offs) improved to 23.2% from 22%
items.quote: Our consolidated operating EBITDA increased 31.3% to INR2,085 crores, which translates into a margin of 22.8% in financial year '26 versus 20.4% in financial year '25. For the hospital business, operating EBITDA margins have improved from 20.5% in financial year '25 to 22.2% in financial year '26.

items.statement: Hospital occupancy 68% in FY26 vs 69% in FY25; occupied beds increased 15% to 3,270; ARPOB grew 3.4% to INR2.51 crores per annum
items.value: 68% occupancy, 3,270 occupied beds, INR2.51 cr ARPOB
items.quote: Our hospital occupancy in financial year '26 was 68% compared to 69% in financial year '25 However, the number of occupied beds increased by 15% from 3,270 beds in financial year '26, up to 2,838 beds in financial year '25. Our hospital business recorded a 3.4% increase in ARPOB, reaching INR2.51 crores per annum in financial year '26.

items.statement: Key procedure volumes grew: Radiation Therapy +19%, Robotic Surgeries +66% in FY26; Focus specialties revenue grew 18.9% contributing 62% of hospital revenue
items.value: Radiation +19%, Robotic +66%, Focus specialties +18.9% (62% of revenue)
items.quote: Key procedure volumes across focus specialties such as Radiation Therapy, Robotic Surgeries witnessed steady growth during the year, increasing by 19% and 66%, respectively. Revenue from focus specialties comprising Oncolog y, Neurosciences, Cardiac Sciences, Gastroenterology, Orthopedics and Renal Sciences grew 18.9% and contributed 62% to overall hospital business

items.statement: International patient revenue grew 18.5% to INR639 crores (7.8% of hospital revenue) in FY26; Q4 international growth slowed to 11% vs 18-20% for full year
items.quote: Revenue from international patients grew by 18.5% during the year to reach INR639 crores, contributing 7.8% to overall hospital business revenue.

items.statement: CGHS/ECHS drug price capping at 30% of MRP in Punjab region led to discontinuation of some oncology patients and occupancy drop; government issued circular, industry represented, no resolution timeline
items.quote: as you know, the drug prices are capped at 30% to the MRP. So that has led to some of the drugs where we are not earning that type of margi n, we have stopped taking those patients. And we have asked patient to take drugs from either CGHS stores or to procure from the market. And that has led to drop in some business

items.statement: Net debt INR2,334 crores, net debt-to-EBITDA 1.09x as of Mar 31, 2026 vs 0.93x a year ago; increase due to acquisitions and investments
items.quote: the company's net debt stands at INR2,334 crores with a net debt-to-EBITDA of 1.09x as on March 31, 2026, as aga inst 0.93 on March 31, 2025. The increase in debt was primarily due to acquisition undertaken during the year, amongst other investments, which we

items.statement: IHH plans to increase stake to 50% with ~INR10,000 crores fresh equity infusion for growth; no specific timeline, capital to be provided as needed
items.quote: Recently, the group CEO of IHH has given an interview where he has mentioned that there is a plan to increase their stake to 50%, and they have also mentioned some amount around INR10,000 crores fresh equity infusion in the company for meeting the growth aspirations.

items.statement: Doctor costs saw slight increase in FY26; no major senior clinician movements expected; clinician pool comfortable for new capacity absorption
items.quote: as far as , Neha, doctor costs are concerned, there has been a slight increase, as you would notice when you go through the details. But we do n't expect anything further to happen because I think we have already taken the necessary steps in this direction, minimum number of movements we can expect in terms of senior clinicians, we are not expecting any major changes

items.statement: Diagnostics preventive health revenue contribution increased to 13% in FY26 from 11% in FY25; added 50+ new tests across oncology, molecular, prenatal, immunology, infectious diseases, gastroenterology, neuro-oncology
items.quote: We continue to see healthy growth in our preventive health and wellness portfolio, supported by increasing awareness and adoption of preventive panels and corporate wellness programs. This preventive health revenues contributed 13% to the overall mix in FY26 versus 11% during the last year, reinforcing its position as a key long-term growth driver.

items.statement: Diagnostics processed 40.8 million tests in FY26 vs 39.2 million in FY25 (+4.1%); Q4 FY26 processed 10 million tests vs 9.6 million in Q4 FY25 (+5%); B2C:B2B ratio stable at 52:48
items.quote: During the year, we conducted 40.8 million tests versus 39.2 million tests last year. The B2C to B2B revenue ratio remained stable at 52 to 48 in the FY26, reflecting balanced traction across both the channels.

items.statement: FY26 capex ~INR700 crores for capacity expansion and medical infrastructure including surgical robots, MRI, cath labs, PET CT
items.quote: To highlight our capital expenditure in financial year '26 stood at approximately INR700 crores, reflecting our confidence to further scale up operations, both in terms of capacity expansion and enhancement of medical infrastructure.

items.statement: BG Road occupancy at 55% (vs 63-64% market) due to low government business, intense competition, TPA/cash mix; on radar for improvement with brownfield expansion pipeline
items.quote: BG Road is one of the unit on our target where the occupancy level is low. And there, we have expansion in pipeline, brownfield expansion in pipeline. So, this unit, the occupancy level is low because, one, we are not taking a lot of government business here. So it is more of the TPA and cash business. Secondly, there is an intense competition around that region.

items.statement: Manesar facility revenue INR140 crores in FY26, occupancy ~48% (deceptive due to phased bed opening); breakeven achieved, positive EBITDA contribution expected in FY27
items.quote: Yes, INR140 crores is the revenue number for last financial year for Manesar. Aman Goyal: And the occupancy, occupancy-wise? Vivek Goyal: It is around 48%, but it is quite deceptive because during the year, we have opened up new beds also. So we are opening beds as we are moving on the occupancy
