items.statement: Shalimar Bagh expansion delayed to FY29 due to approval issues; Mohali, Amritsar towers to take 2.5-3 years; BG Road has 100 beds ready pending occupancy improvement; Mulund at 65% occupancy, planning another tower
items.quote: It's mainly Shalimar Bagh, if I can mention. One is the Shalimar Bagh, which is the big extension, where we are expecting some approval related issues to be sorted out. And once it is sorted out, we will move fast on this expansion. So Shalimar Bagh, defin itely, there is a delay in the expansion

items.statement: PE-backed competition viewed as future opportunity for legacy players; clinical quality and patient satisfaction remain key differentiators; concerns about valuation inflation from PE transactions
items.quote: I think, Sanjay, the main differentiator is going to be the clinical quality outcome, patient satisfaction. And we continue to remain focused on it. As far as the PE-backed platforms are concerned, I think that's a future opportunity for the legacy players who are the kind of strategic in the market.

items.statement: Diagnostics genomic capabilities advanced with Illumina NovaSeq X operational at Mumbai reference lab; validations completed for hereditary cancer panels, whole exome sequencing, carrier screening, genetic disorder panels
items.quote: We also advanced our genomic capabilities with the operationalization of the Illumina NovaSeq X at our global reference laboratory in Mumbai. During the quarter, we enabled routine clinical use of the platform. We also completed validations across key areas, including hereditary cancer panels, whole exome sequencing, carrier screening and genetic disorder panels.

items.statement: Diagnostics expanded network with 675+ customer touchpoints and 20+ labs (including 10 hospital lab management labs) in FY26; geospatial phlebotomist assignment and digital enhancements rolled out
items.quote: We expanded our network with gross additions of over 675 Customer touchpoints and gross addition of 20 -plus labor atories, including 10 hospital lab management laboratories, strengthening Agilus footprint and improving accessibility across focus cities as well as emerging micro markets

items.statement: Jaipur hospital expected to grow ~15% in FY27 with EBITDA margin 13-14%; FEHI margin improving with operational efficiency and new clinical talent; Manesar, Greater Noida, Ludhiana turning positive from losses
items.quote: As regard to Jaipur is concerned, Jaipur has also shown last year a very good progress. It is -- we expect the Jaipur to grow around 15% pl us next financial year with EBITDA margin in the range of 13%, 14

items.statement: International patient growth dipped in Q4 (11% vs 18-20% FY); mitigating by broadening market base focusing on Africa and other countries; domestic growth offsetting international dip
items.quote: As regard international business is concerned, we are tracking well. We are broadening our market base. We are concentrating more on Africa and other countries to mitigate this international business dip, which we have witnessed in the l ast quarter. Having said that, the domestic business growth has more or less taken care of what we have lost in the international business

items.statement: Digital/preventive health strategy: not collaborating with external platforms (past experience dilutive); will gradually enhance own app and digital presence but not focus area due to cash burn concerns
items.quote: We have had experiences earlier on. We believe that, that is dilutive to our presence. And so we are not at the moment looking to do -- go on that direction. But we do understand the importance of this, and we will continue to develop our platform, which requires a lot of improvement.

items.statement: Indian auto industry saw broad-based growth in Q4 FY26 supported by GST rate cut, income tax relief, and repo rate cuts
items.quote: During that quarter, the Indian automobile industry continued to witness broad-based growth across all major vehicle categories. This robust performance was supported by improved affordability following the GST rate reduction, enhanced purchasing power from personal income tax relief and lower financing costs due to successive repo rate cuts by the Reserve Bank of India.

items.statement: Passenger vehicle production grew 11.3% YoY in Q4 FY26 to 1.57M units; full year FY26 grew 9.4% to 5.54M units
items.quote: Passenger vehicle segment posted strong production numbers of 15,71,000 units in quarter 4 of FY25-'26 registering a growth of 11.3% compared to Q4 of same period last year. The segment also clocked production numbers of 55,39,000 units in '25-'26, posting a growth of 9.4% as compared to previous financial year.

items.statement: LCV production grew 15.8% YoY in Q4 FY26 to 208K units; 3-wheeler production grew 32.4% YoY to 345K units
items.quote: While light commercial vehicle production grew by over 15.8%, reaching 208,000 units this quarter and by 11.2%, reaching 712,000 units in FY26. In quarter 4 of FY26, 3-wheeler posted Q4 production of 345,000 units with a growth of 32.4% as compared to same quarter last year.

items.statement: Industry optimistic about continued growth across all vehicle categories in FY27, but geopolitical risks from West Asia conflict persist
items.quote: Consequently, the industry remains optimistic about continued growth across all vehicle categories in financial year '27, building on the strong domestic momentum seen in the latter half of FY2 6. However, uncertainties stemming from the West Asia conflict, including volatility in crude oil and commodity prices, elevated exchange rates and disruptions to shipping routes continue to pose a risk to

items.statement: FY26 full year revenue INR 3,396.8 cr (+20% YoY), gross profit INR 802.8 cr (+8% YoY), EBITDA INR 419.1 cr (+6% YoY)
items.quote: For the 12 months ended 31st March 2026, total revenues stood at INR3,396.8 crores, marking a growth of 20% over the same period last year. Gross profit for the period was INR802.8 crores, up 8% Y-o-Y again, again, in line with the industry growth. EBITDA for 12-month period stood at INR419.1 crores, up 6% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: BS6.3/WLTP applicable from April 2027 for vehicles below 3.5T GVW; will increase focus on catalyst efficiency, thermal management, durability
items.quote: BS6.3 or WLTP, applicable from 1st of April 2027 for vehi cles below 3.5 tonnes gross vehicle weight is a more real -world representative test procedure and is expected to increase focus on catalyst efficiency, thermal management and durability

items.statement: TREM5 revised draft notification proposes power mode-wise norms across tractor kW categories; near-term domestic opportunity on mufflers and integrated mufflers
items.quote: On TREM5, a revised draft gazette notification has been issued and the road map is now proposed power mode -wise across tractor kilowatt categories. While the near -term domestic opportunity now is on mufflers and integrated mufflers, the technology work alr eady done is helping us in business development discussions, particularly in agri tractor and export -linked opportunities.

items.statement: CAFE III norms (April 2027-March 2032) are multi-fuel technology inclusive; support EVs, hybrids, CNG, ethanol, flex fuel, lightweighting; all non-EV powertrains need engineered emission systems
items.quote: CAFE III is another important development. These norms applicable from April '27 to March 2032 are structured as a multi-fuel technology inclusive regulation. While EVs receive the highest credits, the framework also supports hybrids, CNG, ethanol, flex fuel vehicles, lightweighting and other fuel efficiency technologies. Therefore, the response to CAFE III is most likely to be a combination of EV

items.statement: Lightweighting vertical market share increased to ~14% in FY26 from 12.5% in FY25; expected to rise further in FY27-28 based on booked orders
items.quote: Our lightweighting FY26 market share has increased to approximately 14% and is expected to rise further in FY27 and FY28 based on the orders already booked.

items.statement: Lightweighting comprises ~10% of gross sales; Donghee TLA adds subframes and torsion beams to portfolio; control arms/links scaling, torsion beams/frames in design standardization phase
items.quote: This vertical already comprises of approximately 10% of our gross sales and will continue to be the growth engine for the future and be a large contributor. Further, the Donghee TLA has added to our content per vehicle offering with subframes and torsion beams. These will be the next product segments that will add to lightweighting vertical growth.

items.statement: Received test order from existing US-based heavy industry emission company for India supplies; entry into another US CV OEM
items.quote: We have also received an order from an existing customer, a large U.S. -based heavy industry emission company. This supplies for this OEM export order in India. This is a test order, but of strategic importance as this gives us entry into another U.S. CV OE M.

items.statement: Previously announced North American engine/genset export order SOP moved from Q2 to Q3 FY27 with gradual ramp-up per customer schedule
items.quote: Our previously announced export order with the North American engine and genset manufacturer remains aligned to customer schedules. SOPs moved from Q2 to Q3 FY27 with gradual ramp- up based on customer schedule requirements.

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance INR 90-110 cr for R&D augmentation, new emission norms readiness, new program SOPs; new facility investments over and above this range
items.quote: So as far as FY2 7 is concerned, our broad capex guidance is around INR90 crores to INR110 crores. And we are increasing this because we are augmenting R&D capabilities in lightweighting and readiness for new emission norms and a lot of SOPs of new programs are also taking place this year. Now investments in new facilities to expand the footprint as per customer needs will be definitely over and a

items.statement: Uttarakhand facility progressing per plan, modular scalable capacity for emission and lightweighting products in North India; Chakan 3 lightweighting plant started SOP, ramping up gradually
items.quote: The Uttarakhand facility is progressing as per plan. The facility is being set up closer to customers' manufacturing location and is expected to improve logistics, responsiveness and customer alignment. The capacity will be mod ular and scalable. And the plant will support existing business as well as future opportunities in emission and lightweighting products in North India. The Chakan 3 lightwe

items.statement: FY26 revenue split: CV emissions 44%, PV emissions 43%, off-highway/gensets/exports 1%, suspension 9%, supply chain 2%, misc 1%
items.quote: CV emissions contribution is 44% for this financial year and PV emissions contribution is 43%. Off-highway, gensets and exports together currently contribute 1% because these are growing. Suspension contributes 9%, 2% from supply chain vertical and 1% from miscellaneous.

items.statement: Export margins relatively higher but increased working capital needs; net margins broadly in line with domestic business
items.quote: Yes. So broadly, you're right, export margins relatively are going to be higher. And as you rightly said, there will be an increased working capital requirement. So on a net basis, these will broadly be in line with the domestic business margin. So at net level, these will be broadly in line.

items.statement: Inventory increase from INR 10 cr to INR 75 cr due to 30% revenue growth; inventory days improved
items.quote: So if you see, there has been steep growth in revenues this year, 30%. So obviously, inventories have moved in line with that. If you look at it on a number of days basis, these have rather improved. So this is purely on account of overall increase in scale of operations.

items.statement: M&A approach disciplined but active; strong balance sheet gives flexibility for strategic fit, customer and technology relevance; disciplined on valuation and ROCE
items.quote: On M&A, our approach remained disciplined but active. The current global disruption and supply chain realignment can create opportunities for well -capitalized India-based players. Sharda has a strong balance sheet, which gives us flexibility to deploy capi tal where there is strategic fit, customer and technology relevance. We will remain disciplined on valuation and ROCE potential.

items.statement: Filed 2 patents in Q4 FY26; total filed 22, awarded 4; R&D focused on emission, thermal management, lightweighting, suspension, global business products
items.quote: During Q4 FY26, we filed 2 more patents. With this, the total number of patents filed stand at 22 and total awarded patents stand at 4. Our R&D efforts are focused across emission and thermal management, lightweighting and suspension and global business products.

items.statement: FY27 growth contributors: full year revenue from earlier lightweighting orders, partial revenue from FY26 orders with SOP in FY27, CV adjacency impact, North American export ramp-up, other export orders, supportive OEM volume outlook
items.quote: The production plan and the preparations from OEMs indicate a steady demand. Our growth contributors include full year revenues from earlier lightweighting suspension orders, partial revenue from FY2 6 lightweighting suspension orders with SOP in FY27, CV adjacency impact, North American export ramp -up and other export orders and of course, the supportive OEM volume outlook with SIAM projections

items.statement: Content per vehicle increase of INR 4,000-10,000 expected from lightweighting portfolio enhancement (control arms, links, torsion beams, subframes)
items.quote: We intend to approximately add almost INR 4,000 to INR 10,000 in content per vehicle increase because the portfolio enhancement.

items.statement: Entry into largest PV OEM (with dedicated exhaust partnerships/JVs) is long-term opportunity; not immediate conversion; continue direct/indirect engagement but no specific timeline
items.quote: Now while the opportunity with that company is very attractive and that they represent a significant part of the vehicle market, but they already have a very well -established supplier ecosystem, and they have a dedicated exhaust partnerships and JVs, which have been supplying for a long time. For us, entering into that customer is certainly a long- term opportunity, but it would be a long term ra

items.statement: West Asia conflict creates crude price volatility, commodity price volatility, elevated exchange rates, shipping route disruptions; risk to sector
items.quote: However, uncertainties stemming from the West Asia conflict, including volatility in crude oil and commodity prices, elevated exchange rates and disruptions to shipping routes continue to pose a risk to the sector.

items.statement: Export focus on North America and Europe; products: CV emission components, engine/genset emission, tractor emission, temperature-controlled tubes, heat shields, emission adjacencies
items.quote: Exports remain a strategic growth priority for us with focus on North America and Europe. Our focused products include CV emission components, engine and genset emission components, tractor emission components, temperature-controlled tubes, heat shields and emission adjacencies.

items.statement: Export orders announced so far do not have catalyst component; pure revenue without catalyst pass-through
items.quote: Specifically, to your point, whatever we have announced till now doe s not have a catalyst component in the export orders.

items.statement: Targets 20-25% average growth in micro-irrigation over next three years; aims for solar EPC contribution to equal micro-irrigation in next two years (50-50 split)
items.quote: If we talk about micro -irrigation business, we are targeting a average grow th of 20% to 25 % over the next three years. And on the solar EPC side, we are targeting a higher growth, especially in the water pumps business. So we are targeting that the contribution of solar EPC segment should be equal to micro-irrigation business in next two years

items.statement: Unexecuted solar pump order book is INR11 crores for 500 pumps; executed 1,000 pumps last quarter, targeting at least 1,000 this quarter
items.quote: So, the unexecuted part is the new order which we got recently, which is for 500 solar pumps. So, that value is around INR11 crores.

items.statement: Ahmedabad plant expected to improve micro-irrigation EBITDA margin by 1-1.5% once fully operational in FY27
items.quote: So for the micro -irrigation business, o nce this plant is fully operational during this year, we are expecting that micro -irrigation business EBIT DA margin should improve by 1% to 1.5% only because of the contribution from this plant

items.statement: Current capacity across Rajkot, Kurnool and Ahmedabad plants can support INR400 crores micro-irrigation revenue without additional capex for next couple of years
items.quote: What is the maximum revenue for micro-irrigation business which we can achieve with this existing setup? So, right now based on the current capacity, we can easily achieve INR400 crores without any additional capex for the next couple of years.

items.statement: Micro-irrigation cash (non-subsidy) business contribution was ~15% in FY26; solar rooftop is 100% cash business
items.quote: Yes, for the micro -irrigation business, the cash business segment, t he contribution was around 15% for this year. And if we talk about solar EPC business, then the rooftop business is completely cash business

items.statement: Exports currently ~5% of micro-irrigation revenue, targeting double digits in 5 years; focus on Africa and Latin America for drip lines
items.quote: At present, the export contribution in micro-irrigation business is around 5% of the total revenues. And we are planning that, you know, as we focus more on this segment, this should at least, you know, move to double digit in next five years.

items.statement: Working capital intensity increased due to high growth in both segments; expects stabilization in FY27 with substantial receivable recoveries
items.quote: So because of the high growth, definitely this year the working capital intensity has increased. But we are expecting that this should stabilize in the current year as there are substantial recoveries in both the business segments, especially on the receivable side.

items.statement: Total debt ~INR89 crores at end of March; 30-35% of sanctioned banking limits unutilized
items.quote: if you see at the end of Ma rch, our total debt was around INR89 crores. So we have sufficient cushion in terms of the sanctioned banking limits. We have quite of quite a bit of unutilized limits from the banks. Almost I think 30% to 35

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margin declined 86 bps YoY to 9.96% due to sharp raw material price increase in March from geopolitical events
items.quote: The EBITDA margin came at 9.96% which was a slight decline of 86 basis points year-on-year and that was primarily on account of the sharp increase in raw material prices during the month of March due to unforeseen geopolitical events.

items.statement: Solar pump orders from Maharashtra: 1,500 pumps in first year, plus new 500 pump order worth INR11 crores this quarter
items.quote: The orders for solar pump which we got from Maharashtra was almost 1,500 pumps, which is a very good performance considering that this was our first year of solar pumps business in Maharashtra. And even this quarter, we have received another order of 500 sol ar pumps which is worth around INR11 crores

items.statement: 750 dealer network across major agri states enables fast execution for solar pumps and rooftop; leverages existing trust and service capability
items.quote: Now if we see the actual work execution, then it is almost similar for both micro-irrigation and solar pumps or even solar EPC, you know, solar rooftop business for that matter. So naturally having a network of 750 dealers helps us in terms of fast execution once we go ahead for the business in any of these states.

items.statement: Differentiates via 30-year brand recall, quality, timely service and deep dealer network in micro-irrigation; applies same playbook to solar EPC in tier-2/3/4 markets
items.quote: So because of our presence in this business for almost 30 years now, we have built that brand recall amongst farmers in terms of quality of our products and also because of our deep, you know, network, we are able to provide timely service and timely availability which are th e key criteria for the farmers

items.statement: Micro-irrigation penetration only 17-18% of 70 million hectare potential; >80% under-penetration remains
items.quote: Now till now in last almost two to three decades, we have only achieved penetration of around 17% to 18%. So, still there is an under-penetration of more than 80% for micro-irrigation.

items.statement: Capex intensity not significantly high; primary capital need is working capital which is fungible and allocable dynamically between segments
items.quote: At at the moment, if you see even our micro-irrigation business, in terms of capex intensity, is it is not very high. So, even going forward also, capex intensity for the overall business would not be significantly high. The only capital investment which goes for both the segments is working capital.

items.statement: No significant risk of policy discontinuation for micro-irrigation or solar pumps; government continues strong support for sustainable farming and renewable energy
items.quote: Government is strongly focusing on both sustainable farming and renewable energy. So we don't, you know, foresee a situation where there would be any change in policy support from the government side.

items.statement: Mindful of external variables: subsidy timelines, competitive intensity in both businesses, and broader macroeconomic conditions
items.quote: At the same time, we also remain mindful of external variables including subsidy timelines, competitive intensity in both the businesses and of course the broader macroeconomic conditions.

items.statement: Invested in infrastructure, people and systems during FY26 to support next phase of growth
items.quote: So overall this year has been one where we have shown growth on both our top line and the bottom line and we have also simultaneously invested in infrastructure, people and systems to support the next phase of growth.

items.statement: Solar pump execution timeline typically 60 days; only takes orders confident of executing within timeline; no execution failures to date
items.quote: In solar pumps, as you asked, definitely there is a defined timeline in which the work should be completed, which is typically 60 days. So, we are only taking an order when we are sure that we are going to execute during that period. items.statement: Ahmedabad plant now operational; external credit rating upgraded during FY26 due to good financial performance
items.quote: One, the Ahmedabad plant i s now up and running, which is a good milestone. And the second one is because of the good financial performance which we had during last couple of years, our external credit rating has also been upgraded during FY26

items.statement: FY27 top-line guidance based on 95% utilization of 11,000 tons capacity with slightly better realization than FY26
items.quote: Coming to FY27, the top-line guidance is based on our capacity of 11,000 tons, of which we expect to utilize almost 95%. That will be the guidance. From a pricing perspective, the realization compared to FY26 is slightly better.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin expected to show slight improvement over FY26
items.quote: Margins in the current financial year are showing a slight improvement over the last financial year.

items.statement: FY28 EBITDA margin expected to improve due to premium product mix, better than FY27
items.quote: In FY28, there will definitely be improvement due to the premium product mix, and it will be quite better than FY27.

items.statement: FY29 EBITDA margin structure expected to improve further
items.quote: In FY29, more or less, the margin structure will improve further.

items.statement: FY28 EBITDA margin targeted around 20-21% with 8-9 months freeze-dried production
items.quote: If we are going to take nine months of production for freeze-dried coffee, around eight to nine months of production, it will be in the region of around 20% to 21%.

items.statement: FY29 EBITDA margin targeted around 22-24%
items.quote: But going forward, in FY29, it will be much better. It should be in the region of around 22% to 24%.

items.statement: Brownfield expansion completed, capacity increased from 6,500 to 11,000 metric tons annually (69% increase), fully operational from Q1 FY27

items.statement: Current plant utilization at full capacity of 11,000 metric tons
items.quote: The current utilization of the plant is at full capacity. We have installed an additional capacity of 4,500 metric tons, bringing the total capacity to 11,000 metric tons, and we are now operating at the full capacity of 11,000 metric tons.

items.statement: FY27 capacity utilization expected around 95% of 11,000 tons, approximately 10,200-10,400 metric tons production
items.quote: For the whole year, although the installed capacity remains 11,000 metric tons, we are expecting around 95% capacity utilization. Out of this 95%, production should come to approximately 10,200 to 10,400 metric tons.

items.statement: Freeze-dried coffee facility of 5,500 metric tons annual capacity expected to complete by Q2 FY28, commercial operations from July 2027
items.quote: I am happy to share that execution remains on track and we currently expect 5,500 metric tons annual capacity facility to be completed by Q2 FY27-'28.

items.statement: Second phase freeze-dried capacity (additional 5,500 tons) capex estimated INR370-400 crores, land and building ready
items.quote: Yes, it should be in the region of around INR 370 crores to INR 400 crores, since the land and building are already available because we are now also taking care of the second line in our land and building plans.

items.statement: Additional debt of INR300 crores for freeze-dried project plus INR100 crores working capital by FY28, peak debt INR400 crores
items.quote: An additional debt component of around INR 300 crores will be added to the existing debt for FY28, along with INR 100 crores for working capital. That will be the peak debt level.

items.statement: FY27 debt level in line with FY26 with marginal increase of INR30-40 crores, interest rate 8.3-8.4%
items.quote: FY27 debt level will be more or less in line with FY26, with a marginal increase of around INR 30–40 crores. The debt interest rate will be approximately 8.3% to 8.4%.

items.statement: INR300 crores ECB at 5-6% cost, with hedging around 6%; INR100 crores working capital at 8.3%
items.quote: Out of INR 400 crores of debt, INR 300 crores is at a cost of around 5% to 6%, and INR 100 crores is in the range of 8.4%.

items.statement: Coffee prices stable globally, slight increase in packaging material costs (metal tins, aluminium) passed on to customers, realization slightly improved
items.quote: The prices will remain stable as of today. If you see globally, coffee prices are stable and have more or less settled at these levels. With regard to production and input costs, they have also more or less remained the same. Yes, I agree that there is a slight increase in packaging material costs due to the geopolitical situation, which we are passing on to customers.

items.statement: Realization improvement of 2-3% expected in FY27 due to premium product mix (agglomerated coffee in consumer packs)
items.quote: Yes, it should be in the region of around 2% to 3%.

items.statement: 19-20 global customers, top 5-6 contribute 45-50% of business, freeze-dried coffee to be sold to existing and new customers
items.quote: Right now, we have around 19 to 20 customers globally across all segments, regions, and geographies. Out of these, the top five to six customers contribute approximately 45% to 50% of the business.

items.statement: Sales mix: Africa 31%, CIS/Russia 22%, Southeast Asia 22%, Americas/Europe 18%, local 5%; no Middle East exposure
items.quote: Currently, the mix is as follows: Africa accounts for about 31%, CIS and Russia about 22%, Southeast Asia around 22%, the Americas and Europe around 18%, and local sales about 5%.

items.statement: Coffee bean price decline to reduce working capital days and improve operating cash flows; FY27 Q1 lean season slightly negative, Q3-Q4 positive, overall positive
items.quote: Yes, definitely coffee bean prices are coming down. This will reduce working capital days, and it will directly impact operating cash flows. On the positive side, it will improve and grow further.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR0.15 per equity share for FY26 subject to shareholder approval
items.quote: In line with the company's philosophy and balanced capital allocation and commitment towards shareholders' value creation, the Board has also recommended a dividend of INR0.15 per equity share for FY26, subject to approval of shareholders.

items.statement: Global instant coffee production ~1,000,000 metric tons, growing ~30,000 metric tons annually
items.quote: So, as per the sources we have, the current total production of instant coffee, including freeze-dried coffee, is close to 10,00,000 metric tons. This is expected to grow every year by around 30,000 metric tons.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions no direct impact as company not focused on Middle East/Western Asia; markets are Central America, America, Europe, Africa, Southeast Asia, Russia
items.quote: The geopolitical situation has not really had any sort of direct impact on our company because we are not focused on the Middle East, Western Asia, or any of these regions. We are focused more towards Central America, America, Europe, as well as Africa, Southeast Asia, and Russia.

items.statement: Full capacity utilization visibility with customer commitments; 95% utilization expected for FY27, 70-75% of annual sales committed in Q1, full capacity sales from Q2
items.quote: Exactly, you are right. Around 95% capacity utilization will be there this year out of the 11,000 metric tons, and 95% of whatever production we are doing, the entire thing will be exported because we see visibility for the orders and sales.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 18.5%, FY27 expected ~19% with 0.5% improvement from capacity leverage, consumer packs already included in current margin
items.quote: Currently, it is approximately around 18.5%; it may go up by another 0.5% to up to 19%. And if we go with consumer packs and all, there will be an additional 2%, as we mentioned to you earlier as well.

items.statement: EBITDA per kg growth driven by product mix shift to packed form (35% to 53% in FY26), further 5-10% increase expected in FY27
items.quote: If you see last financial year, we improved significantly in packed form, moving from almost 35% to around 53%. That is the reason there has been growth in EBITDA per kg in FY26. Coming to FY27, there will be further slight growth in packed form, so definitely it will increase by around 5% to 10%, here and there.

items.statement: Equity capital raised for freeze-dried coffee manufacturing facility
items.quote: In parallel, the company has also raised equity capital for setting up the freeze-dried coffee manufacturing facility, which represents an important strategic step in expanding our capability into higher value-added segments.

items.statement: FY27 booking value growth guidance of 35% to 40%
items.quote: So long-term guidance remains at 25% to 30% CAGR over the 4 to 5 years. I think this year, we have a chance of being able to do better. So I think we have a chance that we can do about 35% to 40% in the current financial year.

items.statement: FY27 business development target of INR4,000-5,000 crores GDV
items.quote: We believe this year, we can have BD lock in about INR4,000 crores to INR5,000 crores for the financial year.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin target of 22% to 25% for new projects
items.quote: And our guidance is we are looking at projects with a 22% to 25% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity ratio ceiling of 1:1
items.quote: But our guidance remains that we will not exceed a ratio of 1:1. So that is our net debt-to-equity ratio that we have already guided for.

items.statement: FY26 booking value of INR1,550 crores, up 22% YoY
items.quote: During the year, we achieved our highest ever annual booking value of INR1,550 crores, representing a strong 22% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 bookings crossed INR600 crores for first time
items.quote: During the quarter, we achieved our highest ever quarterly booking and collections with bookings crossing INR600 crores milestones for the first time.

items.statement: FY26 new launches contributed INR930 crores (60% of bookings)
items.quote: New launches contributed nearly 60% of annual bookings amounting to approximately INR930 crores, reflecting both healthy market demand and strong customer confidence in our offerings.

items.statement: Bengaluru contributed INR485 crores (31% of FY26 bookings)
items.quote: Bengaluru continues to be a key growth engine for us, contributing INR485 crores and accounting for almost 31% of our annual bookings.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 Arvind Skycrest launch: 164 units, INR262 crores, 53% inventory sold in a week
items.quote: In Bengaluru, we launched Arvind Skycrest in Bannerghatta towards the end of the quarter, where we achieved bookings of 164 units amounting to INR262 crores, translating to approximately 53% of the total inventory. This was within a week of the launch.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 Arvind Greenfields Vadodara launch: 323 units, INR178 crores, 42% inventory sold
items.quote: Similarly, in Vadodara, we launched Arvind Greenfields on Ajwa road and achieved bookings of 323 units, amounting to INR178 crores, representing nearly 42% of the launched inventory.

items.statement: FY26 business development added INR3,140 crores top line potential
items.quote: During the year, we added projects with an estimated cumulative top line potential of INR3,140 crores, significantly enhancing our medium-term growth visibility.

items.statement: Post FY26 signed largest Mumbai high-rise project with INR2,400 crores top line potential
items.quote: Subsequent to the year-end, we also signed our largest ever high-rise project in Mumbai with an estimated top line potential of approximately INR2,400 crores.

items.statement: FY26 investing activities for BD deployment ~INR600 crores
items.quote: So last year, if you see across our portfolio, Amit, we have actually got investing activities exceeding about INR600 crores. So that is the amount which is actually going towards the BD, which has been done.

items.statement: FY27 BD deployment spend slightly higher than FY26's INR600 crores
items.quote: So we may probably have slightly more than last year, but it is a proportion of how much we actually get in the JD and how much in the outright structure. So it could be slightly more.

items.statement: FY27 launch pipeline: 6 projects, inventory INR3,000-3,500 crores
items.quote: We think put together, we might be putting out inventory about INR3,000 crores to INR3,500 crores with these 6 launches as some of the launches which are fairly big will be brought in the market in phases.

items.statement: FY27 launches: 1 in Ahmedabad (Vastrapur), 3 in Bengaluru, 2 in Mumbai
items.quote: Our expectation is that we'll be launching one project at least in Ahmedabad. So that is a project in Vastrapur. We are looking at 3 launches in Bengaluru, and we are at least looking at 2 launches coming up in Mumbai.

items.statement: Mumbai Pen-Khopoli plotted project first phase INR500-600 crores
items.quote: I think our sense is we might be breaking into 3 phases most likely. So I think while the first phase should be somewhere between INR500 crores to INR600 crores is currently what we think.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 adjusted EBITDA grew 26% YoY to INR56.4 crores
items.quote: Q4 adjusted EBITDA grew 26% year-on-year to INR56.4 crores, while PAT grew 103% year-on-year to INR44 crores against INR21.8 crores in the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: FY26 adjusted EBITDA INR156 crores vs INR196 crores FY25
items.quote: For FY26, we reported revenues of INR564 crores as against INR713 crores last year. Adjusted EBITDA stood at INR156 crores compared to INR196 crores last year.

items.statement: Commodity costs up ~4% post-war; budgeted contingency absorbs increase without price hikes
items.quote: So what we have seen actually pre-war and post-war, if I were to compare it immediately across the portfolio, we are seeing almost a 4% increase in the costing of the product that we are actually offering to the customer.

items.statement: FY26 net operating cash flow INR417 crores; Q4 INR96 crores
items.quote: Strong collections and healthy profitability translated into net operating cash flows of INR417 crores during FY26, further reinforcing the resilience and quality of our business model. During Q4 alone, operating cash flow stood at INR96 crores.

items.statement: Unrealized operating cash flows exceed INR4,970 crores over next 4-5 years
items.quote: Based on the current project pipeline, we estimate unrealized operating cash flows exceeding INR4,970 crores, which we expect to realize over the next 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: FY27 OCF expected flat at FY26 level (INR417 crores) despite higher collections
items.quote: So somewhere, I think we are looking at maintaining the same trajectory for OCF that we have probably delivered in FY26 in terms of the absolute numbers.

items.statement: Current net debt INR167 crores; net debt-to-equity 0.26x
items.quote: Currently, our debt position even right now remains very comfortable. We are at 0.26 net debt-to-equity ratio, as you see.

items.statement: HDFC platform: INR600 crores committed, INR350 crores used; backfilling and adding capacity
items.quote: We had a platform of about INR600 crores with HDFC. From that, we have already used INR350 crores. So the idea is to kind of backfill that number and create additional capital available for us as we expand and grow.

items.statement: NCD approval obtained as additional funding option
items.quote: We have also taken an internal sign-off on NCD. So that is something that we are keeping as an option available for ourselves as well.

items.statement: ~50% of CXO team joined in last 1 year
items.quote: Maybe I think if you look at almost close to 50% of the team that is now working directly with me has actually come in the last 1 year.

items.statement: FY26 sustenance sales >INR600 crores; Q4 sustenance ~INR180 crores
items.quote: And even on sustenance, this will be one of our much stronger quarters what we've managed to deliver in Q4. So I think stable, and that is what we are currently seeing, but we are very watchful of the market.

items.statement: FY27 sustenance sales growth expected ~15% over FY26
items.quote: But when we are looking at our current mix today, our understanding is sustenance can show a growth of about 15% over what we have delivered in FY26.

items.statement: Mumbai redevelopment projects have lower OCF vs outright Bengaluru projects
items.quote: Bengaluru, quite a few of our recent acquisitions, as you know, were outright in nature. And Mumbai the 3 projects that we have, one, is a joint development, the other 2 are actually redevelopment. So hence, the OCF numbers are actually lower than the outright project.

items.statement: Forest Trails Bengaluru 50% unsold; site experience readiness in 3-4 months to drive sales
items.quote: I think we expect it to be ready over the next 3, 4 months. And then we will be going forward with a stronger sales activation so that we are able to convey the premium proposition that we are offering in this project.

items.statement: FY27 order inflow target of INR 12,000 crores
items.quote: Looking ahead to FY27, the company is targeting order inflow of around INR 12,000 crores with a strategic focus on expanding our BOP EPC portfolio and securing new O&M contracts.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth target of 21%
items.quote: And for the FY27, we are projecting around 21% growth.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin target of 12.5% including other income
items.quote: We are hoping that this year we are expecting to touch EBITDA of 12.5%, including other income.

items.statement: FY27 MDO revenue target of INR 500 crores
items.quote: INR 350 crores we are projecting for the FY27 and INR 500 crores for FY28 from KBP.

items.statement: Total order backlog including MDO at INR 55,151 crores; executable book excluding MDO at INR 15,899 crores
items.quote: The total order backlog, including MDO contracts, stands at approximately INR 55,151 crores. Excluding MDO order, the executable book stands at around INR 15,899 crores.

items.statement: FY26 order inflow of INR 7,210 crores vs target of INR 10,000 crores (72% achievement)
items.quote: From an order inflow perspective, the company secured orders worth of approximately INR 7,210 crores during FY26, against our target of Rs 10,000 Cr , achieving around 72% of the annual target.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin stable at 12.3%; Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 11.17%
items.quote: EBITDA for FY26 was INR 750 crores, up 16% YoY, while EBITDA margins remained stable at 12.3%.

items.statement: MDO blended EBITDA margin ~15% currently, targeting 20% at peak capacity
items.quote: We are estimating blended EBITDA together around 20% at peak rate capacity, At present, on an average EBITDA of 15% margin we have got.

items.statement: O&M EBITDA margin 15-16%; construction (erection, civil) margins 8-10%
items.quote: O&M is always around 15% to 16%, and the remaining construction will always be less than 10%.

items.statement: FY27 capex of INR 400 crores at Power Mech level (washery construction) plus INR 400 crores in Tasra SPV for coal handling plant and railway siding
items.quote: Capex, we are constructing washery as of now, and we'll complete the washery activity. So Around INR 400 crores capex will be addition by FY27. And in TASRA SPV, INR 400 crores of Capex Tasra Coal Handling Plant and railway siding is added.

items.statement: Strong thermal power pipeline: government target of 80-100 GW coal-based capacity; Adani targeting 50 GW; NTPC 11,380 MW ordered; BHEL direct orders ~INR 2.8 lakh crores translating to INR 60,000 crores opportunity for Power Mech
items.quote: Therefore, the expectation is that the present opportunities what has been ordered, comes to substantially INR 2.8 lakh crores in terms of the direct ordering done on BHEL, and L&T, on the major packages. That will translate into a reasonable opportunity for us about INR 60,000 crores in various segments like installation business, civil business, structural works and the balance of plants on pack

items.statement: Identified opportunity basket of INR 70,000 crores across power, non-power, infra, O&M, metro, EPC for FY27
items.quote: We have identified about INR 70,000 crores of opportunities in terms of what is visible in the various sectors, in the power sector, non -power sector, infra works, then O&M services, metro maintenance and EPC works, etcetera.

items.statement: Adani orders: 6,400 MW across 4 projects worth INR 3,166 crores; BHEL orders: ~7,000 MW thermal + 1,400 MW nuclear + Singareni BOP worth INR 4,700 crores total
items.quote: Similarly, from Adani side, we are working in about 4 major projects in Adani in Mahan, Phase 2 and Phase 3, Mirzapur Phase 1 and Raipur, totally 6,400 MW and ongoing projects valued about INR 3,166 crores.

items.statement: Metro O&M breakthrough: INR 279 crores Mumbai Monorail contract (15 stations); targeting outsourcing trend across 1,095 km operational metro expanding to 2,000 km
items.quote: Recently, a major breakthrough has been in entering into O&M business in the Metro sector, INR 279 crores. We have taken up light railway in Bombay, that is 15 stations work.

items.statement: Operating cash flow improved from INR 74 lakhs in FY25 to INR 430 crores in FY26 driven by receivables realization
items.quote: The company's operating cash flow improved significantly during FY26, increasing from INR 74 lakhs in FY25 to INR 430 crores in FY26, primarily driven by the improved realization of receivables during the year.

items.statement: Gross debt INR 622 crores, net debt INR 163 crores, debt-equity 0.32x as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: As on 31st March 2026, gross debt was INR 622 crores while net debt was INR 163 crores. The debt equity ratio as on the same date remained comfortable at 0.32x.

items.statement: Domestic contracts have PVC escalation clauses covering steel, cement, diesel price increases; international O&M unaffected by commodity volatility
items.quote: Domestically, there is increase in the pricing, and at the same time, we are covered with the escalation clauses. Every contract we are protected by escalation clauses. We will get the reimbursement from the clients.

items.statement: MDO revenue mix: 7% of total revenue in FY27, 13% in FY28
items.quote: MDO mix will be 7% in overall revenue for FY 27. And the same will jump to 13% in FY 28 revenue.

items.statement: Order book execution rate: ~40% of opening order value per year; average execution period 2.5 years
items.quote: For every year, we are doing 40% execution on opening order value. The 2.5 years, execution time you can assume the average order size.

items.statement: KBP mine: FY27 INR 350 crores revenue, FY28 INR 500 crores; Tasra mine: washery completion by Dec 2026, FY27 INR 150 crores, FY28 INR 750 crores
items.quote: INR 350 crores we are projecting for the FY27 and INR 500 crores for FY28 from KBP. Tasra, our washery construction is undergoing, and maybe by December we'll complete the construction of washery. Maybe by mid of Q4 FY 27, we'll start our production from the Tasra mine. We are projecting INR 150 crores revenue in FY27, and it will increase to INR 750 crores by FY28.

items.statement: Revenue mix FY26: 95% domestic / 5% international; 64% power / 36% non-power
items.quote: For FY26, the geographical mix was 95% domestic and 5% international. The power sector contributed 64% of revenues, while non -power sector accounted for 36%.

items.statement: Bid hit ratio ~15%; typically bid INR 40,000-50,000 crores opportunities annually
items.quote: The general size is that, our previous record is we have been bidding INR 40,000 crores to INR 50,000 crores of opportunities for bidding. The hit ratio can be somewhere about 15%.

items.statement: Government coal gasification plan: INR 37,500 crores initial investment; tracking for future EPC opportunities
items.quote: Government has planned initial investment of INR 37,500 crores because looking at the import dependency of the fossil fuels, particularly the petrol, LNG, and other things, coal gasification is an alternative.

items.statement: Water division: INR 900 crores balance order; INR 128 crores WIP pending certification, INR 90 crores receivable; execution paused, focusing on O&M conversion
items.quote: Balance is around INR 900 crores of order we have to execute, ma'am. So last one year, we have stopped execution of the work, and have instead focused on nearer -to-completion projects.

items.statement: Total headcount >40,000 (70-75% labor); O&M workforce ~18,000; managing labor availability through recruitment and training
items.quote: Our total headcount has gone up more than 40,000. Of that, 70% to 75% is on the labor side. And then O&M, in that O&M is about 18,000.

items.statement: Management will provide firm FY27 guidance during Q1 earnings call; optimistic about strong volume growth and double-digit revenue growth
items.quote: we will take some time and maybe during the Q1 earnings call, we'll be able to give you with a firm guidance for the entire fiscal year. But we are very optimistic and hopeful about FY27 to go well and a strong volume -- with a strong volume growth.

items.statement: Management expects EBITDA margin to be better than FY26's ~11% if conditions remain favorable
items.quote: EBITDA margin this year, we have done around 10.82%. Our EBITDA margin was at almost 11%. And this year also, our margin should be good . So overall, if the situation remains okay and favorable, the margin should be better than what we closed last fiscal.

items.statement: Cotton and yarn prices stabilizing; no further price hikes expected beyond the 4-6% already implemented
items.quote: we don't think that it will continue further because we are seeing the cotton prices and the yarn prices are getting stabilized now. So the price hike that we have taken in the Q1, I think we don't have to take any further price hike now.

items.statement: FY26 full-year gross margin 33.0%, Operating EBITDA margin 10.6%, PAT margin 5.7%; ad spend rationalized to 5.5% of revenue with further moderation expected
items.quote: Operating EBITDA rose 9.3% to INR200 crores with margin of 10.6%. Profit after tax reached INR107 crores, registering 18.0% year-year growth with PAT margin of 5.7%. ... We successfully rationalized our advertisement spend to 5.5% of Operating Income in FY26. As structural operating leverage kicks in at this scale, we confidently expect this ratio to moderate further in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Management expects gross margin improvement in FY27 as price hikes offset input cost pressure
items.quote: No, no, we are ready took the price or we expect it -- we expect that gross margin also improves.

items.statement: Underlying demand intact but retail footfall temporarily reduced due to exceptional heat; Q1 typically strong due to summer wear-and-tear and festive periods (Eid, Holi)
items.quote: But what we are seeing in this particular quarter is because of the exceptional heat conditions across the Indian markets, so the retail footfall for this quarter has reduced a bit, but it's a timing issue. It's not a structural one. So the underlying demand has not changed. It has -- it remains intact.

items.statement: Quick commerce channel grew 437% YoY, contribution increased from 0.5% to 2.5%; non-traditional channels (modern trade, e-commerce, quick commerce) grew 24.2% YoY in FY26
items.quote: Our sustained focus on quick commerce delivered exceptional results with the channel growing 437% year-on-year and increasing its contribution to revenue from 0.5% to 2.5%. Driven by this strong momentum, non -traditional channels, which includes modern trade, e -commerce and quick commerce overall recorded a healthy growth of 24.2% year -on-year in FY26

items.statement: Economic segment growth driven by Tier 2/3 city consumption, shift from unorganized to branded, and 3 years of advertising (Saif Ali Khan for Dollar Lehar); not structural downtrading
items.quote: It's not a structural thing which is happening. It's a very temporary thing. And moreover, we think that Dollar Always or the economy range of products sale is increasing because of high consumption that is happening in Tier 2, Tier 3 cities, majorly in semi -rural or rural areas. And might be, there's a shift from unorganized to organized at that particular segment because people are always aspir

items.statement: Inventory days optimized at 95-100 days minimum due to 90-day production cycle and SKU complexity; FY26 improvement partly seasonal
items.quote: at an optimized level, inventory days will be 95 to 100 days minimum because in our industry, the production cycle is about 90 days from the time we order yarn, from the time we invert the yarn till the final goods and the goods getting sold. So mostly 95 to 100 days is at an optimized level, given the number of SKUs also that we have, the different kind of categories that we have.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR3 per share (15.8% payout ratio) subject to shareholder approval
items.quote: The Board has recommended a dividend of INR3 per share, subject to shareholders' approval, representing a dividend payout ratio of 15.8%.

items.statement: Merger of 9 promoter companies filed with NCLT; first motion announced; expected to reduce related party expenses by INR4-5 crores (royalty, service charges, rent); minimal revenue impact
items.quote: With respect to our merger, we already filed the application with the NCLT. And the first motion is also announced by the NCLT. Basically, the merger of RPT with our main Dollar companies, mainly lead to corporate governance and we reduce our related party transactions. T he revenue effect on the total revenue is not much like in earlier calls, we also expect that around INR4 crores to INR5 crores

items.statement: Exports (3% of sales) primarily to Middle East/Gulf, some African countries, Southeast Asia (Myanmar, Burma)
items.quote: So most of our exports that happens. It happens in the Middle East, Gulf countries. There are some African countries. And in the Southeast Asia, Myanmar and Burma is a market that we supply.

items.statement: G.O.A.T JV (Pepe Jeans license) generated INR49 crores revenue (+45% YoY) with INR4.9 crores PAT (~10% margin) in FY26
items.quote: In full year FY26, this partnership generated a revenue of INR49 crores, that is up 45% compared to last year. In the same period, PAT stood at INR4.9 crores with a PAT margin of about 10%.

items.statement: Lakshya Phase 2 expansion into new states facing competitive pushback; developing tailored entry strategies for non-dominant territories
items.quote: So, in non-Lakshya states to enter new states, we are getting some pushback also in the market. So -- but we are very hopeful that after this Phase 2, we'll again resume entering into new states developing under Lakshya. So that's what we are strategizing now.

items.statement: Women's segment (Missy) seeing degrowth in leggings/churidar but growth in pants; lingerie/intimate wear growing at industry standards; hopeful for outer garment growth in FY27
items.quote: Given the overall test and preference that has changed in the market for the past 2 years. A couple of years, we are seeing a degrowth in the market with respect to the leggings and churidar sales. But overall pant sales are increasing simultaneously, but not up to the 100% mark. items.statement: Management targets 30% EBITDA margin for FY26 and aims to maintain it going forward
items.quote: Now, if you go to the financial year, the margin comes to around 31.95%. And why there is a dip up to 27%? Because in this quarter, we have booked some exceptional items. If we deduct those exceptional items in this quarter, it will be around 30% only.

items.statement: Catering revenue growth target of 15%, tourism 20%, internet ticketing 10% non-convenience fee revenue growth
items.quote: You see, revenue-wise primary growth I see in catering it will continue to maintain around 15%. And tourism we are eyeing to continue with around this year we are looking to 19% should continue to be around 20%. And IT business is 7%. We want to increase the non -convenience fee. And for that we are already working on unified portal and iPay. So, that will be around 10%.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 27.33% impacted by exceptional items; full year FY26 EBITDA margin 31.95%
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at Rs. 399 crores with a healthy EBITDA margin of 27.33%. While margins were impacted slightly due to a change in revenue mix particularly higher contributions from catering and tourism segments, the company continued to maintain strong and sustainable profitability.

items.statement: Catering EBIT margin declined from 10.4% to 6.3% in Q4 due to higher ECL, CSR, legacy item absence and GST on premium sales
items.quote: In the catering, the margin dip because of this exceptional item. First of all, last year, same quarter, we have provided for ECL item of only Rs. 5 crores. This year, it is Rs. 16 crores. CSR allocation under catering was done as against Rs. 1 crore. It's Rs. 5 crores. And legacy item, this year, it is not there. Last year, Rs. 33 crores. items.statement: Internet ticketing EBIT margin declined from 85% to 76% in Q4 due to CSR allocation, direct cost and UPI share increase
items.quote: Then, as regards IT business, the margin, the reason for the down is allocation of CSR of additional Rs. 17 crores on this. Direct cost around Rs. 8 crores. And increase in the UPI share, it is again Rs. 8 crores.

items.statement: Target to maintain current EBITDA margin levels in FY27 despite Q1 pressure from Rajasthan manpower deployment
items.quote: With regards to the margin profile, we are working towards maintaining the current level of EBITDA margins. There might be some impact in the Q1 where there is upfront deployment of manpower.

items.statement: Like-to-like organic growth for continuing PPP projects at ~13%
items.quote: Our organic growth for like-to-like projects which are continuing is almost in the range of around 13-odd percent.

items.statement: PPP contracts have rate escalation clauses of 2-5% annually or biennially
items.quote: So for the PPP tenders, we have rate escalations which are factored into the agreement. They are contractually embedded. And these rate escalations vary for each tender, ranging anywhere from 2% to 5%.

items.statement: DSO reduced from 155 days in Q3 to 139 days in Q4 FY26; highest quarterly collection of INR1,580 million in Q4
items.quote: Through the sustained engagement, disciplined receivable management and tighter execution across the projects, we have successfully reduced our DSO from 155 days in quarter 3 to 139 days at the end of the quarter 4 FY '25-'26.

items.statement: H1 FY26 collections at INR2,910 million including INR1,580 million in Q4; virtually zero bad debt in 14 years
items.quote: In the half year alone, collections stood at approximately INR2,910 million, including INR1,580 million in Q4, the highest quarterly collection in our history. 14 years, virtually 0 bad debt.

items.statement: Borrowings include INR4,300 million NCD to ADB, term loans and working capital; funded via internal accruals, operational cash flows and vendor finance capex model
items.quote: Our borrow ings include NCD issued to ADB were 4,300 million, term loans and working capital. We continue to fund our growth through a combination of internal accrual, operational cash flows and efficient vendor finance capex model

items.statement: Apulki Healthcare investment: INR222 million value gain in FY26; exclusive diagnostics rights for 30+ years across Apulki hospitals
items.quote: Our strategic investment in Apulki Healthcare has been in the right direction. The value gain of approximately INR222 million during the year validates our investment thesis around integrated tertiary health care and long-duration health care infrastructure partnerships.

items.statement: Radiology-pathology revenue split approximately 50-50 in FY26
items.quote: I think there is a different -- I mean, the split within radiology and pathology is in the range of 50%, 50%.

items.statement: Retail contribution 8% of FY26 revenue (sixfold growth from INR10 crores to INR60 crores)
items.quote: Our retail business scaled from almost INR10 crores in FY '25 to INR60 crores in '26, which is a sixfold growth in a single year that firmly establishes the consumer appetite for Krsnaa's brand of affordable and quality diagnostics.

items.statement: Long-term retail aspiration: 25-30% of group revenue in 3-5 years
items.quote: Well, good afternoon, Mr. Manoj. And over the longer horizon, around 3 to 4 years or 5 years kind of a period that we are looking for, having contribution of retail alone within the entire group revenue close to 25% to 30% should be there in the line with.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu only major contract up for renewal in FY27; discussions ongoing for extension
items.quote: So I think except for Tamil Nadu, there are not major contracts which are up for renewal during the year. Because typically in this journey also many times, the authorities also give us enough to extend, the discussions are happening if tender is published or not.

items.statement: Receivable delays in Karnataka and Himachal due to administrative issues (official transfers, new SNS SPARSH system); collections progressing
items.quote: For example, when an MD NHM officer or a government official gets transferred or moves out, the new officer takes his own time to look into the records. There were also some challenges from the funds that were coming from the central and the new system, the SNS SPARSH that is being deployed, where there are operational challenges at the respective governments.

items.statement: Leadership team stable: Group CEO Mitesh Dave, Chairman Yash Mutha, Interim CFO; previous CFO left after 5 years for personal growth
items.quote: So I think the team is intact and strong to deliver growth and value in the coming years or coming quarters as well. And any specific details, you can reach out to Sujoy, and we'll share more of the details offline.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 12.3% YoY to INR 456 cr, driven by 18.9% online and 5.5% distribution channel growth
items.quote: Our revenue from operations grew by 12.3% year-on-year to INR 456 crores, largely benefited by higher revenue in the online channel, which has registered a growth of around 19% and distribution channel, which has grown by around 5.5%.

items.statement: ASP grew 7% YoY to INR 683 in FY26 driven by sneaker range and women/kids mix
items.quote: Our ASP grew by 7% YOY to INR 683 driven by robust demand for our sneaker range and our healthy product mix in women and kids category, reinforcing Campus as a trusted brand for the entire family.

items.statement: Sneaker portfolio grew ~100% YoY in FY26 and 50%+ quarterly
items.quote: We have grown this portfolio about a 100% year-on-year. But this year we have delivered also like a 100% plus growth on an annual b asis. And quarterly it's been like 50% plus growth with respect to a sneaker portfolio

items.statement: Pant Nagar and Haridwar plants currently deliver ~2 lakh pairs/month, targeting 8-9 lakh pairs/month sneaker capacity
items.quote: We are targeting in totality 8-9 lakh pair monthly production of sneakers and we are well on track to do that. So it is a phase development.

items.statement: FY26 gross margin 53.5% (+120 bps), EBITDA margin 17.5% (+145 bps), PAT margin 8.4% (+80 bps)
items.quote: Our gross margins were at 53.5% in FY26 versus 52.3% in FY25 and improvement of 120 basis points driven by product and channel mix. Our EBITDA for the year FY26 was at INR 314.7 crores. The EBITDA margin stood at 17.5% during the year and improvement of 145 basis points versus last year driven by revenue growth.

items.statement: Price hikes taken across range to cover RM inflation and minimum wage impact; peak RM pricing seen, prices now correcting
items.quote: We have taken enough increase in pricing to cover the inflationary impact. We do not see the RM impact going worse from here. I think we have seen the peak and with time, in maybe a quarter or so, it should start coming down as the war settles, but the pricing will not change.

items.statement: No formal margin guidance for FY27 but will endeavor to stay within previously guided 17-19% EBITDA margin band
items.quote: No guidance, unfortunately. But we will definitely endeavor to stay within the range we have guided before, 17% to 19%.

items.statement: FY27 capex to normalize after FY26 Pant Nagar acquisition; routine maintenance, molds, EBO stores, IT infra; Pant Nagar expansion over next 3 years
items.quote: So we don't see FY26 like CAPEX spends in FY27.

items.statement: Distributor meet orders 100% aligned with AOP till September; strong order visibility
items.quote: Depending on the AOP alignments with our distributor partner, we were able to close that over 100%. So, the total alignment, which was deployed to the partner network till September, after excluding April revenue, which is already recognized by that thing. The balance number is what was committed and was aligned with the partners to come and place an order for, and they were 100% of that number.

items.statement: FG inventory days increased 5-6 days in FY26 to right level for growth; will sustain at this level
items.quote: Last year we reached to a FG inventory level in terms of pairs or in terms of days of cover to a very, very minimal level and we had to do that correction. We were deferring that correction. First, we were prioritizing liquidation of non-BIS inventory and then eventually where we have reached as of March '26, that is the right level of inventory to sustain the kind of growth or what we are aspirin

items.statement: Lease liability spike due to 71-year Pant Nagar land lease accounting; normal rental ~INR 65.4 cr lower
items.quote: It is a technical accounting thing. The Pantnagar facility which we acquired, technically it is on a 71-year lease from the state government. So, the cash outflow is shown as a payment of lease liability, whereas like in a normal course you would treat it as a fixed asset acquisition. So that is why that number looks a bit inflated compared to previous year.

items.statement: BIS compliance on track; fully compliant by July 31; no official relaxation heard
items.quote: I think it's just a chatter at the point, like there is nothing that we have heard of officially from the government yet. And as a company, we are fully covered with respect to the compliance. So, as we speak, we are left with hardly any stock of BIS. So, we will be fully compliant by 31st of July.

items.statement: Industry grew 7-8% vs Campus 12% in FY26; market share gains evident; smaller players struggling to pass on cost inflation
items.quote: We don't think the industry has grown last year beyond 7% to 8%, you know, at most. And us growing at about 12%, we think we have definitely gained market share. So there is some bit of consolidation that has happened in the market, both with respect to sports and sneaker range.

items.statement: EBO network steady at 300 stores in FY26; plan to open 60-80 new stores in FY27 (40% COCO, 60% FOFO)
items.quote: Going forward, this year we will be back wit h respect to opening of new stores and we expect to open anywhere between 60 to 70 stores or about 80 stores, I would say

items.statement: Major RM inflation in EVA and PU linked to crude; peak seen, latest purchases at lower prices
items.quote: But major impact we have seen is in EVA and PU pricing. But already, like I mentioned before, we have seen the peak of it. And as we speak, the prices have started to come down a little. And our latest purchase was at a slightly lower price, which is encouraging signs because the market is reacting to it.

items.statement: Demand impact uncertain if geopolitical conflict prolongs; March saw some demand impact but not significant
items.quote: Going forward, of course, if the war sustains, then it's anybody's guess, to be very honest. Nobody will be able to commit any kind of numbers with this kind of scenario, prolonging for a very long time, right? But if it sort of settles at this point, we see a good recovery in place and the market should recover also fairly soon.

items.statement: Expect double-digit growth in contrast media segment in FY27 driven by new launches and volume growth
items.quote: we do expect 1 or 2 validations and 1 commercial launch, which should actually like ensure that we will actually get into a sort of double-digit growth. That's what we are expecting.

items.statement: Annual forecast from contrast media customer shows mid-single digit growth for FY27
items.quote: Annual forecast from the customer has a mid-single digit growth for FY27.

items.statement: Expect PI/API segment to normalize and grow over FY25 peak in FY27
items.quote: Our participation in the supply network in FY27 of this innovator customer will enable us to normalize the growth and grow over the peak sale we had achieved in FY25.

items.statement: Total Vizag greenfield capex approximately INR1,000 crores over 3 years
items.quote: The total capex that we envisage for the Vizag project is approximately INR1,000 crores over a period of approximately 3 years.

items.statement: Plan to spend approximately INR400 crores in FY27 on Vizag, Mahad completion and Ambernath additions
items.quote: We propose to spend approximately INR400 crores in FY27 towards Vizag greenfield, completion of Mahad and other additions in Ambernath.

items.statement: Vizag Phase 1 to develop dedicated blocks for contrast media intermediates, high-intensity sweeteners, pharma intermediates
items.quote: In Phase 1, we plan to develop dedicated manufacturing blocks across contrast media intermediates, high-intensity sweeteners, and pharma intermediates.

items.statement: Mahad Unit 3 backward integration plant to go onstream in FY27 with slow ramp-up
items.quote: Yes, we will -- the plant will go onstream this year, and we will start consuming the quantities that we produce, but we plan a slow ramp-up.

items.statement: Vizag greenfield capacity expected to come online in 24-30 months
items.quote: And we envisage 24 to 30 months for that capacity to get online.

items.statement: PI segment inventory destocking complete, shipments and order visibility improving
items.quote: Encouragingly, the PI segment, which had witnessed inventory buildup over the previous quarters, has now started normalizing and shipment trends and improving order visibility are evident.

items.statement: Tracking ~20 active RFPs in PI/CDMO segment, 2 expected to commercialize in FY27
items.quote: Within the PI and CDMO segment, we have been tracking approximately 20 active RFPs, primarily across chronic therapeutic areas, including intermediates linked to GLP -1 programs and peptide building blocks. Encouragingly, we believe that 2 of these opportun ities are expected to move into the commercialization phase during the current year

items.statement: Evaluating 2 high-conviction lateral entry opportunities with dedicated Vizag capacity planned
items.quote: In addition, we are evaluating 2 high conviction commercial stage opportunities, which may potentially evolve into strategic lateral entries, for which dedicated capacity is being factored into our long-term planning at Vizag.

items.statement: Expect 3-4 new contrast media product launches in FY27
items.quote: In the contrast media segment, we expect 3 to 4 new product launches during the current year, further expanding our participation across advanced intermediates within this space.

items.statement: High-intensity sweetener product under validation, trial quantities expected in coming quarters
items.quote: In the high-intensity sweetener segment, one high-volume product is currently under validation and we expect trial quantities to be shipped over the coming quarters.

items.statement: Peptide building blocks lab supplies started to innovators and large peptide CDMOs
items.quote: Yes. We have started lab supplies to some innovators and we have also started some lab supplies to some very large peptide CDMOs.

items.statement: FY26 gross margin 54% vs 55% in FY25; Q4 gross margin 56%
items.quote: For the full year FY26, our reported gross margin is at 54% compared to 55% in FY25.

items.statement: Freight costs increased post March 2026, logistics costs in FY27 to be evaluated
items.quote: Freight cost post March '26 have increased. While the impact is not felt in FY26, logistics costs in FY27 will have to be evaluated.

items.statement: Rupee depreciation improved export realization and negated raw material price increase in FY26
items.quote: In FY26, rupee depreciation improved realization of exports and negated raw material price increase, which happened in the last month of the financial year due to Iran war.

items.statement: Discussions encouraging with select customers on pricing pass-through based on geopolitical situation
items.quote: The discussions are encouraging with select customers on pricing and pass-through based on current geopolitical situation.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with liquid financial assets of INR400 crores at FY26 end
items.quote: As on year-end, we are a debt-free company. Cash flow from operating activities stood at INR334 crores.

items.statement: No immediate fundraise planned; accelerating capex with internal liquidity
items.quote: I think from a company standpoint, given the liquidity it has, I think we are going -- rather accelerating our capex plan. So we are well positioned as a debt-free company.

items.statement: Mahad backward integration for contrast media key raw material progressing well to strengthen supply chain reliability
items.quote: At Mahad Unit 3 site, we are progressing well on the backward integration project for the key raw material within our contrast media portfolio. This project is strategically important as it strengthens supply chain reliability, improves integration, and enhances resilience against global disruptions.

items.statement: Close to 70% of energy consumption supported through renewables
items.quote: Today, close to 70% of our energy consumption is supported through renewables, and the company is awarded the CII National Award for Excellence in Energy Management.

items.statement: Contrast media growth driven by deeper partnerships with select customers on key molecules
items.quote: thematically, we believe there are some select partnerships that we have on key molecules is just translating into deeper partnerships. So we feel their offtake requirements also increasing, and that's a combination of the existing molecules plus the launch of new molecules in FY26.

items.statement: Customer warning letter monitored; no supply disruption seen currently; business as usual
items.quote: From my side, I think it's business as usual in this particular segment. And we don't see -- foresee any disruption in the coming quarters also.

items.statement: Peptide segment may see faster price erosion compared to contrast media and patented CDMO
items.quote: But then you must understand that as compared to the other segments, there could be faster, higher price erosion in this segment. In contrast media and the patented CDMO segment, we don't have that type of price erosion, which perhaps we may see in the peptide segment.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at approximately 25% to 27%
items.quote: Together, this total will constitute a revenue growth of approximately 25% to 27% for the full year.

items.statement: FY27 gross seat addition guided at 22,000 to 25,000 seats
items.quote: We have given guidance on the number of seats that we would add this year would be between 22,000 to 25,000 seats that we would add.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected to be similar to FY26 levels
items.quote: In terms of th e overall capex, the way we are projecting and seeing is it would be almost on similar lines of FY '26 across for these seats

items.statement: Enterprise and MNC clients now account for 64% of client base
items.quote: Enterprise and MNC clients now account for 64% of our client base.

items.statement: GCC clients contribute approximately 23% of rental revenues across 100+ unique GCC clients in 9 cities
items.quote: Awfis now serves 100-plus unique GCC clients across 9 cities contributing approximately 23% of our rental revenues.

items.statement: Closed 14 major GCC mandates in FY26 with 6 committed for FY27 and 7 in advanced discussions
items.quote: We closed 14 major GCC mandates in FY '26 with 6 already committed for FY '27 and another 7 in advanced stages of discussion.

items.statement: FY26 operating EBITDA margin expanded 350 bps to 36.8%
items.quote: Operating EBITDA grew 37% to INR550 crores, with EBITDA margins expanding by approximately 350 basis points to 36.8%.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin at 37%
items.quote: Operating EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR152 crores, a 31% increase year-on-year with EBITDA margins expanding to 37%.

items.statement: Design and build net margins at 7% to 8%
items.quote: The design and build margins are close to 7% to 8%, and this is the net margins that I'm referring to.

items.statement: FY27 Transform pipeline of INR130 crores already won for delivery over next 6-7 months
items.quote: The pipeline going into FY '27 is materially stronger with INR130 crores of mandates already won in delivery across the next 6 to 7 months.

items.statement: Pre-committed over 4 lakh sq ft under managed aggregation model through Q2 FY28
items.quote: We have already pre-committed over 4 lakh square feet under our MA model through Q2 FY '28.

items.statement: FY26 gross seat addition of 30,000 seats across 41 new centers, 100% in Grade A/A+ assets
items.quote: During FY '26, we added nearly 30,000 seats across the network on a gross basis across 41 new centers with 100% of new supply in Grade A/A+ assets.
